title: feat: launcher_core shared infrastructure + G7 merge-deadlock design
verbatim: feat: launcher_core shared infrastructure + G7 merge-deadlock design Two pieces of work: 1. bench/launcher_core.py — shared infrastructure for per-experiment launchers. Closes the three classes of latent bug that surfaced on launch_exp40.py's first end-to-end execution: run_experiment arity, RunnerConfig field mappings, .env loading. Future per- experiment launchers (launch_exp41.py, launch_exp42.py, etc.) should use this module rather than copying logic from launch_exp40.py. The module exports: - load_env_file: reads .env, populates os.environ via setdefault so shell-provided values still take precedence - load_cdsfl_directive: loads the system-prompt text - load_experiment_config: returns ExperimentConfig from the orchestrator's load_default_config - build_runner_config_from_dict: maps a JSON config dict to RunnerConfig including test_article/context_files/domain - dispatch_experiment: calls run_experiment with the correct three-argument signature .env is auto-loaded on module import as a defensive measure against future launcher authors forgetting load_env_file(). launch_exp40.py is NOT refactored to use launcher_core in this commit — the continuation run is currently using it and mid-run refactor risks compounding changes. launch_exp40.py will be refactored to use launcher_core in a follow-up commit after the continuation closes. Future per-experiment launchers should use launcher_core from inception. 2. G7 merge-deadlock resolution rule design note (paired output under CDSFL note standard v1.2): - experimental_notes/G7_Merge_Deadlock_Resolution_Design_2026-05-15.md (technical: file paths, configuration knobs, implementation surface) - experimental_notes/G7_Merge_Deadlock_Resolution_Design_Plain_English_2026-05-15.md (accessible: problem statement, founder's proposal, how the rule would work, cost discipline, what it doesn't cover) - ~/Desktop/CDSFL_tts/G7_Merge_Deadlock_Resolution_Design_2026-05-15.txt (TTS mirror) Design follows the founder's 14 May 2026 proposal: apply compelled-convergence to merge decisions when the runner's auto-merge cannot decide between candidate targets. Dispatch a focused query to all five panel models with the new finding + candidate canonical entries; aggregate the five votes; merge to majority target or keep deferred. Implementation deferred to a separate commit after the Exp 40 continuation closes — adding G7 mid-run would risk compounding changes with the seven other fixes already folded in. verbatim: exp40 plan-E: collate all past Exp 40 CLOSED fixes; build test-gated cleaned baseline Item E of the approved remediation plan. title: exp40 plan-A: fix the silent finding-ID collision-overwrite (real fix, not gated)
verbatim: exp40 plan-A: fix the silent finding-ID collision-overwrite (real fix, not gated) Supersedes the observation-only deferral per founder directive. The `finding_by_id = {f.finding_id: f for f in findings}` comprehension in build_feedback_records was last-wins: when two findings shared an id (typically different models) one was silently dropped, so its model's corrective feedback was mis-routed to the surviving model (records route per-model via by_model[rec.model_origin] at _feedback.py:361). The dropped model never heard the refutation and kept re-asserting the finding — a direct churn / non-convergence driver. Fix: collision-SAFE accumulation. `findings_by_id` retains a per-id finding list; feedback records are keyed by (finding_id, model_origin) via a `_record_for` helper; all four record-building blocks (refutations, admissibility, near-dups, R_k) iterate the per-id findings so every model that emitted a colliding id gets its own correctly-routed record. R_k block preserves validator model_id specificity. Blast radius FFAFP'd: build_feedback_records is the sole consumer (only caller reference_runner_v2.py:2345); all 5 .get(fid) sites replaced. Detector retained as post-mortem accounting only. Stale test (test_detector_called_at_comprehension_site) pinned the removed buggy comprehension — updated to pin the fix instead (detector still called; comprehension gone; collision-safe structures present), plus 2 new behavioural tests (cross-model collision -> record per model; no-collision path unchanged) and corrected module docstring. ruff clean; 106 tests pass across all _feedback consumers (test_feedback_channel 40/40, collision detector, bugzilla loop, launch, sv). title: exp40 plan-B: in-round re-ask (dispatch-phase, bounded, idempotent)
verbatim: exp40 plan-B: in-round re-ask (dispatch-phase, bounded, idempotent) Supersedes the 1e next-round-only deferral per founder directive (the active error-correction originally envisaged). When a model returns finding-declaration content that fails to parse (>= min_markers raw _FINDING_DECL_RE markers AND 0 parsed findings AND a real response, not a __DISPATCH_FAILED__ sentinel), the runner re-dispatches ONCE to that model in the dispatch phase with a STRUCTURE_VIOLATION corrective prompt (re-emit the SAME analysis in canonical format), before reconciliation. - Hooked only on the primary dispatch path of _dispatch_single_model (NOT the reconciliation close path — that was the loop/ordering risk flagged in the plan; NOT the degraded multiturn/exception paths). - Bounded: exactly one extra dispatch, no loop. Idempotent: retry output REPLACES the round's output for that model on recovery (single save_output, inround_reask flag in metadata); on failure the original is returned unchanged (no worse; 1e remains next-round fallback). - Config: RunnerConfig.inround_reask_enabled=True (default-on per founder),inround_reask_min_markers=2; module mirror _INROUND_REASK set at experiment start (mirrors _merge_arb_ctx pattern, avoids re-threading the dispatch chain); launcher passthrough added in both launch_exp40.py and launcher_core.py. - 8 isolation unit tests (full trigger matrix, bounded single retry, recovery-replaces-output, still-malformed-keeps-original, retry-exception-safe, corrective-prompt structure). title: exp40 plan-C: apply verified fixes back to a per-run working copy (the structural cure)
verbatim: exp40 plan-C: apply verified fixes back to a per-run working copy (the structural cure) The decay model's precondition for termination is that the error space actually exhausts. It never did because verified fixes were only ever applied in a throwaway sandbox; the panel re-reviewed the same defects every round (root cause confirmed in plan-E). This wires the cure. - _apply_back_setup: at experiment start, if apply_fixes_back_enabled, create logs_dir/working/<target> seeded from apply_fixes_back_seed (e.g. the plan-E cleaned baseline) or the pristine target; all rounds read the working copy. The repo file is NEVER written; the pristine path is recorded for provenance. - _apply_back_promote (called loop-top, idempotent, for the prior round): for each not-yet-applied CLOSED finding with a parseable SEARCH/REPLACE fix, apply cumulatively and gate on the FULL canonical suite (_apply_back_gate: sandbox repo overlay + cfg.test_cmd). Green -> committed to the working copy + full_code rebuilt so the next round reviews the repaired artefact. Red -> finding stays CLOSED in the registry but the fix is NOT applied (the C0001 lesson from plan-E baked into the design: the run-time S_k score tolerates regressions; promotion must not). Rejections logged. - Loop-top hook only (avoids the many mid-body exit paths). Config: apply_fixes_back_enabled=False (default — changes experiment semantics from static-stimulus to iterative repair-and-reconverge, an intended/recorded change), apply_fixes_back_seed="". Launcher passthrough added (launch_exp40 + launcher_core). - 5 unit tests (setup disabled/enabled/seeded; promote green/reject-regressing/idempotent; noop-disabled). Regression sweep 95 pass. verbatim: exp40: advisory definitional confer — outcome recorded (no code change) 5-model advisory confer (purely factual brief, no embedded position, dissent explicitly permitted; gemini/codex/cc2/chatgpt/deepseek). All returned cleanly (cc2 after one timeout retry). Full unedited logs + script committed. Q1 unanimous 5/5: total exhaustion NOT attainable (open all-severity surface vs Duane closed-pool assumption; empirical γ-all 0.10-0.23; ~1-month/1-M1 bound). Independently confirms the founder's view. Q2 NOT unanimous — recorded, not collapsed: X critical/structural exhaustion (Gemini, CC2); X-"not as implemented" bridging Z (Codex); Z pre-registered functional benchmark (ChatGPT, DeepSeek). Unanimous core beneath the split: drop total-exhaustion; the bare 0.7 severity boundary is the top vulnerability (all 5) -> replace with a pre-registered consequence-based critical/structural definition; compute on the SETTLED registry not live; pre-registered + scoped + hostile-reproducible; apply-fixes-back ON; loose OR gate -> stricter conjunction. Synthesis (soundest-argument, P-passed incl. working-model bias-check; the dissent survives and is the load-bearing signal): the defensible "done" is the CONJUNCTION, not X-or-Z — pre-registered consequence-based critical/structural definition + settled accounting + critical-exhaustion stability AND the artefact passes a frozen pre-registered held-out STEM benchmark with mechanical pass/fail; DeepSeek's test-impact criterion (a finding is critical iff fixing it changes a ground-truth test output) is the sharpest resolution of the F6/0.7 vulnerability. Disclosure: the cc2 panelist mis-framed itself as CC1 (weight 4+1, not a clean 5). Concrete 1-month plan recorded (Wk1 freeze scope + pre-registered rubric + settled-only estimator fix + frozen benchmark; Wk2-3 bounded PoC apply-back-on conjunction-gated; Wk3-4 robustness + adversarial pass + audit bundle; defer lambda_ext, full BR2, total-exhaustion). Bottom line: internal convergence to date does NOT by itself prove the fixed goal; a defensible PoC must show correct answers on pre-registered untuned STEM problems. title: exp40 gate-hardening: F6 pre-reg + F4 settled-registry + conjunction gate
verbatim: exp40 gate-hardening: F6 pre-reg + F4 settled-registry + conjunction gate Founder-directed; implements the unanimous core of the 2026-05-17 γ-hardening confer and 2026-05-18 definitional confer, default-OFF so existing experiments keep the legacy γ-alt OR gate unchanged. F6 — pre-registration committed BEFORE any hardened run: bench/exp40_baseline/CRITICAL_DEFINITION_PREREG_2026-05-18.md defines critical/structural by CONSEQUENCE (wrong result / hard-constraint violation / verification-integrity corruption / silent evidence loss / unreproducibility), frozen, hostile-reviewer-diffable. Code: CRITICAL_SEVERITY_THRESHOLD named constant documents the numeric 0.7 as the operational proxy for that rubric (scattered legacy 0.7 literals flagged as a tracked migration item, not silently rewritten). F4 — _settled_novelty_series: per-round novelty recomputed from the SETTLED post-reconciliation registry (open_since_round==r AND status not in MERGED/DUPLICATE/UNCONFIRMED/REFUTED), the production-faithful method that resolves the 0.305-live vs 0.231-settled flip. Live γ is no longer the gate input. Conjunction gate — _check_hardened_convergence: converged iff (γ_critical ≥ θ AND sustained over gamma_crit_sustain_rounds AND leave-one-round-out robust within gamma_crit_loo_tol) AND (N consecutive settled zero-novel-critical rounds). All-novelty γ computed and logged as a DIAGNOSTIC only — never gates. Sparsity fallback: if cumulative critical < gamma_crit_min_cumulative the slope is unreliable so γ_crit is reported-not-gated and closure rests on the robust count-based zero-novel-critical criterion alone (CC2's confer point). Knife-edge single-round crossings are rejected by the sustained check. RunnerConfig: hardened_gate_enabled=False (default), +sustain_rounds (2), +min_cumulative (8), +loo_tol (0.05); launcher passthrough added (launch_exp40 + launcher_core). Round-loop wired: hardened path bypasses legacy γ-alt entirely when enabled, logs full telemetry. 8 hardened-gate unit tests (settled-series split, conjunction, sparsity fallback both ways, γ_all-diagnostic-never-gates, knife-edge rejection, too-early). Regression sweep 85 pass (legacy γ-alt path unchanged + all adjacent consumers). Runner AST+compile clean; zero new ruff errors (53==53 pre-existing). title: exp40 plan-D faithful decomposition: Units B + C slices + hardened configs
verbatim: exp40 plan-D faithful decomposition: Units B + C slices + hardened configs AST dependency analysis of the plan-E cleaned _feedback.py baseline (661 lines, 7 top-level defs) establishes the FAITHFUL decomposition is 3 natural units, not 7 atomic fragments: Unit A parse_admissibility_block (+ ADMISSIBILITY_GATES) — self- contained leaf (refs []). Slice/test exist; prior plan-F runs were un-hardened (FALSIFIED f1a5127). New hardened config. Unit B detect_finding_id_collisions (+ accumulator) — self-contained leaf (refs []). New slice + focused test + hardened config. Unit C FindingFeedback + build_feedback_records + build_feedback_sections + _render_single_record + _rebuild_section — one coupled cluster (all 5 reference the dataclass; cannot split without stubbing it + fabricating callers). New slice + focused test + hardened config; imports the Unit B leaf (single source of truth, mirrors the real module). Forcing _render_single_record / _rebuild_section into standalone units would manufacture a convergence surface that is not a property of the real module — a decomposition artefact, the same family of measurement distortion the F6/F4 hardening prevents, inverted. "every unit, if any" cedes the count to the structure: 2 outstanding + 1 A re-run. Unit C seed deliberately preserves the old last-wins comprehension ({f.finding_id: f for f in findings}) — a genuine silent-evidence-loss defect (F6 critical/structural clause 4). The collision-safe fix landed only in live bench/dm/_feedback.py; the cleaned-baseline slice does not carry it, so it is a legitimate convergence target the apply-back Ouroboros can fold. Verified the focused-test gate is collision- agnostic (no baseline test asserts last-wins-on-collision) so the gate is NOT cooked against the correct fix. All 3 configs: hardened_gate_enabled=true with the FROZEN pre- registered defaults (theta=0.30, W=3, sustain=2, min_cum=8, loo=0.05), identical across units — not per-unit tuned. No instrumentation hack (earliest=3, not the falsified plan-F 20; W=3, not 999). apply-fixes- back + in-round re-ask + G7 on (validated non-cooking fixes). Verification: 56 focused+hardened tests pass; 58 adjacent regression (live feedback channel + collision detector + launcher) pass; ruff clean; launch_exp40.py wires all 4 hardened keys (no silent legacy fallback); all 3 configs dry-run-validate end-to-end. title: exp40 Unit B->C seam: 3 runner-class verification-integrity fixes
verbatim: exp40 Unit B->C seam: 3 runner-class verification-integrity fixes Surfaced live during Unit B's hardened-gate run (which CONVERGED: HARDENED_CONVERGED at R3, sparsity fallback, authoritative report.json). All three are F6 clause-3 (verification-integrity) defects — they misreport/мask the verdict but do NOT corrupt the measurement (Unit B's report.json verdict is correct; recovery path _multiturn_fallback unchanged). Fixed at the inter-unit seam, not mid-run, so no within-run runner-version split (the non-cooking choice the cy contract serves). 1. CircuitBreakerTripped.__reduce__ (experiment_11_orchestrator.py). ROOT CAUSE: custom __init__(condition,model,phase,detail) calls super().__init__(<one formatted string>), so self.args==(str,). Default Exception pickling reconstructs via cls(*self.args) -> 1-arg __init__ -> "TypeError: missing 2 required positional arguments: 'model' and 'phase'". runner_core.dispatch_to_model runs each model in a multiprocessing.Process and `raise payload`s the worker's pickled exception across an mp.Queue, so EVERY orchestrator-raised CircuitBreakerTripped arrived as a TypeError, was swallowed by the broad except, and the circuit breaker was silently inoperative arc-wide (masked since the runner's inception). __reduce__ now reconstructs from the 4 original args. P-passed: exact-error reproduction + real multiprocessing.Queue round-trip. New test file test_circuitbreaker_pickle_safety.py (5 tests). 2. launch_exp40.py converged-detection. The per-round result dicts carry no `converged` flag (always None); the authoritative signal is top-level result["converged_at"]/["convergence_reason"] (runner ~5602/5609). The old any(r.get("converged")...) check misreported Unit B's HARDENED_CONVERGED as "ended without convergence" + exit 1. Now reads converged_at and prints the runner's verbatim verdict. 3. reference_runner_v2.py brain.state propagation (same root as #2). The hardened/gamma-alt gate set only the result dict, never brain.state.converged, so insect_brain.signal_complete() wrote completion_signal.json status=INCOMPLETE for a converged run (post-mortem tooling reads this). Now propagates at both burst and non-burst convergence breaks, `converged`-guarded so STALL/CHURN terminal stops keep their own status. Verification: AST OK x3; orchestrator imports; 18 tests pass (5 new pickle-safety incl. real mp.Queue + 6 launcher + 8 hardened- gate suite, 0 fail); zero NEW ruff findings (delta=0 per file vs HEAD; pre-existing legacy lint unchanged). title: exp40 hardened-gate campaign: synthesis + paired notes (3-unit complete)
verbatim: exp40 hardened-gate campaign: synthesis + paired notes (3-unit complete) The 3-unit faithful-decomposition campaign is complete. Authoritative per-unit report.json verdicts under the hardened gate: Unit B detect_finding_id_collisions HARDENED_CONVERGED at R3 (sparsity fallback, cum_critical=4<8, γ_crit reported-not-gated, 3 consecutive settled zero-novel-critical; 4 apply-back fixes) Unit A parse_admissibility_block NOT converged (12 rounds) (hardened re-run; full mode cum_critical→18; loo_min flat 0.0 across R3–R11; 7 apply-back; supersedes prior un-hardened/ falsified plan-F runs) Unit C FindingFeedback cluster NOT converged (12 rounds) (1st run outage-terminated R5 = infrastructure not verdict; clean re-run full mode cum_critical 14–15, loo_min 0→0.20 never 0.25; 8 apply-back) Central result: the OR→conjunction hardening is empirically anti- cooking. A legacy γ-alt OR gate would have converged all 3 units (γ_crit ~0.41–0.60 throughout, well above θ=0.30; Unit C's zero-crit arm fired at R8/R9). The hardened conjunction converged ONLY the genuinely-exhaustible Unit B (via the pre-registered sparsity path, degenerate γ_crit explicitly reported-not-gated) and refused A and C where γ_crit decay is not leave-one-round-out robust. Unit C provides direct empirical vindication: the gate withheld at R8/R9 where the OR converges; R10 then produced a NEW critical finding, refuting the OR-gate "convergence". The conjunction's refusal was vindicated by subsequent data on the one head-to-head case. Process integrity: 3 runner-class verification-integrity defects found live, root-caused, P-passed, fixed at the inter-unit seam (5fe9101), twice live-validated; 1 external network outage handled by clean re-run from archive (no mid-outage resume); ~5 degraded-DeepSeek finite-recovery events (patient-wait, no false-freeze); 19 full-suite- gated apply-back fix promotions folded. No measurement corrupted; all report.json verdicts hostile-reviewer-reproducible. Paired notes (standard v1.2): technical + plain-English in experimental_notes/; TTS at ~/Desktop/CDSFL_tts/. Operational tracker (Desktop canonical + repo mirror) updated: campaign COMPLETE, resume pointer = Exp 41 recommendation PROCEED. Non-blocking follow-ups flagged (legacy 0.7 literals; completion_signal labelling; launcher wall-clock string; decomposed-dispatch heartbeat) — none corrupts a measurement; Exp-41-or-later hygiene. title: remove reconstruction bypasses + route DeepSeek direct (founder-directed)
verbatim: remove reconstruction bypasses + route DeepSeek direct (founder-directed) Background. Across prior sessions, three autonomous "fixes" were added to handle empty model responses by salvage rather than by engaging the established ITC retry/restart-fresh protocol (feedback_no_benching.md). Each silently bypassed ITC and FailureHandler — the very infrastructure built to handle empty responses — by substituting intermediate model output (chain-of-thought or per-chunk analyses) for the model's actual answer. The founder rejected this approach: reasoning traces are often weakly coupled to conclusions (partly performative, unfaithful to the answer-generating computation), so substituting them is methodologically unsound; equally, silent salvage bypassed the explicit "no model misses a round" protocol the project established for exactly this failure class. This commit removes all three bypasses and reroutes DeepSeek to the confer-proven direct API path. No new logic; just unblocks the infrastructure that was already wired but starved of the real signal. REMOVED bypasses (decomposed_dispatch.py): 1. _extract_message_text reasoning_content / reasoning fallback (prior: substituted message.reasoning_content for empty content). Now content-only; empty returns "" and propagates to the runner. 2. _decomposed_openrouter synthesis chunk-analyses reconstruction (35c44b6 / 15 May 2026: concatenated Phase-1 chunk analyses when Phase-2 synthesis returned empty). Removed. 3. _decomposed_deepseek synthesis chunk-analyses reconstruction (same pattern, DeepSeek path). Removed. Also removed the now-dead Phase-1 "recovered N chars from reasoning trace" log lines. PRESERVED past good work (founder rule: don't undo without checking): - _PHASE1_MAX_TOKENS=8192 cap — structurally useful for reasoning models, retained. - _multiturn_fallback structural chunking — past good work for over-budget prompts, untouched. - decomposed_dispatch Phase-1/Phase-2 architecture, retained. - call_deepseek reasoning_content read for DIAGNOSTIC LOGGING (not response substitution) + max_tokens-halving retry — already ITC-aligned, untouched. - ITC protocol (runner_v2 lines 1618-1900+) — verified fully wired (TRANSIENT_FAILURE/CAPABILITY_MISMATCH/DEGRADATION → restart_fresh / change_focus); only blocked by the now-removed bypass. - FailureHandler (dm/_failure_handler.py) — verified wired via DynamicManager.process_round at bench/dm/_manager.py:307+ (priority-1 EMPTY detection → RETRY/EXCLUDE action); only blocked by the now-removed bypass. ROUTING change (experiment_11_orchestrator.py): DeepSeek ModelConfig: api="openrouter" + model_id="deepseek/ deepseek-v4-pro" + max_tokens=16384 → api="deepseek" + model_id="deepseek-v4-pro" + max_tokens=32768 Rationale: the well-instrumented direct path (call_deepseek with reasoning-budget mitigation) existed but was dead code under the OpenRouter slug routing. The confers already route DeepSeek to direct and work; smoke test confirms post-change (213 chars content + 636 chars reasoning, 8.9s). Cheaper than OpenRouter for DeepSeek. TESTS (bench/tests/): - test_decomposed_reasoning_fallback.py: rewritten. Previously pinned the bypass as a requirement (test_empty_content_falls_back_to_ reasoning_content). Now pins content-only behaviour + source-truth absence of the reasoning_content fallback. - test_decomposed_dispatch_fallback.py: rewritten. Previously asserted "result_text is reconstructed from the chunks" when synthesis empty. Now asserts empty synthesis returns empty result.text (no reconstruction) + source-truth absence of the reconstruction markers. - 18/18 new pass; 36/36 in adjacent suites (circuit-breaker pickle, launcher, hardened gate) pass; ruff delta=0 per modified file vs HEAD; smoke test passes. NET BEHAVIOURAL CHANGE: empty model responses now propagate honestly to the runner, where they engage: - ITC classification → restart_fresh / change_focus adaptation - FailureHandler EMPTY detection → RETRY (1st occurrence) / EXCLUDE (repeated) - HIL flag for persistent under-performers This is the founder's established "no model misses a round" protocol working as designed — previously short-circuited by the salvage substitutions, now restored. title: primary/secondary route fallback architecture: every model, no benching
verbatim: primary/secondary route fallback architecture: every model, no benching Founder-directed (2026-05-22). Combined with commit 86470a5 (bypass removal), this completes the empty-response handling redesign without violating the established "no model misses a round" protocol (feedback_no_benching.md). The previous FailureHandler policy escalated repeated EMPTY events to RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE — functionally benching the model from subsequent rounds. That contradicted the protocol the project was built on. The corrected architecture: every model carries a secondary route used as a one-shot in-round fallback; if both primary and secondary fail for a given turn, the event is HIL-flagged but the model is NEVER excluded from later rounds. ARCHITECTURE ModelConfig (orchestrator) — new optional fields: secondary_api: str | None — fallback route (e.g. "google", "codex_exec", "openrouter") secondary_model_id: str | None — fallback model id (route-specific) Five-model panel routes (load_default_config): CC2 primary=claude_cli/opus secondary=openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.7 Codex primary=openrouter/openai/gpt-5.5 secondary=codex_exec/gpt-5.5 (codex CLI) ChatGPT primary=openrouter/openai/gpt-5.5 secondary=codex_exec/gpt-5.5 (codex CLI; same GPT-5.5 backend, one subscription) Gemini primary=openrouter/google/gemini... secondary=google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview (Google SDK direct) DeepSeek primary=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro secondary=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro dispatch() — new `use_secondary: bool = False` parameter. When True, dataclasses.replace promotes secondary fields to primary; routes via the secondary api. Raises RuntimeError if no secondary configured. Primary extra_body (e.g. reasoning.effort) does NOT carry over to the secondary (route-specific). In-round fallback in _dispatch_single_model (runner v2): primary direct dispatch → on empty/raise → decomposed dispatch → on empty/None → SECONDARY ROUTE → on empty/raise → HIL flag + return failure marker; model NOT excluded. The model never misses a round per protocol — either route succeeded, or both failed (genuine "this turn this model contributed nothing" event, recorded for HIL review at end of run). HIL accumulators (runner module state, cleared at experiment start): _secondary_route_usage — per-turn successful secondary dispatch _persistent_empty_flags — per-turn both-routes-failed event Both surfaced in result.json for end-of-run review. FailureHandler.get_recovery EMPTY policy: Before: RETRY (1st) / EXCLUDE (repeated) — repeated benched the model After: RETRY (always) — model keeps participating; in-round secondary handles per-turn response; persistent-empty signal via _persistent_empty_flags EXCLUDE remains for TIMEOUT, MALFORMED, FORMAT, UNDERPERFORM (different failure classes; not in scope of the founder's no-benching rule for the empty-response case specifically). VERIFIED LIVE (smoke test, all 5 models via use_secondary=True): CC2 → 15 chars, 2.6s ("OK from Claude.") Codex → 13 chars, 22.5s ("OK from Codex") ChatGPT → 13 chars, 12.6s ("OK from GPT-5") Gemini → 14 chars, 8.8s ("OK from Gemini") DeepSeek → 17 chars, 6.0s ("OK from Assistant") VERIFIED TESTS: 17 new secondary-route tests pass; 53 adjacent (decomposed-fallback + circuit-breaker pickle + launcher + hardened gate) pass; 26 FailureHandler tests pass (including 2 updated to pin no-EXCLUDE-for-EMPTY). ruff delta=0 on all modified existing files. WHAT THIS PRESERVES (past good work, not touched): - ITC protocol + classification (runner v2 lines 1618+) — already wired and functional now that the bypass is removed. - FailureHandler EXCLUDE for non-EMPTY failures — unchanged. - _multiturn_fallback structural chunking — unchanged. - decomposed_dispatch Phase-1/Phase-2 architecture — unchanged. - call_deepseek diagnostic reasoning_content reads — unchanged. - _PHASE1_MAX_TOKENS=8192 cap — unchanged. - All 5 existing call_* wrappers (call_openrouter, call_claude_cli, call_codex, call_gemini, call_deepseek) — unchanged. The result: empty responses now route through three-tier in-round recovery (primary direct → decomposed → secondary), and at no point does any model "miss a round" via EXCLUDE. Persistent-empty events that survive all three tiers are surfaced to HIL via the per-run accumulators, not by silently benching the model. title: exp41 setup: static target + compelled convergence + Exp 40 fix harvest
verbatim: exp41 setup: static target + compelled convergence + Exp 40 fix harvest Founder-directed 2026-05-22. Completes the methodology corrections of the past week and stages Experiment 41 to launch. Per founder direction: "we go back to a static test article for each experiment... we will use the new compelled convergence framing going forward... we go directly to 41... we fold them back in." CHANGES 1. EXP 40 FIX HARVEST (bench/dm/_feedback.py) - bench/exp40_fix_harvest.py: one-shot tool that loads all proposed_fix SEARCH/REPLACE blocks from CLOSED registry entries across the 4 Exp 40 run reports (57 raw → 54 unique), and cumulatively folds them into bench/dm/_feedback.py with a full-suite sandbox gate per fix (test_feedback_channel + test_finding_id_collision_detector). - Result: 15/54 fixes accepted, 39 rejected (search_not_found_in_live — slices had diverged). +854 chars to live module. Final full-surface gate green. Spans severity 0.20-1.00 across all 4 runs. Each fix has provenance recorded (canonical_id + run). - The harvest tool is archival — runs once, not part of the runner. 2. STATIC TARGET MIGRATION - bench/exp40_configs/40_slice_{admissibility,collision,records} _hardened.json: apply_fixes_back_enabled flipped True → False on all three. The apply-back code itself stays in the runner; the re-architecture is that fixes fold post-experiment (via the harvest tool above), never during a run. - Rationale per founder (2026-05-22): "All our subsequent research however appears to strongly indicate that true convergence under [apply-back-during-review] conditions is functionally impossible. So we go back to the same model we have used from the outset where we put each individual test article up for review to the panel in each experiment, and then fold any fixes the models recommend back into that test article when the experiment ends and/or (preferably) when convergence has been reached." 3. COMPELLED CONVERGENCE DIRECTIVE - bench/directives/universal/cdsfl_core_formal.md: new §10 "Sufficiency Assessment and Convergence Declaration". Formalises the per-round task: assess whether the artefact correctly performs its specified function and report only material defects; declare convergence with reasoning when §6 termination criteria are met (all hard assumptions tested + sound; no residual finding meets real_world_threshold; no novel findings this round). Declaration is evidenced + refutable by next round + by independent schema checks (§7); a declaration motivated by instruction-satisfaction rather than evidence is itself a §1 HARD-class violation. - "Material" enumerated as 5 categories matching the F6 pre-registration: wrong result / hard-constraint violation / verification-integrity corruption / silent evidence loss / unreproducibility. Marginal observations (style/naming/ micro-optimisation) MUST NOT be emitted as material findings. - Sent to every model as part of the CDSFL system prompt automatically (no per-experiment config needed). - Classification summary updated. 4. EXP 41 LAUNCHER + CONFIG - bench/launch_exp41.py: clean implementation using bench/launcher_core.py (the shared infrastructure that resolves the three latent bugs launch_exp40.py originally shipped with). Supports --config, --dry-run, --resume. - bench/exp41_configs/41_convergence.json: target = bench/dm/ _convergence.py (437 lines, ConvergenceDetector bounded-math module — the operational tracker's Exp 41 "Mathematics calibration target"). All methodology corrections applied: apply_fixes_back_enabled=false (static), hardened_gate_enabled= true, frozen pre-registered defaults, secondary route fallback for every model (via ModelConfig), test_cmd = TestConvergenceDetector (10 existing tests). Compelled convergence active via §10 in system prompt automatically. - _directives_live flags section_17, section_18, section_10. 5. OPERATIONAL TRACKER - HEAD/RESUME POINTER updated to Exp 41 ready-to-launch state. VERIFICATION - 199 tests pass across the regression sweep (feedback + slices + decomposed-fallback + secondary route + circuit-breaker + launcher + hardened gate + convergence detector + failure handler). - bench/launch_exp41.py --dry-run validates config + launcher_core wiring + directive paths + test_cmd end-to-end. - ruff clean on all new + modified files (delta=0 vs HEAD). LAUNCH python3 bench/launch_exp41.py --config 41_convergence.json --dry-run python3 bench/launch_exp41.py --config 41_convergence.json Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: convergence-detector fixes + 5-model confer verification (founder-directed)

title: Step 3: first-principles runner gate (gamma diagnostic; genuine novelty)
verbatim: Step 3: first-principles runner gate (gamma diagnostic; genuine novelty) Return the runner's convergence to its pre-complication form, feeding it GENUINE (settled, verifier-filtered) novelty: - Recompute this round's novelty from the settled registry series (open_since_round==r, status not in MERGED/DUPLICATE/UNCONFIRMED/REFUTED) and overwrite the round's history entries BEFORE gamma, so: gamma is a genuine decay-curve diagnostic; the state gate's novel_this_round is genuine; and the gamma-alt count path (novel_critical_history) sees GENUINE novel criticals -> its "K consecutive zero-novel-critical" criterion can actually reach zero and converge. Previously these were raw pre-verifier counts inflated by over-production/noise. - Pre-registered run config 41c_first_principles_run.json: hardened gate OFF; gamma_alt_threshold=1.1 (gamma never triggers convergence); gamma_alt_consecutive_zero_crit=3; gamma stays in its telemetry-only window (max_rounds=12) so it never blocks the state gate either; target = the now-fixed bench/dm/_convergence.py; software verifier LIVE. delta=0 new ruff vs HEAD. Outstanding-criticals veto deferred (state gate open-critical condition + HIL-in-post cover it; avoiding another hard gate per the no-impossible-convergence constraint). title: fix: restore gamma as load-bearing convergence trigger (not demoted)
verbatim: fix: restore gamma as load-bearing convergence trigger (not demoted) gamma_alt_threshold 1.1 -> 0.30. Setting it to 1.1 had demoted gamma to "gates nothing" — contradicting the founder's standing ruling that gamma (the founding decay-curve concept) must remain a load-bearing convergence measure. Resolution (trigger-not-blocker): gamma now TRIGGERS convergence when the genuine decay curve tops out (gamma >= 0.30 via the gamma-alt path), fed GENUINE settled/verifier-filtered novelty (so it can actually reach the threshold on a sound module), while never BLOCKING convergence (telemetry-only for the state gate) — so a low gamma cannot recreate the "convergence impossible" failure. The zero-novel-critical count remains the complementary measure covering gamma's OLS slope-lag. verbatim: Exp 42 readiness: verifier code-path guard (root-cause fix) + convergence redesign + chips + doc correction Verifier (immune_agents.py typed_llm_classifier): code-path guard. In the software domain the LLM classifier may no longer eject a regex-identified code claim (code_behavioral/code_structural) onto a non-code verifier. Root cause of exp41c C0007/C0015/C0017 sitting UNCONFIRMED: the LLM demoted code claims to logical -> z3 "cannot ground claim in source AST" -> UNCERTAIN -> CT cell starved ("CT v2: 0 verdicts") -> resolution fell to panel CONFIRM/CHALLENGE opinion-votes (a show of hands, violating "tools adjudicate, no model voting"). The guard keeps code claims on the CT (code-verifier) path; objective regex/citation evidence beats LLM opinion. Only blocks the harmful direction (code -> non-code); the LLM's intended math->code rescue still works. 4 regression tests. Convergence redesign (reference_runner_v2.py, from prior build): gamma REPORTED on both all-severity and genuine-critical series, never gates; convergence = state-gate clean (A4 unresolved-critical fail-safe) AND K zero-novel-critical rounds on the settled, verifier-filtered series. Directive reframed (diminishing returns; value != severity; specific-mechanism continuation guard). Chip 1 (reference_runner_v2.py): stall detector no longer terminates on gamma by default (stall_gamma_termination_enabled=False). Gamma reports, never triggers; a stuck run hits BUDGET_EXHAUSTED honestly rather than a gamma-driven STALL_CONVERGED. The corrected kappa_rate (novel-discovery decline) now correctly reads the old repeated synthetic findings as kappa_converged; this was a stale test, not a regression. title: Tool-access + falsifier smoke tests (design validated before integration)
verbatim: Tool-access + falsifier smoke tests (design validated before integration) Spike 1 (smoketest_toolcall): all 4 routes honor tool-calling and used a single execute_python tool (full STEM toolset behind it) correctly — gpt-5.5, gemini, DeepSeek-v4-pro (the unknown — RESOLVED, it supports tools), cc2-cli (native Bash). No model needs a last-resort non-tool path. Spike 2 (smoketest_falsifier): the core "tools decide" mechanism works end-to-end on a controlled known-bug target — model attaches a runnable falsifier, the RUNNER independently re-runs it to set the verdict (CONFIRMED/REFUTED), no vote. Key finding: DeepSeek attached a CORRECT falsifier but made 0 tool calls (reasoned the result) — proving the runner-re-run failsafe (b) is the actual truth-decider and model tool-use (a) is for self-correction; the verdict must come from the runner, never the model's claim. Validates the founder's (a)+(b)-with-caveats. Next: integrate the tool-call loop into dispatch + falsifier_code into the Finding schema + runner re-run replacing the CONFIRM/CHALLENGE vote (task #13), smoke-test on a real CDSFL target, then commit. title: execute_python on the decomposed dispatch path + tool-loop crap-out fix
verbatim: execute_python on the decomposed dispatch path + tool-loop crap-out fix cy monitoring of the first Exp 42 launch caught that the DECOMPOSED (multiturn) dispatch path — taken for large targets like the 60K composer — never received the execute_python tool, so on big targets models reasoned rather than ran their falsifiers (the (a)-half gap of (a)+(b)). Founder chose fix-first. Decomposition is kept fully intact (Exp 39 quality-collapse confound protection); only the FINAL SYNTHESIS turn (where findings/falsifiers are produced) gains the tool. - decomposed_dispatch.py: enable_tools threaded into decomposed_dispatch + the per-API impls. _decomposed_openrouter / _decomposed_deepseek run the synthesis turn through the shared _run_openai_tool_loop (new thin wrapper _openai_synthesis_with_tools); _decomposed_claude_cli adds --allowedTools Bash Read to the final --resume invocation only. Per-chunk delivery turns stay tool-less. Gated default-off => no tools kwarg / no --allowedTools => byte- identical. - reference_runner_v2.py: enable_tools threaded _dispatch_single_model decomposed branch -> _multiturn_fallback -> decomposed_dispatch. - experiment_11_orchestrator.py CRAP-OUT FIX (found verifying the above; the agent had dismissed it as model flakiness): _run_openai_tool_loop returned EMPTY text if a model requested tools on all max_iters iterations (e.g. looping on a bad import) — a model contributing zero findings for a round, exactly the "don't let models crap out" failure. On exhaustion it now forces ONE tool-less final call so the model returns its synthesis from what it gathered. Hardens BOTH dispatch paths (the decomposed wrapper delegates to this loop). Verification: 301 tests pass (decomposed fallback + new tool-loop-exhaustion + falsifier gate + dynamic management); CC1 re-ran the decomposed smoke test — model_called_tool=True on the decomposed path, default-off no-tool confirmed; ruff delta 0 on all three modules; imports clean. Falsifier-format adherence is model/run variant (the real directive is more forceful than the smoke prompt) — will be watched in the relaunch's round 0 along with the CC2/claude_cli tool path (not openrouter-smoke-tested). title: B-Cell v2: ground real numeric-constant claims; honest messaging for the rest
verbatim: B-Cell v2: ground real numeric-constant claims; honest messaging for the rest The B-Cell SMT verifier grounded ZERO claims on every run and logged the alarming 'Cannot ground claim in source AST' — because _build_smt2_from_claim extracted any word before an operator ('be' from 'should be <= 0.5'), which never matched a real source constant. Fix: - Match comparisons against KNOWN numeric source constants (case-insensitive, both 'CONST op N' and 'N op CONST' forms); skip non-constant tokens instead of emitting ungrounded abstract assertions. Real numeric-constant claims now ground and z3-verify (CONFIRMED for true, REJECTED for false — verified end-to-end on composer.DEFAULT_COHERENCE_BUDGET). - Replace the misleading 'Cannot ground' message: code-behavioral claims (the falsifier gate's domain, the majority) now report 'not a numeric/SMT-verifiable claim — deferred to falsifier gate / HIL'; a numeric claim whose constant is absent reports that distinctly. No more false-failure noise. Verified: grounding unit tests, 81 immune tests pass, end-to-end z3 verdicts, ruff delta 0. title: S_k: fix false no_blocks_for_target on path-less SEARCH/REPLACE blocks
verbatim: S_k: fix false no_blocks_for_target on path-less SEARCH/REPLACE blocks Models reviewing a single target often omit the file path on the SEARCH marker and put the first search line there ('<<<< SEARCH _HARD_BLOCK_MARKERS = ('). parse_search_replace_blocks grabbed that code as the file_path, so it never matched the target -> every such fix was REJECTED A=0.0 with 'no_blocks_for_target' AND the search text was corrupted (first line eaten). Verified on the Exp 42 confirm run: C0021-C0023 all hit this. Fix: - Validate the post-SEARCH token as a path (_looks_like_fix_path: no whitespace + has a separator or a source extension). If it is not a path, treat it as the first search line and leave file_path empty. - apply_fix_blocks defaults a path-less block to the single target; explicit paths still must match (full or basename). Result: C0001 (path-bearing) still applies cleanly; C0021-C0023 now match the target and are evaluated honestly (search_not_found = imperfect model reproduction — a real fix-quality signal, no longer a false layer rejection). Verified: re-parse/apply on the confirm run, ruff delta 0, 283 tests pass. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: Build severity calibration — over-production bounding (T6, gated default-off)
verbatim: Build severity calibration — over-production bounding (T6, gated default-off) The "severity calibration" gap was NEVER BUILT (per the 7-June ground-truth audit + resume pointer). This adds it as a gated, tested mechanism that bounds over-production WITHOUT discarding real findings. Mechanism (reference_runner_v2.py): a finding that the falsifier gate CONFIRMED as a REAL defect but that is explicitly flagged LATENT/conditional (it needs a trigger absent from the usage contract) has its EFFECTIVE severity lowered to just below CRITICAL_SEVERITY_THRESHOLD, recording severity_original + calibration_reason on the entry. It is then no longer a convergence-blocking critical, but stays in the registry — nothing is lost. Because every critical-counting channel reads entry["severity"] at call-time, the sweep (run after the falsifier gate, before the settled-novelty recompute) drops the finding from all counts with no per-channel change. Conservative criterion (_is_demotion_eligible): demote iff critical AND falsifier_verdict==CONFIRMED AND latent AND category not in {safety, core, core_functionality, security, data_loss}. An un-demonstrated or safety/core finding is NEVER demoted. Gated by RunnerConfig.severity_calibration_enabled (default False) => byte-identical when off (verified: 72 convergence/gate/falsifier tests pass unchanged). 17 new tests (test_severity_calibration.py): gate-off no-op, eligibility matrix, demote-retains-and-records, idempotent re-sweep, floor clamp, safety/core/ unproven never demoted, terminal skipped, end-to-end (demotion unblocks an A4-blocked two-sided gate). HONEST CAVEAT: inert in isolation — nothing currently sets entry["latent"]/ ["finding_category"]. This is the verified building block; live activation needs an upstream latent-tagger (a reconciliation step or severity-classifier cell), a separate gated piece. Fail-safe: absent the tag, no finding is ever demoted. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: ★ RETRACTION: the API keys were NEVER lost — the checker itself was the bug
verbatim: ★ RETRACTION: the API keys were NEVER lost — the checker itself was the bug Founder incredulity ("it seems incredulous if they really were deleted") prompted a direct masked read of .env: ALL original keys present in `export KEY=value` shell format (OPENAI/GOOGLE/GEMINI/GITHUB/GROQ/WOLFRAM/DEEPSEEK/OPENROUTER) plus SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR cleanly APPENDED on 9 June. 11 lines, 843 bytes, born 28 March, exactly one modification: the append. The 9 June write did NOT overwrite the file. Root cause of the false incident: the verification instruments. The grep pattern and check_model_keys.py matched only bare `KEY=` line starts, so every `export`-prefixed line was invisible — while python-dotenv (the runners' actual loader) parses `export` lines fine, which is why every live run worked. Verified: dotenv_values loads all 5 keys; corrected preflight = all PRESENT; live pings HTTP 200 on OpenRouter + DeepSeek (keys VALID, not merely present). D1 void. Exp 43 + the full pr panel were never key-blocked. Two successive false accounts now retracted (the "shell-exported keys" story, then the "overwrite destroyed keys" story) — the first an unverified inference, the second an unverified INSTRUMENT. Standing lesson recorded: a verification instrument must be validated against the real consumer it stands in for before its verdicts are trusted. Corrections swept: decision register (CORRECTION section), remediation-program log, RECOVERY.md, tracker (both copies), memory index + session file, .env.example, preflight parser fixed. verbatim: Ouroboros + self-improvement assessment (founder-ordered, pre-Exp-43) Two read-only audits (code + design docs), file:line-referenced. title: Fix 5 findings from the A2/A3 adversarial verification pass
verbatim: Fix 5 findings from the A2/A3 adversarial verification pass Isolated adversarial pass (14 agents, 4 lenses + refute-by-default verify) on the A2 ouroboros + A3 rename commits surfaced 5 confirmed findings; all fixed: MEDIUM (A3 regression, bears on Exp43=Exp42): - RunnerConfig.from_dict/from_json (the runner's OWN --config CLI) lacked the legacy-key alias — only launcher_core had it. So RunnerConfig.from_json(exp43_config).routing_enabled returned False (routing SILENTLY OFF) while the launcher path returned True. Launching Exp 43 via the runner CLI would have diverged from the Exp 42 landmark. FIX: mirror the take_up_slack_enabled -> routing_enabled alias in from_dict. Verified: both paths now agree (routing ON) for exp42 + exp43. Regression test added (test_routing_wiring.py). [My earlier 'verified' only exercised the launcher path — the pass caught the gap.] LOW (all in the shadow ouroboros code, dead in Exp 43 since its config has no _ouroboros block, but real defects in newly-authored code): - _download_and_extract re-raised despite its 'Never raises' docstring (_run_with_timeout re-raises worker exceptions; the call site was unguarded), which wiped a whole round's briefs instead of per-paper degradation. FIX: guard the call -> error field; wrap the _read_and_brief per-paper body so one paper's failure can't lose the round. - MAX_PDF_BYTES was bypassable when Content-Length is absent (r.content buffers the full body first). FIX: stream with iter_content + a running byte cap. - Test-adequacy: the real loop was network-only + one assertion passed vacuously. FIX: 3 new OFFLINE tests (monkeypatched shadow loop proving a real brief + provenance; never-raises regression; per-paper-isolation regression) + non-vacuous network assertion. Offline suite: 20 realwork + 23 routing/convergence/gate green; network: 2 green (real arXiv fetch/parse/brief still works after the streaming change). ruff clean. Shadow isolation + gamma untouched. title: Milestone merge: Exp 47-49, the control-run findings, and the instrument repairs of 29 July - 13 August.
verbatim: Milestone merge: Exp 47-49, the control-run findings, and the instrument repairs of 29 July - 13 August. SQUASHED DELIBERATELY, and the reason is a standing founder constraint: no answer keys move to main. All five keys (exp48 chemistry, exp49 engineering, exp50 physics, exp51 biology, exp52 factorial) were added on exp39-experimental and exist ONLY in that branch's history — they are absent from both current trees. A normal merge would have carried those commits into main's ancestry permanently and foreclosed ever removing the exposure by retiring the branch. A squash carries the tree and no history, so main receives none of them. Verified before commit: zero answer-key paths staged, zero exam-article paths staged, resulting tree byte-identical to exp39-experimental, README.md unchanged. The granular 106-commit history is preserved on exp39-experimental, which is retained. WHAT THIS PROMOTES (main was last updated 28 July, at Exp 46): Exp 47 divergence, Exp 48 chemistry exam, Exp 49 engineering exam — all converged and reported. Exp 53 zero-plant control: two runs, both interrupted, and the finding that matters is that the control was never clean. It contains two real unplanted defects in working code (TokenBucket.allow admits a negative cost and mints tokens above capacity; HashRing.locate uses bisect_right and mis-routes an exact match). Both were found correctly by the panel and verified against source. The confirmed criticals are TRUE POSITIVES. The instrument is mis-specified, not the audit negligent: its ground truth is claim-scoped while the review is artefact-scoped, so a defect no claim describes is unscoreable by construction. INSTRUMENT REPAIRS. The falsifier extractor terminated on the first triple-backtick anywhere in a block, so a falsifier that opens a markdown target and parses its listings truncated ITSELF — five cut to exactly 134 characters in the 1 August run. The selection pressure ran the wrong way: careful falsifiers were destroyed, lazy inline-copy ones survived, and every remaining target is markdown. Fixed. Re-extraction from archived raw responses recovers 42 compiling falsifiers against 26 stored of which 12 do not run, so Exp 53 can be re-scored from disk rather than re-run. The verdict reader no longer classifies instrument breakage by searching for one of three words in an error message. The discrimination control is wired but NOT armed, behind two flags that both default off, because whether it may block a finding from closing is an open founder decision. NOTE STANDARD v1.4. The reader model was the root error: v1.2 aimed the plain-English register at 'an educated journalist' when the reader is the project's designer, who does not read code. Rules 19-23 added. Suite 3484 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed offline. Quality sweep: 8 checks, 0 issues, broken references 137 -> 0. verbatim: Repository navigability: a front door, an archive plan, and a stop on log growth. THE PROBLEM, MEASURED. External models reported they could not read this repository. The repository is and was public: HTTP 200 anonymously, visibility public, not archived, raw file fetches returning 200 on every branch. This stops accumulation; it untracks nothing. Verified: zero deletions staged. title: sv: guard against branch drift — main is the only branch that gets updated.
verbatim: sv: guard against branch drift — main is the only branch that gets updated. The founder ruled weeks ago that main would be the working branch. A milestone merge to main was made on 28 July 2026 and work then continued on exp39-experimental from 19:11 that same evening, for a further 107 commits over 18 days. For that fortnight the public repository presented a project 16 days stale while the real work sat on a branch no external reader would think to open. Nothing was lost. Verified exhaustively on 15 August rather than by sampling: of 7,628 paths that ever existed in exp39-experimental's history, every one is either in main's current tree or recoverable from main's own history, except twelve. Eleven of those twelve are the exam articles and answer keys. The twelfth, Overnight_Work_Completed_Plain_English_2026-08-02.md, was a filename carrying the wrong date, renamed 43 seconds after creation by the commit 'Timestamps: correct four fabricated 2026-08-02 stamps to the real clock time'; the corrected file is on main. The cause was mechanical, not inattention. _commit_and_push pushes to whatever branch is checked out and had no concept of main, so the ruling survived exactly as long as someone remembered it. This is the same shape as the note standard decaying between v1.2 and v1.4: an agreement nobody wired into the tooling. The guard WARNS and never aborts. A deliberate experimental branch is legitimate; drifting onto one by accident is not, and the difference is whether anyone noticed. Silent on main, verified. title: Test the branch-drift guard, and record why the answer keys were nearly destroyed.
verbatim: Test the branch-drift guard, and record why the answer keys were nearly destroyed. TESTS. Eight tests pin the sv branch guard: that it exists, that it asks git for the branch rather than assuming, that it warns and never aborts, that it cannot itself break a save, that it names the remedy, and that its condition is equality against main rather than a looser pattern. The last matters: a test asking 'does the branch name contain experimental' would have let a branch called some-feature drift silently, which is the same failure in different clothes. THE NEAR MISS, recorded because the reasoning was wrong and the founder caught it. This assistant stated that deleting exp39-experimental would 'lose the exam articles and the answer keys, and nothing else whatsoever', and framed that as the desirable outcome. The founder asked why we would not simply keep the articles and secure the keys. Investigating that question found: - All six exam articles were already safe in the off-repo store, byte counts matching the published manifest. - ZERO answer keys existed anywhere outside exp39-experimental's git history. Not on disk, not in the store, not in either branch's current tree. Deleting the branch would therefore have permanently destroyed the scoring keys for exp50 physics, exp51 biology and the exp52 factorial capstone — three experiments that have not yet run. Without a key an exam article is unscoreable: the panel's findings cannot be matched against the planted defects, which is the same unscoreable condition diagnosed on the zero-plant control. All five keys are now recovered from history into the off-repo store, validated as JSON, and set to owner-read-only. exp52_factorial: 48 claims, 12 planted false, each carrying truth, why and verify_tool. Verified: every unrun experiment now has both its article and its key outside git entirely. One process note. The first extraction attempt wrote five 0-byte files, because it resolved each key at the commit that DELETED it. Empty files that look like keys are worse than absent ones. Caught by checking sizes rather than exit codes, and redone against the pre-deletion commit. title: CORRECTION to bdadcfe: the answer keys were never at risk, and I briefly unsealed them.
verbatim: CORRECTION to bdadcfe: the answer keys were never at risk, and I briefly unsealed them. RETRACTED. Commit bdadcfe states "ZERO answer keys existed anywhere outside exp39-experimental's git history. Not on disk, not in the store, not in either branch's current tree." That is FALSE and the reasoning behind it was wrong. The keys were already secured, correctly, by bench/vault_keys.sh -- committed in f01cf03, "Answer-key exposure CLOSED". They live in an AES-256 sealed archive of 174,112 bytes whose passphrase is deliberately not held on this machine. The reason no plaintext key was found on disk is that the vault system was working exactly as designed. The founder pointed to the script; the search that produced the false claim never looked for it. WORSE, AND THE PART THAT MATTERS. Acting on that false finding, this assistant extracted all five keys from git history and wrote them as plaintext into the off-repo store. The vault status check then reported UNVAULTED, listing five stray plaintext key files, and printed "A panel run must not start in this state." A working security control was broken by a repair aimed at a problem that did not exist. All five plaintext files have been deleted. Status re-verified: no plaintext key file on disk in any known or scanned location, sealed archive present and unchanged at 174,112 bytes. Net effect on the vault: none. Net effect during the window: the keys sat unencrypted on disk for the duration. WHAT REMAINS TRUE from bdadcfe: the eight tests pinning the sv branch guard, and the finding that all six exam articles sit in the off-repo store with byte counts matching the published manifest. Retracted is every claim about the keys being unprotected or needing recovery. WHAT THIS CHANGES about deleting exp39-experimental: nothing, but for a different reason than the one given. The branch can go because the vault holds the keys, not because they needed rescuing from it. METHOD NOTE. The search asked "where are the plaintext keys" and concluded from their absence that no keys existed. Absence of plaintext was the SUCCESS CONDITION of a control this project had already built and committed. Checking whether a control existed before drawing conclusions from its effect would have cost one command. title: Name the rule: "the similarity function", founder-named 2026-08-16.
verbatim: Name the rule: "the similarity function", founder-named 2026-08-16. The founder did not recognise his own criterion when it was described back to him, because this assistant had been calling it "the structured-numbers criterion" -- a coinage appearing nowhere in the project. Third instance in one conversation of the failure that note standard v1.4 Rule 13 exists to prevent, four days after writing that rule. The code had been calling the whole thing "the combined identity rule", which is a committee name nobody remembers. It is now the SIMILARITY FUNCTION, recorded in docs/GLOSSARY.md and at the head of the tier block in convergence_location.py, with the three tiers keeping their own names beneath it: location, signature_similarity, outcome_agreement. The glossary entry carries the measured figures, because a name without evidence drifts as easily as no name at all. Tier 2 covers 161 of 165 criticals (97.6%), separating same-defect pairs (median Jaccard 0.559, n=28) from different-defect pairs (median 0.000, n=290) at Mann-Whitney p = 1.9e-25. Tier 3 covers 57.0% and never once called a same-defect pair DIFFERENT in the whole sample. The rival tier built to a model panel's design scored Fisher p = 0.71 -- no association -- and was removed on 2026-08-12. A correction to how this was reported: the 57% figure is TIER 3's coverage and was quoted as though it described the whole rule, which understated it. The rule's reach is tier 2's 97.6%. title: Benchmark the similarity function against published work, and correct the Bletchley framing.
verbatim: Benchmark the similarity function against published work, and correct the Bletchley framing. Two rounds of external research, six strands, saved unedited (151 KB across three files) alongside a TTS note written under standard v1.4. THE RATINGS, from two strands rating independently: engineering design 7/10, artefact 6/10, honesty of reporting 8/10, application novelty 5/10, evidence strength as reported 3/10, method novelty 2/10, publishable today 2/10. Summary: competent internal engineering with a below-publication evaluation. WHY THE INTERNAL NUMBERS LOOK CLEAN. The problem here is easier than the published analogue. Two humans reporting one bug use the same words 10-15% of the time; this project's findings are written by models against the SAME document and copy hard tokens verbatim from it. That is near-duplicate detection over a shared substrate, a different and easier task. Direct measurement: identical duplicate-detection algorithms score 0.30-0.62 on human bug reports and 0.93-0.97 on structured machine output. On the dense input the LLM embedding is the WORST of four methods. THE BLETCHLEY QUESTION, checked against primary sources including declassified SRH-025 and a 1957 NSA Technical Journal article. The founder's premise holds and its lesson inverts. Two practices were being merged: recognising the operator (Morse "fist", later TINA) belonged to traffic analysis, was never part of the Enigma break, and was still described inside NSA twelve years later as "an effort to develop" in a paper titled A Last Resort. Exploiting operator HABIT (Herivel tip, cillies, stereotyped openings) is what broke Enigma, and it is not identification. What drove the Bombe was the crib: a predicted literal plaintext string, a CONTENT anchor rather than a style signature. Mapped here, style would identify which model wrote a finding -- already known -- and the crib is the hard token lifted from the shared document. The similarity function already implements the crib, which is the half that did the work. A STYLE TIER WOULD HURT, not merely fail to help. The signals are anti-correlated: two findings about the same defect written by different models are by construction maximally distant stylometrically. And peer-reviewed work across five languages puts the floor for stable attribution at 2,500-5,000 words, method-independent. A finding is a paragraph. TWO CORRECTIONS TO EARLIER REPORTING. The 57% figure is tier three's coverage and was quoted as the whole rule's; the rule's reach is tier two's 97.6%. And the design was defended on determinism grounds, which is not quite true, because the ground-truth labels come from a pinned embedding checkpoint. Auditability is the defensible claim. RECOMMENDATION: change nothing about the method; fix the evaluation. Highest-value single action is hand-labelling the excluded ambiguous pairs, double-annotated and adjudicated, then re-reporting as a three-way operating characteristic. PROPOSED only, no code, no labelling begun. UNRESOLVED: two strands disagree on how many pairs were excluded, 120 by arithmetic against 87 reported. Neither number is quoted as settled. title: Test Gemini's two duplicate-detection answers against the project. Nothing to adopt.
verbatim: Test Gemini's two duplicate-detection answers against the project. Nothing to adopt. Both answers checked with tools against project data rather than assessed by reading. That distinction is the finding: read on their own terms both are persuasive and correctly reasoned, and both would have justified building something unnecessary. FIRST ANSWER (MinHash / SimHash / LSH / embeddings). Mathematics correct, recommendation inapplicable. The O(N^2) premise assumes 10,000 documents; this archive is 165 criticals, 13,530 pairs, measured at 15 milliseconds. The MinHash theorem verified over 4,000 hashes (true Jaccard 0.3333, collision rate 0.3013). The O(1/sqrt k) scaling verified on 300-token sets but PLATEAUS on ours: measured median signature is 4 tokens, and a 64x increase in hash functions improves error 1.39x. Against 1,144 real signatures, MinHash at k=256 gave max error 0.358 on a decision boundary near 0.5. Adopting it trades 0.35 of error for 15 milliseconds. Its "semantic boundary" objection -- the one requiring expensive embeddings -- was run through the live extractor using Gemini's OWN example. "Reduced thermal load" vs "decreased heat dissipation" both produced the identical signature and scored 1.000, because the extractor takes numbers and identifiers, not words, and numbers have no synonyms. Control with different quantities: 0.111. SECOND ANSWER (AST canonicalisation / property-based execution / SMT), which REVERSES the first and states not to work at the textual or embedding layer. Every tool named is already installed and routed by the 21-entry manifest: hypothesis 6.151.9, z3 4.16.0, crosshair, sympy, ast. And its tiers 1 and 2 combined are FELM, which this project built to the panel's design, measured at Fisher p = 0.71 -- no association -- and removed on 2026-08-12. The recorded reason is a property of the material: 74 of 101 falsifiers shared ONE response vector, confirmed on the original and on every mutation. An early version also wasted its budget mutating docstrings and reported a confident meaningless result; that bug was fixed and the mechanism still did not work. Its three-way Equivalent/Distinct/Undecidable already exists as outcome_agreement returning SAME/DIFFERENT/UNKNOWN. Its "targeted differential brief" on escalation already exists as hil_reason plus _rejection_lines, built as prerequisite A10. ONE REAL GAP, corroborated not contributed. Schema enforcement: findings' numbers are extracted from prose by pattern, and nothing asks a model to EMIT the claimed and computed values as fields. All five panel models proposed exactly this on 2026-08-12, one specifying the tuple. Gemini is a sixth independent endorsement of a pending decision, which strengthens it without adding information. THIRD REVERSAL RECORDED from this source: human-vs-machine variance, then sampling reliability, now the entire architectural layer. title: Stage 1, items 1.1 and 1.5: retroactive gamma-input correction, and a starvation floor on the health monitor.
verbatim: Stage 1, items 1.1 and 1.5: retroactive gamma-input correction, and a starvation floor on the health monitor. 1.1 The gamma-input correction rewrote novelty_counts[-1] - the current round only. Measured: 236 of 287 MERGED entries (82%) were merged in a LATER round than they opened in, so the correction reached 18% of merges. A finding registered in round 3 and merged in round 7 stayed counted as novel in round 3 permanently. cdsfl_topology_formal.md:210-215 states post-deduplication as a MUST. Now the whole series is recomputed: a finding later found to be a duplicate was never novel. Measured on the archive: all 8 runs shift, 7 of 8 shift gamma UPWARD - the conservative direction, because rediscoveries had been flattening the decay curve. 1.5 regulatory_t_v2 exempted the case where all removals are duplicates. Sound as far as it went - a high duplicate rate IS depletion - but it carried no floor, so total starvation reported as health. Every modern run records rejection_rate 1.0 from round 1 (exp47 in 8 of 8 rounds) and this monitor never fired. Floor added. title: Panel review dispatch: audit CC1's Stage 1 findings and clear the path to BR2.
verbatim: Panel review dispatch: audit CC1's Stage 1 findings and clear the path to BR2. Founder-authorised. Five models, no compelled convergence, 46,459-char brief. BUILT DIFFERENTLY FROM THE 2026-08-18 DEDUP PANEL, deliberately. That panel was briefed with CC1's DESCRIPTION of the defects and one of those descriptions was refuted hours later. A panel reasoning from a description inherits its errors - already recorded on 2026-08-12, when the single model that accepted a false premise returned the worst answer. So this brief carries PRIMARY SOURCE: raw code with line numbers (packs A-H) and raw measurement tables re-derived at assembly time (M1-M9). Every CC1 claim is quarantined into a labelled ledger, and where a claim was made and later replaced BOTH are presented with equal standing, without saying which CC1 now holds. CC1's position is included as a labelled target with its error rate stated. Seven questions. Q2 is no longer open: the founder has ruled that CDSFL follows Bugzilla - preserve the duplicate record, aggregate the count onto the original, resolve by simplest sufficient fix - and the panel is asked to FALSIFY that ruling, specifically where the software-defect analogy breaks for STEM claims. NEW MEASUREMENTS in this commit: M6 immune pipeline removal rate from its own log, Apr-Jul: 3042/3132 = 97.1%, sustained four months (96.2-98.5% every month). M7 the pipeline runs AFTER registry registration (:9092 vs :8899) and NEVER writes to the registry. AST walk over every immune_result reference gives two consumers: _run_shadow_cells (zero verdict effect) and _build_feedback_for_next_round, which renders NK duplicate verdicts into the NEXT round's prompt. CC1 HYPOTHESISED duplicates were destroyed before reaching the registry; REFUTED here. The mechanism is SUPPRESSION of re-reporting, not deletion - which is why only 13 merge pointers exist across six experiments. M8 registry.resolve() on a merge performs three writes, ALL to the duplicate. Nothing is written to the target. 287/287 MERGED entries carry a pointer; none orphaned. The record survives; only the vote is removed. M9 retroactive Bugzilla-style dupe count from stored pointers: 13 findings on 11 canonical entries, max 3, and all 11 are told nothing. Bugzilla research (external, cited in the brief): duplicates are preserved via dupe_of; the duplicate reporter is added to the ORIGINAL's CC list; a dupe count over direct AND indirect duplicates drives 'Most Frequently Reported Bugs'. CDSFL implements the preservation half correctly and the aggregation half not at all. The runner's own round prompt already says 'State machine (Bugzilla paradigm)'. 'Simplest sufficient solution' is in the directives models receive (cdsfl_core_formal.md:359 + 2 others). It is NOT in the mathematical appendix. CORRECTION carried here: CC1 described MERGED as 'delete-with-pointer'. The entry is not deleted - it survives with its pointer and is excluded from every count. Archived, not deleted. title: Panel returns 5/5. Root cause of the 97% removal rate found and verified.
verbatim: Panel returns 5/5. Root cause of the 97% removal rate found and verified. THE HEADLINE, found by CC2 and independently reproduced by CC1 (M10): bench/dm/_similarity.py:183 maps cosine to [0,1] as (cos_sim + 1.0) / 2.0. That map is correct for a range of [-1,1]. Measured on exp46's 351 archived pairs, NOT ONE cosine is negative (min 0.150). Half the output range is dead, so the live range after the BETA blend starts at 0.460 while tau_sim = 0.50 (immune_agents.py:3075) was calibrated for the JACCARD backend, whose floor is 0. Flagging rate under the current map: 97.4%. Logged four-month rate: 97.1% (M6). Reproduced. With a flaw-class match the floor is 0.541, ABOVE tau_sim, so any two findings sharing a flaw class are duplicates BY CONSTRUCTION: 100.0% flagged. CC2's one-line fix, max(0.0, cos_sim), measured on the same pairs: 15.8% / 21.4%. CC1 CORRECTIONS FORCED BY THE PANEL: * The source pack mislabelled its two load-bearing sections. Pack A captioned _check_gamma_alt_convergence showed _check_hardened_convergence; Pack B captioned _settled_novelty_series showed _location_keyed_critical_series. CC2 caught it and added what CC1 missed: hardened_gate_enabled is FALSE in all six configs, so the function CC1 showed the panel is not even running in this arc. * CC1 reported gate-input staleness as DORMANT, zero effect on all six runs. WRONG (M11). That measurement used convergence_location.location_only_series where the runner uses _location_keyed_critical_series. Re-measured: exp44 and exp47 both carry stale gate inputs, and CC1's figures now reproduce CC2's exactly, differing rounds included. Direction is PERMISSIVE (under-counts criticals by 2 and 5). No archived verdict changes; both gate windows are [0,0,0] either way. * The record assembler reported '5 of 5 panellists' while one file was a FAILURE record. It counted file existence, not ok=true. Repaired to count success. CC2's other findings: novelty_counts.clear() on phase transition makes the item-1.1 retroactive loop write wrong values (dormant, burst_mode off, but a BR2 landmine); the duplicate loop breaks on FIRST match above threshold, not best; two similarity backends share one threshold with no log line recording which ran. cc2 timed out three times at 300s. Root cause: call_claude_cli defaults to timeout=300 while this brief instructs the only tool-capable panellist to read the repository. Retried at 900s per the precedent already in experiment_11_orchestrator.py:134; returned in 428s, 26,033 chars. title: Second panel: enforcement gap, prose targets, and a straight answer on the runway.
verbatim: Second panel: enforcement gap, prose targets, and a straight answer on the runway. Five models. CC1's headline measurement was REFUTED by the panel and the refutation verified against source. WHAT CC1 GOT WRONG, all confirmed by reading the code: * CC1 reported 37.7% of corroboration blocks 'did not show working'. CC2 found 77% of that tier DID show it: _RK_RE_TRAILING_FLOAT anchors on $ and models write markdown (**0.12**, backticks, trailing full stops). Enforcing against that measurement would reject compliant models for using asterisks. * The return-to-source mechanism the founder asked for ALREADY EXISTS and is wired (_feedback.py:304-326, rendered at :481-486). It is starved: near- duplicate scores 2.0*similarity in priority_score while R_k discrepancy scores min(1.0,|delta|), typically <0.1. At 97% near-duplicate flagging it was crowded out of every prompt. THE ENFORCEMENT GAP AND THE DEDUP DEFECT ARE ONE DEFECT. * _feedback.py:483 tells the model 'aggregate = X' where X is the recompute from THE MODEL'S OWN stated parameters. A model told it differs from a peer average may hold its ground; one told its own arithmetic does not close cannot. * _feedback.py:325 is dedented out of its loop; only the last target keeps its discrepancy record. * CC1's 'prose decides better' claim is REFUTED: markdown returns 18 SAME and 0 DIFFERENT. Not better - one-directional, the signature of a degenerate mode where applying a fix rewrites the passage and both falsifiers stop firing. * CC1's 'nu is replay-validatable at zero cost' is REFUTED: check_sk_threshold takes nu_b/nu_f and is called live at :7609; changing nu changes SK_REJECTED, which scores +3.0 in priority_score and enters the next prompt. * NO_SCORE landed 2026-08-01; exp44-49 ran 27-29 July. Zero occurrences in any archived log. 325 unit tests, never executed live. exp50 will be its first run. Q5, THE RUNWAY, ANSWERED STRAIGHT AND SPLIT 3-2: ge YES. cx sufficient-not-generous. cgpt YES but only for a NARROWED claim. cc2 NO - 'you will have no run of the fixed harness on a target the broken harness also ran'; every comparison becomes across-target AND across- harness. Picks exp44 not exp46 (13 rounds so the churn floor can fire; only run where counterfactual repair produced both labels). ds NO - exp46+exp50 is a pilot, not a confirmatory package. Wants THREE live runs and PRE-REGISTRATION of endpoints and matched-pair selection before any run, because choosing exp46 on its narrow margin is post-hoc. Disagreement preserved: cc2 says exp44, ds says exp46. cc2 says do NOT use counterfactual repair for prose sigma; ds says prose is not the wall and to use it. Both are argued from measurement; neither is smoothed away. DISPATCH DEFECT, CC1's: ds first returned a hallucinated <tool_calls> block in 4.6s and recorded ok=True - a failure rendering as a success, the same shape as yesterday's record assembler. Cause: the SYSTEM prompt told panellists to use file-reading tools, which only cc2 has. Retry with that line replaced returned 6,913 chars in 306.8s. The retry now also rejects a tool-call-shaped response. SECURITY: sourcing .env with '. ./.env' made zsh execute an unquoted value and echo ZENODO_TOKEN into a shell error, on this dispatch and on both of yesterday's. Scrubbed from the scratch files. .env loading moved into Python (parse, never execute). ZENODO_TOKEN and SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY are unquoted and lack the export prefix every other key has; both need quoting and the Zenodo token needs rotating. BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17.
