title: Items 1-6: repair the R_k reader, the feedback wording and priority, and clamp the similarity map.
verbatim: Items 1-6: repair the R_k reader, the feedback wording and priority, and clamp the similarity map. Suite 3573 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed. ITEM 1 - the R_k extractor could not read markdown. _RK_RE_TRAILING_FLOAT ended in $, requiring the number to be the last thing on the line. Models write '= **0.12**.' and '`R_k = 0.385`'. MEASURED EFFECT of the repair on exp44-49's raw responses: SKIP 145 -> 30, 115 blocks recovered. BEFORE PASS 90 (23.4%) WARN 12 FAIL 138 (35.8%) SKIP 145 (37.7%) AFTER PASS 143 (37.1%) WARN 12 FAIL 200 (51.9%) SKIP 30 ( 7.8%) CC1's morning claim that 37.7% of models 'did not show their working' is WITHDRAWN. Most of that tier showed it and the reader could not see it. The defensible figure is the one above: 51.9% of corroboration blocks state an R_k that does not follow from the model's own stated parameters. ITEM 2 - the feedback told models 'aggregate = X' where X is the recompute from THEIR OWN stated eta, d, p, S_k and nu. A model told it differs from a peer average may reasonably hold its position. Reworded to say whose arithmetic it is. ITEM 3 - _feedback.py: two lines sat at the loop's own indent level, so they ran ONCE after it finished using whatever leaked from the final iteration. With more than one target per finding id, every earlier record silently lost its discrepancy. Found by the CC2 audit. ITEM 4 - R_k FAIL priority raised from min(1.0,|delta|) to a flat 2.5, above near-duplicate (2.0) and below REFUTED (3.0). This OVERRIDES A DELIBERATE DESIGN DECISION recorded in test_priority_refutation_beats_admissibility_beats_duplicate_beats_rk, so the reasoning is recorded in that test rather than the invariant being quietly flipped. CC2 measured the starvation (the R_k record fired in 20 of 170 exp44 files against a 31.7% FAIL rate). Simulation adds the part CC2 did not have: clamping the map does NOT fix this alone and makes it worse. Once duplicates are rare they stop being a constant and start discriminating, so the minority carrying a duplicate flag outrank every R_k failure. Fraction of R_k-failing findings reaching the prompt: 65.8% before the clamp, 46.3% after it under the old weights, 66.4% under these. The sub-threshold cap is preserved. ITEM 6a - the cosine map is clamped: max(0.0, cos_sim) replaces (cos_sim+1)/2. MEASURED in the live code path on exp46's 351 pairs: 98.0% -> 21.4% flagged. ITEM 6b - the early-exit break in the duplicate search removed. It stopped at the FIRST candidate over threshold, so duplicate_of named an arbitrary neighbour rather than the nearest. Invisible at 97% flagging; a real misattribution at 21%. ITEM 6c - scored against the 85 tool-decided labels, the repaired function still flags 95.3% with precision 0.494 against a base rate of 0.471. Those 85 are the HARD residue by construction. This re-confirms the panel's ruling: do not set a new similarity threshold. No similarity method separates the hard cases, which is why the tool-gated merge is the actual fix. MEASUREMENT WORTH RECORDING, not yet acted on. Both similarity paths scored against the 85 tool-decided labels: STEM signature AUC 0.503, embedding 0.582. The STEM signature's documented separation (median 0.529 vs 0.000, p=8.4e-14) REPRODUCES - but against the system's own merges, which were decided by MODEL VOTE. Against tool verdicts on the hard cases it is at chance. Most likely a population effect: 13 merges and 10,048 mostly-easy distinct pairs versus 85 deliberately-hard ones. They are also complementary: the STEM signature has zero signal on 30.6% of the hard pairs and the embedding scores AUC 0.618 on exactly that blind subset. BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: Item 7: no voting. Remove every model-vote path to MERGED.
verbatim: Item 7: no voting. Remove every model-vote path to MERGED. Founder ruling, 2026-08-19: "There will be no voting in CDSFL. They can classify, ideate and research, but ultimately truth should always be deterministic and be decided via tools." Suite 3573 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed. MEASURED 2026-08-18: all 13 merges across exp42-49 were written by model vote. None came from a tool. A merge removes a finding from every count, every series and the convergence gate, so a show of hands could delete a critical finding from the convergence calculation - in a project whose founding rule is that findings are confirmed programmatically or by HIL, never by model vote. THREE PATHS REMOVED, all in _update_finding_statuses, which runs unconditionally: * "if len(distinct_models) >= 2: # Clear consensus - merge" (the live path that wrote all 13 archived merges) * the small-panel single-vote path beside it, which merged on ONE model * "D4 MERGE QUORUM" at the plurality branch - its own log line named it a quorum * and a fourth, in the verdict-application path: a merge on a model-DECLARED "DUPLICATE" action. Declaring a duplicate is not demonstrating one. Each now records merge_candidate_of and merge_blocked_reason and logs MERGE WITHHELD. The finding stays OPEN and non-blocking, visible in the registry with the reason recorded - the founder's stated design. A false split leaves two entries for one defect, which is visible and recoverable. A false merge deletes a real finding, which is neither. WHY NOT WIRE THE TOOL HERE. Counterfactual repair is the replacement and it exists: it decided 85 pairs at 0.287 s/pair, zero API cost. It cannot be called from this function, which receives (registry, round_idx, cfg) and no target path, and RunnerConfig carries none. Plumbing it is a separate change. Until then the conservative default holds and NOTHING merges without a tool verdict. TWO MERGED WRITERS REMAIN, both inert in this arc and both audited: reference_runner_v2.py:1752 _try_merge_arbitration - merge_arbitration_enabled defaults False and is unset in every exp44-52 config reference_runner_v2.py:3319 _apply_routing - routing_enabled defaults False, unset in every exp44-52 config. Note for whoever enables it: its confirmed_duplicate() decides on prose Jaccard at threshold 0.85, which is a similarity judgement, not a tool verdict. title: Items 8, 9, 11, 14: the gate's own count input, exp47's lost rounds, the prose control, and rho's floor in shadow.
verbatim: Items 8, 9, 11, 14: the gate's own count input, exp47's lost rounds, the prose control, and rho's floor in shadow. Suite 3573 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed. ITEM 8 - the convergence gate's count input was corrected in ONE position only. "novel_critical_history[-1] = location_crit_history[round_idx]" wrote the current round and nothing else - exactly the single-position defect item 1.1 repaired in novelty_counts. Item 1.1 fixed the copy that does NOT gate and left this one, which DOES: the gate reads novel_critical_history[-window:]. _location_keyed_critical_series recomputes the WHOLE series from the registry on every call, so every earlier element stayed frozen at the vintage it was written with. A finding opened in round 3 and later merged kept crediting round 3 for the rest of the run. Now the whole series is copied across. MEASURED with the runner's own function: exp44 recorded [4,2,2,1,0,2,0,1,0,0,0,0,0] -> resettles at rounds 2 and 6 exp47 differs at rounds 0, 3, 7, 8, 10 exp45, exp46 identical Direction is PERMISSIVE: the gate saw 2 fewer criticals than the registry held in exp44 and 5 fewer in exp47, and under-counting criticals makes convergence easier. No archived verdict changes - both gate windows read [0,0,0] either way. ITEM 9 - exp47's report holds 9 rounds starting at round 5 while the run recorded converged_at=13 and total_rounds=14. CAUSE FOUND: round 5 carries 15 per-model response files against 5 for every other round. That is a resume. The report was rebuilt from the resume point and rounds 0-4 were dropped from `rounds` and gamma_critical_history; location_crit_shadow_history was rebuilt from the registry and kept all 14. Raw responses for all 14 rounds are intact. report_reconstruction_rounds_0_to_4.json recovers what is genuinely derivable - per-round response counts from the files, and novel/novel-critical recomputed via _settled_novelty_series. elapsed_s, gamma and rho for rounds 0-4 are recorded NULL, not estimated: they were computed live and are not recoverable. No field in that file is inferred. ITEM 11 - control_two_distinct_defects.md, generated so ground truth is a property of the generator rather than of adjudication. One passage, two defects that are genuinely distinct (a misquoted Nyquist criterion with a true conclusion; a correct computation with a conclusion that does not follow) but which a single edit - "increase N" - could appear to cure, because it rewrites the passage the first falsifier quotes. This settles the disagreement the second panel preserved. CC2 holds that counterfactual repair is degenerate on prose (18 SAME, 0 DIFFERENT on markdown). DeepSeek holds that prose is not the wall. If the tool calls these two SAME, CC2 is right. Ground truth is DISTINCT and is recorded beside the target. ITEM 14 - rho_earliest_round is 12 with no derivation on record. A structural floor is 2 * rho_rolling_window = 6, derived from the window so the two cannot drift apart again. It is computed in SHADOW and logged when it would differ; it does NOT gate, and the shadow value never leaves _compute_rho (verified by AST). NOT promoted, for two measured reasons. A floor of 6 would have REFUSED convergence in exp46 (corrected rho_avg 0.2176) and exp48 (0.1944), both under the 0.25 threshold, and churn is blocking condition (d) in _check_gamma_alt_convergence. And rho's input is distorted by the similarity defect repaired in this same window, so a value fitted now would be calibrated on contaminated data. The operating value is to be set from exp46's re-run. BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: Items 10 and 13: the fix-complexity measurer (shadow only) and the pre-registration draft.
verbatim: Items 10 and 13: the fix-complexity measurer (shadow only) and the pre-registration draft. Suite 3587 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed (14 new tests). ITEM 10 - nu's missing input. The appendix DEFINES the re-injection term as a complexity measure: "Localised one-line changes have low nu. Changes to shared interfaces have higher nu." The runner derives it from two constants, nu_eff = 1 - (1 - nu_b) * (1 - (1 - sk) * nu_f) nu_b=0.05, nu_f=0.20 whose only free variables are the fix's efficacy and those constants. It depends on nothing about the fix. So the mathematics for the simplest sufficient solution is already in the model and its input is a constant. bench/dm/_fix_complexity.py supplies the measurement: blocks, distinct paths, lines changed, and signature, import and decorator touches - the appendix's own "shared interface" case. CALIBRATED against 435 archived fixes that carry a parseable SEARCH/REPLACE block. Raw complexity min 7, median 23, max 181. 187 of those fixes touch a function or class signature, so the shared-interface case is not rare. IT RETURNS A PERCENTILE RANK, NOT A PROBABILITY. DeepSeek's calibration point: with no held-out outcome labels a fitted probability would be overfitted to the same archive it was fitted on. complexity_index() returns None when there is no population to rank against - an honest absence, since 0.0 would read as "maximally simple". SHADOW ONLY, and this is not caution for its own sake. CC2 refuted CC1's claim that wiring nu is replay-validatable at zero cost: check_sk_threshold() takes nu_b and nu_f and is called live, and below the break-even S* a fix is marked SK_REJECTED, which scores +3.0 in the feedback priority and enters the next round's prompt. Changing nu changes which fixes are rejected, which changes prompts, which invalidates replay. 467 Valley-of-Bad-Fixes lines across the arc say that path is live. The shadow guarantee is ASSERTED, not trusted: a test walks the module's AST and fails if it imports the runner or calls compute_rk or check_sk_threshold. String matching would not do - the module's docstring names both while explaining why it stays out of them. DeepSeek's counter is recorded in the module rather than answered: a hidden measure is good against gaming and is NOT an enforcement mechanism. If the goal is pressure toward simpler fixes, the model needs a signal. If the goal is accurate reporting, hidden is right. ITEM 13 - pre-registration DRAFT, deliberately not frozen. Awaiting the founder. Raised by DeepSeek and by no other panellist: exp46 was chosen AFTER seeing it had the narrowest convergence margin, which is a post-hoc selection a reviewer is entitled to attack. The draft fixes the three runs (exp46 matched, then exp50 and exp51 as two clean domains - three live runs, because on two it is a pilot and must be called one), the primary and five secondary endpoints with their measured baselines, and FOUR DECLARED FAILURE CONDITIONS including the real one: that exp46 may not converge at all once the panel is no longer under a standing instruction to stop reporting. CC2's argument for exp44 over exp46 is recorded in the document as considered and not taken, with the founder's reasoning. BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: Design reviews: the Bugzilla question answered at last, and perturbation assessed.
verbatim: Design reviews: the Bugzilla question answered at last, and perturbation assessed. Four read-only reviews, CC2 and Fable on two questions, no metered cost, nothing modified. Verbatim record committed at 64,622 chars. THE URGENT ONE, found independently by both and verified by CC1: discrimination_control_ask is a DEAD FLAG. reference_runner_v2.py:593 is its only occurrence - the definition. Nothing reads it. The real gate is _gate_falsifier_directive(ask_corrected_copy=False), whose single caller at :5529 passes nothing, so the main panel has NEVER been asked for a corrected copy. That is why zero exist in the archive. Fable: this is the launcher-drop defect shape the control's own comment names as having shipped three times - a fourth instance, inside the control itself. CC1's recommendation to enable it for exp46 was worthless as stated. BOTH AGREE, on Bugzilla: * Drop DUPLICATE. Zero writes, eleven terminal-status sets. A dead value in a state machine is the value someone will one day write to, bypassing the guards. * OPEN -> CONFIRMED is a vote and worse than reported: required = min(2, panel) at sev >= 0.7, else 1. One model suffices for the majority of findings. * Split it: CORROBORATED (model-attested, scheduling only) vs CONFIRMED (tool re-executed the falsifier). Fable's rule: existence-votes may schedule; only tools settle. CC2 reframes the axis as REVERSIBILITY rather than identity-vs-existence - a wrong CONFIRMED is recoverable, a wrong MERGED is not. * EXTEND is the answer to ledger-vs-instrument, reached independently by both. Make it carry a falsifier; run it against the target, then against the parent's fix. Still fires = the parent fix is demonstrably insufficient and the system names what it misses. CC2 is honest that only 11 archived entries can replay it. THEY DISAGREE on the missing state. Fable: a resolution value (TARGET_REFUTED) on a restored status-x-resolution PAIR. CC2: not a state at all - Bugzilla handles it by RETARGETING plus a blocked_on edge, and the difference between software and STEM is not lifecycle but who owns the target. Preserved, not resolved. FABLE'S STRUCTURAL FINDINGS, all verified by CC1: * bench/reference_runner.py (v1) still merges by vote at 4 sites, and test_runner_status_transitions.py imports V1 - 31 tests pass asserting two votes merge into an unregistered target, and one vote merges on a small panel. * Inverted test pressure: the abolished behaviour has 31 green tests, the replacement has one, and that only because CC1 added it today. * add_verdict stores evidence[:200], so a why-channel cannot be rebuilt later. CC2's fourth, and the most serious: >1000 of ~1200 CONFIRMED entries carry NO field identifying what decided them, and every MERGED entry's justification was overwritten at write time. The archive cannot answer whether any archived CONFIRMED was tool-established or vote-established. The founding principle is currently unauditable on its own record. BOTH RECOMMEND FIRST: a transition log in resolve(), the single status write in the runner, recording {to, from, round, wall_clock, mechanism, actor, evidence_ref} with mechanism as a typed enum - then one test forbidding MODEL_ATTESTATION from writing CONFIRMED/CLOSED/MERGED. CC2: nothing else converts 'tools decide, not votes' from a policy into a constraint. PERTURBATION: both say yes for sameness, but ONLY with the corrected copy as the perturbation, never an arbitrary one - an arbitrary perturbation destroys the shared substrate and collapses every co-located pair to a false SAME. It is counterfactual repair with its 46.8% failure mode removed. The gaming defeat is real and cannot be closed: the examinee supplies both instrument and stimulus, so a change-detector falsifier passes every probe while testing nothing. THE URGENT ONE, found independently by both and verified by CC1: discrimination_control_ask is a DEAD FLAG. reference_runner_v2.py:593 is its only occurrence - the definition. Nothing reads it. The real gate is _gate_falsifier_directive(ask_corrected_copy=False), whose single caller at :5529 passes nothing, so the main panel has NEVER been asked for a corrected copy. That is why zero exist in the archive. Fable: this is the launcher-drop defect shape the control's own comment names as having shipped three times - a fourth instance, inside the control itself. CC1's recommendation to enable it for exp46 was worthless as stated. BOTH AGREE, on Bugzilla: * Drop DUPLICATE. Zero writes, eleven terminal-status sets. A dead value in a state machine is the value someone will one day write to, bypassing the guards. * OPEN -> CONFIRMED is a vote and worse than reported: required = min(2, panel) at sev >= 0.7, else 1. One model suffices for the majority of findings. * Split it: CORROBORATED (model-attested, scheduling only) vs CONFIRMED (tool re-executed the falsifier). Fable's rule: existence-votes may schedule; only tools settle. CC2 reframes the axis as REVERSIBILITY rather than identity-vs-existence - a wrong CONFIRMED is recoverable, a wrong MERGED is not. * EXTEND is the answer to ledger-vs-instrument, reached independently by both. Make it carry a falsifier; run it against the target, then against the parent's fix. Still fires = the parent fix is demonstrably insufficient and the system names what it misses. CC2 is honest that only 11 archived entries can replay it. THEY DISAGREE on the missing state. Fable: a resolution value (TARGET_REFUTED) on a restored status-x-resolution PAIR. CC2: not a state at all - Bugzilla handles it by RETARGETING plus a blocked_on edge, and the difference between software and STEM is not lifecycle but who owns the target. Preserved, not resolved. FABLE'S STRUCTURAL FINDINGS, all verified by CC1: * bench/reference_runner.py (v1) still merges by vote at 4 sites, and test_runner_status_transitions.py imports V1 - 31 tests pass asserting two votes merge into an unregistered target, and one vote merges on a small panel. * Inverted test pressure: the abolished behaviour has 31 green tests, the replacement has one, and that only because CC1 added it today. * add_verdict stores evidence[:200], so a why-channel cannot be rebuilt later. CC2's fourth, and the most serious: >1000 of ~1200 CONFIRMED entries carry NO field identifying what decided them, and every MERGED entry's justification was overwritten at write time. The archive cannot answer whether any archived CONFIRMED was tool-established or vote-established. The founding principle is currently unauditable on its own record. BOTH RECOMMEND FIRST: a transition log in resolve(), the single status write in the runner, recording {to, from, round, wall_clock, mechanism, actor, evidence_ref} with mechanism as a typed enum - then one test forbidding MODEL_ATTESTATION from writing CONFIRMED/CLOSED/MERGED. CC2: nothing else converts 'tools decide, not votes' from a policy into a constraint. PERTURBATION: both say yes for sameness, but ONLY with the corrected copy as the perturbation, never an arbitrary one - an arbitrary perturbation destroys the shared substrate and collapses every co-located pair to a false SAME. It is counterfactual repair with its 46.8% failure mode removed. The gaming defeat is real and cannot be closed: the examinee supplies both instrument and stimulus, so a change-detector falsifier passes every probe while testing nothing. title: sv: the 97% removal rate was one line of arithmetic; every model-vote path to MERGED closed; the founding principle found unauditable on its own record.
verbatim: sv: the 97% removal rate was one line of arithmetic; every model-vote path to MERGED closed; the founding principle found unauditable on its own record. Suite 3587 passed, 20 skipped, 0 failed. Both remote experimental branches deleted; main is the sole branch. One file rescued that existed in no ref at all. THE HEADLINE. bench/dm/_similarity.py mapped cosine to [0,1] as (cos+1)/2. Measured on exp46's 351 pairs, NOT ONE cosine is negative, so half the scale was dead and the live range began at 0.460 against tau_sim = 0.50 - calibrated for the Jaccard backend. With a flaw-class match the floor was 0.541, ABOVE threshold: any two findings sharing a class were duplicates by construction. Flagging 97.4% measured vs 97.1% logged over four months. Clamped: 98.0% -> 21.4% in the live path. Consequence: every convergence in exp44-49 was reached while models were told each round to withdraw prior findings. Those curves are curves of a suppressed process. NO VOTING - six paths removed. All 13 archived merges were vote-written. Two of the six were found only by independent reviewers, and both were CC1 over-generalising from a default instead of reading the configs: merge_arbitration_enabled is TRUE in every config exp40-51 (exp46/50/51 included), and routing_enabled is set via the legacy alias take_up_slack_enabled. CC1 had catalogued the routing path as live in its own document the day before. NO code path writes MERGED now. Wiring counterfactual repair is ONE ARGUMENT - target_path is in scope in the caller at :8132. Highest-priority outstanding item. THE MOST SERIOUS FINDING (CC2). Over 1000 of ~1200 CONFIRMED entries carry no field identifying what decided them, and every MERGED entry's justification was overwritten at write time. The archive cannot answer whether any archived CONFIRMED was tool- or vote-established. Both reviewers' first recommendation: a transition log in resolve() recording {to, from, round, wall_clock, mechanism, actor, evidence_ref} with mechanism a typed enum, then one test forbidding MODEL_ATTESTATION from writing CONFIRMED/CLOSED/MERGED. BUGZILLA ANSWERED after seven reviews that could not, because none had the material. Drop the dead DUPLICATE STATUS (not detection - 'duplicate is a relation, MERGED is the state that records it'). Split CONFIRMED, which is a vote requiring only ONE model below severity 0.7. EXTEND is the additive mechanism, used 183-543 times and read by nothing. Reviewers disagree, preserved, on whether the missing state is a resolution value or a retarget-plus-blocked_on edge. PERTURBATION. The discrimination control is built, has never run, and its switch is DEAD - discrimination_control_ask is never read. Sound for sameness only with the corrected copy as the perturbation, never an arbitrary one. MEASURED TODAY. gamma_critical exceeds gamma_all in 10 of 10 runs (p = 0.001), and survives a sparsity null: random same-size subsets give -0.004, the real critical subset +0.115 (p = 0.005). Hard-constraint findings deplete faster than soft ones, and it is severity not sparsity. title: Geometry dialogue, two rounds: 'geometry' dropped, and CC2 refutes its own objection by measuring it.
verbatim: Geometry dialogue, two rounds: 'geometry' dropped, and CC2 refutes its own objection by measuring it. Run as a conversation rather than a questionnaire - round 1 independent, round 2 with each reviewer shown the other's answer. Both converged; both moved and said where. NAMING - SETTLED. Both reviewers independently reached the same conclusion and named the same lineage: Duane / Crow-AMSAA reliability growth (1962, aircraft engine testing). _estimate_gamma fits ONE log-log slope per series. Information geometry studies Riemannian structure on statistical manifolds - metric tensor, connection, curvature - and this codebase has none of them. CC2: 'calling it geometry imports a vocabulary whose actual objects you do not have.' Fable: 'two slopes are not a geometry, they are two rates.' And the right word was already in the code: GAMMA_BANDS reads 'Strong depletion / Moderate depletion / Weak depletion'. CC2: 'you named it correctly years ago and are now being talked out of it.' The founder's buzzword instinct was correct, for a checkable technical reason rather than a stylistic one. PERTURBATION - SETTLED, and the founder was right against CC1. One mechanism at two scales, not two mechanisms. CC2: CC1 split them on access, which is 'a distinction about where you stand, not about what the operation is'. Both measure a dependency footprint. Fable adds that each version's defeat analysis transfers to the other. d_i - CC1 WAS WRONG AND IT IS WORSE. reference_runner_v2.py:7803 passes d=1.0, p=1.0 HARDCODED; q reads model_params, whose own comment at :7741 says it 'is never populated'; zero q values across every archived exp4x report. The entire eta.d.p channel has NEVER EXECUTED - R_k has run 1750 times on constants. Fable conceded in full: 'wiring a dead channel, not tuning a live one.' MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md:354 already mandates d = f(tool output), which the runner cannot satisfy. CC2 REFUTED ITS OWN STRONGEST OBJECTION BY TESTING IT. Round 1 it argued the 0.1*severity tie-breaker in priority_score preferentially fed high-severity findings into the correction list for four months. Round 2 it measured: build_feedback_records takes round-K findings only, cut at top_k=10, and across all 11 archived runs the most any model filed in one round is EIGHT. The cut never bound. Verified independently by CC1: 11 runs, max 8, zero groups over 10. Objection withdrawn. THE CONVERGED SENTENCE, narrower than either wrote, because CC2 showed the two apparent lines of evidence are ONE measurement reported twice - _estimate_gamma reads only per-round counts, so 'crit curve steeper' is definitionally equivalent to 'criticals arrive earlier', which is what Spearman(severity, round) = -0.38 says: 'Across ten multi-model review runs, model-assigned critical findings arrive earlier in the round sequence than findings overall: the Duane depletion exponent is higher for criticals in 10/10 runs (mean +0.14, Wilcoxon p = 0.002). The partition variable is a model self-assessment; whether this reflects exhaustion of hard constraints or reporter de-escalation is not determined by these data.' THE SEPARATING TEST, and it is elegant: decouple the round index SHOWN to models from the true one. Reporting-order predicts severity tracks the displayed counter; depletion predicts it tracks true exhaustion. One run, one prompt field. Fable adds a free archive-only alternative: classify hardness from what each falsifier ASSERTS (wrong value / exception / violated invariant = hard) rather than from the severity float. BUILD ORDER - they disagree with reasons. Fable: transition log first, because every named test produces new rows and rows without provenance recreate the problem. CC2: null-perturbation control first - it runs offline today (449/465 archived falsifiers import project code, only 75 read the target as text), the existing discrimination control cannot substitute because nothing supplies a corrected copy, and it is logically prior: if the mechanism does not discriminate, the log faithfully records a meaningless verdict. Both agree the transition log goes into the next live run alongside the round-index control. BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The null-perturbation control: built, run on the archive, and it comes back clean.
verbatim: The null-perturbation control: built, run on the archive, and it comes back clean. Run before building anything else, on the founder's instinct and CC2's argument that it is logically prior: a provenance log that records WHICH mechanism settled a verdict is worthless if the mechanism does not discriminate. RESULT, 397 archived findings with a falsifier and an in-repo target: fired on the unmodified target 360 flipped on an appended COMMENT 0 (0.0%) flipped on an UNRELATED CODE CHANGE 0 (0.0%) of the 304 testable no unrelated def available to rename 56 CC2's own promotion criterion was '<10% flip'. 0% clears it, so by its stated terms the instrument is fine and the typed transition log becomes the binding constraint. TWO PERTURBATIONS, because one alone is a control that cannot fail. Appending a comment changes bytes and nothing else - but 449 of 465 archived falsifiers IMPORT the target rather than reading it as text, and an importer cannot see a comment, so a 0% flip rate there proves only that falsifiers are not byte-sensitive. The second renames a module-level def the finding does NOT accuse and leaves an alias behind, so behaviour is preserved and every caller still resolves: semantically equivalent, visible to an importer, genuinely unrelated to the claim. That is the one that could have failed. WHAT IT PROVES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It closes the change-response hole: these falsifiers do not react to superficial edits. It does NOT close access-versus- dependence (reference_runner_v2.py:2972) - a falsifier that opens the target and discards the contents would pass this control too, because the perturbation is semantically null BY DESIGN. That hole needs the discrimination control, which asks whether repairing the claim makes the falsifier go quiet, and which has never run because nothing supplies a corrected copy and its config flag is dead. The real targets were never written: each run builds a symlink mirror of the repo in a temp dir via _build_discrimination_overlay, replaces one file there, and rmtrees it in a finally. SEPARATELY MEASURED, answering the founder's question about claiming that different intelligences show different 'shapes': per-model decay profiles across exp44-49 give Codex 0.693, ChatGPT 0.528, CC2 0.517, DeepSeek 0.413, Gemini 0.183 - an ordering spanning nearly 4x - but within-model sd runs 0.23-0.37 and Kruskal-Wallis gives H=6.98, p=0.137 on 6 runs each. MODELS DO NOT DIFFER DETECTABLY. The claim is not currently supportable - underpowered, not refuted. BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The founding principle IS auditable from exp42 on — but the gate measures "fired", not "fired BECAUSE".
verbatim: The founding principle IS auditable from exp42 on — but the gate measures "fired", not "fired BECAUSE". The founder asked whether five days of defect-finding means the work to date is bunk, and required a plain yes if so. Answered with measurement and a five-model panel (5 of 5 returned, no compelled convergence). The answer is neither hypothesis, and the split is now located precisely. WITHDRAWN, and it was mine. "The founding principle is currently unauditable on its own record" — taken from a reviewer on 21 August, repeated on 22 August, never checked. It is FALSE from exp42 on. `falsifier_verdict` entered the code 2026-06-03 (4fba6cc); `falsifier_gate_enabled` is unset in all 8 exp40/41 configs and True in all 17 from exp42 on — configs read, not the code default. Modern arc: 85.3% of terminal verdicts carry a recorded tool verdict, 97.4% of closures do, status tracks the tool verdict at 99.8%, and 8 of 8 archived series replay exactly. The claim is true only for exp34-41, where the mechanism did not exist. The engine analogy holds and its boundary is a dated commit. ALSO WITHDRAWN, and it is the more instructive one. The M6 sign test (25/25, p=2.98e-08, then 25/26, p=4.02e-07 after DeepSeek objected to the exclusion) is DELETED. apply_falsifier_verdicts runs AFTER _update_finding_statuses and overwrites status unconditionally, so "the tool prevails" is deterministic and the p-value was arithmetic on a foregone conclusion. I cited that exact ordering as the refutation of the panel's tautology objection and did not notice it gutted my own statistic. The table survives as a REGRESSION CHECK — the gate was on and nothing bypassed it — which is worth having given six model-vote paths to MERGED were found on 19 August. CC2's decomposition: the 26 disagreements are 18 tool-failures (sound: votes are not SUFFICIENT), 6 housekeeping votes (MERGE/REOPEN are not truth claims; my construction, not defensible), and 2 truth contests. "The tool overrules the panel on truth" rests on n=2. THE FINDING THAT OUTRANKS ALL OF IT. CC2 executed the gate rather than reasoning about it, reproduced here: reverify_falsifier("assert False, 'FALSIFIED: trivially'") -> CONFIRMED reverify_falsifier("print('FALSIFIED')") -> CONFIRMED The gate measures that a falsifier FIRED, never that it fired BECAUSE of the claim. 0 of 2,030 archived entries carry a discrimination record: the control has never run once in the project's life. THE NEXT STEP CHANGED. Four of five panellists name the discrimination control. It does NOT need a live run: 367 of 437 modern CONFIRMED findings carry a machine-applyable fix, and CC2's second route needs no fix at all — re-run each archived falsifier against the commit that later fixed the defect it accuses. Pre-registered from CC2 before measuring: >=95% quiet -> H-BUILD without reservation; >=10% still firing -> materially toward H-VOID. FW.5 drops to second (MERGED is 13 modern entries; CONFIRMED/CLOSED is 436), still verified that no code path writes MERGED at all. NEW EXCLUSION. exp48/exp49 out of headline claims: answer-key contamination already in the errata; both target documents deleted from disk so 68 falsifiers can never re-run; and 100% of the archive's detached falsifiers live there. CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN BRIEF, all CC2's, all verified: 2,247/27.5% double-counted exp36_evidence_latest — true figures 2,030 / 1,442 terminal / 31.5%; all four M7 cases carry escalated=True, so "killed on no evidence" overstates it; and a gamma-stability check attempted tonight compared two different series and is withdrawn. DISCLOSED BY CC2: it ran null_perturbation_control.py --limit 12, which writes unconditionally, overwriting the committed 397-row result. It reported this before anything else and did not restore the file itself. Restored from git; the script needs --dry-run. Suite 3589 passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed offline, netguard strict, 41 outbound attempts all denied. Memory exclusion ledger 108 -> 112, the FIFTH consecutive correction in the same direction — the 2026-08-17 remedy (bump it in the sv path) was never built. Reproduce every figure: python3 scripts/track_record_audit.py Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

The M6 sign test (25/25, p=2.98e-08, then 25/26, p=4.02e-07 after DeepSeek objected to the exclusion) is DELETED. apply_falsifier_verdicts runs AFTER _update_finding_statuses and overwrites status unconditionally, so "the tool prevails" is deterministic and the p-value was arithmetic on a foregone conclusion. title: The discrimination control, run at last, both routes: half the archive's confirmations are demonstrated, half are not.
verbatim: The discrimination control, run at last, both routes: half the archive's confirmations are demonstrated, half are not. THE RESULT, AND THE PRE-REGISTERED RULE IS HONOURED RATHER THAN RENEGOTIATED. Of 263 archived confirmations that could be tested, 132 (50.2%) are backed by a falsifier demonstrated to fire on the accused defect and go silent on its repair. 131 still fire after their own accused defect is repaired. The rule taken from CC2 before any number existed was >=95% quiet -> H-BUILD without reservation, >=10% still firing -> materially toward H-VOID. 50.2% FAILS IT, on the H-VOID side. Half the modern arc's confirmations are demonstrated; half are not, and are now known not to be. THE CONFOUND WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. "Still fires" conflates "the falsifier is blind" with "the proposed fix was bad" -- these are model-proposed fixes mostly never applied or reviewed, and a perfect falsifier facing a bad fix is right to keep firing. Each still-firing falsifier was re-run against up to 8 OTHER findings' fixes for the same file, known-substantive because each had silenced some other falsifier. 2 of 130 (1.5%) were sensitive, so their own fix is what failed. 128 (98.5%) never went quiet on anything. The bad-fix explanation accounts for 1.5%, not 50%. The counter-objection is stated in the note rather than buried: firing on someone else's fix is EXPECTED of a correct falsifier, so the 98.5% is not itself proof -- the evidence against the 131 is that they fire on their OWN fix. THE MIRROR CONTROL: THE PASSING HALF PASSES CLEANLY. Of the 132, 92 (69.7%) are specific -- quiet on their own fix, firing on all 8 others. Of the 40 that were not, 35 were silenced by only 1-2 of 8, which is the signature of DUPLICATE findings sharing a root cause; this project's own repair adjudicator uses exactly that as its SAME criterion. Exactly 1 was silenced by 8 of 8. So the fragile population is 1-5 of 132, not 40. ROUTE B IS LARGELY UNINFORMATIVE AND ITS 3.9% MUST NOT BE QUOTED. 346 of 360 fire on every stored version -- but 126 findings went quiet on their own fix while firing on every version. This runner suggests fixes to a human and does not commit them, so most accused defects were never repaired in git and a correct falsifier is RIGHT to fire on every version. Route A is load-bearing. Recorded because a 3.9% headline would have been read as catastrophic and would have been wrong. WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW. Not that the design is unsound. 50% is not 0%: 132 falsifiers do exactly what the design specifies, including staying fired through 8 substantive unrelated edits, and a design that did not work would return near 0% rather than a clean split. The failure is located in the GATE, not the concept -- reverify_falsifier("print('FALSIFIED')") returns CONFIRMED because nothing ever required a falsifier to demonstrate dependence on its target. And the measurement IS the repair: run this script in-loop and the 131 never reach CONFIRMED. METHOD. 372 CONFIRMED falsifiers, exp42-47 code targets; exp48/49 excluded, their targets are deleted. Every execution inside a throwaway symlink overlay built by the runner's own _build_discrimination_overlay -- THE REAL TREE WAS NEVER WRITTEN TO. Four preconditions before anything is scored: tripwire (8 excluded, never read the target), baseline via `git log --all` version search (4 excluded, no state where it fires), determinism, and whole-fix application cross-verified two ways (262 of 263 carry exactly one block by both counts). QUEUE RE-ORDERED. 1: feed the in-runner control, which already exists with 8 outcomes and 3 self-probes and is presence-gated on a corrected copy no panel has ever been asked for. 2: re-grade the archive, 132 demonstrated / 131 asserted -- this IS Codex's typed-provenance work and the data now exists. 3: the 67 NO_APPLICABLE_FIX and 30 INDETERMINATE_ERROR, a quarter of the population that could not be scored at all. NO LIVE RUN UNTIL ITEM 1 LANDS. Suite 3593 passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed offline, netguard strict. title: The decision inventory: nine rulings pending, seven items needing no ruling, six struck off.
verbatim: The decision inventory: nine rulings pending, seven items needing no ruling, six struck off. Everything is on hold until the nine are answered. The founder asked for the full inventory in terms they can adjudicate, so this triages 72 hours of accumulated open items (and older ones still live) into three lists rather than presenting a pile. GENUINELY THEIRS (9). The discrimination gate -- block, label or retry, recommend retry-then-block because a filter that only subtracts converts a quality problem into a volume problem. Whether a finding reclassified as equipment error stops counting -- recommend UNRESOLVED, otherwise a run looks more converged the more its instruments fail. The similarity pairs -- 33 of 133 machine-settled both ways, 100 still need a human, recommend a stratified sample of 30 rather than all 100. The 0.7 critical threshold -- keep it and finally cite the frozen pre-registration from the live queue, which does not mention it. exp50/51 -- redesign before running, same TRUE/FALSE pairing that contaminated exp48/49. The load balancer -- retire. The survived-falsification ledger, verified not read by the runner -- withdraw the claim it exists. The exp46 pre-registration -- do not sign, it predates the result it must account for. .env quoting and the Zenodo rotation -- needs their hands, open 3 days. PROCEEDING ON ONE ASSUMPTION: the archive re-grade writes sidecars and modifies no archived report, per the 2026-07-29 standing rule that a fold-forward never alters a completed experiment's record. NEEDING NO RULING (7), to be done and reported: the instrument inventory; the 67 NO_APPLICABLE_FIX and 30 INDETERMINATE_ERROR; the ERROR-can-write-a-terminal-status fault; --dry-run on the perturbation control; moving the memory-ledger bump into the sv path after five consecutive manual corrections; measuring whether the shadow-described component leaves any trace; the docs sweep. STRUCK OFF (6), verified rather than assumed: the perturbation instrument (built and run 21 Aug); the file-access check (answered by last night's control); Write/Edit in panel dispatch (the route grants Bash/Read/Grep/Glob/WebFetch/WebSearch only); "the founding principle is unauditable" (withdrawn); the early-convergence alarm (refuted 17 Aug); the two faults in the old control document (clean target built 20 Aug). AFTER the nine: the instrument inventory FIRST -- ~17 components emit a number or a verdict and nobody has ever listed them or recorded which are commissioned. That is what converts an apparently endless defect stream into a finite burndown. Then the fix experiment. title: Founder rulings on the nine. Three changed shape, and one of my recommendations was reversed.
verbatim: Founder rulings on the nine. Three changed shape, and one of my recommendations was reversed. RULING 1 SUPERSEDES MY PROPOSAL, and the founder was right. I proposed designing a retry loop for falsifiers that fail the discrimination control. The mechanism already exists: _apply_routing (reference_runner_v2.py:3279) routes a failed critical up a ladder of progressively stronger writers, excluding the failed source model, with reverify_falsifier deciding, and HIL only after the ladder is exhausted. Only its TRIGGER needs changing -- it fires on escalated=True AND not CONFIRMED, and a falsifier that fails discrimination is CONFIRMED, so it never reaches the ladder today. One condition, not a new component. Also verified: routing_enabled is unset in every config and take_up_slack_enabled (the legacy alias, honoured by both ingestion paths) is set instead; two exp42 configs set NEITHER, so the ladder was off for those runs. RULING 7 REVERSES ME. I recommended withdrawing the claim that the survived-falsification ledger exists. The founder asked what it was, and reading it shows the recommendation was wrong: SurvivedFalsificationLedger in bench/evidence.py, built 2026-08-08 with a full test suite, records that a claim was TESTED AND STOOD. It closes the gap where a clean run of the zero-plant control produces an ABSENCE that is indistinguishable from a dispatch failure or a document nobody read. Verified not read by the runner. It should be WIRED. Small, tested, and it closes exactly the gap the founder's own scientific-method anchor cares about. RULING 3 IS RE-FRAMED BY THE FOUNDER AND THE RE-FRAMING IS BETTER. Tool-undecidable similarity pairs are irreducible HIL items and belong in the normal guarded queue, severity-filtered, arriving a few at a time. The request for a 30-pair sitting is withdrawn. The founder also correctly separated what the machine did (counterfactual repair TESTED them and settled 33 of 133) from what the panel did (argued about categorisation). RULING 6: SHELVE the load balancer, do not retire it, and mark it clearly -- avoid widening the error surface by deleting rather than quarantining. The founder flagged that it may be distinct from the routing ladder and was right: dynamic_management.py is not bench/routing.py. RULING 5: redesign exp50/51 AFTER the build experiment, with every fix it uncovers in place too. Later than I proposed and better sequenced. RULINGS 2 and 4 taken as stated: equipment error counts as unresolved and escalates to HIL; the 0.7 critical threshold stands. RULING 9 CLARIFIED: no signature and no publication is involved -- quote the values in .env, and revoke/reissue one Zenodo API token printed into an error on 19 August. RECORDED HONESTLY: both halves of the perturbation instrument are, as of this commit, exactly the "built but never wired" pattern the founder named. The null half is a standalone script that has never affected an experiment; the discrimination half is in the runner and has never fired once. What changed on 22 August is that the missing input was shown to already exist -- the finding's own proposed_fix, which applied cleanly to 367 of 437 archived findings. Nothing built, nothing run. Rulings recorded only. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: Phase 0: the instrument inventory. 34 components, and the inventory caught its own detector lying.
verbatim: Phase 0: the instrument inventory. 34 components, and the inventory caught its own detector lying. The founder's diagnosis, made concrete. Every defect found this week was found by a measurement nobody had run: each component was built, switched on, and used to produce results without a check that it did what it said. That is a FINITE backlog nobody had enumerated, not an endless problem. This is the enumeration. 34 instruments, not the "seventeen-ish" I estimated before counting. The inventory is bigger than the guess, which is the point of writing it down. IT CAUGHT ITS OWN DETECTOR IN THE HOUSE FAILURE MODE. The heuristic -- a test names the component AND carries both a positive and a negative assertion -- scored I14, THE FALSIFIER GATE, as commissioned. It is not: reverify_falsifier("print ('FALSIFIED')") returns CONFIRMED, measured last night. It also scored I33, the survived-falsification ledger, as commissioned; it has a full test suite and nothing calls it. A tested component nothing calls is shelved, not commissioned. So direct measurements now OVERRIDE the heuristic, and the script reports the heuristic's own error rate against them rather than leaving a reader to find it: 5 rows measured, 3 disagreements, 2 in the CONFIDENT direction (I14, I33) and 1 in the cautious direction (I34, an offline instrument with no test naming it). The 27 remaining "yes" rows are UNVERIFIED, not reassurance, and the file says so. An earlier draft of the calibration line claimed EVERY disagreement was in the confident direction. That was false -- I34 disagrees the other way -- and it is corrected rather than left standing. Same shape as the week's other overstatements. ALSO FIXED: the flag reader checked routing_enabled only, which is unset in every config because they set the legacy alias take_up_slack_enabled. Reading both, the routing ladder is on in 17 of 19 configs; the two earliest exp42 configs set neither, so the ladder was off for those runs. Founder ruling 2026-08-22 stands: the panel confirms or refutes each row with tools in phase 2. This is a first pass, not a verdict, and is labelled as one. cy log: bench/logs/build_experiment_2026-08-22/CY_LIVE.log Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: The build experiment's acceptance gate, commissioned before use. 8 of 8.
verbatim: The build experiment's acceptance gate, commissioned before use. 8 of 8. THIS IS THE ANSWER TO THE FOUNDER'S BOOTSTRAP QUESTION, IN CODE. They asked how a broken instrument can be used to repair itself. It cannot, and this is not the same instrument: the falsifier gate accepts a falsifier IF IT FIRES, which is ONE-SIDED and is why reverify_falsifier("print('FALSIFIED')") returns CONFIRMED. This gate requires the model's test to FAIL AT THE PARENT, PASS WITH THE PATCH, and leave the FULL SUITE GREEN. Two-sided, plus a third constraint the model does not control. A test that always fails cannot pass step 2; a test that always passes cannot pass step 1. The fail-before/pass-after requirement IS the discrimination control, present at construction rather than bolted on. title: The gate's own step 3 assumed a green suite instead of measuring it. Caught on the first candidate, fixed, and P-passed.
verbatim: The gate's own step 3 assumed a green suite instead of measuring it. Caught on the first candidate, fixed, and P-passed. THE DEFECT WAS MINE AND IT WAS IN THE INSTRUMENT BUILT TO END THIS EXACT FAILURE. The build experiment's first dispatch returned a valid patch from Codex for T07. Steps 1 and 2 judged it correctly -- 2 failed at the parent, 2 passed with the patch. Step 3 rejected it as REJECTED_SUITE_WENT_RED. MEASURED, no patch applied at all: bench/tests/test_falsifier_cannot_read_the_key.py passes in the repo working tree (35 passed) and FAILS in a bare worktree at the same commit. It scans "the whole tracked archive" and bench/logs is gitignored, so a fresh worktree has no archive for it to scan. Full suite in a bare worktree: 1 failed, 3602 passed, with nothing patched. FOLLOW. Every one of the eleven tasks would have been falsely rejected at step 3. The experiment would have reported near-0% acceptance, and near-0% is this harness's OWN pre-registered tell for "the models cannot do the task". A harness artefact would have rendered as a confident verdict about six models' competence. The run was stopped after one metered dispatch. FIX. Step 3 is now TWO-SIDED like steps 1 and 2: suite_baseline() measures which tests already fail at the parent in a worktree, and only failures the parent does not have are blamed on the patch. Cached per parent, so it costs one extra suite run for the whole experiment rather than one per candidate. Also dropped -x, which stops at the first failure and therefore cannot see the full failing set to compare. Green-at-parent was an assumption, and refusing assumptions is the entire design of this gate. P-PASS, the only test that counts: Codex's T07 patch re-evaluated through the corrected gate is ACCEPTED -- test fails at parent, passes with the patch, and the one remaining suite failure is the parent's own. SO THE FIRST MODEL OUTPUT THIS HARNESS EVER JUDGED WAS JUDGED WRONGLY, BY ME, IN THE CONFIDENT DIRECTION. Codex's work was valid and the instrument was broken. Recorded rather than quietly corrected. Commissioning 8 tests -> 10, pinning both sides: a pre-existing parent failure must NOT be blamed on a patch, and a genuinely new failure must still be rejected. Two fixture bugs of mine were caught by those tests before they shipped. ALSO BUILT: bench/build_experiment_tools.py, five read-only repository tools (read_file, grep, list_dir, run_pytest, run_python) with path-escape refused. The existing openrouter_tools.py offers sympy/z3/pytest/ruff/mypy and NO WAY TO READ A FILE, so the four metered models could run a checker and not see the source it checked. The tool loop fired for the first time in this project's history on that first dispatch: 45.6s, 10,789 chars. Suite 3605 passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed offline, netguard strict. title: Rung 1 was never a fair test: the tool budget could not reach the file, and I reintroduced the DeepSeek bug this repo documented four days ago.
verbatim: Rung 1 was never a fair test: the tool budget could not reach the file, and I reintroduced the DeepSeek bug this repo documented four days ago. MEASURED, not inferred. Every metered model failed at rung 1, and not for lack of ability. Two causes, both mine. CAUSE 1 -- THE TOOL BUDGET CANNOT COVER THE FILE. bench/reference_runner_v2.py is 10,510 lines and 527,304 characters; read_file caps at 24,000, so reading it whole takes 22 calls. max_tool_iters was 8. ChatGPT stated the problem in plain English and I had no measurement until now: "The tool budget was cut off before those parts of bench/reference_runner_v2.py were available." Response sizes make it unmistakable -- free models 15,507 to 51,063 bytes of substantive work, metered models 378 to 10,799 bytes truncated mid-investigation. CAUSE 2 -- I SHIPPED A BUG THIS PROJECT FOUND AND WROTE DOWN ON 2026-08-19. DeepSeek has no tool loop on its API route. My SYSTEM prompt said "USE YOUR TOOLS", so it hallucinated a <tool_calls> block and returned 215 chars in 3.4s. That is verbatim the failure recorded in bench/confer_enforcement_ds_retry.py, with the fix written beside it. I sent one SYSTEM prompt to every route and reintroduced it. FOLLOW, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: these results CANNOT be read as a comparison of model ability. Rung 1 was not a fair test, so any per-model ranking drawn from this run would be an artefact of my configuration, not a property of the models. The free models at rungs 2 and 3 carried the run. FIX. max_tool_iters 8 -> 30, with an explicit instruction to grep FIRST and read only the located region rather than paging a half-million-character file. DeepSeek gets the no-tools SYSTEM variant that already existed in this repo. And a response that is predominantly a tool-call block is now recorded as CONFIG_ERROR_TOOLCALL_ BLOCK -- a configuration failure and a model failure must never render alike, which is this project's single most repeated lesson. STATE AT PAUSE: T01 HIL, T02/T03/T05 accepted from cc2, T04 accepted from fable, T06-T11 not yet attempted. Accepted patches are recorded but NOT yet applied; they were each validated against the parent independently, so they still need a composition check before anything is claimed about them together. title: A model wrote to the repository and my `git add -A` committed it. Reverted, quarantined, and the hole closed.
verbatim: A model wrote to the repository and my `git add -A` committed it. Reverted, quarantined, and the hole closed. WHAT HAPPENED. T01 rung 1 returned REJECTED_PATCH_DID_NOT_APPLY. The SEARCH block could not match because bench/reference_runner_v2.py ALREADY CONTAINED a T01 fix, carrying the comment "T01 (founder ruling 2026-08-22): NON_DISCRIMINATING joins ERROR". I never applied it. `git log -S` names commit 902bcde -- my own harness-fix commit, which carries 14 changed lines in the runner and a NEW 143-line test file, neither of them mine. A model working T01 at rung 2 or 3 edited the working tree directly instead of returning a patch, and my blanket `git add -A` swept it in. FIVE HARMS, NONE OF THEM THE MODEL'S FAULT: 1. feedback_fixes_hil_only violated -- a fix reached the repo with no HIL sight. 2. The commit message is false: it describes three harness fixes and silently carries 157 lines of unrelated model-written code. 3. The gate was bypassed. That code never faced fail-before/pass-after and sat in the tree UNVALIDATED -- the exact category this experiment exists to end. 4. It poisoned the parent. Every dispatch after 20:53 patched against a tree already containing a partial T01 fix, so cx's "SEARCH block does not match" is an artefact of MY contamination, not a failure by cx. 5. I told the founder "accepted patches go to a branch, not to main". An UNACCEPTED patch went straight into a commit instead. ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS A HOLE IN AN EXISTING RULING. On 2026-07-29 this project ruled: "Remove Write/Edit from panel dispatch -- restores feedback_fixes_hil_only, makes 'frozen target' true." I verified that ruling DONE earlier today by checking --allowedTools and finding no Write and no Edit. It grants Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch -- and BASH IS A SUPERSET OF WRITE. The inline comment beside that list reads "No file modification", which is false. The ruling was implemented incompletely and the "frozen target" guarantee has been untrue in every Claude-CLI panel dispatch this project has run since. THE FIX ALREADY EXISTED AND HAD NEVER BEEN CALLED. set_panel_cwd() sits in experiment_11_orchestrator.py for precisely this, and its own docstring says "failing open here would put the panel back in the repo, which is the exposure this exists to close." No dispatch in this project has ever called it. Claude-CLI dispatches now run inside a throwaway git worktree at the commit under test: reads work, tests run, and writes cannot reach the repository. Restored in a finally and the worktree removed either way. REMEDIATION. The model's runner diff and its 143-line test are quarantined intact at bench/logs/build_experiment_2026-08-22/QUARANTINE_T01_model_written/ -- the work may well be good and will be put through the gate as a candidate, on its merits, rather than left in the tree as a fait accompli. The runner is restored to ec95acb and the test file removed. RUN STOPPED at T01 of the resume. Accepted so far: T02, T03, T05 (cc2), T04 (fable), T07 (cx). T01 remains HIL. title: It happened twice, and the second time was while I was writing up the first. `git add -A` is the defect.
verbatim: It happened twice, and the second time was while I was writing up the first. `git add -A` is the defect. SECOND CONTAMINATION. While I was diagnosing the first model write, the resumed run's T01 rung-2 dispatch wrote to the tree AGAIN, and my second `git add -A` committed it again: commit 98ddede carries bench/reference_runner_v2.py +27 lines and a NEW 201-line bench/tests/test_disc_failure_reaches_the_ladder.py, neither of them mine. Two tests went red as a result. Both writes are quarantined intact under bench/logs/build_experiment_2026-08-22/QUARANTINE_T01_model_written/ and the runner is restored byte-identical to ec95acb (git diff = 0 lines). Nothing is discarded: the model's work may well be good and will face the gate as a candidate rather than sit in the tree as a fait accompli. MY DEFECT IS `git add -A`, NOT THE MODEL'S BEHAVIOUR. Naming what the model did is not a fix. The fix is that I must never stage a wildcard while a dispatch can write to the tree. This commit stages explicit paths only, and that is the rule going forward. THE SANDBOX IS IN PLACE for future dispatches: Claude-CLI routes now run inside a throwaway git worktree via set_panel_cwd(), which has existed in this repo for exactly this purpose and had never been called by any dispatch in the project's history. A GUARD CAUGHT ME AND IT WAS RIGHT. Two response files went red under test_sim_naming_and_integrity_directive.py. CC2's answers legitimately contain SIM-A / SIM-B fixtures -- this project's own simulated-agent convention -- which makes the FILE structurally self-declare as a simulated artefact, and a bare vendor name in such a file's path is a provenance failure under the 2026-08-08 ruling. Two renames were needed before it was right: adding "-LIVE" did not help because the guard matches the TOKEN, not the phrase. Response files are now T<id>_rung<N>_response.md with model identity in RESPONSE_MODEL_INDEX.json and results.json, which is better provenance than a filename. THE GUARD WAS NOT WEAKENED. Its own docstring warns that the repair for a red guard is never an exclusion list, because that produces a dead guard. The artefact was renamed instead. Suite green. Run remains stopped; T06, T08-T11 not yet attempted. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: read_file's line-number prefix made a verbatim SEARCH block impossible. Third harness defect tonight, third false verdict about a model's work.
verbatim: read_file's line-number prefix made a verbatim SEARCH block impossible. Third harness defect tonight, third false verdict about a model's work. FIND. T01 rung 1 was rejected as REJECTED_PATCH_DID_NOT_APPLY against a tree I had verified byte-identical to ec95acb. The tree was clean and the rejection still happened, so the cause was not contamination this time. MEASURED. Codex's SEARCH block matches the file EXACTLY after removing two leading spaces from every line. read_file returned f"{i:>6} {line}" -- a 6-character number plus two spaces, an 8-character prefix. The model stripped the DIGITS and kept the two-space separator, so every line it sent carried +2 indentation and could never match. Its Python was correct. The formatting trap was mine. FOLLOW. This poisons every task in which a model reads source and returns a patch, which is every task. It renders as REJECTED_PATCH_DID_NOT_APPLY -- a MODEL failure -- when it is a HARNESS failure. That is the third time tonight my own instrument produced a confident wrong verdict about someone else's work: 1. step 3 assumed a green suite instead of measuring it 2. git add -A committed a model's direct writes and poisoned the parent 3. read_file's prefix made a verbatim SEARCH block impossible FIX THE READER, NOT THE MATCHER. read_file now returns RAW text by default, so what a model copies is exactly what is in the file; line numbers are opt-in via numbered=true for citing a location. Loosening the SEARCH matcher instead would let a patch land somewhere it was never meant to, which is a far worse failure than a rejection. The system prompt now says so explicitly. PINNED. bench/tests/test_build_experiment_tools.py, 6 tests: default output is verbatim, numbered output is opt-in and distinguishable, a slice round-trips, paths cannot escape the repository, and no tool in the module can write. ALSO ADDED: scripts/build_experiment_compose.py. The gate validates each candidate INDEPENDENTLY against the same parent, which is the right unit for judging one model's work and says nothing about the set. "Each part was verified therefore the whole is verified" is a composition fallacy this project has shipped before, so the accepted set is proved separately -- applied in order, conflicts recorded rather than dropped, all accepted tests run together, and the full suite compared against the parent's own failing set rather than an assumption of green. Suite 3605 -> 3613 passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed offline. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: Build experiment results: nine of ten defects fixed by the panel, and five defects found in the instrument that judged them.
verbatim: Build experiment results: nine of ten defects fixed by the panel, and five defects found in the instrument that judged them. NINE OF TEN PATCH TASKS ACCEPTED, one escalated to HIL. Acceptance was mechanical and no model or assistant adjudicated it: the model's test must FAIL at the parent, PASS with its patch, and leave the full suite green relative to the parent's own failing set. T07's acceptance came from manual re-evaluation after the step-3 repair rather than the live loop, so both figures are given: 8/9 = 88.9% exact 95% CI [51.8, 99.7], or 9/10 = 90.0% CI [55.5, 99.7]. THE PRE-REGISTERED TELL, HONOURED WHERE IT DOES NOT FLATTER THE RUN. "The models cannot do the task" is decisively rejected, p ~ 1e-16. "The checks are not binding" is NOT rejected at conventional significance: p = 0.087 and 0.096. So the acceptance rate ALONE does not rule out a near-vacuous gate, and that is stated plainly rather than buried. What establishes the checks bite is independent of the rate: the gate was commissioned before use with 10 tests and demonstrably refuses a vacuous test, an always-failing test, a non-matching patch, a testless patch, prose, and a suite regression -- and 8 in-run attempts were genuinely rejected, with T01 rejected by three independent writers. THE COMPOSITION CHECK CAUGHT WHAT IT WAS BUILT FOR. Six of eight compose cleanly; T04 and T05 conflict because four patches touch the same 10,510-line file and their SEARCH blocks no longer match once T02 and T03 land. The six that apply give 56 accepted tests passing together and 3,668 suite passes with ZERO failures the parent does not already have. T04 and T05 are not wrong -- they need rebasing, which is integration work, not a model defect. Skipping this step would have deferred the discovery to the branch. FIVE DEFECTS IN MY OWN HARNESS, EACH RENDERING A HARNESS FAILURE AS A MODEL FAILURE: step 3 assumed a green suite (ec95acb); `git add -A` committed a model's direct writes twice and poisoned the parent (386c8d4); read_file's line-number prefix made a verbatim SEARCH block impossible (36ab4e3); a collection error is labelled as a failed fix (logged, not yet fixed, cannot cause a false ACCEPT); results.json is clobbered by every resume (worked around by rebuilding from the append-only log). 5 of 25 attempts were decided by one of these rather than by the model's work, so NO per-model ranking is offered. THE FROZEN-TARGET HOLE. The 2026-07-29 ruling "remove Write/Edit from panel dispatch" was verified DONE by checking --allowedTools for Write and Edit. It grants Bash, and BASH IS A SUPERSET OF WRITE; the comment beside it reads "No file modification", which is false. set_panel_cwd() existed for exactly this and had never been called by any dispatch in this project's history. Closed for this harness and VERIFIED BY TEST -- a simulated model write lands in the sandbox and does not reach the repo. EVERY OTHER PANEL DISPATCH IN THIS PROJECT STILL RUNS WITH BASH IN THE REPOSITORY. ROUND-ROBIN DEMONSTRATED THE FOUNDER'S OBJECTION. T09 asks a model to edit a document; round-robin handed it to DeepSeek, the one route with no tool loop, which cannot read the file it was asked to edit. A configuration mismatch, not a model failure. bench/routing.py already implements capability-aware routing, is runner-agnostic by design, carries an empirical ordering, and says in its own docstring that it exists to replace the flat dispatch I hand-rolled instead. TWO MORE GUARDS CAUGHT ME AND BOTH WERE RIGHT, NEITHER WAS WEAKENED. quarantine_to_candidate.py could never emit "unrecognized arguments" because argparse reports missing positionals first -- fixed with nargs="?" and explicit validation, so a retired flag fails loudly rather than being silently accepted. And results.json ingested quoted pytest output containing SIM-A / SIM-E / simulated_bench from TEST NAMES, which made it self-declare as a simulated artefact and put its bare vendor tags in violation of the 2026-08-08 ruling; it now records rung and route, with vendor identity one hop away in RESPONSE_MODEL_INDEX.json. WHAT ACTUALLY GOT FIXED. T02 matters most: the discrimination control has sat in the runner with eight outcomes and three self-probes and HAD NEVER FIRED ONCE, because it waits on a corrected copy nothing supplied. It is now fed from each finding's own proposed fix. T03 wires the survived-falsification ledger. T04 stops a crashed falsifier writing a terminal verdict. T05 gives the Bugzilla design its status vocabulary and machine-readable catalogue, which had zero lines before tonight. NOTHING IS MERGED. Accepted patches remain candidates; fixes-HIL-only stands. Suite 3615 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed offline, netguard strict. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'fr' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The panel has never once recorded two models finding the same thing, and four convergence deciders have never been tested.
verbatim: The panel has never once recorded two models finding the same thing, and four convergence deciders have never been tested. THE FOUNDER'S QUESTION, PUT TO THE ARCHIVE INSTEAD OF ARGUED. What does a six-model panel working IN TURN buy over one capable model? The 22 August build experiment used a serial ladder and could not answer it. v2's star dispatch puts every model on the same target in the same round, so the archive can. CO-DISCOVERY HAS NEVER BEEN RECORDED. source_aliases records every model that raised a finding before dedup collapsed them. Across exp42-49: 566 findings, 566 total aliases, exactly 1.00 per finding, and ZERO findings raised by two or more models. That is not remarkable diversity; it is the aliasing mechanism never firing, already known as runway 1.6 ("the alias map is a bijection in all 28 registries"). THE CONSEQUENCE: the project cannot currently measure whether its models find different things, so the central claim for running a multi-model panel has no measurement behind it in its own archive. CROSS-EXAMINATION, the weaker signal: 299 of 566 (52.8%) carry any verdict; 156 (27.6%) are judged by a model other than their source; 410 (72.4%) are raised by one model and never examined by another. TWO READINGS AND THE DATA CANNOT SEPARATE THEM -- either the panel cross-examines only a quarter of the time, or the recording is as under-populated as the aliasing. This note refuses to choose. Same shape as the 22 August discrimination finding: the mechanism may work and the record cannot show it. WHAT THE STAR DOES THAT THE LADDER CANNOT, verified in code: the star branch injects rho, its 3-round rolling average, gamma and the registry counts INTO EVERY MODEL'S PROMPT EVERY ROUND -- "models use gamma, rho, registry state to calibrate effort". The maths model is a feedback signal to the panel, not bookkeeping. A serial ladder has no rounds, no registry state and nothing to calibrate against. RHO, PRECISELY. rho is discovery efficiency: what fraction of a round's raw findings were genuinely new. It is COMPUTED EVERY ROUND AND SHOWN TO THE PANEL. Only the CHURN VERDICT is gated, on rho_earliest_round = 12, a constant the code itself says has "no derivation on record" against a rolling window of 3. Saying "rho does not work" would be false; the detector built on top of it is what cannot fire. A CORRECTION TO THE RUNWAY, APPLIED WHERE IT STANDS. Row 1.8 said "of exp44-49 only exp44 (13 rounds) reaches R12". Re-measured: exp44 (13) AND exp47 (14) both reach it, so 2 of 6, and 5 of 11 across exp42-49. At the derived floor of 2 x window = 6, 9 of 11 would qualify. The row predates exp47's round reconstruction on 2026-08-20, so it was stale rather than wrong. THE INVENTORY SWEEP. Six of 34 instruments cannot affect a live run today: the discrimination control (presence-gated, fed by nothing until T02 merges), fix complexity (shadow), the load balancer (shelved), shadow stage-6, the survived-falsification ledger (NOT WIRED), and the null-perturbation control (offline script). SEVEN HAVE NO COMMISSIONING EVIDENCE AT ALL, and FOUR OF THEM ARE CONVERGENCE DECIDERS -- the things that end a run: I02 THE TWO-SIDED GAMMA GATE, which the founder holds as a standing directive that GAMMA IS LOAD-BEARING; I04 state-convergence; I07 stall convergence; I08 budget extension. None has ever been shown to answer differently on a known-good and a known-bad input. That is not a claim they are wrong -- it is the exact position the falsifier gate was in before it was tested on 22 August and found to accept print('FALSIFIED') as a confirmation. T01, AND WHY ITS FAILURE MATTERS FOR THE NEXT RUN. It asks for discrimination failures to reach the escalation ladder. The ladder fires on escalated AND not CONFIRMED; a falsifier that FAILS discrimination is CONFIRMED because it fired, so it never arrives. Three independent writers produced patches that applied and failed their own tests. Merging the six composable patches therefore wires the discrimination control and leaves its failures unable to reach the ladder. THAT IS A HALF-REPAIR AND MUST BE STATED AS ONE. Suite green offline under netguard-strict. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: CORRECTION: co-discovery DOES happen. 21 confirmed instances, recorded nowhere the registry can see.
verbatim: CORRECTION: co-discovery DOES happen. 21 confirmed instances, recorded nowhere the registry can see. WITHDRAWN, hours after writing it: "the project cannot currently measure whether its models find different things." That asserted a universal after checking ONE field -- source_aliases -- which is the exact error shape recorded in feedback_check_the_whole_set. MEASURED. The 133 similarity pairs adjudicated by counterfactual repair, cross- referenced against the model that raised each finding: 106 of 133 pairs were raised by DIFFERENT models 27 by the same model 21 cross-model pairs were called SAME IN BOTH DIRECTIONS by the tool Those 21 ARE co-discovery: two models independently raising one defect, confirmed by a tool rather than a vote, sitting in the archive as two unlinked canonical entries. THE CORRECTED FINDING IS NARROWER AND MORE USEFUL. The REGISTRY cannot record co-discovery: source_aliases is written once at creation (:1057) and NO CODE ANYWHERE APPENDS TO IT; _alias_map gains an entry only when a NEW canonical is minted (:1053). Verified on exp44: 82 map entries for 82 findings, 0 canonical IDs with more than one alias. There is no mechanism, not a mechanism that fails to fire. But the SIMILARITY AND DEDUP ANALYSIS does capture it and found at least 21 instances. The RATE is unknown and the archive systematically UNDER-REPRESENTS agreement, because only pairs inside the similarity function's candidate band were ever adjudicated. 21 is a floor, not an estimate. The practical consequence is unchanged and better supported: the fix is AN APPEND AT THE DEDUP SITE, so a finding recognised as another model's defect adds its id to source_aliases rather than minting an unlinked twin. It converts a quantity the project currently recovers by expensive after-the-fact adjudication into something the registry records for free. Corrected in the note, the plain-English companion and the Desktop TTS before the founder read any of them. title: CORRECTION: budget extension HAS fired -- five times. My "never, not once" was a scope error.
verbatim: CORRECTION: budget extension HAS fired -- five times. My "never, not once" was a scope error. I told the founder in conversation that budget extension "has never fired, not once". WRONG, and wrong the same way as twice before this week: I scoped the measurement to exp42-49 and asserted a universal. MEASURED ACROSS THE WHOLE ARCHIVE. It fired FIVE times, all April 2026: exp33 24 rounds vs budget 21 (+3) no convergence exp34 24 rounds vs budget 21 (+3) no convergence exp35 23 rounds vs budget 21 (+2) converged at 22, reason EXTENSION_STALLED exp36 45 rounds vs budget 21 (+24) STATE_CONVERGED at round 45 exp38 24 rounds vs budget 21 (+3) no convergence ONE CLEAN SUCCESS IN FIVE, at a cost of 45 rounds against a budget of 21. The founder's recollection -- that it rarely worked -- is exactly right and is now quantified: three of five produced no convergence at all, one stalled after extending. AND exp36's success used consecutive_required = 2. The rule became 3 CONSECUTIVE PASSES AT exp41 and has been 3 ever since, so the single success this component can claim was under a WEAKER convergence criterion than the current one. Codex inherited my error and its patch defends a state the runner cannot produce; CC2 and Fable both checked and said so. "THREE WRITERS FAILED" IS WITHDRAWN. THERE WERE NO FAILURES. parse_test (build_acceptance.py:92) matches ```(?:python)?\n(.*?)``` non-greedily with no line anchor. Every T01 test embeds a ```python fence inside a string literal -- because a fence is what the code under test parses. VERIFIED with the harness's own extractor: 1403 / 5390 / 2853 chars extracted, all three SyntaxError "unterminated string literal". With correct extraction both reviewers re-ran all three: every patch applied and every writer's own test passed. FOURTH HARNESS DEFECT, THREE MORE FALSE VERDICTS ABOUT MODELS' WORK. FIFTH DEFECT, Fable's, and it invalidates part of my composition report: the composer breaks on a failed hunk WITHOUT REVERTING the hunks already written. VERIFIED -- no rollback/restore/revert anywhere in the apply loop. So T04's partial application poisoned T05's match, and the T05 conflict I reported was MANUFACTURED BY MY OWN COMPOSER. On a clean T02+T03 tree Fable measures T05 matching 14/14. TWO MORE, CC2's, both verified by reading: build_acceptance accepts ANY non-zero pytest exit as "fails at parent", but 2 is a collection error and 5 is nothing collected -- neither is a failing test, so step 1 cannot tell a broken test from a demonstrating one. And src.replace(search, replace, 1) has no uniqueness check, so a SEARCH block matching twice silently patches the first occurrence. Q2: no pair is exclusive, confirmed by both. THEY DISAGREE ON ORDER and the disagreement is preserved: CC2 says T02->T03->T04->T05, Fable says T02->T03->T05->T04 on the grounds that rebasing T04's 5 hunks onto T05's 14 is the smaller job. Both name the same two non-mechanical decisions in the merge. Q3: I WAS WRONG AND MY rg WAS INCOMPLETE. I searched docs/, resources/, experimental_notes/ and .claude/ and never searched bench/directives/universal/, where the FORMAL SPEC lives. cdsfl_core_formal.md:359 reads "Default to the simplest sufficient solution. Justified complexity is complexity the user cannot do without." §10 at :275 is Sufficiency Assessment with a formal predicate at :310; :303 forbids marginal observations as material findings; :372 is Objective and Diminishing Returns. CC2 further identifies nu <= nu* in the appendix as exactly the founder's "two sides of one coin", and the real gap as nu's input being a CONSTANT (nu_b=0.05, nu_f=0.20) with bench/dm/_fix_complexity.py built, tested and having zero non-test callers.
