title: Four more harness defects, found by the panel, fixed and commissioned. Three of my verdicts on models' work were false.
verbatim: Four more harness defects, found by the panel, fixed and commissioned. Three of my verdicts on models' work were false. DEFECT 4 -- THE FENCE. parse_test matched the closing fence non-greedily with NO line anchor, so it stopped at the first ``` ANYWHERE, including one inside a Python string literal. Every T01 test embeds a ```python fence BECAUSE A FENCE IS WHAT THE CODE UNDER TEST PARSES. VERIFIED with the harness's own extractor: 1403 / 5390 / 2853 chars, all three SyntaxError "unterminated string literal". The harness then reported REJECTED_TEST_STILL_FAILS_WITH_PATCH on three sound patches. After the fix: 2069 / 14917 / 9925 chars, all three COMPILE. Found independently by CC2 and Fable. DEFECT 5 -- THE COMPOSER (Fable). It broke on a failed hunk WITHOUT REVERTING the hunks already written, so a half-applied patch stayed in the tree and the NEXT patch was matched against it. VERIFIED: no rollback/restore/revert anywhere in the apply loop. THE T05 CONFLICT I REPORTED ON 2026-08-22 WAS MANUFACTURED BY MY OWN COMPOSER -- it was matched against a half-applied T04, not against T02/T03 as the report said. On a clean tree Fable measures T05 matching 14/14. Now snapshots each file before the first hunk and reverts the whole patch on any failure. DEFECT 6 -- THE EXIT CODE (CC2), AND MY FIRST FIX FOR IT WAS WRONG. The gate accepted ANY non-zero pytest exit as "fails at parent", but 2 is a collection error and 5 is nothing collected. My first repair refused 2 outright -- and the commissioning suite immediately caught it REJECTING THE KNOWN-GOOD CASE, because a test for a NEW SYMBOL legitimately fails to import at the parent and that IS the demonstration. The correct rule, now implemented: 3/4/5 are harness errors; 2 is allowed at step 1 and caught at step 2 only when it errors IDENTICALLY on both sides, which discriminates nothing. That case gets its own outcome, REJECTED_TEST_DOES_NOT_COLLECT -- closing the labelling defect I logged during the run, because "the defect persists" and "the model's test does not import" must never render alike. DEFECT 7 -- AMBIGUOUS ANCHORS (CC2). src.replace(search, replace, 1) had no uniqueness check, so a SEARCH block matching twice silently patched the first occurrence, which may not be the site the model meant. Now refused with a message telling the model to widen the anchor. None of the eight accepted patches hit it and it was still live. COMMISSIONED: 10 tests -> 14, one per new branch, each driven with an input built to trigger it -- a fence inside a string literal, a test broken on both sides, an ambiguous anchor, and a partial-application rollback assertion. That is seven harness defects in two days, all mine, every one of them rendering a HARNESS failure as a MODEL failure. The panel found four of them in twenty minutes by running the code instead of reading the report. title: T04 rebased onto T01 and T03. The two patches turn out to be the same design, reached independently.
verbatim: T04 rebased onto T01 and T03. The two patches turn out to be the same design, reached independently. BOTH DISPUTED ORDERS GAVE THE IDENTICAL RESULT, so the disagreement was moot: 9 of 10 applied either way, T04 conflicting in both, zero new suite failures. FABLE WAS RIGHT that T05's earlier conflict was manufactured by my composer; with rollback it applies cleanly in both orders. CC2 WAS RIGHT that T04's is real -- and it is with T03, not T05, which is why reordering changed nothing. TWO REBASES, and the second is the interesting one. (a) Hunk 2 vs T03: T03 inserts _to_ledger(cid, e, "UNTOOLABLE") inside T04's anchor. The union keeps the ledger write AND widens the demotion from == "CONFIRMED" to in TERMINAL_STATUSES. Both reviewers described it. (b) Hunk 4 vs T01 -- WHICH NEITHER REVIEWER SAW, because T01 was in HIL when they composed. Both patches modify THE SAME LINE for the same reason: an equipment failure should reach the ladder. T01 widens "ERROR" to ("ERROR", "NON_DISCRIMINATING"); T04 generalises to a named frozenset {"ERROR", "UNTOOLABLE"}. The same design reached independently, so the union is T04's named set carrying T01's member -- which is also exactly what CC2 asked for in Q1: name the constant so the write site and the read site cannot drift on a bare literal. The comment keeps the distinction rather than flattening it: ERROR and UNTOOLABLE mean the instrument produced NO reading; NON_DISCRIMINATING means it produced a reading that does not depend on the target. PROVENANCE WITHOUT BREAKING A DELIBERATE RULE. bench/logs/** is gitignored because raw per-model responses live in a separate archive; force-adding the rebased candidate would break that rule for convenience. The full unified diff of my edit to Fable's patch is recorded instead in experimental_notes/T04_Rebase_Record_2026-08-23.md, which is tracked. TWO OF MY OWN ERRORS, both caught by assertions rather than shipped: a line-based edit commented out the T05 dict entry (KeyError), and I reported T04's sixth hunk as failing at parent by comparing a test-file hunk against the runner's source. Neither reached a verdict about anyone's work. All six T04 hunks now match exactly once against a T01+T02+T03 tree. title: v3: ten mechanically-validated patches applied to v2. The discrimination control fires for the first time in this project's life.
verbatim: v3: ten mechanically-validated patches applied to v2. The discrimination control fires for the first time in this project's life. v3 IS A DIRECT DERIVATION OF v2, NOT A REBUILD (founder instruction). The file keeps its name -- reference_runner_v2.py is imported by configs, tests and launchers, and renaming it would change the blast radius from ten patches to every import in the project for no gain. The version is a banner in the module docstring, and it reaches each run's report, which is where a reader needs it. NOTHING HERE RESTS ON ANYONE'S JUDGEMENT. Every patch was accepted by a gate that requires the patch's own test to FAIL at the parent, PASS with the patch, and leave the suite green against the parent's OWN failing set. No model vote and no assistant adjudication appears anywhere in that path. The set was then proved to compose: 10 of 10 applied in order, 141 accepted tests passing together, zero failures the parent does not already have. WHAT LANDED. T01 discrimination failures now reach the escalation ladder. T02 THE DISCRIMINATION CONTROL IS FED -- it had eight outcomes and three self-probes and had never fired once, because it waits on a corrected copy nothing supplied; it now derives one from each finding's own proposed fix. T03 the survived-falsification ledger is wired, so a clean control run produces a positive record rather than an absence indistinguishable from a dispatch failure. T04 an equipment failure can no longer write a terminal status (4 of 24 did, two writing REFUTED on a falsifier that never ran). T05 the Bugzilla vocabulary and machine-readable catalogue, with CORROBORATED making co-discovery visible and every status declaring who may assert it. T06 the load balancer shelved and marked. T07-T10 the smaller items. THREE REBASES, EACH RECORDED IN ITS OWN FILE WITH THE ORIGINAL UNTOUCHED. T04 onto T03's inserted ledger line. T05 onto T04's equipment guard, placed AFTER T05's authority substitution and made to FALL THROUGH rather than return -- CC2 caught that returning early would leave the one status write in the runner with no logged transition, inside a patch whose whole claim is that resolve is the single chokepoint. And T01's guard re-scoped: it asserted "the widening is exactly ERROR + NON_DISCRIMINATING, nothing else", which was true of T01 alone and became false when the founder's amendment to item 5 put UNTOOLABLE into routing on purpose. Its intent -- no widening beyond instrument faults -- is preserved against a verdict no task routes. THE TWO-SET SPLIT IS LOAD-BEARING AND MY FIRST MERGE GOT IT WRONG. EQUIPMENT_FAILURE_VERDICTS drives DEMOTION; ROUTABLE_INSTRUMENT_FAULTS drives ROUTING and additionally carries NON_DISCRIMINATING. I first collapsed them into one set, which turned discrimination BLOCKING on by the back door -- and blocking is default-off by founder ruling because the 2026-08-12 panel refuted the blocking design as satisfiable by ACCESS rather than DEPENDENCE. Three tests caught me, including one written for exactly that purpose: "Blocking is a founder decision and stays default-off; the supply must not change that by the back door." z3 confirms the corrected design: with two sets a NON_DISCRIMINATING finding cannot be demoted while blocking is off, and the one-set collapse is unsatisfiable against that constraint. Suite 3760 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed offline under netguard-strict. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The three gaps: co-discovery recorded, spend recorded, 971 temp dirs stopped.
verbatim: The three gaps: co-discovery recorded, spend recorded, 971 temp dirs stopped. GAP 1 -- CO-DISCOVERY WAS NEVER RECORDED, AND THERE WAS NO MECHANISM TO RECORD IT. Measured across the modern arc: 566 findings, 566 source aliases, exactly 1.00 per finding, ZERO raised by two or more models. `_alias_map` is keyed `model_id:finding_id`, so `lookup_alias` can only ever match the SAME model re-raising its own finding across rounds -- never a different model raising the same defect. Two models finding one defect therefore minted two unlinked canonicals. The project HAS measured co-discovery, expensively and after the fact: of the 133 similarity pairs adjudicated by counterfactual repair, 106 were cross-model and 21 were called SAME in both directions by the tool. Those 21 are co-discovery the registry could not see. title: Exp 55: the v3 control, with its answer key split OUT of the target before anything ran.
verbatim: Exp 55: the v3 control, with its answer key split OUT of the target before anything ran. THE CONTROL HAD ITS OWN GROUND TRUTH INSIDE THE FILE THE PANEL WOULD READ. Section 3 of control_two_distinct_defects.md was headed "Ground truth, stated for the scorer only" -- inside a document the runner reads WHOLE and places in the panel prompt. Every model would have been handed the answers. That is the exposure class that removed exp48 and exp49 from every headline figure, and it was found by reading the target before the run rather than by explaining a result afterwards. Split into a panel-visible target (623 chars) and control_two_distinct_defects_KEY.md, which is never staged. The TITLE leaked too -- "Two Distinct Defects Sharing a Plausible Repair" gives away the count AND the relation the run exists to measure -- and is now a neutral technical heading. Swept for residual leaks: zero occurrences of control, ground truth, defect, distinct, or scorer in what the panel sees. THE KEY IS NOW VERIFIED, NOT TAKEN ON THE GENERATOR'S WORD. SymPy, symbolically: CT-01's stated criterion (f_s > f_max) and the real one (f_s > 2*f_max) are DIFFERENT expressions with a real counterexample region -- f_s=300, f_max=180 satisfies the stated rule and violates the criterion -- while at the document's own numbers the conclusion happens to hold, which is what makes it a REASONING defect with a TRUE conclusion and the hardest kind to catch. CT-02: df = 400/256 = 25/16 = 1.5625 Hz exactly, and 1.5625 > 1, so the inference fails on a true premise. The masking mechanism is real: N=1024 gives df=0.3906, making CT-02's conclusion true and rewriting the passage a CT-01 falsifier quotes. A FIRST VERSION OF THAT VERIFICATION HAD A TAUTOLOGICAL LINE -- it compared two booleans rather than two criteria, so it could not have failed. Corrected to compare the expressions symbolically before being relied on. PRE-REGISTRATION FROZEN IN THE CONFIG, five falsifiable predictions, the first being that THE DISCRIMINATION CONTROL FIRES AT LEAST ONCE -- it never has in this project's life. A silent zero on that, on CORROBORATED, or on the survival ledger means the corresponding patch did not take and must be reported as such rather than explained away. No tuning after results. Declared deltas from the Exp 46 instrument: prose target so sk_enabled=False (A2 forces it in code anyway); location keying OFF because it is AST-symbol based and prose has no symbols, so the count falls back to the settled series -- declared, not silent; external literature retrieval OFF, because a control whose value is that its inputs are known must not take an uncontrolled input. title: Exp 55 paused at round 0: prediction 1 was failing. The prose anchor fallback existed and was never wired.
verbatim: Exp 55 paused at round 0: prediction 1 was failing. The prose anchor fallback existed and was never wired. FOUND BY WATCHING THE RUN, NOT BY EXPLAINING A RESULT AFTERWARDS. Round 0 logged: corrected copies from proposed fixes: 0 derived, 10 DECLINED, of 10 findings discrimination control: no_control=4 Every decline gave the same reason -- "the original passage does not occur in the target verbatim". So T02, whose entire purpose is to feed the discrimination control, derived nothing on a prose target and the control did not fire. That is pre-registered prediction 1 failing, and the pre-registration says a silent zero there means the patch did not take and must be reported as such. PAUSED IMMEDIATELY rather than at the end of the run: every further round would spend metered dispatch on an instrument that cannot produce the measurement the run exists for. 11 dispatches had gone out. THE CAUSE IS NOT PARAPHRASE, AND THE FIX ALREADY EXISTED. _splice_corrected_copy matched anchors with target_text.count(original) -- exact only. Models strip markdown emphasis when they quote: the document says `**CT-01.**`, the model writes `CT-01.`. scripts/adjudicate_by_repair.py had already solved and MEASURED this in _apply_prose_fix / _md_normalise -- "median similarity between a SEARCH block and its true paragraph is 0.99 and the whole difference is markdown emphasis; normalising both sides took the locatable share from 14% to 80%" -- and it was never wired into the runner. Built, measured, never used: the week's refrain, one more time. THE FALLBACK KEEPS THE ORIGINAL PRECEDENCE AND REFUSES AMBIGUITY RATHER THAN GUESSING. A unique EXACT match still wins outright; only then is a unique NORMALISED paragraph match tried; two normalised matches refuse and say why. Restricted to non-.py targets, because on code exact is both correct and achievable and loosening it would let a patch land where it was never meant to -- a far worse failure than a decline. P-PASSED ON THE REAL TARGET: a bare quote of the marked-up CT-01 claim, which is exactly what the models wrote, now derives; the verbatim path still takes the exact route; a whitespace-differing quote against a .py target is still declined. FOUR COMMISSIONING TESTS, and one of them was MINE and wrong: the ambiguity case used one marked-up and one bare paragraph, which is exact-count 1, so the exact path correctly won and the fallback was never reached. Corrected to two marked-up paragraphs. The test was wrong, not the code. Suite green offline under netguard-strict. Run resumes from round 0 on a clean tree. title: The co-discovery wiring was in a function with no registry, and its NameError vanished into a handler. Caught live by the cy monitor.
verbatim: The co-discovery wiring was in a function with no registry, and its NameError vanished into a handler. Caught live by the cy monitor. MY BUG, MY GAP-1 WIRING, FOUND AT 15:31 ON THE ROUND-1 BOUNDARY: [feedback] build failed: NameError: name 'kwargs' is not defined I placed the call inside _build_feedback_for_next_round, which takes no `registry` and no `**kwargs`. `locals().get("registry") or kwargs.get("registry")` short- circuits into a name that does not exist, so it raised on EVERY round -- and that function's own defensive handler swallowed the exception and returned empty feedback. The ONLY visible symptom was the feedback channel silently going dark: the near-duplicate flag and prior-round findings stopped reaching the panel. A defect whose sole effect is the disappearance of a feature is the hardest kind to notice, and the cy monitor is what noticed it. FIXED by moving the recording to the round loop, where `registry` is genuinely in scope, and by making its failure path LOG rather than vanish. Two tests pin the placement and the loudness, because the behaviour cannot be asserted from outside and the placement can. TWO ARCHIVE GUARDS WENT RED, AND THEY WERE RIGHT TO. Both assert that NO archived finding carries a corrected copy -- written when no run had ever produced one, to show the wiring does not reach BACKWARDS into the record. Exp 55 is the first run WITH the feature, so it legitimately carries them: the feature working, not the rule reaching backwards. SCOPED, NOT WEAKENED. The exclusion is exp55-and-later, the same v3 boundary the runner's version banner sets -- a principled line, not "whatever happens to be failing". Each guard's claim and its denominator over pre-v3 runs are unchanged, and the reasoning is written into the docstring so a future reader can see the scope moved deliberately. AND I REPEATED A DEFECT I HAD JUST FIXED ELSEWHERE. My scoping edit used replace(x, y, 1) against an anchor that occurs twice in the file, so it landed in the WRONG TEST -- which is exactly the ambiguous-anchor defect CC2 found in the acceptance gate on 2026-08-23 and which I fixed there the same day. Corrected by anchoring at an offset inside the target function instead of by occurrence count. Suite 3779 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed offline under netguard-strict. title: Exp 55: the control halted at round 0, the alarm diagnosed itself correctly, and the relative-path fix it demanded is in.
verbatim: Exp 55: the control halted at round 0, the alarm diagnosed itself correctly, and the relative-path fix it demanded is in. THE RUN. First run of the v3 runner, on a target whose correctness is a property of its generator. HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM at round 0: six criticals locked as irreducible against a bound of two. 10 findings, 2 CONFIRMED, 8 UNCONFIRMED, gamma 0.000, 19 minutes. THE ALARM DIAGNOSED ITSELF AND WAS RIGHT: "overwhelmingly a MECHANICAL failure -- routing, dedup, or A GATE THAT CANNOT SPEAK TO THIS TARGET -- presenting as irreducibility." That is the same conclusion I reached independently by reading the round-0 falsifiers. It also refused the suppression in advance: "Do NOT raise max_irreducible_queue to clear this -- that is how the same alarm was suppressed twice on 2026-08-01 while it was right." AGAINST THE FIVE FROZEN PREDICTIONS. (1) MET IN LETTER: the discrimination control fired -- 2 records, the first in this project's history -- but both INDETERMINATE_NOT_INTERCEPTED, so it decided nothing. (2) MET: 5 findings cite CT-01 and 5 cite CT-02, including the hard case whose conclusion is TRUE. (3) NOT REACHED. (4) PARTIAL, and my own script's verdict of "MET" is corrected here: aliases reached 1.10, above 1.00 for the first time in 566+ findings, and one co-discovery record was written -- but it is Gemini with Gemini, a SAME-model duplicate, NOT cross-model co-discovery, and no CORROBORATED status was written. (5) NOT MET: zero falsifiers were REFUTED and the ledger records survivals only. THE FIX THE RUN DEMANDED. Every falsifier reaching CONFIRMED was uncontrollable for two reasons the control reported identically: relative-path readers the overlay could not redirect (ours) and detached falsifiers that never open the document (the model's, same class as Exp 48/49). execute_python and reverify_falsifier now take an optional cwd, defaulting to today's throwaway scratch dir so no existing call site changes, and the discrimination control passes the overlay root at all FIVE of its execution sites. P-passed: a relative-path falsifier goes from exists=False to reading the overlay's REPLACED target. A TEST I WROTE CAUGHT A REAL BUG IN THE FIX. reverify_falsifier still wrote its snippet into tmp_cwd, which is now the overlay -- a SYMLINK TREE, so a stray .py could have landed in the real repository. Both execution paths now write the snippet to the scratch dir and a test asserts it. AND I USED AN AMBIGUOUS replace(x, y, 1) ANCHOR FOR THE THIRD TIME TODAY, which is how that bug got in. Also corrected: an assertion that counted "cwd=str(" file-wide and guessed 5, when there are 7 -- two belong to unrelated pre-existing sandbox calls. Now scoped to the control's own function body. Measured, not guessed. RESIDUAL RISK, STATED NOT GLOSSED: the overlay is a symlink tree and the audit observer confines by path STRING, so a write to a relative path landing on a symlink inside the overlay would follow it into the real tree. No worse than the status quo, since absolute-path falsifiers are already retargeted into the same overlay -- but "no worse" is not "safe". Flagged for a founder ruling, not decided here. A results-currency guard also went red because Exp 55 had a report and no entry. It was right to. The entry is written, including the halt, the partial prediction 4 and the two unmet predictions. Suite 3783 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed offline under netguard-strict. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: Absolute paths only: the prompt was telling models to use the one path form the machinery cannot handle.
verbatim: Absolute paths only: the prompt was telling models to use the one path form the machinery cannot handle. FOUNDER RULING, 2026-08-23: "Models should never be fed just relative names. They should always be fed the full direct path and file name to the target under consideration... Leave nothing open to the models for either interpretation, or potential hallucination." THE DEFECT. Falsifiers execute in the sandbox's throwaway working directory, which is empty by design so a falsifier cannot write into the real tree. A falsifier told to open its target by a repo-relative name therefore resolved against an empty folder and died on FileNotFoundError; the gate recorded ERROR and routed the finding away. A DETACHED falsifier, one that opens nothing and restates the document's numbers from memory, does not care where it runs, executed cleanly, and was recorded CONFIRMED. The gate was selecting FOR the falsifiers that ignore the document, which is exactly the pathology the discrimination control exists to catch. Exp 55, measured, twice: 6 relative-path falsifiers ERRORed, the 2 detached ones CONFIRMED, six criticals locked irreducible against a bound of two, run halted at round 0. 1152 s and 1178 s of paid dispatch, both wasted. WHY THE FOUNDER'S FIX IS BETTER THAN THE PANEL'S. Both reviewers proposed populating a scratch working directory and overriding cwd. That compensates for the ambiguity; the ruling removes it. And _retarget_falsifier already redirects a falsifier into the control's overlay by substituting the ABSOLUTE repo root -- so relative was the one form NEITHER layer supported. The prompt was contradicting machinery that was already correct. Measured: absolute path takes the gate ERROR -> CONFIRMED and retarget_substitutions 0 -> 1, with no new code path and no cwd override. Model-facing prompts now name the full path at all five sites (round prompt, apply-back, sweep prose, sweep module, routing ladder) via _absolute_target. The internal canonical form stays relative: _build_discrimination_overlay requires it, and _fix_block_targets already matches a fix header by full path OR basename. THREE REPAIRS TO THE MECHANICAL ACCEPTANCE GATE, found by CC2 and Fable in a compelled-convergence review, the first two independently by both: A. failing_nodeids matched only ^FAILED, and rc_suite was assigned and never read. A pytest COLLECTION error emits no FAILED line, so a patch that broke every test in the repository read as an empty failure set and was ACCEPTED. Now ERROR lines count, and exits 2/3/4/5 -- and exit 1 with an unparseable failure set -- refuse. B. suite_baseline cached frozenset() on worktree-add failure or ANY exception. An empty baseline makes every pre-existing failure read as newly caused, rejecting every later candidate and driving acceptance towards zero, which this project pre-registered as the tell for "the models cannot do the task". Now returns None, is not cached, and all three callers refuse rather than judging. C. Model-supplied TEST_FILE and SEARCH paths were joined unvalidated, and pathlib discards the left operand on an absolute right operand, so a confused model could overwrite the live runner. _confine ports the guard the runner's overlay builder already had. 30 new tests, all executing rather than asserting on mocks (verified by timing). Suite 3813 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed. GLOSSARY: "mechanical acceptance gate" was the module's own first line and in project notes since 20 April, but never in the glossary, which is why the founder did not recognise the term. Added, and distinguished from the falsifier gate. Full unfiltered reviews preserved with file/line references intact. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: Three record-only instruments: the defect-rate curve, the competence-provenance check, and a vagueness linter that fails on its own motivating sentence.
verbatim: Three record-only instruments: the defect-rate curve, the competence-provenance check, and a vagueness linter that fails on its own motivating sentence. FOUNDER RULINGS, 2026-08-23/24. None of these changes any behaviour. All three record. 1. THE HARNESS-DEFECT CURVE (Fable's Q3 dissent, founder-authorised). "Demonstrably closer to iron-clad" needs defects-per-run over time and nothing tracked it. This is gamma one level up: gamma fits Duane NHPP to cumulative novel findings WITHIN a run; this fits the same model to harness defects ACROSS runs. The founder's picture (cumulative rising to an asymptote) and Fable's (rate bending down) are one curve from two sides -- neither was wrong, and the reconciliation is recorded in the script. The founder's further point: the same series could later feed the capability mechanics, since a falling defect rate is what licenses trusting the instrument's own competence figures. Not designed, not attempted, costless now. Seeded with 11 defects across 2 occasions. It REFUSES to compute gamma on 2 points and says why. Author: CC1 11 of 11. Rendered as model failure: 7 of 11. 2. COMPETENCE PROVENANCE (founder observation; NEITHER reviewer raised it). Measured competence is not a write-up statistic here -- routing.py orders the falsifier ladder by it, so a contaminated confirm rate re-orders which model resolves the hardest findings. VERIFIED SOUND TODAY: the order came from Exp 42, whose target was composer.py, and a code falsifier reaches its target by import, which PYTHONPATH carries regardless of working directory. H08 could not touch it. THE FORWARD HAZARD, MEASURED: re-deriving from Exp 55 gives Gemini 2/2 = FIRST and DeepSeek 0/2 = LAST -- ranking models by willingness to ignore the document, the exact inversion the discrimination control exists to detect. The check exits 2 and prints UNSAFE TO RANK ON; routing.py now carries the warning and names the check. 3. NOTE STANDARD v1.5 + A LINTER THAT FAILS ON THE OFFENDING SENTENCE. The founder: "you already said several times that you had fixed it". A rule restated and re-violated does not need restating. Rule 24: a quantity carries a NAME as the system names it, a DIRECTION, and a VALUE. Rule 25: never hard-wrap. scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py catches "debited the models' measured competence" and passes the rewrite that names falsifier-confirm rate, the direction, and 2-of-2 vs 0-of-2. Today's TTS went 12 findings -> 2 (one a direct source quote, one the sentence-boundary limit the standard documents). Report-only: a linter that blocks gets worked around. TWO REGRESSIONS I MADE WHILE WRITING IT, both pinned as tests: accepting spelled numbers (TTS spells them by standard) initially made it miss its own motivating sentence via "every ONE of them"; and a substring test matched "the measure" inside "the measurement". ALSO ANSWERED, and it corrects both reviewers and me: 10 of 11 prose configs already used ABSOLUTE target paths. The single relative one is 55_v3_control.json, which I created on 2026-08-23 in 28725d2. The models did not miss H08 for months -- it was unreachable until I made it reachable yesterday. CC2's "every prose target in the archive is affected" and "any archived ERROR verdict on a prose finding is suspect" are both overstated. Entrypoints conformed to the house `raise SystemExit(main())` form rather than widening the test that enforces it. Suite 3840 passed, 34 skipped, 0 failed. verbatim: sv: THE GATE WAS SELECTING FOR FALSIFIERS THAT NEVER READ THE DOCUMENT, and the founder's absolute-path ruling beat both reviewers' fix. Exp 55 halted at round 0 twice because the falsifier gate ran every falsifier in the sandbox's empty working directory: a falsifier that OPENED its target died on FileNotFoundError and was recorded ERROR, while a DETACHED falsifier that opens nothing and restates the document's numbers from memory ran cleanly and was recorded CONFIRMED. The gate was selecting FOR the exact pathology the discrimination control exists to catch. Six criticals then locked irreducible against a bound of two and the alarm halted the run, correctly, naming the layer itself: 'a gate that cannot speak to this target'. With the obstruction removed the control returns DISCRIMINATES, the verdict it was built for and had never once produced on a live run: CC2 produced it six times, Fable called its instance the first in the project's history. BOTH REVIEWERS PROPOSED POPULATING A SCRATCH DIRECTORY AND OVERRIDING cwd; THE FOUNDER RULED THAT MODELS MUST NEVER BE HANDED RELATIVE NAMES, AND THAT IS STRICTLY BETTER, because _retarget_falsifier already redirects into the control's overlay by substituting the ABSOLUTE repo root, so relative was the one form NEITHER layer supported. The prompt was contradicting machinery that was already correct. Measured: gate ERROR to CONFIRMED, retarget_substitutions 0 to 1, no new code path. THE DEFECT WAS ONE DAY OLD AND I INTRODUCED IT: 10 of 11 prose configs already used absolute paths, and the single relative one was 55_v3_control.json, written 2026-08-23, so CC2's 'every prose target in the archive is affected' is overstated. THREE OF MY CLAIMS WERE REFUTED IN REVIEW: retarget_substitutions==0 does not detect detachment (it counts absolute-root substitutions only; CC2 ran six counterexamples including linecache.getlines, which contains none of the usual file-opening words); '2 of 2, 100%' was arithmetically right and inferentially invalid, the sample being size two and selected by the very defect under investigation; and '7 of 34 instruments remain' was wrong by roughly four times in the reassuring direction, the true open count being 29 of 34 with the heuristic behind the other 27 wrong 3 times in 5, always over-claiming. RUNWAY 1.7 DELIVERED AS FAR AS THE ARCHIVE PERMITS: the exit test reproduces all 8 archived series exactly so the replay is a valid instrument, the delta half was a stub and is now built, and NO RUN CHANGES ITS CONVERGENCE ROUND under the repaired accounting. Not circular, because convergence_location.py changed after the last archived run, so exact reproduction measures behaviour-neutrality. One third of 1.7 is permanently unavailable: no archived report carries a rho series in any form. I ALSO REPEATED A WITHDRAWN ERROR INSIDE THAT WORK, comparing archived gamma_critical_history against a slope fitted to a different series, manufacturing a false 'exp47 converges at 11 instead of never'; the same error was withdrawn on 2026-08-22. THE THREE UNRUN ARTICLES WERE NEVER LOST and my report that they were is withdrawn: they recover from ddd74bde^ matching the MANIFEST's published hashes, and I had searched the staging names the configs point at rather than the names they were committed under. The real blocker on Stage 3 is the held-out ruling outstanding since 2026-08-08. TWO THINGS THAT MUST SURVIVE COMPACTION: exp39-experimental must NOT be deleted before the encrypted bundle is verified, because ddd74bde and eecdb0f are reachable from that branch and nothing else; and exp53 must NOT be dropped, because an instruction to drop it came from reading a question of mine as a recommendation, and exp53 is the zero-plant control measuring stopping-decision contamination while exp55 is a two-plant harness control. Also landed: three acceptance-gate repairs, three record-only instruments, note standard v1.5 with a vagueness linter that fails on its own motivating sentence, and the competence-provenance check for a founder observation neither reviewer raised. NOT PUSHED: control_two_distinct_defects_KEY.md is tracked at HEAD on this branch and pushing would publish Exp 55's answer key, which is the identical failure that produced the exp50/51/52 exposure. title: Two decision surfaces, neither pointing at the other: the hold was lifted 22 Aug and both trackers went on saying it stood.
verbatim: Two decision surfaces, neither pointing at the other: the hold was lifted 22 Aug and both trackers went on saying it stood. The RUNWAY still declared "EVERYTHING IS ON HOLD PENDING NINE FOUNDER DECISIONS" at the top of the file. The founder ruled on all nine at 16:49 BST on 2026-08-22 in d713379, and the instrument inventory that block names as the next thing to build landed at 17:41 the same day in 239d5c8. The file was edited twice on 24 August (fa4a86b, 95c9d36) and the block was not touched, so a fresh instance reading the tracker MEMORY.md flags as "where we are on the path to BR2" would conclude the project was frozen pending answers that already existed, and would either re-ask the founder for them or rebuild the inventory. Worse than merely stale: the table under that block holds the recommendations put TO the founder, not the rulings that came back, and three of the nine changed shape in the ruling. A reader taking the table as current would read row 6 as "retire the load balancer" when the ruling was SHELVE, and row 7 as "withdraw the survived-falsification ledger" when the ruling REVERSED that recommendation and said wire it. The superseded marker names the ruling commit and its time, lists the three that changed shape, and relabels the old block as the record of what was ASKED. Four rulings were verified against running code rather than against the notes, because "the ruling was given" and "the ruling was executed" are different claims and only one of them is checkable here. Ruling 1 is live: a falsifier failing the discrimination check writes NON_DISCRIMINATING, verified=False, escalated=True and demotes CONFIRMED to UNCONFIRMED at reference_runner_v2.py:3729, which is what carries it into _apply_routing's existing "escalated=True, not CONFIRMED" trigger. A shallow grep for a discrimination outcome near the routing site returns nothing and would have supported a false report that ruling 1 was never executed; following the readers refuted it. Ruling 6 is marked SHELVED in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, bench/dynamic_management.py and the instrument inventory. Ruling 7's ledger is wired at reference_runner_v2.py:9053. Ruling 2's equipment-error branch escalates to HIL without vetoing. The 24 August handover is corrected in place rather than rewritten, and gains a header recording three things. It cites the 22 August rulings nowhere: its single mention of that date concerns a repeated arithmetic error. Its item FIVE is not open, because a founder position on numbering is already recorded in OUTSTANDING_QUEUE_to_BR2.md section E as "keep the new sequence; docs to match. Founder: cosmetic". And its item EIGHT is not a decision at all but an overnight status report occupying a numbered slot in a list headed "decisions waiting". Seven of the nine are genuinely open; four of those need the founder's key or judgement. Companion TTS on the founder's desk: ~/Desktop/CDSFL_tts/Decisions_Awaiting_Founder_2026-08-24.txt, 111 lines, note standard v1.5, zero markdown, zero non-ASCII, no hard-wrapping, vagueness linter 0 findings. Not in this commit, because they are outside the repository: MEMORY.md line 31 was cut back to a pointer, and ce_state.md gained the live figures plus a provenance note. That line had attributed "3484 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed; qc 8 checks" to ce_state.md, which has never contained it. title: Note standard v1.6, Rule 26 -- and the pointer that was supposed to stop drifting had drifted twice.
verbatim: Note standard v1.6, Rule 26 -- and the pointer that was supposed to stop drifting had drifted twice. Rule 26 covers a case Rules 20 and 21 do not. Rule 20 labels the status of FIXES (PROPOSED/BUILT/TESTED/COMMITTED/ENABLED), Rule 21 labels DEFECTS (OBSERVED/HYPOTHESISED), and both assume a reader inside the project. Neither covers a document read from outside making claims of mixed epistemic status. The Stage 5 explorer's README was the artefact: a derived closed-form limit, a result sampled over 309,760 parameter combinations, and an untested central assumption, all sitting as flat assertions with nothing on the page to tell them apart. The three labels are DERIVED (follows from the equations; says nothing about the world), MEASURED (obtained by running something, with the method AND its extent named in the same breath), and OPEN (not established). Extent is part of a measurement's meaning, which is Rule 24 applied to provenance rather than to quantity: "measured" without "over what" is the same defect as "improved" without "by how much". THE LOAD-BEARING HALF OF THE RULE IS THE FOUNDER'S CONSTRAINT, not the vocabulary. Verbatim: "don't overdo it, by somehow peppering it everywhere. That will read like irrational doubt... It might sound like I don't know what I'm doing and/or have no faith in it." So labels appear ONLY where a reader could reasonably mistake one status for another, most sentences carry none, and the document must say so explicitly -- an unlabelled claim is a plain one, not an unchecked one. Measured density on first application: three labels in 115 lines. Every label must also be self-explaining, so the key is a formalisation and never a prerequisite. STATE THE CONVENTION, NEVER THE STANCE. Do not write that the project is careful or does not over-claim. That is a claim about oneself, it is unfalsifiable, and it has the exact shape this project exists to catch -- an assertion about a property, offered confidently, never checked, which is what the tamper detector and the load balancer both were. A convention is checkable and can be held to line by line, and the reader draws the conclusion themselves, which is the only way it sticks. THE DRIFT THIS COMMIT ALSO REPAIRS, AND IT IS A REPEAT. Commit e49a021 on 13 August recorded a "STRUCTURAL FIX" because .claude/CLAUDE.md named v1.2 while memory named v1.3, and stated that this was why the earlier improvement did not survive. Measured today: this file still named v1.4 as current, so v1.5 (locked 23 August) never propagated here at all, and the foot-line convention paragraph still named v1.2 -- four months stale and untouched by the August correction, which fixed the instance and not the class. Nothing in bench/tests/ or scripts/cdsfl_qc.py references the note standard version, so nothing has ever checked that the two pointers agree. Both are now v1.6. The check itself is NOT BUILT and is recorded here rather than claimed. Memory ledger 116 -> 117 for cdsfl_note_standard_v1.6.md, mirrored 59 -> 60. SEVENTH consecutive manual bump and the second inside one session, which is the clearest argument yet for the 2026-08-17 remedy of deriving the table inside sv instead of typing it. Also NOT BUILT. 26 tests pass across both memory-ledger suites. NOT PUSHED. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: RUNWAY Stage 5: the reviewer reproduction pack, recorded as the terminal item so it is not lost -- and the Desktop mirror was 127 lines stale.
verbatim: RUNWAY Stage 5: the reviewer reproduction pack, recorded as the terminal item so it is not lost -- and the Desktop mirror was 127 lines stale. Founder instruction: place the test suite as a final item on the runway, because there is no point in losing or forgetting it. Status DEFERRED BY DECISION, trigger "after BR2, and not before handover item 9 clears". THE FOUNDER'S REASON, AND IT IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I ARGUED. I argued from a trigger; the founder argued from the state of the thing: "You can't build a test suite for something that is yet to be built." Sharpened in discussion to the operative form now recorded in the section: the pack would technically work today, because it reproduces measurements that are already complete, but the SET of headline numbers is still moving -- the discrimination result is days old, Stage 1's exit test landed yesterday, exp50/51/52 have not run, and BR2 supersedes much of it. Assembling now creates a second estate pinned to a snapshot that is about to change, which is the exact drift this project hit twice today. THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN LOST, and the reason this row is worth its length: eight scripts already regenerate the project's headline numbers at zero cost, and NOTHING signposts them. Verified today by reading each one rather than running it, in deference to the recorded lesson that a --help must never cost money: zero network references, zero dispatch references, zero key references across all eight; five read only the local archive. Meanwhile docs/REPRODUCING.md, the only route an outsider would find, is organised as Prerequisites -> Running an Experiment -> Cost Estimates and carries 16 references to API keys and paid dispatch. The cheap path exists and the expensive one is the only one documented. All eight are now named in the row with what each reproduces. THREE THINGS GET CALLED A TEST SUITE AND THE ROW NAMES THEM APART. (a) The software suite exists -- bench/tests/, 3840 passing -- and is the wrong audience, because it tests the instrument rather than the theory. (b) The reproduction pack is this row. (c) A theory-testing kit, letting a reviewer apply CDSFL to their own artefact, is OUT OF SCOPE and deferred past BR2 with no date. The objection to (c) is not its cost. It is that a strange result from it would be UNINTERPRETABLE: neither party could distinguish a refutation of CDSFL from an unvalidated instrument, and that confusion has already happened once here, when a mis-specified zero-plant control read as a substantive false-positive result. FOUR DESIGN CONSTRAINTS AGREED BEFORE ANYTHING IS BUILT. The explorer is the front door and NOT the backbone -- it demonstrates one stage at d=1 and says in its own words that it is not evidence, so a pack centred on it leads with the least evidential artefact in the project; the eight scripts are the spine because they regenerate measurements. Runnable things plus one short index, links never copies. Point at the instruments, not at their outputs, because a list of scripts stays true when numbers move while a list of numbers rots. Two README links doing different jobs: one near the top as the anti-wading fix, one in context after the mathematical core. DESKTOP MIRROR WAS 127 LINES STALE -- 326 against the repo's 453 -- so the copy on the founder's Desktop was missing everything from roughly 22 August, including the discrimination control result and today's superseded-hold marker. Re-synced from the repo, which the file itself names as canonical; now byte-identical. Third instance today of the same drift class, after the RUNWAY hold that outlived its rulings by two days and the MEMORY.md index line carrying a figure its target file never held. NOT PUSHED. title: Pages config: exclude the experiment archive, which was being published as a 385 MB website.
verbatim: Pages config: exclude the experiment archive, which was being published as a 385 MB website. Enabling GitHub Pages exercised something nothing ever had: with no _config.yml, Jekyll builds the entire repository as a site. Measured on origin/main: 7,580 tracked files, 405.5 MB, of which 385 MB across 6,433 files is bench/logs/. The first build ran 14.8 minutes against the documented 10-minute Pages timeout and never completed, and the site returned 'Site not found' throughout. Excluding the archive takes the published site to 20.5 MB across 1,147 files, a 95 percent reduction in bytes, and the build to seconds. Jekyll is kept rather than disabled with .nojekyll, because .nojekyll would serve README.md as raw markdown and leave the site root with no landing page, and it would not stop 405 MB being copied either. exclude REPLACES Jekyll's default list rather than extending it, so the ten defaults are restated in the file to avoid silently starting to publish vendor and cache directories later. BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: Jebus197.

title: RUNWAY Stage 6: outreach, deferred to the same post-BR2 slot as Stage 5 -- and two of the four outreach documents are for a different project.
verbatim: RUNWAY Stage 6: outreach, deferred to the same post-BR2 slot as Stage 5 -- and two of the four outreach documents are for a different project. Founder instruction: record it alongside Stage 5 so it is not lost. Status DEFERRED BY DECISION. WHAT EXISTS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. Outreach.docx of 21 March is the substantial document: roughly 48,500 characters of verified-contact dossier covering Hinton, Bengio, Russell and the IASR network, each with role, fit rationale, interests and published contact address. Real work went into it. But outreach_plan.md and Gemini Candela Outreach.docx, both 7 February, are for CANDELA and Guardian -- Mini-BERT, on-chain anchoring, Sepolia -- and predate this repository by five weeks, and Project_Genesis/cw_handoff/OUTREACH_STRATEGY.md is Genesis. Two of the four are not a CDSFL plan and the row says so, because "the outreach plan" is otherwise a phrase that resolves to a February document about a different system. THE HOLD HAS BEEN KEPT DELIBERATELY. Persistent memory records first emails planned for 2026-03-17 and the reason for waiting: starting before finishing would be a distraction and would risk never completing the work. That date passed five months ago and the hold held. Recorded as discipline rather than slippage, because the row would otherwise read as an overdue item. THE AGENT QUESTION, ANSWERED WITH A SPLIT. The founder asked whether an autonomous agent could handle most of the initial outreach, and the concern behind it is volume, which is well founded: tailoring an approach to every name in that dossier is more drafting than one person finishes by hand. Agreed split now recorded: the agent researches, drafts, tracks and prepares; the founder reads and sends, every time. Three reasons, the first being the one a reviewer would raise in public. The medium would refute the message: a methodology for keeping AI work honest and human-supervised, delivered autonomously to Stuart Russell, who works on bounded oversight, contradicts its own thesis in the act of announcing it. This project's own architecture forbids it, since CDSFL keeps the human in the loop for decisions carrying consequences. And these contacts are one-shot: a failed experiment re-runs, a first email to Hinton does not. Independently of all three, an assistant cannot send on the founder's behalf without explicit per-message permission, so a fully autonomous sender was never available anyway. WHAT THE AGENT SHOULD DO, which is the actual answer to the volume worry: a freshness pass over a five-month-old dossier whose affiliations move; per-target preparation rather than templating, because ten tailored openings are agent-days and human-minutes while ten templated ones are worthless; a tracker that is generated rather than maintained, for which this file's own history is the argument, three stale-document defects having been found on 2026-08-24 alone; and materials pointing at the Stage 5 reviewer pack rather than at the 540-line README. LADDER REORDERED, DO NOT OPEN WITH HINTON. Persistent memory already names the Stanford and Harvard POPPER team as priority contact: nearest methodological neighbour, complementary statistical approach in e-values against this project's Bayesian R_k, most likely to engage on substance, and a survivable place to learn what lands. Desktop mirror re-synced. Repository homepage field set to the now-live Pages URL. NOT PUSHED. title: README 6.8: name the figure for what it is -- a bifurcation diagram -- and stop disclaiming it.
verbatim: README 6.8: name the figure for what it is -- a bifurcation diagram -- and stop disclaiming it. The previous note read: 'What it shows is the model's internal dynamics. It is not evidence that real review pipelines behave this way... The sliders are hypotheses.' Founder objection, and it is correct: that reads as 'this is not real, it is a cartoon', which is not how a scientific figure is annotated. THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE PROJECT'S OWN RULE, POINTED THE OTHER WAY. Note standard v1.6 Rule 26 says state the convention, never the stance -- do not assert that the project is careful, describe what it does and let the reader conclude. The same rule generalises: state what a figure IS, not what it ISN'T. Disclaiming and virtue-claiming are the same error in opposite directions, both substituting an assertion about the artefact for a description of it. Rule 26 was applied to the project's character two hours before this and not to its own figure. A theory figure containing no data is entirely standard -- phase diagrams, stability boundaries, sensitivity analyses and bifurcation diagrams all contain none. The risk was never that a reader finds it empty; it is that nothing announced the genre, so the reader had to work it out while a disclaimer told them not to trust it. That combination produces 'this tells me nothing'. THE CLASSIFICATION IS EXACT AND WAS CHECKED BEFORE PUBLISHING. Sweeping sigma passes the system through a genuine bifurcation, and it is TRANSCRITICAL rather than saddle-node: R = 1 is a fixed point for ALL parameter values, verified symbolically, so nothing annihilates. The interior fixed point nu/(q(sigma + nu(1-sigma))) crosses R = 1 exactly where nu crosses nu* evaluated at R = 1, and the two exchange stability. Measured at sigma=1, nu=0.05: at q=0.20 the interior point sits at 0.25 and attracts while |f'(1)|=1.188 repels; at q=0.03 the interior point has left the unit interval and |f'(1)|=0.979 attracts; at the crossing q=0.05 the multiplier at R=1 is exactly 1.000, which is the textbook signature. An earlier verbal description of this as a saddle-node collision was WRONG and is withdrawn -- a fold would have destroyed both fixed points. Also corroborating, from the night before: six anomalies in a 600-point parameter sweep all sat within about 1e-3 of exactly this boundary, where convergence becomes arbitrarily slow. That is the expected behaviour near the crossing and was originally mistaken for measurement error. REGISTER CHANGES. 'Parameters are indicative, and the tool exists so that measured values can be substituted for them' replaces 'no parameter has been estimated from a real run' -- the engineering-chart convention, an instruction to the user rather than a confession by the author, and true, since substitution is the tool's purpose. 'Is live work' replaces 'is untested': same fact, an activity in progress rather than a gap. One label remains in the block. title: README 6.8: name the figure for what it is -- a bifurcation diagram -- and stop disclaiming it.
verbatim: README 6.8: name the figure for what it is -- a bifurcation diagram -- and stop disclaiming it. The previous note read: 'What it shows is the model's internal dynamics. It is not evidence that real review pipelines behave this way... The sliders are hypotheses.' Founder objection, and it is correct: that reads as 'this is not real, it is a cartoon', which is not how a scientific figure is annotated. THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE PROJECT'S OWN RULE, POINTED THE OTHER WAY. Note standard v1.6 Rule 26 says state the convention, never the stance -- do not assert that the project is careful, describe what it does and let the reader conclude. The same rule generalises: state what a figure IS, not what it ISN'T. Disclaiming and virtue-claiming are the same error in opposite directions, both substituting an assertion about the artefact for a description of it. Rule 26 was applied to the project's character two hours before this and not to its own figure. A theory figure containing no data is entirely standard -- phase diagrams, stability boundaries, sensitivity analyses and bifurcation diagrams all contain none. The risk was never that a reader finds it empty; it is that nothing announced the genre, so the reader had to work it out while a disclaimer told them not to trust it. That combination produces 'this tells me nothing'. THE CLASSIFICATION IS EXACT AND WAS CHECKED BEFORE PUBLISHING. Sweeping sigma passes the system through a genuine bifurcation, and it is TRANSCRITICAL rather than saddle-node: R = 1 is a fixed point for ALL parameter values, verified symbolically, so nothing annihilates. The interior fixed point nu/(q(sigma + nu(1-sigma))) crosses R = 1 exactly where nu crosses nu* evaluated at R = 1, and the two exchange stability. An earlier verbal description of this as a saddle-node collision was WRONG and is withdrawn -- a fold would have destroyed both fixed points. Also corroborating, from the night before: six anomalies in a 600-point parameter sweep all sat within about 1e-3 of exactly this boundary, where convergence becomes arbitrarily slow. That is the expected behaviour near the crossing and was originally mistaken for measurement error. REGISTER CHANGES. 'Is live work' replaces 'is untested': same fact, an activity in progress rather than a gap. One label remains in the block. title: README 6.8: seven sliders, not five. Reported by Fable, confirmed by counting, and it was in three places rather than one.
verbatim: README 6.8: seven sliders, not five. Reported by Fable, confirmed by counting, and it was in three places rather than one. The deployed explorer carries seven range inputs -- pi, p, eta, sigma, nu, theta, and the perturbation -- confirmed both in the file and in what the live site actually serves. Section 6.8 said five. ROOT CAUSE, because the miscount was not random. Five is the number of the MODEL's parameters: prior flaw risk, detection efficacy, novelty, fix efficacy, re-injection rate. Theta is a stopping threshold on the marginal return and the perturbation injects extra risk part way through a run; both are controls on the experiment rather than on the model. I counted parameters and wrote 'sliders', which is a user-interface count. A category slip, not a typing error, which is why it reproduced. AND IT REPRODUCED THREE TIMES, not once. Fable reported the README instance. Sweeping for it found two more in the Desktop assessment: 'the tool has five dials', and 'sweep the five dials'. In those two the number five was conceptually correct -- both passages are about the model's parameters -- but 'dials' was the wrong noun for the same reason. Fixed as 'seven sliders, five of which are the model's own parameters and two are controls on the experiment', and 'sweep the five model parameters'. That is the check-the-whole-set rule applied to someone else's finding: a report of one instance is a report about one instance, and the quantifier still has to be established. Verified after: no remaining occurrence of the wrong count in the README, the Desktop TTS files, the runway, or the explorer's own README. title: docs/WORKING_DIRECTIVES.md: the portable two-thirds of the working configuration, published because a run cannot be understood without it.
verbatim: docs/WORKING_DIRECTIVES.md: the portable two-thirds of the working configuration, published because a run cannot be understood without it. The results in this repository depend not only on the code and the equations but on how claims are made, checked, withdrawn and written down. That layer has been in force throughout the experimental record and existed only in a personal configuration file. A reviewer attempting reproduction could not see it. THE SPLIT WAS CLEANER THAN EXPECTED. Lines 1 to 233 of the source -- Core Directives, P-pass logic, non-STEM rigour methods, verification and freshness, selection and tie-breaking, failure tracking, execution discipline, documentation integrity, FFAFP, public-facing attribution and the style preservation layer -- contain no personal or machine-specific material at all, verified by grep before extraction. They transfer verbatim, unedited. 3,308 words of 4,925, or 67 percent. WHAT STAYS BEHIND IS ABOUT EIGHTEEN LINES, four of them personal and the rest machine-specific paths and tracker locations. The header states that machine-specific configuration and personal working accommodations are held separately and that nothing methodological has been withheld, which is a claim checkable against the document itself. THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL, and it is the founder's framing rather than mine. The readable-companion convention -- two files per substantive note, plain text with zero markup alongside the technical markdown, third-party voice, plain English without simplification -- originated as an accessibility measure. It is published here as a CONVENTION, under a neutral name, with the accommodation it was built for omitted. The founder's argument for publishing it at all: a reader following an automated harness needs a way in that does not require reading code or rendering markdown, and providing one is ordinary courtesy. His analogy was the automatic door button, which is intended for wheelchair users and used by everyone who passes through. That reasoning is stated in the document; whose disability prompted it is not. This is the project's own Rule 26 applied one level up: state the convention, never the stance. TWO RULES WERE FOLDED IN from the project configuration rather than the personal one, because both are reproduction-critical. no-fake-model-labels: a simulated agent never carries a vendor name, because a result attributed to a model that did not produce it is downstream indistinguishable from a fabricated one. And the unfiltered-findings policy: full findings first, summaries only after the full output exists and never instead of it. One self-referential absolute URL to this repository was made relative, since a document living inside a repository should not link to itself by URL. Cross-referenced from REPRODUCING.md, which is 433 lines about running an experiment and answers a different question. Captured at 2026-08-25 10:18 BST. title: Commission the four stopping components, guard the drift class, and fix the instrument that measures instruments.
verbatim: Commission the four stopping components, guard the drift class, and fix the instrument that measures instruments. Four items, none of which touches the runner. Every test below was falsified before being trusted: the component was broken deliberately and the test confirmed to catch it. A commissioning test that cannot fail is the defect it exists to find. ONE. THE FOUR COMPONENTS THAT DECIDE WHEN A RUN STOPS ARE NOW COMMISSIONED. I02 two-sided gamma gate, I04 state-convergence check, I07 stall convergence, I08 budget extension. The inventory of 22 August found that not one of them was named by any test, while every convergence result in the archive was declared by one of them. 14 tests, each feeding a known-good and a known-bad input and asserting the component answers DIFFERENTLY. Mutation-tested: five deliberate breaks -- gate always converges, gate never converges, stall always fires, state always converges, budget raises NameError again -- and all five were caught. A CORRECTION IS RECORDED IN THE FILE ITSELF. The founder pointed out that the two-sided gamma gate HAS fired in production, and the archive confirms it: exp40_slice_admissibility closed at gamma=0.305 against a 0.30 threshold at round 7, exp41c on three consecutive zero-critical rounds, and four further runs closed on critical quiescence. It also does not fire on everything, which is evidence that it discriminates. The earlier claim that these components had never been shown to distinguish a converged run from an unconverged one was too strong and is withdrawn. These tests are the controlled confirmation that was missing, not a rescue of something believed broken. The fake registry in that file was DISCOVERED rather than assumed: a first version carried only the two methods the stall check reads, and the state-convergence tests failed on a missing undemonstrated_subcritical_ids. A fake narrower than the real interface produces tests that pass for the wrong reason. TWO. THE INSTRUMENT INVENTORY HAD BAD REFERENCE DATA FOR FIVE OF ITS THIRTY-FOUR ROWS, and the root cause is uniform: four rows used the MODULE name as the symbol, and the heuristic searches file CONTENT, so a module that does not contain its own name could never match. Those rows reported "no commissioning candidate" for a reason that had nothing to do with the component. Corrected: I02 pointed at _check_gamma_gate, a different function from the two-sided gate it is named after; I19 and I20 named bench/dm/_similarity.py while the symbols live in bench/convergence_location.py; I24 named the module instead of fix_complexity_features; I27 named the module instead of ShadowStage6Calibrator. THE FIX IS NOT THE FIVE CORRECTIONS, it is _symbol_resolves, which checks every row's symbol against the file the row names and reports failures LOUDLY as unlooked-at rather than silently as absent. This is the reassuring-direction failure one level up: the instrument that measures instruments was reporting a lookup failure as an absence of evidence. Falsified by breaking a symbol deliberately and confirming the warning fires. THREE. THREE DRIFT GUARDS, on founder instruction to ensure there is no repeated drift. The note standard version named in the project instructions must match the newest in memory -- this drifted two versions and four months AFTER commit e49a021 recorded a "structural fix" for exactly it, because that fix corrected the instance and not the class. The foot-line convention must name the current standard; it was three versions stale. Every document declaring a Desktop mirror must match its canonical repo copy; the runway's was 127 lines behind. And the memory ledger total must match the directory, asserted a second independent time because the derive-it-in-sv remedy has needed seven consecutive manual corrections. All three falsified by introducing each drift and confirming capture. STATED LIMIT: cross-document supersession -- a document asserting what a later ruling overturned -- is not mechanically detectable and is not attempted. The RUNWAY hold that outlived its rulings would still not be caught. FOUR. I33, THE SURVIVED-FALSIFICATION LEDGER, IS COMMISSIONED AND ITS STATUS CHANGES. Measured 22 August as NOT commissioned: full test suite, nothing called it. The founder ruled it be wired. Wiring is not working, so it was EXERCISED: a REFUTED verdict writes a survival row; CONFIRMED, ERROR and UNTOOLABLE write none, so equipment failure cannot read as corroboration; the verdict denominator is kept so an empty ledger can state why it is empty; the report carries its own not-proof-of-truth caveat. The 22 August reading was correct when taken and is superseded rather than withdrawn. title: Commission the four stopping components, guard the drift class, and fix the instrument that measures instruments.
verbatim: Commission the four stopping components, guard the drift class, and fix the instrument that measures instruments. Four items, none of which touches the runner. Every test below was falsified before being trusted: the component was broken deliberately and the test confirmed to catch it. A commissioning test that cannot fail is the defect it exists to find. ONE. THE FOUR COMPONENTS THAT DECIDE WHEN A RUN STOPS ARE NOW COMMISSIONED. I02 two-sided gamma gate, I04 state-convergence check, I07 stall convergence, I08 budget extension. The inventory of 22 August found that not one of them was named by any test, while every convergence result in the archive was declared by one of them. 14 tests, each feeding a known-good and a known-bad input and asserting the component answers DIFFERENTLY. Mutation-tested: five deliberate breaks -- gate always converges, gate never converges, stall always fires, state always converges, budget raises NameError again -- and all five were caught. A CORRECTION IS RECORDED IN THE FILE ITSELF. The founder pointed out that the two-sided gamma gate HAS fired in production, and the archive confirms it: exp40_slice_admissibility closed at gamma=0.305 against a 0.30 threshold at round 7, exp41c on three consecutive zero-critical rounds, and four further runs closed on critical quiescence. It also does not fire on everything, which is evidence that it discriminates. The earlier claim that these components had never been shown to distinguish a converged run from an unconverged one was too strong and is withdrawn. These tests are the controlled confirmation that was missing, not a rescue of something believed broken. The fake registry in that file was DISCOVERED rather than assumed: a first version carried only the two methods the stall check reads, and the state-convergence tests failed on a missing undemonstrated_subcritical_ids. A fake narrower than the real interface produces tests that pass for the wrong reason. TWO. THE INSTRUMENT INVENTORY HAD BAD REFERENCE DATA FOR FIVE OF ITS THIRTY-FOUR ROWS, and the root cause is uniform: four rows used the MODULE name as the symbol, and the heuristic searches file CONTENT, so a module that does not contain its own name could never match. Those rows reported "no commissioning candidate" for a reason that had nothing to do with the component. Corrected: I02 pointed at _check_gamma_gate, a different function from the two-sided gate it is named after; I19 and I20 named bench/dm/_similarity.py while the symbols live in bench/convergence_location.py; I24 named the module instead of fix_complexity_features; I27 named the module instead of ShadowStage6Calibrator. THE FIX IS NOT THE FIVE CORRECTIONS, it is _symbol_resolves, which checks every row's symbol against the file the row names and reports failures LOUDLY as unlooked-at rather than silently as absent. This is the reassuring-direction failure one level up: the instrument that measures instruments was reporting a lookup failure as an absence of evidence. Falsified by breaking a symbol deliberately and confirming the warning fires. THREE. THREE DRIFT GUARDS, on founder instruction to ensure there is no repeated drift. The note standard version named in the project instructions must match the newest in memory -- this drifted two versions and four months AFTER commit e49a021 recorded a "structural fix" for exactly it, because that fix corrected the instance and not the class. All three falsified by introducing each drift and confirming capture. STATED LIMIT: cross-document supersession -- a document asserting what a later ruling overturned -- is not mechanically detectable and is not attempted. The RUNWAY hold that outlived its rulings would still not be caught. FOUR. I33, THE SURVIVED-FALSIFICATION LEDGER, IS COMMISSIONED AND ITS STATUS CHANGES. Measured 22 August as NOT commissioned: full test suite, nothing called it. The founder ruled it be wired. Wiring is not working, so it was EXERCISED: a REFUTED verdict writes a survival row; CONFIRMED, ERROR and UNTOOLABLE write none, so equipment failure cannot read as corroboration; the verdict denominator is kept so an empty ledger can state why it is empty; the report carries its own not-proof-of-truth caveat. title: sy and the missing half of FFAFP: two hand-picked points do not prove a gate implements what it says.
verbatim: sy and the missing half of FFAFP: two hand-picked points do not prove a gate implements what it says. Founder question: has this work been f-checked and sy-checked? Honest answer at the time: FFAFP partially -- Find, Follow, Fix and P-pass yes, but the ANALYSE step used only pytest, grep and mutation -- and sy not at all. Both gaps are now closed and the second one caught something real. THE GAP THAT MATTERED. Mutation testing proves a test can fail. It does not prove the test measures the property it claims to. A commissioning test can pass because the component answered correctly by accident, which is this project's own central lesson applied one level up: the falsifier gate measured that a test FIRED and never that it fired BECAUSE of the claim. The original three tests here sampled two points of the input space and asserted a boolean. THREE ADDITIONS. Reason assertions. The gate must not merely return True; its stated reason must cite BOTH arms of the two-sided rule. Verified live: the good case reports gamma_critical=0.550 >= 0.3, decay curve flattened, AND 3 consecutive zero-new-critical rounds. The bad case reports novel_crit_recent=[2,2,2] -- refusing on the COUNT arm specifically, which is the intended reason given gamma is above threshold. A test that only checked the boolean could not tell those apart. Exhaustive specification check, which is the sy contribution. 8 gamma values against 1,344 history patterns, 10,752 cases, each compared against the stated rule: converge if and only if the decay slope is at or above threshold AND K consecutive rounds produced no new critical. Result: ZERO disagreements. The implementation matches its documentation across the whole enumerated space. The vacuous-curve degeneracy, pinned. Commit 2887106 repaired a case where two OPPOSITE series both drive a Duane fit to about zero -- no critical ever found, the best possible outcome, and criticals arriving at a constant rate, the worst. Neither now converges on the slope alone; both verified False at gamma 0.0. THE EXHAUSTIVE TEST EARNS ITS PLACE, DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. A mutation was introduced that flips the verdict ONLY where gamma exactly equals the threshold -- a boundary-only defect. Sixteen tests passed, including every hand-picked one; only the exhaustive check failed. So it catches a class the sampled points cannot, which is precisely why sampling two points was insufficient. 17 tests in the file, all falsified before being trusted. Runner untouched. NOT PUSHED. title: sv tooling: the Desktop mirror cannot be maintained from this process, and the save now says so instead of crashing.
verbatim: sv tooling: the Desktop mirror cannot be maintained from this process, and the save now says so instead of crashing. MEASURED PERMISSION MODEL, established by direct test rather than inferred: creating a NEW file under ~/Desktop succeeds; stat() succeeds; read() is denied on 6 of 6 attempts; overwriting an EXISTING file is denied; listing the directory is denied. Content comparison and mirror refresh were the two operations sv depended on, and both are exactly what is unavailable. FOUR ROUNDS OF THIS, EACH WRONG DIFFERENTLY, RECORDED BECAUSE THE PATTERN IS THE POINT. First: treat unreadable as a third state and report parity UNKNOWN -- honest, but it left the save ambiguous, which the founder rejected outright. Second: compare by size and refresh from canonical -- right in principle, but it assumed write_bytes would work, and it does not. Third: report NOT REFRESHED and complete -- correct behaviour, but it referenced repo_bytes, a name that does not exist in that function. Fourth and current: this function's own names (mirror, mirror_size), verified by running the save rather than by reading the patch. EVERY WRONG VERSION WAS CAUGHT BY EXECUTING IT. None was caught by inspection, including by me re-reading my own patch. The lesson is narrow and specific: patching a function without reading its enclosing scope produces NameErrors that look like working code. THE DESIGN POINT. The repo copy is canonical by founder ruling 2026-08-06; the Desktop copy is a convenience. A save of canonical state must not fail, nor become ambiguous, because a convenience copy is unwritable. sv now depends for success only on canonical state and reports the mirror as a definite fact -- STALE from this save onward, with reason and remedy named -- rather than as an unknown. THE DRIFT GUARD, INDEPENDENTLY, GOT THE SAME TREATMENT. cdsfl_sv.py contains ZERO references to it; they hit the same condition separately, which is why one defect appeared twice. The guard first reported the denial as DRIFT, then skipped. Skipping is how a guard quietly stops guarding, so it now compares SIZE via stat, which is permitted, and fails on mismatch. Both mirrors currently report matching sizes, so parity is answered rather than unknown. title: "Not mechanically detectable" was wrong: withdraw the claim and build the checker that refutes it.
verbatim: "Not mechanically detectable" was wrong: withdraw the claim and build the checker that refutes it. The founder asked "Is not mechanically detectable? For sure?" about a limit I had stated twice -- in the drift-guard docstring and in a note on their desk -- saying cross-document supersession could not be caught, and that the 24 August defect "would still not be caught". General supersession cannot be. That defect was not general. The RUNWAY asserted a hold and NAMED the file holding the decisions; that file had carried "# FOUNDER RULINGS" for two days. Both halves are machine-readable, so the pair is detectable. scripts/supersession_check.py fires on the actual historical file at c8f63ec~1. Its first version also fired on resources/ONBOARDING.md:514 -- a real hold naming a real file, recorded inside a dated 2026-04-22 log entry with four months of later entries below it. A record of what was pending in April is not a claim that it is pending now. Rather than exclude the file, which would silence the check, the tool now follows the document's own convention: a hold is live only in the newest dated entry, or in none at all, which is where the RUNWAY's banner sits. Commissioned rather than asserted: one known-bad and three known-good fixtures, plus the real git file, and the three deliberate breaks (drop the SUPERSEDED escape, drop the history discriminator, return no findings) fail 5, 5 and 3 tests respectively. 7 pass restored. title: Keys move out of the repository -- and the door they were guarding has been open since 20 August.
verbatim: Keys move out of the repository -- and the door they were guarding has been open since 20 August. THE BLOCKER AS RECORDED IS VOID. The operational plan carries, as item 2 of its standing rules: "NEVER push this branch. control_two_distinct_defects_KEY.md is Exp 55's answer key, tracked at HEAD. Pushing publishes it." The key file is indeed tracked. But control_two_distinct_defects_GROUND_TRUTH.json, its sibling, states the SAME two defects in the same terms -- CT-01 "Nyquist criterion misquoted as f_s > f_max; correct form is f_s > 2*f_max" CT-02 "df = 1.5625 Hz computed correctly; conclusion that it resolves 1 Hz does not follow" -- and has been on the PUBLIC main branch since commit bd9c569, 2026-08-20 01:21 BST. The target itself is public too. Both exp55 runs started 2026-08-23, three days after that. The 23 August key split was correct and necessary -- it took the answers out of the file the runner stages into the panel prompt, which is the exposure that removed exp48 and exp49 -- but it was not sufficient, and nothing said so. WHAT CHANGES. Both files now live in ../CDSFL_experiment_keys/, outside any git tree, per the founder ruling of 2026-08-25. .gitignore refuses *_KEY.md, *_GROUND_TRUTH.json and *_ANSWER_KEY* so the class cannot recur by accident. No Python references either file, so nothing breaks. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. This does not rewrite history. title: sv now MEASURES the remote after pushing, and says public main is 58 commits behind.
verbatim: sv now MEASURES the remote after pushing, and says public main is 58 commits behind. FOUNDER, 2026-08-26: "a push/commit should cause both local and remote to be *fully* in sync. Surely that is the point of the entire exercise? Whatever you are doing that might be preventing this, you should fix it." And: sv must finish with "zero errors and zero ambiguity about the completed sv state". WHAT WAS AMBIGUOUS. The summary said "Remote before this sv: <N ahead>. Pushed: yes." Both true, neither an after-state. A push that pushed a branch nobody reads produced the same two lines as a push that worked. The remedy is not wording; it is measuring again afterwards. WHAT IT NOW SAYS, and this is the answer to the question. Running it here: REMOTE SYNC: NOT VERIFIED -- origin/build-experiment-2026-08-22 does not exist: this branch has never been pushed PUBLIC main IS 58 COMMITS BEHIND this branch. Pushing 'build-experiment-2026-08-22' does NOT update main. Anyone reading the public repository sees main, not this branch. So the thing preventing sync was not a fault in the push. sv pushes whatever branch is checked out, that branch had never been pushed at all, and even a successful push of it would have left the public repository 58 commits stale while reporting success. The same mechanism left main 16 days stale in August. An unmeasurable divergence is now None and reads as NOT VERIFIED -- never as zero, never as "in sync". A failed check that reads as a pass is the class this project keeps finding. Commissioned: 9 tests over a real bare remote covering synced / behind / never- pushed / side-branch-gap, asserting the three verdicts differ. Three deliberate breaks (force in_sync, report the unpushed case as zero, drop the main gap) fail 1, 3 and 1 tests. Also: operational-plan rule 2 rewritten. It said "NEVER push this branch" because the key was tracked; it is now out of the tree, and the reason the rule existed was already void -- see the previous commit.
