title: sv printed "State save complete." BEFORE committing and pushing. Same defect, one level up.
verbatim: sv printed "State save complete." BEFORE committing and pushing. Same defect, one level up. Verified end-to-end against a real bare remote rather than asserted, and the end-to-end run exposed a second instance of the defect just fixed. sv printed: State save complete. ... Remote: up to date with origin/main [tracker warning] Committed: c7d83ae ... Pushed to origin/main "Complete" came first and then it did more work, and the Remote line under that heading was a PRE-COMMIT reading. A before-state under a final-sounding heading is exactly what the previous commit fixed for the push; it was also true of the banner above it. Now: when a commit is coming, the heading says "State files written. Commit and push STILL TO RUN -- the lines below are the state BEFORE that", the remote line is labelled "Remote BEFORE this sv", and one SV COMPLETE block runs last and RE-MEASURES commit, branch, working tree and remote. Measured on the three paths in an isolated clone: --commit --push, on main -> Remote: origin/main == HEAD. Fully in sync. --commit, no push -> Remote: NOT PUSHED. Local is ahead of the remote. --commit --push, side branch -> Remote: origin/sidework == HEAD. Fully in sync. PUBLIC main: 2 COMMITS BEHIND this branch. The public repository does NOT show this work. The third is the case that bit this project: the push succeeds, the branch is genuinely in sync, and the public repository still shows nothing. Both facts now print together. Six further tests, and three deliberate breaks (claim sync when unpushed, hide the main gap, always report the tree clean) each fail exactly the test written for them. 15 pass restored. ANSWERING THE QUESTION DIRECTLY: sv works. Exit 0, no errors, all paths. The sensitive-material hold is a separate matter and is not an sv fault. title: Measuring first refuted the renumbering premise: the order is already correct, and two other things are not.
verbatim: Measuring first refuted the renumbering premise: the order is already correct, and two other things are not. FOUNDER INSTRUCTION 2026-08-25: renumber the experiments by actual run order. MEASURED BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING. Sorted by start time, the experiment NUMBER is already perfectly monotonic across all 44 non-empty run directories -- ZERO violations. The only apparent violations are three EMPTY directories written on 2026-08-07 by aborted re-invocations of exp35 and exp36, which are not runs. A renumber by run order would change nothing, and it is not free: the run directory name AND the report filename both embed the experiment number, so renumbering means renaming 56 directories and severing every document reference that points into them. TWO REAL DEFECTS SIT UNDER THE REQUEST, and the ledger surfaces both. HOLE 1 -- four numbers in the exp29-exp55 span never ran. exp50/51/52 have configs and no directory; exp54 has neither. A reader counting the span infers 27 experiments; 23 numbers produced a directory, 22 produced a report. HOLE 2 -- status is recorded TWICE and the two disagree. 20 of 31 completion_signal.json files carry an EMPTY reason, and in 7 of those the run report DOES name an outcome the signal lost: exp36 and exp37 STATE_CONVERGED, exp40 twice, exp35 EXTENSION_STALLED, and both exp55 runs HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM. Tooling reading only the signal sees a converged run as INCOMPLETE. reference_runner_v2.py:11002 names this defect in its own source and dates a partial fix to 2026-05-18; runs after that date still show it. CORRECTION CARRIED INTO MEMORY. exp43's completion signal is INCOMPLETE and its report holds NO converged_at and NO convergence_reason. resources/RECOVERY.md was right all along -- "formal 3-consecutive convergence was blocked by ONE mechanical artifact" -- and the persistent memory was wrong: "five straight convergences 42-46" is FOUR. Both memory entries corrected against the artefacts. Also corrected here: I told the founder both exp55 runs produced no final report. They produced reports; I probed for the wrong filename. The reports say HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM at round 1, which is a better fact than the one I gave and does not change the conclusion that the runs yielded nothing usable. The ledger is DERIVED, never typed -- `--check` fails if the committed copy stops matching bench/logs. COMMISSIONED, AND FALSIFYING THE TESTS FOUND A HOLE IN THEM. Five deliberate breaks were introduced; four failed tests and the fifth -- making --check exit 0 unconditionally -- passed all twelve, because --check was only ever run against a ledger that already matched. A guard exercised only on the passing case is not a guard. Five more tests now run it on the failing case, and all six breaks are caught. That fix also exposed `LEDGER.relative_to(REPO)` throwing ValueError for any path outside the repo -- the SECOND time that exact defect was written in this session, after scripts/supersession_check.py. It is a `_rel()` helper now rather than an inline patch. 17 tests pass. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: Scaling spec: at the measured correlation, fifty architectures do the work of about four.
verbatim: Scaling spec: at the measured correlation, fifty architectures do the work of about four. FOUNDER INSTRUCTION 2026-08-25: a spec sheet framing CDSFL as striving toward a general-purpose STEM calculator on massively distributed compute and epistemic diversity, inspired by the @home projects without copying them. `re` enabled for external research on the load-balancing question. THE PRIOR QUESTION, ANSWERED WITH A NUMBER. Does adding cognitive architectures buy coverage? Part XIII's model says it depends on rho, the inter-architecture correlation. rho has been recorded per round all along and nobody had summed it: across 289 observations in 31 run directories, mean 0.564, median 0.556. At that rho the decay is severe. The FIFTH architecture contributes 3.6% of what the first contributes; the panel fields five. Going from 5 architectures to 50 gains +0.0049 / +0.0041 / +0.0022 coverage at p = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8. Optimal stopping gives n* = 3, 4, 5, 6 at eps = 0.05, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005 -- which DERIVES the "n = 3-6 saturation" the project has carried as an observation. It was never a property of the problem; it is a property of how correlated the panel is. SymPy against an independent NumPy implementation, agreeing to 1e-12. THE @HOME INVERSION, which is the substantive distinction. BOINC's homogeneous redundancy sends replicas ONLY to numerically equivalent hosts, because cross-architecture disagreement there is NOISE. CDSFL's Property 3 says the opposite: at rho=1 coverage collapses to D(1). Same topology, inverted correlation objective. The inspiration is real and the copy would be a category error. TWO THINGS THIS PROJECT REDISCOVERED THAT HAVE NAMES. Spot-checking IS the planted-defect control -- probe tasks with known answers, used to estimate worker credibility. Its documented central caveat is the one that has cost this project five experiments: a spot-check works only while it is indistinguishable from real work. The exp48-52 exposures and the exp55 finding of 2026-08-26 are instances of a known failure mode, not novel accidents, which is what makes them fixable by construction. Refusing model voting IS collusion resistance. Majority voting over workers is known-vulnerable to Sybil and collusion, and correlated workers ARE a collusion. At rho=0.564 the standing no-voting rule is not a preference. SO n IS NOT THE SCALING AXIS. Two remain: reduce rho (ceiling 0.761 at 0.564, 0.921 at 0.30, 0.999 at 0.10 -- halving rho beats ten times the panel by more than an order of magnitude), and scale by ARTEFACT COUNT, where the work is genuinely embarrassingly parallel. Six numbered specification points and four falsifiable predictions, including the uncomfortable one: about a quarter of consequence-weighted defect classes are outside the current panel's reach whatever is spent. 10 tests re-derive every quoted figure from the archive, including the Part XIII reduction property at rho=0 and monoculture collapse at rho=1, so the spec cannot quote a number the artefacts stopped supporting. title: sv crashed mid-session because existence is not readability -- and I had just told the founder sv works.
verbatim: sv crashed mid-session because existence is not readability -- and I had just told the founder sv works. WHAT HAPPENED, MEASURED. At 00:53 BST `python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py` exited 0. At 01:52 the same command on the same tree exited 1 with a traceback. Nothing in the repository changed between them. This process lost read access to ~/.claude/projects/.../memory partway through the session, forty minutes after edits to files in that directory had succeeded. Under that permission state: exists() -> True is_dir() -> True iterdir() -> PermissionError read_text() -> PermissionError glob(...) -> [] <-- EMPTY LIST, does not raise Every memory access in sv and in the drift guards was gated on exists() or is_dir(). Neither fires. So: * _update_memory_exclusions_ledger called mem.iterdir() unguarded and took the whole save down. * _audit_memory_index globbed for *.md, got [], and would have reported every indexed file as missing had an earlier read not already aborted it. * test_project_instructions_name_the_current_note_standard globbed for the note standards, got [], and failed with "no cdsfl_note_standard_vN.N.md found in the memory directory" -- asserting ABSENCE where there was only DENIAL, inside the drift guard written on 2026-08-25 to catch exactly that class. * test_foot_line_convention died with "TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable": a permission denial wearing the costume of a type error, in a message about document drift. THE DISTINCTION NOW ENFORCED. Absent means there is nothing to count and a skip is honest. Unreadable means the count DID NOT HAPPEN: it must not crash the save, must not write 0, must be said out loud, and must NOT refresh the "counted <date>" stamp -- because that stamp is a claim about when the number was last verified, and refreshing it after a failure is a lie about provenance. sv now prints: MEMORY LEDGER NOT RECOUNTED — the directory is unreadable: ... The count did not happen; this is not evidence that the directory is empty. Counts and the 'counted' date are LEFT AS THEY WERE. This is a failed measurement, not a clean bill of health. and exits 0. Verified: the stamp stayed at 00:53, the last successful recount, and the total stayed at 118. Test side gets the same treatment via bench/tests/_private_memory.py, which probes by ATTEMPTING the read -- enumerate, then open an entry, because enumeration has been observed to succeed while per-file reads were denied. Five existence-checks across two files replaced. COMMISSIONED: 8 tests, including the end-to-end regression that sv exits 0 AND says NOT RECOUNTED, since a silent survival is indistinguishable from a successful recount. Three deliberate breaks fail 6, 2 and 1 tests. One of those breaks was initially a no-op -- a mis-escaped regex meant the injected fault never applied, and the suite's 8 passes proved nothing. title: sv crashed mid-session because existence is not readability -- and I had just told the founder sv works.
verbatim: sv crashed mid-session because existence is not readability -- and I had just told the founder sv works. WHAT HAPPENED, MEASURED. At 00:53 BST `python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py` exited 0. At 01:52 the same command on the same tree exited 1 with a traceback. Nothing in the repository changed between them. This process lost read access to ~/.claude/projects/.../memory partway through the session, forty minutes after edits to files in that directory had succeeded. Under that permission state: exists() -> True is_dir() -> True iterdir() -> PermissionError read_text() -> PermissionError glob(...) -> [] <-- EMPTY LIST, does not raise Every memory access in sv and in the drift guards was gated on exists() or is_dir(). Neither fires. So: * _update_memory_exclusions_ledger called mem.iterdir() unguarded and took the whole save down. * _audit_memory_index globbed for *.md, got [], and would have reported every indexed file as missing had an earlier read not already aborted it. * test_project_instructions_name_the_current_note_standard globbed for the note standards, got [], and failed with "no cdsfl_note_standard_vN.N.md found in the memory directory" -- asserting ABSENCE where there was only DENIAL, inside the drift guard written on 2026-08-25 to catch exactly that class. * test_foot_line_convention died with "TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable": a permission denial wearing the costume of a type error, in a message about document drift. THE DISTINCTION NOW ENFORCED. Absent means there is nothing to count and a skip is honest. Unreadable means the count DID NOT HAPPEN: it must not crash the save, must not write 0, must be said out loud, and must NOT refresh the "counted <date>" stamp -- because that stamp is a claim about when the number was last verified, and refreshing it after a failure is a lie about provenance. sv now prints: MEMORY LEDGER NOT RECOUNTED — the directory is unreadable: ... The count did not happen; this is not evidence that the directory is empty. Counts and the 'counted' date are LEFT AS THEY WERE. This is a failed measurement, not a clean bill of health. and exits 0. Verified: the stamp stayed at 00:53, the last successful recount, and the total stayed at 118. Test side gets the same treatment via bench/tests/_private_memory.py, which probes by ATTEMPTING the read -- enumerate, then open an entry, because enumeration has been observed to succeed while per-file reads were denied. Five existence-checks across two files replaced. title: I typed five timestamps tonight instead of reading them, and three were in the future.
verbatim: I typed five timestamps tonight instead of reading them, and three were in the future. Committed at 2026-08-26 01:28 BST, captured with `date` rather than typed, which is the whole point of this commit. WHAT WAS WRONG. Across the overnight window I wrote "02:20 BST" as the header of the founder's decisions note, "02:40 BST" on the tracker's new resume pointer, "01:45 BST" in two docstrings for when the memory directory became unreadable, and "01:52" for when sv crashed. The clock read 01:26 when the first two were written. Three of the five were LATER than the actual time. They were not estimates that drifted; they were invented. WHY THE EXISTING GUARD DID NOT CATCH IT. This project installed a UserPromptSubmit hook on 2026-08-25 that supplies the wall clock and the elapsed gap on every user turn, precisely so a temporal expression is never emitted without the clock in hand. A long autonomous stretch has no user turns. The hook was silent for hours and the rule quietly stopped being enforced by anything. The rule's own wording already covers this -- if the hook is absent or silent, capture `date` explicitly -- and I did not. WHAT THE RECORD NOW SAYS. Where a minute was genuinely captured it stands: the ledger stamp 00:53 is real, written by sv itself. Where it was not, the artefacts now carry the bracket the evidence supports -- "between 00:53 and 01:27 BST" -- together with a note saying the exact minute was not recorded and why that is itself the defect. A false precision replaced by an honest interval is a better record than either the invention or a silent deletion. Also changed: the fixture in test_sv_memory_unreadable used "2026-08-26 02:00 BST" as an arbitrary counted_at value. It is arbitrary test data rather than a claim, but a future-dated timestamp sitting in a file about timestamp discipline invites exactly the misreading this commit is about. It is now the literal string "RECOUNT-STAMP", which cannot be mistaken for a measurement. Suite at the close of the window: 3925 passed, 1 failed, 40 skipped. The single failure is the drift guard correctly reporting that the tracker's Desktop mirror is stale, which needs one `cp` from the founder because this process cannot overwrite files there. title: A literal "BROKEN-STAMP" sat in a canonical document through 3929 tests, because the guards watched the number and not the date beside it.
verbatim: A literal "BROKEN-STAMP" sat in a canonical document through 3929 tests, because the guards watched the number and not the date beside it. resources/MEMORY_EXCLUSIONS.md line 11 read: ## Accounting (counted BROKEN-STAMP ;OLD: 2026-08-26 00:53 BST) while the prose directly beneath it still said "Every figure below was counted from that directory on the date in this heading". BROKEN-STAMP appears in no Python source anywhere -- not a fixture, not a constant. I typed it by hand while checking that sv REFUSES to advance the stamp when a count fails, and sv's auto-staging swept it into 80faf11 alongside docs/CURRENT_STATE.md. WHY IT SURVIVED. Two guards already watch this file, in test_documentation_drift_guards_2026-08-25.py and in test_recovery_memory_doc_repairs.py, and a third watches the bucket sum. All three check NUMBERS. Nothing checked the date sitting next to them. Same shape as every other finding in this arc: the quantity was guarded and the thing beside it was not. FIXED BY THE MECHANISM THAT OWNS IT, not by hand. sv's own recount now runs -- the private memory directory became readable again this morning, having been denied when the 01:28 save ran. Note sv behaved correctly then: it refused to count, left the figures alone, and printed "Counts and the 'counted' date are LEFT AS THEY WERE. This is a failed measurement, not a clean bill of health." The stale 118 was the honest answer available at 01:28. Now: stamp 2026-08-26 11:32 BST read from the clock, total 119, prose updated in step ("120 files ... leaving 119 individual"), buckets 62+15+3+39 = 119. THE GUARD WAS WRITTEN FIRST AND FAILED ON THE REAL DEFECT before anything was fixed -- 2 failed, 13 passed -- which is a stronger falsification than a synthetic break. It asserts the heading PARSES as sv's own format, rejects nine non-dates including the actual string, refuses a stamp ahead of the clock (the 26 Aug defect where five timestamps were typed instead of read and three were in the future), and refuses scratch markers anywhere in the file. title: A run that halts on a named alarm now SAYS so: stop_reason, because the reason was guarded by a flag that only meant "converged".
verbatim: A run that halts on a named alarm now SAYS so: stop_reason, because the reason was guarded by a flag that only meant "converged". MEASURED ACROSS THE WHOLE ARCHIVE, 2026-08-26. 20 of 31 completion signals carry status INCOMPLETE with an EMPTY reason. In 7 of those the run report DOES name the cause the signal lost: exp35 EXTENSION_STALLED exp36 STATE_CONVERGED at round 45 exp37 STATE_CONVERGED at round 15 exp40 GAMMA_ALT_CONVERGED (gamma=0.305 >= 0.3 at round 7) exp40 HARDENED_CONVERGED (sparsity fallback) exp55 HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM exp55 HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM MECHANISM. reference_runner_v2 writes the cause into its result dict, then copies it to brain.state.convergence_reason only inside `if converged:`. signal_complete reads that field. So every NON-convergence stop reached the report and never reached completion_signal.json, and any tool reading the signal alone saw a run that halted on a named alarm as a run that just stopped. Both exp55 runs are that case exactly, and last night I told the founder those runs produced "no final report" -- wrong on the evidence, right on the conclusion. They produced a report naming the alarm and a signal naming nothing. WHY A THIRD FIELD RATHER THAN WIDENING convergence_reason. signal_complete derives STATUS from that field's CONTENTS ("BUDGET_EXHAUSTED" in ...). Merging stop reasons into it would make the status depend on the wording of an unrelated halt. stop_reason leaves the status logic untouched by construction rather than by argument -- and the test test_a_stop_reason_containing_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_still_does_not_flip_status asserts precisely that, using the adversarial wording. The runner's source names a cousin of this defect at reference_runner_v2.py:11002 and dates a partial fix to 2026-05-18 -- "post-mortem tooling read every hardened convergence as INCOMPLETE". July and August runs still showed it, because that fix corrected the instance and not the class. 12 tests, including checkpoint round-trip so a resumed run does not lose why its predecessor stopped. Four deliberate breaks -- drop the fallback, drop it from the checkpoint, merge it into convergence_reason, re-guard the runner propagation -- fail 4, 1, 1 and 1 tests. An empty reason remains possible and remains visible: it now means nothing anywhere recorded a cause, which is worse than any named stop and should stay reportable. Full suite after this change: 3959 passed, 1 failed (the Desktop mirror, which needs a command this process cannot run), 34 skipped. title: The stray temp file was the symptom. The cost was 99 MB of bytecode nothing ever deleted.
verbatim: The stray temp file was the symptom. The cost was 99 MB of bytecode nothing ever deleted. FOUND BY THE FOUNDER'S SCREENSHOT: "a full test-suite run drops a stray Python temp file in the project root." Caught in the act mid-run -- tmpjwur6y1n.py, present in one `ls`, gone from the next, which is why `git status` never showed it and a first look found nothing. TRACING IT. _run_hard_gate_compile wrote a temp .py into _anchor_dir_for(source_path) and unlinked it in a `finally`, so the .py was transient. py_compile ALSO writes bytecode beside it, and nothing removed that: repo-root __pycache__ 17,874 entries, 70 MB -- EVERY ONE named tmp* bench/__pycache__ 371 of 505 tmp*, 29 MB The root ones come from bare-filename targets like the test fixture's "x.py": Path("x.py").parent is ".", the working directory, which during a suite run is the repository root. The bench/ ones come from REAL runs, whose targets live in bench/ -- so this was never test-only. 99 MB, growing with every gate call, and the visible symptom was a file that deleted itself. THE FIX IS THE SMALL ONE. This gate only asks whether the source compiles, and the builtin compile() answers that from a string with no file I/O at all. The anchoring was pointless HERE regardless: it exists so ruff and bandit walk up to the repository config, and py_compile walks up to nothing. The three ruff/bandit sites still write real files, because those tools need one, and they write no bytecode. Second half: _anchor_dir_for no longer returns "." for a path that names no directory. There is no directory context to gain from a bare filename, and returning the working directory is how strays reached the project root. "bench/insect_brain.py" -> "bench" is unchanged, so ruff and bandit keep their config parity. CLEARED: root __pycache__ 17,874 -> 0 entries; bench/__pycache__ 505 -> 134, 29 MB -> 3.9 MB, the 134 real module caches kept. 95 MB reclaimed. Only tmp* entries were removed and every root entry was one. 15 tests. The load-bearing one snapshots the repo root, bench/, and both __pycache__ directories around a gate call and asserts NOTHING new appears -- across valid and broken source, real and bare paths, and then fifty calls in a row, because one call leaking nothing is weaker than fifty. A separate guard fails if any tmp*.py is ever found in the root, which catches a run killed before its finally. Reverting both halves fails 7 tests; reverting the anchor alone fails 4. title: Every suite run rewrote three canonical state files, and that is how BROKEN-STAMP got committed.
verbatim: Every suite run rewrote three canonical state files, and that is how BROKEN-STAMP got committed. FOUND WHILE CHASING THE TEMP-FILE LEAK. docs/CURRENT_STATE.md, resources/ONBOARDING.md and resources/RECOVERY.md were modified in the working tree with a timestamp of 11:40:09 -- inside a suite run, and nothing I had run by hand touched them. CAUSE. test_sv_memory_unreadable_2026-08-26.py invoked sv's main() with cwd=REPO, the real repository, and no --dry-run. sv did exactly what sv does and regenerated its three state files. On every suite run. CONSEQUENCE, which is the part that matters. Those files were therefore ALWAYS dirty in git status, so they were always swept up by sv's auto-staging into whatever was being committed next. That is the route by which a hand-typed "BROKEN-STAMP" reached resources/MEMORY_EXCLUSIONS.md and shipped in 80faf11 -- fixed two commits ago as an instance. This is the class. FIX. Pass --dry-run. Measured both ways before changing anything: the dry run dirties 0 files and still prints "MEMORY LEDGER NOT RECOUNTED", "failed measurement" and exits 0 -- every string the test asserts on. The live run dirties 3. The test exercises the identical path and now leaves nothing behind. GUARD. A static check over the whole test corpus, 164 parametrised cases: no test may invoke sv's main with cwd set to the real repository unless it also passes --dry-run. Static rather than runtime, because a runtime "are these files clean" check depends on test ordering and on whatever the developer left dirty before running pytest. It carries its own commissioning case, feeding it the code as it stood this morning (must fail), the accepted fix (must pass) and a tmp-cwd test (must not fire), so a guard that matched nothing could not pass forever. title: Note standard v1.7: stop spelling numbers out. The invented rule was written into three places as fact.
verbatim: Note standard v1.7: stop spelling numbers out. The invented rule was written into three places as fact. FOUNDER, 2026-08-26, having asked persistently: stop the "inexplicable vagueness/dumbing things down much too much", and make the word-numbers go. "I am a non coding engineer and founder of this project, but not an idiot!" MEASURED across the three TTS files written for them in the previous 24 hours: 59 violations. "three thousand eight hundred and seventy eight passed" -> 3878 "one hundred and seventy eight thousand nine hundred and seventy one bytes" -> 178,971 "one point five six two five hertz" -> 1.5625 Hz "five six four" -> 0.564 "at fourteen forty six" -> at 14:46 "the save routine", 7 occurrences -> sv THE STANDARD NEVER REQUIRED THIS. v1.5 says a value may be "spelled or in digits". Rule 11 governs SCIENTIFIC-NOTATION EXPONENTS ONLY. The blanket habit was a generalisation of Rule 11 -- and it had been recorded as fact in THREE places, which is how an invented rule acquires the authority of a real one: 1. the habit itself, in every note written; 2. a comment in scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py reading "TTS files write numbers as words by standard", so the TOOL taught it back; 3. a test docstring in test_note_vagueness_lint_2026-08-23.py asserting the same thing, so the SUITE enforced it. All three corrected. The test is narrowed rather than deleted: its real intent -- that a spelled value still satisfies the quantity check, so an old compliant note is not retroactively vague -- was right and is preserved. v1.7 ADDS THREE RULES. (27) Numerals stay numerals; small counts used as prose stay words. (28) Call it what the founder calls it: sv, not "the save routine". (29) Do not explain what the reader built -- no gloss on gamma, the gate, falsifiers, the panel, rho; that IS the dumbing down. AND THE LINT WAS RUN AGAINST NOTHING. It has existed since v1.5 with a unit test and no user -- the same shelved-but-tested shape as I33. That is why v1.7 ships as a check rather than a fourth restatement: the lint now reports 27 and 28, and test_note_standard_v17_enforced holds any note declaring v1.7 to them, with known-good and known-bad fixtures proving it discriminates. TWO FAULTS FOUND BY RUNNING IT ON THE FIRST v1.7 NOTE. Quoted violations were being reported -- a note naming a bad form in order to correct it is doing the opposite of committing it -- so quoted text is exempt, uniformly across every rule rather than only the new ones. And the note itself carried "the machinery" where a name belonged, a Rule 19 fault, now named. verbatim: The stray-file guard scanned the root only -- and real targets live in bench/. Written this morning, widened this evening after actually measuring the two gates it does NOT cover. title: A permission denial from yesterday was recorded in five places, and each lent authority to the others.
verbatim: A permission denial from yesterday was recorded in five places, and each lent authority to the others. MEASURED 2026-08-25: this process could create a new file under ~/Desktop and stat() one, but read() and overwrite were denied, 6 attempts of 6. That was true when taken. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-26 22:36 BST: stat, read AND overwrite all succeed. WHY IT SURVIVED A WHOLE DAY UNCHALLENGED. The finding had been written into five places -- two comments in cdsfl_sv.py, a comment in the drift guard, a standing "ONE COMMAND FOR THE FOUNDER" line at the top of the operational tracker, and an item in the decisions file on the founder's desk. Each cited the same measurement, and the number of places carrying it made it read as settled. I repeated it to the founder three times today without retesting it once. A measurement of a permission is a measurement of a MOMENT, not a property. That is the same shape as the note-standard defect fixed two commits ago, where an invented rule was recorded in a lint comment and a test docstring until the tooling was teaching it back. THE CODE WAS ALWAYS RIGHT. sv ATTEMPTS the write on every save and only reports NOT REFRESHED if it actually fails; the drift guard falls back to a size comparison only when read raises. Both fallbacks are RETAINED deliberately -- access evidently moves in both directions, and a guard that assumes today's permissions misreports tomorrow. Only the comments asserted a permanent state, and only the comments are changed. The founder-facing ask is CLOSED: the mirror is refreshed and byte-identical at 185,270 bytes. The tracker line now records why it was there and why it is not needed, rather than being silently deleted. title: The supersession checker read "FOUR OLDER OPEN RULINGS" as evidence they were closed.
verbatim: The supersession checker read "FOUR OLDER OPEN RULINGS" as evidence they were closed. FOUND BY THE CHECKER FIRING ON MY OWN EDIT, hours after I wrote it. Recording the founder's proposal in the tracker added a line reading "FOUR OLDER OPEN RULINGS, named not imported", which names resources/RECOVERY.md. The checker reported it as a stale hold -- reading a statement that four decisions are OPEN as evidence they had been GIVEN. CAUSE. The RULED pattern was unanchored, so it matched the PROSE inside RECOVERY.md: "6 delete + ~17 archive candidates + 4 founder rulings; execution = ONE post-arc commit" -- a sentence COUNTING rulings that are still pending. The pattern this tool exists for is a DECLARATION, not a mention. The real 2026-08-24 defect was a heading: "# FOUNDER RULINGS, 22 August 2026". A heading is anchored to line start; prose is not. That is the whole discriminator, and it is now the pattern. VERIFIED BOTH WAYS. The current tree is clean. The checker STILL fires on the actual historical file at c8f63ec~1, 2 hits, which is the case it was built for and the one my withdrawn "not mechanically detectable" claim said was uncatchable. Reverting the anchor fails 5 tests including the new regression. ALSO IN THIS COMMIT, and it is the more important half. The tracker now records DECISION 7, THE FOUNDER'S OWN PROPOSAL, which had been written down NOWHERE: a free simulated experiment with CC1, Fable 5 and CC2 under full experimental conditions against an EXTERNAL, entirely untested target -- "Does the thing work, beyond just what we have built here and beyond just looking at and consuming itself?" It survived only in conversation and would have been lost at the next compaction. It is already load-bearing: it is why CC1 read only sizes, line counts and section counts of exp50/51/52 today and never their contents. CC1 cannot both sit on that panel and hold the ground truth, so decisions 3 and 7 must be taken together. Plus DECISION 8 (persist rho from the next run, RECOVERY.md:159, never decided, in no summary) and four OLDER open rulings named rather than imported, so the consolidated file does not pretend to be exhaustive over all time. title: Runway Stage 4B: the BR2 bridge, which was on no stage and had never been named.
verbatim: Runway Stage 4B: the BR2 bridge, which was on no stage and had never been named. Placed on the founder's ruling: after the arc and the open decisions, immediately before BR2. Inserted as 4B rather than renumbering 5, 6 and 7, whose numbers are referenced elsewhere. BR2 *IS* the external target source and was specified on 8 April -- 27 frontier STEM tasks across 8 domains. A discussion on 26 August reasoned about external targets as though they needed inventing. That was wrong, and the founder corrected it. THE TASKS ARE NOT THE GAP. All 27 exist in bench/tasks_frontier/, median 5,096 bytes, all 8 domains, and 26 of 27 carry expected_single_pass_accuracy -- a pre-registered prediction written months before any run. INCONSISTENCY 1: reference_runner_v2.py, last touched today, references tasks_frontier ZERO times. The runners that consume them were last touched 13 April, 19 March, 18 March and 15 August. BR2 as wired would run on machinery predating the two-sided gate, the falsifier-gate hardening, location-keyed convergence and the v3 patches. The whole Exp 40-55 arc hardened a runner BR2 would not use. INCONSISTENCY 2 [OPEN]: prompt and ground_truth_notes share a file in all 27 -- the structure that cost exp48 and exp49 and burned exp55. NOT shown to leak; shown to permit leaking, three times bitten. Splitting needs nothing from the rewiring and is free, so it is item 4B.1. THE INFINITE-LOOP QUESTION gets a stopping rule instead of an argument. Measured machinery commits between consecutive runs: 10, 1, 4, 4, 7, 0, 0, 0, then 32 at exp55 -- the v3 runner's first run -- and 26 since. The decay was real and broke when the instrument changed generation. Caveat stated: the proxy is confounded by cadence (exp48 and exp49 ran 100 minutes apart). Consequence: 4B.3 creates a new generation, so BR2 immediately after it runs at the PEAK of a fresh defect curve. The escape is not more hardening but refusing to let BR2 absorb the shakeout -- the free simulated experiment and a one-task burn-in are the shock absorber. Pre-registered rule: if the fix curve flattens across two consecutive probes, spend BR2; if not, that answer cost a simulated run rather than 27 real ones. Internal runway is unchanged at three shots. 4B costs about one BR2 task. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: Runway 4B.1: BR2's answers split out of the repo -- and they have been PUBLIC for 162 days.
verbatim: Runway 4B.1: BR2's answers split out of the repo -- and they have been PUBLIC for 162 days. FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-27: do 4B.1 now if straightforward. It was. WHAT MOVED. Each of the 27 encodings in bench/tasks_frontier/ held its answer in `ground_truth_notes`, in the same JSON object as the `prompt` -- the structure that removed exp48 and exp49 from every headline figure and burned exp55's target three days before it ran. 14,528 characters of answer text now live in CDSFL_experiment_keys/br2_keys/, outside any git tree, one key file per task. THE FIELD IS DELIBERATELY RETAINED, holding a pointer. run_benchmark.py:242 and run_round_robin.py:152 validate that the key is PRESENT, and 14 test files touch those loaders, so deleting it would break them. Traced before touching anything: `ground_truth_notes` never reaches a model prompt -- it is consumed at exactly two sites, both copying it into a result dict -- and no test asserts on its content. So the exposure was LATENT, not active, and a pointer makes any read of it loud rather than silently wrong. 345 dependent tests pass unchanged. ★ AND THE PART THAT NEEDS THE FOUNDER, found while verifying this. THE SPLIT DOES NOT UN-PUBLISH ANYTHING. Measured: all 27 answer-bearing files have been on the PUBLIC GitHub repository since 2026-03-18, first landing in 05df68e -- 162 DAYS, 14,528 characters, 27 of 27 files, across 4 commits on main. So BR2's answer key has been public for five months, before BR2 has ever run. This is the exp55 situation at 27 times the scale and 162 times the duration. Splitting stops the exposure growing; it cannot reverse it. title: Decision 8, persist rho -- and the record's "permanently unavailable" was refuted before acting on it.
verbatim: Decision 8, persist rho -- and the record's "permanently unavailable" was refuted before acting on it. FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-27: "Persist it." CHECKED THE PREMISE FIRST, and it did not hold. resources/RECOVERY.md:159 read: "One third of 1.7 is permanently unavailable: no archived report carries a rho series in any form." MEASURED across all 31 archived exp* reports: 22 carry per-round `rho` AND `rho_avg` for EVERY round, exp42 through exp55, complete. What was absent is ONLY the top-level `rho_history` array -- 0 of 31 -- the same hoisting that gamma_history, gamma_all_history and gamma_critical_history all get. exp44 recovers as 13 rounds: mean 0.7536, sd 0.2233, min 0.3333, max 1.0000, Spearman rs=-0.477 (p=0.099, n=13) against round index. That is an analysable series, not a gap. So the rho third of Runway 1.7 was never lost. It is RETROACTIVELY AVAILABLE ON 22 RUNS, and the replay work declared impossible can be done. RECOVERY.md corrected. THE FIX IS ONE LINE, because the runner already tracked it: rho_history is declared at :9340, appended at :10030 and checkpoint-restored at :9433, and simply never reached the report while every gamma series did. FOUND BY THE TEST CRASHING ON ITS FIRST RUN: older report generations store `rounds` as an INTEGER COUNT rather than a list of round records. The test now scopes to exp* directories, matching the measured population, and tolerates both schemas rather than assuming one. That schema split is worth knowing independently -- anything walking reports across generations will hit it. 6 tests: the write is pinned, its placement beside the gamma histories is pinned, the runner is checked to still track what it writes (a NameError there would fire at run END, after the expensive part), and the archive claim is asserted both ways -- at least 20 reports recoverable, and no recovered series covering less than 99% of its rounds, because a series present in one round of thirteen is not a series. title: Decision 1 executed: the exp55 key is purged from 80 commits, and 41 hash citations are remapped.
verbatim: Decision 1 executed: the exp55 key is purged from 80 commits, and 41 hash citations are remapped. FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-27: "Do it exactly as you suggest. Permission granted in full." WHAT WAS DONE. git filter-branch --index-filter over origin/main..HEAD, removing bench/cdsfl_registry/targets/control_two_distinct_defects_KEY.md from every commit that carried it. VERIFIED THREE WAYS, because a history rewrite that quietly changes content is worse than no rewrite: 1. HEAD TREE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. f6d3baa6d3321d785025ed03feee6cb6344f2764 before and after. NOTHING in the working tree changed. 2. KEY PURGED. 37 commits carried the blob; 0 do now. 3. NOTHING LOST. Backup tag pre-rewrite-2026-08-27 and branch backup-pre-rewrite-2026-08-27 both pin the pre-rewrite history. THE HASH REMAP. filter-branch's map directory was already cleaned up, so the old-to-new mapping was rebuilt by commit SUBJECT over the two ranges: 80 commits each side, 0 subject mismatches, so the pairing is verified rather than assumed positional. 27 hashes were cited in markdown; 21 CHANGED and 6 did not. The 6 are the expected signature -- they predate 28725d2, which introduced the key, so neither their trees nor their parents moved. 41 citations rewritten across 10 files, using a word-boundary match so a 7-hex run inside a longer hash is untouched. VERIFIED AFTER: 590 hash citations across the repository resolve to real commits. 34 do not, and NONE of them is a commit this rewrite touched -- they are Semantic Scholar corpus IDs in the similarity and stylometry notes plus foreign hashes, all non-resolving before the rewrite as well. ★ FOUNDER RULING ON THE BR2 EXPOSURE, recorded because my framing was wrong. I reported that BR2's 27 answer keys have been public since 2026-03-18, 162 days, and called the validity of BR2 an open question. The founder ruled it a NON-ISSUE: BR2 has never run, so the exposure never reached a run; the repository has never been cloned; and splitting the keys before the first run is exactly the lesson exp48, exp49 and exp55 taught, which item 4B.1 has now done. title: Decision 5 answered: G7's MERGE path is dead code, and I repeated a refuted claim about its default.
verbatim: Decision 5 answered: G7's MERGE path is dead code, and I repeated a refuted claim about its default. FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-27 on decision 5: "Do it." THE ANSWER IS NO, AND NOT BECAUSE IT IS INCAPABLE. When merge arbitration votes MERGE, reference_runner_v2.py:2183 does not merge. It sets merge_candidate_of, writes merge_blocked_reason -- "a model vote is not authority to delete a finding from the gate" -- logs MERGE WITHHELD, and returns KEEP_DISTINCT. That closure is the founder's own no-voting ruling of 2026-08-19, correctly applied. So G7 today only ever produces KEEP_DISTINCT: it is a de-duplication PREVENTER, never a merger. KEEP_DISTINCT itself is live and does real work, clearing stale MERGE verdicts so a quorum cannot be assembled from votes many rounds apart. ★ AND A CORRECTION I OWE. I told the founder G7 "ships disabled by default". MEASURED: merge_arbitration_enabled is True in EVERY config from exp40 to exp52. The False is a dataclass default that no run has ever used. That is the identical error the runner's own comment records CC1 making on 2026-08-21, where an independent Fable 5 review measured it True across exp40 to exp51 including exp46, the pre-registered matched re-run. The comment names the cause exactly: "CC1 read the default in RunnerConfig and never opened a config file." I did the same thing, five days later, having read that comment. CAN IT BE MADE CAPABLE. Not by enabling anything; it is already on. Genuine merging in the Bugzilla sense needs three things, and the data model has one: a canonical survivor -- HAS IT (result.target) the absorbed finding's CONTENT folded into the survivor -- ABSENT ENTIRELY a reversible link so a merge can be undone -- ABSENT MergeArbitrationResult carries decision, target, votes, tally and rationale. There is no content-combination step anywhere in the module or its caller. So it needs BUILDING, not enabling. And the design question underneath is the sharper one: merging by model vote is precisely the family already retired. Merging that survives the no-voting rule cannot be five models agreeing -- it needs a TOOL verdict, a programmatic demonstration that two findings are one, in the way the falsifier gate demonstrates a claim rather than polling opinion about it. Until "what counts as programmatic evidence that two findings are the same" is defined, building a merge path only relocates the voting. Put to the founder rather than answered here, because it is a definition question and definitions in this project are theirs. Tracker resume pointer advanced with the night's rulings and what remains. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: The clock hook fixed "never knew the time". It cannot fix "knew it once, then extrapolated".
verbatim: The clock hook fixed "never knew the time". It cannot fix "knew it once, then extrapolated". MEASURED 2026-08-27 01:11 BST: two notes written during this turn were stamped 01:30 and 01:35. That is 18 and 23 minutes in the FUTURE. THIS IS NOT THE DEFECT FIXED YESTERDAY, and the difference is the whole point. On 2026-08-26, commit 8f9fe35 recorded five timestamps TYPED rather than read, three in the future, and the response was a UserPromptSubmit clock hook. The hook WORKED. It supplied 00:40 at the start of this turn. The turn then ran for thirty minutes and I extrapolated forward instead of re-reading. A hook that fires at turn START cannot police a turn that RUNS for half an hour. Yesterday's fix addressed knowing; today's failure was in remembering that knowing decays. GUARDED RATHER THAN PROMISED, because this is the second variant of a defect already promised away once. note_vagueness_lint.py now compares a note's own stated stamp against the file's mtime and reports FUTURE TIMESTAMP -- the file is the only witness that does not depend on remembering to look. Two minutes of slack, because writing takes a moment and minute-rounding can legitimately land one minute ahead, and a linter that fires on rounding gets ignored. 9 tests. Known-bad is the actual 19-minute case. Known-good includes a stamp in the PAST (notes are often written up after the fact; only the future is wrong) and a one-minute rounding case, so the check cannot pass by firing on everything. Plus four never-raises cases: no stamp, missing file, unparseable date, and the wiring assertion that main actually calls it -- a check nobody runs being the exact shape this project keeps finding. Both notes corrected. feedback_read_the_clock updated: capture `date` immediately before writing a timestamp, not at turn start. The hook is a floor, not a substitute. ALSO IN THIS COMMIT: the exp52 re-authoring brief (decision 3), prepared and deliberately NOT dispatched. `cy` requires a terminal the founder can watch and a 60-second cadence; neither is possible while they sleep, and a paid two-model authoring run nobody reads for six hours defeats the protocol's purpose. The brief carries its hard constraints -- key separate from the outset, planted count NOT equal to sections minus one, every defect mechanically checkable -- and an acceptance test written before the run rather than after. title: A guard this project already had caught my own code, twenty minutes after I wrote it.
verbatim: A guard this project already had caught my own code, twenty minutes after I wrote it. test_no_script_discards_a_verdict_by_testing_the_tuple flagged note_vagueness_lint.py:213 -- `fs` bound whole from future_stamp() and then tested for truth. That guard exists because a function returning (bool, message) is TRUE in every case, including failure, and this project has been burned by it. MY CASE WAS ACTUALLY CORRECT. future_stamp returns Optional[tuple]: None, or a 2-tuple of non-empty strings that can never be falsy. So `if fs:` did the right thing. FIXED ANYWAY, and the reason is the point. At a glance `if fs:` is indistinguishable from the defect the guard exists to catch. A reader cannot tell an Optional from a verdict tuple without opening the function. title: Fable found a live regression vector: a demotion-era comment that re-seeds the design the founder ruled against.
verbatim: Fable found a live regression vector: a demotion-era comment that re-seeds the design the founder ruled against. FABLE 5 (chat instance, reading main at 3b09c6d) reported a comment in the runner stating "Gamma — REPORTED, NEVER a trigger or blocker (panel redesign 2026-05-23) … deleted as a convergence trigger on the critical-quiescence path". CONFIRMED VERBATIM. Fable placed it at ~9572; it is at 10545 in this tree, the line numbers having shifted under 88 commits Fable could not see. The text matches exactly. ★ BUT THE DIAGNOSIS IS SHARPER THAN THE REPORT, AND IT CHANGES THE FIX. The comment is HALF TRUE, and the false half is the dangerous one: TRUE gamma_all IS telemetry-only in the STATE gate. Measured: every live config has gamma_telemetry_only_until >= max_rounds (14>=12, 20>=16), and _check_gamma_gate references only that setting. Fable called this "a non-default config"; it is in fact the config in use, so the clause should be kept, not deleted. FALSE "deleted as a convergence trigger on the critical-quiescence path." _check_gamma_alt_convergence requires gamma_critical >= gamma_alt_threshold on exactly that path and says so itself: "gamma is an ACTIVE convergence condition, NOT merely 'reported'". The root cause is a CONFLATION OF TWO GATES ON TWO SERIES, proved by introspection: _check_gamma_gate references only gamma_telemetry_only_until and takes gamma_all; _check_gamma_alt_convergence references gamma_critical and emits CRITICAL_QUIESCENCE_CONVERGED. Different functions, different series, different configs. So a wholesale rewrite would have destroyed a true statement. Corrected in place, both gates named explicitly. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS, and Fable's argument here is right. Anyone grepping for gamma and landing on 10545 before 4993 restores a demotion the founder ruled against on 2026-06-10, in good faith. Fable's own earlier stale report repeated this comment back, which is direct evidence the vector fires. THE SWEEP FABLE ASKED FOR, with a negative result worth recording: no other gamma-demotion language exists in the file. The remaining hits are finding-SEVERITY demotion (EQUIPMENT_FAILURE_VERDICTS, NON_DISCRIMINATING) and the legitimate state-gate config. This one comment was the whole vector. COMMENT-ONLY: verified by diffing the file with all comment lines stripped -- zero executable lines changed. title: The 133 "pending founder ruling" were adjudicated by tool ten days ago; only the record was pending.
verbatim: The 133 "pending founder ruling" were adjudicated by tool ten days ago; only the record was pending. FOUNDER CHALLENGE 2026-08-28, and it was right on every count: "a very large and growing HIL pile was almost invariably an indication of broken/incomplete machinery, rather than the system being fundamentally incapable of clearing this pile… are these issues genuinely irreducible/non-computable, in which case it would be a genuine HIL condition?" MEASURED. They are not. scripts/adjudicate_by_repair.py, 444 lines, decides "same defect or two?" by COUNTERFACTUAL REPAIR -- apply A's fix, re-run B's falsifier, both directions must agree -- and IT ALREADY RAN, on 2026-08-18, writing experimental_notes/data/adjudication_by_repair.json. decided BOTH directions 33 (SAME 23, DIFFERENT 10) decided one direction 52 ------------------------------ tool evidence 85 of 133 (64%) UNDECIDABLE 33 DISAGREE 8 (directions conflict; reported, never resolved by preference) NO_BASELINE 7 (falsifier did not reproduce -- EQUIPMENT FAILURE, not a hard case) So at most 41 of 133 are candidates for genuine irreducibility, and those are TOOL outcomes needing more tool work, not judgements needing a human. AND THE SCRIPT SAYS SO ITSELF, in its own docstring, before any of this: "Asking the founder to adjudicate put a chemistry/engineering/programming judgement in front of the one participant with no domain access, and it is not an HIL-irreducible question. Asking a model panel to vote was worse… A panel eyeballing pairs and voting is the free pass the whole project exists to refuse." WHAT I DID WRONG. On 2026-08-27 I wrote up this ruling for the founder, recommending Option 2: route every hard pair to adjudication by default. I read RECOVERY.md:374 saying "PENDING FOUNDER RULING" and never opened the data. That is the PROBLEM GENERATOR failure the founder has named repeatedly and says I endlessly forget -- a calculator that answers by handing back 133 questions. The defect was never the pile. It was this line, stale for ten days, describing work as pending that a tool had already done. title: The report showed 0.253 while the gate read 0.453. Name which one decided.
verbatim: The report showed 0.253 while the gate read 0.453. Name which one decided. RULING B, and the founder's question was whether the display change is still valid given they proposed averaging the two series instead. IT IS, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS WHY. exp44's final four rounds: gamma 0.208 0.221 0.237 0.253 <- what a reader sees gamma_critical 0.382 0.409 0.432 0.453 <- what the GATE reads Threshold 0.30. A reader taking the unqualified "gamma" as the headline concludes the gamma condition FAILED when it held comfortably. That single misreading is the whole source of the impression that gamma does not work, and until yesterday a demotion-era comment in this file actively encouraged it. WHY NOT AVERAGE OR SUM, which the founder proposed. Measured across 94 paired observations in 10 archived runs. The two series correlate at r = 0.92 and gamma_critical reads higher in 94.7% of observations, so the founder is right that they are not rivals. But they are not two views of one curve either: gamma_critical IS gamma_all with the minor findings filtered out. Combining them re-adds the noise the filter removed. MEAN: 8 disagreements, EVERY ONE blocking a convergence gamma_critical allows. exp45 round 3 is the clearest -- gamma_critical 0.563 (critical discovery flattened) against gamma_all 0.014 (footnotes still arriving); the mean reads 0.288 and blocks, because of footnotes. That is exactly the population mismatch the two-sided gate was built to remove. SUM: 6 disagreements the other way. Two numbers each up to ~0.9 against a 0.30 threshold clears trivially; it would have converged exp44 FIVE ROUNDS EARLY. THE CHANGE IS A POINTER, NOT A RENAME. 22 archived reports carry `gamma` and `gamma_history` under the all-severity meaning, and redefining either would silently change what every one of them says. Same problem the location-keyed series had, same solution: deprecate in place. Both series stay untouched and a new `gamma_gate_series` field names the authoritative one, per round and at top level. No data duplicated. 6 tests, including two that assert the gap this exists for is REAL -- the largest divergence in the archive exceeds 0.10, and exp44 still contains a round where the legacy field reads below threshold while the gate series reads above it. If those two ever fail the pointer is decoration and should be deleted rather than kept. title: Zero of the 133 are HIL-irreducible. The 48 "undecided" reclassified by cause.
verbatim: Zero of the 133 are HIL-irreducible. The 48 "undecided" reclassified by cause. Following the 2026-08-28 finding that the 133 were tool-adjudicated ten days ago, I took the 48 undecided apart rather than leaving them as "candidates for irreducibility", which was still too generous a description. 17 NO_APPLICABLE_FIX in BOTH directions -- the finding carries no fix, so counterfactual repair had nothing to apply. title: The rho third of Runway 1.7: the "not measurable" claim was TYPED, and building it found a real numerator mismatch.
verbatim: The rho third of Runway 1.7: the "not measurable" claim was TYPED, and building it found a real numerator mismatch. FOUNDER 2026-08-28: "This recovery work however is also still to be done? Should you do it?" Yes, and doing it produced two findings. FINDING 1: THE CLAIM THAT BLOCKED IT WAS NEVER A MEASUREMENT. scripts/replay_accounting.py:224-230 prints "No archived report carries a rho series in any form -- measured across every report in bench/logs, the count of rho-shaped keys is zero ... NOT MEASURABLE from the archive and no amount of replay will make it so." Checked by AST: the word "rho" appears in that module five times and EVERY occurrence is inside a print() string. There is not one string literal equal to a rho key name and no code that counts anything. It asserts a measurement it never performs. That assertion propagated into RECOVERY.md as "one third of 1.7 is permanently unavailable" and reached the founder as a decision to make. What is actually there: 22 of 31 reports carry per-round rho AND rho_avg for every round. Absent is only a TOP-LEVEL rho_history -- which is what a top-level-only scan finds, and presumably what happened. FINDING 2, FROM ACTUALLY BUILDING THE REPLAY. scripts/replay_rho.py recomputes rho from the archived inputs and diffs against what was recorded at run time. IT FAILS ITS OWN EXIT TEST ON 10 OF 18 RUNS, and by this project's own rule -- a replay that cannot reproduce the past is measuring itself -- it therefore WITHHOLDS the churn delta rather than quietly delivering a number. The failure is the finding, and it is specific. Replayed rho is exactly novel_this_round / findings_count. Archived rho is consistently higher: exp42 round 9: archived 0.4 = 2/5, report records novel_this_round = 1 exp42 round 11: archived 0.875 = 7/8, report records 3 exp42 round 12: archived 0.3333 = 2/6, report records 1 So `novel_this_round` IS NOT THE NUMERATOR THAT FED rho. The report and the rho computation disagree about how many findings were novel in the same round -- one settled, one not. That is the SAME all-versus-settled population split that made gamma look wrong on exp41c, now appearing in a second measure. It does not establish which number is correct; that needs the run-time counts. So those are now persisted: rho_novelty_counts and rho_raw_counts, the same one-line shape as rho_history. The rho third becomes replayable rather than arguable from the next run. My own diagnostic was broken on first run and printed "round 1: archived 0.7826 -> replayed 0.7826", two identical numbers, because a next() with a default of 0 fell through to index 0 when the mismatch was in the average rather than the series. Fixed before reporting anything from it. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: A structural answer to the conflation: documents cannot check themselves, so their claims now get checkers.
verbatim: A structural answer to the conflation: documents cannot check themselves, so their claims now get checkers. FOUNDER 2026-08-27: "Make deliberate and real efforts to ensure such issues do not occur again! We have significant and previously effective resources designed to guard against such errors and conflation, such as MEMORY.md, RECOVERY.md, ONBOARDING.md, the repo and Git itself, our docs and our experimental notes. Use them as appropriate in all cases." THE CLASS, three instances in 48 hours, each reaching the founder as a decision: merge arbitration "defaults False and is unset in every exp44-52 config" -> True in EVERY config exp40..exp52. Read the dataclass, never opened a config. The SECOND time that exact error was made. "the 133 unadjudicated pairs -- PENDING FOUNDER RULING" -> adjudicated by tool on 2026-08-18, results in experimental_notes/data/. Led to recommending 133 human judgements: the problem-generator failure. "no archived report carries a rho series in any form -- measured" -> 22 of 31 do. The word "measured" described no code in that module. Identical shape every time: A PROSE CLAIM ABOUT DATA, aging silently while the data moved, and a reader who trusts the document inheriting the staleness. scripts/claims_audit.py holds a registry of claims whose data source is NAMED, and checks each one. It is deliberately narrow: it does not attempt to verify prose in general, which is not decidable. It verifies specific claims. The implied standard is the useful part -- a claim that cannot be checked does not belong in a canonical document as a fact. It found a live one on its first run: replay_accounting.py still asserted the rho claim while 24 of 34 reports refuted it. Corrected, and the correction says plainly that the word "measured" was doing work no code did. COMMISSIONED, not asserted. 10 tests. The load-bearing pair re-introduces the stale wording into the REAL tree, confirms the audit fails, and restores the file in a `finally` -- then asserts the restore was byte-exact. Without a known-bad the audit could pass forever by matching nothing, which is exactly what the vagueness linter did from v1.5 until someone finally ran it. title: The 23 SAME verdicts are 11: panel-refuted, and I re-counted it myself rather than take their word.
verbatim: The 23 SAME verdicts are 11: panel-refuted, and I re-counted it myself rather than take their word. Fable audited the detail fields of the 23 rows CC1 offered as the merge evidence base. Only 11 are clean; 12 carry at least one ERRORed leg, 22 ERROR legs in total. CC1 had read the summary counts and never opened the rows -- the same read-the-summary error as the merge-arbitration default and the 133 pairs. Independently re-counted here rather than accepted: 11 clean, 12 with an error-ish leg. Exact agreement. A model saying so is not evidence; the count is. An errored leg is an equipment failure, not a verdict, so the merge evidence base is 11 and not 23. Fable adds the consequence CC1 missed entirely: MERGED is terminal with no REOPENED exit, unlike REFUTED and CLOSED which both have one. A wrong merge is therefore unrecoverable, which raises the evidence bar rather than lowering it. title: SAME was the fall-through, so an errored falsifier did not contaminate a verdict -- it produced one.
verbatim: SAME was the fall-through, so an errored falsifier did not contaminate a verdict -- it produced one. Fable flagged 12 contaminated SAME rows. Following it into _direction rather than accepting the count found the hole is bigger and is not confined to SAME: the final `return "SAME"` was the fall-through, so any leg that was not CONFIRMED landed there, and the same fall-through reaches DIFFERENT. Measured per-direction across both recorded legs, not per-row on the first: 40 of 178 leg-bearing directions rest on legs that cannot carry them 29 SAME + 11 DIFFERENT, touching 34 of 133 pairs Only three leg values ever occur -- REFUTED 165, CONFIRMED 138, ERROR 53. A verdict now requires self=REFUTED and other in (REFUTED, CONFIRMED). Anything else is INCONCLUSIVE_EQUIPMENT, which says what actually happened. The FIX_INEFFECTIVE branch is untouched: self=CONFIRMED is a real observation about the fix and holds whatever the other leg did. This matters because MERGED is terminal with no REOPENED exit, unlike REFUTED and CLOSED. Wiring the merge path to the old adjudicator would have deleted findings unrecoverably on the strength of crashes. Commissioned rather than asserted: removing the guard fails exactly the 5 known-bad leg pairs and leaves the 5 known-good ones passing. A test also pins the archived counts, so the corrected figures in RECOVERY cannot go stale the way the three claims refuted earlier tonight did. title: The ERROR legs are two different things, and only one of them is equipment.
verbatim: The ERROR legs are two different things, and only one of them is equipment. Followed the panel finding one step further: what IS the ERROR? Re-ran 25 findings from ERROR-bearing pairs against the pristine tree and captured stderr for the 9 that errored. Two classes, not one. exp45 C0003/C0022 error because ImmuneMemory._check_count RAISES on a negative count -- the guard firing IS the answer the falsifier asked for, so the right verdict is REFUTED and the recorded one is ERROR. The other 7 are FileNotFoundError on missing targets, which is real equipment failure, and 6 of those are on exp48, already excluded for the key read. Recorded rather than generalised. The first example alone would have supported "the ERROR legs are refutations in disguise", which the other 7 refute. The recorded legs were also measured on a PATCHED tree, not the pristine one, so this probe measures an adjacent condition; 16 of 25 do not error pristine at all, and exp44 and exp49 are entirely unexplained. Note says so. Not fixed: separating "target guard fired" from "instrument broke" changes verdict semantics in the runner core, and tonight is not the night for that. title: Canary seeding, built and tested: convergence as a demonstration rather than an absence.
verbatim: Canary seeding, built and tested: convergence as a demonstration rather than an absence. Founder ruling 2026-08-27 on the fable reviewer Note 5 route B: "Build it, test it, implement it in its own independent 3 model panel review." The two-sided gate reads only what reviewers said, so it cannot tell a clean document from a dead panel -- both are silence. A seeded defect of known type and location discriminates them: silence plus killed canaries is affirmative evidence of exhaustion, silence plus missed canaries is a panel that stopped looking. Mutation testing (DeMillo/Lipton/Sayward 1978) pointed at reviewers. title: A test file that switched itself off when its component broke, and two gates that could never say no.
verbatim: A test file that switched itself off when its component broke, and two gates that could never say no. Instrument confirmation panel, 2026-08-28. Both reviewers ran mutation tests over all 34 inventory rows and independently refuted the "32 of 34 commissioned" figure. CC2 scored 23 confirmed, 9 refuted at the named test, 2 refuted outright. The worst one, found by both: test_immune_memory_consumption.py computed its own skip guard by CALLING compute_sk, the component under test. Reproduced here -- blinding compute_sk took the file from 45 passed to 33 passed, 12 SKIPPED, exit code 0. Break the component and its tests stop running rather than failing. The guard now checks the tooling it claims to check, ruff and bandit, and the same break produces 11 failures. check_sk_threshold could be hardwired to `return True` with 321 tests passing. That is the Valley of Bad Fixes gate, live in 19 of 19 configurations, and nothing anywhere required it to reject anything. Now three assertions: a fix below S* is refused, one above is admitted, and s_floor can refuse a fix the threshold would admit. _update_finding_statuses could have its CHALLENGE collection deleted with every test naming it green -- a model disagreeing with a CONFIRMED finding would vanish, contested would undercount, and gate condition (c) would open early. And a suite-wide guard so the class cannot return: no skipif condition, or any module-level name it resolves to, may call a function defined in the runner. Two of these three did not catch their defect when first written and were rewritten until they did. The CHALLENGE mutation ALSO had to be corrected: the line occurs twice in the file, so replacing the first occurrence patched a different function entirely and the test was being blamed for a bad mutation. title: Probe whether archived falsifiers touch their targets at all -- measurement only, no verdict changes.
verbatim: Probe whether archived falsifiers touch their targets at all -- measurement only, no verdict changes. Tonight the instrument panel reconfirmed that reverify_falsifier records CONFIRMED for a falsifier that never touches its target, and added scale: 346 of 372 archived falsifiers fired on every historical version and were never quiet. That is suggestive, not decisive -- a defect genuinely present throughout gives the same pattern. This supplies the decisive test. Replace the target with unrelated but VALID python and re-run. A surviving CONFIRMED is proof the falsifier never touched the file. ERROR and REFUTED are both evidence of coupling, so the probe undercounts independence and never overcounts it, which is the safe direction for a number that would be used to discount evidence. The substitute is deliberately valid rather than broken: a syntax error would make every falsifier ERROR and the probe would measure the breakage instead. Two corrections made during the build, both from checking rather than assuming. The archive rows carry no falsifier_code field, so an earlier draft would have reported every row undecidable while looking like a completed measurement; the source is now resolved from each run report. And the first field name, reads_ target, over-claimed: coupling here is established by IMPORT, so a falsifier that imports its target and then asserts something unrelated scores identical to a rigorous one. Renamed, and the limit is stated where the number is printed. First 8 rows: all CONFIRMED on the real target, all ERROR on the substitute -- coupled, every one. That is the opposite of what 346-of-372 suggests, and the two do not conflict; they answer different questions. Nothing here changes a verdict, a gate or a stored finding. title: Measured: 9 of 372 falsifiers are target-independent, not 346. The scare shrinks by two orders of magnitude.
verbatim: Measured: 9 of 372 falsifiers are target-independent, not 346. The scare shrinks by two orders of magnitude. Ran the probe over the whole archive. Verdict pairs (real target -> unrelated file): CONFIRMED -> ERROR 346 coupled: reached for the target, could not use it REFUTED -> ERROR 10 coupled CONFIRMED -> CONFIRMED 9 TARGET-INDEPENDENT: never touched the file ERROR -> ERROR 5 undecidable CONFIRMED -> REFUTED 2 coupled So 348 of 372 are coupled to their target and 9 are provably not -- 2.4 percent, not the 93 percent the 346-of-372 figure invites. Those two figures do not conflict, they answer different questions: 346 fired on EVERY HISTORICAL VERSION, which this probe does not address and which remains unexplained. The 9 sit in three runs on three files: exp44 C0007/C0008/C0022/C0023/C0078 on bench/evidence.py, exp46 C0023 on bench/dm/_shadow_stage6.py, and exp47 C0010/C0058/C0061 on bench/dm/_divergence.py. Their falsifier evidence is void. CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE NUMBER: coupling is established by IMPORT, not by test content. A falsifier that imports its target and then asserts something unrelated to the accused defect scores identical to a rigorous one. This rules out only the crudest failure. It is not a clean bill of health for the other 348. Measurement only. No verdict, gate or stored finding was changed. title: Canary build panel: nine defects found in a module I had already attacked myself, all fixed.
verbatim: Canary build panel: nine defects found in a module I had already attacked myself, all fixed. Both reviewers ran the module rather than reading it. Ranked by what they cost. SECURITY The guard protected the wrong tree. REPO_ROOT was parents[1] of the MODULE, so a copy running in a throwaway worktree -- which is how panels are dispatched, including this one -- would read a catalogue in the canonical tracked tree. Containment is now decided by walking for a .git, so ANY work tree is covered. Path.resolve() does not case-normalise on macOS and relative_to is a string comparison, so a case-mangled path read the key. The reviewers DISAGREED here and both were right about what they ran: mangling a component BELOW the root was already refused, mangling a component OF the root read it. Verified both, fixed with os.path.normcase + realpath. A hardlink made outside a tracked tree read the tracked bytes. Refused now. And the finding I had recorded as a mere docstring caveat: the SEEDED DOCUMENT is itself an answer key, and a worse one than the catalogue, because git diff returns the planted set at precision 1.000 with no key needed -- MANIFEST.md measured exactly this on 2026-07-29, Fisher p = 1.3e-05. seed() now refuses a target inside a work tree. MEASUREMENT An id present in BOTH splits let a calibration kill score as held-out detection, which is the precise Goodhart failure the split exists to prevent. An empty or whitespace generator name counted as a second generator and defeated the multi-generator guard; generators now normalise before counting. The denominator was unlinked from what was actually seeded, so an unseeded and therefore unkillable canary silently deflated every model. p_hat now requires the seed manifest. Catches for ids in no catalogue were silently intersected away, hiding upstream id drift; refused. BLINDING It scanned the whole document rather than what the edit INTRODUCED, producing a confirmed false refusal that would have bitten the biology corpus: a clean target saying "a seeded random number generator" was rejected outright. It now counts tokens against the clean text. Plurals were also uncovered -- \\bmutant\\b does not match "mutants". And the docstring claimed the split name was checked when it was not; it is now, and the claim is true. PROVENANCE My docstring said exp48 happened "through a path that looked innocuous at the call site". The record says otherwise: a MODEL wrote a falsifier that opened the key, and its recorded reason was that editing the file would destroy "a seeded fault the panel is scored on". SEEDING CREATED THE MOTIVE. That is the closest thing to a base rate this design has and it indicts the design rather than excusing it. Corrected in place. 42 tests, each pinned with the attack the reviewer actually ran. title: rho becomes a contributory condition of convergence, not a veto. Founder ruling 2026-08-29.
verbatim: rho becomes a contributory condition of convergence, not a veto. Founder ruling 2026-08-29. "It is a contributory condition of convergence, not a veto. It was never intended as this." And: if it blocks convergence, that is "pretty much the opposite of what it should do." The founder is right about the inversion. rho detects that no new meaningful discoveries are being made. Taken with a flattened gamma that is EVIDENCE THE SPACE IS EXHAUSTED, not evidence against it. Blocking on it made rho anti-correlated with the outcome it certifies: the closer a run got to genuine convergence, the closer it got to being refused for churning. Two veto sites removed. _evaluate_gate_conditions: churn was appended to `failures`. _check_gamma_alt_convergence: churn was an EARLY RETURN, so it fired before the two-sided gate was evaluated at all -- a run could satisfy both halves and still be refused for the very quiescence the gate exists to certify. Nothing is hidden. churn is still computed, still recorded, and now carried into the reason string on all seven return paths, so it appears on every verdict. f AND sy, as required. z3 (three properties, all discharged): P1 new predicate true while a gate half is false -> unsat. It can never converge without BOTH gamma_critical >= threshold AND K zero-critical rounds. The two-sided gate is the real guard and it still holds. P2 something converged before but not now -> unsat. Strict widening; no previously valid convergence is lost. P3 states that newly converge -> EXACTLY ONE: gamma flattened AND K zero-critical AND churning. The blast radius is precisely the case the ruling was issued about and nothing else. Archive replay, 21 runs carrying a rho series: churn was eligible and true in exactly ONE, exp42_composer_takeupslack at round 12, rho_avg 0.1921. That is the run Fable found. exp43 dips lower, 0.1587, but at round 7, before churn is eligible, so it was never affected either way. Two tests asserted the OLD rule and now fail by design. Inverted rather than deleted, so the change of rule is visible where the old one was encoded, and each is paired with a new guard: churn must not change the verdict, must still be REPORTED on it, and must not be able to manufacture a convergence while critical findings are still arriving. title: The fix-efficacy probe: ask whether a fix cures the defect its OWN falsifier demonstrates.
verbatim: The fix-efficacy probe: ask whether a fix cures the defect its OWN falsifier demonstrates. Founder, 2026-08-29: "We should already have much of this machinery. Why isn t it being used in these specific cases?" The founder is right, and the answer is better than expected -- the machinery exists IN FULL and was built for something else. What runs today asks "did this fix break anything" (ruff, mypy, bandit and the experiment s generic test_cmd, against a sandbox copy). It never asks "does this fix cure the defect THIS finding claims". That is FIX_INEFFECTIVE, and it is 16 of the 48 undecided pairs. The obvious repair fails, measurably. A sandbox copy at another path is invisible to 57 of 70 exp44 falsifiers, which reach their target by IMPORT -- every probe would report "ineffective", confidently and wrongly. And adjudicate_by_repair s write-to-the-live-target-and-restore is unusable in flight: the runner hashes the target every round, and a kill between write and restore corrupts the article. So this reuses the discrimination control s overlay, built 2026-08-22 and never reused: a throwaway repo root, symlink-mirrored, identical except for ONE file, so imports resolve through it and the real tree is never touched. Plus its tripwire, which MEASURES that the overlay is load-bearing instead of trusting it. Three passes in the order that makes a wrong answer unreachable: interception, then baseline reproduction, THEN the verdict. The first two are the only ways a sound fix could be falsely condemned and both are checked before any verdict can be produced. My own test caught a real defect in the first version. The tripwire is an import that raises, so a falsifier that READS THE FILE AS TEXT sees only the raising source, finds nothing, and exits clean -- read as "never touches the target". It would have refused a verdict on every path-reading falsifier. Interception now accepts either route: the tripwire firing, or a rewritten absolute path. Cross-verified against the post-hoc adjudicator on exp44. They agree where both looked (C0012). The apparent disagreement on C0011 is not one: C0011 appears in no similarity pair, and the post-hoc tool only ever examines findings that HAVE a near-duplicate. Which is the larger finding. Across the archive, 382 findings carry both a falsifier and a proposed fix. 85 appear in an adjudicated pair. THE OTHER 297 -- 78 percent -- have never been checked for fix efficacy by any instrument at all, because a finding with a bad fix and no twin was never in scope for anything. Decides nothing. It cannot close, open, merge or refute. Not wired to the feedback channel; that is a founder ruling. 10 tests, including that the real target is byte-identical afterwards and no overlay leaks.
