title: `rs` now has to report the recovery script's exit code, and it never had an obligation at all
verbatim: `rs` now has to report the recovery script's exit code, and it never had an obligation at all TWO FOUNDER-APPROVED FIXES. 1. THE AMBIGUOUS SENTENCE THAT CAUSED A REAL MISREADING. The overnight report said "that inventory is now known to be incomplete in 2 directions", meaning the inventory FILE omits rows. The founder read it as "the night's work is not fully inventoried", which is the more natural reading of that sentence, and I wrote it. Now: "The night's work is fully inventoried. What is incomplete is the inventory FILE itself, which is missing rows in 2 directions." Corrected in both the TTS text and the markdown companion. 2. `rs` MUST NOW REPORT AN EXIT CODE, AND THE ROOT CAUSE WAS STRUCTURAL. During the `rc` run this morning I executed scripts/cdsfl_recover.py --full, piped it to `tail`, and reported that it ran -- without ever examining its exit status. Re-run properly afterwards: exit 0, 520 lines, empty stderr. It had succeeded, but that was an assumption at the time. MEASURED, and it explains why nothing prompted me: of the 22 recognised commands (excluding model routes), only 17 carry an obligation -- 77.3%, Wilson [56.6%, 89.9%]. `rs` was one of the 5 SILENT ones, named in the turn and asking for nothing. The others are `r`, `rt`, `x`, `y`; `x` and `y` legitimately need no artefact, but `r` and `rt` are read/recover commands with real requirements and no statement of them. Flagged, not changed -- only `rs` was approved. `rs` now carries an obligation demanding the exit code be captured AND reported, plus the universal checks, the tracker, RECOVERY, MEMORY and the MC command table. Verified by executing the hook, not by reading it. The definition is updated in all 4 documented locations as well. ALSO: `ag` added to the project table and REPRODUCING.md, closing the last parsed-but-undocumented gap -- the `t` failure inverted. AND A CORRECTION TO THE PREMISE OF THE INSTRUCTION. The founder asked that the duplicate removal also cover his canonical Desktop MC file. Measured: `ext`, `rc` and `rr` are absent from ~/Desktop/keyboard_shortcuts.txt and always were. That file only ever carried `rs`, `re` and `ag`. There was nothing to remove; his own reference never adopted the duplicates. Suite 5350 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors. title: Five approved fixes: Opus seats, severity wiring, round-0 root cause, S* promoted, second key store
verbatim: Five approved fixes: Opus seats, severity wiring, round-0 root cause, S* promoted, second key store Founder go-ahead 2026-09-07, under a/f/e/sy/d. 1. THE SIMULATED SEATS RUN OPUS, NOT SONNET. "They should be Opus Agents. Opus is your dedicated coding platform. Sonnet is its 'chatbot' cousin and significantly less capable." Sonnet was a default in 2 function signatures plus a bare literal in a third file, with NO rationale anywhere in the record, and `--models` is a COUNT so there was no way to choose at all. A stand-in weaker than the seats it stands in for biases the rehearsal in the one direction that makes it useless: it under-finds, and the run looks cleaner than the real one will be. `--model` now exists and defaults to opus. 2. THE SIMULATED RUN NOW EXERCISES THE SEVERITY WORK IT EXISTS TO STUDY. The harness built RunnerConfig with 24 keyword arguments and severity_calibration_ enabled was not among them, so it took its default of False and the sweep returned 0 immediately. latent_tagger_enabled feeds the same path and was equally absent. Both now passed, both default ON, `--no-severity-calibration` to opt out. 24 -> 26 keyword arguments, verified by AST. 3. ROUND-0 ESCALATION ROOT CAUSE. `_apply_routing` had NO round guard: a finding whose rungs failed in ONE round was stamped irreducible, and the comment called that "full routing ladder exhausted". MEASURED over 83 archived escalations: 33 carry no falsifier code, Wilson [29.9%, 50.5%]; 49 carry no S_k evaluation, Wilson [48.3%, 69.0%]. Roughly half were never assessed, then labelled as findings no machine could assess. Now deferred instead, using state that already exists -- no new mechanism, no round counter. HONEST LIMIT: replaying the archive, the new predicate defers 19 of 83, 22.9%, Wilson [15.2%, 33.0%] -- and NO archived run falls under the alarm bound of 2. Necessary, not proven sufficient. The alarm stays unchanged; it was right. The first version read `sk_result`, which tripped a structural guard: that field is the only carrier of R_k(0) and must be read nowhere outside its writer. Now a flat `sk_evaluated` boolean carrying no R_k(0), so the invariant is preserved. 4. THE CORRECTED S* THRESHOLD IS PROMOTED (ruling of 2026-09-06, "better to run with corrected values and precision"). The pair is INVERTED, not dropped: the shipped verdict is still recorded, so decisions stay auditable in both systems. At the shipped operating point sk=0.30 now REJECTS at 0.504931 where it passed at 0.0. Over 1100 grid points the corrected gate is looser at 0, Wilson [0.000%, 0.348%], stricter at 215. It can only ever reject more. MY FIRST VERSION WAS INERT AND READ AS DONE. I called sk_break_even(R, q, nu_b, nu_f) against a signature of (nu_b, nu_f, q, R), so it returned None on every real input and fell through to the shipped gate. The P-pass caught it: 1100 of 1100 identical verdicts, impossible if the corrected floor were in force. 5. THE SECOND PLAINTEXT KEY STORE IS COVERED. ~/CDSFL_keys held 5 files -- 2 canary catalogues and 3 seed manifests, all naming planted defects -- and NO scan pattern matched them, so the status could read VAULTED with answer-key-class material at mode 644. Folded in; scan extended. Status now reports 31 + 5. AND A REGISTER, per the founder: "Humans sometimes forget passwords. The last thing we need is for you to forget what you have called a thing." `vault_keys.sh register` describes every key resource -- names, purposes, hashes, no answers -- readable WITHOUT the passphrase, mirrored to the Desktop. Its first run proved the point: the existing 174,112-byte archive predates the manifest feature, so NOTHING on disk records what is inside it, and the 2 completed exams' answer keys are nowhere loose on the filesystem. `unvault` is therefore no longer optional in the sealing procedure. Suite 5351 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The panel broke 4 of my 5 fixes. All repaired, and the two seats disagreed on the worst one.
verbatim: The panel broke 4 of my 5 fixes. All repaired, and the two seats disagreed on the worst one. Both free seats reviewed all 5 inside a copy of the repo under the project's FORMAL simplest-sufficient standard, quoted to them in full. They found defects in 4, and they DISAGREED on Fix 3 -- adjudicated by execution, never by counting seats. FIX 3, THE ADJUDICATION. cc2: my deferral silently de-triggered the alarm. fable: the alarm still fires. MEASURED across the 6 archived runs that alarm: my predicate silenced 3, Wilson [18.8%, 81.2%]; cc2's OWN proposed predicate silenced 5. Both seats were wrong about the remedy and cc2 was right about the fault -- `irreducible_escalation` did TWO jobs, excluding an item from the A4 blocker AND counting it toward the alarm, so any deferral silenced the alarm unless the count was repaired too. Those runs would have burned to max_rounds and ended BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, spending paid dispatch on rounds that cannot close, which is exactly what halting exists to prevent. "The alarm stays unchanged" was false by execution when I wrote it. Repaired three ways, every one extending machinery that already existed: * the predicate is now EQUIPMENT_FAILURE_VERDICTS (line 1373), whose own comment already states the rule. My version re-derived a subset of it -- "no falsifier_code" coincides with UNTOOLABLE at 22 of 22 -- and MISSED the 25 entries whose falsifier RAN AND CRASHED. And `sk_evaluated` was dead where the defect lives: _apply_routing runs at 12442, _evaluate_sk_for_findings at 12713. * irreducible_queue_count counts deferred items, so the alarm is byte-for-byte shipped behaviour: 4 alarming runs before, 4 after, 0 silenced. * unverified_critical_count honours `exhausted`, already honoured by its sibling open_crit_high_count ("this cannot block for ever"), so a deferred critical cannot block A4 for the life of the run. Result: 70 of 83 archived escalations, Wilson [75.0%, 90.6%], are now deferred rather than falsely called irreducible, with the alarm unchanged. FIX 4. fable supplied the better repair and it DELETES machinery: the gate needs no root-finding and no fallback, because break-even is defined by compute_rk(R,q,s)==R and the only question is the sign at the s under test. My fallback delegated to the shipped gate on 21.56% of the reachable slice and admitted risk-RAISING fixes in 489 of 4800 sampled cells. cc2 supplied the missing guard: R == 1 is what the non-finite guard coerces a corrupt R_old to, and under a pure sign test nothing raises risk there, so everything passed. Both applied. Now, over 13,750 points: 0 looser than shipped and 0 admissions of a risk-raising fix, both Wilson [0.000%, 0.028%]. Also cc2: `s_star` keeps the shipped raw value because scripts/measure_rk_and_gate_are_disconnected.py walks that key across the archive; the corrected effective threshold gets `s_star_effective`. FIX 5. cc2 proved in a sandbox that the manifest and count were TOP-LEVEL ONLY -- `shasum -a 256 *` errors on br2_keys/, 2>/dev/null swallowed it and `|| true` cleared the status -- so the manifest omitted 27 of 31 keys, `verify` compared against the truncated manifest and PASSED, and the register described only what it listed. The register's own stated purpose was defeated. fable found the fold loop and the register loop expanding the store list UNQUOTED, so a store path with a space is silently NOT FOLDED at seal time: keys left in plaintext while the operator believes they are sealed. My own new test then found a THIRD top-level count in unvault. All fixed. On refusing to seal an unclassified key the seats split; synthesis: do not block (cc2's argument that it makes the safe action require a code edit is stronger), but write the register AS PART of sealing (fable's point that seal time is the unique enforcement moment) and make UNCLASSIFIED loud on stderr. FIX 2. Both seats independently: the wiring is sound and MY CLAIM WAS FALSE. There is a third gate. `latent` is true for 1 of 467 falsifier-CONFIRMED criticals, 0.21%, Wilson [0.04%, 1.20%], and severity_is_proven requires a stamped proof. So the flags exercise the tagger and the sweep, not the demotion. The comment now says so instead of implying the opposite, and the counters are recorded into the run report so the question is answerable from the artefact. FIX 1. Sound, minimal, both seats agree -- except my comment complained that the model was "a bare literal with no parameter at all" and then left it one. It is a parameter now. Suite 5363 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The additive standard, enforced in both directions -- and it was itself unwired
verbatim: The additive standard, enforced in both directions -- and it was itself unwired FOUNDER, standing: "never disable or remove a feature; removal only when something better renders it redundant." He asked whether it could be mechanically enforced, and whether the 3 options I offered were exclusive or complementary. THE IRONY THAT SETTLED IT. Checking the record first: the rule lived in ONE memory note recording that it had been pasted into ONE panel brief on 2026-08-31. It was in NO standing-rules file and NOT in the dispatcher's SYSTEM prompt. THE RULE GOVERNING WHETHER WORK IS ADDITIVE WAS ITSELF AN ADDITION WIRED TO NOTHING. It failed its own standard, which is the strongest available argument for wiring it rather than restating it. AND I PRESENTED 3 OPTIONS AS A MENU, which breaks feedback_binary_thinking -- "check composability before presenting proposals as alternatives." Measured instead. Injecting one defect per layer and running all 3 guards against each: injected defect L1 L2 L3 1: standard dropped from SYSTEM prompt FAIL pass pass 2: a capability removed, not retired pass FAIL pass 3: new switch no test reaches pass pass FAIL The matrix is the IDENTITY. Zero overlap: composed they catch 3/3, the best single layer catches 1/3, the best pair 2/3. No layer substitutes for another and every omission leaves one defect class wholly unguarded. They were never alternatives. THE RULE IS ENFORCED SYMMETRICALLY, on this project's own evidence. Since 2026-08-01, 11 confirmed defects were ADDITIONS that did nothing and 0 were removals of something needed -- addition-side share 100%, Wilson [74.1%, 100.0%]. An unqualified "never remove" points at the failure mode that has not occurred and away from the one that keeps happening. The removal half still binds: the one near-miss was CC1 proposing to replace the model-derived severity with a rubric it had ALREADY measured as no better than chance (kappa = -0.0227), caught by the founder rather than by a mechanism. So "better" is made decidable -- removal requires a COMMITTED MEASUREMENT showing the replacement dominates on a named property. WHAT LANDED * The standard is in the dispatcher's SYSTEM prompt BY CONSTRUCTION, so a seat cannot miss it because of who wrote the brief; and in .claude/CLAUDE.md, docs/WORKING_DIRECTIVES.md and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md as `additive-standard`. * scripts/capability_snapshot.py DERIVES the capability set -- 160 names across config fields, MC commands, vault subcommands and public entry points -- so the register is never a number someone types. A name may leave only via RETIRED, which must cite the successor and the measurement. * A RATCHET on the addition side: 22 of 89 config fields are named in no test, Wilson [16.9%, 34.6%]. Pinned, not demanded -- failing a suite on a backlog teaches people to delete the test. What it forbids is GROWTH. MY OWN TEST VIOLATED execute-do-not-grep AND THE P-PASS CAUGHT IT. The first layer-1 test sliced the source between the SYSTEM parens, which includes COMMENTS, so renaming a comment left it green while the prompt text could be gone. It now evaluates the constant. Each layer was then broken deliberately and each failed as it should. Suite 5374 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The panel's tool-call counter was 0 by construction, and I invented a provenance for a number that was already right
verbatim: The panel's tool-call counter was 0 by construction, and I invented a provenance for a number that was already right Panel `panel_toollog_20260907T152800Z`, seats cc2 (Opus) and fable, both with provable tool logs for the first time in this dispatcher. Suite 5392 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors under --netguard-strict. THE COUNTER COULD ONLY EVER SAY 0. `confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.dispatch` set `tool_log = []` and reassigned it on 1 of 3 route branches -- the `openrouter` one. The `claude_cli` branch carrying cc2 and fable never touched it, so `n_tool_calls` read 0 for every Claude seat on every panel this dispatcher ever ran, while the docstring 12 lines above promised every seat's calls were recorded and "checkable rather than asserted". `set_tool_log_sink` existed, is thread-local (safe under the pool), and also switches the CLI to stream-json -- the only format carrying tool_use blocks. 1 of 37 dispatchers wired it, Wilson [0.5%, 13.8%]. Built and unwired, the shape this same file names 40 lines below about its sibling `set_panel_cwd`. Proof by execution, not reading: the next dispatch gave cc2 33 calls and fable 26. I CORRECTED A NUMBER THAT DID NOT NEED CORRECTING AND FABRICATED ITS HISTORY. `sk_threshold_shadow` read "3181 of 3181"; I changed it to 3816 and wrote into the permanent record that 3181 was `dynamic_management.py`'s line count. False, and never tested -- that file is 78 lines. Both seats measured independently: 3181 records store `s_star` as float 0.0 and 635 as the string "0", confined to 4 sim45_* families that stringify every numeric. Strict `x == 0.0` gives 3181, coercing `float(x) == 0.0` gives 3816. Neither number was ever an error -- 2 predicates over 1 corpus. Sequence kept in the docstring because no party was right by holding a position: cc2 flagged it, I refuted cc2 on a bad measurement, I reversed and adopted cc2's untested theory, and cc2 re-measured and refuted its own theory. Corpus corrected too (bench/logs holds 6663 JSON files / 3816 records; quarantine excluded holds 78 more; the "7351 files" figure matched neither), and `measure_sk_threshold_gate_fire_rate.py` was miscited as an independent route -- it never reads `s_star` and agrees only by exact co-occurrence. The load-bearing claim survives: `passes_threshold` reads false 0 times under every method and corpus. THE CHECKER I BUILT COULD NEVER FAIL ON ITS OWN DEFECT CLASS. cc2 proved it structural: at k = n the Wilson lower bound n/(n + z**2) is strictly increasing, so a stale interval from any upward correction is necessarily wider, and the "wider is conservative" rule forgave it. Repaired via `_n_that_fits`, which already computed the implied band and was only called on the failing path. cc2 also defeated the attribution rules 4 ways; the serious one, "3816 of 3816 across 70 files, Wilson 95% CI [...]", was disarmed by the bare integer 70. THE OPERATOR CONTROL PLANE WAS OUTSIDE EVERY WATCH. At 15:04:45 a sandboxed seat wrote to the real ~/.claude/settings.json; `canonical_was_touched` digests tracked repo files and $HOME is not among them. `control_plane_fingerprint` and `control_plane_was_touched` now cover 143 files. Detection, not prevention -- rewriting HOME would break OAuth exactly as --bare did on 2026-07-29. A REJECTED ATTEMPT'S TOOL CALLS WERE ERASED by the attempt replacing them, since the sink write sits inside the retry loop and write_text replaces. 7 calls then 2 recorded as 2. The bias runs the wrong way: `accept_reply_or_work` rejects the short reply, so the erased attempt is systematically the busiest. Now accumulates, with a per-attempt breakdown, plus failure-path counter keys and a stale-sink freshness guard. A CITATION CHECKER MANUFACTURING ITS OWN FINDINGS: `test_line_citations_resolve` matched [A-Za-z0-9_/] with no hyphen, cutting every dated filename at its last hyphen (`confer_panel_2026-08-28.py:173` -> `28.py`). 913 citations parsed, 2 mangled, 0 hyphenated citations genuinely missing. ARITHMETIC IN 2 DELIVERED NOTES: "90 escalated + 41 irreducible across 6,929 = 1.30%, Wilson [1.06%, 1.59%]" -- 90 + 41 = 131 = 1.89%; that percentage and interval were 90's alone. Corrected additively with all 3 figures. Attribution recorded BEFORE the alarm: the canonical-tree alarm named 7 files and a pre-dispatch snapshot shows all 7 are main-session edits, so no seat touched the tree. The standing rule not to edit during a live panel was nonetheless broken, and cc2's "that test was never committed" is an artefact of it -- the test was committed after its sandbox copy was taken. New: scripts/wilson_interval_consistency.py, and 3 test files -- test_stated_gate_count_matches_measurement_2026-09-07.py, test_control_plane_containment_2026-09-07.py, test_tool_log_survives_retries_2026-09-07.py. Each falsified by reintroducing the defect it guards. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: One defect shape, 12 instances, and 2 things that would have made a PoC release misleading
verbatim: One defect shape, 12 instances, and 2 things that would have made a PoC release misleading Suite 5400 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed in 544 s under --netguard-strict, pytest exit code 0 -- captured directly rather than through a pipe, because a pipeline reports its LAST command's status, which is the same defect class this file fixed in vault_keys.sh and which I then reproduced in my own monitoring command. THE SHAPE: A BOUNDED TRAVERSAL STANDING IN FOR A COMPLETE ONE. The `chmod 600 "$STORE"/*` bug that cost the founder 3 failed seals and a 60-mile round trip was the 5th instance in one file. A sweep for that class ran 14 agents over 406 tool calls: 8 findings raised, 7 CONFIRMED by adversarial verification that reproduced each by execution, 1 REFUTED. A SAFETY GATE COULD NOT SEE THE REPOSITORY. `vault_keys.sh` scanned for stray plaintext keys with `find "$HOME" -maxdepth 5`. The repo sits 2 levels below $HOME, so a FILE in bench/cdsfl_registry/targets/ is at depth 6 -- the directory the Exp 48 leak came from, and where the exp48-53 answer keys were tracked. Measured: bounded 0 matches, unbounded pruned 6. bench/arc_sequencer.sh:50 launches an entire experiment arc on that verdict. Cost of the repair, measured: 0.37 s -> 8.56 s for the scan, `status` 2.15 s -> 11.5 s, once per arc. It also invalidated a committed number: "the corrected patterns match 0 files inside the repository" came from the truncated walk; the true count is 6. Removing the ceiling exposed 2 defects it had been masking. `*canary*.json` matched 6 run-output files whose DIRECTORY is named sim45_canary_*, none answer-bearing (0 canary_id / defect_id / planted_location / seeded_defects) -- left broad it would have blocked every arc on ordinary logs; narrowed to `canary_catalogue_*.json`, which is what the 2 real catalogues are named, with the residual stated. And, surfaced only by writing a fixture with an EMPTY CDSFL_LEGACY_STORES, a trailing `|` in the exclusion alternation matches the empty string, so `^(...)/ ` matches every absolute path and EVERY stray file is suppressed. A total false all-clear from one empty config value. TWO RELEASE BLOCKERS, both found by review seats, both fixed. 1. docs/EXPERIMENTAL_RESULTS.md reported Exp 48 as "γ_crit 0.8847 -- the highest pair in the record" with 0 occurrences of C0012, key access or compromis, while cdsfl_core_formal.md:539 states the figure "cannot be reported as a blind measurement". The disclosure existed in the overnight notes, the integrity note and the schema -- and nowhere a reader would look. Added. 2. `bench/tools/simulated_bench.py --scripted` runs 18/18 stages with every API credential unset (verified by execution) and was mentioned 0 times in START_HERE.md, README.md, docs/REPRODUCING.md and scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py. Every documented path led to paid dispatch, so a reader would conclude the project needs the author's keys. It never did. Documented in both entries. THE PANEL REFUTED ITS OWN §10 CONVERGENCE DECLARATION when 2 commissioned checks returned above-threshold findings -- the sufficiency criterion behaving as specified, on the first dispatch ever to carry the formal schema in its system prompt (measured: 0 of 37 dispatchers had, Wilson [0.0%, 9.4%]). MY OWN TOOL-COUNTER FIX WAS PARTIAL AND UNGUARDED. Mutating `set_tool_log_sink(str(_sink))` to `None` restores the original "0 by construction" defect and 88 of 88 tests still passed. A 4th path was never enumerated: the except arm reads `tool_log`, but the sink is read back only AFTER call_claude_cli returns, so n_tool_calls read 0 EXACTLY WHEN A SEAT FAILED -- the case the panel hit on 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-07. Both fixed; both mutations now fail a test. CORRECTIONS TO CLAIMS I MADE TO THE FOUNDER THIS SESSION. - "7 answer keys recoverable from the PUBLIC repo": wrong. Only the local branch exp39-experimental reaches them and no remote carries it. The real public residual is 1 file of 635 bytes, Exp 55's control ground truth. - "8 of 37 dispatchers compose the schema, Wilson [11.4%, 37.2%]": a substring match on cdsfl_registry. True figure 0 of 37. - "None of the remaining findings touch a safety gate": 2 do -- arc_sequencer.sh:74 and :173, both containment gates of the same class. - A test I wrote tonight could not fail: `assert "VAULTED" in stdout` passes when the output reads UNVAULTED. Caught within the hour by mutation. Also: the additive-standard test guarded a HEADING, not the rule -- deleting the prohibition while keeping the words ADDITIVE STANDARD left it green. It now asserts the operative clause and the symmetric one, and all 4 mutations fail. Its slice-and-exec of the SYSTEM assignment is replaced by an import, justified by measurement: the slice broke on an expression referencing an outer name. title: The seat cap sat inside the distribution: a clean run was a 1-in-200 event
verbatim: The seat cap sat inside the distribution: a clean run was a 1-in-200 event The simulated Exp 45 run lost 3 of its 6 seats in round 0 -- the BLIND BASELINE -- each killed at exactly 900s having returned 0 chars, while the 3 that survived took 624s, 768s and 845s. The largest success was 94% of the cap, and the runner accepted the half-empty round and continued. `--timeout 900` was justified in source as matching "the live CC2 timeout in the real panel". That is a per-seat argument for a parameter whose failures compound per RUN: 6 seats x 16 rounds is 96 dispatches. Measured by the new scripts/seat_timeout_budget.py over 2,221 deduplicated archived dispatches (median 288s, p95 932s, p99 2068s): at 900s the per-seat loss is 5.45% and P(a run loses NO seat) is 0.5%. Raised to 3600s (0.32%, 73.9%). PROVEN THE SAME HOUR -- the clean run's round 0 returned all 6 seats at 662, 887, 958, 976, 1076 and 1870s. FOUR of those exceed the old ceiling, 3 of them by only 6.4%, 8.4% and 19.6%. They were never hung. Yield: the half-panel round produced 8 findings, the full panel 27. Also fixed, all of one shape -- a bounded traversal standing in for a complete one: - arc_sequencer.sh:74 counted panel_cwd with `-maxdepth 1 -type f`, so a second exam document one directory down was invisible to the gate that exists to guarantee exactly one. :173 counted `-type d`, so a sibling staged as a FILE was uncounted. Both gate the withheld-exam arc. test_arc_containment_gates_2026-09-08.py EXTRACTS AND EXECUTES each find from the live script; mutation-verified 4/4 red on the old file. - cdsfl_qc.py and supersession_check.py walked docs with glob("*.md"): docs/ holds 13 top-level and 152 total, so 139 nested files could not fail either. supersession now scans 534 files, still clean. - test_note_standard_v17_enforced widened; v1.7 notes enforced 22 -> 23. reference_runner_v3.py: initialise rk_proof_requests_for_next_round before the round loop. It was read at the top of every round and assigned only near the end, so run_experiment died with UnboundLocalError at round 0 of EVERY run. The severity-proof round trip shipped 2026-09-07 and had therefore never executed end to end. cdsfl_recover.py: _record_recovery_ran finally works. It was wrong 3 times, each failure hiding the next -- never called; then datetime.datetime on a module that imports the CLASS; then timezone.utc without importing timezone, under a blanket `except Exception: pass` that reported success. test_recovery_marker_2026-09-08.py runs the whole path including a mutation test that deletes the marker and requires the alarm to return. docs/REPRODUCING.md now discloses that both Exp 55 runs completed 1 round of 6 and stopped on HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM -- named in 8 other files and absent from the one a newcomer reads. WITHDRAWN: a claim that the memory-exclusions total "wants deriving rather than typing". It is already derived, at cdsfl_sv.py:1550, wired at :2569. Executed to check: identical figures. The drift was ordering, not a missing mechanism. Suite 5418 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed under --netguard-strict, pytest exit code 0 captured directly rather than through a pipe -- a pipeline's status is its LAST command, which cost a false all-clear twice more tonight. title: Withdraw a mechanism I published before checking it: the runner never wrote that file
verbatim: Withdraw a mechanism I published before checking it: the runner never wrote that file The night's report said an aborted run leaves the target rewritten because the runner splices corrected passages into it mid-run. The observation is real -- after the first run was killed, bench/dm/_memory.py stood at 25,861 bytes against its committed 20,605 (+99/-9), mtime inside that run's window, and the restart inherited it. The EXPLANATION was wrong, and was written from the log line rather than from the code. Read rather than assumed: - `_splice_corrected_copy` and `_derive_corrected_copy_from_fix` in reference_runner_v3.py are pure string transformations. Neither contains a disk write of any kind. - The log line "corrected copy DERIVED C0027 ... spliced into bench/dm/_memory.py (20,829 chars)" names the target path for context and describes an IN-MEMORY string. - The only write to a target anywhere in the runner is line 9436, into a SANDBOX copy, under a comment saying exactly that. So something else wrote a tracked source file during a run. The seats launch with `working directory: (inherited -- repo)`: they execute inside the repository, and panel agents editing the repo mid-run is already measured twice (2026-09-01). A seat applying a fix it had just proposed is the leading explanation and NOT an established one -- the write was never observed and nothing in the record attributes it. The clean run was watched for a repeat and is clean: git status shows no tracked file differing from HEAD, the target is byte-identical to 539f6a4, and 3 unrelated tracked files had mtimes touched during adjudication with content identical to HEAD. The remedy is unchanged by the correction and is now more important: compare the run banner's byte count against `git show HEAD:<target> | wc -c` before accepting any restart, and check `git status` during and after a run -- not only the target. Corrected in the consolidated note, its TTS mirror, the operational plan, RECOVERY.md and the persistent memory entry. title: panel_cwd was inert for every threaded dispatch -- and confining the cwd is not enough
verbatim: panel_cwd was inert for every threaded dispatch -- and confining the cwd is not enough TWO FINDINGS, THE SECOND LARGER THAN THE FIRST. 1. INERT. `set_panel_cwd` stores into a threading.local, and run_experiment calls it ONCE on the MAIN thread (reference_runner_v3.py:11395). Every seat is dispatched from a ThreadPoolExecutor (:8244, :8337), where a fresh worker has no value, so each seat launched with cwd=None and inherited the repository. Demonstrated: main thread sees the sandbox, 3 workers see [None, None, None]. The confinement that exists to keep a panel away from exam answer keys has therefore never applied to a seat. Repaired the way this project already chose for its confer panel on 2026-09-07: carry the value in a module mirror (_PANEL_CWD_FOR_WORKERS, the _DIRECTIVE_OMISSION pattern) and apply it ON THE WORKER'S OWN THREAD. A first attempt put a module-level fallback inside _get_panel_cwd_raw so a main-thread set would reach workers; that broke test_panel_sandbox_2026-09-07.py, which exists to stop precisely that -- the thread-local is deliberate, so one dispatch's cleanup cannot unsandbox another. Withdrawn, and recorded in the new test file so it is not retried. 2. NOT SUFFICIENT. With the repair verified live (1 main-thread call, 6 per-worker calls), a seat rewrote the repo target TWICE MORE -- 24,834 bytes at 04:20:52 and 25,650 at 04:22:22, against a committed 20,605. Captured mid-cycle: it is a seat's proposed fix carrying its own experiment in prose. A cwd confines RELATIVE paths. Seats are handed the ABSOLUTE repo path by `_absolute_target` under the founder's 2026-08-23 ruling, and that ruling is correct for reasons its own docstring records -- a relative name cannot be redirected into the discrimination overlay, nor found from a throwaway cwd, which is what left 6 Exp 55 falsifiers ERRORed. Bash is a superset of write, so an absolute path defeats any cwd. panel_cwd is not merely unwired; for a shell-bearing seat it is the WRONG MECHANISM. The remaining repair -- resolve that absolute path against the sandbox, which `_absolute_target` already supports via repo_root -- changes the paths appearing in findings and touches the ruling, so it is left to the founder rather than taken unilaterally. The source comments say so rather than claiming a fix that does not hold. A CAUSAL CLAIM WITHDRAWN. The target mutation was presented as the cause of the round's 9-of-11 escalation. It does not survive checking: panel_cwd has been inert throughout, so the archived exp45 that converged at R3 with 2 of 23 escalated was equally exposed. A condition shared by both runs cannot explain the difference. What does remains open. Also: scripts/hil_escalation_by_run.py measures ABSORPTION, which is the diagnostic that separates the record -- mechanically impaired runs absorbed 1/50 (2.0%), the rest 82/120 (68.3%), z = 7.88, p = 1.6e-15. exp49 escalated 76.5% at the gate, the archive's highest, and was healthy because its ladder absorbed 25 of 26. A high gate rate is not the alarm; a ladder that absorbs nothing is. The pooled 39.35% figure cited earlier was a mixture of a broken era and a working one, and the script refuses it in its own output. Suite 5425 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed under --netguard-strict, pytest exit code 0 captured directly. title: The answer: absorption 6 of 7, indistinguishable from a healthy run
verbatim: The answer: absorption 6 of 7, indistinguishable from a healthy run The founder's rule fired on round 0 escalating 9 of 11, and it was right to fire -- chasing it found two real defects. But the gate tally is the load ARRIVING at the absorber, not the queue leaving it. The measurement that settles it is what the routing ladder clears. Round 0 of the confined run, 04:30 to 05:51, 80.7 minutes, all 6 seats back (825, 997, 1139, 1252, 1274, 1562 s -- 4 of 6 over the old 900 s cap), 27 findings, rho 1.000. gate: 4 CONFIRMED, 0 REFUTED, 7 -> HIL routing: 6 resolved by strong writer, 0 dedup'd, 1 -> HIL, 1 deferred Absorption 6/7 = 85.7%, Wilson [48.7%, 97.4%], Clopper-Pearson [42.1%, 99.6%]. Against the impaired band (2.0%): z = 6.32, p = 1.3e-10; Fisher exact p = 1.3e-6, odds ratio 294; exact mpmath tail 4.4e-10. Against the healthy band (68.3%): z = 0.97, p = 0.333 -- INDISTINGUISHABLE. All 7 escalations drew substantive dispatches of 7,400-11,500 chars across a ladder bounded at max_rungs=2. The exp55 / exp43-rerun failure mode is a ladder that engages and resolves NOTHING (0/28, 0/13). The 1 deferred finding is a recent repair working, not a fault. reference_runner_v3.py:5417 records that findings with no falsifier and no S_k were previously "never assessed, then labelled as findings no machine could assess", and that EVERY irreducible-queue alarm in the archive, 4 of 4, fired at round 0 on that mislabelling. Such a finding now stays open and blocking -- the fail-safe direction. The founder's heuristic has therefore been correct in every archived instance, and the instrument it detected has since been repaired. ALSO CHECKED AND REFUTED, recorded because it nearly shipped: the B-cell looked like an instrument that decides nothing -- 2,176 UNCERTAIN verdicts archive-wide and no positives. `VERIFIED` is not in its vocabulary, so the query could not have found a positive if one existed. Counted correctly it is 2,176 UNCERTAIN / 40 REJECTED / 28 CONFIRMED: decisive on 68 of 2,244, 3.03%, Wilson [2.40%, 3.82%]. UNCERTAIN routes onward to the gate and HIL rather than blocking, and most findings on a Python target are not SMT-shaped. Not a defect. Third time tonight a negative result came from a query whose scope I had not verified. title: The halt was right, and its evidence bundle was empty
verbatim: The halt was right, and its evidence bundle was empty Exp 45 ran 4 rounds in 311.6 min and stopped at HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM with 61 findings. Under the founder's rule a non-converging run is diagnosed, not reported, and the diagnosis found a real fault -- though not where the investigation had been looking. THE FAULT IS FALSIFIER SUPPLY, upstream of every mechanism under examination. 5 of the 14 critical findings arrived with NO runnable falsifier -- 64.3% supply, Wilson [38.8%, 83.7%] -- from 4 different seats, and those 5 ARE the queue that halted the run. The project's founding requirement is that every critical arrives with a runnable check; it held for 9 of 14. FOR THE FOUNDER. EVERYTHING DOWNSTREAM WORKED. The ladder absorbed 10 of the 12 it was actually given (83.3%, Wilson [55.2%, 95.3%]): vs the impaired band z = 5.13, p = 1.4e-7, Fisher p = 2.6e-6, OR 54; vs the healthy band p = 0.179, INDISTINGUISHABLE. Residual human queue across all 4 rounds: 1. TWO DEFECTS IN THE ALARM'S OWN EVIDENCE PATH, both found by trying to act on the halt, both defeating the adjudication it exists to enable: - The bundle was EMPTY. irreducible_queue_count() counts `irreducible_escalation OR routing_deferred`; the evidence collector tested only the first. The 2026-09-07 repair added routing_deferred to the COUNT and not to the COLLECTOR, so a queue of deferred items fires the alarm and describes nothing: "5 criticals are locked" then "Evidence for all 0 item(s)". Fixed to match the count predicate; verified against the halted run's saved state (headline 1, bundle 0 -> 1 and 1) and mutation-tested. - The defer reason stated a FALSEHOOD: "no falsifier and no S_k evaluation exist" on entries carrying one -- C0055 tristate REJECTED, C0057 a complete ADMISSIBLE at 0.9782 with 52/55 sandbox tests. It now names the verdict that triggered the deferral and claims nothing about S_k. A FIRST VERSION OF THAT SECOND FIX QUOTED THE ENTRY'S S_k STATE, which put a read of sk_result inside _apply_routing. FIVE tests across 4 files caught it -- immune-memory consumption, both static-queue-closure wiring tests, target-kind, and the location bucket -- because S_k must not be readable where routing decides, or R_k(0) can reach a verdict. The fix now claims less rather than reading more. An earlier draft also hardcoded "an equipment failure", which printed "the falsifier verdict is CONFIRMED, an equipment failure" when replayed; the phrase is checked, not asserted. ONE RUN, TWO DIRECTORIES. The runner writes sim45_memory_...033008Z (report) and ...033012Z (48-file state) 4 seconds apart, BOTH carrying the registry, so any directory-walking archive scan double-counts. It has now corrupted two measurements in one night, both in the reassuring direction: a duration scan (p99 1605 -> 2068s, loss 3.43% -> 5.45% once deduplicated) and the latent tagger's tripwires. Whether the runner should stop is FOR THE FOUNDER. Tripwires updated in the safe order, never suppressed: the tagger was shown unchanged before its exposure list moved (5 -> 11, of which 6 are 3 findings twice), and `added == []` was re-verified before the removal record grew (2 -> 6, of which 4 are 2 findings twice). sk_threshold_shadow re-measured because the archive grew: 3816 -> 4142 of 4142, Wilson [99.90%, 100.00%] -> [99.91%, 100.00%], 6663 -> 6727 files, strict floats 3181 -> 3507, strings UNCHANGED at 635. Count and interval corrected together, as the drift guard demands. test_a_write_inside_the_sandbox_does_not_reach_the_canonical_tree failed 1 of 4 full runs and passed the other 3 plus isolation. Recorded in the test as an observed flake with its evidence rather than widened or excluded -- the sensitivity that produces the false alarm is what lets it see a real escape. Suite 5425 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed under --netguard-strict, exit code 0. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: The compaction alarm never reached the founder, and my own P-pass silenced it
verbatim: The compaction alarm never reached the founder, and my own P-pass silenced it MEASURED. 0 of 11 compactions in this session produced an alert he could see, Wilson 95% CI [0.00%, 25.88%]. Two causes in sequence: - 10 of 11: the hook ran with suppressOutput=True. It reached the assistant and nobody else; delivery depended on my relaying it, and over the 2026-09-07 compaction it fired 42 times in 10.69 hours and was relayed once. Fixed at 02:20:40 today. - 1 of 11: the compaction at 01:25:08Z was silenced by MY OWN P-PASS. Three runs of `cdsfl_recover.py --full` between 01:26:22 and 01:29:37 wrote the marker at 01:28:04Z, 175 s later, and the hook's `ran >= compaction` predicate read True. Proven by replaying the real hook in a sandboxed HOME: no marker -> fires; that marker -> silent; a marker predating the compaction -> fires. ROOT CAUSE IS THE EVENT BEING RECORDED, NOT THE TEST. The marker answered "did this script execute?" while the alarm asks "has context been restored?" -- a proxy standing in for the restore itself. A test run and a real restore execute identical code, so nothing intrinsic separates them and explicit intent is the only honest discriminator. NOT a one-off: 6 of 11 compactions (54.5%, Wilson [28.0%, 78.7%]) had a real --full invocation after them that would have cleared the alarm regardless of whether anyone rebuilt context. FIX: the marker now requires --record-restore (implies --full). --full alone records nothing and SAYS so. Fail-safe -- forgetting the flag leaves the alarm sounding; the old default failed the other way. 10 tests, one pinning that --full alone must not record. Docs swept: the rs definition updated in .claude/CLAUDE.md, resources/SHORTCUTS.md and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, because a stale command line would silently reintroduce the failure. The remaining --full in ONBOARDING.md is a historical account of a past incident and was left. A TIMESTAMP ERROR, founder-caught: I said the compaction was "3 hours and 24 minutes" earlier when it was 13h31m -- understated by 607 minutes, with the clock hook's 15:56:07 in hand on that same turn. Having the time is not using it; elapsed figures get computed, not estimated. rs RAN, exit code 0, marker recorded by a genuine restore. Context rebuilt from git, Open Brain session-context, the operational tracker, RECOVERY.md and the outstanding queue. Both canonical state blocks were stale at 04:45, still describing the Exp 45 run as live; both now carry the finished verdict. STALE IN THE rs DEFINITION: it names ACTION_QUEUE.md and QWERTY_CHECKPOINT.md; neither exists in the repo. Suite 5425 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed under --netguard-strict, exit code 0. title: Preserve the target-mutation watch evidence and measure its arrival pattern
verbatim: Preserve the target-mutation watch evidence and measure its arrival pattern The 15-second poll loop that watched bench/dm/_memory.py during the 2026-09-08 Exp 45 run logged 12 distinct blob states between 07:15:03 and 09:31:15. That log and its 22 file snapshots lived only in the session tmpdir, which is exactly the defect measured-rate-travels-with-its-script names: evidence quoted in prose with nothing committed that reproduces it. Both are now in the repo alongside a script that recomputes the arrival statistics from the log. The measurement changes what can honestly be said about the rewrites. They were not spread across the run: 7 of the 12 states landed inside the first 600 s of a 8172 s window. KS against uniform arrivals gives D=0.5465, p=0.002496; the gap coefficient of variation is 1.8643 against a uniform-null mean of 0.9307, Monte Carlo p=0.00141 over 200,000 draws; the binomial tail for 7-or-more of 12 in that slice is 6.541e-06, computed identically by scipy and mpmath. Wilson 95% for the burst share is [0.3195, 0.8067], Clopper-Pearson [0.2767, 0.8483], and mpmath's closed-form Wilson reproduces statsmodels to 4 decimal places. A burst and an even spread have different causes and different remedies, so the distinction is not cosmetic. This is consistent with one agent editing repeatedly in a short window rather than six agents each editing as they worked, but the log records blob hashes and not authors, so attribution stays OPEN. The working file is byte-identical to HEAD (539f6a4c) and has been since 09:31. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: The archive I committed as evidence was being read as production source
verbatim: The archive I committed as evidence was being read as production source Commit 3c4987d preserved 22 snapshots of a file a panel seat rewrote during the 2026-09-08 Exp 45 run, storing them as .py under bench/logs/. The full suite then went red: test_update_drift_has_no_production_caller globs bench/**/*.py and reads every match as production, one snapshot calls is_drifting, and the checker reported that a dormant feature had acquired a live caller. 1 failed, 5439 passed. The exclusion that fixes it was already written down twice. Of the 3 checkers that walk bench/ for Python files, test_panel_sandbox_2026-09-07.py skips "/logs/" and test_python_floor_2026-09-07.py skips "bench/logs/"; test_immune_memory_evaluation.py alone did not. So this is not a new convention, it is one sibling missing the lesson its two siblings had learned. title: Morning report: 12 outstanding items verified, and 4 of yesterday's claims corrected
verbatim: Morning report: 12 outstanding items verified, and 4 of yesterday's claims corrected Twelve outstanding items were checked against the repository by 12 read-only verification agents rather than recalled from session memory. That was the right call: 4 of the resulting findings contradict claims made in the preceding session. The remote-access fault is not on the Mac. The host recovered unaided after both forced restarts on record, in 75 s on 2026-09-04 and 40 s on 2026-09-08, the same persisted session reconnecting each time with no failed attempt anywhere in the log. 2 of 2, Wilson [34.24%, 100.00%], Clopper-Pearson [15.81%, 100.00%] -- wide because 2 is a small number. If the host is back in under 80 s and the session is still unreachable, the failure is client-side, and driving home is very unlikely to be what restores it. The P-pass on scripts/remote_bridge_recovery_2026-09-09.py found that its first version could not have refuted its own hypothesis: it paired each restart with the first reconnection at ANY later time, so a reconnection 6.3 hours afterwards -- precisely what a physical return looks like -- would have scored as unaided recovery. It also credited any session's reconnection to this one, and divided by zero on a log with no restart. All 3 repaired, 12 tests, both mutations caught (unbounded window takes 3 red, dropping the no-restarts guard takes 1 red), and the conclusion survives at every window from 120 s upward. The 4 corrections: 1. The v3 capabilities are not broken, they are switched off. All 4 of fingerprinting, routing, the sweep and decomposed dispatch are still reached by live callers; routing and the sweep are disabled in all 3 exp56 configs. This is the misconfiguration case the founder's 2026-09-08 ruling anticipated, arriving within a day of the ruling. 2. The two-directories account was wrong in its premise. Only 1 of the 2 directories is the runner's; the launcher creates the other and correctly sets ExperimentConfig.logs_dir, which the runner reads 0 times. A written-but-never- read field, which is the unwired-addition half of the additive standard. 3. The falsifier-supply diagnosis was too shallow. The 5-of-14 criticals with no runnable falsifier is downstream; the dominant loss is the intake parser, which recovered 26 of 69 FALSIFIER blocks across the run (Wilson [27.18%, 49.48%]) and 1 of 9 in the round that halted (Wilson [1.99%, 43.50%]). 4. title: I broke the suite writing a memory file and not running sv, one day after recording that exact lesson
verbatim: I broke the suite writing a memory file and not running sv, one day after recording that exact lesson The full suite went red at 5 failed, 5467 passed. Every failure was mine, all from after the last green run, and 4 of the 5 have one cause: a memory file was written on 2026-09-08 at 18:44 and sv was never run, so the ledger that sv DERIVES was left stating the old count. - test_memory_ledger_total_matches_the_directory: 139 files on disk, ledger 138 - TestMemoryExclusionsAccounting.test_the_accounting_matches_the_directory: same - TestBoldTitlesAreEntriesToo.test_the_live_index_has_no_over_long_entries: the new index entry was 198 characters against the 150-character one-line rule - TestTheOneLineRuleRefuses.test_the_live_index_passes_the_rule: same entry - TestEveryCitationNamesSomethingReal.test_no_live_citation_names_a_missing_file: the tracker cited SEAT_064003_03845310.py:360 by bare filename, which does not resolve; its real path is under bench/logs/target_mutation_watch_2026-09-08/ The tracker records this lesson at the 2026-09-08 pointer, in these words: "The drift exists because the guard ran before sv did. No mechanism is missing; the remedy is ordering." That sentence was written the same evening the ordering was then broken. Recording a remedy is not applying it. Repairs, all measured rather than asserted: - The index entry is now 149 characters. - The ledger is DERIVED by _update_memory_exclusions_ledger rather than typed, and now states 139, matching the directory. - The citation carries its full repo-relative path. - A sixth check then surfaced, memory-index-headroom: the index stood at 191 lines against a refusal threshold of 190, which is 0.95 of the 200-line loader limit. Consolidated the 7 SUPERSEDED note-standard pointers into 1. All 8 files remain on disk and remain reachable by name; only the index got terser. 184 lines now, 16 lines and 6063 characters of headroom. Both guards mutation-verified: restoring the over-long entry takes 2 tests red, setting the ledger total wrong takes 1 red. One self-inflicted slip caught mid-repair and recorded because it is the same shape as the defect: the first consolidation filter tested each line for the string "v1.7", and the v1.6 entry survived it because its own description reads "superseded by v1.7". Filtering on the LINK TARGET rather than the prose fixed it. A substring test that matches the thing it means to exclude is the execute-do-not-grep failure in miniature. Also corrected in this commit: the 4 skipped tests are NOT network-gated as previously reported to the founder. All 4 are in test_br2_keys_are_split_out_2026-08-27.py and skip because the Bench Run 2 key store lives outside the repository and is absent on this machine, so the tests that verify the keys are properly split out cannot run at all. Full suite after the repair: 5472 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed, pytest exit code 0 captured directly, in 669.92 s. Their unfiltered output is experimental_notes/Research_FULL_RECORD_2026-09-09.md, 1221 lines, per the standing instruction that findings are presented in full and summarised only afterwards. WOLFRAM, URGENT. The Engine is documented to reactivate itself near expiry and on this machine it has NOT: the licence file still carries its original mtime of 2026-08-02T21:09:38+0100 with 2 days left, while the Engine has demonstrably run and reached the cloud since. No Wolfram-owned page promises an email reminder, so the founder's assumption that one would arrive is not supported. At expiry the kernel prompts for reactivation, which is a stop rather than a degradation, and how that prompt surfaces to a non-interactive wolframscript call from a bench runner is unconfirmed -- a live risk given this project's record of error strings being ingested as answers. Separately the WolframCloud MCP route has failed 39 times since 2026-09-04 against 2 successes and should be retired, not repaired. QWERTY_CHECKPOINT AND ACTION_QUEUE. Both are Project_Genesis artefacts from February and March 2026, later copied into Metis, and never present in this repository across 1,161 revisions. The founder's hypothesis is SUPPORTED with one refinement: the ancestor of the MC list is the shorthand table that CONTAINED `qwerty`, not the checkpoint file, which was merely the file that command wrote. 4 of that table's 5 entries survive verbatim today. `qwerty` -- a 5-point per-turn self-verification protocol -- is the single one that does not. The self-check command is the one that was dropped, which bears directly on the item below. THE RELIABILITY MECHANISM WAS NEVER BUILT. Discussed on 5 occasions between 2026-08-25 and 2026-09-07. All 4 installed hooks are UserPromptSubmit context injectors making 0 subprocess calls, emitting 0 blocking decisions and always exiting 0. No git hook, no CI, core.hooksPath unset. Commit 57d5a0e reached HEAD on 2026-09-09 at 08:16:17 with the suite red, which is the proof rather than the theory. WHERE TO SITE IT, MEASURED. Of 19 self-inflicted defects caught over 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-09: suite 7 (36.8%, Wilson [19.1%, 59.0%]), later self-check 7, founder 4 (21.1%, Wilson [8.5%, 43.3%]), linter 1. Mechanisms took 8 of the 12 that fell to mechanism-or-founder, NOT distinguishable from chance (exact binomial p = 0.194, Fisher p = 0.110). The P-pass then attacked the classification, which is CC1 judging its own record: reclassifying every arguable entry in all 16 combinations pushes the worst-case p to 0.598, so the counts are fragile. What survives is the part that does not depend on them -- all 4 founder-caught defects are CLAIMS and all 8 mechanism-caught defects are artefacts a checker can read. A test suite evaluates code; nothing here evaluates a claim. SIMPLICITY: THE FOUNDER IS RIGHT AND THE SOURCE OF THE ERROR IS IDENTIFIED. memory/feedback_simplest_sufficient.md carries "Prefer extending machinery that exists and is already trusted over inventing a new component", and that line is what reappeared on 2026-09-07 and again on 2026-09-09. It is wrong: simplicity is a property of the solution, not of its ancestry, and framing it as a preference for reuse tells models never to innovate. Sufficiency IS formalised in the maths (sigma/S_k) and is the hard constraint; simplicity IS defined there as nu, but nu ships as a constant blind to complexity and its measuring module has no caller; additivity appears 0 times in either maths file and is governance, not a model term. One correction to his framing: the simplicity-versus-sufficiency chat is real and documented 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04, but additivity was a neighbouring strand -- the word appears 0 times in either 2026-09-02 note -- so it was a 2-way conversation, not a 3-way one. THE PANEL FORMAT DOES NOT EXIST TO BE SAVED; IT MUST BE WRITTEN. The SYSTEM string in bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py carries the 28,183-character formal schema and is the only 1 of 39 dispatchers that does. The USER prompt is a hand-written brief read straight off disk with no template, schema, validation or test. Across 49 archived briefs: 0 require a seat to use the mathematical model as an instrument, 8 require a fix, 2 require the fix to be tested. His diagnosis is confirmed; his presupposition that a format exists to save is contradicted. The ledger was derived and the 4 cheap guards run BEFORE this commit rather than after -- by hand, because the hook that should do it is item 1.1 and does not yet exist. 56 passed, exit 0. title: The quote worry was real, measured, and 0.54 percent of the corpus
verbatim: The quote worry was real, measured, and 0.54 percent of the corpus The founder asked what the quote was and why it was a blocker. It is not a blocker, and describing it as a standing issue over-stated it: the linter's own output reads "Reported, not enforced". It IS a genuine defect, found by execution rather than by reading. note_vagueness_lint.py already exempts quoted text, stripping the balanced pattern at :163 for the stated reason that a sentence quoting someone else's vagueness is not itself vague. But the checker examines 1 SENTENCE at a time at :151, while the stripper needs a balanced pair of quote marks inside whatever it is handed. A quotation spanning more than 1 sentence therefore carries an unbalanced quote mark in every sentence except its last, and loses the exemption on all of them. Reproduced directly: splitting the founder's 3-sentence Wolfram quotation gives sentence 0 an unbalanced quote and the vague phrase survives stripping there. THE SCALE REFUTES THE CONCERN THAT PROMPTED THE MEASUREMENT. Across 376 notes and 1183 findings, 560 are UNNAMED SUBJECT and 3 of those 560 are this artefact -- 0.54 percent, Wilson [0.18%, 1.56%], Clopper-Pearson [0.11%, 1.56%]. The hypothesis that founder quotations were generating meaningful lint noise, and that the notes remediation might therefore shrink, is REFUTED. The remediation scope stands at 1183. Script: scripts/lint_quote_exemption_defect_2026-09-09.py. The fix is 1 line -- strip quotes per paragraph before splitting into sentences -- and it is low priority precisely because the measurement says so. The 1 finding in the task list is left standing. It falls inside a verbatim founder quotation and editing his words to make a checker green would corrupt the record to satisfy a tool. Also in this commit, per founder ruling 2026-09-09 verbatim -- "Zenodo key switching can go at the very bottom of this list. It isn't pressing." -- the Zenodo token rotation moves from R10 to a new section Z at the foot of the list. It is moved rather than deleted, because the instructions he asked for on 2026-08-19 are still unanswered and should not be lost by being deprioritised. title: The linter finds the founder vague twice and me 1181 times, and I made the binary error for the 12th time
verbatim: The linter finds the founder vague twice and me 1181 times, and I made the binary error for the 12th time Two founder corrections, both supported by measurement rather than by agreement. FIRST, THE LINTER'S SCOPE. He objects to a tool that marks his input as vague and says the vagueness is mine, particularly in the TTS outputs. Measured across 376 notes and 1183 findings: 1181 are in the assistant's own prose and 2 fall inside a quotation of anyone at all -- 99.83 percent, Wilson [99.39%, 99.95%], Clopper-Pearson [99.39%, 99.98%]. The tool has found him vague twice, in passing, and the assistant vague 1181 times. His claim is supported without qualification. The fault is not that his work was refused -- it never was, and the linter's own output reads "Reported, not enforced" -- but that 1 of his sentences was made the subject of a compliance discussion across 2 turns. That is the behaviour he named. Rule recorded as L1: his text is data to be preserved exactly, never input to be corrected. L2 records the underlying linter defect, which is genuine and small: the quote exemption strips quoted text at :163 while the checker examines 1 sentence at a time at :151, so a quotation spanning more than 1 sentence loses the exemption on every sentence but its last. 3 of 560 unnamed-subject findings, 0.54 percent, Wilson [0.18%, 1.56%]. Low priority BECAUSE the measurement says so, not despite it. SECOND, THE BINARY ERROR. I presented the 2 task-list status designs as alternatives. He asked whether they could be used to cross-check each other. They can, and it is the better design. Measured: the note standard's Rule 20 statuses against a task state give 20 joint cells, 17 reachable and 3 contradictory. Neither determines the other -- a COMMITTED item can still be OPEN because it is not enabled, and a DONE item can carry no code when it is a documentation write-back -- so the 3 contradictory cells are a fault a single vocabulary cannot express. This was the 12th time since 2026-07-29 he has had to make the composability point, and memory/feedback_binary_thinking.md already records it verbatim as "a recurring failure mode". The memory is correct, was available, and was not applied. An honest caveat that argues FOR the work: 2 different regular expressions over the task list counted 29 entries and 48. The list cannot currently be counted mechanically, which is the strongest argument for the explicit marker. Nothing implemented, per the discuss-first directive. title: The commit guard, built over 3 FFAFP passes, each pass finding what the last one introduced
verbatim: The commit guard, built over 3 FFAFP passes, each pass finding what the last one introduced FFAFP is a cycle, not a single sweep, and the first version of this work stopped after 1 pass and declared the item complete. Founder correction 2026-09-09: "'f' or full FFAFP, is a continuous cycle. You keep doing it until all meaningful issues are resolved in every issue and/or until diminishing returns are reached." Three passes were run. Each found defects the previous pass had introduced. PASS 1. FIND: no git hook, core.hooksPath unset, .git/hooks holding 14 samples and nothing live, and commit 57d5a0e reaching HEAD on 2026-09-09 at 08:16:17 with the full suite red. FOLLOW, before touching anything: sv commits via a plain git commit so the hook fires there too; nothing uses --no-verify; no git-hook-name collision in hooks/; and, unlooked for, 3 of the 4 live hooks existed only under ~/.claude/hooks and were in no repository at all. ANALYSE: the 4 cheap guards cost 1.00 s to 2.02 s over 3 runs against 669.92 s for the full suite, which is why the gate is 4 files. FIX: hooks/pre-commit, fail-closed even on infrastructure faults, with --no-verify as the documented deliberate escape; core.hooksPath wired by wire_git_hooks() in scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py rather than by hand, because it is per-clone configuration and a fresh clone would otherwise have no guard; the 3 unversioned hooks brought into hooks/. P-PASS: 3 of 4 mutations caught at once. The 4th was not, and that is the finding: deleting the python3 check left all tests green because git and python3 both live in /opt/homebrew/bin, so the test's PATH restriction never removed python3 and it passed for an unrelated reason. A test that survives deleting the check it guards is "a guard that cannot fail". Rebuilt with a PATH holding 1 symlink and an assertion that python3 is genuinely absent before the test claims anything. PASS 2 found 2 defects introduced by pass 1, both the same shape -- two representations of one truth with no comparator. First, the 3 newly versioned hooks had no drift detector: the existing tests point at the LIVE copies under ~/.claude/hooks, so the repository copies were backups nothing compared, which is the "addition nothing reaches" half of the additive standard introduced by the fix for an instance of that same standard. Second, the guard list was hardcoded in both the hook and its test, so editing the hook left the test green. Fixed by parsing the list out of the hook and by adding a per-hook drift test. All 3 mutations caught. PASS 3 found 4, of which 2 were above threshold. Below threshold and left alone: the hook does not run its own test so there is no self-lock-out, and the drift test's skip branch is unreachable on this machine. Fixed: the guard-list parser raised IndexError if the block were renamed, failing obscurely instead of reporting -- the third instance of that class found today; and no test proved a commit is refused in a real clone of THIS repository rather than in a synthetic one, so every refusal test together proved only that the control flow works. Separately, the full suite caught 2 defects in scripts written earlier today: except Exception: pass in decision_label_staleness, the shape that hid 3 successive faults in _record_recovery_ran on 2026-09-08, and then the fix for it tripped a second guard by printing unparsed[:5] without stating the remainder. Both fixed and mutation-verified. Measured before fixing: 0 timestamps actually failed to parse, so the 311 figure reported to the founder was sound. Full suite before the pass-3 edits: 5492 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The evidence I said I preserved was never tracked: 0 of 22 snapshots reached the repository
verbatim: The evidence I said I preserved was never tracked: 0 of 22 snapshots reached the repository FFAFP pass 5 on the commit guard cloned the repository and ran the guards inside the clone. They failed there while passing locally, and the cause is not the hook. Commit 3c4987d on 2026-09-08 said, in its own message, that the target-mutation evidence "lived only in the session tmpdir, which is exactly the defect measured-rate-travels-with-its-script names" and that both the log and its 22 snapshots "are now in the repo". They were not. They were copied into bench/logs/, which .gitignore:41 excludes with `bench/logs/**`. Measured: 22 files on disk, 0 tracked. The evidence still existed on exactly 1 machine, which is the single point of failure the commit set out to remove, and the commit message asserting otherwise was false. The same applies to the data the measurement runs on. scripts/target_mutation_ arrival_2026-09-08.py read target_state_transitions.log from the ignored path, so the script was committed and its input was not: nobody else could reproduce the figure. That is precisely the rule the script was written to satisfy, broken by the script written to satisfy it. FOLLOW put the blast radius well beyond this commit. Across the repository 3803 distinct bench/logs paths are cited and 177 of them are untracked -- 4.65 percent, Wilson [4.03%, 5.37%], Clopper-Pearson [4.01%, 5.37%] -- so a body of cited evidence exists only on this machine. This commit fixes its own instance; the 177 are a policy question for the founder and go on the task list. FIX. The log, the 22 snapshots and a README explaining all of the above now live under experimental_notes/evidence/target_mutation_watch_2026-09-08/, which is tracked. The snapshots carry a .py.txt suffix deliberately: they are Python a panel seat wrote, and stored as .py under a tracked directory they would be parsed by the repository's source scanners -- the same scanners repaired on 2026-09-08 after archived model output was read as production code. Checked before choosing the suffix rather than after: test_python_floor's _sources() excludes only .git/ and bench/logs/, so experimental_notes/*.py IS scanned. The arrival script, its test and 2 document citations now point at the tracked copy, with the ignored path kept as a fallback so the script still runs on the machine that produced it. Same output after the move: 12 states, KS D=0.5465 p=0.002496, burst probability 2.538e-05. WHY NO EARLIER PASS FOUND THIS. Passes 1 to 4 inspected the repository they were run in, where the files are present on disk and every guard passes. Only cloning distinguishes "exists" from "is tracked". Pass 4 returned 0 findings and, on the two-consecutive-clean-passes rule, work would have stopped there. Pass 5 returned 3, which collapsed to 1 real cause. Diminishing returns had not been reached; it only looked as though they had, because passes 1 to 4 shared a blind spot. title: Item 1 complete: the commit guard, the task-list markers and the pulse hook, with the cross-check finding a real fault on its first run
verbatim: Item 1 complete: the commit guard, the task-list markers and the pulse hook, with the cross-check finding a real fault on its first run M1 and M2, built as ONE composed design rather than the 2 alternatives originally offered. The founder's correction, verbatim: "Can you not use them both to cross check the list?" He was right, and the composition earned its place immediately. THE COUNTING WAS THE DEFECT. Three regular expressions over the master task list counted 23, 29 and 48 entries. The true figure is 59. The worst of the three was the one that reported the list "coherent" while silently skipping 16 entries, because a parser that omits is worse than one that fails: it reports success. The cause was a pattern that matched `**R1. Title**` but not `**0.1 Title`. Every entry now carries an HTML-comment marker, invisible in rendered markdown, and scripts/task_list_markers.py is the only thing that reads or writes them. THE CROSS-CHECK FOUND A GENUINE FAULT ON ITS FIRST RUN, and the fault was in the vocabulary rather than in the list. Entry 1.3 read state=DONE status=PROPOSED, which the checker flagged as contradictory -- a task closed before its work was committed. It was right: 1.3 is the QWERTY item the founder CLOSED BY RULING, so it has no work product at all, DONE falsely implies work was completed, and no Rule 20 status describes it. Neither vocabulary could express "closed because it will not be done". A 5th state, WITHDRAWN, was added. A single vocabulary could not have surfaced this, which is the argument for the composition in one example. M2, the pulse hook, is registered as the 5th UserPromptSubmit hook and shares the same engine, so the line the assistant sees each turn and the `--check` the founder can run cannot disagree. It reports every state (an earlier version printed 4 of 5 and produced a line summing to 58 of 59, a silent falsehood of the same kind the truncated-list guard exists to catch) and it surfaces contradictions rather than swallowing them. THE SUITE THEN REFUSED THIS COMMIT, correctly. A repository guard collects BY NAME every function returning a tuple and objects when such a name is bound whole and tested for truth. `parse` in scripts/remote_bridge_recovery_2026-09-09.py returns a tuple, so it poisoned the unrelated `parse` in task_list_markers.py. The guard's name-based scope is a deliberate over-reach and the right answer is not to weaken it: it is to stop using a name so generic that 2 unrelated functions collide under it. Renamed to parse_events and parse_entries, which is Rule 19 -- name the subject -- applied to code. Mutation-verified: restoring the colliding name turns the guard red again. Mutation coverage across item 1: 4 on the pre-commit hook, 4 on the marker engine, 3 on the pulse hook, 1 on the naming. All 12 caught. Also fixed, found by FFAFP pass 6 running the whole suite inside a fresh clone: test_the_live_repository_is_actually_wired asserted a property of the developer's machine, so it failed in a clone -- correctly, since a fresh clone IS unguarded until onboarding runs, but uselessly, because it made an unavoidable condition look like a defect. It now detects a fresh clone and skips WITH THE REASON STATED. The remaining 10 clone failures are logged as issue I6 and are NOT chased here, per the founder's instruction that emerging issues go to a closing report and do not detract from the work list. title: The panel brief format now exists, and the dispatcher refuses a brief that does not meet it
verbatim: The panel brief format now exists, and the dispatcher refuses a brief that does not meet it Founder ruling 2026-09-09: panel review must be "full CDSFL panel review format (so not just some simple open ended prompt)", seats "must use whatever aspects of the harness are currently working, including our mathematical model and all relevant mechanics in the formation of their answers/fixes", and the format becomes the standard for the full 6-model paid panel. His diagnosis was confirmed by measurement and his presupposition was not: there was no format to save. The SYSTEM half is solid and test-guarded -- the 28,183 character formal schema, no compelled convergence, the additive standard and the one-shot notice all reach every seat by construction. The USER half was 49 hand-written markdown files read straight off disk with no template, no schema, no validation and no test. BUILT. bench/directives/universal/panel_brief_template.md carries the 6 required sections. scripts/panel_brief_validate.py checks them. bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py now REFUSES a failing brief before any seat is reached, because 3 of the 5 seats are paid and the record already holds a case where a briefing defect broke 2 seats and forced a re-dispatch. A warning above a dispatch that proceeds anyway would be a guard that cannot fail. PANEL_BRIEF_UNCHECKED=1 is the documented deliberate bypass and announces itself. MEASURED ON WIRING: all 49 archived briefs would be refused. That figure alone would be worthless -- a rule rejecting everything tells you nothing -- so the spread matters more: failures range from 1 to 7 of the checks, mean 2.4, and the best archived brief fails only 1. It discriminates. The 2 universal gaps are the output shape, missing in 44 of 49, and a termination criterion, missing in 43. THE VALIDATOR'S OWN TEST TIGHTENED IT TWICE, and the second time is the instructive one. Version 1 accepted a bare "## Output" heading with nothing under it: a heading is not a shape. Version 2 required a named field but searched the WHOLE DOCUMENT, so a brief mentioning "verdict" anywhere in passing satisfied it -- and deleting the entire output specification from a compliant fixture left the check green. A check that cannot fail in the direction it exists to check is the fault this project names repeatedly. A document-wide search is simply the wrong instrument for a question about one section; it is now section-scoped. 3 mutations, all caught: reverting to a document-wide search, making the dispatcher warn instead of refuse, and emptying the check list. title: Item 2.1: the recommended falsifier fix was refuted by measurement, and the real one is a union
verbatim: Item 2.1: the recommended falsifier fix was refuted by measurement, and the real one is a union THE FIX ON FILE WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A REGRESSION. The recommendation was to widen _FALSIFIER_BLOCK_RE so it tolerates text between the label and the opening fence. Measured across 6,727 archived reply files, a widened single pattern recovers 4,867 blocks against the current 5,295 -- a net LOSS of 428. Applying the recommendation unmeasured would have made the halt cause worse. THE DIAGNOSIS UNDERNEATH WAS RIGHT. Of 6,363 labels carrying a fenced block within 3 lines, 5,282 are captured and 1,081 missed: a 16.99% miss rate, Wilson [16.09%, 17.93%], Clopper-Pearson [16.07%, 17.93%]. 1,066 of those misses carry a DESCRIPTION between the label and the fence, which is essentially the whole loss. So the repair is a UNION of the existing pattern with a new _FALSIFIER_BLOCK_DESCRIBED_RE, not a replacement of it. A union cannot lose a block the first pattern already captures, and that invariant is ASSERTED by a test rather than assumed, because the replacement approach was measured losing 428. THE GAP IS CONSTRAINED, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART. A looser tolerant pattern recovered 507 additional blocks, of which 4 were the label appearing INSIDE test code -- `assert "FALSIFIER:" not in minimal` -- a 0.8% false-positive rate, Wilson [0.3%, 2.0%]. A false falsifier is worse than a missing one BECAUSE THE HARNESS EXECUTES IT. Requiring the gap to open with a letter or bracket and to carry no quote or backtick recovers 492 and excludes all 4, at a cost of 11 genuine blocks out of 6,363, which is 0.17%. An earlier measurement of this same question returned 0 recovered from 9,849 labels and was MY OWN defect, not the parser's: the archived replies are JSON, so their newlines are escaped and a regex requiring real newlines finds nothing in the raw file text. Decoding the JSON first is what produced the figures above. ALSO IN THIS COMMIT: the brief validator moved from module level INTO main(). Wiring it at module level took the full suite red at 4 tests, because 2 test files IMPORT the dispatcher to read its real SYSTEM string -- executing rather than grepping, which is the project's own rule -- and stage a stub BRIEF.md purely to pass the file-exists check. They never dispatch. A validation running at import punished INSPECTION, which is not the thing that costs money. main() is the only path to a paid seat, so the guard belongs there, and neither test was edited to accommodate it. A METHODOLOGICAL FINDING, logged as I8. A mutation that fails to apply is indistinguishable from a mutation that was not caught. Twice today a mutation reported "all tests still pass" when its search string simply never matched: once because only 1 of 2 required renames was reverted, once because of a stray backslash in an escaped regex. Both times the first reading was "my test is weak", which is the wrong conclusion and the more alarming one. Every mutation must now assert that the file actually changed before the tests are run.
