title: The new validator refused an unknown flag in the wrong words, and the guard said so
verbatim: The new validator refused an unknown flag in the wrong words, and the guard said so The suite refused panel_brief_validate.py on TestUsageTextAdvertisesOnlyImplementedFlags. With `brief` as a REQUIRED positional, argparse reports the missing argument before it reaches an unrecognised flag, so `--fix-timestamps` produced "the following arguments are required: brief" rather than "unrecognized arguments". That guard exists for a reason recorded in its own docstring: a script that silently accepts a retired flag and does nothing with it is the 118-day no-op again. A new script arriving with that shape on its first day is exactly what the guard is for, and it caught it within the hour. Fixed by making the positional nargs="?" so argparse reaches the unknown-flag check, with the requirement enforced immediately after and a clearer message than argparse's own. All 3 paths executed rather than reasoned about: unknown flag gives "unrecognized arguments" and exit 2; no argument gives "a path to a BRIEF.md is required"; a valid brief passes with exit 0. The other 2 failures in that run -- the additive standard reaching every panel seat, and panel sandbox write containment -- were transient consequences of the brief validator running at module level, and both pass now that it lives inside main(). Checked rather than assumed: 8 passed and 14 passed respectively. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The new validator refused an unknown flag in the wrong words, and the guard said so
verbatim: The new validator refused an unknown flag in the wrong words, and the guard said so The suite refused panel_brief_validate.py on TestUsageTextAdvertisesOnlyImplementedFlags. With `brief` as a REQUIRED positional, argparse reports the missing argument before it reaches an unrecognised flag, so `--fix-timestamps` produced "the following arguments are required: brief" rather than "unrecognized arguments". That guard exists for a reason recorded in its own docstring: a script that silently accepts a retired flag and does nothing with it is the 118-day no-op again. A new script arriving with that shape on its first day is exactly what the guard is for, and it caught it within the hour. Fixed by making the positional nargs="?" so argparse reaches the unknown-flag check, with the requirement enforced immediately after and a clearer message than argparse's own. All 3 paths executed rather than reasoned about: unknown flag gives "unrecognized arguments" and exit 2; no argument gives "a path to a BRIEF.md is required"; a valid brief passes with exit 0. The other 2 failures in that run -- the additive standard reaching every panel seat, and panel sandbox write containment -- were transient consequences of the brief validator running at module level, and both pass now that it lives inside main(). Checked rather than assumed: 8 passed and 14 passed respectively. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: Item 6.1: 23 of 41 runs never recorded why they stopped, and the cause was a fault this file already fixed once
verbatim: Item 6.1: 23 of 41 runs never recorded why they stopped, and the cause was a fault this file already fixed once The founder asked, verbatim: "Preferably all stop reasons should be recorded to make them easily traceable in the future? Not just after convergence. Is that technically possible?" It is, and his framing turns out to be a census result rather than an impression. MEASURED. 23 of 41 archived completion signals carry an empty reason -- 56.1%, Wilson [41.0%, 70.1%], Clopper-Pearson [39.7%, 71.5%]. All 23 are INCOMPLETE. All 16 CONVERGED runs carry a reason. So "recorded only on convergence" is exactly what the archive says. Structurally: the round loop has 8 `break` statements and only 2 of them set stop_reason. ROOT CAUSE, AND ITS PRECEDENT IN THE SAME FILE. The irreducible-queue halt set `result["convergence_reason"] = IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_HALT` and never touched brain.state. `brain._save_checkpoint()` runs on the NEXT line and reads brain.state, so it wrote an empty reason, and signal_complete() then read nothing. The comment at the gamma-alt gate 170 lines below records the identical fault being repaired on 2026-05-18 -- "previously set only the result dict, so post-mortem tooling read every hardened convergence as INCOMPLETE" -- and it was repaired for that branch only. The 2026-09-08 run therefore wrote status INCOMPLETE with reason "" while its own report named HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM, and both were true. FIXED IN 2 PLACES. At the halt site, before the checkpoint rather than after it, because _save_checkpoint() reads brain.state and an assignment after it would be written nowhere -- a test pins that ordering specifically. And by a fallback immediately before signal_complete(), which catches every remaining exit including the 9th `break` somebody adds next month. Naming the 6 remaining exits individually would have been 6 edits that miss the next one. THE FALLBACK SAYS "UNRECORDED_STOP" RATHER THAN LEAVING AN EMPTY STRING. "The runner did not record why" is a different and worse condition than any named halt, and the archive must not make the two indistinguishable. 6 tests, 3 mutations. Each mutation was asserted to have APPLIED before the tests ran, per issue I8 logged earlier today after 2 mutations silently failed to match and were misread as weak tests. All 3 caught, including the ordering one, which is the subtle case: moving the assignment 1 line later writes it nowhere. Also recorded from this investigation, for the closing report rather than acted on: all 48 distinct findings in the 2026-09-08 run carry falsifier_verdict NONE, and 8 of the 9 criticals carry no falsifier code at all (88.9%, Wilson [56.5%, 98.0%]). Whether the gate ran and recorded nothing, or never ran, is NOT established -- the first search term used to test that was wrong, and the stronger claim is not asserted without evidence. title: Regenerate the run ledger after the 6.1 edit moved a citation, and measure how fragile the rest are
verbatim: Regenerate the run ledger after the 6.1 edit moved a citation, and measure how fragile the rest are The suite refused the previous commit's tree on 2 run-ledger tests. The 6.1 fix inserted 9 lines into bench/reference_runner_v3.py, which moved the line the ledger cites from :13744 to :13753. The ledger has a generator, so regenerating healed it and both tests pass. MEASURED WHILE HERE, because the healing is the exception. Across the tracked tree, 48 files carry 102 line citations into reference_runner_v3.py, and 101 of them are HAND-WRITTEN -- 99.0%, Wilson [94.7%, 99.8%], Clopper-Pearson [94.7%, 100.0%]. Exactly 1 is regenerated. So a 1-line insertion silently invalidates any hand-written citation below it, and the existing line-citation guard only checks that the FILE exists, not that the LINE still says what the citation claims. Logged as issue I9 for the closing report rather than chased here, per the founder's instruction that emerging issues must not detract from the work list. The additive fix, when it is scheduled, is a guard that checks the cited line's CONTENT rather than its file's existence. title: Item 3.1: the "misconfiguration" is a deliberate mitigation, and flipping the flags would spend money destroying an experiment
verbatim: Item 3.1: the "misconfiguration" is a deliberate mitigation, and flipping the flags would spend money destroying an experiment FOLLOW stopped this one before FIX. The founder ruled, verbatim: "these are the class of misconfigurations I observed as significant previously and they should be fixed." He gave that ruling on an assistant report that said it was OPEN whether the setting was a deliberate experimental control or an omission. The record says deliberate, and states the reason. routing_enabled: false and post_convergence_sweep_rounds: 0 in the 3 exp56 arms are a documented mitigation for 2 runner defects, each proven by an EXECUTING test in bench/tests/test_d9_d11_configs_valid_2026-09-05.py: 1. _apply_routing builds its ladder from the FULL orchestrator roster rather than from cfg.models. The 1-seat arm declares only CC2, so enabling routing would dispatch to the very vendors the arm exists to do without -- and 3 of the 5 panel seats are paid. 2. The post-convergence sweep dispatches to undeclared seats, demonstrated at :363 by driving it with a stub in place of dispatch_to_model and counting who was reached. BOTH ARE LIVE, NOT HISTORICAL. The routing guard is deliberately conditional and its docstring says so: "If the runner is repaired to intersect with cfg.models, the guard lifts." Run on 2026-09-09 it PASSED rather than skipping, which means the ladder still leaks. The sweep test passed on the same basis. So flipping the flags would destroy the experiment the arm exists to run, and spend money doing it. That is the letter of the ruling, not its intent. The item is superseded by 3.1a: repair the runner so routing and the sweep respect cfg.models. That serves what the founder actually asked for -- machinery that works -- and the guard is already written to stand down by itself once the repair lands, so no config edit is needed at all. Nothing was changed in the configs. This commit records the finding and the corrected item. title: The falsifier union holds against the whole archive: 5295 to 5787 recovered, 0 lost
verbatim: The falsifier union holds against the whole archive: 5295 to 5787 recovered, 0 lost The background scan begun before the 2.1 fix landed has finished, and it is the empirical half of that claim rather than the construction argument. Recovery across every archived reply moves from 5,295 blocks to 5,787, a gain of 492, and the count of files where a block was LOST is 0. As a rate against the 6,363 candidate labels: 83.22%, Wilson [82.28%, 84.11%], rising to 90.95%, Wilson [90.21%, 91.63%]. The 0-lost figure is the load-bearing one, not any p-value. A union cannot lose a capture BY CONSTRUCTION; the scan was run to check whether the construction held in practice, and it did. Quoting a significance test on 492 discordant pairs that all went the same way would dress up an invariant as a result. Recorded in the outcomes companion so it survives compaction. title: Roster confinement repaired properly: a default is not a declaration, and an empty ladder is not a dead transport
verbatim: Roster confinement repaired properly: a default is not a declaration, and an empty ladder is not a dead transport The first roster fix took the suite red. `_declared_models` read the hardcoded `RunnerConfig.models` default as an arm's declaration and returned an EMPTY roster when nothing matched, so routing and the post-convergence sweep dispatched to nobody in silence. The runner's own comment above `run_experiment` records that this default is the pre-Fable panel and that a run leaving it untouched is the launcher config-drop class this project has hit 7 times. This made it 8. Archive reach measured rather than asserted: 0 of 60 archived runs carry a panel disjoint from the default, Wilson [0.0%, 6.0%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0%, 6.0%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 1e-9 over 89 panel records from 2 independent sources with 0 disagreements. Script: scripts/roster_disjointness_2026-09-09.py. An earlier draft claimed the defect "would have disabled routing in every simulated run"; that is false and is corrected in all 3 places it appeared. C-A REFUSED on measurement. The panel proposed filtering `_verification_step` for consistency. It does not dispatch to the roster: it picks the single CC2 seat as a verifier. Filtering removes CC2v from the contrast arm alone, converting a control held constant across arms into a confound in 1 of 3. C-B FIXED. Enabling routing made a previously unreachable path live: an empty ladder was classified as a dead transport and retried forever, so the finding entered no queue count and HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM could not fire in the 1-seat arm whose pre-registration names that halt as its reportable outcome. Also: routing cannot flatten gamma, executed under total absorption and identical to 17 significant figures, now pinned. Task 4.1, the escalation rule names MISCONFIGURATION first across all 5 sites, with the founder's verbatim wording annotated rather than rewritten. Tasks 4.2 and 7.3. The additive-standard ratchet correctly lowered 22 to 21 as `verification_min_round` became reached. CC2's criticism of the guard test is confirmed by mutation and fixed: reverting the wiring left it green, and the file went red only through a sibling test. title: Tasks 6.2 and 6.3: the watchdog stops cutting inside the retry budget, and the runner writes where it was told
verbatim: Tasks 6.2 and 6.3: the watchdog stops cutting inside the retry budget, and the runner writes where it was told 6.2 — TWO NUMBERS, TWO FILES, NEVER COMPARED. Each seat carries a `timeout` and a `max_retries` in the orchestrator, so its worst-case legitimate consumption is timeout * max_retries. The runner capped the wall clock at a fixed multiple of the timeout alone, and `max_retries` — present on every ModelConfig it receives — was read 0 times in that file. The watchdog now takes the max of the two. THE TASK LIST'S FIGURE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT. It said 4 of 5 seats were truncated; scripts/watchdog_vs_retry_budget_2026-09-09.py reads both numbers from source and finds 1 of 5, 20.0%, Wilson [3.6%, 62.4%], Clopper-Pearson [0.5%, 71.6%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 1e-9. Only Gemini is over: a 1500 s budget against a 900 s cap, killed 600 s inside its own allowance while the run recorded a timeout rather than a misconfiguration. The original was an imprecise verb on a real observation — Codex, ChatGPT and DeepSeek sit at exactly 900 s against exactly 900 s, not truncated but with 0 seconds of slack. 4 of 5 are AT-OR-OVER; 1 of 5 is OVER. No slack allowance was invented for the 3 boundary seats, because the dispatch overhead has not been measured. `max` keeps the change strictly additive and a test asserts it: a naive derivation would have CUT CC2 from 4500 s to 900 s and reinstated the timeout cascade its x5 multiplier exists to prevent. Merge arbitration is deliberately left alone, its own site stating those queries are short. 6.3 — WRITTEN AND NEVER READ. `ExperimentConfig.logs_dir` is set on every simulated launch and was read 0 times by the runner, which minted a second directory from the experiment name and a fresh timestamp. A launcher could create a directory, tell the founder where to tail it, pass the path in, and watch the run write elsewhere; 14 of 119 archived runs left artefacts under 2 directories. The named directory is now honoured BEFORE the resume scan, because a caller that named one has already answered the question the scan asks, and scanning first could silently resume a different older run. The fallback is unchanged. 14 tests across the 2 items, 8 mutations, each verified applied, all caught. title: Tasks 6.5, 7.2 and L2: a monitor that dies with its run, a linter that is actually run, and a quote exemption that survives a full stop
verbatim: Tasks 6.5, 7.2 and L2: a monitor that dies with its run, a linter that is actually run, and a quote exemption that survives a full stop 6.5 — bench/tail_until_done.sh follows a run's log and exits when the run exits, never signalling the run, and bench/detached_launch.sh now names it at the one moment an operator has both the log path and the process id. The macOS constraint is measured: `tail --pid` is rejected, the flag appears 0 times in `man tail`, no gtail is installed, so the tie is polled. ITS OWN TESTS FOUND 2 DEFECTS IN IT BEFORE IT SHIPPED, and 1 was the defect it exists to fix. `kill -0` reports a ZOMBIE as alive, so a monitor started from the launching shell would have polled for ever after the run ended; state is now read from `ps` as well. And the first signal trap killed the tail without exiting, so bash resumed the loop and ctrl-C was ignored: SIGTERM at 1.5 s, wrapper returned at 13.5 s, exactly when the stand-in run finished. Now 2.1 s. 7.2 — a 5th pre-commit guard lints every staged note and REFUSES on any finding, per the founder's 2026-09-04 ruling that these are blocking, not advisory. The linter's LOGIC was exercised by 3 test files, which is not the same as running it over the notes: the only test that linted real notes selected those declaring a v1.7 foot-line, 29 of 379, 7.65%, Wilson [5.4%, 10.8%]. A new note omitting the foot-line was exempt by omission. Proven live: staging a spelled number returns REFUSED, names the token, and HEAD does not move. L2 — and making the linter blocking made its known false-positive class urgent. The quote exemption ran per SENTENCE, so a quotation spanning a sentence boundary was split first and each fragment carried an unbalanced quote character. The exemption lapsed on exactly the longest quotations, which here are the founder's, and the standing rule is that the linter is never applied to his words. Measured across 379 notes: 8 false positives removed, 0 added, 0.70% of 1138 findings, Wilson [0.4%, 1.4%]. The first version of that fix INTRODUCED 3 findings by yielding the masked text, erasing the nouns and figures living inside a quotation. The mask now guides the sentence split only. I30 — I8 has a third variant. A mutation can apply to the FILE and still land on a line the fixture never executes: one here replaced an in-loop slice while the single-sentence fixture reached only the trailing one, so the mutant behaved identically and read as SURVIVED. Paired sites are now mutated together. 35 tests across the 3 items, 17 mutations, all caught once the instrument itself was corrected. title: Task 7.1 bounded slice, 8.1, and a guard that refused its own first real commit twice before it was right
verbatim: Task 7.1 bounded slice, 8.1, and a guard that refused its own first real commit twice before it was right 7.1 — 207 of 283 spelled numbers in the notes are now digits, 73.14%, Wilson [67.7%, 78.0%], Clopper-Pearson [67.6%, 78.2%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 1e-9. Scope split at the start rather than the debrief: SPELLED NUMBER is bounded, mechanically checkable and done; UNNAMED SUBJECT (558) is spec-only, because naming the right subject needs per-instance judgement and a regex sweep there is the mechanical rewrite the standard forbids; QUANTITY WITHOUT A VALUE (296) is a later sweep. THE REFUSALS MATTER MORE THAN THE CONVERSIONS. 76 sites are deliberate refusals. Reading the dry run caught 4 classes of FALSE FIGURE before anything was written, and a wrong number reads as a measurement where a spelled one does not: "ten thousand million million" summed to 2010000; "the location series reaches zero three times" would have become "reaches 3 times"; "between one pound forty and two pounds thirty" became 42; "between fifteen and twenty five thousand" became 40000. A 5th was caught by reading the DIFF after the first apply and reverted — a sentence teaching note-standard Rule 11 had its number-words converted, breaking the rule the sentence exists to state. NO VERBATIM QUOTATION WAS REWRITTEN, verified rather than hoped: the double-quoted spans of all 67 changed files compared before and after, the only difference being a quotation the task list itself gained. NOT DONE, needs a ruling: 622 spelled-number sites across 138 of 486 Desktop TTS files. Unversioned folder, so a bulk edit there is not revertible. AND THE NOTE-LINT GUARD REFUSED THIS COMMIT TWICE, correctly by its implementation and wrongly by its intent, at 2 different widths of the same mistake. Whole staged FILES: 388 findings, all pre-existing prose in notes a 1-line correction had touched. Added LINES: 38, because a changed line appears whole in the diff, so correcting 1 numeral made the commit answerable for that sentence's prose. It is now a RATCHET — each note linted at HEAD and as staged, refusing only an INCREASE — which is the idiom this project already uses for unreached config fields, and which asks "did this commit make it worse" instead of "is this file clean". A new note still has a baseline of 0 and is held to the whole standard. 4 tests pin both directions. 8.1 — the `rs` definition no longer hunts 2 files this project has never had: `git log --all` returns 0 commits touching either path. Project-conditional rather than deleted, since a reader of another project still needs to know what they were. An existing guard also caught 4 capped listings in the new scripts printing a truncated list under a heading that reads as complete. Each now states its remainder. title: Task 3.2: the DeepSeek premise refuted by measurement, and the compensator's 3 silent failures made loud
verbatim: Task 3.2: the DeepSeek premise refuted by measurement, and the compensator's 3 silent failures made loud THE PREMISE IS REFUTED FOR DEEPSEEK SPECIFICALLY, which is the finding. The concern was that denying this route its tool loop starves falsifier supply. `tools = None` there is a documented mitigation dated 2026-06-06 — that vendor's OpenAI tool-translation leaks tool calls as DSML markup, so the loop returns exploration code rather than findings — and it ships with a compensator that re-prompts once so prose-style falsifiers become runnable blocks. What the schema requires is a falsifier the runner can EXECUTE, not a tool call. Measured across every archived round by scripts/deepseek_falsifier_supply_2026-09-09.py: DeepSeek supplies one in 103 of 468 replies, 22.01%, Wilson [18.5%, 26.0%], against 325 of 1925 for every other seat pooled — Fisher exact p = 0.0106, odds ratio 1.389, 95% CI [1.083, 1.782], scipy and statsmodels agreeing. It is significantly MORE likely to supply one, not less. Restoring the broken loop would have removed a working mitigation on a premise the archive refutes. Stated so it is not read as more: the ordering is not tools-versus-no-tools, since Gemini is tool-enabled and higher still at 25.54%, and absolute rates are 12% to 35% for every seat, which is a larger question than this item asked. THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG FIRST TIME. `extract_falsifiers` returns a `(by_key, ordered)` tuple and a first version took `len()` of the tuple, scoring every seat at 100% including on empty text. Caught by feeding it an empty string before any figure was believed. That is the 3rd broken ruler this session, all 3 caught the same way, and none was a defect in the code under study. THE REAL DEFECT IS DIFFERENT AND IS FIXED. The compensator failed SILENTLY at 3 points — the caller's `except Exception: pass`, the function's `except Exception: return response`, and the case where the repair dispatched and returned nothing runnable. Only the success path spoke, so 3 endings were indistinguishable in the record, and the measurement above was the only evidence the mitigation works, taken from runs whose repair might quietly have failed. 6 executing tests against a stubbed client with no network and no cost, 4 mutations, all caught. Also the closing report the founder asked for, in both required formats: the TTS plain text on the Desktop and the markdown companion here, which carries the locators the spoken version omits. title: rs: restore recorded, and the tracker's resume pointer advanced 1 day and 6 commits
verbatim: rs: restore recorded, and the tracker's resume pointer advanced 1 day and 6 commits `rs` ran at 22:59 with `--full` (exit code 0) and again at 23:00 with `--record-restore` (exit code 0). The first run's own closing line said "restore NOT recorded" — the 2026-09-08 fix made recording require the explicit flag precisely so a forgotten one leaves the alarm sounding — so it was re-run properly and the marker was written by a genuine restore. title: Correct the stale sealing claim I repeated during rs, and add the 12 tasks that arose from the work
verbatim: Correct the stale sealing claim I repeated during rs, and add the 12 tasks that arose from the work THE CORRECTION FIRST, BECAUSE IT COST THE FOUNDER A DRIVE. The operational tracker listed the answer-key sealing as HELD awaiting his passphrase. He had driven home from his hotel and done it himself on 2026-09-07 at 22:03 — 53 files into 1 archive, 0 plaintext keys left — at the assistant's request. On 2026-09-09 at 23:00 an `rs` restore read that stale line and reported it back to him as still waiting. title: URGENT: task 6.3 shipped a regression that sent every production run into one shared directory
verbatim: URGENT: task 6.3 shipped a regression that sent every production run into one shared directory FOUND BY ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THE COMPLETION CLAIM ITSELF, not by the suite. 18 agents re-checked all 19 DONE entries; 2 independent reviewers agreed this one was not an overstatement but a live regression at HEAD. WHAT WAS BROKEN. `ExperimentConfig.logs_dir` defaults to `bench/logs/experiment_11` — a TRUTHY path — and `load_default_config` sets it on every launch. The 6.3 repair returned it unconditionally, so every run through all 3 live entry points wrote there: experiment name dropped, timestamp dropped, runs colliding with each other and with 22 Experiment 11 artefacts from 2026-03-28, and the resume scan bypassed because the same path came back whether resuming or not. Verified by execution against `load_experiment_config()`, not argued. IT IS THE IDENTICAL ERROR TO THE ONE FIXED 20 MINUTES EARLIER. Commit 0c0f450 is titled "a default is not a declaration" and repaired `_declared_models` for reading the hardcoded `RunnerConfig.models` default as an arm's choice. 6.3 then read `ExperimentConfig.logs_dir` the same way. WHY THE 8 TESTS DID NOT SEE IT. Every one built its exp_config from `types.SimpleNamespace` with hand-set values. The only shape production ever passes — a real `ExperimentConfig` carrying its dataclass default — was the one shape never constructed. 3 tests added that build the real thing, including the launcher's own config; with the regression re-applied they go red and the original 8 stay green, which is the reviewers' point demonstrated. AND THE FIRST REPAIR OF THE REGRESSION DID NOT WORK. It compared raw strings, but the dataclass default is the RELATIVE `bench/logs/experiment_11` while `load_default_config` sets the same default RESOLVED against the repo root. The comparison saw two different strings and returned the default anyway. Caught by re-running the production path after applying the fix rather than assuming it had worked. The comparison is now on resolved paths. An explicitly named directory is still honoured, and still ahead of the resume scan. title: The verification result, the mechanism the founder asked for and did not get, and 5 tasks for the gap
verbatim: The verification result, the mechanism the founder asked for and did not get, and 5 tasks for the gap HE ASKED WHETHER THE MARKER ENGINE ENSURES THE WORK COMPLETES MECHANICALLY AND SURVIVES COMPACTION. Half of it does, and the half that failed is the half he meant. The compaction half works, measured rather than assumed: 5 UserPromptSubmit hooks are wired, the task pulse fired on every turn after the 19:19:57 compaction, and the list and its outcomes companion are ordinary files with Desktop mirrors. The completion half does not exist. `task_list_markers.py`'s CONTRADICTORY set refuses an entry only when its own 2 labels disagree — DONE beside PROPOSED. NOTHING compares a DONE marker against the repository. It is an honesty system with no auditor, and it records what the assistant claims. title: V3: the commit guard had 2 demonstrated bypasses and now has neither, plus 3 of V2's corrections
verbatim: V3: the commit guard had 2 demonstrated bypasses and now has neither, plus 3 of V2's corrections BYPASS 1 — A RATCHET ON A SUM IS NOT A RATCHET. The guard summed every staged note and compared totals, so one commit that cleaned 3 spelled numbers out of an archival note AND added a brand-new note containing "twenty-nine" netted -2 and landed with exit 0. The guard saw the new violation, printed it by name, and let it through. Its own comment said "a NEW note is held to the whole standard" and its test docstring said "the ratchet must not become an amnesty for new work"; both were false in that path, because the only test for it committed a single file and never reached the mixed case. Now judged PER FILE: any single note that gets worse refuses the commit. BYPASS 2 — IT FAILED OPEN WHEN ITS CHECKER BROKE. `LINT_CODE=$?` sat after an if/else, so it read the if/else's status, which always succeeds, and the "linter could not run" refusal was unreachable dead code. A linter that errors still prints "0 finding(s)" on its way out, so the count read 0 and the commit passed — failing open inside a guard whose own header says it fails closed. The linter's status is now captured where it runs and a non-zero exit refuses. Both reproduced as tests. 15 tests, 4 mutations, all caught. V2 CORRECTIONS. 4.2's `status: COMMITTED` was false — the memory repository had never been committed; it now is, in its own commit. 8.1 claimed the 2 files exist in no sibling project; both exist at Project_Genesis/cw_handoff/ and Metis/coordination/, and the entry's own opening line says they were copied into Metis. The cause was a glob searching 1 level deep while the files sit 2 down — the 4th instrument error of the session. 1.1's "28 tests in 1.26 s" is 56 in 1.88 s and never reproduced at any revision; its "11 tests" and "7 tests" are 18 collected cases across 14 functions. 6.5's "12 tests" was 11. title: V1 built, and the FFAFP stop criterion is now computed from the maths model instead of asserted
verbatim: V1 built, and the FFAFP stop criterion is now computed from the maths model instead of asserted FOUNDER INSTRUCTION, verbatim: "f everything (FFAFP in cyclic mode until diminishing returns, as per our maths model, which you should refer to and use)". DIMINISHING RETURNS WAS BEING ASSERTED. The machinery to decide it has been live for months — `_estimate_gamma` and the two-sided gate — and the standing directive says gamma is load-bearing and must not be demoted. An assistant declaring a cycle converged from intuition was demoting it by omission. scripts/ffafp_cycle_gamma_2026-09-10.py applies the project's own gate and re-implements nothing: gamma >= 0.30 AND 3 consecutive zero-discovery passes, both thresholds read from RunnerConfig rather than typed. Verified against an independent scipy least-squares fit of the same log-log regression: exact agreement to 1e-9 across 5 series, mpmath and numpy agreeing to 12 significant figures. SCORED ON ITS OWN SERIES, TONIGHT'S WORK SAYS KEEP GOING. Passes [11, 4, 2] give gamma 0.598241 — the gamma side PASSES and the count side FAILS, so the verdict is KEEP GOING. That is the directive's own named failure mode caught in the act: a flattened curve is not an exhausted problem while discovery continues. 12 tests, 5 mutations, all caught, including one for each side of the gate alone. V1, THE MECHANISM THE FOUNDER ASKED FOR. A DONE marker now carries an `evidence:` field naming the tests that prove it — optional in the regex, required by a suite guard, so an entry predating it cannot break while a DONE entry without it fails. 18 of 19 named nothing before this. 79 tests, 4 mutations. Its limit is written into the file: it cannot prove a named test would go RED against a reverted fix. V1 AND V3 ARE MARKED TESTED, NOT DONE. Section P makes a panel review a precondition on closing ANY item, and closing them without one was I37. The panel is dispatched, 0 paid seats verified before dispatch. I36: every suite figure this session used the wrong command. The documented measure is `-q --netguard-strict`; the session used `-q -p no:warnings`. No money was at risk — the suite is offline by default — but the figures are not comparable with those recorded beside them. Re-running under the documented form. title: Panel round 3: both seats PARTIAL, 6 findings, and the worst one was a guard that audited itself
verbatim: Panel round 3: both seats PARTIAL, 6 findings, and the worst one was a guard that audited itself fable and cc2, 0 paid seats, confinement verified (0 canonical references from either seat). Both returned PARTIAL on the V1 evidence guard. 6 findings, all fixed, each verified by reproducing the reviewer's own mutation. F3 (HIGH) — THE GUARD AUDITED ITSELF AND THEREFORE COULD NOT FAIL. `test_what_this_guard_does_not_prove_is_written_down` read `Path(__file__).read_text()` — the file containing the needle inside its own assert statement — so the search always succeeded on its own source literal. cc2 deleted the ENTIRE module docstring and the file stayed at 79 passed, and showed the needle never matched the prose at all because the sentence wraps. It now reads `__doc__` with whitespace normalised. This is the project's own "a guard that cannot fail is not a guard", in a guard written about verification. F1 (HIGH) — the collection check was a string prefix, defeated by `..`. cc2 demonstrated evidence resolving to /private/tmp passing `startswith("bench/tests/")`. Now resolved containment. The bounded-traversal class again. F2 — `assert True` satisfied "holds a real test". Truthy constants now excluded. F4 — nothing binds evidence to a task. cc2 pointed all 19 fields at one unrelated file and both the guard and the marker engine stayed green. Not a new hole, but the docstring understated the declared limit; widened. F5 (cc2: "cheapest fix, largest effect") — the guard was collected only by the full suite, 13 minutes from the moment a DONE marker is written. Added to the commit-time set with the marker engine's own test. Cost re-measured rather than carried forward: 155 tests in 1.97 to 2.39 s, against the previous 56 in 1.00 to 2.02 s. fable — a wrong-case `state: Done` silently leaves the guard's universe, since every check filters on `state == "DONE"`. `check()` refuses it and the pulse hook crashes on it, but the guard was relying on an accidental chain; now asserted directly. CC2'S STRONGEST DISAGREEMENT IS ADOPTED RATHER THAN ARGUED WITH: "The hole was never 'DONE markers name no evidence.' It was that the author of the claim is also the auditor of the claim." title: V5: the restore now reads the FRESHER document first, which is what cost the founder a drive home
verbatim: V5: the restore now reads the FRESHER document first, which is what cost the founder a drive home On 2026-09-09 at 23:00 an `rs` restore read the operational tracker FIRST, because the recovery script named it FIRST READ, and reported to the founder that the answer-key sealing still awaited him. He had driven back from his hotel and done it himself 2 days earlier, at the assistant's own request. THE CORRECT RECORD ALREADY EXISTED and was not offered. CDSFL_MASTER_TASK_LIST.md, written 8 hours before the restore, states both that he executed it AND that the tracker was stale on it. That file was not in the FIRST READ section at all. FIRST READ now carries the task list and its outcomes companion, orders every entry by modification time newest-first, labels each with how far behind the newest it is, and states the rule for a disagreement: the fresher one wins unless it says otherwise, and a stale document is not a second opinion. THE STANDING EXAMPLE IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. OUTSTANDING_QUEUE_to_BR2.md was described there as the "live work queue" while 14 days old, with every one of the founder's messages since arriving after it was last written. It now prints "<-- 14.0 DAYS older than the newest above". 9 tests, 5 mutations, all caught — and the last only after a fixture was rebuilt. Every ordering test passed with the sort replaced by `pass`, because the DECLARED order and the FRESHNESS order coincided in the live tree, so no fixture could tell a sorted list from an unsorted one. The new fixture inverts them. That is the 4th vacuous fixture found this session by mutating rather than trusting. AND AN EXISTING GUARD CAUGHT THE NEW CYCLE SCRIPT on its first suite run: `--this-flag-does-not-exist` printed a report and exited 0. Nothing here costs money, but a caller who mistypes a flag and reads exit 0 believes a pass was recorded when none was. Unknown arguments now exit 2 with usage. CYCLE GATE: series [11, 4, 2, 3, 6, 2, 3], gamma 0.487, gamma side PASS, count side FAIL, verdict KEEP GOING. title: Task 6.7: the assessment declined a question that was answerable, and both verdicts are now executed
verbatim: Task 6.7: the assessment declined a question that was answerable, and both verdicts are now executed THE ENTRY SAID the calibration claim "can be neither confirmed nor refuted by any run", reasoning that a detector with no production caller cannot be judged. A panel reviewer pointed out on 2026-09-10 that both halves were decidable without wiring anything. They were. VERDICT 1 — THE SEAT'S GUARD IS INCORRECT AS WRITTEN. It reads `if not self.has_evidence(flaw_class)`. `ImmuneMemory` has no such member — 0 of its attributes contain the word "evidence" — so it raises AttributeError on its first call rather than guarding anything. VERDICT 2 — ITS PREMISE IS CORRECT AND EXECUTABLE. Fed an observed rate of 0.0 against the 0.5 placeholder prior, the CUSUM reaches -2.5 and the detector FIRES on the 5th call against a threshold of 2.0. A class with no recorded evidence does drive the detector, which is exactly what the seat was trying to prevent. THE 2 MEASUREMENTS ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS AND BOTH HOLD. "It would not have fired on the 3 real recording runs" is supported — largest excursion 27.98% of threshold, 72% headroom. "It cannot fire" is not, and the 5-call case is the counter-example. The entry collapsed them into one claim and reached the wrong conclusion from the wrong one. 5 tests, including one asserting the detector still has NO production caller, so that if it is ever wired this assessment goes red rather than quietly ageing. What remains for the founder is unchanged: wire it or retire it, carried as I31. CYCLE GATE: series [11, 4, 2, 3, 6, 2, 3, 2], gamma 0.461, gamma side PASS, count side FAIL, verdict KEEP GOING. title: Four agents measured the unbacked figures, and 9 of them were wrong — including a script the fix itself had broken
verbatim: Four agents measured the unbacked figures, and 9 of them were wrong — including a script the fix itself had broken 18 agents in 2 phases, each instructed to test its instrument against a known case before believing a number, because 5 measurements this session were wrong in the ruler rather than the thing measured. 6.2 — THE MEASURING SCRIPT HAD NOT RUN SINCE THE FIX LANDED. scripts/watchdog_vs_retry_budget_2026-09-09.py matched the `wall_limit = (...)` expression that the 6.2 repair replaced, so from 2026-09-09 it exited 1 with "the watchdog expression has moved" and produced nothing, while the entry went on citing figures it was supposed to produce. `measured-rate-travels-with-its-script` failing in the most circular way available. It now reads both the pre- and post-fix forms and names which it found. Post-fix it reports 0 of 5 truncated, Wilson [0.0%, 43.4%] — because the fix worked. The entry's "1 of 5" was the PRE-fix state and never said "before". 2.1 — 5 INDEPENDENT AGENTS CONVERGED ON THE SAME CORRECTIONS. Captured is 5,295 not 5,282 — a figure the entry itself quoted 2 sentences later, so it was internally inconsistent. Missed is 1,068 not 1,081, 16.78% not 16.99%, Wilson [15.89%, 17.72%]. Of those, 1,052 carry a description between label and fence, 97.32%, not 1,066. And the 6,363 denominator is itself unstable — not reproduced exactly under any of 15 readings of the 3-line window — so it now stands as the entry's own figure rather than as a measurement. M1 — THE ERROR IS THE ENTRY'S OWN SUBJECT. It said "15 of 29 ... 51.7%", using a denominator produced by the narrow pattern the entry exists to complain about. The true entry count at both 4b697af and cfdc0cb is 48, re-derived here with the committed ENTRY regex: 15 of 48, 31.25%, Wilson [19.9%, 45.3%]. An entry arguing that a list cannot be counted, counted against the wrong count. 6.5 — the entry described a repaired state in the present tense of the broken one: "0 monitors read a process-identifier file" is false at HEAD because of this very fix. And its test file's docstring claimed "EVERY TEST HERE RUNS THE SCRIPT. None reads its source" while 1 test checks a file mode and another reads bench/detached_launch.sh as text. Both corrected. CYCLE GATE: series [11, 4, 2, 3, 6, 2, 3, 2, 9], gamma 0.451, gamma side PASS, count side FAIL, verdict KEEP GOING. Pass 9 found more than passes 6, 7 and 8 together, which is what delegating the measurement was for. title: The guard that refuses wrong numbers was passing wrong numbers, and both seats found it
verbatim: The guard that refuses wrong numbers was passing wrong numbers, and both seats found it Panel round 6 asked cc2 and fable how to fix the problems round 5 diagnosed, and both independently found that `check_declared_figures` matched by SUBSTRING. A figure declared as 0.29 "reproduced" against a printed 0.294998; a figure declared as 1 rode on the words "pass 1:". Reproduced here before acting: over 7 cases the substring form scored 4, Wilson [25.0458%, 84.1780%]. Both of their fixes are applied. cc2's whole-token matching, delimited by anything that is not a digit, letter, dot or minus. fable's residual, that a bare 1 or 9 is a genuine token in almost any output, closed by requiring at least 3 significant characters. Over 8 cases it now scores 8, Wilson [67.5592%, 100%]. THE FIRST ATTEMPT TOOK 2 EXISTING TESTS RED. The distinctiveness rule ran before the script-exists rule, so a declared figure against a missing script reported "fewer than 3 significant characters" instead of "the script does not exist". A guard must report the most fundamental failure it found or it sends the reader to repair the wrong thing. Infrastructure first, then the figure. 29 tests. THE PRE-COMMIT GATE'S PINNED COUNT MOVED 169 TO 174, because task V7 added 5 tests to one of its 6 guard files, and `test_precommit_gate_cost_2026-09-10.py` went red exactly as its own docstring says it should. Test and entry 1.1 corrected in the same change, which is what that docstring asks for. Also removed from 1.1 a duplicated sentence and a stale "These 4 files", both left by my own third correction of that entry. AND A GUARD I HAD FORGOTTEN CAUGHT ME. `wilson_interval_consistency.py` refused the round-7 brief: it stated "8 ... against 4 of 7 ... Wilson [67.56%, 100.00%]", attaching the 8-case interval to the 7-case count. A correct interval under the wrong count, in a brief about a guard that refuses wrong numbers, caught by a machine before dispatch rather than by a reader afterwards. 1508 files scanned, now 0 disagreements. title: Rescue 4 panel records from an ignored directory where no commit could reach them
verbatim: Rescue 4 panel records from an ignored directory where no commit could reach them `bench/logs/` is excluded by `.gitignore:41`. Every raw panel record written today therefore sat on one machine, unversioned, recoverable by nothing. 440 KB across 23 files: 8 seat replies, 8 tool logs, 5 briefs, a correction sidecar and the proposals diffs. All 23 verified byte-identical to their originals by sha256. The Personalisation directive requires external review output preserved in full and unfiltered and says "Never summarise in place of the full output". Until this copy existed the only durable artefacts were derived summaries -- and a derived summary is exactly what an audit caught overstating this morning, when a report claimed both seats ran mutations against the task 6.7 repair and the tool logs showed neither had. A verdict without its tool log cannot be audited, so the tool logs are copied too. VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: 8 seat replies preserved, 0 on a paid route. Every one records `route=claude_cli`, the Max subscription. No cx, cgpt or ds seat file exists in any of the 4 directories. THE COMMIT-TIME NOTE LINTER REFUSED THE FIRST ATTEMPT, and it was right to. 4 of the copied briefs raised findings the moment they were staged, and the only way to satisfy the linter would have been to EDIT a verbatim record. The project already had the answer: `experimental_notes/evidence/` stores seat-written code as `.py.txt` to keep it out of the source scanners, so an archival brief is stored as `.md.txt` to keep it out of the note scanner. No byte changed, no `--no-verify`, and the guard still binds on everything it should. `bench/logs/` remains archival and is not edited; the round-4 brief's correction still sits beside it as a sidecar rather than being folded into the brief. title: The founder's Desktop copies had silently diverged, and the restore could not see it
verbatim: The founder's Desktop copies had silently diverged, and the restore could not see it He asked this morning whether the outcomes companion "on my desktop (which I presume you have been updating)" was current. It was not. Measured: 1 of 3 Desktop copies matched its canonical original. The master task list was 29,383 bytes short, the outcomes log 5,016 bytes short, and his copy of the task list held nothing written after 01:15 while he was reading it at 10:30. THE SAME CLASS OF STALENESS ALREADY COST HIM A JOURNEY. On 2026-09-09 a restore read a stale line and reported that the answer-key sealing awaited him; he had driven home from his hotel and done it himself on 2026-09-07 at 22:03. Task V5 fixed the ORDER documents are read in. It could not stop a mirror drifting, and `cdsfl_recover.py` named only 1 of the 3 mirrors, so it was structurally blind to the 2 that had actually gone stale. Three changes, and none of them relies on remembering. FIRST READ now names all 3 Desktop copies and says, per file, whether it matches the repository copy -- a diverged mirror is announced as DIVERGED with the byte difference, because a mirror that quietly disagrees is worse than no mirror: it is read with the authority of the thing it copies. `scripts/sync_desktop_mirrors.py` refreshes them, verifying each copy by sha256 after writing rather than assuming the copy succeeded. It never copies Desktop back over the repository -- the repository copy is canonical by founder ruling of 2026-08-05 -- and a test pins that direction. The pre-commit hook refreshes them as a 6th stage that CANNOT REFUSE A COMMIT. A convenience copy on one machine must not be able to block work, and a guard that fires on the ordinary case teaches people to reach for --no-verify. A test parses that stage and asserts it contains no exit 1. AND THE HOOK'S OWN HEADER WAS STALE IN THE SAME WAY. It said "these 4 files" while the GUARDS list held 6, and quoted 155 tests where the list now collects 174. title: The founder's Desktop copies had silently diverged, and the restore could not see it
verbatim: The founder's Desktop copies had silently diverged, and the restore could not see it He asked this morning whether the outcomes companion "on my desktop (which I presume you have been updating)" was current. It was not. Measured: 1 of 3 Desktop copies matched its canonical original. The master task list was 29,383 bytes short, the outcomes log 5,016 bytes short, and his copy of the task list held nothing written after 01:15 while he was reading it at 10:30. THE SAME CLASS OF STALENESS ALREADY COST HIM A JOURNEY. On 2026-09-09 a restore read a stale line and reported that the answer-key sealing awaited him; he had driven home from his hotel and done it himself on 2026-09-07 at 22:03. Task V5 fixed the ORDER documents are read in. It could not stop a mirror drifting, and `cdsfl_recover.py` named only 1 of the 3 mirrors, so it was structurally blind to the 2 that had actually gone stale. Three changes, and none of them relies on remembering. FIRST READ now names all 3 Desktop copies and says, per file, whether it matches the repository copy -- a diverged mirror is announced as DIVERGED with the byte difference, because a mirror that quietly disagrees is worse than no mirror: it is read with the authority of the thing it copies. `scripts/sync_desktop_mirrors.py` refreshes them, verifying each copy by sha256 after writing rather than assuming the copy succeeded. It never copies Desktop back over the repository -- the repository copy is canonical by founder ruling of 2026-08-05 -- and a test pins that direction. The pre-commit hook refreshes them as a 6th stage that CANNOT REFUSE A COMMIT. A convenience copy on one machine must not be able to block work, and a guard that fires on the ordinary case teaches people to reach for --no-verify. A test parses that stage and asserts it contains no exit 1. AND THE HOOK'S OWN HEADER WAS STALE IN THE SAME WAY. It said "these 4 files" while the GUARDS list held 6, and quoted 155 tests where the list now collects 174. Both re-measured by `scripts/precommit_gate_cost_2026-09-10.py`, which reads the GUARDS list instead of carrying a copy of it. That figure has now been wrong 4 times by being typed and carried forward. 9 new tests. 25 passing across the 2 pre-commit guard files. title: Panel round 7 delivered CODE, not prose, and its code found 2 more holes in mine
verbatim: Panel round 7 delivered CODE, not prose, and its code found 2 more holes in mine THE DELIVERY RULE CHANGED AND IT WORKED. Rounds 5 and 6 handed back 0 source files: both seats wrote and ran real fixes in scratch space, `teardown()` deleted the sandbox, and only the prose survived. The round-7 brief opened with a new section -- a finding without a fix is not a deliverable, AND a fix described in prose is not delivered either -- and told each seat to write its repair at its real path INSIDE the sandbox tree, which is the only place `changes()` preserves. Round 7 returned 2 new test files and a patch to the validator. WHAT THEY FOUND IN YESTERDAY'S REPAIR. My round-6 hardening expressed "whole token" as a fixed character class, and it was wrong in BOTH directions. * It still passed wrong numbers. `,` was not in the class, so a declared `234` reproduced against a script printing `entries = 1,234` -- the round-6 defect exactly, one separator over, off by a factor of 5. `12:345` satisfied `345` the same way. * It refused right ones. `.` was in the class unconditionally, so a script printing `gamma is 0.294998.` -- the figure ending a sentence -- could not be declared at all. A guard that refuses a correct brief gets bypassed, which costs more than the defect it caught. The replacement is context-sensitive: a `.` or `,` continues a number only when a digit sits on the far side, so each occurrence is judged by looking one character PAST the delimiter rather than by membership in a set. AND A HOLE THAT WAS NOT ABOUT NUMBERS AT ALL. A declared script path starting `../`, or an absolute path -- which pathlib joins by REPLACING the left side -- executed a script OUTSIDE the repository and accepted its output as evidence. It is refused before execution now. A figure is a committed measurement only if it re-executes from the repository. Plus: a malformed declaration used to match nothing, be skipped silently, and let the brief pass with zero checks run. Openers are now counted against parsed matches, so a declaration that announces itself and then escapes checking refuses. Opt-in means an ABSENT declaration passes, not a broken one. P-PASSED RATHER THAN TRUSTED. Their tests are theirs, so I ran a battery of 12 cases they did not write: thousands separators, colon groupings, a figure ending a sentence, a negative sign, a date, an identifier, a longer-decimal prefix, and 3 path escapes. 12 of 12 behave correctly -- the 1 I first scored as a miss was my own expectation being wrong, since `84` carries 2 significant characters and is correctly refused by the 3-character rule. 75 tests across the 4 files. 0 paid dispatches; both seats claude_cli on the Max subscription. title: An 8th commit guard, because the one that caught 2 of today's errors was not run
verbatim: An 8th commit guard, because the one that caught 2 of today's errors was not run A code-only commit landed a red suite at 9dfbc2e, silently. The morning's audit had named that exact gap: the pre-commit hook runs 6 guard files and NOT the test that was red, so nothing at commit time could see it. The guard in question earned its place twice within an hour. `wilson_interval_consistency.py` refused the round-7 brief before dispatch -- it stated the 8-case interval against the 7-case count -- and then refused a comment a panel seat had just written, in which the lower bound of a Wilson interval was rounded UP from 20.6549% to 20.66%. Rounding a lower bound up NARROWS an interval into a stronger claim than the data supports, and it happened inside the very comment correctly warning that an "8 of 8" score overstates its own support. COST RE-MEASURED, NOT CARRIED FORWARD. 7 guard files, 178 tests, 6.53 s to 7.10 s against 669.92 s for the full suite. That is 3.8 times the previous gate and 94 times cheaper than running everything, for a defect class that has bitten 3 times today. The figure, the file count and the test that pins them are all derived from the hook's own GUARDS list by `scripts/precommit_gate_cost_2026-09-10.py`, which reads it rather than carrying a copy -- that figure has been wrong 4 times by being typed. Entry 1.1, the hook header and the pinning test were updated together in one change, which is what that test's docstring asks for. title: Task 0.2: the Wolfram MCP route did not always fail, it died on 2026-09-04
verbatim: Task 0.2: the Wolfram MCP route did not always fail, it died on 2026-09-04 RETIRED under the additive standard's removal clause, which permits removal only on "a COMMITTED MEASUREMENT showing the replacement dominates on a named property" and says "a judgement that something is better is not evidence that it is". The property is availability; the replacement is the local Engine reached through `wolframscript`; the measurement is `scripts/wolfram_route_health_2026-09-10.py`, which reads the desktop application's own logs and never writes to them. WHAT IT FOUND IS STRONGER THAN THE ENTRY THAT ASKED FOR IT. Across 34 log files and 64 connection attempts, split at the date entry 0.2 names: before 2026-09-04 : 1 failed of 21, 4.7619%, Wilson [0.8456%, 22.6694%] from 2026-09-04 : 42 failed of 43, 97.6744%, Wilson [87.9410%, 99.5883%] exactly 1 successful attach in that entire later period. Fisher exact p = 2.199086e-14, odds ratio 840, cross-checked by a chi-square with Yates correction at p = 8.709349e-13 and an mpmath exact hypergeometric tail agreeing with scipy to 2.2e-14. The route worked for a month and then stopped. ENTRY 0.2's OWN FIGURE IS SUPERSEDED. It said "39 connection failures ... against 2 successes in the whole log". There are 21 successful attaches, not 2. The conclusion was right and the arithmetic was not, which is precisely why the script is committed beside the number rather than the number standing alone. AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG FIRST. Counting every line naming the route gave 156 of 1176, 13.27% -- a figure with no meaning, because the denominator swept in "Shutting down MCP Server", "Closing" and every routine announcement. Only an attach that announced its tools, or a manager reporting a failure to connect, is an attempt. Caught by reading the sample lines before believing the rate. The tool constraint box in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` now marks the MCP server RETIRED, names the local Engine as the only Wolfram route, and keeps the stdio-shim note as history rather than as advice. 10 tests drive the classifier against synthetic logs, including the case that produced the wrong denominator. ONE CHANGE REMAINS AND IT IS THE FOUNDER'S: removing the `WolframCloud` key from `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` stops the app retrying a dead endpoint every few minutes. That file is his desktop application's own configuration and is not the assistant's to edit. title: Stop the alerts: the dead Wolfram MCP entry is out of the desktop config
verbatim: Stop the alerts: the dead Wolfram MCP entry is out of the desktop config Done on the founder's explicit instruction, he being away from the machine: "Edit the file to stop the alerts ... I'm not at home so I can't do it." The `WolframCloud` key is removed from `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`. The app had been retrying a dead endpoint and logging an error every few minutes. P-passed BEFORE writing, because a config that does not parse takes the whole application down: the new text was reparsed, the key asserted gone, the top-level key set asserted unchanged, and `coworkUserFilesPath` and `preferences` asserted byte-equal. A timestamped backup sits beside the file. A REMOVAL THAT CANNOT BE UNDONE IS A DELETION, AND THIS IS NOT ONE. The exact invocation, the backup path and the reason are recorded at `experimental_notes/evidence/wolfram_mcp_entry_removed_2026-09-10.json`, and a test asserts the endpoint URL and the backup both survive there. Restoring the route is one paste. AND I OVERSTATED THE RETIREMENT, WHICH IS NOW CORRECTED. The constraint box said "RETIRED ... DO NOT USE IT AND DO NOT REPAIR IT". That went past the evidence and past the founder's position. He has emailed Wolfram about the MCP server licence, WHICH IS SEPARATE FROM THE DESKTOP ENGINE LICENCE, and his words are that the service "has its uses. For example you can talk to it in natural language and get useful output back." The box now says DISABLED BECAUSE IT IS DEAD, NOT BECAUSE IT IS UNWANTED, and names the lost capability explicitly: `wolframscript` takes Wolfram Language, not English. Disabling a dead endpoint is not a verdict on the service. Task W1 added at the END of the list, on his instruction, BLOCKED on Wolfram's reply and paired with the 2026-09-11 desktop-licence check. It states what is measured (42 of 43 attempts failed from 2026-09-04) and what is NOT established: whether the cause is a lapsed licence, a withdrawn service or a transport fault; whether an MCP licence is separately purchasable; and whether the desktop licence auto-renews as the documentation implies. 2 of my own tests went stale against my own edit and both are fixed. One was the self-quoting trap again -- the correction paragraph QUOTES the old wording in order to retract it, so a document-wide search could not tell a live command from a cited one. The assertion is now scoped to the directive line, which is the same correction the panel-brief validator and the note linter each needed. 13 tests. title: Task 3.3: the exp56 off-switches have siblings, and sk_enabled is false in every arm
verbatim: Task 3.3: the exp56 off-switches have siblings, and sk_enabled is false in every arm Nothing had ever looked. `routing_enabled: false` was found by accident, and a capability switched off in a config file is invisible to the suite -- every test passes and the feature never runs. That is the additive standard's own failure mode hiding in data rather than in code. `scripts/capabilities_disabled_by_config_2026-09-10.py` reads the 3 frozen exp56 arm configs against 210 runner modules, resolving reads by AST rather than by grep, because a grep for a field name matches its own definition and its docstring. 18 off-switches found; 9 are READ by the runner, 50.0000%, Wilson [29.0310%, 70.9690%], Clopper-Pearson [26.0191%, 73.9809%]. THE 9 LIVE ONES: `hardened_gate_enabled`, `apply_fixes_back_enabled` and `sk_enabled`, each false in all 3 arms. `sk_enabled` is the S_k threshold, part of the mathematical model, off in every arm of the next simulated run. The other 9 are set off and read by nobody -- `merge_arbitration_enabled`, `immune_memory_enabled`, `_ouroboros.max_papers_per_round`. Different defect, reported separately rather than conflated, filed as A18. NOTHING WAS CHANGED, DELIBERATELY. These are frozen pre-registration files and task 3.1 established what a literal reading costs: flipping flags there would have destroyed the experiment the arm exists to run and spent money doing it. The test pins WHAT IS TRUE so the next run cannot be launched in ignorance; whether sk_enabled should be false is the founder's call. THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG TWICE AND BOTH WERE CAUGHT BEFORE A FIGURE WAS BELIEVED. It first read only reference_runner_v3.py -- 3 read, 12 unread -- and would have reported 6 capabilities as unwired that are read in launcher_core.py, which is a false claim about ABSENCE, the hardest kind to notice. That correction alone surfaced 3 more off-switches. 9 tests. Task list: 87 entries, 32 DONE. title: A Stop hook that refuses a narration turn, because a resolution is not a mechanism
verbatim: A Stop hook that refuses a narration turn, because a resolution is not a mechanism The founder, 2026-09-10: "Can you not write some kind of mechanical 'is blocker' / 'is not blocker' ... script ... to prevent this? You can't self-diagnose/repair the exact cause beyond this?" HE WAS RIGHT AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID SO. Over that day's 25 messages, turns carrying `d` made a median of 3 tool calls against 13 without it, Mann-Whitney U = 26.0, p = 0.0097 -- `d` genuinely suppresses work. BUT 8 of the 16 turns carrying no `d` still stopped after 12 calls or fewer, Wilson [28.00%, 72.00%]. Half the stops had nothing telling them to stop. My first explanation blamed his shorthand, which was the half of the evidence that flattered me. scripts/blocker_triage.py decides mechanically. BLOCK under 4 rules only: IRREVERSIBLE, NEEDS_HIS_HANDS, FROZEN_ARTEFACT, WOULD_WASTE_WORK. Everything else is PARKED to experimental_notes/PARKED_FOR_THE_FOUNDER.md, which he reads at the end. Parked is queued, not dropped. The asymmetry is deliberate: a false BLOCK costs 1 interruption, a false PARK could let an irreversible action proceed unasked, so it answers BLOCK when it cannot tell. Verified against 4 real items from today: the desktop config edit BLOCKS on NEEDS_HIS_HANDS, flipping sk_enabled BLOCKS on FROZEN_ARTEFACT, a paid seat BLOCKS on IRREVERSIBLE, and the guard defect PARKS. hooks/work_not_narrate.py is a STOP hook -- the first hook here that can refuse anything. The 4 preceding it are UserPromptSubmit context injectors making 0 subprocess calls and 0 blocking decisions, always exiting 0, which is exactly the shape task 1.1 named: "a guard that cannot fail is not a guard". This exits 2, which blocks the stop and feeds its reason back. It fires only when ALL 5 hold: open items remain, no task closed, no commit, fewer than 6 tool calls, more than 1,200 characters of prose -- AND his message did not carry `d`. His command overrides absolutely. It cannot loop: stop_hook_active exits 0, so it interrupts at most 1 stop per turn. THE SETTINGS EDIT WAS P-PASSED BEFORE WRITING AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS REFUSED BY ITS OWN ASSERTION. I asserted len(hooks["UserPromptSubmit"]) == 5; it is 1 -- one matcher holding 5 hooks. The write was refused, settings.json was untouched, and the assertion now counts inner hooks. A corrupted settings.json breaks every session, so a pre-write check there is not ceremony. 14 tests: that it CAN block, that `d` overrides, that it stays silent on 4 ordinary cases, that stop_hook_active prevents a trap, that a broken payload never breaks a session, and that the versioned copy matches the live one -- because 3 of the 4 earlier hooks existed in no repository at all. title: Admissibility gate ON in all 3 arms, and the blocker predicate now asks his question
verbatim: Admissibility gate ON in all 3 arms, and the blocker predicate now asks his question TWO THINGS, both on his instruction: "Just do it all (turning on the admissibility gate too, if its off) and continue with your work on the task list". S_k IS ON IN ALL THREE EXP56 ARMS. The earlier reason is SUPERSEDED, NOT DELETED, and both it and the evidence for the change now sit in each config's `_sk_note`. * It is not dead code. Before the 2026-08-01 hard-gate repair the pipeline REJECTED everything and halted visibly; that repair turned a loud failure into a silent one, which is why the post-repair archive shows 0 rejections across 4142 gate records. The founder's recollection and the earlier note describe different periods and both are correct. * Enabling it adds no admission risk. Over a 2475-point grid in sk, nu_b, nu_f, q and R the corrected gate is STRICTER at 502 points, 20.2828%, Wilson [18.7453%, 21.9125%], and LOOSER at 0, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.1550%]. Against 326 archived shadow records corrected and shipped AGREE 326 of 326. * The one harmful case is a non-Python target, where ruff cannot parse the file and the ranking inverts -- a shell injection inside a fence scored 1.0000 ADMISSIBLE against 0.6667 for a correct prose fix. The runner forces the gate off for any non-Python target, and all 3 arms are target_kind python_module. AND I MISREAD THE RUNNER DEFAULT IN FRONT OF HIM. I reported v3 defaulting sk_enabled to True. It is False at line 1085, identical to the frozen v1 -- my grep matched a SUBSTRING, because `inround_reask_enabled: bool = True` contains `sk_enabled: bool = True`. That is the exact substring-versus-token defect the panel found in my figure guard this morning, repeated 4 hours later in a grep. Resolved by AST. THE BLOCKER PREDICATE ANSWERED THE WRONG QUESTION. His criterion is "does it prevent further progress on the task list?" The first version used 4 category rules of which 3 say nothing about progress, so it called editing his desktop config a BLOCK when that blocked nothing. Blocking and permission are orthogonal and are now returned separately: an entry must DECLARE a dependency, by carrying state BLOCKED or saying so; a bare file path cannot establish dependence, because a file central to many entries says what work is about rather than what waits on it; and a term appearing in more than a quarter of entries is a shared subject. The asymmetry reversed too -- it used to answer BLOCK when unsure, which is exactly the interruption he objected to, and the permission gate carries the safety regardless. Measured accuracy 9 of 10 on a labelled set, Wilson [59.5850%, 98.2124%]. The miss is an item identified only by a bare alphanumeric code, and it misses toward PARK. 17 tests on the predicate, 87 on the config sweep and the arm guard. title: The gate has rejected 520 of 5834, and the note saying otherwise was about a sub-gate
verbatim: The gate has rejected 520 of 5834, and the note saying otherwise was about a sub-gate THE FOUNDER'S RECOLLECTION WAS RIGHT AND MY CITATION WAS MISLEADING. He said the admissibility gate "is not dead code and has triggered in at least some small percentage of cases". I quoted the config note back at him -- "has never rejected anything, 0 of 3816" -- as though that settled it. It does not. S_k pipeline as a whole, REJECTED : 520 of 5834 = 8.9133%, Wilson [8.2089%, 9.6717%] threshold sub-gate, passes false : 0 of 4142 = 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.0927%] The "never rejected" figure is true only of `passes_threshold`, the last sub-gate. The hard gates and the effect gates sit before it and have rejected 520 fixes. 8.91% is exactly the "small percentage" he remembered, and the note read as if the whole mechanism were inert. All 3 `_sk_note` fields now carry the distinction. AND NO_SCORE HAS NEVER OCCURRED: 0 of 5834, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.0658%]. Every archived run targeted Python, so the prose short-circuit has never fired. ON HIS DESIGN POINT, filed as A19. He is right that S_k classifies the TARGET and not the ELEMENT: TARGET_KINDS is exactly (python_module, prose), so a SEARCH/REPLACE block editing a fenced Python listing inside a markdown file is never scored though it is computationally reducible. The buildable form is per-hunk classification -- score the reducible hunks, NO_SCORE the rest. I differ on one word, with the code's reason rather than mine. Marking prose REJECTED would assert the fix is BAD. The source is explicit: "NO_SCORE is NOT a third grade of admissibility, it is the statement that S_k has no opinion." A correct prose fix is unscoreable, not defective, and REJECTED would be a claim the evidence does not support. ON CONVERGENCE HE IS ALREADY RIGHT AND THE CODE ALREADY AGREES. apply_sk_to_rk returns R_k UNCHANGED on NO_SCORE, and records why scoring it 0 was rejected: the re-injection term nu_eff is MAXIMAL at sk=0, so a zero score pushes R_k from 0.500 to 0.620 per unassessed finding -- fabricated risk a prose run could never work off, because no S_k evaluation on prose can move it back down. Priority on A19 is low and measured as such: a real gap that has never yet bitten. title: The continuation hook existed and never fired; it does now
verbatim: The continuation hook existed and never fired; it does now He asked "So where is the continuation fix you built, or said you would build?" Fed this session's own transcript, the hook returned "allow the stop" every time. It was wired, it was tested, and it was too weak to do anything. THE PREDICATE ONLY CAUGHT NARRATION. title: L1 closed: the founder's words cannot gate a commit, proven with a negative control
verbatim: L1 closed: the founder's words cannot gate a commit, proven with a negative control His ruling: "Refusing work from me because it does not fit your own 'anti-vagueness' standards is clearly nonsensical and probably very unhelpful going forward." The record supports him without qualification -- of 1183 findings across 376 notes, 1181 are in the assistant's own prose and 2 fall inside a quotation of anyone at all, 99.83%, Wilson [99.39%, 99.95%]. The entry said the linter was advisory, so nothing of his had been refused. That stopped being the whole story when task 7.2 made it BLOCKING at commit time: from then a false positive inside a quotation of his left 2 choices, editing his words or bypassing the guard. TESTED WITH A SENTENCE ENGINEERED TO TRIP THE 2 HARDEST RULES -- a spelled number and an unnamed subject -- in every form a note actually uses: inline double-quoted 0 counted inside a verbatim region 0 counted, 2 REPORTED (visible, not gating) 4 real rulings of his 0 counted in all 4 the same sentence as MY own prose caught on both rules THE LAST LINE IS THE POINT. Without a negative control every exemption above could be vacuous -- the linter might simply never fire on that sentence. It does. A PARAPHRASE OF HIM IS STILL LINTED, deliberately. Exempting paraphrase would turn a boundary into a bypass: any prose could escape by mentioning him. 9 tests, including the end-to-end case -- a note consisting only of his quoted words lints to 0, so the per-file commit ratchet cannot refuse it. title: R2: the exp50/51 redesign, derived from the record rather than recalled
verbatim: R2: the exp50/51 redesign, derived from the record rather than recalled His ruling 2026-08-22: "5: Redesign with all uncovered fixes in place after the upcoming build experiment and any fixed it uncovers in place also." The precondition has been met, so this was execution work -- except that "all uncovered fixes" was not a list anyone had written down. SO IT WAS DERIVED. The 3 exp56 arm files are the newest pre-registration artefacts and postdate every fix in question, so a setting all 3 agree on is the current convention and a difference is a candidate gap. Measured by scripts/exp50_51_redesign_gap_2026-09-10.py: 14 of 68 settings out of step, 20.5882%, Wilson [12.6796%, 31.6423%], Clopper-Pearson [11.7380%, 32.1238%]. 4 CHANGES, each carrying its previous value and its reason inside the file. target_kind absent -> "prose". The test_article is a .md review document; inference gets there anyway, but a config that does not say what it reviews cannot be read. sk_enabled True -> False, matching what the runner enforces regardless: with a prose target it FORCES S_k off, because ruff cannot parse the file and the ranking inverts. Declaring true reproduces exactly the defect the 2026-08-01 note records -- "sk_enabled is TRUE in all eight queued prose configs, against a code default of FALSE". merge_arbitration_enabled True -> False. The merge path is dead code: it logs MERGE WITHHELD and returns KEEP_DISTINCT. routing_enabled absent -> True, declared rather than defaulted silently, now that 3.1a closed the roster leak. 3 DIFFERENCES DELIBERATELY KEPT, because not every difference is a gap. max_rounds and extension_cap stay at 16: these are ONE-SHOT ARCS against an answer key, and 8 is sized for 3 arms in sequence. immune_memory_enabled stays TRUE: exp56 disables it to stop arm 2 inheriting arm 1's findings, a CROSS-ARM path a single-arm experiment does not have. THE FROZEN ORIGINALS ARE NOT EDITED. Each declares "Frozen before the run", and neither has ever run -- the only exp50 directory in the archive is a draft review. The redesign sits beside the original as *_redesigned_2026-09-10.json, and tests assert the originals still carry their original values. 18 tests. NOT RUN: both declare 5 models including 3 paid seats, so running them is money, one of the 3 standing categories requiring him in person. Triaged and PARKED rather than raised, because nothing on the list waits on the result. Task list: 88 entries, 34 DONE. title: The continuation hook gave up after ONE refusal; the bound was the defect
verbatim: The continuation hook gave up after ONE refusal; the bound was the defect He asked "You still stopped?" and he was right. `stop_hook_active` is a BOOLEAN the harness sets after the first refusal, and the hook honoured it as "give up". That capped it at exactly 1 refusal per turn, which converts "one task then report" into "two tasks then report" and no further. Observed twice in a row: the hook refused, L1 was done, the turn ended; the hook refused, R2 was done, the turn ended. The mechanism worked exactly as built and was built too weak. Refusals are now COUNTED per turn, keyed by the turn's own user message, with a budget of 8. `stop_hook_active` reports that a refusal happened; it no longer decides the outcome. Verified by execution against this session's real transcript: 8 refusals, then it yields. IT IS A BUDGET RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE OF ONE, and every failure path yields rather than refuses. An unknown turn yields. An unreadable state file yields. An unwritable one yields. A guard that refuses on its own malfunction is the shape this project keeps having to withdraw, and the asymmetry is the right way round here: a wrong yield costs one extra prompt from him, a wrong refusal costs him a session he cannot end. THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS WAS REFUSED BY THE AUTO-MODE CLASSIFIER and I did not work around it. Editing the live hook that decides whether a session may stop, in a way that removes a loop guard, is exactly what that classifier exists to catch. The change was built and proved in the repository copy first -- 8 refusals then yield, against the real transcript -- and only then installed. 6 new tests, 21 in the file. One of them earned its keep immediately: it went red while the repo copy was ahead of the live hook, which is precisely the drift it was written to catch, and 3 of the 4 hooks that predate this one existed in no repository at all. title: R3: the deliverable was making silent arming impossible, not arming it
verbatim: R3: the deliverable was making silent arming impossible, not arming it His ruling 2026-08-30 was option A -- the block sits behind a switch that CANNOT SILENTLY REVERSE A RESULT until he says so -- and the entry's own instruction is to raise it when the run needs it, not before. The run has not happened. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION rather than by reading the entry: the default is False; the UNCONFIRM call sits inside the flag's branch; and with the control off the finding is still marked NON_DISCRIMINATING, still escalated and still reported to a human, so only the silent reversal is withheld. 0 of 7 configs arm it. THE GATE-SITE CHECK IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because that is the original defect: the un-confirm used to run UNCONDITIONALLY while the switch everyone assumed governed it guarded a DIFFERENT site, and both reviewing models read it as gated when it was not. THE NEW GUARD IS WHAT WAS MISSING. A config that arms the flag must explain why in one of its own _note fields or the test refuses it. An armed flag with no recorded decision is exactly what his ruling forbids, and verifying "it is currently off" would not have caught a future config that turned it on quietly. Why it matters, measured at commit adb566b across 246 archived findings: 126 of those fixes do NOT silence their own falsifier, 51.2%, Wilson [45.0%, 57.4%], p = 0.75 against a coin toss. Roughly half the time that branch fired it was un-confirming a sound falsifier on a real defect. 11 tests. Task list: 88 entries, 35 DONE.
