title: Section R write-backs, and the commit hook that would have refused every one of them
verbatim: Section R write-backs, and the commit hook that would have refused every one of them THE HOOK COULD REFUSE EVERY REMAINING COMMIT, AND CARRIED ITS OWN CURE OUT OF REACH. The section-R commit below was refused by the Desktop-mirror drift guard. The stage that REPAIRS mirror drift was stage 6 of the same hook, 6 stages below the exit, so the repair sat downstream of the check that needed it. From the moment the RUNWAY joined the guarded set, every commit touching a mirrored file was refused permanently -- and CDSFL_MASTER_TASK_LIST.md is a mirrored file. Fixed by ordering: the refresh is stage 0. It cannot mask a defect. The repo copy is canonical by founder ruling and the refresh only ever copies repo -> Desktop; the guard still runs afterwards and still refuses if the refresh failed or is absent. The check keeps its authority and stops preventing its own remedy. 3 HAND-WRITTEN MIRROR TABLES EXISTED AND ALL 3 DISAGREED. 3 names in scripts/sync_desktop_mirrors.py, 2 pairs in the drift guard, 3 names again in scripts/cdsfl_recover.py. Union 4, intersection 1. All 3 keyed on a bare filename, so none could express RUNWAY_to_BR2_2026-08-18.md, which declares its mirror at its own line 229 as ~/Desktop/CDSFL_RUNWAY.md -- a different name. The sync script's comment asserted "the mirror must never be renamed", which was already false when written. A structure that cannot express a case does not report it; it omits it. So the RUNWAY was guarded by a test and refreshed by nothing, the task list and outcomes log were refreshed and guarded by nothing, and the restore could not see the RUNWAY mirror at all -- it would have called a stale one ordinary, which is the exact failure that on 2026-09-09 sent the founder home from his hotel for a job already done. One table of pairs now, in the sync script, imported by all 3 consumers. The panel named this hand list on 2026-09-01 in bench/logs/panel_fixes_20260901T123808Z/fable.json; the finding stood 9 days. The drift message reported line counts alone, so the first real failure read "has 814 lines, has 814" -- 2 equal numbers offered as evidence of difference. It now reports bytes, the first differing line, and the command that repairs it. MUTATION-VERIFIED IN BOTH HALVES. Moving the refresh back below the guards takes 3 tests red, one of which RUNS the hook against a deliberately drifted Desktop under a fake HOME (only Desktop is fake; the rest of HOME is symlinked through, because 2 guards read ~/.claude and a test that reddens unrelated guards proves nothing). Dropping the renamed mirror takes 3 different tests red. Sources restored byte-identical. 15 tests pass. SECTION R -- 5 rulings written back into the documents that still asked for them. The defect the section exists for, measured 2026-09-09: all 5 sources an inventory read were written BEFORE at least 1 later message from him, Wilson [56.6%, 100.0%]. A document written before he spoke cannot record what he said, so a settled decision keeps resurfacing as a question. R4, severity is a vote (FW.7). 3 documents written back; the 4th already carried it. The runway row said "Structural. Not actionable without a design decision on what would replace it" -- it now records that he rejected BOTH removal and the rubric swap and ordered worked proofs. The rubric agrees with the number at kappa = -0.0227, Fisher p = 0.78: a different oracle, not a better one. DECISIONS_AWAITING_YOU is ANNOTATED, never rewritten, and a test enforces that. It records the assistant recommending the swap he rejected; rewriting it would erase that he was given a wrong recommendation. R5, C0015/C0017 materiality: RECOVERY.md no longer carries it as PENDING. R5a stays open and separate, as the entry already said. R7 was ALREADY DONE and nobody had noticed -- the tracker reads "DONE BY THE FOUNDER HIMSELF, 2026-09-07 at 22:03". A write-back task that had itself gone stale, which is this section's own defect one level up. R8, BR2 blind validity. The docstring said the question "is open". He answered 6 minutes and 46 seconds after it was written: "The answer kets for BR2 being public is a non-issue, since clearly it has never been ran." A blind experiment that never ran cannot have been unblinded. Splitting the keys still matters and the docstring still says why. R9, the load balancer: "retire" becomes "SHELVED, NOT RETIRED". The findings behind the recommendation are kept and a test asserts they survive -- he rejected the disposition, not the evidence. 10 tests for section R, 15 for the mirrors. Task list: 88 entries, 40 done, 42 open, 3 blocked, 3 withdrawn. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: R5a: the materiality population 11 / 6 / 2 is withdrawn; the review it sizes is not
verbatim: R5a: the materiality population 11 / 6 / 2 is withdrawn; the review it sizes is not THE CLAIM. Decision 32 of the 51-decision file states the unstarted materiality review's population as "11 Exp 49, 6 Exp 48, 2 Exp 47 HIL residuals". CLOSING_2026-09-06.md:39 recorded that it does not reproduce, that it appears in exactly 2 places with no post mortem, artefact or script behind it, and that it should not be quoted until something reproduces it. This is that something. A SEARCH, NOT A SPOT CHECK. Checking 1 definition and reporting a mismatch shows only that the definition I happened to pick disagrees -- a universal asserted after checking 1 member, which is the error this project keeps making. So scripts/materiality_population_2026-09-10.py enumerates every count the archives can produce: every registry field, every value it takes, every severity band, every round series. 690 candidate definitions -- 187 for exp49, 204 for exp48, 299 for exp47. NOT ONE reproduces 11 / 6 / 2 as a single measure. THE LABEL FAILS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE ARITHMETIC. No HIL-labelled measure yields exp49's 11 or exp48's 6. The measured escalated counts are exp47 6, exp48 1, exp49 0 -- the OPPOSITE ORDER to the claim, so it is not a mis-scaled or mis-transcribed version of the truth; it is ordered against it. THE INNOCENT READING WAS TESTED, NOT ACCEPTED, AND IT FAILS. The closing report offered one and called it "probably the right one": an exam finding is adjudicated against the held answer key, so the number may be real and simply uncheckable today. That reading has a boundary and the boundary is decisive -- it can only cover a target that needs an answer key. 1 of the 3 runs does not. exp47 reviews bench/dm/_divergence.py, a CODE target, named as such in its own report, readable in full today. Its escalated count is 6, its human-queue count 3, its irreducible count 3. None of those is 2. ONE QUALIFICATION, RECORDED BECAUSE THE SCRIPT REFUTED THIS RULING'S FIRST DRAFT. The draft said no HIL-labelled measure produced ANY of the 3 figures. False: exp47's 2 is exactly the number of distinct MODELS flagged for review in that run. 2 models is not 2 findings, so it cannot be the shared meaning of a triple stated as a population of findings -- but the coincidence is real, it is printed by the script, it is asserted by a test, and it is not hidden. THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS THE LOAD-BEARING TEST. A search that reports "nothing reproduces this" is worthless if it could never report anything else. One test feeds the search a triple that IS a single measure -- the archives' own escalated counts, 0, 1 and 6 -- and requires it to name `escalated == true`. Without that, the null result would be unfalsifiable. Ruling written back to the 3 documents that still ask the question. DECISIONS_AWAITING_YOU is ANNOTATED, never rewritten, and a test enforces it: that file records what was ASKED, and what it records is a population put in front of the founder that no run produced. Deleting it would erase that. The review itself remains worth doing. Its population must be derived before it starts, rather than quoted. ALSO: THE HOOK PRINTED 25 LINES OF NOISE INSTEAD OF THE FAILURE. On a refusal it ran `tail -25` over pytest's output, and on this machine the last 25 lines are TMPDIR cleanup warnings from unrelated tests -- 0 of them naming what broke. Twice in one session the real cause had to be found by re-running the guards by hand, which is the hook costing time rather than saving it. It now prints the FAILED, ERROR and assertion lines first, keeping the tail as a fallback for a failure that produces none. bench/tests/test_materiality_population_2026-09-10.py, 10 tests, all executing the script rather than reading it. title: R6: both factual questions about the absolute-path defect, answered by measurement
verbatim: R6: both factual questions about the absolute-path defect, answered by measurement He ruled the fix itself on 2026-09-08 -- "for sure we should fix it" -- so the ruling was never in question. What was owed was 2 facts, and they are the assistant's to establish, not his to decide. The 2 answers are not equally strong, and saying so is part of the answer. (b) NOTHING NEEDS REVERTING. THIS HALF IS FULLY DECIDABLE. A rewrite that never reached a commit cannot need reverting, and whether it reached one is a question the whole history answers exactly. All 3 observed rewrites of bench/dm/_memory.py -- 25,861 bytes after the first aborted run, then 24,834 at 04:20:52 and 25,650 at 04:22:22 on 2026-09-08 -- appear in NO commit on any ref. That file has had exactly 2 distinct committed sizes across its entire history, 10,734 and 20,605, and 20,605 is the size the records give as correct. No tracked file differs from HEAD. (a) THE BLAST RADIUS IS BOUNDED BELOW AT 0 AND CANNOT BE BOUNDED ABOVE. Of 39 archived run reports, 0 show a target that changed mid-run and 0 show target content that was never committed. But the instrument that decides it -- the per-round target_hashes digest -- was recorded by only 4 of 39 runs, 10.26%. The other 35, 89.74%, Wilson [76.42%, 95.94%] and Clopper-Pearson [75.78%, 97.13%] by a 2nd tool, are NOT CLEAN AND NOT DIRTY: the instrument was not running when they ran. Folding them into the clean count would be "a guard that cannot fail is not a guard" arriving by another route, so they are reported separately and loudly. The 2 exam runs among the 4 take targets outside the repository, so git cannot check those either. POSITIVE CONTROLS ON BOTH INSTRUMENTS, because a detector that could never fire prints the same "0 mutated" as one that fired correctly. A synthetic report whose target hash changes between rounds must be caught; a size that IS in the history must be found. The classifier was extracted from main() specifically so the null result could be falsified -- inline, the only available input was the real archive, which contains no mutated run. A COVERAGE FIGURE DISAMBIGUATED, NOT CORRECTED. reference_runner_v3.py's docstring states 9 run directories and 38 hashed rounds. That counts a DIFFERENT population -- all run directories, simulation harnesses included -- and re-measuring that population today gives 17 directories and 66 rounds, of which 13 are simulations. Both figures are legitimate for what they count; quoting one against the other is not. The docstring now carries the date of its measurement and cites the script, because a bare count that grows is a stale claim waiting to be repeated, and this project has corrected the same cost figure 3 times for exactly that reason. scripts/target_mutation_blast_radius_2026-09-10.py, and bench/tests/test_target_mutation_blast_radius_2026-09-10.py with 10 tests. verbatim: R10: the reading his own precondition required, written as a file he can read He deferred the references selection to a discussion CONDITIONAL on both parties having read the sources first, ruling twice in 69 minutes on 2026-09-06. The reading was then delivered in conversation only. A condition that cannot be met is not a deferral, it is a stall, and the stall was on this side. TWO FILES, per the standing protocol. ~/Desktop/CDSFL_tts/Reductionism_Reading_ 2026-09-10.txt, 752 words in spoken form with 0 markup characters, and experimental_notes/Reductionism_Reading_2026-09-10.md for the repository. The markup-free property is asserted by a test, not by intention: he is dyslexic and this file is read aloud, so a hash or a backtick is either voiced as noise or swallowed. THE SUBSTANCE. Nickles (1973, J. Phil. 70(7):181-201) is the right lead, because the direction inverts: the richer, later theory reduces TO the simpler, earlier one in a limit, as special relativity does to Newtonian mechanics. Nagel (1961) is the WRONG lead -- Nagelian reduction derives across vocabularies via bridge laws, and C(n), F_n, D(n) and G_n never leave theirs, so the apparatus does no work. Batterman (2002) is the objection that must be answered rather than a claim being made: where a limit is singular the limiting-case reduction fails, so all 4 branches were executed and all 4 are REGULAR, the value at the point equalling the two-sided limit. IT CARRIES WHAT EXECUTION REFUTED, not only what it confirmed. A reading that reported only the confirmations would be advocacy. 2 of the 5 claims at PAPER.md:528 failed. One omitted the independence condition: at rho = 0.5 with p = 0.2, the value 0.58016 is C(n) for no integer n at all. One asserted a universal without the enumeration: R_k(i) does NOT nest, carrying a pole at 1/q and a novelty floor against a degree-3 polynomial kernel. THE CENTRAL CLAIM WAS RE-EXECUTED BEFORE DELIVERY, not quoted from the record. scripts/verify_paper_reduction_properties.py, 7 groups of checks under SymPy and mpmath and cross-checked in Wolfram, re-run 2026-09-10: every check passes. The test runs it too, so a reading whose central claim had gone stale cannot sit in front of him looking current. ONE CORRECTION TO THE ENTRY ITSELF: it said the material was in resources/RECOVERY.md, and it is -- under "reduction", not "reductionism". The first search used the wrong stem. bench/tests/test_reductionism_reading_delivered_2026-09-10.py, 6 tests. Task list: 88 entries, 43 done, 39 open. title: 4.3 and R11: complexity measured and reported, and it reaches no decision
verbatim: 4.3 and R11: complexity measured and reported, and it reaches no decision HIS RULING, VERBATIM, 2026-09-09: "Yes we should measure complexity and make it a reported statistic in our reported results at the end of each experiment. But maybe as an informative statistic only, since I don't think you are saying if measuring it should also change behaviour too?" R11 IS NOT A NEW DECISION. That ruling already answers it. The closing question is not rhetorical, and the answer is YES: putting a real measurement in nu would have changed behaviour. nu_b and nu_f are literal arguments to the live fix-admission gate. Over the reachable box, [0, 0.5] squared at 26 x 26, 570 of 676 grid points give a DIFFERENT admission verdict from the shipped constants -- 84.3%, Wilson [81.4%, 86.9%], Clopper-Pearson [81.4%, 87.0%], the 2 tools agreeing to 1e-9. Widening to [0, 1] squared gives 645 of 676, 95.4%, so the conclusion does not turn on where "reachable" is drawn. So the statistic goes to gamma_input, which no decision path reads, and "informative only" now holds BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by intention: a test walks every call to the gate and fails if it ever receives the complexity value. THE 84.3% HAD NO PRODUCING SCRIPT. It was written into the task list on 2026-09-09 and existed only as prose, which this project's own rule calls a claim about evidence rather than evidence. Caught while writing it into a source comment, before it shipped. scripts/nu_carries_complexity_moves_the_gate_2026-09-10.py now calls the live gate and reproduces it exactly. THE FIRST ATTEMPT TO CHECK IT SWEPT THE WRONG BOX, got 645 of 676, and was about to report that 84.3% did not reproduce. The 2 worked points reproducing exactly is what said the gate call was right and the BOX was wrong. The figure was correct; the check was not. IT ALSO CLOSES THE ADDITIVE STANDARD'S OWN FAILURE MODE. compute_gamma_input was imported by the live runner at :221 and CALLED NOWHERE -- an addition nothing reaches, which the standard forbids as squarely as a removal, and which task 4.3's own text named: "its measuring module is unreached". A FALLBACK THAT LOOKED LIKE A MEASUREMENT NEARLY SHIPPED. Below MIN_WINDOWS the function returns an ASSUMED beta of 0.5 -- gamma 0.5, K 0.0, r_squared 0.0. The default window is 10,000 chars and converts to tokens at a fixed 4:1, but this repository's code runs at about 14:1 -- bench/dm/_memory.py is 20,563 chars and only 1,485 tokens -- so EVERY ordinary code target fell below the threshold and the report would have carried gamma_input 0.5 in a field a reader takes as measured. Found by a test written to check the statistic's DIRECTION, which returned 0.5 for both a repetitive and a novel text. Repaired by counting rather than guessing: the window is derived from the module's own tokeniser, aiming for 2 x MIN_WINDOWS because a 3-point fit returns r_squared 1.0000 by arithmetic rather than evidence. Nothing in input_complexity changed, because other callers depend on its defaults. The record carries an explicit fit field, measured or ASSUMED_DEFAULT, and an assumed value ships with a reading that says in words that it carries no information about the target. ONE ASSERTION WITHDRAWN DURING THE WORK: that r_squared > 0 marks a real fit. It does not. A perfectly saturated text has zero variance to explain and returns r_squared 0.0 while beta 0.0 and gamma 1.0 are exactly right. n_windows against MIN_WINDOWS is the correct discriminator, which is what the runner keys on. Measured on a real target: _memory.py gamma 0.394127, r_squared 0.996892, 7 windows. bench/tests/test_target_complexity_is_reported_2026-09-10.py, 10 tests. Task list: 88 entries, 45 done, 37 open. title: 0.2: the Wolfram route disabled and the alerts stopped, with the cut FITTED not chosen
verbatim: 0.2: the Wolfram route disabled and the alerts stopped, with the cut FITTED not chosen He instructed this himself, being away from the machine: "Edit the file to stop the alerts then continue with the remaining work. I'm not at home so I can't do it." The WolframCloud entry is out of the desktop application config, so it no longer retries a failing endpoint every few minutes. A DISABLING, NOT A DELETION. The exact invocation, a full timestamped config backup and the reason are recorded at experimental_notes/evidence/wolfram_mcp_entry_removed_2026-09-10.json, and restoring it is one paste. That matters because W1 is him asking Wolfram whether the MCP licence can be renewed -- separate from the desktop Engine licence -- and of the route he said "It has its uses. For example you can talk to it in natural language and get useful output back." That capability is a NAMED LOSS: wolframscript takes Wolfram Language, not English. THE FIGURES THAT CARRY THE WORD "DEAD" HAD NO PRODUCING SCRIPT. .claude/CLAUDE.md cited scripts/wolfram_route_health_2026-09-10.py for the change-point analysis -- 1 of 21 before, 42 of 43 after, Fisher p = 2.199086e-14, odds ratio 840 -- and the script emitted only the pooled 67.1875%. Of everything in that block those are the numbers that least belong in prose alone, because the additive standard permits a removal only on a COMMITTED MEASUREMENT and these are that measurement. `change_point()` now produces them. THE CUT IS FITTED, NOT CHOSEN. Every candidate date is tried and the split minimising Fisher exact p is reported. It lands on 2026-09-04 and reproduces every figure the box already carried, so it CONFIRMS that block rather than supplying it, and would have contradicted it just as readily. A FIRST VERSION CUT AT THE FIRST FAILURE and got 2026-08-25, 0 of 10 against 43 of 54. That failure is a 1-off: the next attempt succeeded 19 seconds later and 20 more succeeded after it before anything else broke. Cutting at an isolated blip is how a change-point analysis launders a hand-picked date as a derived one. A SECOND CORRECTION, TO MY OWN WORDING. The evidence file first said "21 of 64 attempts SUCCEEDED and the most recent was 2026-09-09, so the route is unreliable rather than dead". Every number in that sentence is true and the sentence is still misleading, because it pools across the change point -- the 2026-09-09 success is the single surviving attach in the whole post-cut period. Withdrawn in place, with the reasoning kept. The odds ratio is reported in both orientations. scipy's (before, after) table gives 0.00119048; the box records 840, the same number inverted, which is the direction a reader means. Printing one without the other reads as a contradiction between 2 measurements when there is only 1. 13 tests pass. Task list: 88 entries, 46 done, 35 open, 1 deferred. title: 2.2 partial: the missing-falsifier population was wrong by a factor of 29
verbatim: 2.2 partial: the missing-falsifier population was wrong by a factor of 29 His ruling was "fix and test all remaining missing falsifiers". Before any of them could be fixed, "all" had to mean something countable, and the obvious count is wrong. 817 IS A CATEGORY ERROR. Sweeping every archived registry for a critical finding with an empty falsifier_code returns 817. But the falsifier mechanism was BUILT on 2026-06-03 -- components at ed12c7f, the voting replacement at 4fba6cc. A run from April could not carry a falsifier, and calling that a missing falsifier is like calling a 1990 car's absent airbag a manufacturing defect. Split at the build date: 789 pre-mechanism, 28 after. 28 IS THE TASK: 9 against live targets, 19 against zero-plant controls. The controls are counted separately on purpose -- a finding raised against a target with nothing planted in it is a candidate FALSE POSITIVE, so writing its falsifier tests whether the finding was real, not whether a defect is. 28 of 440 post-mechanism criticals is 6.36%, Wilson [4.44%, 9.04%], Clopper-Pearson [4.27%, 9.07%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00. scripts/missing_falsifiers_2026-09-10.py. ALL 28 CARRY THE VERDICT "UNTOOLABLE", AND THE FIRST ONE EXAMINED WAS NOT. exp47 C0053, raised by Gemini at severity 0.8 and escalated to the human queue, claims the cross-round recidivism check punishes a model for supplying a previously-missing contrast statement: parse_contrast_statement strips the new contrast line, the stripped bodies are then identical, and the check scores them 1.0 and rejects the repair as a near-copy. That is a claim about 2 named functions in a module still in this repository. Nothing about it is untoolable. Nobody wrote the tool. THE FINDING WAS CORRECT AND THE DEFECT IS ALREADY FIXED. _recidivism_text folds the contrast statement back in for the cross-round comparison, and the source comment beside it names Gemini's exact scenario. So the falsifier does the 2 things a falsifier is for: it demonstrates the current code is right, and a control reverts the fix in place and reproduces the 1.0 score, because a falsifier that cannot fail confirms nothing -- the vacuity found in 8 of this project's own mutation tests on 2026-09-09. C0053 also carries 3 pairs in adjudication_by_repair.json as NO_BASELINE, "CONFIRMED/NO_FALSIFIER (no version reproduces both)". A missing falsifier is an equipment failure blocking adjudication, not a hard case. CHECKED AND SET ASIDE: exp48 C0015 appears in the same NO_BASELINE bucket but is NOT a missing falsifier. It has one, 2,213 characters, CONFIRMED and verified. Its adjudication fails on a target-path mismatch -- the falsifier reads bench/cdsfl_registry/targets/exp48_chemistry.md while the run's target was /Users/georgejackson/CDSFL_review_targets/exp48_chemistry.md. A different defect, recorded rather than folded in. 3 API mistakes were made building the falsifier and each was fixed by reading the source rather than guessing: AlternativeRecord takes no alternative_id, requires dimension, and check_sibling_admissibility takes a LIST as its first argument. 2.2 stays OPEN at status BUILT. 1 of 28 done, 27 remaining, and the UNTOOLABLE label on each of those is now suspect rather than trusted. title: 2.2: exp42 C0002 was toolable AND still live -- compose() mutated the caller's packet
verbatim: 2.2: exp42 C0002 was toolable AND still live -- compose() mutated the caller's packet THE SECOND "UNTOOLABLE" FINDING EXAMINED WAS NEITHER UNTOOLABLE NOR STALE. CC2 raised it on 2026-06-06 at severity 0.7: "compose() mutates the caller's situation DirectivePacket in-place ... The docstring claims the function is 'Pure'." It was recorded UNCONFIRMED with an empty falsifier and the verdict UNTOOLABLE. It is a claim that calling a function changes an object the caller still holds, which is 3 lines to check. IT WAS TRUE, AND STILL TRUE AT HEAD 96 DAYS LATER. bench/cdsfl_registry/composer.py:1362 wrote through to the caller's situation packet, and the loop above it wrote through to each domain packet, while the docstring at :1310 promised "Pure: no side effects, no state mutation". FIXED by replacing rather than mutating, in both places. THE SEVERITY IS NOT OVERSTATED, and the limit is asserted rather than implied. Nothing live was corrupted: build_interaction_pattern constructs a NEW DirectivePacket from the preset tuple rather than returning the preset, and _load_domain_directive reads from disk per call, so no shared object was reachable. The defect was a false docstring plus a trap armed for the first caller to reuse a packet -- at which point the phenotype transform compounds on every pass. A test holds that boundary by clobbering one packet and checking the next call is unaffected. THE CONTROLS. The model whose phenotype transform is used is chosen by EXECUTION, not by name: if the transform were the identity, the purity assertions would pass whether or not compose mutated anything, which is the vacuity found in 8 of this project's own mutation tests on 2026-09-09. A second control performs the pre-fix mutation on a copy and requires it to change the text, so the assertion it mirrors is shown to have teeth. 2 of 2 UNTOOLABLE findings examined were toolable, and 1 of the 2 was a live defect nobody had looked at since June. 26 remain. bench/tests/test_falsifier_C0002_compose_purity_2026-09-10.py, 5 tests. The composer's own 45 tests still pass. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: 2.2: C0019 and C0031, one defect found by 2 models -- mechanism real, harm not demonstrated
verbatim: 2.2: C0019 and C0031, one defect found by 2 models -- mechanism real, harm not demonstrated DeepSeek raised C0019 and Gemini raised C0031 in the same exp42 run, both at severity 0.80, both against _block_is_hard: a directive block is classified HARD, and so protected from pruning, on the strength of an ordinary modal verb. Both were recorded UNCONFIRMED with the verdict UNTOOLABLE and an empty falsifier_code. Two independent models agreeing on a mechanism is the strongest signal this project's registry produces, and nobody wrote the 5 lines to check it. THE MECHANISM IS REAL and is now asserted: adding " You must keep them short." to a plainly SOFT block flips it to HARD. Their implementation reading is exact, including the case-insensitivity Gemini quoted. THE HARM THEY IMPLY IS NOT DEMONSTRATED. 59 of 90 real compositions exceed the coherence budget -- 65.5556%, Wilson [55.2835%, 74.5541%], Clopper-Pearson [54.7960%, 75.2596%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00 -- but every one raises a UserWarning naming the model, the density, the budget and exactly what was pruned, and ComposedDirectiveSet carries constraint_density and coherence_budget as fields. That is an operating point compose() reports on every occurrence, not a silent failure. Recorded as CONFIRMED MECHANISM / HARM NOT DEMONSTRATED. Whether 65.5556% is acceptable is a design question for the founder, not a defect to fix quietly by tightening a classifier -- and tightening it would risk dropping genuine HARD constraints, which is the failure direction that actually matters. ONE THING BOTH FINDINGS MISSED, in the implementation's favour: the markers are space-delimited, so "mustard" and "remastered" do not fire. The substring trap that has bitten this project 3 times elsewhere is already defended against here. TWO OF MY OWN CLAIMS WERE WITHDRAWN BY EXECUTION, and both are kept as tests so they cannot return. 1. "80.9524% of HARD blocks are classified incidentally." The proxy was "does the block also contain an explicit HARD keyword", and the blocks it selected refuted it immediately: "Sample size must be pre-specified", "Randomisation must be computer-generated", "Informed consent per Declaration of Helsinki ... must be obtained BEFORE any study-specific procedure". Those are genuine hard constraints in a clinical directive and "must" is the marker, not an incidental verb. The proportion was real and measured the wrong thing. 2. "The budget miss is silent." composer.py:1478 warns. I had read the 4 return paths of _prune_for_coherence, seen the last fall through without a check, and concluded silence from the returns while the warning sat 500 lines away. That is execute-do-not-grep failing in the direction it always fails. bench/tests/test_falsifier_C0019_C0031_hard_blocks_2026-09-10.py, 7 tests. 4 of 4 UNTOOLABLE findings examined were toolable. 24 remain. title: 2.2: C0040 confirmed -- every model gets 9.0026% of the universal directive, as flags
verbatim: 2.2: C0040 confirmed -- every model gets 9.0026% of the universal directive, as flags ChatGPT raised it on 2026-06-06 at severity 0.88. It was recorded UNCONFIRMED, UNTOOLABLE, with an empty falsifier_code, and nobody looked at it for 96 days. It is the largest finding in the set and it is about the HARD directive every seat receives. CONFIRMED, AND NOT "WHENEVER" -- ALWAYS. The full universal directive is 27,803 characters; the largest max_directive_chars in the roster is 12,000. So the reduced rendering goes to 5 of 5 models, Wilson [56.5518%, 100.0000%], Clopper-Pearson [47.8176%, 100.0000%]. The docstring promises "Full text for large-context models" and no such model exists -- the branch cannot fire. THE REDUCED FORM IS A FLAG DUMP, NOT A SUMMARY. 2,503 characters of policy.constraints.falsification_required=true. 0 of the full directive's 16 section headings survive it. A model told a flag is set has not been told what falsification is or how to perform it. AND THE PART THAT KEEPS THE SEVERITY HONEST, which must travel with the finding. The models are NOT left holding flags. reference_runner_v3.py:8339 appends cdsfl_operational.md -- 44,157 characters -- to every model, explicitly exempt from the phenotype caps. The prompt a seat receives is 46,660 characters and over 90% prose. Reporting the substitution without this would be alarming and wrong. WHAT IS LOST BY BOTH PATHS. The operational directive covers 6 of the 16 sections of the full universal directive: 37.5000%, Wilson [18.4812%, 61.3590%], Clopper-Pearson [15.1984%, 64.5654%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00. The other 10 include "Runnable Falsifiers for Critical Findings" and "Falsifier Integrity -- Do Not Reach for the Answer" -- the section instructing models not to cheat on the falsifiers this project's verdicts rest on. THE HEURISTIC IS CRUDE AND THE TEST SAYS SO. First 3 words of 4 or more characters per heading, all required to appear somewhere in the operational text. A section covered under different wording reports NOT FOUND, so 10 of 16 is an UPPER BOUND on the loss, not a measurement of it. The tests assert the bound and never the point estimate. NO FIX APPLIED, DELIBERATELY. Changing which directive text a model receives changes every dispatch and invalidates replay of every archived run. title: 2.2: C0037 confirmed -- the directive dedup deleted a formula and kept its special case
verbatim: 2.2: C0037 confirmed -- the directive dedup deleted a formula and kept its special case DeepSeek raised it on 2026-06-06 at severity 0.70, recorded UNCONFIRMED and UNTOOLABLE with an empty falsifier_code. It is 5 lines to check and it deletes mathematics. THE MECHANISM. _semantically_duplicate calls a short line a duplicate of a longer one whenever intersection / min(len(left), len(right)) >= 0.95, and the dedup keeps whichever came FIRST. The survivor is decided by position, not by content. It runs for 4 of the 5 models -- every concise and minimal phenotype. MEASURED over the real directive corpus: 14 of 1,677 lines are dropped as duplicates, 0.8348%, Wilson [0.4979%, 1.3964%], of which 11 are dropped by CONTAINMENT ALONE with a Jaccard below the 0.85 bar -- 78.5714%, Wilson [52.4108%, 92.4286%], Clopper-Pearson [49.2024%, 95.3421%]. THE CASE THAT TURNS A MECHANISM INTO A HARM. In logistics_supply_chain.txt the dedup DROPS SS = z * sqrt(LT * sigma_d^2 + d_bar^2 * sigma_LT^2) and KEEPS SS = z * sigma_d * sqrt(LT) The kept line is the dropped line at sigma_LT = 0: a strict special case, constant lead time. SymPy gives general^2 - simple^2 = d_bar^2 * sigma_LT^2 * z^2, positive for positive quantities, and z3 returns UNSAT for "can the general form be smaller than the special one". At z = 1.645, LT = 9, sigma_d = 20, d_bar = 100, sigma_LT = 0.5 the survivor understates safety stock by 29.778607 units -- 128.478607 against 98.700000, or 23.1770% -- with mpmath and numpy agreeing to 1e-9. A model reading that directive is told to size safety stock with a formula that cannot see lead-time variability at all. sp.ask could not decide the inequality symbolically and that is not glossed: the domination is proved through the squares, where the gap is a single positive term, and confirmed independently by z3. THE DROP RATE IS STATED ALONGSIDE THE HARM. 0.8348% is rare, and reporting the formula case without the rate would inflate the finding. A test asserts the rate stays rare and fails if it rises above 5%. NO FIX APPLIED. The patch is 1 line -- on containment, keep the line with MORE tokens rather than the earlier one, which never loses information and changes only which of a matched pair survives. It changes the directive text every model receives and so invalidates replay of archived runs, the same class as C0040 and the S* threshold promotion. Parked with the patch described in experimental_notes/PARKED_FOR_THE_FOUNDER.md. bench/tests/test_falsifier_C0037_containment_dedup_2026-09-10.py, 7 tests. 6 of 6 UNTOOLABLE findings examined were toolable. 22 remain. title: Panel round 8: CC2 and Fable delivered fixes as files, and 5 of them land on my work
verbatim: Panel round 8: CC2 and Fable delivered fixes as files, and 5 of them land on my work Dispatched under PANEL_ONLY=cc2,fable, Max subscription, 0 paid dispatch. The brief was REFUSED TWICE by scripts/panel_brief_validate.py before it went out -- no refutation clause, no termination criterion, no output shape, and 2 declared figures too short to verify. It passed all 7 checks on the third attempt and the validator re-executed every declared figure against its producing script. THE DELIVERY RULE WORKED. Both seats left files in the sandbox tree. Rounds 5 and 6 returned 0 source files; this round returned 2 new test files and 7 edited ones. Both verdicts: SOUND_WITH_CAVEATS. All 3 declared figures reproduced exactly at both seats. FIVE FINDINGS LAND ON MY OWN WORK AND ALL FIVE ARE CORRECT. 1. MY "GAP CLOSED" CLAIM ON THE MIRROR TABLE IS REFUTED. There was a FIFTH mirror. Exp40_to_54_Consolidated_Plan_2026-04-21.md -> ~/Desktop/CDSFL_Consolidated_Plan_2026-04-21.md is declared 3 times in the notes, the Desktop copy exists and is diverged right now by 2,606 bytes, and Document_Estate_Audit_2026-08-06.md:421 records it as CORE/KEEP_AND_CONVERT with a live instruction to brief panels from it. It escaped BOTH directions of the new test: my declaration regex required the Desktop path within 20 non-backtick characters of the word "mirror", and that declaration puts a backticked repository path there first, so the reverse sweep written to catch exactly this reported nothing. The failure class the fix claims to close, recurring while the closure was being written. Table now holds 5 pairs; the widened regex was enumerated over every note before shipping -- 5 real mirrors, 0 false positives. 2. MY C0053 CONTROL WAS A TAUTOLOGY. It compared prior.alternative_text with fixed.alternative_text -- the SAME str object, since both records are built from one BODY constant. The assertion was score_isomorphism(s, s) == 1.0, a property of score_isomorphism and nothing else, and it survives destroying _recidivism_text entirely. It also short-circuited the mechanism: parse_contrast_statement never ran, so the stripping step C0053 is about was never exercised. In the file whose own docstring says "A falsifier that cannot fail confirms nothing". Replaced with a control that rebinds the module-level _recidivism_text and drives check_sibling_admissibility itself, restored in a finally. VERIFIED HERE BY MUTATION AGAINST THE REAL MODULE: destroying the fix in bench/dm/_divergence.py takes 3 tests red; restored byte-identical, 9 pass. 3. THE CHANGE-POINT p WAS A MAXIMALLY-SELECTED STATISTIC. 17 candidate cuts, the minimising Fisher p reported as a single test. Corrected by the union bound -- Sidak correctly rejected, since nested cuts share data and are not independent: Bonferroni p = 3.738445e-13, permutation p <= 4.9975e-04 over 2000 shuffles, a resolution bound at 1/(B+1) because 0 shuffles reached the observed minimum. THE CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED; the number was overstated by exactly the factor 17. Independently replicated here: 17 cuts confirmed, and a 400-permutation null sweep rejects at 0.05 in 20.2500% (Wilson [16.6034%, 24.4626%]) uncorrected against a nominal 5%, and 0.5000% (Wilson [0.1372%, 1.8045%]) corrected. A seventh-digit discrepancy in the Bonferroni figure resolved in CC2's favour: it computed from full precision, and I had multiplied a rounded display value. 4. "DEAD" OVERSTATES WHAT THE 0.2 DATA SHOW. The most recent attempt of ANY kind, 2026-09-09 09:07:25, SUCCEEDED. The entry quoted the most recent FAILURE at 09:02:48. The post-cut rate is "almost always fails", not "never works", and the defensible claim is availability too low to depend on -- which still satisfies the additive standard's removal clause on the named property. 5. THE ASSUMED_DEFAULT FLAG HAD A THIRD CASE THAT RECORDED 1.0 BESIDE PROSE SAYING 0.5. When a target tokenises to nothing, compute_gamma_input returns early with gamma 1.0 and never reaches the assumed-default branch, so the flag read ASSUMED_DEFAULT while the field held the extreme "maximally simple" value. Reachable: tokenize keeps only [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]* runs longer than 2 characters, so any CJK, RTL, minified or short-identifier target yields 0 tokens. Now 3 states, with the reading interpolating the actual gamma so prose cannot drift from the field again, and the except broadened to Exception because a MemoryError or TypeError would otherwise reach the outer handler -- which returns BEFORE target_hashes is recorded, letting an informative statistic blind the integrity control in a project where 35 of 39 archived runs already carry no target hash. CONFIRMED IN MY FAVOUR, and recorded because a panel that only finds fault is not being read properly: CC2 independently derived that n_windows >= MIN_WINDOWS is the correct key for the fit flag, since _fit_heaps cannot reach its (0,0,0) sentinel at 3 or more windows. And Fable extended the R5a search from 690 to 1,679 definitions -- adding the negation and conjunction families the space could not express, including "escalated AND not resolved", the claim's most natural reading -- and the triple is STILL NONE. Its sharpener: that reading yields exactly 2 for exp47, matching its claimed 2, 1 for exp48 against a claimed 6, and is inexpressible for exp49. Even granted its best reading the claim matches 1 run of 3. 71 tests pass across every file the seats touched. title: Repair the 6 suite failures tonight's work caused, including 2 I introduced myself
verbatim: Repair the 6 suite failures tonight's work caused, including 2 I introduced myself A clean full-suite run against the committed state returned 6 failures. All 6 were caused by this evening's work and all 6 are now green. Each is recorded with its cause rather than just its fix. 1 and 2. THE LEDGER WAS STALE, NOT WRONG. Adding bench/logs/panel_round8_2026-09-10 moved the artefacts the ledger derives from, and the committed copy had not been regenerated. The line citation it carries -- reference_runner_v3.py:14280 -- is DERIVED by _gamma_alt_comment_line(), not typed, so it was already correct; only the committed copy lagged. Regenerated with the command the failure message names. 17 tests pass. 3. I REINTRODUCED THE INLINE Path.home() CALL THAT DESKTOP_MIRROR EXISTS TO PREVENT. Deriving the mirror SET from sync_desktop_mirrors.MIRRORS was right; rebuilding each path with an inline Path.home() / "Desktop" was not. The constant exists precisely so a fixture can displace it -- the comment above it says so -- and test_the_desktop_mirror_is_a_module_constant went red the moment the inline call returned, with the live machine's Desktop leaking into a tmp_path run. Every mirror path now derives from DESKTOP_MIRROR, so there is ONE substitution point, and the tracker keeps using the constant itself rather than a path rebuilt from its parent, because the fixture substitutes it by full path and then asserts that exact path is offered. One fixture moved with it: test_a_diverged_mirror_is_announced_loudly patched Path.home, which only worked while each path was rebuilt inline. Its ASSERTION is untouched -- a diverged copy must be announced -- and only the substitution point changed, to the one the other test demands. The 2 fixtures wanted opposite structures and the module constant is the correct one. 4. THE GATE COST MOVED 178 -> 277, AND THE FIFTH CORRECTION HAS A STRUCTURAL CAUSE THE FIRST 4 LACKED. test_done_markers_carry_evidence parametrises ONE TEST PER DONE ENTRY, so the pre-commit gate's cost is a function of the task list, and this evening closed 12 entries. The figure will go stale every time an entry is closed: it is not a fixed price, and 4 of the 5 corrections were made by readers who assumed it was. Re-measured rather than retyped: 277 tests, median 7.09 s over 5 runs, range 6.39 s to 8.51 s, macOS 26.5.1 arm64, Python 3.13.3. The treadmill is kept deliberately -- the guard going red on each closure is what has kept this number true since 14:20, and a figure nobody is forced to refresh is exactly how the first 3 corrections became possible. 5 and 6. MY OWN ROUND-8 BRIEF BROKE THE DISAGREEMENT GUARD. It matched the literal phrase "strongest disagreement", the wording of the round-4 output shape. My round-8 brief asked for the same field as "WHERE I DISAGREE WITH THE OTHER SEAT OR WITH CC1", both seats supplied it in full, and the guard reported both as misses. A guard keyed to one literal phrase, checking a requirement each brief states in its own words, is the substring-versus-token defect wearing a different hat -- the same shape that has now cost this project 4 separate findings. It matches the CONCEPT now: a section about disagreeing, in any of 4 phrasings. Nothing was loosened to make a test pass. The 2 assertions that changed are the mirror fixture's substitution point and the disagreement detector's breadth, and both changed because the thing being asserted was right and the way of detecting it was wrong. title: 2.2: C0036 and C0054 -- the conflict detector is blind to 95.6120% of the directives
verbatim: 2.2: C0036 and C0054 -- the conflict detector is blind to 95.6120% of the directives One defect, raised twice by DeepSeek in a single exp42 run at severity 0.80 and 0.70. Both recorded UNCONFIRMED, UNTOOLABLE, empty falsifier_code. resolve_layer_conflicts decides which contradictory directives survive composition, and it asks _directive_topic_and_stance what each directive is about. title: 2.2: C0001 -- the coherence pruner makes the metric it optimises worse, provably
verbatim: 2.2: C0001 -- the coherence pruner makes the metric it optimises worse, provably CC2 raised it on 2026-06-06 at severity 0.90, the highest of the 28. Recorded UNCONFIRMED, UNTOOLABLE, empty falsifier_code, and untouched for 96 days. _prune_for_coherence deletes SOFT directive text to bring constraint_density under a budget. Density is _count_constraints(policy) / token_estimate, and the numerator is counted from the TOML policy dict, which pruning cannot touch. So removing text shrinks the denominator and density RISES with every prune. PROVED UNREACHABLE, NOT MERELY OBSERVED. SymPy: d(C/t)/dt = -C/t**2, negative for positive quantities. z3: with C fixed, t1 <= t0 and the entry condition C/t0 > budget, asking whether C/t1 <= budget can hold returns UNSAT. Both early exits in the function are dead code. The graduated pruning design never operates: it always strips everything prunable, then exits worse than it started. THE CONTROL THAT HOLDS THE DIAGNOSIS. The same z3 query with a RECOMPUTED count that may fall returns SAT. So the unreachability is caused specifically by the fixed numerator, not by the shape of the loop -- without that control, "unreachable" would be an observation about this code rather than a diagnosis. DEMONSTRATED ON A REAL COMPOSITION (deepseek_v3, software): 7,090 chars and density 0.011851 before, 3,994 chars and density 0.021042 after -- 1.7756 times worse against a budget of 0.01 -- with every prunable packet exhausted and the domain directive deleted outright. THE HARM, AND MY FIRST FRAMING OF IT WAS WRONG. 10 of the 50 compositions that HAD a domain directive lose it entirely: 20.0000%, Wilson [11.2438%, 33.0371%], Clopper-Pearson [10.0302%, 33.7183%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00. A first pass counted 50 of 90 compositions with no domain packet afterwards and would have reported 55.5556% -- but 40 of those never had one, because no directive file exists for that domain. Absent is not deleted, and the overstatement would have been 2.8-fold. CC2's downstream point, recorded separately because it is a second defect: calibrate_coherence_thresholds observes these densities, so it is calibrating against a curve inverted by construction -- high density correlated with LESS directive text. NOT APPLIED, PARKED, same reason as C0040, C0037 and C0036: the repair changes which packets survive composition, so it changes the prompt every model receives and invalidates replay of archived runs. bench/tests/test_falsifier_C0001_prune_inversion_2026-09-10.py, 6 tests. 9 of 9 UNTOOLABLE findings examined were toolable. 19 remain. title: 2.2: the 8 exp55 control findings are 2 true positives found 4 times each
verbatim: 2.2: the 8 exp55 control findings are 2 true positives found 4 times each Across the 2 exp55_v3_control runs, 3 independent models -- ChatGPT, Codex and CC2 -- each raised the same 2 defects. All 8 records carry the verdict UNTOOLABLE with an empty falsifier_code. They are arithmetic about a 614-byte target in this repository whose filename says it carries exactly 2 planted defects. BOTH FINDINGS ARE TRUE POSITIVES, and this file proves it with SymPy, NumPy, mpmath and pint rather than by agreeing with 3 models. That distinction matters more than usual here: agreement among models is exactly what this project refuses to treat as confirmation, so 4 of them agreeing is a reason to check, not to accept. CT-01 -- RIGHT ANSWER, WRONG RULE. The target satisfies Nyquist, 400 > 2 x 180 = 360, but justifies it "because f_s = 400 Hz exceeds f_max = 180 Hz", and that is not the criterion. The distinction is falsified by counter-example rather than asserted: at f_s = 250 Hz and f_max = 200 Hz the stated reason holds and Nyquist fails. CT-02 -- RIGHT ARITHMETIC, FALSE CONCLUSION. df = f_s/N = 400/256 = 1.5625 Hz is correct, and the buffer therefore CANNOT resolve a 1 Hz separation, which sits below the bin spacing. The test also states what the buffer does resolve, so the finding carries a correction and not only a refusal. BOTH DEFECTS SHARE ONE SHAPE and a test asserts it: in each the number is right and the inference drawn from it is wrong, so a reviewer checking only the arithmetic passes both. That is what makes this target a good control. All 9 live-target falsifiers are now written. 11 remain, all in the exp53 zero-plant runs, where the question is different in kind -- a finding against a target with nothing planted is a candidate false positive. bench/tests/test_falsifier_exp55_control_claims_2026-09-10.py, 11 tests. 17 of 17 UNTOOLABLE findings examined were toolable. title: 2.2 DONE: all 28 missing falsifiers written, and the last 11 ARE the control's measurement
verbatim: 2.2 DONE: all 28 missing falsifiers written, and the last 11 ARE the control's measurement Exp 53 is the zero-plant control and its pre-registration says what these findings are for, verbatim: "FALSE-POSITIVE RATE = findings raised against true claims divided by 44, the only clean estimate available anywhere in the programme". SW-21-REF-04.md carries 44 numbered claims and nothing planted. 11 critical findings were raised against it, every one recorded UNTOOLABLE with an empty falsifier_code. Writing their falsifiers IS that measurement. ALL 11 ARE FALSE POSITIVES, BY ONE MECHANISM REPEATED. Every claim in that document names the scope it is asserted over -- "under single-threaded use", "with non-negative costs", "unit-cost requests" -- and each finding is raised by stepping outside it. The claims are TRUE AS STATED. The code behaviours the findings describe are REAL. Both hold at once and neither cancels the other. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not by reading. ZC-14 survives 120,000 non-negative-cost calls with 0 violations, reproducing the document's own stated evidence, while allow(-5.0) on a drained 1-token bucket does return True and leave tokens at 5.0 -- real, and outside the scope ZC-14 names. C0005 MISQUOTES THE CLAIM IT ATTACKS. It says ZC-20 states the retry schedule "never shortens". ZC-20 says the opposite: "the sampled delays are not ordered, since each is drawn uniformly below its own cap". The phrase does not occur in it. C0003 CONCEDES ITS OWN CASE IN ITS TEXT: "The document itself later states this in ZC-26" -- and ZC-26 does, at length, with its own instrumented demonstration. C0007's bisect_right versus bisect_left point is a real convention observation with no measured effect: the 2 functions disagree on 0 of 262,144 keys, Wilson [0.00000000%, 0.00146538%], and ZC-17's actual claim -- that the subscript stays in range -- holds. RATE: 11 of 44 = 25.0000%, Wilson [14.5742%, 39.4406%], Clopper-Pearson [13.1927%, 40.3380%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00. The first draft of this entry typed intervals that did not match the computation -- Wilson lower 14.5926 against 14.5742, Clopper-Pearson [13.1216, 40.4589] against [13.1927, 40.3380] -- caught before commit by recomputing. Typed figures drifting from their measurement is the defect this entry is about, and it nearly shipped inside it. THIS IS NOT A FINDING THAT THE PANEL PERFORMED BADLY. Every one of the 11 describes real code behaviour and several would be worth fixing in production software. What the control measures is the STOPPING DECISION, and on a document where every claim is true the panel kept producing critical findings by widening the scope of the claims until something failed. TASK 2.2 IS COMPLETE: 28 of 28. And 28 of 28 findings the system had labelled UNTOOLABLE were toolable -- 9 against live targets, 8 against a 2-defect control, 11 against a zero-plant one. The label meant "nobody wrote the tool", never "no tool exists". Among them: a live defect in compose() untouched since June, a severity-0.88 finding about the HARD directive every seat receives, a pruner whose early exits z3 proves are dead code, and a dedup that deleted a general formula and kept its special case. bench/tests/test_falsifier_exp53_zero_plant_2026-09-10.py, 8 tests. title: 2.3 DONE: falsifiers misread rather than missing -- 4 of 583, and the label is the defect
verbatim: 2.3 DONE: falsifiers misread rather than missing -- 4 of 583, and the label is the defect Task 2.2 covered findings with no falsifier. This is the other half: a falsifier that ran, produced a verdict, and had that verdict read as something it is not. THE INVARIANT. falsifier_verdict == "ERROR" means the test did not run to a verdict -- broken import, syntax error, setup guard firing. This project's record is explicit that "an errored leg is an equipment failure, not a verdict", and reference_runner_v3.py tells the model exactly that. So an entry may not carry verified: True on the strength of an ERROR unless some OTHER instrument demonstrated it. MEASURED across every post-mechanism archive: 4 of the 583 findings that carry a falsifier have ERROR + verified: True + no second instrument. 0.6861%, Wilson [0.2671%, 1.7507%], Clopper-Pearson [0.1872%, 1.7473%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00. FOUR THINGS KEEP IT IN PROPORTION, and omitting any would overstate it. 1. All 4 are escalated: True. They went to the human queue. Nothing was silently accepted. 2. Only 1 ever reached CLOSED -- exp42 C0046. The other 3 are OPEN or UNCONFIRMED. 3. For 2 of them the underlying finding is demonstrably TRUE: exp55 C0003 and C0010 are the CT-01 and CT-02 defects proved under 2.2 with SymPy, NumPy, mpmath and pint. Their flag is right in substance and unearned in provenance, which is a different complaint from being wrong. 4. The second instrument works where it exists. exp47 C0055 carries an ERRORed falsifier AND bugzilla_verified: True -- the closed loop applied the fix and re-ran the test. It is correctly closed and is NOT in the population. A first pass of this measurement counted it and would have reported 5; checking for the second instrument is what makes the number a measurement rather than a grep. SO THE DEFECT IS A LABEL, NOT A DECISION. "verified" is supposed to mean an instrument demonstrated the finding. In these 4, nothing did. BUILT AS A RATCHET, NOT A BAR. Archives are the record of what happened and must not be rewritten, so the only useful guard is one that stops the population growing: the 4 are recorded by name with reasons, and anything new fails. TWO ERRORS OF MINE WERE CAUGHT BY THE TEST ITSELF. A run identifier typed instead of read from the measurement, and an assertion searching for "It demonstrated nothing" -- a phrase that WRAPS across a line in the runner's source, so the search failed against text that is present. The grep-the-source trap, committed inside a file about misreading instrument output. bench/tests/test_errored_falsifiers_are_not_read_as_verification_2026-09-10.py, 7 tests. title: I broke a test in another file by setting mpmath's GLOBAL precision
verbatim: I broke a test in another file by setting mpmath's GLOBAL precision The full suite finished 6367 passed, 2 failed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed in 982.41 s. One failure was my own concurrent edit to the task list while the drift guard read it. The other was real and mine. test_sk_break_even_2026-09-06.py::test_closed_form_agrees_with_independent_root_finding failed in the full run and passed in isolation, 5 times out of 5. That signature -- fails together, passes alone -- is cross-test state, and the state was mine. 3 of the test files I wrote tonight set `mp.mp.dps = 30`. That is mpmath's GLOBAL precision and it outlives the test that sets it. `mp.findroot` reads it, and at 30 digits it demands a tolerance the break-even function cannot reach: ValueError: Could not find root within given tolerance. title: 7.1 DONE: every live note now says where its figures come from -- 17 of 33, now 0
verbatim: 7.1 DONE: every live note now says where its figures come from -- 17 of 33, now 0 His ruling: "Fix them all, or at least those that a technical reader would be likely to find insufficient in the interests of reproducibility." THE SCOPE WAS SPLIT AT THE START, not at the debrief, which is this project's own rule. 383 notes exist and most must NOT be touched: a FULL_RECORD of a panel session is a TRANSCRIPT, and rewriting it destroys the record it exists to preserve. The bounded set is DERIVED rather than chosen -- a note is LIVE if a canonical document points a reader at it -- and comes to 118. The other 265 are reported, not repaired, and a test FAILS if a provenance block is ever added to one. INSUFFICIENT MEANS ONE FALSIFIABLE THING: the note states a percentage or a p-value, names no script that exists, and declares no provenance. BEFORE: 17 of the 33 live notes carrying such a figure, 51.5152%, Wilson [35.2184%, 67.4960%], Clopper-Pearson [33.5444%, 69.2037%]. AFTER: 0 of 33, Wilson [0.0000%, 10.4270%]. THE FIGURES WERE NEVER LOST, WHICH IS THE FINDING. 10 of the 17 have surviving archives in bench/logs and simply never named them: the note stated a method in prose and no artefact, so a reader had nothing to run while the data sat in this repository the whole time. That is a citation problem, not an excavation. The other 7 have no artefact and NOW SAY SO, in those words, because inventing a source would be worse than naming its absence. THE LARGEST NOTE'S FIGURES WERE RE-VERIFIED, NOT MERELY SOURCED. scripts/exp36_verification_figures_2026-09-10.py reproduces 3 of 3 headline figures exactly: R8 novelty 72.4138% against a stated 72.4%, early mean rho 39.7652% against 39.8%, late mean rho 20.6563% against 20.7%. ONE FIGURE DOES NOT REPRODUCE, AND IT IS THE P-VALUE. The note reports p = 0.17 under a method described as a "Mann-Whitney U test comparing early and late", which reads two-sided. The two-sided p is 0.3400. 0.17 is the ONE-SIDED (greater) result -- exactly half -- and the sidedness is not declared. Anti-conservative by a factor of 2, the same direction as the maximally-selected p CC2 found tonight. The VERDICT is unaffected: UNCERTAIN at 0.05 either way, and the note now says both things. A LOOSER FIRST MEASUREMENT IS NOT QUOTED. Counting "N of M" as a figure returned 110 of 180 notes, 61.1111%, but most of those matches are ordinary prose -- "1 of 3 rounds", "2 of the 5 seats". A percentage or a p-value is a claim about a measurement in a way that "one of three" is not. ONE MISTAKE, CAUGHT BY THE INSTRUMENT. The repair script matched notes by BASENAME, and experimental_notes holds 4 files called README.md. A provenance block landed on one carrying 0 figures and 3 live scripts, which needed nothing, while the flagged file went untouched. The scan still reporting 1 outstanding is what caught it. Matching a path by its last component is the same shape as matching a token by substring, which has now bitten this project 5 times, and the misplacement is recorded in the file where it belongs. bench/tests/test_live_notes_are_reproducible_2026-09-10.py, 6 tests. title: 8.2: the branch inventory, and the 12 unique paths are 5 exam answer keys
verbatim: 8.2: the branch inventory, and the 12 unique paths are 5 exam answer keys His ruling: "Get Fable and CC2 to look at this with you, decide which elements on this branch remain useful and should be adopted in light of everything else we have done and which should be considered superseded." They are dispatched as round 9. This commit establishes the facts they and he need. THE ENTRY SAID "12 file paths existing nowhere else" AND DID NOT SAY WHAT THEY ARE. They are 5 EXAM ANSWER KEYS -- chemistry, engineering, physics, biology, factorial -- the 6 exam targets they belong to, and 1 note. REACHABILITY IS NOT EXPOSURE, which is the founder's own ruling of 2026-09-07, and the qualifier is load-bearing here. `git ls-remote --heads origin` returns refs/heads/main ALONE: exp39-experimental was never pushed. Each of the 5 keys is reachable from origin/main in 0 commits. Nothing on this branch was published. The branch's own commit eecdb0f is titled "CLOSE THE ANSWER-KEY EXPOSURE" and already names the residual in its message: "git-history recovery by deliberate archaeology". THE TIP TREE DIFFERS FROM MAIN BY EXACTLY 1 PATH: bench/reference_runner_v2.py. That is the file the founder separately asked me to look at, and it is now the central question of the adjudication rather than a footnote. I CREATED A TAG AND THAT NEEDS SAYING PLAINLY. exp39-experimental-pinned-2026-09-10 makes all 107 unreachable commits safe from garbage collection -- and it pins the 5 keys along with them. A tag CREATES a ref and removes nothing, the entry itself recommends pinning before any disposition, and the branch ref already reached those objects, so the tag adds no exposure. But it does make them durable, and the founder should hear that from me rather than find it. DELETING A GIT REF IS ONE OF THE 3 CATEGORIES HE RESERVES TO HIMSELF IN PERSON. Nothing here approaches it. The panel brief forbids it explicitly and says any patch containing `git branch -D`, `git tag -d`, `git push --delete`, `git gc --prune`, `git reflog expire` or filter-repo will be refused whole. THE BRIEF WAS REFUSED TWICE BEFORE DISPATCH by scripts/panel_brief_validate.py -- no requirement that a fix be TESTED, and a declared figure of "12" too short to verify in output. It passes all 7 checks now and the validator re-executed both declared figures against the producing script. ONE LIMIT OF MY OWN MEASUREMENT, DECLARED AND HANDED TO THE PANEL TO BREAK: the comparison walks the last 400 commits of main's history for tractability. A cut-off can manufacture a difference, so the brief asks them to check whether any of the 12 appears earlier than that and to fix the script if so. scripts/exp39_branch_inventory_2026-09-10.py. It decides nothing and deletes nothing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: 8.2: v2 against v3 -- no capability lost by name, 46 implementations differ
verbatim: 8.2: v2 against v3 -- no capability lost by name, 46 implementations differ The founder asked separately and recently: "Look at the v2 runner too." bench/reference_runner_v2.py is the ONLY path on the exp39-experimental tip tree that is not on origin/main, so it is the whole of the tip-level difference and the centre of the adjudication. COMPARED BY AST, because reading 10,221 lines against 15,008 is not a method. Every definition in each file is extracted and compared by name, then by normalised source. NO CAPABILITY IS LOST BY NAME. v3 defines every one of v2's 153 definitions and 48 more: 0 of 153, Wilson [0.0000%, 2.4493%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 2.3730%]. 107 of the 153 shared definitions are byte-identical after normalisation -- 69.9346%, Wilson [62.2536%, 76.6392%]. 46 differ. MY FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS AN ARTEFACT AND IS NOT QUOTED. Comparing v2's UNPARSED lines against v3's RAW source reported 45 functions carrying "lines absent from all of v3". ast.unparse rewrites quote style and spacing, so entry.get('falsifier_code') never matches a source line written with double quotes. Normalising both sides drops it to 37 definitions and 133 lines. That is the same format-versus-token trap this project has now been bitten by 5 times, and it took 1 run to catch because the number looked too large. WHAT THIS SETTLES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It settles that nothing is missing by name. It does NOT settle whether any of the 46 differing implementations is a REGRESSION rather than a revision -- that is per-function judgement, it is the panel's to make, and the script says so rather than implying an answer. scripts/v2_vs_v3_runner_2026-09-10.py. Round 9 is dispatched to cc2 and fable with this as one of its named targets. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: 8.3: the 20 of 21 does not reproduce, and the real figure is 5 of 117
verbatim: 8.3: the 20 of 21 does not reproduce, and the real figure is 5 of 117 "20 of 21 falsifiers reproduce against an earlier stored version" existed only as prose and as a code comment at scripts/adjudicate_by_repair.py:270. The rule covering this names code comments explicitly, so a comment is not an exemption. IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE FROM THE COMMITTED OUTPUT, for a structural reason rather than a lost file. adjudication_by_repair.json records PAIR verdicts -- 133 rows, 7 NO_BASELINE, 15 adjudicated at a non-HEAD version -- while the claim is about FINDINGS. Counted as findings the nearest quantities are 9, 16 and 25, and none is 21. The per-finding search the comment describes was never stored. RE-DERIVING IT WOULD MEAN RE-RUNNING THE ADJUDICATOR, which WRITES TO THE TARGET FILE inside a version loop, restored in a finally. Reconstructing a figure is not worth writing to real targets, so it was not done and the reason is recorded instead of the attempt. WHAT IS REBUILT IS THE QUESTION THE COMMENT ITSELF RESTS ON. `_versions` says "`--all` is load-bearing ... the branch exp39-experimental holds 107 commits main does not". Measured read-only over the 18 in-repo targets of archived runs: 117 stored versions reachable with --all, 7 reachable from no ref on origin/main, and 5 of those supplied by the branch -- _divergence.py, _memory.py, evidence.py and runner_core.py twice. 5 of 117 = 4.2735%, Wilson [1.8390%, 9.6152%], Clopper-Pearson [1.4019%, 9.6914%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00. ATTRIBUTION WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Of the 7 off-main versions, 1 came from local main running ahead of origin/main -- my own composer commit from earlier tonight -- and 1 from the pre-rewrite backup refs. Crediting the branch with all 7 would have overstated it by 40%, and a test holds that distinction. TWO THINGS THE GUARDS CAUGHT IN THIS COMMIT. The entry rewrite left a DUPLICATE marker, the old OPEN one surviving below the new DONE one; the parser takes the first, so the count was right and the file was not. And the DONE marker first named a SCRIPT as its evidence -- test_done_markers_carry_evidence refused it, correctly, because a script in scripts/ is collected by nothing. Evidence must be a test the suite actually runs. bench/tests/test_branch_supplies_versions_2026-09-10.py, 5 tests. Task list: 88 entries, 51 done, 30 open. title: A3 and A9: 6 citations pointed at the wrong place, and 1 removal that must not happen
verbatim: A3 and A9: 6 citations pointed at the wrong place, and 1 removal that must not happen A3. ALL 6 CHECKABLE CITATIONS POINTED OUTSIDE THE SYMBOL THEY NAME. The existing citation guard checks only that the FILE exists. cdsfl_utils.SUPPRESS_LINE says so in as many words: "the FILE exists; line numbers NOT checked". The run ledger self-heals because it has a generator; hand citations do not. Measured after the runner grew by roughly 90 lines this evening: of the 46 citations into bench/reference_runner_v3.py, 6 name a symbol whose span is known and ALL 6 pointed outside it. 100%, Wilson [60.9666%, 100.0000%], Clopper-Pearson [54.0742%, 100.0000%]. The offsets were +17, +19, +59, +424, +1091 and +6837 lines. The last would send a reader to a completely unrelated part of a 15,008-line file. All 6 repaired to their symbol's definition line: check_sk_threshold_corrected twice, run_experiment, check_sk_threshold, _estimate_gamma, and compute_rk_with_eta_channel. THE CHECK IS BY AST SPAN, NOT BY TEXT, and the first version proves why. Looking for the symbol within 5 lines of the citation reported 12 of 12 failures -- several of which were CORRECT citations pointing deep inside a long function body. The strict version would have sent me repairing things that were right. An AST span decides containment exactly, and is not defeated by the name appearing in a comment 400 lines away. WHAT IT CANNOT CHECK IS COUNTED, NOT HIDDEN. 40 of the 46 citations carry no backticked symbol before them, or name something that is not a def or a class. They are reported UNCHECKABLE. Folding them into the pass count would be the "a guard that cannot fail" defect; folding them into the fail count would invent findings. Controls in BOTH directions: a deliberately wrong citation must be caught, and a correct one must not be flagged. A9. WITHDRAWN. THE TASK LIST ASKED FOR A REMOVAL AND THE EVIDENCE SAYS DO NOT. The stray .py under experimental_notes is unextracted_sandbox_2026-08-30/test_repair_loop_wiring_2026-08-30.py, and bench/tests/test_every_test_file_is_collected_2026-09-01.py:36 already carries an explicit exemption for it: "the archived artefact of what a reviewer wrote inside its sandbox on 2026-08-30, kept as a record of the review ... this one stays frozen and still names reference_runner_v2, which is what the file was called when it was written." Removing it would destroy a record of what a reviewer wrote -- the same class of act as rewriting a transcript, which task 7.1 refused in the opposite direction earlier the same day. And there is no live problem. The integrated copy at bench/tests/test_repair_loop_wiring_2026-08-30.py carries the same 8 tests with 1 renamed, is a superset at 159 lines against 142, and passes 8 of 8. The frozen draft errors on collection only if pytest is pointed at experimental_notes, which the suite never does: pytest bench/tests/ collects 6471 tests and not that file. The draft asserts module aliases which, as the integrated file's own docstring records, "neither exists and neither ever did in this tree". bench/tests/test_citation_content_2026-09-10.py, 5 tests. title: A10: no harness parks a mutant in git, and now none can
verbatim: A10: no harness parks a mutant in git, and now none can A harness that holds the pristine file in `git stash` and restores it with a later `pop` depends on that pop running, and nothing enforces it. An exception, a timeout, a killed process, or a second harness stashing on top leaves the mutant in the working tree and the original somewhere nobody will look -- and the next `git status` reads as though the mutation were intended work. A `finally` runs on the exception path; a `pop` on a later line does not. MEASURED BEFORE WRITING THE GUARD: no file in scripts/ or bench/tests/ calls `git stash` at all. The single textual match, scripts/cdsfl_sv.py:2247, is a COMMENT about agents editing the tracker. So this is a ratchet against the pattern returning, not a repair of a live instance, and the entry's "I18 is the live instance" no longer holds. IT MATCHES A CALL, NOT THE WORD. A subprocess argument list or shell string naming git and the subcommand, inside a file that also writes to a source path. A grep for "stash" would fire on that comment, on the guard's own docstring, and on any note quoted in a test. IT WAS TOO BROAD ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT AND THE NARROWING IS RECORDED. Matching checkout, reset, revert and restore as well flagged scripts/cdsfl_sv.py:895 and 5 sites in bench/tests/test_sv_sync_verification_2026-08-26.py -- every one legitimate sync and branch tooling, none a mutation harness. "A guard that fires on the ordinary case teaches people to ignore it" is this project's own recorded reason for keeping the commit hook cheap, and it applies here. `stash` is the shape the entry names: it defers a restoration to a step that may never run, which checkout and reset do not. A test now asserts those legitimate sites stay unflagged, so the guard cannot be quietly widened back. THREE CONTROLS, because a guard with nothing to catch passes on an empty codebase: a synthetic stashing harness must be caught, the safe in-memory-and-finally pattern must not be, and a read-only `git log` must not be. bench/tests/test_mutation_harness_touches_no_git_state_2026-09-10.py, 6 tests. title: 8.2 DONE: the branch is adjudicated, nothing is adopted, and no ref was touched
verbatim: 8.2 DONE: the branch is adjudicated, nothing is adopted, and no ref was touched His ruling: "Get Fable and CC2 to look at this with you, decide which elements on this branch remain useful and should be adopted." Panel round 9, PANEL_ONLY= cc2,fable, 0 paid dispatch. Both seats responded. THE 2 SEATS DISAGREE AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS KEPT. fable: SUPERSEDED -- nothing should come to main. cc2: SPLIT -- same call on adoption, but it argues reference_runner_v2.py earns retention as the ACCEPTANCE GATE'S OWN CONTROL: reference_runner_v3.py:63 records v3 as v2 plus 10 patches, each accepted on "FAIL at the parent, PASS with the patch", and the parent IS v2, so losing it makes the fail-at-parent leg of all 10 acceptances unreproducible. Both converge on: do not adopt, keep the pin. V2 IS SUPERSEDED AS RUNNING CODE, PROVEN BY EXECUTION. v3 is v2 renamed at ce08914 and continued for 82 commits; 0 of v2's 153 definitions are missing and 0 CLI flags lost. Head-to-head on compute_rk with sk=nan: v2 returns 0.3667, scoring a NaN as a PERFECT fix through a min(1.0, nan) trap, while v3 returns 0.62 and fails safe. The only direction of difference found is v3 strictly safer. THE KEYS: 5, BRANCH-ONLY, VERIFIED AT BLOB LEVEL. All 17 distinct key-blob OIDs were hunted with git log --all --reflog --find-object; every containing commit is an ancestor of the branch. Stashes, git notes and 311 unreachable objects from fsck carry none. bench/vault_keys.sh status reports VAULTED, no plaintext on disk. The exposure surface is exactly {branch, pin tag}, both local. MY REACHABILITY CLAIM WAS TRUE BUT UNDER-SCOPED as an exposure statement: it did not cover stash, reflogs, refs/original/* -- which exists in this repo -- or dangling objects. fable checked all of them and the claim survived. MY KEY MATCHER WAS UNSOUND, AND ITS OWN PREDICTED DOWNGRADE APPLIES. KEY_MARKER = "answer_key" is blind to ft-NNN_KEY.json, *_KEY.md and *GROUND_TRUTH.json, and this IDENTICAL blindness was diagnosed and fixed 4 days earlier in test_vault_status_sees_the_real_keys_2026-09-06.py, where the narrow pattern matched 0 of 29 real keys. I repeated a defect the record already held. Re-measured with the full vault glob set over the FULL 1021-commit history rather than my 400-commit window: 5 branch-only key paths, all *answer_key*.json. My marker found all 5 and missed 0. Unsound, and not yet wrong. THE WIDENED MATCHER REDISCOVERED A KNOWN EXPOSURE, NOT A NEW ONE. control_two_distinct_defects_GROUND_TRUTH.json is in origin/main's history from bd9c569, 2026-08-20 -- recorded on 2026-08-26, three days before exp55 ran, with the standing ruling that that target is SPENT. Not on the tip; removed by 20d2ccf. Nothing new is exposed by this work. A DESIGN DEFECT IN MY OWN BRIEF, and cc2 is right about it. Neither seat could re-run either declared figure: both need a git repository and the panel sandbox has none, so the script correctly exits 4. "A figure only one party can compute is a vote, not a tool result." That is this project's founding standard and this round did not meet it for those 2 figures. Panel briefs carrying git-dependent figures need either a sandbox with history or figures computable without it. fable's non-repo finding has the same root: my script printed "no branch in this clone -- nothing to measure" and exited 0 in the sandbox. A false clean, which fired during the panel itself. It now refuses with exit 4 and says nothing was measured. Both seats' repairs applied and verified by execution: 13 tests pass. NO REF WAS CREATED, DELETED, PUSHED OR RENAMED by either seat. The pin tag exp39-experimental-pinned-2026-09-10 stands, and both seats endorse keeping it. Task list: 88 entries, 54 done, 26 open. title: 9.1 and 9.4: "reported on 0 of 6" was a fact about the REPORT, not about the run
verbatim: 9.1 and 9.4: "reported on 0 of 6" was a fact about the REPORT, not about the run His 2026-09-06 rulings scheduled 6 items for a run to report on. Measured against the most recent archived report: 1 of the 6 has any field at all (post_convergence_sweep) and 5 have none. The report had nowhere to put the answers, so no run could have reported them however well it went. study_programme_report() now emits all 6 at the end of every run. IT EMITS STATE AND DECIDES NOTHING -- no gate reads it, no status turns on it, no prompt changes -- so unlike the 4 parked composer findings it does not invalidate replay of archived runs. 4 ARE ANSWERED FROM THE RUN. The critical-severity ceiling, with threshold, max observed and the count at or above 1.0. Why the sweep cannot clear a critical: it only re-examines NON-terminal entries and CONFIRMED is terminal to it, so it was never able to -- the answer is a property of the design, not a failure. Falsifier ERROR causes, tallied, with the honest note that the cause is recorded only as routed-or-not because the runner discards the interpreter's own message. And the corrected S* count, still SHADOW pending a founder ruling. 2 ARE UNANSWERABLE AND SAY SO WITH THE REASON, because a blank is indistinguishable from a question nobody asked. The cross-architecture correlation is task 9.4's precondition: every seat in the last run resolved to one model wearing several labels, so there are no distinct architectures to correlate. The reach question rests on the fable/cc2 split, preserved rather than smoothed. 9.4 IS DONE AS FAR AS IT CAN GO WITHOUT HIM. Fixing the precondition needs genuinely distinct architectures, which means paid dispatch -- his category. What is built is the DETECTION: the item counts distinct source_model values and refuses when there is only 1, so a future run cannot report a cross-architecture correlation it did not have the architectures to measure. A control feeds 3 distinct models and requires the item to become answerable, so the refusal is conditional rather than hardcoded. WRAPPED SO IT CANNOT BREAK A RUN, with a LOUD failure branch: an absent block would read as "nothing to report", which is the failure mode this project has now named 5 times. A test asserts both the guard and the failure branch, and a deliberately broken registry must still return all 6 items. bench/tests/test_study_programme_is_reported_2026-09-10.py, 12 tests. verbatim: 9.2 DONE: every fix is in the programme, and the sweep found 2 defects of mine "Add every fix in this list to the study programme, and measure how each performs."
