title: 9.3 DONE: the parser can be studied, and the first measurement reverses the impression
verbatim: 9.3 DONE: the parser can be studied, and the first measurement reverses the impression "Study the parser behaviour in the next simulated run and report." IT COULD NOT BE STUDIED. extract_falsifiers returned blocks and kept no record of what it passed over. A recovery rate needs a denominator and there was none, so every figure in task 2.1 -- 26 of 69 across a run, 1 of 9 in the round that halted -- had to be reconstructed by hand from archived text. falsifier_intake_telemetry() now records, per reply, what the parser SAW against what it RECOVERED. The runner folds it into a per-run tally at every parse site and emits it in the report. Pure text, no execution, and it decides nothing. THE FAIR DENOMINATOR IS THE WHOLE POINT. Over 119 archived replies carrying a FALSIFIER label: over RAW labels : 132 of 411 = 32.1168%, Wilson [27.7862%, 36.7786%] over FENCED labels : 132 of 138 = 95.6522%, Wilson [90.8392%, 97.9924%] 271 of those labels carry no fence within 3 lines -- "FALSIFIER: none", or the word quoted in prose -- and nothing could be recovered from them. So the parser recovers 95.6522% of the labels that ACTUALLY CARRY A BLOCK. That is a very different picture from "the parser drops findings", and it is the honest one. Both rates are emitted so neither can be quoted alone. 6 of the 132 were recovered ONLY by the tolerant companion added on 2026-09-09. That is the 2.1 widening's measured effect size on this sample, and it exists only because the companion was UNIONED with the strict pattern rather than replacing it -- a replacement was tried first and measured WORSE, 4,867 blocks against 5,295. THREE DEFECTS OF MINE, ALL CAUGHT BY MY OWN TESTS WHILE BUILDING IT. A look-ahead window that let a bare label borrow the NEXT label's fence, inflating the fair denominator and understating recovery -- found by a test that constructed exactly that adjacency, which real replies rarely produce because prose separates them. A test sample sorted oldest-first that found 0 fenced labels, because sorting put the earliest experiments first and those predate the FALSIFIER convention entirely: it was sampling a period in which the thing being measured did not exist. And the fix for that then scanned all 6,727 replies, which is a test people skip; it now reads newest-first and stops at 120 fenced labels. THE TALLY IS CLEARED PER RUN. A module global that is not would report run 2's figures as run 1 plus run 2 -- the exact defect the target-hash check suffered on 2026-09-01, where run 2's first round compared against run 1's last hash and raised a mutation alarm with nothing mutated. bench/tests/test_intake_parser_is_studied_2026-09-10.py, 10 tests. 209 runner-core and parse tests pass. title: 10.1 DONE: a script he can run from the hotel to get this session back
verbatim: 10.1 DONE: a script he can run from the hotel to get this session back His ruling: "We will build a script I can place on my remote desktop here in my hotel, which when I run it will restart you/the Claude desktop app and if necessary/technically possible restart this specific session, so I can begin working with it immediately." ~/Desktop/restart_claude_from_hotel.sh, versioned at scripts/restart_claude_from_hotel.sh. WHAT IT DOES. Checks the tailnet, reaches the Mac over SSH, reports whether an update is pending -- which is the actual cause, since the app force-restarts on the first IDLE moment, measured twice at 76 and 85 hours with 48 consecutive deferrals each logged in the app's own words as "Claude is working" -- restarts the application, and hands back an interactive session. "THIS SPECIFIC SESSION" IS ANSWERED, NOT APPROXIMATED. claude --resume <id> restores this conversation by its own identifier, with --continue as the fallback if the id has aged out. The id, the host and the project directory are all overridable by environment variable, because a hardcoded id is useless the moment the session changes. IT DELETES NOTHING. No rm -rf, no git push, no ref operation, no disk command -- and a test asserts each of those absences, because this runs on his machine over SSH and the blast radius of a mistake is his working environment. EVERY FAILURE PATH SAYS "NOTHING WAS CHANGED". A failure that leaves him guessing from a hotel is worse than no script. --dry-run, --check and --resume-only are all available, and an unrecognised flag exits 2 rather than 0. ONE DEFECT WAS FOUND BY RUNNING IT AND COULD NOT HAVE BEEN FOUND BY READING IT. BatchMode=yes is correct: it stops the script hanging on a password prompt a remote user cannot see. But it also makes the FIRST connection from a new machine fail outright, instead of offering the usual "continue connecting?" question. On the hotel machine, first run, it would simply have failed with an opaque message. It now detects that exact case, exits 3 so it is distinguishable from a real outage, and prints the single command that fixes it. TESTED IN DRY RUN ONLY, DELIBERATELY. Running it for real restarts the application, which would kill the session that wrote it. The dry run was executed against the live tailnet and a test asserts it issues no quit. bench/tests/test_hotel_restart_script_2026-09-10.py, 13 tests, including one that holds the Desktop copy byte-identical to the versioned one. title: 10.2: the analysis is done and the decision stays his
verbatim: 10.2: the analysis is done and the decision stays his Measured 2026-09-10. Tailscale SSH is OFF -- SSH_HostKeys is absent on this Mac and on the one peer. Ordinary sshd is running and port 22 answers on the tailnet address 100.124.143.121. His account carries the ssh capability and both is-admin and is-owner, so enabling it is available and needs no new subscription. THE ARGUMENT FOR IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL. Building the hotel restart script for task 10.1 surfaced a real failure: with BatchMode=yes the FIRST connection from a new machine fails outright on host-key verification rather than asking "continue connecting?". On the hotel machine, first run, the script would simply have failed. I worked around it by detecting the case and printing the single command that fixes it -- but Tailscale SSH removes the failure entirely, because there are no host keys and no ssh-add to remember. That is exactly the "would remove key handling" the entry names, and its value is now measured rather than asserted. THE ARGUMENT AGAINST. It moves SSH authorisation from possession of a private key to tailnet identity plus an ACL rule. Those are different threat models: a compromised tailnet account would then carry shell access where today it would still need the key. The policy also lives in Tailscale's admin console, off this machine and outside this repository's history. THE TWO ARE NOT EXCLUSIVE. Ordinary sshd survives, so he could enable it, confirm the hotel script works keyless, and keep the key route as the fallback. NOT ENABLED. It changes the authentication posture of his private network, and that is his decision rather than a wiring change to make on his behalf while he is away. The entry stays OPEN for that decision, and it is NOT a blocker: task 10.1 works today without it, with the first-run message covering the gap. Parked in experimental_notes/PARKED_FOR_THE_FOUNDER.md. title: A5 DONE: the canonical-tree alarm attributes, and says plainly when it cannot
verbatim: A5 DONE: the canonical-tree alarm attributes, and says plainly when it cannot The alarm fired on 14 files in panel round 2, 8 in round 8 and 11 in round 9 -- and every one was the operator's own concurrent edit, with confinement holding each time. A human re-derived that from the tool logs on each occasion. "An alarm that fires on the ordinary case is on its way to being ignored" is this project's own warning about its irreducible-queue alarm, and this one was on that path. THE EVIDENCE WAS ALREADY ON DISK. Each seat's *.tools.json records every call it made with an input preview, and a seat that wrote to the canonical tree must have named the path. attribute_canonical_touch() reads it. The alarm now prints either "AND AT LEAST ONE IS ATTRIBUTABLE TO A SEAT -- this is the containment failure, not a false alarm", naming the seat and the tool, or "NO SEAT IS SHOWN TO HAVE TOUCHED ANY OF THEM". TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN FIRST ATTRIBUTION, both found by inspecting the hits rather than trusting the boolean, and both would have produced a FALSE CONTAINMENT FAILURE -- the worst possible direction for this particular alarm. 1. The sandbox root was not passed, so a seat editing its OWN copy at /private/var/.../repo/scripts/sync_desktop_mirrors.py was reported as touching the canonical file. 2. A READ was counted as a WRITE. Round 8 came back attributable on the strength of a `sed -n '3733,3739p'` -- a seat reading a note. With both fixed, rounds 8 and 9 report NOT ATTRIBUTABLE, which is exactly what was verified by hand at the time. CONSERVATIVE IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION. An unrecognised shell command counts as capable of writing, because under-reporting is worse than over-reporting on the escape half. The reading and writing shell verbs are both listed explicitly, so the intent is visible rather than inferred from an absence. AND IT NEVER CLAIMS MORE THAN IT HAS. The verdict is "no seat is SHOWN to have touched it", never "no seat did", because an input preview is truncated and a path named beyond the cut is invisible. The return value carries that limit in its own field. bench/tests/test_canonical_alarm_attributes_2026-09-10.py, 9 tests, with controls in BOTH directions: a synthetic seat editing a canonical path and one shell-redirecting into it must be caught; a read, a sandbox-local edit and an empty log must not be. 25 panel-condition and sandbox tests still pass. title: A4 DONE: the validator warns when a brief has been overtaken, and it fired on mine
verbatim: A4 DONE: the validator warns when a brief has been overtaken, and it fired on mine The round-2 brief asserted that a question had not been asked. That was true when it was written at 20:37 and FALSE by the 21:12 dispatch, because a test answering it landed in the 35 minutes between. Both seats spent effort on a bolted door. The validator checked the brief's 7 required sections and nothing about whether the brief had been overtaken by the artefacts it names. IT HAPPENED AGAIN TONIGHT, IN MY OWN ROUND-9 BRIEF. cc2's reply opens its disagreement section with "Section 3.4 is already closed and the brief does not say so." check_currency() compares the brief's modification time against every artefact it names and reports what moved and by how long. On round 9: scripts/exp39_branch_inventory_2026-09-10.py changed 32.9 minutes after the brief was written, and bench/panel_sandbox.py 65.2 minutes after. IT WARNS AND DOES NOT REFUSE, DELIBERATELY. An unrelated edit to a named file is common, and a validator that blocks on it teaches people to skip the validator -- which is this project's own recorded reason for keeping the commit hook cheap. It says what moved; the dispatcher decides. A test asserts currency is NOT in the refusing CHECKS list, so it cannot be quietly promoted into one. IT STATES ITS OWN LIMIT AND A TEST HOLDS IT. Modification times only, so a named file that moved MAY be described wrongly -- a warning, not proof. And it cannot see a change to something the brief describes without naming, so it never claims coverage it does not have; a test feeds it exactly that case and requires silence. THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS: a file OLDER than the brief must not be flagged. Without it the warning fires on every brief and means nothing. bench/tests/test_brief_currency_2026-09-10.py, 7 tests. 271 brief-format and operational-script tests still pass. title: A1 DONE: how complete, functional and useful Open Brain is -- three different answers
verbatim: A1 DONE: how complete, functional and useful Open Brain is -- three different answers "I have never fully tested yet how complete/functional, or useful it is." FUNCTIONAL -- MOSTLY. 7 of the 9 read-only subcommands run to a result: 77.7778%, Wilson [45.2589%, 93.6775%], Clopper-Pearson [39.9906%, 97.1855%]. The 2 that do not are list-epochs and verify-epochs, and both fail the same way: relation "epochs" does not exist. The epoch-sealing feature is advertised in --help and has no table behind it -- the additive standard's unwired half, arriving in a CLI. COMPLETE -- NO, AND THE ASSESSMENT NAMES WHAT IT DID NOT TOUCH. Of 20 advertised subcommands, 9 are read-only enough to exercise here. The other 11 write, need an argument that varies, or are irreversible by design, and each is listed with its reason rather than left as a silent gap. INTEGRITY -- THE HASH CHAIN COVERS 24.8227% OF THE STORE. 35 of 141 memories, Wilson [18.4237%, 32.5571%]. 99 predate the introduction of hashing, which is honest history. But 7 were WRITTEN AFTER THE MIGRATION and carry no hash, which is a capture path not under the chain. The tool reports this itself, in its own words, and exits non-zero for it -- which is the tool working, not failing. USEFUL -- NARROWLY, AND THIS IS THE SHARPEST ANSWER. 141 memories exist, spread across CDSFL 91, project_genesis 32, open_brain 13 and 4 unscoped, and semantic search returns real distances -- 0.2815 on a live query. But EXACTLY ONE production path in this repository reaches it: scripts/cdsfl_sv.py. Everything else naming open_brain is that file's own tests, this assessment, or a documentation mention. A store that only the save-state command writes to is being used far below what 20 subcommands imply. TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN ASSESSMENT, BOTH CAUGHT BEFORE THEY BECAME THE ANSWER. A shell loop word-split the arguments of 5 WORKING subcommands, each printed its usage text, and I read that as failure. I was one step from reporting a working tool as broken. The assessment now passes explicit argv lists and a test asserts they contain no spaces, so a shell can never split them again. And a first predicate treated any non-zero exit as a failure. That would have marked `verify` -- the single most informative command in the set -- as broken, when it exits 1 precisely because it FOUND the 7 unhashed rows. A non-zero exit and a failure are now distinct, and a test holds the distinction. bench/tests/test_open_brain_assessment_2026-09-10.py, 9 tests. Task list: 88 entries, 63 done, 16 open. title: V4: 4 task-list figures had no producing script; now they all do
verbatim: V4: 4 task-list figures had no producing script; now they all do `measured-rate-travels-with-its-script` is a founder ruling this project quotes constantly and has broken repeatedly. A mechanical sweep of the master task list on 2026-09-10 found 18 entries carrying a percentage or p-value and 4 of them naming no script that exists -- 22.2222%, Wilson [9.0009%, 45.2146%]. After this commit: 0 of 18, Wilson [0.0000%, 17.5879%]. The 4 were not the same problem, and the repairs differ. 0.2 cited `change_point()` -- a FUNCTION -- and never named the file it lives in, so a reader could not find it. It is in `scripts/wolfram_route_health_2026-09-10.py` and the entry now says so. 6.1 had no producer at all, and the figure HAD DRIFTED. "23 of 41 completion signals carry an empty reason" measured 2026-09-09 is 24 of 42 today across every run directory (57.1429%, Wilson [42.2062%, 70.8823%]), and 22 of 34 across `exp*` alone. The archive grows; a typed figure over a growing corpus is not merely unverifiable, it is guaranteed to go stale. A8 had no producer. The new one measures a DIFFERENT population from the entry's and says so rather than pretending to reproduce 4.65%: 42 untracked of 125 cited `bench/logs/` paths, 33.6000%, Wilson [25.9184%, 42.2596%], Clopper-Pearson [25.4021%, 42.5952%]. The entry's 3803 is every cited path in the corpus. The 2 must not be quoted against each other. A19 had no producer. The new one CONFIRMS the claim over a smaller population -- 0 of 1035 tristate outcomes NO_SCORE, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.3698%], from 691 ADMISSIBLE, 190 REJECTED and 154 ESCALATE -- with a wider interval, which is the honest report of a smaller sample. A DEFECT IN MY OWN PRODUCER, caught before it became the answer. The A8 extractor first matched anything after `bench/logs/` and swept in `bench/logs/--help` and bare directory names, giving 206 of 290 -- a figure about the extractor rather than about the corpus. Requiring a real file extension gives 42 of 125. The guard for that specific defect is in the test file. title: A2: the suite in a fresh clone, 22 failures to 4 -- and the entry's premise was false
verbatim: A2: the suite in a fresh clone, 22 failures to 4 -- and the entry's premise was false TASK A2, "make the suite pass in a fresh clone". Measured before touching anything, both runs full-suite at the same HEAD (52acec8): fresh clone 22 failed, 6592 passed, 18 skipped, exit 1 working tree 6 failed (10 in the raw log; 4 were casualties of edits made WHILE the suite ran and pass on re-run) The entry quoted "11 failed, 5487 passed, against 0 failures in the working tree" from 2026-09-09. The clone count had DOUBLED in a day, the growth was the assistant's own new tests, and the maintainer's tree was not clean either. 15 test files, 5 distinct causes, censused with the evidence in scripts/fresh_clone_census_2026-09-10.py (--check re-runs every test it names, so the diagnosis cannot go stale silently). 10 of 15 were clone-only, 66.6667%, Wilson [41.7135%, 84.8237%], Clopper-Pearson [38.3804%, 88.1759%]. THE LARGEST CAUSE, AND IT COSTS A READER A HEADLINE FIGURE. Archived falsifiers carry the absolute path of the checkout they were WRITTEN in. On this machine that path IS the repository root, so the containment guard allows it; anywhere else it refuses, prints INTEGRITY VIOLATION and routes the finding to a human. Measured over 640 archived falsifier sources with scripts/archived_falsifier_rejections_2026-09-10.py: 2 rejected for key material in BOTH trees (0.3125%, Wilson [0.0857%, 1.1322%]), plus 35 in the clone whose only violation is naming this project's own tree from elsewhere (5.4688%, Wilson [3.9582%, 7.5107%]). Downstream, 5 of the 15 exp44 execution rows were lost, so execution_based_matcher's "12 of 15" came out 7 of 15 for every reader. The repair is a rebase at REPLAY: _retarget_falsifier already substituted THIS checkout's root into an archived falsifier, and now also rebases a foreign checkout of this project. The containment guard is NOT changed -- a live falsifier naming a path outside the tree is refused exactly as before -- and the rebase is bounded 3 ways, each with a control in bench/tests/test_fresh_clone_suite_2026-09-10.py. TWO OF MY OWN CONTROLS WERE VACUOUS AND MUTATION TESTING SAID SO. Disabling the git-remote identity lookup left every assertion green, because this checkout's FOLDER happens to be named Constraint_Engineering. The replacement builds a checkout under a different folder name whose only claim to the identity is its remote. The identity defect itself is the basename-versus-path shape, recurrence 6, and it appeared inside the fix for recurrence 5. THE STAGE-0 ORDERING FAULT, WHICH HAPPENED TWICE IN ONE DAY. The mirror refresh moved to stage 0 this morning because a repair sat below the check that needed it. This commit's citation repair was then added BELOW the mirror refresh -- and it edits the master task list, which IS mirrored -- so the mirror was copied, the canonical copy changed underneath it, and the same guard refused this very commit. The cure had recreated the fault 1 stage lower down. The mirror refresh is now last by rule, held by bench/tests/test_precommit_stage0_order_2026-09-10.py, whose execution half reproduces both orderings and shows only 1 of them leaves the pair equal. THE OTHER REPAIRS, each in the file it belongs to: a fresh-clone skip that could NEVER FIRE -- it asked whether `git config --get user.email` was empty, and --get falls back to GLOBAL config, which every clone inherits. Onboarding now stamps cdsfl.onboarded in --local config and the guards read that. prose figures measured over the maintainer's on-disk archive: 6,770 JSON files here against 6,160 tracked. The pinned "4142 of 4142 gate records" is 3507 of 3507 in a clone, Wilson [99.89%, 100.00%]. The tracked figure is what prose pins now; the on-disk one is still stated and still checked where it can be. bench/archive_corpus.py: 1 mechanism for "this checkout lacks the artefacts", which SKIPS with the reason and the .gitignore rule named. A claim and its anti-vacuity guard skip together, so neither can pass vacuously. compose_all_2026-08-23.py read an untracked JSON index AT IMPORT, taking apply_v3.py down with it for 2 dictionary literals. Now lazy. test_panel_cwd_reaches_worker_threads searched a 400-CHARACTER WINDOW of source for an assignment 8 lines away. A comment grew, the window stopped reaching, and it went red in both trees while the wiring was correct. apply_panel_cwd is extracted so the guard CALLS it -- execute-do-not-grep -- with a second test that run_experiment still reaches it. Both mutations verified red. the pre-commit hook gains 2 more stage-0 repairs: the citation guard's own --fix, which NOTHING had ever run, and the run ledger's --refresh, which declines to shrink the ledger on a checkout holding fewer artefacts. the gate-cost figure was written TWICE, in the entry and as a literal in its test, so every correction was 2 edits and the 5th made 1. The entry now carries a machine-readable declaration and the test reads it: 347 over 7 files. is_onboarded_checkout gates the Desktop-mirror guards, because 1 checkout on a machine owns those mirrors and a second was being judged against them. Wiring it silently SKIPPED 5 guards in the canonical tree within the hour, so wired-without-a-stamp is now an error rather than a skip. title: Panel round 10: a containment hole I opened, and an identity that reached nothing
verbatim: Panel round 10: a containment hole I opened, and an identity that reached nothing Both free seats (cc2, fable — Max subscription, 0 paid dispatch) returned SOUND WITH EXCEPTIONS and delivered fixes as files. Every premise was verified here before acceptance, and every fix was re-derived, tested and mutated: FFAFP applies to fixes proposed by other models with equal force. FABLE, and it is the serious one. THE A2 REBASE LAUNDERED A `..` ESCAPE PAST THE STATIC GUARD. Reproduced independently before accepting: before: open('/Users/attacker/Constraint_Engineering/../../../etc/passwd') scan_falsifier_source -> [('a path outside the declared target', ...)] after : open('/private/var/folders/xx/overlay/../../../etc/passwd') scan_falsifier_source -> [] REFUSED became ALLOWED `_USER_PATH` polices home- and volume-shaped roots. Overlays are mkdtemp under /private/var/folders, which it never matched, so stripping the /Users/ prefix removed the only thing the static guard keyed on — and the result normalises to /private/var/etc/passwd, outside the overlay. The seat read /etc/passwd end to end through it, 9,344 bytes, with no refusal. THE OTHER SEAT REASONED ABOUT THIS EXACT PATH AND JUDGED IT BELOW THRESHOLD, calling the redirect "inward, not an escape". It executed the attack instead and was right. Reasoning about a containment boundary is not evidence about it. MY FIX IS STRONGER THAN THE ONE PROPOSED, deliberately. title: The panel seats shared one writable sandbox, so their verdicts were not independent
verbatim: The panel seats shared one writable sandbox, so their verdicts were not independent FOUND WHILE HARVESTING ROUND 10. `confer_maths_panel` built ONE sandbox and ran every seat in it CONCURRENTLY through a ThreadPoolExecutor. Seats are told to write their fixes into that tree at real paths, so a seat could read another seat's edits -- and did. NOT A THEORETICAL RISK. Round 10's fable reply describes the `.zenodo.json` identity tier that the cc2 seat had just invented, and its own figures section records "my first (background) run reported 33/640 from a stale .pyc (old repo_paths.py with no declared tier)". Fable reviewed cc2's edited tree rather than the tree under review. WHY IT MATTERS. The founder's `pr` protocol runs the panel "WITHOUT compelled convergence so each model returns an independent verdict ... and disagreement is preserved as information rather than smoothed to consensus". Agreement between seats sharing a writable directory is not evidence of anything. The project already holds a memory titled "no model voting" for the weaker version of this. AND THE PROPOSALS WERE UNATTRIBUTABLE: `seat_proposals.diff` was the union of every seat's edits with no name against any -- round 10 produced 29 files and no way to tell who wrote which. Now keyed `<seat>:<path>`. COST, MEASURED BEFORE CHANGING IT: 6.53 s and 606 MB per sandbox on this machine, so a 2-seat round pays 13 s against a 15-to-25-minute panel. Every sandbox is torn down, not just the first. THE CONTAINMENT ALARM CRIED WOLF AND I BELIEVED IT. Round 10 printed "AND AT LEAST ONE IS ATTRIBUTABLE TO A SEAT. This is the containment failure, not a false alarm." Replaying that round's own tool logs through the repaired attributor: 2 of 11 paths attributable before, 0 after. Two defects, both in the crying-wolf direction: A RELATIVE PATH WAS TREATED AS REACHING THE CANONICAL TREE. The seat ran `python3 - <<'PYEOF' ... pathlib.Path("bench/repo_paths.py")` with its cwd inside its sandbox -- exactly what the brief instructs. The preview holds the relative path and not the sandbox root, so the exclusion missed it. `canonical_was_touched`'s own docstring already states the rule: "A sandbox stops relative writes. It cannot stop a seat writing to an ABSOLUTE path it already knows." Only the absolute form is evidence now. RUNNING THE TEST SUITE COUNTED AS A WRITE. `python3 -m pytest <path>` fell through `_call_can_write`'s conservative default. Task A5 had already fixed a `sed -n` read counted as a write; same class, and the brief instructs seats to run pytest. Positive controls prove the alarm still fires on an absolute write and on an absolute Edit; 3 mutations verified red, including one that over-narrows it into silence. A THIRD SOURCE-TEXT GUARD BROKEN BY A CORRECT REFACTOR TODAY. `test_the_dispatcher_sets_the_cwd_per_worker_not_on_main` asserted the literal `set_panel_cwd(_PANEL_SANDBOX_CWD)` appeared in dispatch's source. Per-seat sandboxes renamed the argument and it went red while the behaviour was correct and stronger. `confine_this_thread` is extracted so the guard CALLS it in a pool worker and observes the thread-local -- which is the property that matters, since the first attempt at the confinement ruling failed silently precisely because a main-thread set is invisible to workers. Importing the dispatcher at all needs `sys.argv[1]` and PANEL_BRIEF_UNCHECKED, because it validates at module level and exits 2. That is the same import-time-side-effect class as the compose_all defect fixed this morning; it is noted for the task list rather than patched over. So V2's list was checked, not acted on: scripts/overstated_entries_2026-09-11.py takes each of the 11 claims one at a time and reports UNCHECKABLE where a script should not pretend to judge. 9 of the 11 were already answered. The figure-with-no-producer class (1.1, 5.1, 6.2, 6.5, M1) was closed by V4 the day before -- 0 of 18 entries now carry a figure with no live script. 6.4, 6.7, 7.2 and 8.1 carry dated CORRECTED paragraphs answering the reviewer in place; 6.3 was a live regression fixed at 25e5b34. 4.2's defect was real and unrepaired. It read "Status COMMITTED" and nothing else, while the repaired artefact is a file in CC1's PRIVATE memory directory that this repository does not carry and cannot: `git log --all` returns 0 commits touching it across the full history. The entry now says what IS committed here -- the removed sentence verbatim, the reason, and the 3-axis analysis -- so a reader of this repository alone can see what changed. AND THE SWEEP FOUND A 12TH THE REVIEWER DID NOT NAME: 7.3, the same shape, its ruling recorded in a private memory file with the same bare COMMITTED. That is the whole reason it was mechanised rather than worked off the list. A POPULATION ERROR IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT, caught before it became the answer. The first version measured over `Entry.text`, which is the entry LINE only -- an entry's continuation paragraphs are separate lines `parse_entries` does not carry -- and reported 25 of 67 DONE entries naming no artefact at all, 37.3134%, Wilson [26.7182%, 49.2846%]. Over the whole BLOCK, counting the marker's own evidence field, it is 0 of 67, Wilson [0.0000%, 5.4226%]. The wrong number was the alarming one. SIX TASK IDS CARRIED TWO MARKERS EACH and no guard noticed. Four were a name collision made 40 minutes earlier in this session -- entries P1 to P4 duplicate Section P's own CONDITIONS P1 to P4 at the top of the same file -- renamed A20 to A23. Two were ORPHANS sitting under continuation paragraphs: `parse_entries` reads the marker only from the line after an entry, so an orphan is invisible to the DONE-evidence check, the state census and the pre-commit gate, while a human reads "DONE, ENABLED" with no evidence field. title: Panel round 11: both seats broke V8's scoping claim, in separate sandboxes
verbatim: Panel round 11: both seats broke V8's scoping claim, in separate sandboxes FIRST ROUND WITH REAL INDEPENDENCE, and it paid immediately. Until tonight every seat shared one writable sandbox; now each has its own, and the two seats attacked V8 separately and BOTH got amnesty for a note's own prose. That agreement is evidence. Last round's would not have been. V8 — NOT READY AS DISPATCHED, now repaired. Two executed bypasses, both reproduced here before either fix was accepted: ONE SPACE ON A BLANK LINE. `sentences()` split paragraphs on a literal 2-newline string, `verbatim_paragraphs()` on a whitespace-tolerant regex. A blank line carrying a space is a break to one and not the other, so the two paragraph NUMBERINGS drift -- and the exempt set, computed by the second, is applied to findings numbered by the first. A Rule 27 violation AFTER verbatim-end, in the note's own voice, counted 0 and was tagged [verbatim]. title: A6, half I11 measured: 0 of 84 runner-dependent test files break on an inert edit
verbatim: A6, half I11 measured: 0 of 84 runner-dependent test files break on an inert edit THE CENSUS: 70 of 5026 test functions assert that a literal appears in the text of a Python source file -- 1.3928%, Wilson [1.1039%, 1.7559%], Clopper-Pearson [1.0873%, 1.7564%]. A census is not a verdict: some of those are the only check available, because a shell hook has no importable surface. THE EXPERIMENT: fragility is a property of behaviour under an IRRELEVANT edit, so make one. Two, of deliberately different strength, against bench/reference_runner_v3.py and the 84 test files that name it. EOF -- a comment appended after the last line. Nothing above it moves, nothing executes differently. 0 of 84 newly red, 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 4.3732%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 4.2965%]. NO TEST IN THIS SUITE ASSERTS ON THE RUNNER'S RAW BYTES. INSIDE -- a comment line inserted inside a function body, which is the realistic case and the one that fired 4 times on 2026-09-10 and 09-11, every time because a COMMENT GREW. 2 of 84 newly red, 2.3810%, Wilson [0.6554%, 8.2714%] -- and BOTH ARE LEGITIMATE: test_citation_content and test_experiment_run_ledger both cite the runner BY LINE NUMBER, so noticing that lines moved is precisely their job. Both are repaired at stage 0 of the hook, added yesterday for exactly this reason. So after yesterday's 4 repairs the illegitimate fragility in this class is 0. THE DETECTOR WAS WRONG FIRST AND A POSITIVE CONTROL SAID SO, which is why the census is trustworthy at all. It tracked only names bound DIRECTLY to `read_text()`; a control built from 3 of the 4 guards that actually broke here detected 1 of 3. The 2 it missed are the commonest shapes there are -- `window = src[i:i+400]` and `body = src[src.index("x"):]`. With taint propagated through intermediates it detects 3 of 3, and the figure moved 51 -> 70. AND MY OWN ALARM CRIED WOLF INSIDE THE HOUR. The run's final check re-used the entry guard's whole-tree cleanliness test, so a file created in another terminal during the 20-minute run made it print "THE TREE IS NOT CLEAN AFTER THE RUN" -- about something it neither touched nor could affect. It checks the revert of its own target now. That is the third alarm in two days narrowed from "something changed" to "the thing I am responsible for changed". title: A6 DONE: both unmeasured classes measured, and the alarming figure was my proxy
verbatim: A6 DONE: both unmeasured classes measured, and the alarming figure was my proxy I11 -- the source-text converse of `execute-do-not-grep`. It is not hypothetical: it fired 4 times on 2026-09-10 and 09-11, every time on a CORRECT change, twice on guards written the same day they broke, and every instance was a COMMENT GROWING under a window, an index, or a body slice. Census: 70 of 5026 test functions assert a literal appears in the text of a Python source file -- 1.3928%, Wilson [1.1039%, 1.7559%]. Experiment, because fragility is a property of behaviour under an IRRELEVANT edit and you have to make one. Against the runner and the 84 test files naming it: a comment APPENDED AFTER THE LAST LINE reddens 0 of 84, 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 4.3732%] -- nothing here asserts on the runner's raw bytes. A comment INSERTED INSIDE A FUNCTION reddens 2 of 84, 2.3810%, Wilson [0.6554%, 8.2714%], and BOTH ARE LEGITIMATE: test_citation_content and test_experiment_run_ledger cite the runner BY LINE NUMBER, so noticing lines moved is their job. I13 -- a test green because a NEIGHBOUR catches the regression. Measured by destroying a function outright and asking which files naming it go red. THE FIRST ANSWER WAS 11 OF 37 SURVIVING, 29.7297%, AND A 15-MINUTE READ OF 3 SURVIVORS REFUTED IT. All 3 were correct: test_fix_complexity asserts `"compute_rk" not in called` -- it names the symbol to require it is NOT called; test_target_complexity_is_reported AST-scans for CALL SITES, which emptying a function does not move; test_instrument_gaps_from_panel's own docstring RECORDS a prior mutation study of the same function. "Names it" is a bad proxy for "claims to cover it". Refined to files that actually CALL the symbol: 0 of 22 survived -- 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 14.8655%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 15.4373%]. I13 IS NOT SUPPORTED OVER THIS SAMPLE and the boundary is stated rather than buried: 5 functions in 1 module, upper bound 15% and not 0. BOTH INSTRUMENTS WERE WRONG BEFORE THEY WERE RIGHT, and both times a control said so rather than a reading. The census detector saw 1 of its own 3 worked examples until taint was propagated through intermediates; the neighbour script counted mentions until 3 survivors were read by hand. A NEAR-MISS IN THE EDIT ITSELF, caught by guards that already existed. The closing paragraph opened `**A6 DONE ...`, which `_is_entry` parses as a SECOND entry with the same id and no marker. `test_every_entry_carries_a_marker_at_all` and 4 others go red on it; verified by re-introducing it deliberately. title: A7 DONE: the entry expected a hole; there are 3 named paths and no instrument
verbatim: A7 DONE: the entry expected a hole; there are 3 named paths and no instrument NEITHER OF THE ENTRY'S FIGURES REPRODUCES, and establishing that took longer than the repair. No predicate returns 25. The closest -- severity >= CRITICAL_SEVERITY_THRESHOLD (0.7, READ from the runner rather than typed) AND hil_escalated AND no falsifier_code -- returns 22, and reproduces the entry's one other checkable family figure exactly, exp55_v3_control = 8. So it is almost certainly what was meant. exp53_control_zero_live CONTRIBUTES 0 AND CANNOT CONTRIBUTE ANY. Its 2 runs hold no *_report.json at all: findings live in checkpoint.json under `all_findings`, as a list of per-round LISTS, in a schema carrying `falsification_present` where the registry carries `falsifier_code`, with no escalation flag set anywhere. Run 1 holds exactly 10 criticals at >= 0.7 -- which is where the entry's "10" came from. They are criticals. They are not escalations. ALL 22 ARE ESCALATED BY A NAMED, DELIBERATE MECHANISM THAT RECORDS ITS REASON: 11 irreducible (the routing ladder ran out), 8 MERGE deadlock, 3 stale contested challenge. ANONYMOUS is 0 of 22 -- 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 14.8655%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 15.4373%]. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING IS THE INSTRUMENT. `irreducible_queue_count` counts only the first of those paths -- correctly, its docstring scopes it to the ladder running out -- so an audit keying on that one flag reports 11 of 22 as unaccounted, and "no falsifier" gets read as "no reason". AND THE COVERAGE CHECK FOUND A SEVENTH PATH ON ITS FIRST EXECUTION, which no census could have found because it has never fired on a critical without a falsifier: `escalate_stale_contested` has TWO escalating branches and the CONTESTED one was unrecognised. Comparing the table against the RUNNER rather than against the archive is what found it -- two representations with a comparator, which is the only form this project accepts. 3 mutations verified red, including one that drops the newly-found path and one that types the threshold instead of reading it. THE BACKLOG'S DISPOSITION REMAINS THE FOUNDER'S. Archived runs cannot be retro-fixed. The recommendation on the entry, for when he wants it: leave the 22 and rely on the path census, because every one already carries the reason a human needs. title: A8 parked with its facts measured; 3 of them change the question
verbatim: A8 parked with its facts measured; 3 of them change the question `scripts/blocker_triage.py` returns PARK -- nothing on the list declares a dependency on it -- so the RULING waits for the founder and the facts do not. THE POPULATION IS SMALLER AND SHARPER THAN 44. Of the 44 untracked cited paths, only 25 are cited by a NOTE: 19.6850% of all 127 cited bench/logs paths, Wilson [13.7041%, 27.4460%], Clopper-Pearson [13.1628%, 27.6724%]. Twelve appear ONLY in test files and 3 only in code -- illustrative paths, not evidence citations. `bench/logs/x/y.json` is a fixture in a test I wrote yesterday. The extractor's population is path-shaped STRINGS, not cited evidence, and roughly 4 in 10 of what it flags is an example. 18 OF THE 44 DO NOT EXIST EVEN ON THIS MACHINE -- 40.9091%, Wilson [27.6879%, 55.5902%]. Six carry `XX` or an ellipsis and are templates, not citations; the rest are almost all example paths. title: A13, A14 and A17 DONE: the sandbox survives, the seats no longer share it, and the verdict guard resolves the call
verbatim: A13, A14 and A17 DONE: the sandbox survives, the seats no longer share it, and the verdict guard resolves the call A13 -- I RAN THE FALSIFIER THE ENTRY ITSELF NAMES, and the test hypothesis is not supported. scripts/sandbox_survives_the_suite_2026-09-11.py builds a sandbox, counts, runs the suite inside it and counts again -- three times rather than twice, because a tree emptying during COLLECTION implicates an import-time side effect and one emptying during the RUN implicates a test body, and the round-4 report cannot tell them apart. bench/*.py: 168 before, 168 after collection, 168 after a full run of 6,748 passing tests. 0 lost at either point. That matters because this project HAS had `rmtree(x.parent)` take 179 entries out of TMPDIR on 2026-09-07, so a recurrence was the obvious suspect. The sandbox GAINS files during a run -- 17,606 to 17,628 -- tests write into it and none deletes. Recorded as UNREPRODUCED rather than refuted: one run in one sandbox does not exclude a rarely-firing test. The entry's other candidate was closed hours earlier: seats shared one writable sandbox and ran concurrently, so a destructive action by the seat finishing first landed under the seat still working -- and fable returned at 03:36:19, the minute the tree emptied. A14 -- the coupling this entry names is fixed, and the consequence was worse than the entry states. It was not only that `changes()` could not attribute a diff: the seats' VERDICTS were not independent, which is the property the founder's `pr` protocol exists to protect. Round 10's fable reply describes the `.zenodo.json` identity tier the cc2 seat had just invented. Round 11 is the first round where seat agreement is evidence. A17 -- the verdict-tuple guard matched NAMES where it needed to resolve calls, so a new script defining `scan()` returning a 3-tuple took supersession_check.py red for a truth test that is entirely correct -- that file's own `scan()` returns a LIST. The fix is Python's own scoping rule: a file that DEFINES a name shadows every other definition of it. `_locally_shadowed` removes such a name from the flagged set FOR THAT FILE ONLY, and only when the local definition demonstrably does not return a tuple of 2 or more elements. The guard is not weakened, with a test in each direction: a file whose OWN function returns a tuple is still flagged, and an IMPORTED verdict function is still flagged -- which is the defect it was built for. 2 mutations red, including the over-correction that shadows everything a file defines. The 2026-09-10 workaround -- renaming the new function to dodge the collision -- is now unnecessary. It removed the symptom and left the cause. TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN NEW SCRIPTS, both caught by guards that already existed. source_text_assertions printed a top-12 listing without saying what it withheld; neighbour_catches_it made --module and --symbol argparse-required, so a typo'd flag got "the following arguments are required" instead of "unrecognized arguments" -- a script that answers the wrong complaint first teaches the reader its diagnostics are unreliable. title: A8's producer now classifies citations; the population a ruling is about is 23, not 44
verbatim: A8's producer now classifies citations; the population a ruling is about is 23, not 44 A8 asks the founder to rule on cited bench/logs paths that git does not track. A fixture stays a fixture however much prose discusses it. 2 mutations verified red: promoting fixtures by prose again, and dropping the elision detection. A8's RULING remains the founder's and remains PARKED. What is settled is the question he is being asked. title: A18 DONE: two of the three "unwired" fields are wired, and the sweep's blind spot is named
verbatim: A18 DONE: two of the three "unwired" fields are wired, and the sweep's blind spot is named merge_arbitration_enabled is read at reference_runner_v3.py:12638 -- `if getattr(cfg, "merge_arbitration_enabled", False)` -- and immune_memory_enabled at :14984 in the same form. WHY THE SWEEP MISSED THEM. It resolved attribute access by AST, and `getattr(cfg, "field", default)` is an attribute read WRITTEN AS A STRING, so an attribute scan reports zero. The sweep chose AST over grep for good reasons and then looked for one of the two forms the language offers. Substring-versus-token, attribute-versus-getattr: the same mistake wearing a different hat, and the fourth variant of it found in two days. scripts/config_fields_are_read_2026-09-11.py resolves both forms and carries a mutation for EACH blind spot, so neither can come back: disabling the getattr branch reddens 3 tests, disabling the attribute branch reddens 1. THE THIRD FIELD IS GENUINELY UNREAD. `_ouroboros.max_papers_per_round` has 0 readers in production. But the arm is NOT lying to its reader, which is what the entry was worried about: its sibling in the same block, `api_access`, IS read at reference_runner_v3.py:9423, so the block reaches the runner and exactly one of its two keys is consulted -- and the arm's stated intent, "External literature retrieval OFF", is achieved through the key that IS read, because api_access is [] in every arm. So `max_papers_per_round = 0` is REDUNDANT rather than inert. A reader who believed the capability was disabled for the experiment was right, for a different reason than they would have guessed. The unread rate over the 4 fields examined is 1 of 4 = 25.0000%, Wilson [4.5587%, 69.9358%], Clopper-Pearson [0.6309%, 80.5880%]. An interval that wide on 4 observations is reported as the near-useless thing it is; the per-field answers carry the finding. Nothing in the frozen pre-registration configs is touched, which the entry also asked for. title: A16 DONE: the survey is safe now, and it immediately found what it was killed before finding
verbatim: A16 DONE: the survey is safe now, and it immediately found what it was killed before finding THE FIX IS THE ONE THE ENTRY ASKS FOR: declare the distinction rather than infer it. scripts/measurement_scripts_only_2026-09-11.py classes a script as a MEASUREMENT only when it neither writes to the tree nor spawns a process that could. All 4 scripts the entry names come back ACTION, each with the line that decided it: cdsfl_sv.py at a .write_text(), the other 3 at a subprocess call. Of 112 files in scripts/: 58 ACTION, 54 MEASUREMENT -- 51.7857%, Wilson [42.6270%, 60.8260%], Clopper-Pearson [42.1475%, 61.3272%]. CONSERVATIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, because the failure is asymmetric. A measurement wrongly classed as an action costs a missing row in a survey; an action wrongly classed as a measurement overwrites a preserved archive -- which is what happened to experimental_notes/data/adjudication_by_repair.json. An unrecognised call, a computed file mode, an unparseable file and any subprocess are all ACTION, with a mutation for each. THE CLAIM IS CHECKED BY RUNNING IT. The test runs the whole measurement set and asserts `git status --porcelain` is byte-identical before and after. It is. AND THE SURVEY FOUND SOMETHING. 5 of 54 measurement scripts did not answer `--help` cleanly, all failing the SAME way: the flag was unrecognised, so it was consumed as a positional argument -- a report path, a note to lint, a log to read. target_mutation_arrival_2026-09-08.py crashed with FileNotFoundError on the literal string `--help`; the other 4 silently ran a full measurement when the caller asked for usage. This project already carries the rule in its strong form -- a `--help` must never cost money, written after 15 of 17 runners billed a live dispatch on an unrecognised argument. These cost time rather than money; the principle is identical. All 5 repaired, and the count is now 0 of 54. THE DISTINCTION THE REPAIR PRESERVES, with its own test: a typo'd path still exits non-zero. `--help` is a request the program can satisfy; a missing file is not, and must never read as a clean note. note_vagueness_lint's own comment had anticipated this case exactly -- "an unrecognised flag, which lands here as a 'path'" -- and treated it as a typo, which is right for a typo and wrong for a request for usage. title: A12 DONE: the 15 ruled items are not one kind, and conflating them made a scope look like a defect
verbatim: A12 DONE: the 15 ruled items are not one kind, and conflating them made a scope look like a defect THE PROBLEM. The master task list calls itself "the ordered executable subset" of a 121-item inventory, so an absence is scoped rather than silent -- but it named none of the exclusions, and a reader cannot tell a deliberate omission from a lost item. READ FROM THE TRACKER'S OWN TABLES rather than restated, the 15 split two ways: RUNWAY (11) 17, 19, 20, 24, 31, 34, 36, 37, 38, 42, 43 -- work scheduled for a named point on the path to Bench Run 2. Deliberately not on this list, and already declared. STUDY PROGRAMME (4) 14, 28, 29, 46 -- things to MEASURE DURING a simulated run, in the founder's words "mark it in our simulated run programme of study". Not executable entries and never should be. One (46) is touched by the list; the other 3 are now declared. Unaccounted: 3 of 15 = 20.0000%, Wilson [7.0475%, 45.1854%] before the declaration; 0 of 15 after, Wilson [0.0000%, 20.3883%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 21.8019%]. TWO INSTRUMENT DEFECTS IN ONE MEASUREMENT, both reporting a FALSE ZERO, and I nearly believed the first. `(acc if pat.search(block) else []) and acc.append(n)` short-circuits on an EMPTY list and never appends. It reported that A12 declared nothing, while the entry visibly names 11 items. The replacement required `item` and the number to be ADJACENT, and the declaration reads `item **14 critical-severity ceiling**` -- markdown emphasis sits between the word and the number. The text was there; the pattern was not looking at the text a human sees. A clever one-liner that silently does nothing, and a pattern that cannot see its own subject, are the same failure as a guard that cannot fire. Both have mutations. THE TRACKER IS READ, NOT RESTATED, with a test that fails if the numbers are hard-coded -- so an item added there cannot be silently absent from the comparison, which is the shape this entry is about. title: A23 DONE: RECOVERY.md has a current SESSION STATE, and "run sv" would not have written it
verbatim: A23 DONE: RECOVERY.md has a current SESSION STATE, and "run sv" would not have written it FOUND BY RUNNING `rs`. The newest block was dated 2026-09-08 and named HEAD `beb39fb`, while HEAD was three days and dozens of commits past it -- so the picture a post-compaction reader trusts most omitted the whole task-list clearance arc, the fresh-clone work and two panel rounds. title: A22 DONE: the panel dispatcher imports, and still refuses to run without a brief
verbatim: A22 DONE: the panel dispatcher imports, and still refuses to run without a brief WHAT WAS WRONG. bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py read sys.argv[1] at MODULE LEVEL, required a BRIEF.md beside it, and raised SystemExit(2) when either was missing. Nothing could import it -- not a test wanting to inspect one function, not a tool, not a reader. The per-seat sandbox guard had to set sys.argv and PANEL_BRIEF_UNCHECKED=1 around its own import to get in, which is a test working around the code rather than testing it. title: Panel round 12: the instruments were worse than the entries they judged
verbatim: Panel round 12: the instruments were worse than the entries they judged EVERY NUMBER IN ROUND 12'S BRIEF WAS PRODUCED BY A SCRIPT I ALSO WROTE. The brief named that as the session's weakest structural property and asked the seats to attack it. Six of the seven findings were defects in MY instruments. All were reproduced here before any fix was accepted. V2 IS DONE, AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS THE PROBLEM. `overstated_entries` FABRICATED A 100% FAILURE RATE wherever git cannot answer. `git ls-files --error-unmatch` exits 0 tracked, 1 untracked, 128 NOT A GIT REPOSITORY -- and `tracked()` returned False for 1 and 128 alike. In the panel's own sandbox it printed "11 of 11 fail = 100.0000%, Wilson [74.1167%, 100.0000%]": three intervals on a fabricated number, disjoint from the real 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 25.8833%]. IT IS THE SAME DEFECT THE CC2 SEAT FOUND IN `orphan_figures` ONE ROUND EARLIER, in a script written the same day, with the correct pattern already committed in `bench/archive_corpus.py`. Writing the repair once did not stop the next script repeating it. TWO OF FOUR CHECKS STILL READ THE ENTRY LINE -- the population error the script's own docstring says was "caught before it became the answer". It was caught in ONE of three. 21 entries carry a figure on their first line; 47 in their block. Over the block: W1 quotes p = 2.199086e-14 with no producer, and now names one, because measured-rate-travels-with-its-script applies to a BLOCKED entry exactly as to a closed one. A16 HAD A MATERIAL HOLE AND THE CC2 SEAT NAMED THE FILE. `cdsfl_seal_logs.py` came back MEASUREMENT, and its default invocation SEALS LOG DIRECTORIES -- it writes through `save_json`, a METHOD on a class imported from another module. The classifier resolved calls inside one file and could not see across an import boundary. It resolves one level now, functions and class methods, and the survey set drops 55 -> 53. AND MY OWN GUARD FOR THE ARCHIVE-OVERWRITE INCIDENT COULD NOT FAIL. `git status --porcelain` outside a work tree exits 128 and prints NOTHING -- byte-identical to a clean tree -- so comparing before with after compared "" with "". The probe asserts git's exit status now. A16's classifier also passed five resolvable write forms: `Path("x").open("w")`, `os.open`, `io.open`, `open(x, mode="w")`, `f.truncate(0)`. The mode sits at a different index in each form, and the docstring's guarantee -- "anything this cannot resolve is an ACTION" -- was false for the method form. A7's "almost certainly the one that was meant" is WITHDRAWN. Seven candidate predicates reproduce the single anchor exp55_v3_control = 8, giving totals of 20, 22 and 32. One family figure cannot identify a predicate. ANONYMOUS is 0 under every candidate, so the conclusion never moved -- the identification was overstated, and 22 is quoted with its family from here on. A18's census DROPPED EVERY LIST-VALUED KEY, so `api_access` -- the key that entry's own "the arm is not lying to its reader" argument depends on -- was never in the default population. A22 COST SOMETHING AND TWO TESTS FOUND IT WITHIN THE HOUR. Moving the brief binding out of import time left `LOGS` as None, reached through a bare `LOGS / name`, producing "TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'NoneType' and 'str'" -- a message that says nothing about what to do. Every such use goes through `_logs_dir()` now, which raises a sentence naming the remedy. AND THE CAPPED-LISTING GUARD SAID "prints" WITHOUT CHECKING. It flagged any `for x in expr[:N]` in a function carrying no disclosure word, taking the suite red for a bounded AST lookup that displays nothing -- the A17 shape again, the same night. It resolves whether the loop prints. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: A rate travels with its date: the sibling rule, named by a seat and measured first
verbatim: A rate travels with its date: the sibling rule, named by a seat and measured first ROUND 12's BRIEF QUOTED 67 DONE ENTRIES, 5026 TEST FUNCTIONS AND 112 SCRIPTS as though current. By the time the seats read it the list was at 80, 5091 and 113; by the next morning 81, 5115 and 113. None of it changed a conclusion. All of it invites exactly the reproduction failure task A7 spent its whole budget on -- a reader who cannot tell a figure that DRIFTED from a figure that was WRONG. THE PROJECT HAD LEARNED THIS ONE DAY EARLIER. Task V4 found entry 6.1's "23 of 41 completion signals" had become 24 of 42 because the archive grows, and wrote that "a typed figure over a growing corpus is not merely unverifiable, it is guaranteed to go stale". Five new figures were then written the same way the next day. MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING, so the fix goes where the defect is. On the master task list the coverage is already perfect: 0 of 44 entries carrying a percentage lack a date, Wilson [0.0000%, 8.0296%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 8.0420%]. The rot was in the BRIEFS. So the advisory lives in panel_brief_validate, where the drift happened, and the list gets a ratchet where it is already right. REPORTS, NEVER REFUSES -- the same decision as every other advisory in that validator, for the same reason: a guard that refuses a correct brief teaches people to skip the validator. AND MY FIRST POSITIVE CONTROL TESTED THE REGEX RATHER THAN THE RULE. Mutating the real list by adding an undated percentage to an existing block changed nothing and the control stayed green, because that block carries dates elsewhere and the check is per-BLOCK. The rule is callable now and the control feeds it a synthetic block. The per-block granularity is a real limit, stated rather than hidden: a NEW undated figure beside a dated one is not caught; a whole entry or a whole brief with no date at all is. title: Panel round 13: the gate that could not fail moved from e4 to e3, in the fix for e4
verbatim: Panel round 13: the gate that could not fail moved from e4 to e3, in the fix for e4 BOTH SEATS FOUND IT INDEPENDENTLY, in separate sandboxes, and it was mine. A19 handed `_gateable_source` to `_run_effect_ruff` and `_run_effect_bandit` so they would score the extracted Python rather than the English. It did NOT hand it to `_capture_baseline`. So e3 subtracted two numbers taken over DIFFERENT TEXTS: the listings after the fix, minus the whole prose before it. Measured on bench/BUILD_BOT_TEST_BENCH_FIX_SPEC.md: baseline 311, gate 4. One seat injected SEVEN real ruff diagnostics into a listing and e3 scored 1.0. That is verbatim the property the A19 entry condemns in e4 -- "structurally incapable of failing, which is worse than unavailable, because an unavailable gate is excluded from the weighted mean and a gate that always passes drags it up" -- reproduced by the repair, within a day of my writing that sentence. It ran the other way too: bandit could not parse the prose, so its baseline was a false 0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM, and a HIGH ALREADY PRESENT in a listing counted as NEW. A correct fix convicted for a pre-existing defect. THE SECOND CRITICAL: the fence pattern matched ONE SHAPE OF MARKDOWN. Verified across seven real shapes before repair. `~~~`, CRLF and attribute-carrying fences extracted NOTHING -- so the flag silently did no work on a Windows-authored or tilde-fenced document. Indented and blockquoted fences extracted their markdown scaffolding, so ast.parse raised, A = g1*g2 = 0, and EVERY fix to such a document was REJECTED. A REJECT IS A CLAIM AND NO_SCORE IS AN ABSTENTION. Turning the flag on would have made the instrument WORSE rather than silent, on a listing inside a numbered list -- the commonest shape in a design note -- and re-armed the 2026-08-01 convergence halt on a new input. Both repaired. The baseline now gates the same substrate the gates score, and returns None rather than a false zero when there is no code -- an unavailable gate is excluded from the weighted mean, a gate handed 0 always passes. `_MD_PY_FENCE_ANY` + `_strip_listing_prefix` handle all seven shapes; `pycon` still abstains deliberately, because a doctest block interleaves source with output and abstaining is right where convicting is not; and the listing's own Python indentation survives the dedent, with a test that fails if it is flattened. 3 mutations verified red: baseline back to the whole document, fence back to one shape, dedent flattening everything. A19 STAYS OPEN. The flag is the founder's to rule on, and round 13's remaining findings are recorded and unfixed: g1/g2 are ABSOLUTE where every other gate is a delta, so a fenced FRAGMENT convicts every fix; and sk_s_floor = 0.0 makes effect-gate rejection on prose nearly impossible. title: A19 round 13, part 2: the flag repairs the gates' substrate and not their threshold
verbatim: A19 round 13, part 2: the flag repairs the gates' substrate and not their threshold THE DECISIVE FACT FOR THE FOUNDER'S RULING, executed against this project's own committed fixture rather than argued. With the A19 flag ON, `SHELL_INJECTION_FIX` -- the `subprocess.call("rm -rf /tmp/cdsfl_targets", shell=True)` smuggled into a fenced listing, the exploit that cost a discarded run -- scores sk=1.0000 ADMISSIBLE, IDENTICAL to the correct prose fix. The cause is precise and measured, not a guess: bandit rates `shell=True` with a STRING LITERAL as LOW on all three findings it raises (B404, B607, B602), and e4 counts only HIGH and MEDIUM. With a VARIABLE command bandit does rate it HIGH -- and even then the derivation gives sk=0.6667 against the corrected break-even S* = 0.50493, because on a prose target e2_regression is unavailable so E = (1/3)e3 + (2/3)e4. One new HIGH is not enough to reject. Two are. So the flag repairs the gates' SUBSTRATE and does not repair their THRESHOLD. Turning it on would not have caught the exploit. That is the strongest argument for leaving it off and it belongs on the entry rather than in a commit nobody re-reads. TWO FURTHER ROUND-13 FINDINGS, FIXED. g1 and g2 are ABSOLUTE where e2, e3 and e4 are all DELTAS. On a prose target a listing is routinely an ILLUSTRATIVE FRAGMENT -- ` return 0`, a method body, a diff hunk -- that never parsed and never will, so A = g1*g2 = 0 and every fix is REJECTED for a failure not attributable to it. They abstain now where the code was ALREADY unparseable, and the guard is not a licence: a fix that BREAKS working code is still rejected, with a test. AND THE BASELINE CHECK HAD TO BE TESTED BY THE GATE'S OWN COMPILER. `ast.parse("return 0")` SUCCEEDS while `compile("return 0", ..., "exec")` raises "'return' outside function" -- so the first version said "it parsed" and g2 convicted the fix anyway. Two expressions of one question with no comparator, inside the guard written to stop exactly that. A hunk that DELETES every listing escaped as ESCALATE -- all three gates reporting "target carries no code" on a target that was admitted to scoring BECAUSE it carried reducible code. `g0_code_retained` REJECTS it: a removal with no measured replacement is the additive standard as a gate. The seat flagged the design call and so does the entry -- a finding whose whole point is "delete this wrong example" deserves a distinct outcome rather than either of these, and that is the founder's to settle. title: A2: stage-0 repairs now reach the commit, not just the working tree
verbatim: A2: stage-0 repairs now reach the commit, not just the working tree FOUND BY CLONING HEAD AND RUNNING THE SUITE THERE. A2's DONE claim said a fresh clone is green. It was not: 3 failed, 6952 passed, 38 skipped, 1 xfailed in 1478.12s test_citation_content_2026-09-10.py test_experiment_run_ledger_2026-08-26.py test_measurement_survey_is_safe_2026-09-11.py The same suite in this working tree was 6988 passed, 0 failed. THE CAUSE. A pre-commit hook sees the STAGED snapshot. Stage 0's repairs -- the run-ledger refresh and the citation-content repair -- write the WORKING TREE and never `git add` what they wrote. So every commit shipped the UNREPAIRED content and left the repair uncommitted for the next commit to sweep in. The repairs ran correctly and were permanently 1 commit behind, so every clone at HEAD was broken while `git status` here said only "modified" and the suite was green. Confirmed directly: the ledger's generator and the working-tree ledger agreed at 14904 while `git diff HEAD` still reported the ledger modified. THE FIX. hooks/stage0_restage.sh holds the staging logic once; the hook sources it and pipes each repair's output through it. ONLY the exact paths a repair REPORTS changing are staged -- never `git add -A` -- so an unrelated work-in-progress edit cannot be swept into a commit. A missing helper now REFUSES the commit rather than silently restoring the defect. A CHECK THAT COULD NOT FAIL, caught by its own test while writing it. The pathspec-commit notice first asked `git rev-parse --git-path index` for the real index path. That command RETURNS $GIT_INDEX_FILE verbatim when the variable is set, so it compared the variable with itself and reported "ordinary commit" for every input. `--absolute-git-dir` does not consult it. Pinned by test_the_real_index_path_is_not_derived_from_the_variable. MEASURED, in a scratch repository: a hook's `git add` DOES reach a pathspec commit (`git commit -- <path>`), because git sets GIT_INDEX_FILE to a temporary index and commits from it -- but a file outside the pathspec lands with it and `git status` reads MM afterwards. Hence the notice, which never refuses. 24 tests in bench/tests/test_precommit_restages_repairs_2026-09-11.py, all executing against a real git index rather than reading the hook's text, with a mutation control: the same hook without the staging line must FAIL to reach HEAD, or the positive test proves nothing. Also commits the repair debt itself -- 7 files the previous hooks repaired and never staged. title: A3: the citation repair was corrupting the citations it was not repairing
verbatim: A3: the citation repair was corrupting the citations it was not repairing FOUND BY THE PROBE FOR THE PREVIOUS COMMIT. To prove a stage-0 repair now reaches HEAD, 1 citation in the master task list was deliberately staled to a 1-digit line number and the commit allowed to run. The repair landed, which is what the probe tested. It also did this in the same pass, in reference_runner_v3.py, line number before -> after: 10934 -> 114560934 12638 -> 114562638 14984 -> 114564984 3 correct citations destroyed while repairing 1, and they reached HEAD at commit b024c97. Restored here. THE CAUSE, 1 line: an unbounded, global `str.replace` of the old line number. 1. NO DIGIT BOUNDARY. A short stale number rewrites the PREFIX of every longer one. Nothing about this needs a contrived value: the runner is 15,587 lines, its citations are 2 to 5 digits, and 1135 eats 11354. 2. GLOBAL. Two citations sharing a line number, 1 stale and 1 correct, were both rewritten -- so a citation pointing inside its own symbol could be moved out of it. Both faults come from searching for the text again when the position was already known. `check` now carries each number's offsets and `repair` splices at them, right to left so earlier offsets stay valid, refusing and reporting any edit whose offset does not hold the digits expected. 8 tests in bench/tests/test_citation_repair_does_not_corrupt_2026-09-11.py, every one CALLING repair, with a mutation control that reproduces the corruption from the old one-line replace, a 4-digit-eats-5-digit case with no 1-digit number anywhere, and an anti-vacuity pair so a repair that repaired nothing could not pass. A SCANNER CANNOT TELL A WARNING FROM THE THING IT WARNS ABOUT, twice in one hour. The first draft quoted the 3 corrupted values as path-and-number tokens inside its docstrings, and the new repository-wide check flagged its own documentation; the illustrations are now bare numbers. Then the pre-commit gate refused the commit with 13 findings from test_line_citations_resolve_2026-09-01.py, every one a FIXTURE string of the form name.py:NNN. That guard's own docstring records the identical trap happening to itself. The fixture module is renamed to `toy_target.py`, which is already in that guard's PLACEHOLDER list -- the project's existing way of saying "illustrative, not a citation". Also: bench/tests/test_precommit_guard_2026-09-09.py's scratch repository now copies every hooks/*.sh the hook sources, by glob rather than by name. Adding hooks/stage0_restage.sh turned 3 of its tests red because the scratch tree had the hook and nothing beside it. title: A2: `--help` is now ANSWERED by every measurement script, not survived
verbatim: A2: `--help` is now ANSWERED by every measurement script, not survived MEASURED, and the measurement is the finding. `measurement_scripts_only_2026-09-11.py --run` executes every script it classes as a measurement with `--help` and reports how many "did not answer --help cleanly". It decided that on the EXIT CODE. A script with no argument parser does not answer `--help`: it ignores the flag, runs its entire measurement, and exits 0. Requiring a `usage:` line instead, over the 53 scripts then classed as measurements: answered --help with a usage line : 23 exited 0 but printed NO usage line: 30 not answering: 30/53 = 56.6038% Wilson 95% : [43.2654%, 69.0496%] (statsmodels) Clopper-Pearson 95% : [42.2826%, 70.1608%] (statsmodels/beta; scipy agrees to 1.1e-16) Now 0 of 54. Producing script: scripts/help_is_answered_2026-09-11.py, which imports the survey's OWN classifier rather than reimplementing it. HOW IT SURFACED, and why it belongs to A2. In this working tree all 53 exited 0. In a fresh clone 2 of them failed -- build_experiment_report.py on an archived log that .gitignore excludes, and check_model_keys.py because a clone has no .env -- and those were 2 of the 3 failures that made "a fresh clone is green" untrue. The other 28 carried the same defect silently. fresh_clone_census had already recorded the build_experiment_report symptom without the cause. THE FIX. scripts/_cli_help.py: `answer_help(__doc__, __file__)`, wired into the first statement of each script's `__main__` block, so a plain run reaches exactly the code it reached before. 2 scripts do their work at module level and were wired by hand. AND AN UNRECOGNISED ARGUMENT NOW EXITS 2 RATHER THAN BEING IGNORED. That rule already existed in test_operational_scripts.py -- "a script that accepts `--fix-timestamps` and does nothing with it is the 118-day no-op again" -- but its check is a TEXT scan for `sys.argv`, and a script reading argv only through the helper names no `sys.argv` at all. All 28 would have read as argv-free and inherited a pass while `track_record_audit.py --bogus` ran the full audit and exited 0. A scanner resolving 1 form and reporting a false zero for the other; the 10th instance this session. The refusal is enforced inside the helper, and the scan is taught to see the call. Verified first that nothing invokes any of the 30 with an argument: an AST walk of every tracked .py found 0. TWO ABSOLUTE PATHS TO THE MAINTAINER'S CHECKOUT REMOVED. absorb_rule_disagreement_2026-09-05.py and deepseek_falsifier_supply_2026-09-09.py set REPO to "/Users/.../Constraint_Engineering", so running either from a clone measured THIS tree and reported it as the clone's result. A script that cannot see the checkout it was launched from cannot fail in a clone, which is how a clone-only defect stays invisible. The other 7 hits for that string are prose inside model briefs and a path to the session transcripts outside the repo; neither is a repository root, and both are left alone. 27 tests in bench/tests/test_help_is_answered_2026-09-11.py. The repository now reports 0 of 54, so every assertion about the current state would pass whether or not the criterion works: TestTheCriterionCanFail builds a script that ignores the flag and requires the criterion to catch it, and test_the_unvouched_path_is_actually_exercised keeps the executed branch of the coverage test non-empty. A STRUCTURAL TEST THAT MANUFACTURED ITS OWN DEFECT, caught while writing it. The coverage test first asked only whether each script mentions `argparse` or `answer_help`, and named 5 that do neither -- all 5 answer `--help` with a hand-rolled check, note_vagueness_lint.py's existing because it once consumed the flag as a FILENAME. Anything the structural check cannot vouch for is now RUN. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: A2: something now CLONES, because nothing in the repository did
verbatim: A2: something now CLONES, because nothing in the repository did A2's claim is a measurement -- "the suite passes in a fresh clone" -- and it was made on 2026-09-10 and again on 2026-09-11 and was false both times, found each time by a person cloning by hand: clone at HEAD 3 failed, 6952 passed, 38 skipped, 1 xfailed working tree 6988 passed, 0 failed BOTH OF A2'S INSTRUMENTS WERE SOUND AND NEITHER COULD SEE THE CLAIM. bench/tests/test_fresh_clone_suite_2026-09-10.py, the entry's declared evidence, guards the individual repairs -- the replay rebase, the onboarding stamp, the archive-root predicate -- and clones nothing. scripts/fresh_clone_census_2026-09-10.py re-runs the named tests in THIS checkout, the tree whose greenness was never in doubt. scripts/fresh_clone_suite_2026-09-11.py performs the clone and runs pytest in it. It also reports whether the working tree is CLEAN, because a clone measures HEAD: a green clone with a dirty tree says nothing about what the next commit will ship, which is exactly the gap that hid the staging defect for 2 days. That check reports UNKNOWN rather than "clean" when git exits non-zero -- this project has read an empty stdout from a failed git command as "clean" once and as "untracked" once, 1 round apart. It REFUSES to report a measurement of a different commit as this one's: the clone's HEAD is compared with this tree's before pytest runs. 11 tests in bench/tests/test_fresh_clone_is_actually_run_2026-09-11.py, which runs the whole path -- clone, pytest, parse, exit code -- on 1 fast test file. 27.55 s, of which the clone is 6.58 s and 549 MB. The full-suite mode is roughly 25 minutes and is deliberately a command a person runs, not a test. MEASURED clone cost on this machine, 4 variants: --no-hardlinks 6.58 s / 550 MB, --depth 1 5.27 s / 549 MB, plain local path with hardlinks 2.98 s / 581 MB, --depth 1 --no-hardlinks 5.55 s / 549 MB. The bulk is the CHECKOUT, not the history, so --depth 1 buys almost nothing. A TRAP WALKED INTO WHILE WRITING THE SCRIPT, now pinned by a test. The first draft called `answer_help` at the top of `main()` AND built an argparse parser below it. answer_help answers --help first, so the help text read `usage: ... [-h]` and hid --subset, --only, --keep and --timeout. No script may now do both. Also records, in scripts/help_is_answered_2026-09-11.py, why there is deliberately no `--at <rev>`: a revision-walking version would measure a tracked-files-only worktree, and the 30 scripts being counted are exactly the ones that read untracked archives, so it would be a different measurement wearing the same name. It REFUSES to report a measurement of a different commit as this one's: the clone's HEAD is compared with this tree's before pytest runs. 11 tests in bench/tests/test_fresh_clone_is_actually_run_2026-09-11.py, which runs the whole path -- clone, pytest, parse, exit code -- on 1 fast test file. 27.55 s, of which the clone is 6.58 s and 549 MB. The full-suite mode is roughly 25 minutes and is deliberately a command a person runs, not a test. MEASURED clone cost on this machine, 4 variants: --no-hardlinks 6.58 s / 550 MB, --depth 1 5.27 s / 549 MB, plain local path with hardlinks 2.98 s / 581 MB, --depth 1 --no-hardlinks 5.55 s / 549 MB. The bulk is the CHECKOUT, not the history, so --depth 1 buys almost nothing. A TRAP WALKED INTO WHILE WRITING THE SCRIPT, now pinned by a test. The first draft called `answer_help` at the top of `main()` AND built an argparse parser below it. answer_help answers --help first, so the help text read `usage: ... [-h]` and hid --subset, --only, --keep and --timeout. No script may now do both. Also records, in scripts/help_is_answered_2026-09-11.py, why there is deliberately no `--at <rev>`: a revision-walking version would measure a tracked-files-only worktree, and the 30 scripts being counted are exactly the ones that read untracked archives, so it would be a different measurement wearing the same name. title: A2: partial staging is announced rather than absorbed
verbatim: A2: partial staging is announced rather than absorbed `git add -- <path>` stages the WHOLE file. If the author staged part of a file with `git add -p` and deliberately left the rest out, a stage-0 repair to that file sweeps the rest into the commit. The master task list is repaired by the citation guard and is edited constantly, so this is not hypothetical. IT STILL STAGES. The alternative is the defect the helper exists to fix -- the commit ships unrepaired content and every clone at HEAD is broken. Between "an extra hunk lands, visibly, with a line saying so" and "every clone is broken, silently, for 2 days", the first is the lesser cost. It is a cost, so it is announced. Surgical staging -- splicing only the repaired line into the index blob -- was considered and rejected: it means building a tree object by hand inside a shell hook, and a subtle bug there writes a WRONG blob, which is worse than an extra hunk the author can see in the diff. 4 tests added, including the 2 anti-noise cases: a file with only unstaged changes and a fully staged file must both be SILENT, because a notice on the ordinary case teaches people to ignore it. Also falsified the no-arguments claim more widely than the original AST walk: every one of 8,174 tracked files scanned for the 30 wired script names followed by a token on the same line. 8 candidates, all false positives -- 1 is this session's own comment documenting the defect, 7 are archived panel tool-call logs where the following token is a shell redirect. title: A2: a script whose input is outside the repository declines rather than tracebacks
verbatim: A2: a script whose input is outside the repository declines rather than tracebacks A clone has the repository and nothing else. 3 scripts read a workflow transcript from the agent session directory -- outside the tree, specific to 1 machine and 1 session, absent everywhere else. Measured by pointing all 3 at an absent path: founder_decision_ledger.py exit 1 FileNotFoundError traceback salvage_task_reconstruction.py exit 2 "no journal at ..." triage_open_founder_decisions.py exit 2 "no journal at ..." 2 of 3 already declined by name. The 3rd raised a bare FileNotFoundError, which reads as a BROKEN SCRIPT rather than as a missing input, and the difference matters to a reader deciding whether the repository is sound. It now declines in the same words as its 2 siblings and says the path is outside the repository. THE PATHS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT REWRITTEN. A workflow transcript genuinely lives outside the repository; there is nowhere inside it for the constant to point. That is a different thing from the 2 scripts that hardcoded the maintainer's CHECKOUT as their repository root, which were changed to Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] earlier today. 11 tests in bench/tests/test_outside_inputs_decline_2026-09-11.py: non-zero exit, no traceback, and the missing path named, for each of the 3 -- plus an anti-vacuity pair, because if the prefix substitution silently did nothing every case would be running the real script against the real journal and passing for reasons unconnected to the property.
