title: A2: the census records today's causes, and 2 guards caught my own additions
verbatim: A2: the census records today's causes, and 2 guards caught my own additions THE CENSUS WAS STALE IN EXACTLY THE WAY IT WARNS ABOUT. scripts/fresh_clone_census_2026-09-10.py's rows for the citation guard and the run ledger both said the repair was "the hook runs --fix at stage 0, repair before check". That repair is what failed on 2026-09-11 -- it wrote the working tree and never staged what it wrote. Both rows now carry the recurrence, and a new row records the --help class. 11 of 16 files = 68.7500%, Wilson [44.4044%, 85.8354%], Clopper-Pearson [41.3379%, 88.9830%] (statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00). THE CAUSE KEYS ARE THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS and the 2 recurrences keep theirs, because re-keying them would silently change a published proportion to mean something else. The script now says so in its output rather than leaving a reader to assume a running total. AND THE CENSUS'S OWN LIMIT IS NOW STATED: `--check` re-runs the named tests HERE, in the tree whose greenness was never in doubt, so it catches a stale row and CANNOT catch a clone-only regression. fresh_clone_suite_2026-09-11.py is the one that clones. TWO EXISTING GUARDS CAUGHT MY OWN WORK, which is the system working. 1. `test_no_script_prints_a_capped_listing_in_silence` flagged `working_tree_is_clean` printing the first 6 dirty paths and " ...". A cut list under a heading that reads as complete is a silent falsehood, and " ..." says there is more without saying how much. Both capped listings in the new script now name the remainder. 2. `test_the_refresh_stage_cannot_exit_non_zero` went red because stage 0 can now refuse. That test's DOCSTRING says "a convenience copy must never block a commit"; its CHECK forbade `exit 1` anywhere in stage 0. Those agreed only while stage 0 held nothing but repairs. It now holds a check that hooks/stage0_restage.sh is present -- an infrastructure fault, which the hook's own header already says must block loudly. The invariant is restated on the thing it was always about: each of the 3 REPAIR blocks individually may not refuse. That is 3 assertions where there was 1 region, so it is a tightening. A second test counts the refusals in the whole stage and requires exactly 1, the missing-helper check, so a refusal added BETWEEN the blocks cannot slip past the per-block form. title: Panel round 14: 5 defects in my own A2 fixes, 3 found by both seats
verbatim: Panel round 14: 5 defects in my own A2 fixes, 3 found by both seats cc2 and fable, free seats only, no paid dispatch. 5 distinct defects, 3 found by BOTH independently -- 60.0000%, Wilson [23.0724%, 88.2379%], Clopper-Pearson [14.6633%, 94.7255%] (statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00). cc2 found nothing fable missed; fable found 2 more. F1 -- `git add -- <path>` STAGES THE WHOLE FILE, so a stage-0 repair sweeps in hunks the author deliberately withheld. My mitigation, "only the exact paths a repair reports", bounds which FILES are touched and not which HUNKS, and the repaired files -- the master task list, the notes -- are exactly the ones edited incrementally. THE SEATS DISAGREED ON THE MECHANISM AND THE DISAGREEMENT WAS SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT. 8-line file, real index, repair at a varying distance from the author's unstaged hunk: gap 3-way `git merge-file` zero-context `git apply --cached` 0 CONFLICT FAILED (same line -- no answer) 1 CONFLICT OK, WIP excluded 2 OK OK 3 OK OK Zero-context apply succeeds everywhere merge-file does AND at gap 1, which is the common geometry: a citation repair 1 line from an edit in progress. At gap 0 both refuse, correctly. Implemented as a pre-repair snapshot plus a zero-context patch into the INDEX ONLY -- the working tree is never written, so there is nothing to lose if the hook dies. On collision it refuses loudly and the repair lags 1 commit, visibly. F2 -- MY PATHSPEC NOTICE FIRED ON `git commit -a`. Reproduced here from a live hook, git 2.50.1: git commit .git/index real index silent git commit --amend .git/index real index silent git commit -a <gitdir>/index.lock real index WARNED git commit -- <path> <gitdir>/next-index-<pid>.lock TEMPORARY warned Every `git commit -am` was told "this is a pathspec commit" and that files outside the pathspec would land. Both false, on the commonest commit command there is. The first version of that notice could never fire; this one fired when it must not -- a guard that cannot fail, in mirror image. F3 -- `check()` READ WITH errors="replace" AND `repair()` STRICT. One bad byte in one note raised inside repair(), the hook's `|| true` swallowed it, and NO citation was repaired in that pass: the round's headline defect re-entering through the repair that exists to close it. And read_text/write_text translate newlines, so repairing 1 number in a CRLF file rewrote every line ending AND made check()'s offsets index a different string from the bytes on disk. One reader now, bytes in and bytes out, refusing a file whose bytes do not survive the round trip. Reachability today 0 of 866 for each, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.4416%]. F4 -- A CRASHED REPAIR WAS INVISIBLE. A traceback carries none of the success tokens the hook greps for and `|| true` eats the exit code, so a repair that died printed nothing. Greps widened to REFUSED|Traceback|Error. F5 -- A MACHINE-SPECIFIC PATH MY OWN SCAN MISSED, and it was worse than reported. My sweep required the literal `"/Users/georgejackson`; decision_label_staleness_2026-09-09.py builds its path as `Path.home() / ".claude/projects/-Users-georgejackson-..."`, so the scan returned a false zero -- the 11th instance this session of a scanner resolving 1 form of a thing. With its transcript absent it did not crash: it printed "Sources written BEFORE at least 1 later founder message: 0 of 5 = 0.0%" with a Wilson interval and its conclusion, and exited 0. An authoritative no-staleness result manufactured from no data, which is worse than a traceback because it reads as a measurement. It now declines, and is the 4th row in test_outside_inputs_decline_2026-09-11.py. TWO MORE FOUND BY P-PASSING MY OWN FIX, neither reported by a seat. An EMPTY delta returned the same code as a failed apply, so a repair that reported a path it had not changed made the hook announce a collision when nothing had collided. 3 return codes now: staged, collided, nothing-to-do. The POSIX intersection used `for _b in $_both`, which WORD-SPLITS. A path containing a space became several words, was never snapshotted, and took the collision branch -- measured on `A Note With Spaces.md`. It fails SAFE, but the repair does not land and the message is false. `--name-only -z` with line-wise reads. A path containing a NEWLINE is still not handled and the comment says so rather than implying coverage. The first POSIX rewrite was worse: it used `comm -12 - <(...)`, a bashism in a file sourced by a `#!/bin/sh` hook. `sh -n` accepted it only because /bin/sh is bash in POSIX mode here; under dash the hook would not parse and every commit on a Debian-like system would be refused. Now checked with `dash -n` as well as `sh -n`. AND I BROKE 10 TESTS AND DID NOT SEE IT. hooks/stage0_restage.sh is sourced by the hook, which REFUSES without it, and both scratch fixtures copied the hook and nothing beside it -- 3 tests in test_precommit_guard and 10 in test_note_lint_guard. I caught the first 3 and fixed that fixture alone, because I verified with targeted subsets instead of the full suite. The clone run found the rest. bench/tests/hook_fixture.py is now the single installer both fixtures call, so the next file added beside the hook cannot repeat it. Full suite, working tree: 7100 passed, 5 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed in 1832.47s. Every fix mutation-tested: the word-splitting intersection restored turns the spaced-path test red, and an empty patch returning 1 turns the false-alarm test red. title: Panel records: 9 rounds existed only on one machine, and the 3 rescued were incomplete
verbatim: Panel records: 9 rounds existed only on one machine, and the 3 rescued were incomplete THE DIRECTIVE, verbatim: "All P-pass results, external reviews (human or machine), and both potential and actual adversarial findings, must be presented in full and in unfiltered format ... Always save these findings to an appropriate user-defined resource. Never summarise in place of the full output." MEASURED 2026-09-11. Panel output is written under bench/logs/, which .gitignore:41 excludes entirely: panel rounds under bench/logs : 12 fully mirrored : 0 preserved: 0/12 = 0.0000% Wilson [0.0000%, 24.2494%] Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 26.4648%] Nine rounds -- 2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 -- had never been copied at all. The 3 that were rescued on 2026-09-10 were INCOMPLETE: each was missing its seat_proposals.diff, the file recording what the seats actually WROTE rather than what they said. WHY IT WENT WRONG, and it is the shape this project keeps meeting. The 2026-09-10 rescue was an ACT, not a mechanism. It rescued 3 rounds and nothing afterwards, and nothing reported the gap -- so the exposure its own README documented for round 4 quietly reapplied to every round since. scripts/mirror_panel_records_2026-09-11.py does the rescue as a mechanism, verifies every copy against its original by sha256, and its --check mode returns non-zero while any round is unmirrored. 72 files copied, 3.8 MB, 12 of 12 now preserved -- Wilson [75.7506%, 100.0000%], Clopper-Pearson [73.5352%, 100.0000%]. 8 tests in bench/tests/test_panel_records_are_preserved_2026-09-11.py, with anti-vacuity in both directions: the round set must not be empty, and each mirrored round must carry real bytes, because a directory of empty files would satisfy sha256 equality on both sides and preserve nothing. 0 PAID SEATS, ASSERTED RATHER THAN CLAIMED. No cx.json, cgpt.json or ds.json exists in any round, under bench/logs or in the mirror -- with an anti-vacuity case requiring cc2.json or fable.json to be present, since the absence of paid seats proves nothing about an empty directory. The .md.txt suffix is the existing convention, not an invention: the note linter refuses a verbatim archival brief and the only route to compliance would be EDITING the record, which is what experimental_notes/evidence/ already answers with .py.txt for seat-written code. The 2026-09-10 README said "4 rounds" and described the hand rescue; it now carries the correction rather than being rewritten. title: RECOVERY.md carried a claim that had gone false, and the guard could not see it
verbatim: RECOVERY.md carried a claim that had gone false, and the guard could not see it FOUND BY `rg`, on the founder's instruction. resources/RECOVERY.md's newest SESSION STATE block read: "A FRESH `git clone` NOW RUNS THE FULL SUITE GREEN: 6658 passed, 32 skipped, 1 xfailed, EXIT 0" Cloning HEAD that morning gave 3 failed, 6952 passed. This is the 1 document a post-compaction reader trusts most, and the claim had been false for a day. THE A23 GUARD WAS GREEN AND WAS RIGHT TO BE. Its own docstring scopes it: "It does NOT check the prose: no test can tell whether a recovery narrative is a good one, and pretending otherwise would be a guard that fires on style." That is correct and is not weakened here. BUT THAT SENTENCE WAS NOT A NARRATIVE, IT WAS A MEASUREMENT, and this project already has a rule for those. `measured-rate-travels-with-its-script`: a figure may be cited only if the producing script is committed alongside. The 6658 named no producer, because nothing in the repository performed a clone at all -- which is exactly how it survived being false. So a suite-shaped figure in the newest block must now name a script. The paragraph is the unit, not the sentence, because a figure and its producer are routinely a sentence apart and demanding them in one would fire on correct prose. 2 tests, with the anti-vacuity case that the block carries figures at all. MUTATION VERIFIED: reinstating the exact historical sentence turns it red and the failure quotes the figure by name. The block is rewritten and current -- HEAD d33647d, 81 DONE of 92, the staging defect, the citation corruption, the --help class, panel round 14, the mirroring and the cost-control correction -- and every figure in it names its producer. The operational tracker's resume pointer was 28 hours stale, naming HEAD efbaf8a and predating this whole session. It is the file the project CLAUDE.md names as FIRST READ on compaction, so that is the V5 fault in the other document. Now current. AND THE NOTE-LINT GATE REFUSED THIS COMMIT ONCE, correctly: the tracker text added 1 UNNAMED SUBJECT finding, 15 -> 16, on the phrase "the mechanism". The sentence now names cc2's `git merge-file` and fable's zero-context `git apply --cached` instead. Back to 15, which is HEAD's count. title: A8: the whole decision is now 20 files and 1.63 MB, and the question was wrong
verbatim: A8: the whole decision is now 20 files and 1.63 MB, and the question was wrong A8 asks whether 23 cited `bench/logs/` paths should be tracked, relocated, or accepted-and-labelled. `.gitignore:41` excludes that directory by design -- it was 353 MB across 5,840 files -- so RELOCATE CANNOT MAKE A CITED PATH TRACKED: the note still names the original and the original stays excluded. Measured: mirroring every review record moved the untracked count not at all. RECOVERABILITY is the property that matters, and scripts/resolve_cited_evidence_2026-09-11.py measures it. Over every cited bench/logs path: recoverable from the tree : 167 of 215 = 77.6744% Wilson 95% : [71.6500%, 82.7272%] Clopper-Pearson 95% : [71.5125%, 83.0563%] tracked directly : 138 via a mirrored copy : 29 OF THE 48 THAT ARE NOT, 28 ARE ABSENT HERE TOO -- `round_XX.json` and `exp42_.../round7.json` are ellipsis templates and worked examples, citations to nothing at all. THE RESIDUE A RULING IS ABOUT IS THE OTHER 20: cited, present on this machine, in no commit -- **9.3023%, Wilson [6.1026%, 13.9308%], Clopper-Pearson [5.7750%, 14.0009%]** (statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 0.0e+00), totalling 1.63 MB. They are RUN artefacts -- simulation checkpoints, immune pipeline logs, the build experiment's CY_LIVE.log, target-mutation snapshots -- not review records, so the review mirror correctly excludes them and widening its glob would be the wrong fix. WHY THE RESOLVER EXISTS AT ALL. The recommendation on A8 is to LEAVE the citations, because a note records where an artefact was PRODUCED. That is only defensible if a reader can get from the citation to the copy -- recoverable is not the same as DISCOVERABLE -- so the route had to exist before the recommendation could stand. THE RATCHET DOES NOT DECIDE THE DISPOSITION, which is the founder's. Whatever he rules, new cited evidence may not join the unrecoverable set silently. bench/tests/test_cited_evidence_is_recoverable_2026-09-11.py, 8 tests, 2 mutations verified red: lowering the bound by 1 turns the ratchet red, and disabling the mirror lookup turns the anti-vacuity control red -- without that second one the ratchet would be measuring only what git tracks and the whole relocation half would be untested. A CRASH FOUND BY GIVING THE MIRROR A SECOND CALLER. bench/logs/exp36_evidence_latest is a dangling symlink, and mirror_panel_records' date fallback called `f.stat()` over `iterdir()` unguarded, so it died on it. "An addition nothing reaches is not additive" has a second half: the caller is what finds the defect. A dangling link is a legitimate state in an archive, not an error to propagate. It refuses outside a git checkout rather than reporting everything untracked -- the fabricated-figure defect panel round 12 found in overstated_entries, where `git ls-files --error-unmatch` exiting 128 was read as "untracked" and produced "11 of 11 = 100.0000%" with three confidence intervals on it. title: Panel round 14: the full unfiltered record, as the directive requires
verbatim: Panel round 14: the full unfiltered record, as the directive requires The Personalisation directive requires external review output preserved "in full and in unfiltered format" and says "Never summarise in place of the full output". Round 4 has such a note; rounds 5 to 14 did not. This is round 14's. Both seat replies reproduced verbatim inside `verbatim-begin`/`verbatim-end` regions -- the mechanism task V8 built for exactly this collision, since the note linter is BLOCKING at commit time and a verbatim panel record routinely contains findings in the seats' own prose. **V8's MECHANISM WORKED AND THE GATE STILL REFUSED THIS COMMIT ONCE — CORRECTLY, AND MY FIRST READING OF WHY WAS WRONG.** The linter reported 1 finding inside a verbatim region, "reported and NOT counted", and separately counted 1. I read the refusal as the exemption failing to reach the hook, which would have meant V8's central claim was false in the path that matters. It is not: there were TWO findings. cc2's, inside its own quoted words, was correctly exempt. The counted one was in MY prose -- "the seats disagreed on the mechanism", an UNNAMED SUBJECT under Rule 19, and the same phrase the gate caught in the tracker an hour earlier. The sentence now names cc2's `git merge-file` and fable's zero-context `git apply --cached`. 0 counted, 1 reported, committed with neither seat's words altered. That is the exemption doing precisely what it was built to do: a note cannot buy amnesty for its own writing by quoting someone, which is the load-bearing test in V8's own file. The note states what CC1 DID with the findings BEFORE reproducing them, so a reader cannot mistake the summary for the record: 5 distinct defects, 3 found by both seats independently -- 60.0000%, Wilson [23.0724%, 88.2379%]; cc2 found nothing fable missed and fable found 2 more; and the mechanism disagreement settled at gap 1, where merge-file conflicts and zero-context apply succeeds. The raw directory is gitignored, so the note names the byte-identical committed copy under experimental_notes/evidence/ and the test that keeps it there. title: Panel rounds 11, 12 and 13: the full unfiltered records, and a mechanism for the rest
verbatim: Panel rounds 11, 12 and 13: the full unfiltered records, and a mechanism for the rest Round 4's FULL RECORD was written by hand on 2026-09-10, and rounds 5 to 14 then had none -- because writing one by hand is an ACT and an act does not repeat. Measured 2026-09-11: 78 review directories, 10 with a record. scripts/make_panel_full_record_2026-09-11.py builds one from the seats' own replies. It CANNOT write the context -- what was reviewed, why, and what was done with the findings -- so that arrives on stdin rather than being generated, and the script's docstring says so rather than implying coverage it lacks. THE 3 ROUNDS WRITTEN ARE THE ONES WHOSE FINDINGS ARE LOAD-BEARING TODAY. Round 11 broke task V8's scoping claim, from both seats independently, and is the FIRST round with real seat independence -- until task A20 landed that day every seat shared one writable sandbox and in round 10 one seat read another's edits. Round 12 found task V2's instrument fabricating "11 of 11 = 100.0000%" with three confidence intervals wherever git could not answer, the exact inversion of the truth and the same defect a seat had found one round earlier in another script written the same day. Round 13 found the gate that could not fail moving from e4 to e3 INSIDE the commit that removed it from e4, and established the fact that bears on the founder's A19 ruling: with the flag ON, this project's own archived shell-injection exploit still scores sk=1.0000 ADMISSIBLE. Every seat reply sits inside a `verbatim-begin`/`verbatim-end` region -- V8's mechanism, without which the only way to commit a record is to edit what the models said. It holds at scale: the round-13 note is 40,558 bytes with 7 findings inside verbatim regions, reported and NOT counted, and 0 counted. A PAID ROUND IS NAMED, NOT ELIDED. 16 of the 78 directories hold a paid seat reply, all dated 2026-09-05 or earlier, and the builder says so where it is true rather than printing the free-seat line unconditionally. title: The record builder rejected an unknown flag without naming it
verbatim: The record builder rejected an unknown flag without naming it `test_an_unknown_flag_is_rejected_loudly` went red on scripts/make_panel_full_record_2026-09-11.py and I committed over it, because that file is not in the pre-commit GUARDS list. Fixed here rather than left. THE CAUSE. With the 3 positionals REQUIRED, argparse reports the missing positionals BEFORE it reports an unrecognised flag, so `--this-flag-does-not-exist` produced "the following arguments are required" and never the words "unrecognized arguments". The flag WAS rejected, with exit 2 -- but the guard checks the MESSAGE, and it is right to: a script that refuses without saying what it refused teaches the caller nothing, and this project's whole complaint about the 118-day no-op is that an unrecognised argument must be visibly unrecognised. The positionals are now optional to argparse and validated immediately after parsing, so the unknown flag is what gets named. Measured on all 3 paths: `--this-flag-does-not-exist` exits 2 with "unrecognized arguments", no arguments exits 2 with "round_dir, title and out_name are all required", and `--help` exits 0. title: A flake in the clone suite, recorded as OBSERVED and made diagnosable
verbatim: A flake in the clone suite, recorded as OBSERVED and made diagnosable `test_falsifier_cannot_read_the_key.py::test_the_artefact_classifier_cannot_excuse_a_real_escape` failed once in a full clone run at 287c4ff. It has since passed in a second full clone run of the same size (7074 passed), in a 3,011-test slice of the same clone, in isolation, and in a full working-tree run (7100 passed). WHY A FLAKE MATTERS HERE BEYOND THE TEST. Task A2's whole claim is that a reader who clones sees what the maintainer sees. A non-deterministic failure does not make that claim false -- it makes it UNVERIFIABLE, which is worse, because a green clone then proves nothing. READING THE SOURCE PRODUCED NO MECHANISM, and I stopped rather than inventing one. `_names_this_checkout` does ask the filesystem -- `(REPO / tail).exists()` -- which is a real dependence on live state. But the suffixes actually probed for the failing cases are REPO/Users/someone/.ssh/id_rsa, REPO/someone/.ssh/id_rsa, REPO/.ssh/id_rsa and REPO/etc/passwd, and no test in this suite creates any of them. Guessing past that is what `execute-do-not-grep` exists to stop. SO THE FAILURE NOW PRINTS ITS OWN CAUSE. The classifier's answer depends on 2 pieces of state a bare AssertionError does not show: the project names it resolved and where they came from, and whether any probed suffix EXISTS under the repository root. Both are captured in the assertion message, so a recurrence is diagnosable from the log instead of needing to be caught in the act. Verified by mutation -- forgiving every violation produces the message with all 4 fields populated: AssertionError: [('a path outside the declared target', '/Users/someone/.ssh/id_rsa')] was forgiven ... project names : ['Constraint_Engineering'] name source : declared repo root : /Users/.../Constraint_Engineering suffix probes : {'Users/someone/.ssh/id_rsa': False, ...} Recorded as I38 in the issues log, MEDIUM, with the run counts rather than a diagnosis. One observation in 4 full-size runs is not a defect anyone can fix. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: Entry 0.1: the Wolfram observation is made, and the answer is NOT YET with nothing broken
verbatim: Entry 0.1: the Wolfram observation is made, and the answer is NOT YET with nothing broken The entry was DEFERRED to 2026-09-11 because that is the earliest the observation could be made. It is that day. The check it specified: has `$LicenseExpirationDate` moved, and has the licence file been rewritten. NEITHER HAS. `~/Library/WolframEngine/Licensing/mathpass` is 125 bytes with birth time and mtime both still 2026-08-02T21:09:38 -- byte-for-byte the state the entry recorded when it was written, so the file has still never been rewritten. `$LicenseExpirationDate` returns DateObject[{2026, 9, 11}, Day], which is today, unmoved. AND THE ENGINE STILL COMPUTES, which is the half that decides whether anything is actually wrong. A licence date is not a capability check, so 4 calls were made rather than 1: $LicenseExpirationDate DateObject[{2026, 9, 11}, Day] $LicenseType Professional Integrate[x^2 Log[x], {x, 0, 1}] -1/9 N[Zeta[3], 20] 1.20205690315959428539973816151104025515 Cross-verified per the 2-tool rule: SymPy gives -1/9 and mpmath's quadrature agrees to 0.0e+00; zeta(3) agrees with SymPy and mpmath to 15 decimal places. THE FOUNDER'S READING IS NOT YET CONTRADICTED. Wolfram's own text says reactivation happens "when the actual date is close to the expiration date", and 09:37 ON the expiration date is inside that window rather than past it. His ruling was to leave it to auto-renew and observe on the day; the observation is that it has not renewed yet and nothing has stopped working. THE QUESTION BECOMES REAL only if the date has still not moved once today has passed, or if a call starts failing. A re-check is owed then and it is the same 3 measurements. 0 stale MCP-spawned kernels were running, checked FIRST, because .claude/CLAUDE.md records that kernel contention reads as a licence fault and is not one. `$LicenseType` is recorded with its standing caution: that string must never be quoted as a right this project holds. title: Panel rounds 5 to 10: the full unfiltered records, completing the numbered set
verbatim: Panel rounds 5 to 10: the full unfiltered records, completing the numbered set Rounds 4 and 11 to 14 had records; 5 to 10 did not. All 10 numbered rounds now do, built by scripts/make_panel_full_record_2026-09-11.py from the seats' own replies, every one inside a `verbatim-begin`/`verbatim-end` region so not a byte of any seat's words had to be altered to commit them. 0 counted findings in all 6. EACH CARRIES THE CAUTION THAT APPLIES TO IT, which is the part a reader needs most. Until task A20 landed on 2026-09-11 every seat shared ONE writable sandbox and they ran concurrently, and seats are instructed to write fixes into that tree at real paths -- so agreement between seats in rounds 5 to 10 is NOT evidence of independence. Round 10 is where that was proved rather than suspected: fable's reply describes the `.zenodo.json` identity tier cc2 had just invented, and its own figures section records reading a stale `.pyc` from the pre-fix module. It reviewed cc2's edited tree, not the tree under review. WHAT THE ROUNDS FOUND, all of it against CC1's own work: 5 and 6 Both returned 0 source files -- a HARNESS defect, not a seat defect: panel_sandbox.teardown destroyed the fixes before `changes()` ran. Round 7's brief opens with the delivery rule written in response. 7 The seats' patch found 2 holes in mine, the worst a declared figure whose script path began `../` and executed a script OUTSIDE the repository, accepting its output as evidence. 8 A maximally-selected statistic reported as a single test -- 17 candidate cuts, corrected to Bonferroni p = 3.738445e-13 with a permutation test at p <= 4.9975e-04; "dead" overstated, since the most recent attempt SUCCEEDED; and a control of mine that was a tautology, asserting score_isomorphism(s, s) == 1.0 and surviving destruction of the function it guarded. 9 "A figure only one party can compute is a vote, not a tool result" -- neither seat could re-run either declared figure, because both need a git repository and the sandbox has none. 10 The rebase laundered a `..` escape past the static guard and fable read /etc/passwd through it, 9,344 bytes. The other seat reasoned about that exact path and judged it below threshold; fable executed the attack instead and was right. title: Every panel round run under Section P now has a FULL RECORD, and a ratchet holds it
verbatim: Every panel round run under Section P now has a FULL RECORD, and a ratchet holds it Rounds 4 and 11 to 14 had records; 5 to 10 got them an hour ago; the roster-fix round, the roster round 2 and the verification-gap round had none. All 14 rounds dispatched on or after the Section P ruling of 2026-09-09 now have one. MEASURED BEFORE THE GUARD: 10 of 14 -- 71.4286%, Wilson [45.3509%, 88.2786%], Clopper-Pearson [41.8965%, 91.6111%]. Now 14 of 14. AND MY OWN MEASUREMENT PRODUCED A FALSE ZERO FIRST. It searched the first 4,000 characters of each note, and a record names its source directory in the closing "Where the raw record lives" section -- past that window -- so it reported 0 of 14 covered when the true figure was 10. The same shape as everything else this session: a scanner that resolves 1 form and reports zero for the other. Round 4's hand-written note genuinely did name no directory at all, and now does. THE RATCHET IS SCOPED TO THE RULING, NOT TO THE ARCHIVE. 78 directories hold review output and most predate the condition that a record be written; demanding a note for a confer run from May would be asking the past to have been the present. TWO SCOPING ERRORS IN THE FOOT-LINE RULE, BOTH CAUGHT BY THE TEST GOING RED ON ITS OWN FIRST RUNS, and both the same error at different widths. It demanded v1.7, when the standard says "Notes written under earlier versions retain their version-specific foot-lines" and 4 records legitimately end with v1.4. Then it demanded a foot-line at all, when 4 records PREDATE the convention and the standard says a missing one "flags a note that predates or violates the standard". Adding v1.7 to a note from August would misdate it, and editing an archival record to satisfy a checker is the act task V8 exists to prevent. So 2 rules where there was 1: IF a foot-line is present it must be the final content, for every record; and a record documenting a post-ruling round must CARRY one. 3 mutations verified red -- a deleted record, a foot-line with prose after it, and a post-ruling record with none. Also asserts a record is a RECORD: a note carrying no verbatim region and short enough to be a summary fails, because a summary would satisfy a name-matching check and defeat the directive it exists to serve. title: P3 and P5's archive-wide figures were over a partial archive, and P5's instrument read a rename as abandonment
verbatim: P3 and P5's archive-wide figures were over a partial archive, and P5's instrument read a rename as abandonment Both entries quoted figures from `panel_condition_compliance_2026-09-10.py`, which globbed `panel_*` -- 46 of the 78 directories holding review output. P3 IS STRONGER THAN IT RECORDED. Over all 78: under the ruling **28 of 28 = 100.0000%**, Wilson [87.9357%, 100.0000%], Clopper-Pearson [87.6564%, 100.0000%] -- 14 rounds now rather than 5 -- against **8 of 134 = 5.9701%** before it, Wilson [3.0559%, 11.3385%]. **Fisher exact p = 1.495245e-24, odds ratio infinite**, cross-checked by chi-square with Yates at p = 2.051864e-26. The archive-wide rate is 36 of 162 = 22.2222%, not 22 of 84 = 26.1905%. P5'S INSTRUMENT WAS READING A RENAMED FIELD AS NON-COMPLIANCE. The brief asked for `strongest_disagreement` up to round 7 and for "WHERE I DISAGREE WITH THE OTHER SEAT OR WITH CC1" from round 8. Of the 28 seat replies dispatched under the ruling: 12 carry the old field, 14 the new, 2 neither -- and the 2 are `panel_roster_fix_2026-09-09`, which the entry already names as the only round dispatched before the field existed. So the scan reported 12 of 28 = 42.8571% and apparently FALLING, when the figure is **26 of 28 = 92.8571%**, Wilson [77.3546%, 98.0188%], Clopper-Pearson [76.4965%, 99.1230%], and 28 of 28 discuss disagreement in prose. P5 IS A FOUNDER CONDITION -- no compelled convergence -- so an instrument that reads a rename as abandonment would have shown the panel giving up the very property the `pr` protocol exists to protect. AND THE RULE LIVED IN 2 PLACES, OF WHICH ONLY 1 WAS REPAIRED. That is the actual defect and it is worth more than the figure. bench/tests/test_panel_conditions_are_met_2026-09-10.py ALREADY carried the wider pattern, and its own comment records why: "BROKENED BY MY OWN BRIEF, 2026-09-10. This matched `strongest[_ ]disagreement` only ... A guard keyed to a literal phrase, checking a requirement that each brief states in its own words, is the substring-versus-token defect wearing a different hat." So the GUARD knew about the rename and the SCRIPT did not -- and the script is what produces the figure the founder reads, while the guard only ever answers pass or fail. That is why the guard stayed green at 42.8571% and at 92.8571% alike: it was never wrong. A rule written down twice and repaired once is the shape `execute-do-not-grep` names, and it is the same defect as `orphan_figures` against `overstated_entries` one round earlier. Both now match both field names. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: P3 and P5's archive-wide figures were over a partial archive, and P5's instrument read a rename as abandonment
verbatim: P3 and P5's archive-wide figures were over a partial archive, and P5's instrument read a rename as abandonment Both entries quoted figures from `panel_condition_compliance_2026-09-10.py`, which globbed `panel_*` -- 46 of the 78 directories holding review output. P3 IS STRONGER THAN IT RECORDED. Over all 78: under the ruling **28 of 28 = 100.0000%**, Wilson [87.9357%, 100.0000%], Clopper-Pearson [87.6564%, 100.0000%] -- 14 rounds now rather than 5 -- against **8 of 134 = 5.9701%** before it, Wilson [3.0559%, 11.3385%]. **Fisher exact p = 1.495245e-24, odds ratio infinite**, cross-checked by chi-square with Yates at p = 2.051864e-26. The archive-wide rate is 36 of 162 = 22.2222%, not 22 of 84 = 26.1905%. P5'S INSTRUMENT WAS READING A RENAMED FIELD AS NON-COMPLIANCE. The brief asked for `strongest_disagreement` up to round 7 and for "WHERE I DISAGREE WITH THE OTHER SEAT OR WITH CC1" from round 8. Of the 28 seat replies dispatched under the ruling: 12 carry the old field, 14 the new, 2 neither -- and the 2 are `panel_roster_fix_2026-09-09`, which the entry already names as the only round dispatched before the field existed. So the scan reported 12 of 28 = 42.8571% and apparently FALLING, when the figure is **26 of 28 = 92.8571%**, Wilson [77.3546%, 98.0188%], Clopper-Pearson [76.4965%, 99.1230%], and 28 of 28 discuss disagreement in prose. P5 IS A FOUNDER CONDITION -- no compelled convergence -- so an instrument that reads a rename as abandonment would have shown the panel giving up the very property the `pr` protocol exists to protect. AND THE RULE LIVED IN 2 PLACES, OF WHICH ONLY 1 WAS REPAIRED. That is the actual defect and it is worth more than the figure. bench/tests/test_panel_conditions_are_met_2026-09-10.py ALREADY carried the wider pattern, and its own comment records why: "BROKENED BY MY OWN BRIEF, 2026-09-10. This matched `strongest[_ ]disagreement` only ... A guard keyed to a literal phrase, checking a requirement that each brief states in its own words, is the substring-versus-token defect wearing a different hat." So the GUARD knew about the rename and the SCRIPT did not -- and the script is what produces the figure the founder reads, while the guard only ever answers pass or fail. That is why the guard stayed green at 42.8571% and at 92.8571% alike: it was never wrong. A rule written down twice and repaired once is the shape `execute-do-not-grep` names, and it is the same defect as `orphan_figures` against `overstated_entries` one round earlier. Both now match both field names. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: The paid-seat guard could not see a paid dispatch outside one naming convention
verbatim: The paid-seat guard could not see a paid dispatch outside one naming convention P1's guard asserts "no paid seat was dispatched in any round under Section P". That is a MONEY guard, on the category the founder reserves to himself. Its population was `bench/logs/panel_*/*.json` -- 46 of the 78 directories that hold review output -- and it additionally required `"route" in d`. BOTH NARROWINGS POINT THE SAME WAY: AT HIDING SPENDING. 1. The other 32 directories are the `confer_*`, `severity_*`, `track_record_*`, `bugzilla_*`, `independent_*` and `pr_*` reviews, and 12 of them hold paid seat replies. A paid dispatch into a differently-named directory was invisible. 2. 20 of the 30 paid-named seat files in the archive record NO route field -- 66.6667%, Wilson [48.7801%, 80.7695%] -- every one from the older confer harness. Dropping them made the guard blind to precisely the rounds most likely to have cost money. DEMONSTRATED, NOT ARGUED. A paid reply planted in a post-ruling `confer_*` directory: the OLD guard returns 2 passed both with no route field and with `route: "openrouter"`. The new one fails with `a paid seat was dispatched under the ruling: [('confer_probe_2026-09-10', 'codex')]`. AND THE RULING FILTER WORKED BY ACCIDENT OF NAMING. `UNDER_P = "2026-09-"` is a SUBSTRING test on the directory name. Post-ruling rounds are dated with dashes (`panel_round11_2026-09-11`) and pre-ruling September rounds with the compact form (`panel_maths_20260905T032107Z`), which contains no `2026-09-` -- so the PAID round of 2026-09-05 fell outside the filter by luck. One directory renamed to the dashed form and a paid round would have been asserted as running under the ruling. Dates are parsed and compared to 2026-09-09 now. The selector is IMPORTED from scripts/mirror_panel_records_2026-09-11.py rather than reimplemented. This file and the compliance script drifting apart is the defect that produced 4 wrong figures today, and a third copy would be a third rule. FOUND BY SWEEPING RATHER THAN BY MEETING IT AGAIN. After correcting the same defect in the cost-control count and in P1, P3 and P5 one at a time, an AST-and- regex sweep asked which scripts select `bench/logs` with a narrow glob AND claim breadth in their prose. 6 hits, 5 of them legitimate -- `r*_*.json` is a reply file within a round -- and this one real. That is `feedback_check_the_whole_set` applied: a universal asserted after checking one member. title: One definition of what a panel round is and when it ran, after briefly having four
verbatim: One definition of what a panel round is and when it ran, after briefly having four Correcting the narrow-population defect in the cost count, P1, P3 and P5 left 4 private copies of the same 2 date regular expressions -- in the compliance script, the Section-P guard, the full-record ratchet and the preservation test -- and 3 copies of "which directory holds review output". All written on 2026-09-11, within an hour, WHILE correcting exactly this defect elsewhere. A rule written down 4 times is 4 rules, and today's own evidence is that copies drift rather than agree. The disagreement-field pattern was repaired in the guard and not in the script. The paid-seat population was widened in the script and not in the guard. Each divergence produced a wrong figure or a blind guard. `scripts/mirror_panel_records_2026-09-11.py` now owns both: `holds_review_output` decides what a review directory is, by CONTENT, and `round_date` parses a round's date in both live conventions. Every other consumer imports them. The compact regex `(20\d{6})T\d{6}Z` now appears in exactly 1 file, verified by git grep. WHY THE DATE PARSER MATTERS AND IS NOT TIDYING. Roughly 30 of the 78 review directories use the compact form, and a parser that knows only the dashed one silently returns None for them. That is how a substring test on "2026-09-" came to separate pre-ruling from post-ruling rounds by luck rather than by design, and it is why the paid round of 2026-09-05 escaped the Section-P filter. MUTATION VERIFIED: deleting the compact branch from the shared parser -- exactly the blind spot that was there before -- turns 2 anti-vacuity guards red. The consolidation is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. A SWEEP I DID NOT ACT ON, recorded because the decision is the point. Generalising the narrow-population check to "any non-recursive glob over a tree with subdirectories" returned 78 files, nearly all false positives: the heuristic pairs any glob in a file with any tree named anywhere in it, and `r*_*.json` is a reply file within a round, not a narrow population. An instrument that fires on the ordinary case is the defect this project names as teaching people to ignore the alarm, so it was discarded rather than shipped. The precise version -- one predicate for "is this a review round", imported everywhere -- is what landed. title: The clone at 5962a04 failed 6 tests, and my premise about clones was wrong
verbatim: The clone at 5962a04 failed 6 tests, and my premise about clones was wrong MY EARLIER CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED EVERYWHERE IT WAS WRITTEN. I said a clone has no `bench/logs/` at all, because `.gitignore:41` excludes it. **6,462 files under it are TRACKED**, committed before that rule took effect, and a clone carries 159 subdirectories. WHAT IS TRUE IS NARROWER AND SHARPER. Of the 78 directories holding review output, **64 were wholly untracked -- 82.0513%, Wilson [72.0976%, 88.9961%], Clopper-Pearson [71.7227%, 89.8251%]** -- and of the 14 that survive a clone, **0 is a post-ruling round**. Every panel round run under Section P was recoverable by no commit. **None was PARTIALLY tracked**, which is the one good thing: a half-tracked record looks present and is incomplete. FOUR OF THE SIX FAILURES WERE MINE, AND ALL FOUR WERE WORKING-TREE FACTS DRESSED AS UNIVERSALS. scripts/resolve_cited_evidence_2026-09-11.py computed a mirror's path from the ORIGINAL directory under bench/logs -- absent in a clone for every relocated record -- so it reported "no mirror" for all of them and only ever worked on this machine. THE A2 DEFECT CLASS INSIDE THE TOOL BUILT TO CLOSE A2: an instrument that reads what the maintainer has rather than what a reader has. The mirror is TRACKED, so it is found by searching the tracked tree now. test_panel_records_are_preserved asserted absolute round counts (>= 70, >= 20) and skipped only when bench/logs was empty. It is never empty. The skip is on the POST-RULING population, which is the population every comparison is about, and the thresholds follow it. THE THIRD WAS A SELECTOR ASYMMETRY THE MIRROR MADE LIVE. `_v17_notes()` globs `*.md` recursively; `_revision_declaring()` asked git grep for the foot-line across `experimental_notes/` with NO extension filter. Committing 364 mirrored files put 2 `seat_proposals.diff` into the tree -- a seat's proposed patch whose diff body contains a note's foot-line -- so HEAD declared 52 notes against the working tree's 50 and the comparison failed in a clean clone. The 2 extra were diffs, not notes. That file's own docstring says "THE SELECTOR IS IMPORTED, NOT RETYPED (`execute-do-not-grep`)", and it is -- for the live half. The HEAD half retyped the POPULATION instead of the pattern. Two expressions of "which files are notes", only 1 of them imported. Mutation verified: dropping the filter again turns it red. THE SIXTH IS I38 AND IT IS NO LONGER A ONE-OFF. test_the_artefact_classifier_cannot_excuse_a_real_escape has now failed in 2 of 5 full-size runs, both in clones, and passes in the working tree and in isolation. The diagnostics that print the classifier's resolved state landed AFTER this run, so this occurrence captured none. The next one will. title: Closing report for 2026-09-11, TTS and markdown
verbatim: Closing report for 2026-09-11, TTS and markdown `tts-output-protocol` requires a spoken-form file after each significant arc, mirrored as readable markdown in the repository. Nothing had been written today and the morning has been substantial. WHAT IT COVERS, in the founder's own reading register -- technical, not simplified, no project concepts explained back to the person who designed them: A2's completion claim was false and nothing in the project could have seen it, because nothing performed a clone. 3 failures against 6952 passes in a clone, 0 in the working copy. The cause: commit-time repairs wrote the working files and never staged what they wrote, so every commit shipped the unrepaired version and the repair sat 1 commit behind, permanently. The probe that proved the fix destroyed 3 correct line references, which reached the permanent record and were restored. 30 of 53 measurement scripts never answered a request for usage information -- 56.6038%, Wilson [43.2654%, 69.0496%] -- and 2 of them were among the clone's 3 failures. Now 0 of 54. Panel round 14: 5 defects, 3 found by both seats independently, and a mechanism disagreement settled by measurement rather than argument. 64 of 78 review directories existed on 1 machine and in no commit -- 82.0513%, Wilson [72.0976%, 88.9961%]. All 78 preserved now. The paid-dispatch count was 30 and reported 10, and the guard asserting it was blind in the same 2 ways. The conclusion is unchanged: last paid dispatch 2026-09-05, 0 of the 24 rounds since. The recurring shape of the whole morning, stated once: an instrument that recognises 1 form of a thing and reports a confident zero for the other. The cost of that shape is that it always returns the reassuring answer. What remains open, and both are decisions rather than work. Two things recorded honestly rather than closed: the test that has failed twice in 5 full-size runs with no mechanism found, and the Wolfram licence observation, made at 09:37 with the date unmoved and the engine still computing correctly. Checked before delivery, per the founder's 2026-09-04 ruling that a spelled-number finding is blocking rather than advisory: `note_vagueness_lint.py` reports 0 findings on both files, and a formatting check confirms 0 hash headings, 0 asterisks, 0 backticks, 0 em-dashes, 0 bullets, 0 pipe tables and 0 bracket links in the spoken-form file. title: 8 committed scripts are reached by nothing, and scripts had no reachability ratchet
verbatim: 8 committed scripts are reached by nothing, and scripts had no reachability ratchet The additive standard's symmetric half: "an addition that nothing reaches is not additive either". `test_additive_standard_2026-09-07.py` ratchets config fields nothing READS. Scripts had no equivalent, and this project's record holds 11 confirmed defects that were additions doing nothing. MEASURED: **111 of 119 scripts are reached -- 93.2773%, Wilson [87.2935%, 96.5544%], Clopper-Pearson [87.1830%, 97.0531%]**. REACHED MEANS 3 THINGS, because a script can be legitimate with no caller: something CALLS it; a note CITES it as a figure's producer, which `measured-rate-travels-with-its-script` requires; or a canonical document names it as a command to run. The 8 satisfy none of the 3. THE FIRST FIGURE WAS FLATTERING AND THE CAUSE MATTERS. A first pass counted mentions inside `experimental_notes/evidence/*/seat_proposals.diff` -- archival copies of what reviewing models proposed, committed that same morning -- and reported 5 unreached instead of 8. All 8 appear there. **The better number came from the review record being filed, not from anything calling those scripts. A measurement that improves when you file your paperwork is measuring the filing.** NOTHING WAS DELETED, deliberately. The removal clause requires a committed measurement that a replacement dominates on a named property, and none exists for any of these; deleting a measurement script also risks breaking `measured-rate-travels-with-its-script` for a figure quoted where the scan cannot see. Parked for the founder, as `update_drift` was under I31. 7 tests. The ratchet refuses a NEW unreached script AND refuses a STALE entry in the list, so the bound cannot loosen by leaving slack in it. 2 mutations verified red: dropping the archival exclusion turns the staleness check red, and adding an orphan script turns the ratchet red by name. title: The record of the orphans declared them non-orphans, and the first fix deleted a real caller
verbatim: The record of the orphans declared them non-orphans, and the first fix deleted a real caller `unreached()` asks whether any tracked file mentions a script. Committing the ratchet put its own 8 orphan paths into a tracked file, so the figure went from 111 of 119 to 120 of 120 within 8 minutes of publishing it. A ratchet whose record of the orphans makes them non-orphans measures nothing. THE FIRST FIX OVER-CORRECTED and is the more interesting half. It excluded 3 WHOLE FILES, one of them the test -- which carries 0 roll-call lines and genuinely runs the script. Throwing the file away threw away a real caller, and the count read 111 of 120 with THIS script as the 9th orphan: the instrument reported itself unreached because the fix had deleted its only caller. Same defect class as the one being fixed, one level up. `_ROLL_CALL` now drops the roll-call LINES and keeps the files, so every other line still counts. 112 of 120 = 93.3333%, Wilson [87.3949%, 96.5835%], Clopper-Pearson [87.2863%, 97.0781%] -- both intervals cross-checked by 2 tools (statsmodels against a 50-digit mpmath Wilson closed form; statsmodels `beta` against `scipy.stats.beta`). `TestTheExclusionListCannotHide` holds the list to files that demonstrably carry a roll call, so a name cannot be added to make an inconvenient orphan vanish. MUTATION-TESTED, 3 mutations, each killed by a different test: whole-file exclusion incl. the test -> 3 fail (the over-correction) SELF_REFERENTIAL handling removed -> test_the_recorded_set_is_still_accurate an innocent file added to the list -> test_every_self_referential_file_carries_a_roll_call 10 passed restored. title: A clone's suite overwrote the founder's Desktop copy, and a guard blocked on a panel seat's own words
verbatim: A clone's suite overwrote the founder's Desktop copy, and a guard blocked on a panel seat's own words 3 defects, all found by measurement rather than by reading, all the session's recurring shape: 2 consumers of 1 rule where only 1 resolves it. 1. A CLONE WROTE ~/Desktop. `scripts/cdsfl_recover.py` reported the Desktop copy of CDSFL_OUTCOMES_LOG.md diverged by 6,413 bytes and NEWER than the repository copy. The flake clone's own copy is 27,669 bytes against the working tree's 34,082 -- the same 6,413 -- so the file the founder actually reads had been replaced by an older one. The pre-commit mirror refresh put it back 13 minutes later; that was luck. `DESKTOP = Path.home() / "Desktop"` is absolute while `REPO` is not, so any clone or scratch fixture copies the wrong source over the right destination. Task A2's shape exactly. ATTRIBUTED BY EXECUTION: 43 candidate test files run under a fake HOME holding sentinels; exactly 1 rewrote them -- test_precommit_guard::test_a_commit_is_refused_in_a_clone_of_this_actual_repository. `refuse_reason()` refuses under pytest or from a repo under the temp root, and both rules are needed: the environment IS inherited through git into the hook, but that file's own test_no_python3 builds a PATH holding only git. It keys on the PASSWD home, not `Path.home()` -- the drills fake $HOME on purpose, so under a faked $HOME the 2 are the same path and a drill is indistinguishable from an escape. Asking "is this HIS Desktop" instead of "is this A Desktop". 2. A GUARD BLOCKED ON A SEAT'S WORDS. The full suite failed on Panel_Roster_Round2_FULL_RECORD_2026-09-09.md at line 290 -- inside `<!-- verbatim-begin: fable -->`, which task V8 exists to protect. The CLI subtracted `verbatim_paragraphs()`; test_note_standard_v17_enforced called `lint()` raw and subtracted nothing. `partition()` now owns the split and `main` CALLS it, so there is 1 implementation, not 2 asserted to agree. 3. A BARE SUBSTRING MATCHED A VERB. `"the decay curve measure" in low` fires on "measureS" and "measureMENT". MEASURED over 402 notes: 28 substring matches, 27 bounded. The fix drops exactly 1 and it is that verb. 2 and 3 are INDEPENDENT: the NOUN form inside a verbatim region is still reported by lint() and not counted by blocking(). 4. test_future_timestamp_guard grepped for the literal `future_stamp(p)` and false-alarmed when the call moved and its variable was renamed. It now RUNS the reporter. Dominance measured, both forms against 2 module states: call present/renamed -> grep FAIL, executing PASS; call deleted -> both FAIL. MUTATION-TESTED, 7 mutations, each killed: partition stops subtracting -> 2 fail bare substring restored -> 2 fail matcher made vacuous -> 5 fail pytest rule dropped -> 1 fail temp-root rule dropped -> 1 fail refuse everything -> 6 fail Path.home() instead of passwd -> 1 fail (the drill) 548 passed across the 12 affected files. title: Writing the verbatim marker in prose silently stopped the linter for the rest of the file
verbatim: Writing the verbatim marker in prose silently stopped the linter for the rest of the file FOUND BY WRITING TODAY'S OUTCOMES ENTRY. Describing the begin-marker inside single backticks opened a REAL region in CDSFL_OUTCOMES_LOG.md. Nothing closed it, so 12 paragraphs from there to end of file stopped being linted -- measured, not inferred. An exemption reports nothing when it swallows a file, which is what makes this shape expensive: the checker stays green while checking less. 2 INDEPENDENT REPAIRS. 1. `_strip_quoted` treats an INLINE code span as quoted, exactly as `_strip_fenced` already treated a fenced block. The fenced rule was already right about shown-versus-used markers; it simply did not reach inline code. `_strip_fenced` is untouched and still called. 2. An unbalanced begin/end pair is a COUNTED finding, prepended so the region it describes cannot exempt the report about it. Counted with the SAME scanner the exemption uses, so the guard and the exemption cannot disagree about what a marker is -- the defect fixed one commit ago, not repeated here. MEASURED across 402 notes: 0 carry an unbalanced region. The new check therefore blocks nothing that exists today, which is exactly why its positive control carries the weight rather than the corpus figure. test_verbatim_regions_are_not_linted's own docstring asked for this: it said the swallow "must be a known property rather than a surprise" while asserting only `_counted(out) == 0`, which pinned the surprise. It now pins both halves -- the quoted violation is still not counted (unchanged, the safe direction) AND the structure is announced. MUTATION-TESTED, 3 mutations, each killed by the right test: inline spans not stripped -> test_a_marker_shown_in_backticks_opens_nothing balance finding dropped -> 2 fail finding moved to exempted -> 2 fail One earlier mutation silently failed to apply and was re-run rather than reported: an unapplied mutation proves nothing. 448 passed across 10 consumers. verbatim: The audit that counted I38's flake had the defect it was counting: 0 failures, and there were 2 I38's row said "1 failure in 4 full-size runs". THE PRODUCER IS COMMITTED AND SO IS ITS EVIDENCE. A BUG THE TESTS FOUND IN THE REFUSAL PATH: `CENSUS.relative_to(REPO)` raises for a census outside the repository, so the "no census" message crashed instead of refusing. title: Panel round 15: both seats broke 2 of my 5 fixes, and I confirmed every bypass by execution
verbatim: Panel round 15: both seats broke 2 of my 5 fixes, and I confirmed every bypass by execution cc2 and fable, free seats only, 0 paid dispatch. Both returned SPLIT, both reproduced their findings, both delivered fixes. Each finding below was re-verified here before being acted on -- `fff-external` applies to a panel seat exactly as to me. 1. THE DESKTOP GUARD FAILED OPEN, WHICH IS THE WORSE DIRECTION. Its first line said "if DESKTOP is not the passwd user's Desktop, this is a drill" and returned None before every other rule. Under `sudo` macOS keeps $HOME while getuid() becomes 0, so the passwd Desktop becomes /var/root/Desktop, the paths differ, and THE GUARD TURNED ITSELF OFF on the highest-privilege run there is -- with the pytest rule and the temp-root rule both dead. Reproduced here: refuse_reason() -> None. Both seats found it independently and both rated it the sharpest finding of the round. Also: a clone OUTSIDE the scratch tree (~/repos, the Desktop, an external drive) passed both rules and replays the original incident exactly; and with TMPDIR unset, gettempdir() returns /tmp so a clone under /var/folders escaped the temp rule entirely. `refuse_reason_for()` now takes every input as an argument, which is what makes those cases testable at all. The drill exemption requires displacement TO SCRATCH rather than mere difference; scratch roots are a resolved SET; unreliable passwd identification fails CLOSED; and a `.cdsfl_canonical_checkout` marker on the Desktop refuses a second checkout by name. This checkout is now registered, and a scratch clone cannot register itself. The remaining limit is STATED in a test rather than hidden: with no marker, a non-scratch clone still gets through. 2. I SHIPPED A TEST THAT WAS RED IN EVERY CLONE. `test_the_founders_own_checkout_is_not_refused` asserted on the live environment, so in any clone under the system temp root -- which is exactly where `fresh_clone_suite` clones -- it failed. Confirmed by cloning to gettempdir() and running it: 1 failed, 20 passed. It was also polluting the I38 flake record, since 6 of 8 censused runs are clones. The property is now checked where it is deterministic. 3. THE REGION GUARD WAS ORDER-BLIND, IN THE GUARD WRITTEN TO END THAT DEFECT. `opens != closes` is a tally, and an unclosed region is a fact about order: a stray `verbatim-end` BEFORE an unclosed `verbatim-begin` gives 1 and 1, so the check said BALANCED while a region was open and exempting to end of file. Worse, `verbatim-end` + `verbatim-begin` in ONE paragraph ended the exemption because a bool-per-paragraph applied `closed` last regardless of position -- so a seat's quoted words were COUNTED, which is the exact V8 defeat. And 2 begins in 1 paragraph read as 1. `region_state()` is one ordered walk and both consumers read it. 4. A RULE 1 VIOLATION COULD BUY ITS OWN AMNESTY. The future-stamp finding was added BEFORE the exempt split while the unbalanced finding was added after, so a note whose first paragraph opens a region exempted its own future timestamp. Both structural findings are now added after the split. 5. THE ROLL-CALL MATCHER HAD THE LIST FORMS IN ITS DOCSTRING AND NOT IN ITS PATTERN. `- scripts/x.py`, `* ...`, `1. ...` and backticked forms all returned False. It worked only because PARKED_FOR_THE_FOUNDER.md happens to use bare indented paths; reformatting that note as a bullet list would have made every orphan read as reached. 6. MY ASYMMETRY TEST STILL MISSED A QUADRANT. fable mutated `vouches` to "both in INSTRUMENT or both out" and all 14 tests stayed green, this one included, because the only direction that flips is an ORDINARY file vouching FOR an instrument and no case covered it. 3 of 4 quadrants is not a decision table. The mutant now dies. 7. THE PANEL HARNESS ITSELF CRASHED AFTER BOTH SEATS REPLIED. `diff -u` under `text=True` raised UnicodeDecodeError on byte 0x91, so `seat_proposals.diff` -- the artefact carrying the seats' FIXES -- was never written. The replies survived on disk. Reproduced with that exact byte; it decodes defensively now. 8. THE CLONE HARNESS DISCARDED THE EVIDENCE IT WAS EXTENDED TO CAPTURE. The I38 flake REPRODUCED at 37cc328 -- the first time since diagnostics were added for exactly that moment -- and the run reported the test's NAME and nothing else. That is why I38 has read OBSERVED rather than diagnosed across 8 runs. The full pytest output is now kept and its path named in the report. I38 re-counted: 3 of 8 full-size runs = 37.5000%, Wilson [13.6844%, 69.4258%], Clopper-Pearson [8.5233%, 75.5137%]. Both seats are right that 8 observations spanning a factor of 5 is a description of 8 runs, not a rate. A TEST OF MINE PINNED AN ABSOLUTE FIGURE OVER A GROWING CORPUS and went red when the census grew -- entry 6.1's lesson, walked into. It now PARSES the figure from the issues log and recomputes it, so producer and note must agree and neither can drift alone. Mutation-verified. Corpus differential for the lint change: 402 notes, 0 whose counted total moved. 535 passed across 16 affected files. verbatim: Adopted the class-level check both seats built, after running it against this tree rather than theirs THE BRIEF'S SECTION 3 ITEM 6 ASKED FOR THE MECHANICAL CHECK THAT WOULD CATCH FALSE ZEROS AS A CLASS RATHER THAN ONE AT A TIME, and both seats built one. The method is metamorphic and it is the right generalisation: take a scanner and an input it answers YES about, apply a transformation that changes the FORM and not the CONTENT, and require the answer not to change. No reading of any regex is involved, which is the point -- 15 instances of this defect were found by reading and the 16th was not prevented by any of those fixes. `scripts/false_zero_probe_2026-09-11.py` imports the REAL scanners and calls them; nothing retypes a pattern, because a retyped pattern proves nothing about the repository's code. Against this tree: 6 scanners, 29 form axes, 0 undeclared false zeros, 2 declared with reasons. Re-planting this morning's anchored matcher makes it report the flip on 3 separate axes. RECOVERED FROM THE SANDBOXES AFTER THE HARNESS CRASH, which is why this is a separate commit: `diff -u` died on a non-UTF-8 byte before writing the proposals artefact, so the seats' files were never captured. The sandboxes survived, and the files were read out of them directly. `fff-external` APPLIES, AND IT EARNED ITS PLACE. The probe raised AttributeError on its first call here: the seat wrote its own `region_state` returning a dataclass, and the one that shipped returns a mapping. An adopted fix is a hypothesis until it has been RUN against the tree it is going into. WHERE THE SEAT'S DESIGN BEAT MINE, IT WAS ADOPTED. `preserve_before_overwrite` is the only rule here about BYTES rather than PATHS, which is why it is right in every case a path rule gets wrong -- and every hole found in the path rules so far was a location they did not anticipate. It converts the one hole still open, a Desktop with no marker written by a clone outside scratch, from silent loss into something recoverable. One hidden slot per mirror, not a growing pile of dated backups on his Desktop, and deliberately not matching `CDSFL_*` so a tool globbing his documents cannot pick it up. MY OWN DOCSTRING OVERSTATED WHAT MY CODE DID. It said unreliable passwd identification "fails closed"; the code only withheld the drill exemption and then returned None. That is true and still the wrong trade for a guard whose failure destroyed a file: failing closed costs a printed refusal on a platform the founder does not use, failing open costs the file. title: Neither the tally nor the ordered walk is sufficient alone, and the mutation proves it
verbatim: Neither the tally nor the ordered walk is sufficient alone, and the mutation proves it REPLACING THE TALLY WAS AN OVER-CORRECTION. The original balance check compared `opens != closes` and missed a stray close before an unclosed open, which balances at 1 and 1. The ordered walk that replaced it then missed 2 begins and 1 end -- ordered-consistent, because regions do not nest so the second begin changes no state and the single end closes, and yet 2 against 1 is malformed. The tally was not WRONG, it was INSUFFICIENT. It is restored beside the other 2 conditions rather than in place of them. MUTATION-PROVED, and this is the whole claim: tally alone -> test_a_stray_close_before_an_unclosed_open_is_reported ordered signals alone -> test_two_opens_in_one_paragraph_are_two_opens Each mutant survives the other's test and dies on its own. 4 GAPS FABLE NAMED THAT THIS TREE DID NOT COVER, written against the signature that shipped rather than ported from its file: a /var/folders clone refused when TMPDIR says /tmp (the refusal end to end, not just the root set); a scratch clone cannot register itself as canonical -- without which the mechanism INVERTS and the clone that caused the incident refuses the founder's own checkout; a future stamp inside a leading region is still counted; and a close-then-open in one paragraph keeps the following seat's words exempt. ONE OF MY OWN CONTROLS COULD NOT PASS. `test_the_founders_checkout_can_register` put the repo under `tmp_path`, which IS scratch, so the guard refused it -- correctly, and the test was wrong. A positive control that cannot pass is the same defect as a guard that cannot fail, pointing the other way. AND ONE ASSERTED THE WRONG PROPERTY. `test_two_opens_in_one_paragraph` asserted the walk calls that case `unclosed`; it does not, and need not. What matters is that the note is REPORTED as malformed. Corpus differential: 404 notes, 0 whose counted total moved. 46 passed across the 3 region files, 32 in the Desktop file. title: I38 was never a flake: a checkout named `clone` could not recognise itself
verbatim: I38 was never a flake: a checkout named `clone` could not recognise itself RESOLVED, deterministically, and the rate computed for it was measuring which harness made each clone. `bench/repo_paths.py` deliberately refuses to treat generic directory names -- `checkout`, `clone`, `git` -- as a project's identity, because a clone sits wherever the reader put it and must not claim its parent folder's name as the project. That blocklist is right. The defect was that `_names_this_checkout` then had NO other way to recognise its own tree, and `scripts/fresh_clone_suite_2026-09-11.py` clones into a directory named exactly `clone`. Every run through that harness failed; every run through a harness that named the directory anything else passed. That is the whole of the apparent intermittency, across 8 full-size runs and several days. MEASURED. Across 4 names at the old revision -- clone, ctrl, Constraint_Engineering, cdsfl_fresh_clone_zz -- only `clone` failed. On the same shape in one command: 1 failed, 35 passed without the fix against 36 passed with it. Deciding "is this my own tree?" by the directory's NAME is this session's recurring false-zero shape, and it was inside the classifier that decides which rejections are location artefacts. The predicate now asks path IDENTITY first and keeps the name checks beneath it, because those still resolve archived strings naming a DIFFERENT machine's checkout, where no identity exists to compare. THE DIAGNOSIS WAS ONLY POSSIBLE BECAUSE THE CLONE HARNESS STOPPED DISCARDING ITS OUTPUT 2 HOURS EARLIER. The assertion prints the resolved project names, their source, the repo root and every suffix probe; before this morning the run reported the test's name and nothing else. The fix to the harness and the diagnosis of I38 are the same story. MY FIRST TEST FOR THIS WAS VACUOUS AND THE MUTATION CAUGHT IT. It asserted on the live REPO, which IS named after the project, so it passed through the NAME check and removing the identity check left all 37 green. It now points `REPO` at a directory called `clone` and first asserts that `clone` is still blocklisted, so it cannot silently stop posing the question. The mutant dies. THE RATE IS RETRACTED AS A RATE. The census rows are kept -- they are the evidence that identified the harness as the variable -- but a proportion over a deterministic phenomenon describes the sample, and the script now says so in its own docstring rather than leaving a reader to quote 37.5000% as a failure rate. title: `--help` destroyed 54,480 bytes of a verbatim panel record and exited 0
verbatim: `--help` destroyed 54,480 bytes of a verbatim panel record and exited 0 MEASURED in a throwaway clone: `python3 scripts/assemble_panel_record_0819.py --help` rewrote Panel_Enforcement_Prose_FULL_RECORD_2026-08-19.md from 55,814 bytes to 1,334 and returned success. The script regenerates a panel record from `bench/logs/`, which .gitignore excludes, so in any clone the source is empty and every seat is written back as "NO RESPONSE FILE" -- the complete verbatim record of a 5-model review replaced by a stub, by a flag whose whole job is to print a sentence. IT HAD BEEN HAPPENING IN EVERY CLONE RUN. The symptom reached this suite as `test_each_record_reproduces_a_seat_verbatim` failing on 2 August notes, which looked like a defect in the records and was a defect in a flag. Found by keeping the clone (`--keep`) and looking at what `git status` said inside it. THE MORNING'S `--help` SWEEP REPORTED 0 OF 54 AND WAS HONEST. Its population is MEASUREMENT scripts and both offenders are ACTION scripts. 122 scripts are tracked; the 68 the sweep does not reach are exactly the ones where a `--help` that acts is destructive rather than rude. A false zero in the POPULATION rather than in the matcher -- the same class one level out. 7 tracked scripts both WROTE something and ignored the flag: 5.7377% of 122, Wilson [2.8068%, 11.3709%], Clopper-Pearson [2.3377%, 11.4648%]. All 7 plus the 2 record assemblers now answer it. Verified by execution in a throwaway clone: all 9 print usage, exit 0, and leave the tree clean. THE RATCHET IS STATIC ON PURPOSE. Running every tracked script with `--help` is exactly what must not be done -- the standing note records 15 of 17 runners BILLING A LIVE DISPATCH on an unrecognised argument, and spending money is reserved to the founder. The executing proof is done once, by hand, in a clone. AND MY OWN RATCHET HAD THE DEFECT IT WAS WRITTEN TO CATCH. `answers_help` asked `"answer_help" in src`, so removing the real call from a script left it green -- the explanatory COMMENT beside the call still contains the word. A guard that reads its own documentation as evidence of the thing documented. It now asks the PARSED module whether `answer_help` or `ArgumentParser` is actually called. The mutation that survived now dies. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: The `--help` guard ran at import and broke 12 tests in the next clone run
verbatim: The `--help` guard ran at import and broke 12 tests in the next clone run MY FIX HAD THE SHAPE OF THE DEFECT IT FIXED. Placing `answer_help` at module level meant every test that IMPORTS one of those modules handed pytest's own argv to the help handler, which refused it and exited 2 -- 4 failures and 8 errors in the confirming clone run, in tests that had nothing to do with `--help`. The established form in `scripts/` guards the call under `__main__`, and 30-odd scripts already did it that way. I did not look before writing, and the full clone run is what found it. That is the second time today a change looked right in a targeted subset and was wrong in the whole. A SECOND BREAK UNDER IT: the mutation harness copies a script to `.mutants/` and runs it there, where `_cli_help` is not importable, so a bare import crashed every mutant. A crashing mutant produces no output and every `not in` check passes, which would have made the harness report mutants as "caught" for the wrong reason -- the harness's own assertion says exactly that and is what caught it. The import is now tolerant, with the reason written beside it: the guard protects real invocations and a mutant copy is not one. VERIFIED IN A THROWAWAY CLONE, both properties at once: all 9 scripts print usage on `--help`, exit 0 and leave the tree clean; and importing them no longer exits. Importing still runs their module-level work, which is unchanged from before and is what the `__main__` guard preserves -- and nothing in bench/ or scripts/ imports any of them, checked. 372 passed across the 9 affected files. title: Guarding `--help` fixed one entrance to a room with two doors
verbatim: Guarding `--help` fixed one entrance to a room with two doors THE NOTES WERE STILL BEING TRUNCATED AFTER THE `--help` FIX, and the confirming clone run said so. `bench/tests/test_operational_scripts.py` probes every script by IMPORTING it (`spec_from_file_location`), and these scripts did their work at module scope -- so they did it whenever they were inspected, flag or no flag. Attributed by the same method as the Desktop escape: clone once, then run each of 89 candidate test files and check the note after each. Exactly 1 truncated it. The work now lives in `main()` under a `__main__` guard in all 3 scripts that had it at module scope. Verified: importing changes nothing, `--help` prints usage and changes nothing, and running them properly still produces byte-identical output -- 5 of 5 panellists, and the topology diagram still writes its 26,069 bytes. title: A fresh clone runs the full suite GREEN: 7,237 passed, 0 failed, exit 0
verbatim: A fresh clone runs the full suite GREEN: 7,237 passed, 0 failed, exit 0 TASK A2'S CLAIM, TRUE FOR THE FIRST TIME. It was asserted on 2026-09-10 and again on 2026-09-11 and was false both times, each time discovered by a person actually cloning rather than by anything in the project. `scripts/fresh_clone_suite_2026-09-11.py` is committed, so the claim is now reproducible rather than asserted, and its full output lands at `bench/logs/fresh_clone_last_run.txt`. THE LAST 3 FAILURES WERE ONE DEFECT IN 3 SETS OF CLOTHES. A checkout named `clone` could not recognise itself, because identity was decided by the directory's NAME. A `--help` ran a script's ordinary work and destroyed a 55,814-byte verbatim record, because the flag fell through. And guarding the flag closed only one of 2 doors: the suite also probes scripts by IMPORTING them, and the work ran at module scope. The session state block I wrote to record this landed INSIDE the previous block rather than above it, so the file's newest-first order was wrong and the guard read the older block. Moved, and the guard passes. AND THE GUARD'S OWN MATCHER READ "7,237 passed" AS "237 passed". It only ever counts how many figures a block quotes, so nothing was wrong today -- but a matcher that reads 7,237 as 237 is one consumer away from reporting the wrong number, and that is the class this session found 16 times. Thousands separators are now in the pattern. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: The triage script re-parked items already parked, inflating the founder's workload
verbatim: The triage script re-parked items already parked, inflating the founder's workload MEASURED 2026-09-11, minutes after he asked whether the workload set out for him was significant. I had just merged 2 duplicate headings by hand -- one decision written twice as an analysis and a triage stub, and an A8 question superseded by a smaller one -- and re-running the triage immediately appended a THIRD A8 heading. The count of DECISIONS was growing with copies of one decision, which is the opposite of what that file is for. `park()` now refuses a title already present, compared on a normalised form: punctuation and case dropped, ARTICLES dropped, and anything after an em dash dropped. All 3 were needed by real pairs in that file -- the pair this was found on differed by the word "the", and headings there gain status notes such as "SUPERSEDED" or "SAME DECISION AS 10.2" after a dash while remaining the same item. IT RETURNS None RATHER THAN A PATH when it refuses, and the caller crashed on that the first time: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'relative_to'`. A refusal path that fails is worse than no refusal path, which is the same note already standing beside the census script's own refusal. MUTATION-TESTED both directions, because only one of them is obvious: allow duplicates again -> 3 fail refuse everything -> 3 fail, including an existing append-only test The second matters more. A check that refused every item would silently DROP new decisions, and losing a decision is far worse than listing one twice. 21 passed. The file is back to 15 headings, 13 of them live. title: 2 of the 6 orphaned scripts were wired rather than ruled on, because wiring is not the half that needs a ruling
verbatim: 2 of the 6 orphaned scripts were wired rather than ruled on, because wiring is not the half that needs a ruling The additive standard has 2 halves and only 1 of them is the founder's. Removal requires a committed measurement that something better replaces the thing; that is his. "An addition that nothing reaches is not additive either" is discharged by giving a script a caller, and a test that EXECUTES it is exactly that. WHICH 2, AND WHY NOT THE OTHER 4, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. An AST walk over all 6 found `measure_round_zero_irreducible_escalations.py` and `priority_starvation_simulation.py` contain no write call, no subprocess spawn and no absolute path, so running them cannot change anything -- asserted as a consequence too, by comparing `git status` either side. The other 4 write files or spawn processes, and the standing instruction against running the scripts directory as a survey exists because it once overwrote a preserved archive. They stay parked and UNRUN. BOTH STILL WORK, which was worth knowing whichever way he rules: a committed measurement that no longer runs is a defect independent of whether it is kept. The test asserts on the figure's LABEL rather than its value, because the archive grows and a pinned count goes stale within the day. 118 of 122 = 96.7213%, Wilson [91.8724%, 98.7177%], Clopper-Pearson [91.8179%, 99.0996%]. I TYPED THOSE INTERVALS FROM MEMORY THE FIRST TIME AND BOTH WERE WRONG -- [92.0227%, 98.7243%] against the computed [91.8724%, 98.7177%]. Substituted from the computation rather than retyped, which is the second transcription slip of the day and the reason the rule says substitute. The ratchet is lowered to 4, and the control that pinned `priority_starvation_simulation.py` as an orphan now names one that still is -- it became false for the right reason.
