title: 3 of the 6 orphans wired, and naming the other 3 in prose un-orphaned one of them
verbatim: 3 of the 6 orphans wired, and naming the other 3 in prose un-orphaned one of them A 3rd script joined the 2 wired earlier, after asking WHICH processes the "spawners" run rather than that they spawn. `inventory_2026_09_06.py` spawns only `git rev-parse --short HEAD` and `git status --short`, both read-only, and has no write call at all. Classifying it by the SHAPE of the call instead of by what the call does was a coarser version of the mistake this session keeps finding. THE REMAINING 3 STAY PARKED AND UNRUN, and the reason is now specific rather than "they write". 2 write files outright. The 3rd spawns `adjudicate_by_repair.py --dry-run`, and THAT script carries 10 write calls -- so its safety rests on a different script honouring a flag. A reasonable bet, and not one to take against a preserved archive, which the standing instruction exists because someone already lost one. AND NAMING THEM IN THE TEST'S DOCSTRING UN-ORPHANED ONE WITHIN A MINUTE. Writing a script's path into a tracked file makes the reachability scan count it as reached, because a mention is all that scan can see. 5th instance in a day of prose ABOUT an orphan stopping it being one -- the roll call, this module's docstring, the test's docstring, an adopted probe's specimen, and now this. The unrun scripts are no longer named here, the list lives in the parked note whose roll-call lines the scan already ignores, and the check READS the ratchet instead of repeating it, so it cannot drift out of step. 119 of 122 = 97.5410%, Wilson [93.0192%, 99.1602%], Clopper-Pearson [92.9818%, 99.4900%], substituted from the computation rather than typed. That is the 5th statement of this figure today. The first 3 moved because scripts were added and the last 2 because orphans were wired; it is a snapshot of a set being actively worked on, and the durable claim is the ratchet. title: Round 15's seat proposals preserved, because the harness crash meant they were never written
verbatim: Round 15's seat proposals preserved, because the harness crash meant they were never written `seat_proposals.diff` is the artefact that normally carries what each seat PRODUCED, as opposed to what it said. The harness died before writing it -- `diff -u` under text mode raising on a non-UTF-8 byte -- so for this round that artefact does not exist. The sandboxes survived the crash and the 4 files were read out of them directly. They are kept unedited, as `.txt`, beside the replies. 3 of the 4 were adopted and ADAPTED here, and the adapted versions differ: the first raised AttributeError on its first call, because the seat had written its own `region_state` returning a dataclass while the one that shipped returns a mapping. These copies are the record of what the seats actually produced, which the adapted versions are not. The 4th was not adopted -- it tests that seat's own implementations rather than the ones that shipped -- and its 4 genuinely uncovered scenarios were ported into the existing files instead. Saying so here means the record shows a deliberate decision rather than an omission. title: All 6 orphaned scripts are wired: 122 of 122 reached, and nothing is left for the founder to rule on
verbatim: All 6 orphaned scripts are wired: 122 of 122 reached, and nothing is left for the founder to rule on The last 2 came off for a reason worth stating, because it is the least obvious step. Both WRITE, which is why they sat unrun while 4 siblings were wired. But neither writes to a fixed place. `readjudicate_pairs.py` builds `REPO / args.out`, and joining a path with an ABSOLUTE path yields the absolute path, so an absolute `--out` redirects the write entirely while its inputs still resolve against the real repository. `quarantine_to_candidate.py` writes beside the diff it is handed. CHECKED BEFORE RUNNING, NOT AFTER. Neither imports a network client and neither spawns a process, so neither can dispatch a model -- which mattered more than the file writes, because "re-adjudicate" is exactly the word that would make a reader assume a dispatch, and spending money is reserved to the founder. AND THAT CHECK'S FIRST VERSION WAS WRONG IN THE FAMILIAR DIRECTION. It treated the IMPORT of `subprocess` as the hazard, and `quarantine_to_candidate.py` imports it without ever calling it -- a dead import that would have kept a harmless script parked indefinitely. title: An ETA from a closure rate is wrong when the list grows while being closed
verbatim: An ETA from a closure rate is wrong when the list grows while being closed The founder asked for an ETA on completing the master task list. A burn-down answers that only if the list is a fixed target, and this one is not: **36 of its 95 entries, 37.8947%, were created AFTER it was first populated**, Wilson [28.7898%, 47.9406%], Clopper-Pearson [28.1364%, 48.4296%]. Closing an entry keeps turning up defects that become entries. Implied multiplier 1.6102. MY FIRST FIGURE UNDERSTATED IT BY MORE THAN HALF, and the producer is why that is known. Measured by hand from the snapshot at the end of the list's second day it came out at 16.8421% -- because 20 entries had already been added before that start point. A figure whose value depends on where the author began measuring is not a measurement. The script starts at the first commit where the list had any entries at all, and a test asserts that, with an anti-vacuity check that moving the start point actually changes the answer. AND THE TEST FOUND A DEFECT IN ITS OWN COUNTING. Asserting that the entry count never falls went red: a fall of 2 at `3b2d9a7`. No entry was deleted -- 6 ids had been DUPLICATED (P1, P2, P3, P4, 2.1, 5.1) and that commit cleaned them up. Counting raw marker LINES read a de-duplication as a deletion, which would have reported an additive-standard violation that never happened. Both the producer and the test now count DISTINCT IDS, which is the invariant that matters. title: The list converges because closure outpaces discovery, not because discovery is decaying
verbatim: The list converges because closure outpaces discovery, not because discovery is decaying The founder asked for an ETA. The tempting answer fits a decay to the discovery series -- 72, 16, 7 across the list's 3 days -- and quotes a date. That answer would be fabricated certainty. DAY 1 IS THE LIST BEING CREATED, not discovery while working it, so there are 2 usable observations. Their day-on-day ratio is 0.4375, which projects a tail of 5.44 further entries ever. But a 95% Wilson interval on the 2-day split is [15.6040%, 50.8658%], which INCLUDES the 50% a non-decaying process would sit at, and admits a ratio up to 1.0352 -- a process that never decays and whose tail is unbounded. 2 points cannot establish a decay rate and this one does not. WHAT IS MEASURED IS THAT CLOSURE OUTPACES DISCOVERY. On the latest day the list gained 7 entries and closed 21, roughly 3 to 1. That is why it converges, and it is a fact rather than a projection. `TestTheConvergenceArgumentRestsOnTheRightThing` pins it and says explicitly that any ETA must be withdrawn if it stops holding. `--per-day` reports both series, with day 1 labelled as creation so a reader cannot compare it against the others by accident. title: The list terminates: R = 0.4444, and the whole 95% interval lies below 1
verbatim: The list terminates: R = 0.4444, and the whole 95% interval lies below 1 THE FOUNDER ASKED WHETHER IT MIGHT NEVER FINISH, and said we should pause and discuss if so. That question has a formal answer, so it is measured rather than argued. Treat each closed entry as an individual in a branching process producing R new entries. R < 1 is SUBCRITICAL and terminates with probability 1; R >= 1 need never terminate. R < 1 is equivalent to p < 1/2 for p = additions / (additions + closures), so it is an ordinary proportion against a threshold. MEASURED over the list's whole worked life: 36 additions against 81 closures. R = 0.4444, 95% Wilson [0.3009, 0.6565], exact binomial test against the critical threshold p = 1.933172e-05. The interval lies ENTIRELY below 1. R was also below 1 on each worked day separately -- 0.3636 and 0.3333 -- and Fisher exact p = 1.0000 between them, so pooling is defensible and no trend toward 1 is visible. Expected entries ever from the 7 now live: 12.60, or 20.38 at the pessimistic bound. About 5.6 more entries, not an unbounded stream. THREE CAVEATS, WRITTEN INTO THE FUNCTION BECAUSE THE NUMBER IS MORE FRAGILE THAN IT LOOKS. R is partly a POLICY variable, since I decide what becomes an entry -- which cuts both ways, because it is therefore controllable. The remaining entries may not resemble the closed ones. And most importantly, this R describes THIS body of work: discovery may be falling because the swept areas are nearly swept, and opening a genuinely new one -- Exp 56 -- could restart it at a rate this window says nothing about. `TestTheListTerminates` fails if R's upper bound ever reaches 1, because that changes the answer to his question and is a conversation rather than a number to quietly restate. Mutation-verified. AND MY OWN PROJECTION COUNTED WITHDRAWN ENTRIES AS OUTSTANDING, inflating the live count from 7 to 11 and the tail from 12.60 to 19.80. Withdrawn entries are closed. Fixed, with a test. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: Adversarial audit: 24 of 71 DONE entries claim more than their evidence establishes
verbatim: Adversarial audit: 24 of 71 DONE entries claim more than their evidence establishes 52 agents read the list entry by entry and asked whether each DONE entry's named evidence establishes its CLAIM, not merely whether that file passes. Everything flagged went to a second agent instructed to REFUTE the flag with the burden on the flag. 42 flagged, 13 refuted, 29 upheld. 24 of 71 real DONE entries = 33.8028%, Wilson [23.8850%, 45.3834%], Clopper-Pearson [22.9970%, 46.0073%]. TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN AUDIT HAD TO BE CORRECTED FIRST. The batch list was written by hand and named 7 ids that DO NOT EXIST -- so 5 of the 29 "confirmed unsupported" were verdicts about nothing. And 13 real DONE entries were never audited at all: coverage was 84.5238%, not 100%. A second run covers them. THE DOMINANT PATTERN IS NOT WORK UNDONE. 25 of the 24 findings quote a figure no committed script produces; 25 name evidence asserting on SOURCE TEXT where the claim is about behaviour; 13 name evidence testing something adjacent; 9 state a claim broader than what was run. Entry 1.2 is representative: its catcher statistics reproduce EXACTLY when the script is run, and its load-bearing sentence about "all 16 combinations" and a "worst case p of 0.598" is produced by no artefact anywhere in the tree. So these are rarely entries that did nothing and usually entries that claim slightly more than they established -- a documentation-integrity problem, not broken code. Every evidence file exists and passes; the full suite ran green in a fresh clone 4 times today. Both full outputs are committed unsummarised: 78 audit judgements (147,208 bytes) and 42 adversarial verifications (274,915 bytes), including the 13 refutations. title: The Stop hook read its own words as the founder's and erased his command
verbatim: The Stop hook read its own words as the founder's and erased his command FOUNDER RULING 2026-09-11: 'all commands issued by me should be considered law, and are non-optional under any condition!' and 'Also scrub the d lock on me!' Claude Code writes hook feedback into the transcript as a user entry flagged isMeta. Both of this hook's transcript readers walked user entries without checking that flag, so after its first refusal it re-read the turn, found its own refusal text where his message had been, and recomputed had_d from it -- which never carries d. The same walk keyed the refusal budget, so MAX_REFUSALS_PER_TURN = 8 reset to 0 on every refusal and never bound. It refused 11 consecutive stops after he said 'Pause all activity'. One predicate, is_founder_message(), now used by both readers so they cannot drift apart. The hook keeps every bit of its refusal power: a stop with work outstanding and no d is still refused, and the self-test's 7 cases still hold. 10 executing tests, non-vacuous under mutation: blinding the predicate to isMeta reproduces the original defect exactly. verbatim: I31: the drift detector is wired, on the founder's conditional ruling He approved it with a condition: defer if it depends on the current mathematical model, wire it now if it does not. verbatim: Onboarding: check every tool the project needs, and prove Wolfram computes FOUNDER RULING 2026-09-16, approved in full: onboarding should recommend and where possible install the tools a user needs before running CDSFL. verbatim: fix: an inert --help on the new producer, and a foot-line for the addendum Both defects were mine, both were found by guards doing their job, and both were introduced earlier tonight. --HELP RAN THE WHOLE MEASUREMENT. immune_removal_rate_exp46_2026-09-17.py had neither argparse nor answer_help, so the flag fell through and the script loaded the embedding model and scored 351 pairs. test_help_is_answered_2026-09-11.py caught it by RUNNING any script it cannot vouch for structurally rather than grepping for argparse, which is the distinction that makes it able to fail. title: fix: one foot-line, with the addendum above it
verbatim: fix: one foot-line, with the addendum above it I CAUSED THIS ONE AN HOUR AGO AND THE SELECTOR CAUGHT IT. The provenance addendum was given its own v1.7 foot-line so that a foot-line would be the note's final content. That satisfied the record guard and broke a different one. THE MECHANISM, EXECUTED RATHER THAN SUSPECTED. The v1.7 enforcement selector holds FOOTLINE = CDSFL note standard v(\d+)\.(\d+) and calls FOOTLINE.search, which returns the FIRST match. On the 2-foot-line file findall returned [('1','4'), ('1','7')], so search read 1.4 and the working-tree selector classified the note as not-v1.7, while the revision reader found the v1.7 line and classified it as v1.7. Identical bytes in HEAD and the working tree, 2 extraction rules, opposite answers, and git reporting nothing to explain the gap. So a note with 2 foot-lines is classified by whichever comes first, and the 2-foot-line design is unworkable whichever guard it is aimed at. Loosening search to findall would have edited a selector, and the classification of every note in the repository, to protect 1 file's layout. THE ADDENDUM NOW SITS ABOVE A SINGLE v1.4 FOOT-LINE. The earlier objection to this -- that an August version line would close content written tonight -- was wrong: the foot-line declares the standard the RECORD was written under, and the addendum is dated and labelled as an editorial addition in its own first sentence. The transcript is still unaltered. A LATENT HOLE, REPORTED NOT FIXED. 5 notes carry more than 1 foot-line marker and in every case the markers are identical, so there are 0 live victims today. But a note that quotes an earlier version in prose before its own v1.7 foot-line would be classified by the quotation and silently exempted from v1.7 enforcement. It blocks nothing, so it goes to the founder for a ruling rather than becoming an unrequested change to a selector. THE BOARD before this fix: 1 failed, 7446 passed, 5 skipped, 1 xfailed in 1328.42s against a clean tree at cea399c. Pass rate 7446 of 7447 = 99.9866%, Wilson 95% [99.9240%, 99.9976%], statsmodels and a scipy closed form agreeing to 0.00e+00 and mpmath at 30 decimal places to 4.75e-17, Clopper-Pearson [99.9252%, 99.9997%]. The 1 failure is the one this commit closes. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: fix: hold a note to its foot-line's version, failing closed; the 15.8% was a mislabel
verbatim: fix: hold a note to its foot-line's version, failing closed; the 15.8% was a mislabel 2 fixes the founder asked to be applied on 2026-09-17 -- "Can you apply your fixes at least?" -- and a correction to a claim this session made overnight. Each was revised twice, after 2 rounds of independent read-only review found real defects in its earlier versions. The review loop was stopped after round 2 by judgement, not by convergence: round 2 found fewer and mostly latent defects, every one that held is fixed below and held by an executing test, and a third round was not run. THE OVERNIGHT CLAIM WAS WRONG, AND SO WERE 2 CORRECTIONS OF IT. The green-board report, the Stage 1 addendum, the removal-rate producer and its test all stated that the comment in bench/dm/_similarity.py quotes a figure, 15.8%, that reproduces nowhere. It reproduces exactly on the set it was measured on: the 272 of exp46's 351 pairs whose findings do not share a flaw class, 265 of 272 flagged before the clamp and 43 of 272 after. Across all 351 pairs, with the class bonus applied per pair, it is 344 to 75, 98.0% to 21.4%, which commit 3660816 states. The set was LABELLED on 2026-08-18. Measurement M10 in experimental_notes/evidence/panel_records_2026-08-18/confer_stage1_audit_2026-08-18/ PRIMARY_SOURCE_MEASUREMENTS.md.txt reads "flagged 97.4% (n=272)". The plain-English note of the same day carried both labels -- it qualified the 15.8% "for pairs without a class match" but, at line 49, called the 97.4% a rate "of all pairs" -- and the code comment kept the wrong one. M10 was written by an earlier session of this assistant, and the independent review of 2026-08-21 had flagged the figures as unlabelled; neither was consulted. The first correction then claimed the set was located by exact arithmetic and that the plain-English note agreed with M10. Neither is true. Arithmetic over the class partition leaves only the 272, but it cannot exclude every other subset, since 20 pair counts up to 351 admit both figures; the identification rests on M10's label, and its medians, 0.594 retired and 0.388 clamped, corroborate it. All 4 of M10's figures match. The record's measurement blocks state 15 figures, not the 9 this session counted; all 15 reproduce and the producer now checks every one. Its docstring said it "can FAIL" while main() returned 0 whatever the comparisons found; it now exits 1 on any failed check, verified by replaying it with a wrong M10 median and with a wrong record figure, each of which exits 1 through the new path. The comment names each set in the same number of lines, so no line citation moves, and its function docstring, which still described the retired (cos+1)/2 map, now describes the clamp. The producer's test ties the comment's 4 clamping percentages and the 2 retired rates beside them to their sets, forbids the original "Same 351 pairs" sentence, and requires the comment's "(n=272)". Its first replacement only checked that each figure appeared somewhere in the output and passed with the 2 sets' labels swapped. It does NOT check the comment's non-percentage figures, which the record-side checks cover. Corrections to the committed report and Stage 1 addendum are struck through and dated, not rewritten. The addendum now records that the transcript's foot-line was moved below it, which its "nothing above this line has been altered" had omitted, and that its own "no class match" figures describe all 351 pairs with the bonus withheld, a different set from the 272. THE VERSION HOLE. The v1.7 enforcement read a note's version with FOOTLINE.search, the FIRST mention of "CDSFL note standard vX.Y" anywhere, so a note quoting an older version in its prose would be classified by the quotation and silently exempted from Rules 27 and 28. The revision reader in scripts/lint_reach_over_notes_2026-09-10.py counted ANY mention, so the 2 halves disagreed whenever a note's mentions fell on both sides of v1.7 -- which turned the suite red at 05:56. 2 earlier fixes were wrong. Taking the LAST strict foot-line let a quoted older foot-line placed after the real one exempt the note, and skipped list, HTML, heading, backtick and non-breaking-space formats the old rule enforced. The tolerant pattern that replaced it backtracked exponentially -- 20 repeats of "<!-- -->" on 1 line took 0.254 s, growing about 15 times per 4 more -- and, once made possessive, silently skipped a foot-line inside an HTML comment and the date-stamped shape 4 existing notes already use. Exemption is silent and over-enforcement is loud, so the adopted rule fails closed: a note is held to the HIGHEST version on any line shaped like a foot-line -- including list markers, HTML tags and comments, headings, and a short date stamp or list number before it -- and a mention in the middle of a sentence never counts. Every part of the pattern is bounded, the prefix is possessive, and case folds in ASCII as `git grep -i` does. A known gap remains: a label before the foot-line, "Footer: Written under ...", which first-mention read and this does not; the direction-aware check below fails on any real note in that shape. The revision reader now parses `git grep -z -a --no-line-number --no-column` as bytes with core.quotePath=false. Its answer had depended on git settings: with grep.lineNumber=true it read 0 of 379 where HEAD's code read 29. It no longer depends on them, cannot be split by a colon in a file name, reads a note holding a NUL byte, treats a lone CR as a line end as the live selector does, and cannot crash on a Latin-1 line. declaring() and the at_revision fallback decide through the same rule, so a substituted pattern can cost time but not change the answer. Measured: 61 notes enforced in the working tree and at HEAD, and 29 of 379 at b593500, unchanged under grep.lineNumber and grep.column. The lint-reach script prints both. GUARDED BY EXECUTION. bench/tests/test_footline_is_read_from_the_footline_2026-09-17.py shows each rejected rule wrong on its own fixture; drives the live selector, the revision reader and declaring() over the same fixtures; runs the reader against a REAL throwaway git repository, under line-number and column settings, and through the slow fallback; ratchets the stall inputs; and checks the real notes in both directions, failing on any note that loses enforcement. The lint-reach mutation test anchors on the call that decides. NOTED, NOT CHANGED: _revision_footlines in the lint-reach script has no caller. The note linter does not flag a spelled count that opens a sentence; the review found 2 in the TTS companion, fixed by hand. Its docstring said it "can FAIL" while main() returned 0 whatever the comparisons found; it now exits 1 on any failed check, verified by replaying it with a wrong M10 median and with a wrong record figure, each of which exits 1 through the new path. The comment names each set in the same number of lines, so no line citation moves, and its function docstring, which still described the retired (cos+1)/2 map, now describes the clamp. The producer's test ties the comment's 4 clamping percentages and the 2 retired rates beside them to their sets, forbids the original "Same 351 pairs" sentence, and requires the comment's "(n=272)". The v1.7 enforcement read a note's version with FOOTLINE.search, the FIRST mention of "CDSFL note standard vX.Y" anywhere, so a note quoting an older version in its prose would be classified by the quotation and silently exempted from Rules 27 and 28. Its answer had depended on git settings: with grep.lineNumber=true it read 0 of 379 where HEAD's code read 29. It no longer depends on them, cannot be split by a colon in a file name, reads a note holding a NUL byte, treats a lone CR as a line end as the live selector does, and cannot crash on a Latin-1 line. declaring() and the at_revision fallback decide through the same rule, so a substituted pattern can cost time but not change the answer. Commit 90873cb wired update_drift because pi_mem "appears nowhere in docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md". It appears as π_mem: 0 ASCII occurrences, 5 Greek, defined at line 1506 in section 1.5 with S_pos, S_neg and the 2.0 threshold at lines 1524 to 1527. scripts/i31_drift_detector_premise_2026-09-17.py, by execution: - SymPy: the code's pi_mem expression minus the appendix formula = 0; ALPHA_0 and BETA_0 are the appendix's 0.5. - the code's CUSUM matches the appendix recursion over 200 seeded sequences to within 5.187e-16. - z3: 1 or 2 same-direction updates from 0 cannot exceed 2.0; 3 can. Confirmed by Reduce on the local Wolfram Engine: False for 2, True for 3 (computed with Wolfram Language). - production makes 1 update per class per run and save() keeps no CUSUM state: 48 replayed cases, 0 fired, largest excursion 0.950032. - immune_memory_enabled is False in all 3 experiment 56 arms. So the condition for deferring was met. Behaviour is unchanged: the false comment at the call site carries a dated correction, and keeping or reverting the report-only call is the founder's verdict (item 12(b)). test_i31_drift_premise_2026-09-17.py holds it; a detector that always fires and a load that keeps drift state each fail it. title: wolfram: the licence renews itself, and the claim that it could not be automated was false
verbatim: wolfram: the licence renews itself, and the claim that it could not be automated was false FOUNDER, 2026-09-17: "You can automate the Wolfram renewal via a small local script, or maybe an Apple automation. It doesn't require a username/password. Make sure it still loads on system reboot whatever you do." He was right and the record was wrong. scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py told the reader activation "needs your Wolfram ID and password, so it cannot be automated from here". Measured with mathpass backed up first: `wolframscript -activate` with stdin CLOSED returned exit 0 and "Wolfram Engine activated", rewrote the licence file, and prompted for nothing. It authenticates through the cloud credential already stored under ~/Library/WolframEngine/ApplicationData/CloudObject, with WOLFRAMSCRIPT_AUTHENTICATIONPATH set in WolframScript.conf. That line is corrected, and no credential is typed anywhere: stdin stays closed, so a build that ever did prompt fails the run instead of hanging. The same measurement showed re-activating early does NOT move the date (2026-10-08 before and after), so renewal lands at or after expiry. The job therefore runs on a schedule and keeps trying. - scripts/wolfram_licence_renew_2026-09-17.py: reads the expiry through bench/wolfram_standard.py (1 retry, failed call is not evidence), skips while another kernel is running (single-kernel licence), activates only inside the window or on --force, redacts anything e-mail-shaped from what it logs, and appends to ~/Library/Logs/cdsfl_wolfram_renew.log. --help does nothing. - resources/launchd/com.cdsfl.wolfram-licence-renew.plist, installed in ~/Library/LaunchAgents: RunAtLoad (so every reboot and login) plus 09:05 and 21:05, with a PATH that can find wolframscript. Bootstrapped at 21:29; it ran itself immediately and logged "nothing to do", last exit code 0. - test_wolfram_licence_renew_2026-09-17.py, 15 tests, drives the real functions with injected runners and starts no kernel. 5 mutations each fail it: busy check removed, stdin left open, always due, success not requiring the word activated, redaction removed. It also asserts the installed agent matches the committed plist. Task 0.1's date-gated observation is discharged: nothing is owed on 2026-10-08. The W1 instructions and tonight's decision note are corrected in both their repository and spoken copies, with the manual steps kept as a fallback. title: wolfram: enabled for every seat and agent as the second falsifier, queued against 1 kernel
verbatim: wolfram: enabled for every seat and agent as the second falsifier, queued against 1 kernel The founder's rulings (d) and (e) of 2026-09-17: "So fully enable it ... Wolfram, although it should always be used wherever possible, should remain the secondary/verification source (a second falsifier), where our other relevant tools should also aways be used and should remain primary in all cases", and "Agents are not exempt from using tools ... Every model and every agent should use tools wherever possible, including Wolfram." The default was the opposite 6 hours earlier, so this is a reversal rather than an addition, and what replaces the refusal is a QUEUE rather than nothing: the free Engine is single-kernel, and 3 concurrent calls measured on 2026-08-02 gave 1 result and 2 "Connection closed by WolframKernel". * bench/wolfram_standard.py: policy `serial` (default) or `deny` (retained, selectable), with gate_dir, claude_cli_args and panel_clause all reading it, so a seat cannot be told one thing while its launcher does another. * bench/tools/wolfram_gate/serial/: the gate a seat reaches. Machine-wide exclusive lock, real binary, exit code passed through untouched, and either Wolfram's required attribution or [NOT EVIDENCE] with the reason appended. Every call recorded to ~/Library/Logs/cdsfl_wolfram_calls.log. * Measured through the real gate against the real Engine, 22:44 BST: the second of 2 simultaneous calls waited 5.1 s while the first held the kernel 5.1 s, windows disjoint, both evidence, both attributed, both answers correct. Producer: scripts/wolfram_serial_gate_probe_2026-09-17.py. * Never a dependency: absent kernel, busy queue and failed call each name SymPy, z3 and mpmath and say it is not a blocker. Onboarding says so too and keeps the 1-command install. * The 1 exception: a STORED falsifier may not call Wolfram, because it is re-run by whoever reproduces the experiment. falsifier_verify pins its sandbox to `deny` explicitly rather than inheriting the policy. * Ruling (f), in this same commit as he asked: .claude/CLAUDE.md carries the ruling verbatim, the corrected connector tool names (mcp__Wolfram__* matched nothing), and the corrected route sentence, with test_wolfram_route_retired_2026-09-10.py amended beside it. * A defect found on the way, older than today: onboarding's wolfram_state required "2" to be the LAST line of Print[1+1], but the binary prints 2 then the Null that Print returns, so a working kernel read as NO_KERNEL and the script offered to reconfigure a correct kernel path. The fixtures replied "2", a shape the binary never emits. Reverting the fix fails 4 tests. 22 new tests; removing the lock fails the concurrency test on overlapping intervals. 868 passed across the affected surface. title: panel: a retry gets a tree of its own, and no sandbox is deleted behind the operator
verbatim: panel: a retry gets a tree of its own, and no sandbox is deleted behind the operator Founder ruling (j), 2026-09-17: "Do it. And make sure this is how all future panel reviews and experiments (both paid and simulated) work in the future too. Take care when a panel review or an experiment completes however that the sandbox does not simply get automatically deleted and that the results do not end up simply being discarded, as has happened in the recent past." The defect, measured in round 17: the fable seat hit the 1,800 s cap and its retry reran in the SAME sandbox the timed-out attempt had been editing for half an hour. 14 of the 19 files that seat left behind had no reply behind them, and its verdict on A23 was measured against its own unreported edits. * call_claude_cli takes on_attempt, called before every attempt, returning the tree that attempt runs in. Attempt 1 keeps the copy already built, so a round with no retry pays nothing; later attempts get a fresh copy of the canonical tree. * The attempt travels with the reply: every seat record carries attempts=[{attempt, path, built}], and each tool-log entry carries its cwd. * seat_proposals.diff is keyed seat:attempt-N:path, so every attempt's tree is read, not only the one the seat ended in. * panel_sandbox.harvest takes whole changed FILES out, not only diffs; release deletes only when asked and only after a complete harvest; harvest_and_retain writes sandbox_manifest.json, says where the copies are and prints the exact command to remove them. PANEL_REAP_SANDBOXES=1 is the opt-in. * The rest of the fleet measured, not assumed: scripts/sandbox_deletion_audit_2026-09-17.py parses every tree-removing call in bench/ with ast. 26 calls, 6 seat trees, and 3 were destroying a seat's work with no harvest -- build_experiment_run, confer_convergence_panel and the SIMULATED runner. All 3 fixed; the audit now reports 0. * That audit's first version missed the simulated runner because it classified by variable name and the worktree is called _wt_parent. It now asks whether the function hands the path to a model. Restoring the round-17 reuse fails the attempt test; restoring the unconditional delete fails the retention test. 1 older test demanded the opposite behaviour and is amended with the ruling recorded in it. title: appendix: the coverage-to-risk inverse at line 169 was the NEGATIVE of the inverse
verbatim: appendix: the coverage-to-risk inverse at line 169 was the NEGATIVE of the inverse Founder, 2026-09-18 02:07 BST: "Fix the appendix line 169 sign error." The appendix stated the inverse of the Mobius readout TWICE and the 2 disagreed. Line 119 carried (π−R)/(π−πR), which is correct and round-trips. Line 169 carried (π_k−R_k)/(π_k(R_k−1)), exactly its negative: it does not round-trip, and at π = 1/2, R = 1/5 it returns C = −3/4, which is not a coverage. The same line claimed "round-trip residual exactly 0", which was false for the form it wrote. Corrected to (π_k−R_k)/(π_k(1−R_k)), with the old form quoted in the retraction so the record shows what changed. Verified after the edit: SymPy says the corrected form round-trips; Wolfram Language returns a residual of 0 independently; the 2 appendix statements are now symbolically identical, with a maximum numerical gap of 2.2e-16 across 16 points under mpmath. 81 tests pass across the 3 guards that read the appendix. NAMED FIRST BY THE PROPOSED REVISION 1.1, as "an isolated inverse sign error", and confirmed here against our own file rather than taken on trust. WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT OUR INSTRUMENTS, and it is the part worth keeping. The guard for exactly this class exists: bench/tests/test_appendix_reduction_properties_ 2026-09-05.py, written because the appendix's verification "lived in prose". It covers 18 reduction claims and never touched this inversion, so the defect walked past the instrument built to catch it. A guard for the inverse is PROPOSED, not built, because the founder's `d` stands. title: Z1: a rotation tool, so the token moves without hand-editing 10 credentials
verbatim: Z1: a rotation tool, so the token moves without hand-editing 10 credentials Founder, 2026-09-19: "lets deal with the Zenodo key rotation first ... Print as much copy and paste(able) instructions as possible so we can at least finally chalk this off our list." MEASURED FIRST. .env was last written 2026-08-16, so the token is 34 days old. Mutating shape() to print the whole value fails the leak test, run and reverted. title: Z1 DONE: the Zenodo token is actually rotated, and doing it found 2 defects
verbatim: Z1 DONE: the Zenodo token is actually rotated, and doing it found 2 defects Founder, 2026-09-19: "lets deal with the Zenodo key rotation first ... so we can at least finally chalk this off our list." Chalked off, and verified. THE ROTATION. The old token (60 characters, starting ievd) had sat in .env since 2026-08-16, 34 days. The new one starts Bu30. zenodo_token_check.py --live returns HTTP 200 with 1 deposition visible -- the CDSFL experimental archive. The other 9 credentials are byte-identical either side, digest 567852245d5e8cf0 printed before and after. Z1 moves COMMITTED -> ENABLED, because until today it described instructions rather than a rotation. DEFECT 1, AND IT COST A ONE-TIME SECRET. .env carries the macOS uchg immutable flag; shutil.copy2 copies that flag to the backup; os.chmod on an immutable file raises EPERM. The first live attempt died there AFTER the founder had pasted a token Zenodo shows exactly once, and the rename over .env would have failed next for the same reason. Fixed 2 ways: the flag is cleared for the write and restored in a finally, and every step that can fail now runs BEFORE the prompt. A test asserts that property directly -- if preparation fails, getpass is never called. DEFECT 2, A FALSE NEGATIVE FROM OUR OWN INSTRUMENT. zenodo_token_check.py read r.read(2000) of a 3,718-byte reply, parsed the truncated JSON, and reported the JSONDecodeError as "could not reach zenodo.org" -- on a run where the server answered 200 and the token was valid. Measured against the live service: both zenodo.org and its API were up and returning JSON throughout. It now reads the whole body and distinguishes REJECTED, UNREACHABLE and UNPARSEABLE, which call for 3 different actions. Also fixed: a paragraph opening "**2 defects were found..." was parsed as task entry "2" by ENTRY's `**<digit><space>` heading shape, breaking 5 marker guards. Reworded; 96 entries parse, Z1 DONE/ENABLED with 2 evidence files. 20 tests. Restoring the truncation fails the regression test; making the tool print the token fails the leak test; a clobbered neighbour restores the backup. All 3 mutations run and reverted. title: security: .env sidecars were not ignored, and a backup full of credentials got committed
verbatim: security: .env sidecars were not ignored, and a backup full of credentials got committed GitHub push protection refused the push. Commit 2f69baf contains .env.backup-20260919-195130 and -195510, each holding all 10 credentials in plaintext; the scanner named the OpenAI API key. Nothing was published -- the push was rejected -- so the exposure is local to this machine's repository. CAUSE, and it is mine. The Zenodo rotation tool wrote its backup beside .env as .env.backup-<stamp>. .gitignore covered `.env` and none of its sidecars, so `git add -A` swept the backups in. * .gitignore now covers `.env.*` with `!.env.example`, which also catches the tool's .env.tmp and .env.writetest. Verified with `git check-ignore --no-index` on all 5 shapes. * The 2 committed backups are untracked and MOVED OUT of the repository to ~/.config/cdsfl/env_backups, mode 0600 in a 0700 directory. Nothing deleted. * The tool now writes backups outside the repo entirely: a file holding 10 credentials has no business in a working tree, however briefly. * The FIRST version of that fix wrote into the founder's real ~/.config during a test run. The vault path is now injectable via CDSFL_ENV_BACKUP_DIR and every test redirects it into tmp_path; verified by counting the real vault before and after a run. 20 tests green. The history rewrite that removes the files from 2f69baf is the next commit; this one closes the hole so it cannot recur. title: panel: 6 seats with Gemini restored, and the 2 OpenAI seats stop sharing a model
verbatim: panel: 6 seats with Gemini restored, and the 2 OpenAI seats stop sharing a model Founder rulings, 2026-09-20. GEMINI IS BACK. "There is no reason why you shouldn't include Gemini! Gemini has traditionally been present for most of the project. If you dropped it in a runner for the experiments, or in a panel review process, then that is clearly an error on your part, and is nothing I have ever told you to do!" It was absent from the live panel table while the project instructions listed it, so the instructions described a panel that had not been running. THE 2 OPENAI SEATS ARE NO LONGER THE SAME MODEL. Both were openai/gpt-5.5: 1 architecture wearing 2 labels, 4 architectures reported as 5. His ruling: "we just run with a normal recent version of ChatGPT and with a separate instance of Codex 5.3 from this point on, until project completion. We mark the potential confound, state our reasons for this choice, and ensure that this choice stick through all future paid panel reviews and experiments." Applied to BOTH rosters, because he said both. * Panel: cx=openai/gpt-5.3-codex, cgpt=openai/gpt-5.5, ge restored, ds, cc2, fable. 6 seats, 6 distinct models, 4 paid. * Experiment roster: Codex=openai/gpt-5.3-codex. * .claude/CLAUDE.md: the table now describes the panel that runs, with fable documented for the first time. * Arm C re-registered as a MODEL contrast with the confound written into the config in his terms, launch_blocked -> False. THE GUARD THAT BLOCKED A MODEL SWAP IS INVERTED, on his ruling: "why should there be a test that breaks/or potentially blocks a run, just because we switch out one model for another? ... it is clearly the test itself in this case that is broken." A harness whose claim is substrate agnosticism cannot carry a test forbidding a substrate change. It still has teeth the other way: 2 seats on 1 model now FAIL, because that makes arm C a duplicate of arm B. Also measured, closing an item I could not verify on 2026-09-18: changing the Codex seat's model breaks EXACTLY 2 tests, both in test_d9_d11_configs_valid_2026-09-05.py. Confirmed by construction rather than taken from the sweep that claimed it. 621 tests green across the affected surface. verbatim: appendix: the inverse is now EXECUTED, not described -- the guard he asked for Founder, 2026-09-20, on the guard proposed after the sign error: "Verdict: build and implement it." THE GAP IT CLOSES. The appendix stated the coverage-to-risk inverse twice and the 2 disagreed: line 119 round-trips, line 169 was exactly its negative and returned a coverage of -3/4 at pi = 1/2, R = 1/5 while claiming in its own words a "round-trip residual exactly 0". test_appendix_reduction_properties_2026-09-05.py was written for that class -- verification living in prose -- and has 35 tests, not 1 of which touched this inversion. This is purely a test, and not yet an adoption plan." Everything known about openai/gpt-5.3-codex came from reading OpenRouter's catalogue, and a catalogue entry is a claim about a route rather than a call. title: sv measured, printed, and exited 0 anyway. 7 of its last 13 repairs are that one shape.
verbatim: sv measured, printed, and exited 0 anyway. 7 of its last 13 repairs are that one shape. The founder, 2026-09-20: "sv should be an entirely mechanical operation. Yet for several weeks now you keep uncovering issues with it? Can't you devise a permanent, definitive fix so it can do exactly as it was originally intended to do, and so that you don't need to keep hand implementing corrections after it runs?" THE RATE, PRODUCED RATHER THAN REMEMBERED. scripts/sv_repair_rate_2026-09-20.py reads the log: since 2026-08-01 there are 14 commits whose subject begins "sv:" and 14 that touch scripts/cdsfl_sv.py. 1 of those 14 is an 867-file milestone merge that carries the script along, so the repair count is 13 and the rate is 0.9286 repairs per save. The script prints every subject beside the class it assigned, so the classification can be overruled by looking rather than trusted. THE CLASS THAT MATTERS IS 7 OF THE 13. sv MEASURED something, PRINTED the measurement, and exited 0 regardless of what it said. _print_final_state re-measures the working tree and the remote and prints a verdict; _verify_remote_sync returns a dict naming exactly whether the remote moved; main() reads neither. On 2026-09-19 GitHub's secret scanner refused the push, and the save printed its own refusal and reported success. WHAT CHANGES, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A NEW MEASUREMENT. The readings sv already takes become a gate. scripts/sv_postconditions.py re-takes 6 of them after the commit has landed and returns a verdict; _run_postcondition_gate turns that verdict into the exit code. The commit is in the object store before the first check runs, so a failure can never cost work. What it withdraws is the claim that the save did what it reports. THE 6 CHECKS, EACH TIED TO A COMMIT THAT REPAIRED IT BY HAND. Working tree clean. HEAD == origin, compared on LOCAL refs so it needs no network and still catches a refused push. The generated docs/CURRENT_STATE.md is identical to HEAD, so a save cannot publish a state file describing the previous save. No "Last updated:" stamp is ahead of the clock (c45d848: "I typed five timestamps tonight instead of reading them, and three were in the future"). No credential-shaped file is tracked (.env.backup-20260919-232601, swept in by git add -A). The newest SESSION STATE block passes the A23 producer guard, which is the check that went red BECAUSE of an sv on 2026-09-19: the sentence recording a green suite is what made the suite red, and sv wrote the block without running the guard over it. THE SECRET PREDICATE IS NARROWER THAN sv's OWN, ON PURPOSE AND ON EVIDENCE. cdsfl_sv._SENSITIVE_PATTERNS contains the substrings "secret" and "credentials", which match 2 tracked files today: scripts/gate_environment_secrets_2026-09-17.py and bench/tests/test_seat_environment_carries_no_secrets_2026-09-17.py. Both are guards named after the thing they guard. A gate that fires on them gets switched off inside a week, and a gate that is switched off measures nothing. .env.example is the 1 deliberate exception on the other side, and it is tested rather than assumed. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. The other 6 repairs are real: 3 were a checker measuring the wrong quantity, 1 a Python version floor, and 2 remain unclassified by the producing script. A postcondition gate does not reach a checker that is asking the wrong question. It reaches a checker that asks the right question and is then ignored. 23 tests, every check driven both ways. Each defect above is reinstated and required to be caught; each clean case is required to pass, because a gate that always fails is as useless as one that never does. The remote check is driven with the bare origin DELETED, proving it answers offline. An unmeasurable required check counts as a failure, which is the project's own rule about a failed measurement. A check that raises becomes NOT MEASURED rather than a crash. The wiring is pinned separately: main() must call the gate inside its successful-commit branch, and sv must hold the same module object the tests drive. Run against the live tree it exits 1 and names why: 2 uncommitted paths, and HEAD 4 commits ahead of origin/main. Committed just before this one, as 135878b: scripts/codex_route_probe_2026-09-20.py, the 1 paid call that confirmed the openai/gpt-5.3-codex route before the panel runs on it. It answered, it offered a tool call, it wrote (1/2)*(1-1/2)/(1-(1/2)*(1/2)), and the value matched SymPy and mpmath at 0.3333333333333333. 501 tokens, $0.002482, about 0.196 pence. title: sv cites the last full suite instead of re-running it: 23 minutes back to seconds
verbatim: sv cites the last full suite instead of re-running it: 23 minutes back to seconds FOUNDER, 2026-09-20, verbatim: "What exactly is this suite doing? It will take how long? sv normally takes minutes? Hopefully we aren't looking at hours?" WHY IT TOOK 23 MINUTES. The newest SESSION STATE block in resources/RECOVERY.md quotes a suite figure, and the A23 guard requires that figure to name a producer a reader can re-run. That was read as requiring the run to happen DURING the save. It never did. The guard asks for a producer, not for freshness. WHAT sv DOES NOW. _print_suite_citation reads scripts/suite_record.py and prints the sentence already carrying its own command, commit, counts, exit code and wall clock, plus a currency line saying how far the record sits from HEAD. Whoever writes the state block pastes that sentence rather than re-measuring. The figure travels with its producer by construction, which is measured-rate-travels-with-its-script applied to the 1 number a post-compaction reader trusts most. WHAT IT PRINTS TODAY, AND IT IS NOT FLATTERING. "The last full-suite measurement, 5 FAILED, at 66c735e on 2026-09-20: 8,029 passed, 5 failed, 6 skipped, 1 xfailed, 1692.80 s, pytest exit code 1", with "Record currency: STALE -- recorded at 66c735e, HEAD is 5 commit(s) later" and a note that the tree was not clean when it was measured. A citation that could only ever report good news would be worth nothing. 3 tests added, 15 in the file. main() must call the printer, or the record is written by nothing and read by nobody. The printed sentence must contain a runnable pytest command, which is what the A23 guard looks for. With the record absent, the printer must say so and must not print GREEN -- a failed lookup reads as a failed lookup, and never turns a completed save into a traceback. title: Both paid launchers now refuse to spend against a RED suite record
verbatim: Both paid launchers now refuse to spend against a RED suite record FOUNDER, 2026-09-20, item 2 of the 3 he approved: the launchers should consult the suite record before dispatching. WHY A RED SUITE IS A SPEND QUESTION. This project has twice paid for a round it could not use. On 2026-09-05 a panel round ran with 16 of 17 tool calls erroring and the errors read as results. On 2026-09-10 a round-4 brief carried a gamma figure wrong in its 3rd decimal, and 2 seats spent part of their round on it. A red suite is the cheapest available statement that the harness the seats are about to reason over does not presently do what it says. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DESIGN, and it is what keeps the gate switched on. STALE is the normal condition of every record after every save, because every commit ages it; refusing on age would refuse nearly every dispatch and the gate would be disabled inside a week. RED is a positive claim that something is broken. MISSING is neither, and unknown is not a licence to spend. So RED and MISSING refuse; STALE only reports how far behind HEAD the figure sits. ONE IMPLEMENTATION, TWO CALLERS. suite_record.gate is called by bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py, where 4 of the 6 seats are paid, and by reference_runner_v3.run_preflight. The second placement matters: run_preflight sends a connectivity probe to EVERY configured model, which is a paid call on every paid route, so the check sits above that probe rather than beside it. 2 copies of a rule drift, and a drifted gate is worse than no gate, because it reads as protection that is not there. The override is deliberate and loud: PANEL_SUITE_UNCHECKED=1 or RUNNER_SUITE_UNCHECKED=1. Each prints what it is overriding, by exit code and failure count, on stderr. A silent override turns a deliberate decision into an invisible one. 15 tests, both call sites executed rather than read. Green proceeds and green-but-stale proceeds while reporting its age, which is the anti-vacuity half: a gate that refuses everything is not a gate. Red raises SystemExit(2) from the panel and returns False from the runner, the difference mattering because main() reads that bool and prints its own abort. A refusal must name the failure count and the exact command that clears it, or the gate becomes something people route around. Both orderings are pinned: the panel gate before the first sandbox build, which costs 6.53 s and 606 MB per seat, and the runner gate before dispatch_to_model. Also corrected here: the brief validator's docstring still said 3 of the 5 seats are paid. It is 4 of 6 since the Codex seat became a distinct model and Fable joined. title: Fable is a seat on both dispatch paths now, not only the panel's
verbatim: Fable is a seat on both dispatch paths now, not only the panel's FOUNDER, 2026-09-20: panels and paid experiments should both run 6 models. WHAT WAS WRONG. bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py has carried 6 seats since that day. bench/experiment_11_orchestrator.load_default_config carried 5. The 2 dispatch paths disagreed about what the panel is, and a reader of either file alone would have been correctly informed and wrong. AVAILABLE IS NOT IMPOSED, and the distinction is pinned by a test rather than left to prose. An experiment runs the seats its own RunnerConfig names, and no shipped config in bench/exp56_configs names Fable, so nothing already designed changes composition by this commit. Whether the Exp 40-54 arc should ADOPT a 6th seat mid-arc is a comparability question -- a 6-seat run is not directly comparable with the 5-seat runs before it -- and that ruling is the founder's. It is going in the morning report rather than being decided here. THE SECONDARY ROUTE IS HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT IS. The founder's rule of 2026-05-22 is that every model carries a secondary, preferring the same underlying model reached another way. Fable has no second route. Its secondary is the other Max-subscription CLI seat, Opus, which keeps billing consolidated -- the rule's other stated aim -- and is a DIFFERENT model rather than the same one by another road. A test asserts that difference so it is recorded rather than mistaken later for a defect. It inherits CC2's CLI budget: timeout 900 s and 1 retry, both set in WP4a to stop a timeout cascade on the slower CLI route, rather than the 300 s and 3 retries the HTTP seats use. 9 tests. Both rosters must hold 6; Fable must appear on both; the free CLI seats must be exactly CC2 and Fable on both sides, so a future drift shows up here instead of during a paid round; the seat must dispatch through the CLI rather than bill a route the subscription already covers; and no shipped experiment config may name it. title: The package the panel reviews is now IN the repository, because the sandbox refuses everything else
verbatim: The package the panel reviews is now IN the repository, because the sandbox refuses everything else FOUNDER, 2026-09-19: "The models should also consider the revised CDSFL explorer and other technical resources present in: 'Responses/Codex, ChatGPT & Grok resources/CDSFL_Mathematical_Review_Suite_2026-09-10'. They should also use the resources there are required." THE DEFECT THIS AVOIDS, FOUND BY MEASURING BEFORE DISPATCHING RATHER THAN AFTER. 4 of the 6 panel seats are paid HTTP routes with no filesystem of their own. They reach the repository through 5 tools -- read_file, grep, list_dir, run_pytest, run_python -- and BOTH of the gates behind those tools refuse a path outside the repository root. bench/build_experiment_tools._safe raises "path escapes the repository", and falsifier_verify.scan_falsifier_source returns "a path outside the declared target" and refuses to execute at all. Measured on the 3 things the brief actually asks for: reading the specification, running the reference core, and loading the check results all came back as INTEGRITY VIOLATION at the package's original location. So a brief pointing at the founder's own folder would have sent 4 paid seats to spend their entire tool budget collecting refusals -- which is the 2026-09-05 failure verbatim, where 16 of 17 tool calls errored and the errors were read as results. THE FIX IS A COPY, NOT A WORKAROUND. docs/maths_revision_review_2026-09-10/ holds the package as the founder assembled it, 42 files, 1.8 MB, unchanged apart from dropping 1 of the 2 PDFs -- READING_COPY.pdf and CDSFL_Review_Reading_Copy_2026-09-10.pdf are byte-identical, md5 03a354999c3319aeb2c0404f8cef2d31 -- and a __pycache__ directory. Re-measured after the copy: all 5 access shapes PERMITTED, and the reference core loads and runs end to end through the seat sandbox, returning its 10 public members. It also belongs here on its own merits. A review package that lives on 1 machine's Responses folder cannot be re-run by anyone who clones this repository, and the thing under review should travel with the review. THE BRIEF, as dispatched, is committed beside it as PANEL_BRIEF_AS_DISPATCHED_2026-09-20.md, because bench/logs/** is gitignored and the brief would otherwise exist nowhere in the record. It passes all 8 required checks of scripts/panel_brief_validate.py with 0 unbacked figures. It carries the founder's "no decorative new maths" instruction verbatim, names gamma as a HARD scope boundary that is not up for demotion, and requires each fix to be delivered as a file at a real path with an executed falsifier behind it. TOOL BUDGET RAISED FROM 6 TO 10 ITERATIONS, at the panel's call site only, leaving MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS at 6 for every other caller. title: The parallel suite found 6 failures, 4 of them mine from tonight, and a gate that could deadlock itself
verbatim: The parallel suite found 6 failures, 4 of them mine from tonight, and a gate that could deadlock itself THE RUN. The full suite at 3fd65fb with 4 xdist workers and --dist loadfile: 6 failed, 8052 passed, 38 skipped, 1 xfailed, 931.90 s. Against the serial record's 1692.80 s that is a 1.82x speedup, consistent with the 1.87x measured earlier on a 504-test slice. Every failure was then reproduced SERIALLY at HEAD before being touched, which is what separates a real defect from a parallelism artefact. 5 of the 6 reproduced serially, so they were real. The 6th, the Wolfram LaunchAgent plist check, passes at HEAD and failed only in the throwaway worktree, where the installed plist points at the main checkout rather than the copy. That one is a worktree artefact and is recorded as such rather than fixed. 4 OF THE 5 WERE INTRODUCED BY ME TONIGHT, and the pre-commit hook could not have caught them: it runs 444 tests, and none of these 4 is among them. 1. SILENT TRUNCATION, twice, in sv_postconditions.py. working_tree_is_clean printed the first 5 uncommitted paths and never said what it withheld, and no_credential_is_tracked did the same with offenders. A list cut to N under a heading that reads as complete is a silent falsehood, which is precisely the class the postcondition gate was built to catch -- so the gate shipped carrying the defect it exists to find. Both now state the remainder. 2 and 3. THE ADDITIVE STANDARD'S UNWIRED HALF. scripts/codex_route_probe_2026-09-20.py was reached by nothing: no caller, no citation, no document. The reachability ratchet and its check-mode both went red on it, reporting 148 of 149 = 99.3289%, Wilson [96.2967%, 99.8814%]. Fixed by citing it where its figure belongs, as runway row 0C.29a, which records the probe's result in full: it answered, offered a tool call, wrote (1/2)*(1-1/2)/(1-(1/2)*(1/2)), matched SymPy and mpmath at 0.3333333333333333, 501 tokens, 0.002482 dollars, about 0.196 pence, re-runnable with --run. 4. suite_record.py did not reject an unknown flag loudly. With the `action` argument declared as a REQUIRED positional, argparse reported the missing argument before it reached --fix-timestamps, so a retired flag came back as a missing-argument error. This repository already solved this once, in panel_brief_validate.py, and the same repair applies: nargs="?" and report the absence here instead. 5. THE BURNDOWN TEST IS RED AND IT IS TELLING THE TRUTH, so it is not touched. On 2026-09-18 the master task list gained 1 entry and closed 0. resources/RECOVERY.md already records this: in aggregate the property holds well, 82 closed against 37 added, exact p = 4.5e-05, and the test reads a single day so a quiet one fails it. It goes green when task A8 closes, and A8 waits only on a Section P panel review. AND THAT EXPOSED A DEADLOCK IN THE GATE I COMMITTED 2 HOURS AGO. The spend gate refuses a dispatch on a red suite record. Section P is discharged by a cc2-and-fable round, which is FREE on the Max subscription. So a red suite blocked the review that closes the entry that turns the suite green. A guard that forbids its own remedy is not a guard. The fix is the gate's own stated rationale applied honestly: unknown is not a licence to SPEND, and where nothing is spent there is nothing to protect. suite_record.gate now takes paid_seats and proceeds, loudly, when it is 0. The panel passes len(paid seats in MODELS), which PANEL_ONLY has already filtered, and run_preflight intersects the roster's non-claude_cli entries with the labels cfg actually selects. 1 paid seat still refuses. 19 tests in the gate file now, up from 15. The new ones execute rather than read: an all-free roster gets past the gate with the connectivity probe STUBBED, and the test asserts both that it passed and that both seats reached the probe, so it cannot pass by the round dying early. A paid seat on the same red record still returns False. The panel's call site must forward paid_seats or the exemption is unreachable, and that is asserted on the parsed call, not on the source text. title: The free-parameter flag answered: it is a LINE, not the single point the package exhibits
verbatim: The free-parameter flag answered: it is a LINE, not the single point the package exhibits FOUNDER, 2026-09-19, on the revised model's own self-report: is "free_parameters_can_fit_any_desired_risk: true" good or bad? The answer needed a measurement rather than an opinion, so scripts/free_parameter_degeneracy_2026-09-20.py produces it. WHAT THE PACKAGE ITSELF CHECKS, at outputs/CDSFL_revised_model_checks.py line 219, is 1 line: for every starting risk z and every target, set removal effectiveness s = 1 - target and introduction rate b = target, and the action step returns the target exactly. That exhibits 1 point in the parameter space for each target. Re-run here in exact rationals it holds over all 81 grid cases, and mpmath at 40 digits gives a worst error of 0.0. THE PRODUCER ESTABLISHES SOMETHING STRICTLY STRONGER, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHAT DECIDES HOW BAD IT IS. Solving the same equation for b given ANY s yields b = (z - s*z - d)/(z - 1): a whole 1-parameter family, not an isolated point. An isolated point can be dismissed as unphysical. A line cannot, and a test holds that it genuinely crosses the physical region: solutions with s and b both inside [0, 1], at values of s different from the exhibited 1 - target, exist and land on the target exactly. THE CONTRAST IS THE POINT. The existing collapse form R(1-p)/(1-pR) has 1 free parameter, bounded to [0, 1], with a direct operational meaning. Its derivative with respect to p is R*(R*p - R*(p - 1) - 1)/(R*p - 1)**2, strictly negative at every sampled point on the open unit square, so more review sensitivity strictly lowers residual risk and no choice of p can raise it. That model FORBIDS outcomes. A 2-parameter form with a free direction forbids none until its parameters are pinned by measurement taken BEFORE the outcome they predict. SO THE FLAG IS NOT AN ERROR AND NOT, BY ITSELF, A VERDICT. The package is being honest by reporting it. What it establishes is a condition on adoption: s and b must be measured from data that does not contain the outcome they are used to predict. Whether the revision's validation plan actually does that, or only describes doing it, is question 3 of the paid panel brief and is not decided here. 8 tests, cross-verified with SymPy, mpmath and exact Fractions per the 2-tool rule. The anti-vacuity control is the one that matters: a removal-only action step, (1-s)z, must have NO free direction, and at z = 1/4 with a target of 1/2 the required s comes out negative, which is impossible. Without that control the tests would pass whatever the model did, and a finding that cannot go away is a property of the test rather than of the model. title: A8's manifest guard could not see a falsified state column: 78 rows made to lie, 16 tests green
verbatim: A8's manifest guard could not see a falsified state column: 78 rows made to lie, 16 tests green PANEL-DELIVERED FIX, Section P review of task A8, 2026-09-20, seat fable: ok=True, 8634 characters, 44 tool calls, 517.0 s, 0 paid seats. THE DEFECT. bench/tests/test_cited_logs_manifest_2026-09-17.py opens by promising that it "re-derives every disposition from the repository and requires the committed manifest to match". It did not. Only the tracked state, in both directions, and the missing-versus-exists direction were re-derived. So the state column could be corrupted at will and the suite stayed green. DEMONSTRATED BY EXECUTION, AND REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY HERE BEFORE THE FIX WAS ACCEPTED. Flipping all 78 prefix rows to "missing" -- which is the exact false statement the 2026-09-17 repair exists to prevent, restated inside the manifest itself -- passes 16 of 16 tests. A truncated prefix names no path that exists(), so the old guard was blind to 92 rows, the 78 prefix plus the 14 template, and to every flip between the non-tracked, non-missing states. The manifest is the deliverable of the founder's accept-and-label ruling, and the label IS the product, so a manifest that can be made to lie silently is silent evidence loss. THE FIX is 20 lines: test_every_row_state_rederives_from_the_classifier requires every row's state to equal disposition() run against the tracked set at the recorded commit. Written by the seat, at a real path in its own sandbox, with its falsifiers executed there. P-PASSED HERE BEFORE ADOPTION, per fff-external, and 1 case goes beyond what the seat demonstrated. Clean manifest with the fix present: 17 passed. The 78-row corruption with the fix present: exactly the new test FAILED, 16 passed. And a SINGLE row flipped, directory to template on bench/logs/analysis -- the subtler case the seat did not test, and the one a guard is likelier to miss -- also FAILS it. The manifest was restored byte-identical to HEAD after every mutation, verified by git status. THE SEAT ALSO CORRECTED THE BRIEF I WROTE. It named c9e7b08 as "the classifier repair"; c9e7b08 is an unrelated commit, the brief for Question 9, at which the manifest is merely PINNED. The repair is 9c5eea3, and git show --name-only settles it: 9c5eea3 touches scripts/orphan_citation_era_2026-09-17.py and c9e7b08 does not. The correct order is b8dc6fd, f22e95e, c9e7b08, 9c5eea3. CLAIMS 1 TO 7 OF THE BRIEF ALL HOLD BY EXECUTION. The manifest reproduces byte for byte, sha256 agreeing on both files. The 6 states sum to 575: tracked 184, local_only 52, directory 197, prefix 78, template 14, missing 50, and 197+78+14+50 = 339 is the figure the 3-state version produced. The absent proportion is 50 of 575 = 8.6957%, Wilson [6.6580%, 11.2815%], which statsmodels and a hand-rolled mpmath Wilson at 30 digits agree on here to 4 decimal places with z = 1.95996398454, and which the seat also checked against the local Wolfram Engine through the serial gate, exit code 0, agreeing to every printed digit. The 50 absent paths appear in no ref's history under 2 independent sweeps. The seat wrote its own shell classifier and got agreement on all 575 rows. A PROCESS FINDING, RECORDED NOT FIXED. The seat reported that its sandbox arrived with no .git, so every git-dependent claim in the brief was unanswerable until it cloned the object database into its own copy, read-only on the source. panel_sandbox.build deletes .git by design. That design is correct for confinement and wrong for any review whose subject is the history; the 2 need reconciling before the next history-dependent round. The tracker's resume pointer is updated in the same commit, with the suite state, the parallel-run figures and what is still in flight. title: A8 closes: both seats found a defect the committed suite could not see, and they were different defects
verbatim: A8 closes: both seats found a defect the committed suite could not see, and they were different defects SECTION P DISCHARGED by panel round panel_a8_section_p_2026-09-20, 2 free seats, 0 paid. cc2 returned 36 tool calls in 814.8 s; fable returned 44 tool calls in 517.0 s. Both verdicts were A8 NEEDS THE NAMED CORRECTIONS FIRST, reached independently and on DIFFERENT defects, which is exactly what running without compelled convergence is for. ALL 7 CLAIMS PUT TO THEM HOLD BY EXECUTION. The manifest reproduces byte for byte, md5 0deae2a9fe95eb7d0fa462659f99ac2a, 83,648 bytes on both files. The 6 states sum to 575: tracked 184, local_only 52, directory 197, prefix 78, template 14, missing 50, and 197+78+14+50 = 339 is exactly what the 3-state version labelled missing. The absent proportion is 50 of 575 = 8.6957%, Wilson [6.6580%, 11.2815%], agreed by statsmodels, scipy, a hand-rolled mpmath Wilson at 40 digits, and the local Wolfram Engine reached through the serial gate, exit 0, no Name::tag, computed with Wolfram Language. The 50 are in no ref's history. Both seats wrote their OWN shell classifier and both got 0 disagreements across all 575 rows. FABLE'S DEFECT: THE GUARD COULD NOT SEE A FALSIFIED STATE COLUMN. The file's own docstring promised it re-derives every disposition; only the tracked state and the missing-versus-exists direction were re-derived. Flipping all 78 prefix rows to missing passed 16 of 16. Reproduced independently here before adoption, and CC1 added a case fable did not test: a SINGLE row flipped, bench/logs/analysis from directory to template, also fails it. CC2'S DEFECT: THE MANIFEST WAS AN INPUT TO ITS OWN CENSUS. It is a tracked file under experimental_notes/, so from the second run every one of its 575 row keys was re-read as a NOTE citation of itself: 568 of 575 rows cited by the manifest, NOTE-labelling true for 575 of 575 BY CONSTRUCTION, and 161 rows carrying a cited_by the manifest manufactured for itself. That breaks the rule the producer's own comment states, for the third time in this project: a classifier that reclassifies a path by being written about is measuring the writing. Fixed by a named EXCLUDE constant. Measured after the fix: 0 rows vanish and 0 of 575 states change; only cited_by moves, NOTE 575 to 414. CC2 ALSO FOUND THE REPAIR'S OWN DOCSTRINGS WRONG IN 4 PLACES: "335 = 194 + 78 + 14 + 49" against the measured 339 = 197 + 78 + 14 + 50, and a stale "283 note-cited untracked, only 52 on disk" against a measured 277 and 42. title: The full suite found 12 failures my 448-test pre-commit hook could not, and an audit found 15 more
verbatim: The full suite found 12 failures my 448-test pre-commit hook could not, and an audit found 15 more THE FULL SUITE AT 02302cf: 12 failed, 8126 passed, 5 skipped, 1 xfailed, 2124.59 s. Every one traced to something committed in the previous 6 hours. In parallel, an adversarial audit of the same commit range raised 32 findings and 15 survived 2 independent refuters each. The 2 sets overlap on the most serious item, which is mutual confirmation rather than duplication. THE WORST ONE DEFEATED THE SPEND GATE COMMITTED THE SAME NIGHT. suite_record.parse hard-coded the token order "failed, passed, skipped, xfailed" and had NO GROUP FOR ERRORS. pytest reports a fixture or teardown failure as a separate ERROR category printed AFTER the passes, so "3 passed, 1 error in 0.17s" parsed as failed=0, record derived exit code 0, cite printed GREEN, and gate would have released 4 paid seats against a run pytest exited 1 on. The same rigidity read "8126 passed, 12 failed" as 0 failed, because the failed group only matched BEFORE the passes. THE REPAIR IS NOT AN EXTRA GROUP. The tail is now read as TOKENS against a table of outcomes, and a count word the table does not name REFUSES rather than scoring 0, because scoring an unmodelled token as 0 is exactly how this went wrong. Verified across 5 real tail shapes; "3 passed, 2 quarantined in 0.5s" now refuses by name. 8 tests added, 23 in the file, and reverting the fix takes 6 red including all 3 consequences: the recorded exit code, the gate's refusal, and cite no longer calling an errored suite green. A CLAIM I MADE IN A COMMIT MESSAGE WAS FALSE AND IS WITHDRAWN. c97bdc4 asserted "no existing config names Fable, so nothing already designed changes composition by this commit." bench/exp56_configs/d9_multi_model_panel.json declares 5 seats byte-equal to the RunnerConfig default, and _declared_models treats a default-equal list as NO DECLARATION, so the frozen arm silently became a 6-seat arm with post_convergence_sweep_rounds iterating every one. Caught twice independently: by test_arm_declarations_bind_2026-09-09.py, written for exactly this day, and by the audit. THE FIX NEEDS NO FOUNDER RULING, WHICH THE PREVIOUS ONE DID. Both panel seats had proposed reordering the frozen pre-registration so list-equality breaks, and both said that needs his sign-off. RunnerConfig now carries models_were_declared, set at ingestion whenever a config FILE names the seats, and _declared_models honours it: a key present in the file is a declaration whatever it happens to equal. The frozen file is untouched, the strict xfail is removed deliberately as its own comment demands, and the old heuristic still applies where it belongs -- a config with no models key still falls back. THE WATCHDOG'S EXPECTED_SEATS WAS A TYPED 5 and went stale the day Fable joined, taking 5 tests with it. A typed number could not do the job it was written for, because it goes stale for 2 different reasons and the message cannot tell them apart: the parser missed a seat, or the roster grew. It now reads the live roster, so a mismatch means the PARSER is short, which is the thing worth shouting about. Proved still able to fire: a trimmed orchestrator yields 1 seat and the alarm says "found 1 seat(s), not 6". THE PANEL HARVEST WAS COPYING A GIT OBJECT STORE IT DID NOT WRITE. Both seats cloned the repository's objects into their sandboxes, read-only, because build() removes .git by design and their brief was git-dependent. Every cloned object then read as a CHANGED FILE and the harvest copied it back out: 112 MB across 63 files, 15 inside .git, including pack files already present 1 directory up. Nothing a seat authors is affected; what stops being copied is a store it cloned rather than wrote. THAT ALSO TRIPPED A PROVENANCE GUARD, WHICH IS HOW IT WAS FOUND, and the guard's own docstring records the identical class from 2026-08-30. Any copy of this repository contains the string -SIM because the codebase implements simulated labels, so the harvest was classified a simulated artefact and the seat directory cc2 then read as a bare vendor name: 44 hits, every one the real cc2. The exemption added is CONDITIONED ON EVIDENCE rather than being an exclusion list: it applies only under a round whose own seat records prove a real model answered. Driven both ways by 5 new tests -- a real round is exempt, a SIMULATED round is not, a round with no seat record is not, an unreadable record is not, and a path outside a harvest never is. It fails closed on unknown provenance. Also repaired: the panel records for the A8 round are mirrored into the tracked evidence directory, 12 files and 7.6 MB with no .git among them; the full record is written at experimental_notes/Panel_A8_Section_P_FULL_RECORD_2026-09-20.md, 34,539 bytes carrying both seats verbatim; and the pre-commit gate-cost declaration is refreshed from 444 to 448. AND A FILENAME THAT CLAIMED SOMETHING UNTRUE. docs/maths_revision_review_2026-09-10/PANEL_BRIEF_AS_DISPATCHED_2026-09-20.md had not been dispatched -- the round is gated on the suite being green and the suite was red. Renamed to PANEL_BRIEF_2026-09-20.md and marked with its real status, and the premature round directory under bench/logs is removed until the round actually runs.
