title: A mirrored machine dump became 91% of the citation census, and I put it there
verbatim: A mirrored machine dump became 91% of the citation census, and I put it there THE CLEAN SUITE AT 1f0c383: 5 failed, 8148 passed, 1807.12 s. Both causes were mine and both were caught by guards built for exactly them. 4 OF THE 5 WERE THE LAUNCHER CONFIG-DROP CLASS, AGAIN. The models_were_declared sentinel was added to RunnerConfig.from_dict and not to launcher_core.build_runner_config_from_dict, so test_both_ingestion_paths_agree went red on 4 configs with "launcher=False runner=True". A field added on one ingestion path and not the other is the shape this project has hit repeatedly, and the guard written for it did its job. The launcher path now sets it from the same signal: it reads exp_cfg["models"] unconditionally, so reaching that line at all means the config named its seats. THE 5TH WAS WORSE AND TOOK 3 HYPOTHESES TO FIND. test_the_narrow_form_is_much_smaller_than_the_wide_one failed with wide 7183 against narrow 7042. The first guess, that panel transcripts were inflating it, was REFUTED by measurement: excluding every panel record changed the unique-path count by 0. The second, that this morning's FULL RECORD note did it, was refuted the same way: it contributes exactly 1 unique path. Walking the history settled it. At 02302cf the narrow population was 595; at 87b55d9 it was 7,042, a 12-fold jump in one commit. THE CAUSE WAS seat_proposals.diff, MIRRORED INTO THE TRACKED RECORD BY ME THIS MORNING. It was 7,823,216 bytes, and an ownership analysis over the whole tracked tree shows it FIRST INTRODUCES 6,430 of the 7,032 unique bench/logs paths in the citation population: 91.4%. A breakdown of the diff explains why. 80.3% of its bytes are the seats' .scratch dumps of git rev-list and git ls-tree output, produced while answering a git-history question; 15.6% is a single .pytest_cache/v/cache/nodeids; the rest was the git object stores the seats cloned in because build() removes .git by design. So a transcript of a machine dump was about to become the dominant source of "citations" in the census that task A8 exists to maintain. That is the same defect cc2 found in the manifest 6 hours earlier, one level out, and I created it while recording cc2's finding. THE REPAIR IS AN ASYMMETRY, NOT AN EXCLUSION, and the asymmetry is the whole of it. changes() now skips ephemeral caches and cloned object stores outright, because nobody authors those, and skips the seat's .scratch by default because the proposals diff is what gets mirrored into the tracked record. harvest() passes include_scratch=True, because it writes to the run's own log directory where founder ruling (j) applies: nothing discarded. Verified on the live sandboxes: the diff sees 21 files and the harvest sees 29, and the harvest on disk still holds 48 files and 109 MB including all 19 scratch files. It also matches what the seats were told. The brief requires each fix "delivered as a file in your sandbox repository tree, at a real path", and .scratch is by construction not one. cc2 followed that and delivered scripts/a8_shell_crossverify_2026-09-20.sh. Regenerated, seat_proposals.diff is 286,657 bytes against 7,823,216: a 96.3% reduction carrying 44 actual proposal files instead of a dump. The citation census tests pass. 4 tests pin the asymmetry, and the third is the one that matters: the harvest must be a STRICT SUPERSET of the diff. Getting the 2 the wrong way round would silently drop the seats' working material while looking like a fix, which is why include_scratch is a parameter with both values driven rather than a blanket rule. An earlier version of this fix had exactly that bug -- harvest calls changes(), so excluding scratch there would have dropped it from the harvest too -- and it was caught by tracing the blast radius before committing rather than after. ALSO APPLIED, from the adversarial audit's surviving findings: The panel discarded stopped_reason. The tool budget was raised from 6 to 10 iterations last night and the comment justifying it named the risk exactly: "a seat that runs out mid-verification returns an UNCHECKED it could have answered". The field that answers whether that happened was being thrown away in the same commit, so a seat cut off at the cap was recorded identically to one that finished. The seat record now carries stopped_reason and tool_iterations, and the console line says STOPPED= when a seat did not finish. --resume bypassed the spend gate entirely. run_preflight was its only caller, and main() calls run_preflight only when not resuming. A resumed paid experiment therefore consulted no suite record at all, while dispatching to the same paid seats for every remaining round. The resume branch now runs the gate, keeping the paid-seat exemption so a free resumed run is still unaffected. The appendix inverse guard read only the denominator. INVERSE carried the numerator (pi - R) inside its own pattern and _as_callable hard-coded the same shape, so the numerator the appendix actually wrote was never read: a statement flipped to (R - pi) would stop matching and the round-trip tests would go on passing against a numerator the guard supplied itself. Measured, the flipped form's residual is 2*(-R**2 + R*pi + R - pi)/(2*R - pi - 1), which is not 0. Both sides are now read by balanced scan, and the 2 inverses the appendix states, (pi-R)/(pi-pi*R) and (pi-R)/(pi*(1-R)), both round-trip to 0. 3 documents stated falsehoods after the roster change. docs/REPRODUCING.md and resources/SHORTCUTS.md still routed cx to Codex GPT-5.5 on openai/gpt-5.5; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md still described 5 dispatch paths over 4 distinct model identifiers and explained at length that the 2 OpenAI seats share weights. panel_brief_validate.py still refused with "3 of the 5 seats are paid". All corrected, with the superseded positions retained as history rather than overwritten. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: No model gets a free pass on tool use: DeepSeek's had never actually run
verbatim: No model gets a free pass on tool use: DeepSeek's had never actually run FOUNDER, 2026-09-20, verbatim: "No model gets a free pass on tool use. In this modern world there shouldn't be a condition in which tool use isn't possible for a model? Including Kimi and Deepseek?" HE WAS RIGHT, AND THE ARCHIVE SAYS SO. Counting recorded tool calls across every archived seat reply: cc2 40 of 72 replies with tools and 2,754 calls, fable 40 of 70 and 2,530, cgpt 5 of 9 with 57, cx 5 of 7 with 48 -- and DeepSeek 0 of 8. Gemini likewise 0 of 2. IT WAS NOT A LOGGING HOLE, WHICH IS WHAT I ASSUMED FIRST AND WAS WRONG ABOUT. Probing the seat live, deepseek-v4-pro on DeepSeek's own API returned the literal text "<run_python> from fractions import Fraction ... </run_python>" as its FINAL ANSWER: unexecuted code presented as a result. A second probe skipped tools entirely and answered from 921 characters of reasoning. Neither produced a structured tool call, so nothing ran and nothing could be recorded. MEASURED PROPERLY RATHER THAN CONCLUDED FROM 1 SAMPLE. 8 trials per model across 4 tasks. deepseek-v4-pro on the direct API: 0 of 8 structured tool calls, Wilson [0.00%, 32.44%]. deepseek-flash on the same API: 8 of 8, Wilson [67.56%, 100.00%]. And tool_choice="required" is REFUSED by both with 400 "Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice". THAT LOOKED LIKE A CHOICE BETWEEN CAPABILITY AND TOOL USE, AND IT WAS NOT. The identical model through OpenRouter, deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, made a structured call in 8 of 8 replies, Wilson [67.56%, 100.00%], and honours tool_choice="required" as well as "auto". Fisher exact p = 1.554002e-04 against the direct route, with scipy and an mpmath hypergeometric tail agreeing to every digit and a Yates chi-square at p = 4.652582e-04. So it is the SERVING and not the model, the seat keeps the capable model, and the panel keeps its standard. The orchestrator already carried this route as DeepSeek's SECONDARY; this promotes it to primary for the panel seat only. KIMI K3 JOINS AS A 7TH SEAT, ON THE FOUNDER'S OWN CREDITS. His instruction: "Why not use the Kimi K3 credits I already paid for rather than burn more of my OpenAI credits?" The repository already reached Kimi at moonshotai/kimi-k3 through OpenRouter, which is a proven route and the wrong one, because it spends OpenRouter credit on a model whose credits are already bought. call_moonshot dispatches to api.moonshot.ai, measured rather than assumed: that endpoint authenticates and serves kimi-k3 while api.moonshot.cn returns 401. Probed end to end it answered 1/3 correctly with 1 recorded tool call. IT IS THE ONLY NON-DETERMINISTIC SEAT AND THE RECORD SAYS SO. kimi-k3 refuses any temperature but 1, returning 400 "invalid temperature: only 1 is allowed for this model", while every other seat runs pinned at 0.0. `temperature` is therefore a parameter of the shared tool loop, defaulting to 0.0 so every existing caller is byte-identical. ITS FINDINGS ARE QUARANTINED, on his instruction: "But quarantine its findings specifically, as it is clearly an untested quantity." Quarantine is not exclusion. The seat runs, its reply is recorded in full and its findings are reported; they are not counted as corroboration for what another seat found, because an untested instrument agreeing with a tested one is not independent evidence until it has a track record. A TAG-FORM TOOL-CALL RECOVERY, because the existing one could not see what DeepSeek actually emitted. The orchestrator already recovered DSML markup delimited by the fullwidth pipe U+FF5C; it had nothing for "<run_python>...</run_python>". The parser now recovers both and the caller executes them, so a model that writes tool markup as prose gets real results instead of having its own unrun code returned as an answer. Driven both ways: the exact text DeepSeek returned is recovered, and prose containing "<html>", "a < b and c > d", or "<foo>bar</foo>" recovers nothing, because the pattern is restricted to the 5 tool names this harness serves. BOTH DIRECT-API ROUTES NOW RECORD. call_deepseek and call_moonshot take a `record` list that wraps the executor, so their calls reach the seat record the way the OpenRouter route's already do. Before today recording existed only on the claude_cli path, via a stream-json sink, and on the OpenRouter path, via its own return value. The third route had neither. COST, ESTIMATED BEFORE SPENDING. Worst case at 10 tool iterations with the history re-sent each turn: 151,500 input and 12,000 output tokens per seat, giving $2.07 = £1.64 across the 4 OpenRouter seats against the £10 authorised. cc2 and fable are free on the Max subscription and Kimi is on the founder's own Moonshot credits. The suite record is updated to the green run: 8,157 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped, 1779.49 s, exit code 0 at abc0e5e against a clean tree. title: The panel's paid seats could not read the thing they were reviewing
verbatim: The panel's paid seats could not read the thing they were reviewing FOUND MID-ROUND, by reading a seat's own reply rather than its summary line. The panel gave its seats 5 tools -- sympy_verify, z3_verify, pytest_run, ruff_check, mypy_check -- and not one of them reads a file or runs a Python script. THE BRIEF ASKED FOR WORK THAT WAS THEREFORE IMPOSSIBLE. It told seats to read outputs/CDSFL_revised_model_specification.md, execute outputs/CDSFL_revised_core.py, and search bench/logs for paired pre-repair and post-repair states. All 3 need a capability the seats did not have. THE SEATS' OWN LOGS SAY SO. cx ran pytest_run against 4 standalone scripts and got "no tests ran" 4 times, then reported "Most substantive package claims remain UNVERIFIED in this seat". ds called read_file, list_dir and bash and received "unknown tool" for each: it tried to read the package and was refused. 3 of the 4 paid seats -- cx, ge and ds -- hit the iteration cap at 10 with stopped_reason max_iterations_harvested; only cgpt finished, in 5. WHY THE PRE-FLIGHT MISSED IT. Every seat was verified before dispatch to MAKE tool calls, and not one check asked WHICH tools. A seat calling a tool it cannot use is still calling a tool, so the check passed while the capability it stood in for was absent. The CLI seats were never affected: cc2 and fable reach the tree through Bash, which is why the archive shows them at 2,754 and 2,530 tool calls against cx's 48. THE FIX IS THE UNION, AND BOTH HALVES ARE WIRED. TOOL_SPECS is now openrouter_tools plus build_experiment_tools: grep, list_dir, read_file, run_pytest, run_python, sympy_verify, z3_verify, pytest_run, ruff_check, mypy_check. A spec without a handler is worse than no spec, because the model calls the tool, gets "unknown tool" and spends a turn learning that -- so _TOOL_DISPATCH gains handlers for the 5 access tools, routed to the executor that implements them. Verified live: read_file returns the package's START_HERE, run_python runs VERIFY_PACKAGE.py to its "PASS: 41 files match the package manifest", and an unknown name still returns an error rather than silently succeeding. THE ITERATION CAP IS RAISED FROM 10 TO 16, AND 16 IS COUNTED RATHER THAN ROUNDED. What the brief asks of a seat: 3 turns to read the specification, 1 to run the reference core, 3 for the package's check scripts, 5 for the symbolic and z3 checks of the derivations it must falsify, 2 for the appendix and the live gate, 2 to search the archive. Cost scales worse than linearly because the whole history is re-sent each turn; measured against live OpenRouter pricing the worst case across the 4 paid seats is 1.64 pounds at 10, 3.56 at 16 and 5.23 at 20. The cap is raised WITH the tool fix and not instead of it: a seat that can read the artefact needs more turns, a seat that cannot needs none. THE BRIEF NOW NAMES THE RIGHT TOOL. The package's checks are standalone scripts, not pytest files, and run_pytest returns "no tests ran" on every one of them. The brief says so, tells seats to use run_python with runpy.run_path, lists the 10 tools they actually have, and warns them not to assume a shell. DEEPSEEK'S SEAT WORKED, which is the half of the round that went right. Moved to the OpenRouter serving of the same model it made 21 tool calls, the most of any paid seat, against 0 across 8 archived replies on the direct API. TESTED AND RECORDED, from the founder's Gemini transcript on DeepSeek tool use: deepseek-chat does support tool calls on the direct API under both tool_choice auto and required, on the standard endpoint and on /beta with strict mode. It does NOT rescue deepseek-v4-pro, which returns 0 calls on auto and refuses required with "Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice" on both endpoints. A first beta test here failed on a malformed strict schema -- strict mode requires every property listed in required -- and was redone correctly before any conclusion was drawn. The blocker is thinking mode, not the endpoint and not strict mode. Round 1's replies are preserved and round 2 will be dispatched into its own directory, because the dispatcher writes seat files by name and a re-dispatch into the same directory would overwrite them. title: Round 2 setup: Kimi timed out at 904.5 s and the direct routes ignored the iteration budget
verbatim: Round 2 setup: Kimi timed out at 904.5 s and the direct routes ignored the iteration budget ROUND 1 CLOSED WITH 6 OF 7 SEATS. cc2 103 tool calls and 15,150 chars; cgpt 18 and 20,709, the only paid seat to finish rather than hit the cap; fable 35 and 11,887; ds 21 and 10,561; cx 16 and 5,549; ge 10 and 5,275. kimi returned ok=False, 0 chars, 0 tool calls, APITimeoutError after 904.5 s. THE PROBE MEASURED THE ROUTE, NOT THE WORKLOAD. Kimi was verified before dispatch with a 1-line question answered in seconds, and that is exactly the gap between 'the seat works' and 'the seat can do this job': the real brief is about 2,900 tokens with a 16-iteration tool budget. The moonshot branch now gets 1500 s where the HTTP seats keep 300. BOTH DIRECT ROUTES WERE ALSO IGNORING THE PANEL'S ITERATION BUDGET, which is a second defect the same line hid. call_deepseek and call_moonshot default to max_tool_iters=6 and the panel never passed its own value, so the raise from 10 to 16 reached the OpenRouter seats only. Both now receive PANEL_TOOL_ITERATIONS. NO SEAT TOUCHED THE CANONICAL TREE. The attribution check reports 'no seat is shown to have touched it' with 0 hits for all 3 flagged paths -- bench/confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py, bench/openrouter_tools.py and the brief copy. Those 3 are CC1's own mid-round edits, made while fixing the tool set. The detector distinguishing an operator's edit from a seat's is the property it exists to have. ROUND 2 GOES IN ITS OWN DIRECTORY. The dispatcher writes seat files by name, so re-dispatching into maths_panel_2026-09-20 would overwrite 6 replies that cost money and produced findings. Round 1 is preserved whole, including its sandbox harvest and seat_proposals.diff. title: A review seat could write to the repository it was reviewing, and I opened that hole this morning
verbatim: A review seat could write to the repository it was reviewing, and I opened that hole this morning MEASURED 2026-09-20, 3 HOURS AFTER IT WAS CREATED. Giving the panel's paid seats run_python so they could execute the package under review also gave them an unconfined python3 with cwd set to the repository. A probe wrote a file into the repository root and into /tmp, and both succeeded. WHY THE EXISTING CONFINEMENT DID NOT COVER IT. panel_sandbox confines the CLI seats POSITIONALLY, by working directory, and an HTTP seat has no working directory to confine. The paid seats' confinement therefore rested entirely on their having no filesystem tool at all. Giving them one removed the only thing that was stopping them. The tool's own description says it runs a short read-only snippet and must not write files, which is an instruction and not a guard, and this project has twice recorded panel agents editing the repository mid-run. NOTHING HAPPENED. git status is clean after both rounds and no seat chose to write. The capability existed; the damage did not. THE FIX IS KERNEL-ENFORCED, NOT A DENYLIST. run_python is wrapped in sandbox-exec under a profile that allows reads anywhere and permits writes only to /tmp and /dev. A denylist over source text would be guessable around; this is refused by the operating system. Measured: a write into the repository now raises PermissionError, while the package's own VERIFY_PACKAGE.py still runs to its 41-file PASS, SymPy still evaluates, and read_file still reads. IT FAILS CLOSED. Where sandbox-exec is unavailable the call is REFUSED rather than run unconfined, and the refusal says why. A guard that silently degrades to no guard is the defect it was written to prevent; the cost is that the tool does not run on platforms without it, and the message states that plainly rather than pretending. 5 tests. A relative write is refused, an absolute write is refused, reading and symbolic work still succeed so the guard is not vacuous, and the refusal path is driven with sandbox-exec monkeypatched away to prove it does not degrade. ROUND 2 ALSO LANDED, AND THE TOOL FIX WORKED. All 5 paid seats read and executed: cgpt 30 calls with 12 reads and 9 run_python, finishing rather than hitting the cap; ds 35 with 16 reads; cx 23; ge 16; kimi 13 calls and a 20,187-character reply after returning nothing at all in round 1. Against round 1, where seats ran pytest against standalone scripts, made 0 reads, and cx reported everything UNVERIFIED. Both rounds cost 1.886 dollars, about 1.49 pounds, against the 12 authorised. Round 1's harvest is complete at 232,352 bytes with 2 copies kept and 0 incomplete attempts; round 2 harvested 0 because its seats are all HTTP routes with no sandbox to write to. title: The fix score was measuring absence of harm; the appendix defines it as presence of repair
verbatim: The fix score was measuring absence of harm; the appendix defines it as presence of repair `compute_sk` produces the number `compute_rk` uses as sigma -- `R_base = sk*R_det + (1-sk)*R_old`, term for term against the appendix's Phase 2. Appendix line 214 defines sigma as "Does the proposed fix actually resolve the detected flaw?" and line 377 admits it only as `g(V_pre, V_post)`. All 3 effect gates measured absence of harm instead: does the suite still pass, did it add lint findings, did it add security findings. None asked whether the flaw was gone. EXECUTED, NOT INFERRED. A real repair, a no-op leaving the bug untouched, a fix swapping `/` for `*` so every answer is silently wrong, and one gutting the function to `return None` ALL scored sk = 1.0 ADMISSIBLE, identical to 4 decimal places. With a suite available the 2 destructive ones drop to 0.7333 and are still admitted; the no-op and the real repair stay identical, because a no-op breaks nothing. MEASURED OVER THE ARCHIVE. Across the 135 entries carrying both a verdict and a probe result, sk is statistically independent of whether the fix worked: 104 that cure their own falsifier mean 0.950140, 31 that do not mean 0.950206 -- higher -- with identical medians at 0.978200. Mann-Whitney p = 0.678, Welch t p = 0.992, Kolmogorov-Smirnov p = 0.852, seeded 20,000-resample permutation p = 0.627. 4 tests, none rejecting. 31 of 31 ineffective fixes ADMITTED, Wilson [88.9745%, 100.0000%]. This is why 672 of 902 sit at exactly 1.0: the pile at the ceiling is harm being measured accurately and read as repair. THE REPAIR ADDS NO APPARATUS. `bench/fix_efficacy.py` already applied each fix to a disposable copy and re-ran the finding's OWN falsifier against it -- precisely the comparison line 377 requires -- and was "contributory, never gating", feeding 1 model-facing line. Wired in as `e1_efficacy` at weight 2.0, equal to the heaviest existing gate rather than above it, because "it deserves more" is a judgement and the additive standard does not accept a judgement as evidence. Only the 2 outcomes `ProbeResult.is_verdict` calls verdicts are scored; the 5 equipment outcomes return None and leave the weighted mean, as an unavailable e2_regression already does. Call ordering verified by AST, not assumed. AFTER, same entries: gap +0.285672, Mann-Whitney p = 1.428e-18, Welch p = 9.274e-50, KS p = 6.295e-31. Sigma handed to compute_rk for a fix known not to work falls from 0.9502 to 0.6787. THREE MORE DEFECTS, ALL FOUND BY EXECUTION. * `e4_bandit` has ZERO variance across 902 decisions at the heaviest weight. It is not broken -- fed `shell=True` it returns 0.5, fed `eval` as well 0.3 -- it had nothing to catch at 40% of the weight. That floors sk at 0.4 (SymPy min = 2/5, z3 unsat below it), so the disputed threshold 0.395043 was UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION and could never have refused anything, whatever the corpus. * `_rejection_lines` selected failed gates with `v == 0` against dicts, so the list was ALWAYS empty and every rejection read "hard gate returned 0" while the details held `ParseError: '(' was never closed`. It now reads `score`, and the detail travels with the gate name. * `test_citation_content_2026-09-10.py` unpacked 5 fields from a 7-tuple, so it crashed the first time it found drift instead of reporting it. Fixed; the 6 citations it correctly found were repaired by the guard's own --fix. ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, DECLARED. With every other gate silent a probe verdict alone now writes a terminal status, because ESCALATE's "the evidence gates went silent" is false once an instrument has spoken. T04 is respected by construction. Measured reach 0 of 1,247 archived records, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.3071%]. Tests: bench/tests/test_sk_measures_fix_efficacy_2026-09-20.py, 14 tests, 12 red against the parent. The 2 that are green there are the SymPy invariant pinning compute_rk to the appendix and the new latent-path test. They CALL rather than read, because this defect was 2 modules each describing itself correctly and disagreeing with the other. Suite: 8,256 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed, pytest exit code 0. title: I attacked the maths model's Phase 2 and lost; 3 corrections landed, 0 equations changed
verbatim: I attacked the maths model's Phase 2 and lost; 3 corrections landed, 0 equations changed THE FOUNDER'S QUESTION. "the core of the model itself remains largely unchanged? These are just corrections and qualifications?" -- YES, with 3 corrections rather than 1. The appendix gained 43 lines and lost 1: a false table row, replaced by 2 correct ones. No equation was touched. CC1 PROPOSED THAT PHASE 2 WRONGLY REVERTS TO THE PRIOR, AND WAS REFUTED. A free 2-seat panel (cc2 + fable, PANEL_ONLY, ZERO SPEND, founder asleep) refuted it independently by 2 different derivations in a single round. R_det is the posterior given NO detection, which only holds under P(detect|clean) = 0, and those same assumptions force a second branch: detection, probability q*R_old, posterior 1, risk 1-sigma after repair. The mixture is R_old*(1-q*sigma), exactly R_old at sigma = 0. CC1's premise -- "the evidence still happened" -- was right and is PRECISELY WHY the answer is the prior: the observation occurs on both branches and unrepaired they average back. That is the tower property. The appendix does not discard the observation; the revision discards the unfavourable half. A 2nd defect CC1 missed entirely: at sigma=1, nu=0 the revision returns identically 0, asserting certainty. Re-verified on SymPy + z3. 3 CORRECTIONS, ALL TIGHTENINGS OF STATEMENTS ABOUT THE EQUATIONS. 1. The sigma=0 endpoint is now DERIVED rather than asserted. The old gloss stated it without showing it, which is what invited the misreading. 2. The stated substrate ceiling lim R >= nu is TRUE BUT LOOSE BY 1/q. The attracting fixed point at sigma=1 is nu/q. At q=0.2, nu=0.05 the true floor is 0.25 -- 5x the stated 0.05 -- confirmed against the shipped compute_rk over 20,000 cycles in 3 of 3 cases. README and PAPER corrected too. 3. The stopping-rule gloss holds only BELOW the peak. Delta R is unimodal, not monotone, peaking at R* = (1-sqrt(1-q))/q with second derivative -2q/sqrt(1-q) < 0. At q=0.3, theta=0.05 the greedy rule says STOP across R in [0.855089, 0.999999] -- at the HIGHEST-risk states, where continuing would soon reach a gain 21x larger. Also recorded: Phase 2 never understates risk (z3 unsat) while the detection posterior is the phi=0 no-false-alarms special case and is optimistic. 2 biases, opposite directions, and phi has never been estimated. THE SCORER REPAIR WAS ITSELF BROKEN, BY A SEAT, THE SAME NIGHT. Dropping the "probe returned no verdict" case from the weighted mean PAID FOR DESTROYING THE INSTRUMENT: crashing the falsifier scored 1.0 against 0.6 for letting it run and fail, +0.4000, flipping compute_rk(0.5, 0.3) from risk-up 0.516729 to risk-DOWN 0.441176. 18 of 18 archived records are the post-baseline site, Wilson [82.4121%, 100.0000%]. Fixed: PROBE_BROKEN_AFTER_BASELINE is a DISTINCT outcome, not a detail-string match, and compute_sk returns ESCALATE. Not scored 0, because those 18 details cannot separate a broken patch from a timeout. Crashing now costs -0.6000. STILL OPEN, 2 items, both the founder's: no FINITE weight makes an arithmetic mean decisive (5/(5+w)), sigma is floored at 2/7 while e4_bandit is constant, and attaching NO falsifier still outscores attaching one that fails. NOW-2 RUNNERS. The round-record circularity is closed: holds_review_output is true for a BRIEF ALONE, so a round whose dispatch failed owed a full record of replies that do not exist. was_dispatched added; the mirror still preserves briefs, because narrowing the inclusive predicate would fix a guard by REMOVING a preservation. panel_condition_compliance printed 89 under a label true of 87. Adopted the cc2 seat's e2_regression silent-loss fix after reproducing it. NOW-5. THERE IS NO REVISED EXPLORER ON THIS MACHINE -- the 2 copies are byte-identical. work/math-review/ holds the INPUT COPIES Astra was given; across 4 canonical documents the only substantive difference from today is the line-169 sign. The founder's caution was right and measurable: 11 days stale. AN 8-DOCUMENT AUDIT, 25 claims verified against the LIVE repo with SymPy + a 2nd tool each: 21 ACTIONABLE, 1 WRONG, 2 ALREADY DONE, 1 STALE. 1 applied (a false Reduction Properties row contradicting the appendix's own Phase 3 prose); the rest REPORTED, because they change what the model says about its own assumptions. LARGEST, AND LATENT: a correctly detected, genuinely present flaw that happens to be published can only RAISE modelled risk -- R_new - R_old = nu*(1-R_old), z3 unsat on the negation, 0 of 200,000 NumPy samples. 0 of 39 archived runs carry c_ext, Wilson [0.0000%, 8.9667%], so nothing already run is affected. THE SUITE CAUGHT 4 THINGS I LEFT, INCLUDING MY OWN RULE USED AGAINST OTHERS: the morning report quoted 16 figures with NO declared producer. 4 producers now exist and every number regenerates. Suite: 8,280 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed, pytest exit code 0. title: Mark the 7.12 confound the founder ruled on, and correct my own first draft of it
verbatim: Mark the 7.12 confound the founder ruled on, and correct my own first draft of it THE RULING. The founder, on being asked whether to "charge" the project for the degeneracy 7.12 has carried since 2026-03-31: "What do you mean charge? You mean report it to the police? Lol. Or you mean mark the confound, just as we always have whenever any issue or confound has ever been found? ... We mark the confound in our docs." My word choice was the unclear part; his answer was never in doubt. THE CONFOUND, VERIFIED BEFORE BEING WRITTEN. D* = eps*/(1-nu) carries 2 free parameters and 1 observable. For ANY observed D* there is a valid pair producing it -- eps* = D*(1-nu) for any nu in [0,1) -- solved directly by SymPy, and z3 returns UNSAT on the existence of a D* the model cannot produce. The fixed point forbids nothing. Recorded with what would retire it: an independent measurement of nu, taken from something other than the run being fitted. nu has never been estimated independently in this project. AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST DRAFT, CAUGHT BY P-PASSING THE EDIT BEFORE IT STOOD. The draft claimed 7.12 and the proposed revision were NOT the same object, citing a residual of -eps*z. That residual is real and it belongs to a DIFFERENT substitution -- s = 1-nu with b = eps held CONSTANT -- which was my own choice and not the panel's. Holding eps constant is an extra assumption 7.12 does not make: it defines eps_n as "novel defects surfaced by consequence analysis", a per-round quantity. Under the panel's substitution (nu = 1-s, eps = b(1-z)) the residual is EXACTLY 0 and the 2 are the same object. The earlier "term for term" record was correct and my correction overstated it. Both substitutions are now run against each other in the entry rather than either being asserted. What remains a genuine difference is domain, not form: D_n is a COUNT on [0,inf) and z is a probability on [0,1]. The algebra is identical; the objects counted are not. Appendix: 20 insertions, 0 deletions, no equation touched. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: Astra landed 3 correct hits; 1 of my claims is withdrawn and 1 of my figures had no producer
verbatim: Astra landed 3 correct hits; 1 of my claims is withdrawn and 1 of my figures had no producer THE FOUNDER ASKED WHETHER THIS WAS UNBOUNDED LLM CHURN. It is not. The review explicitly declines to propose new machinery, says "I do not recommend another mathematical rebuild or general panel round", accounts for the 2026-09-21 commits, and recommends LESS work rather than more. All 3 of its substantive claims were checked here by execution and all 3 hold. HIT 1 -- MY CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN AS MIS-SCOPED. I reported that the revision "returns identically 0 at sigma=1, nu=0, asserting certainty". Executed against the revision's OWN `expected_binary_review` on its own worked example: it returns **1/10**, because it averages BOTH observation branches. The 0 belongs to `update()`, the single-branch action step, NOT the procedure. I adopted the claim from 2 seats without running the revision's code. The revision ALSO already carries a `false_positive` parameter, so the phi gap I reported as missing from the appendix is already specified in the revision -- the fix the founder approved is an adoption, not an invention. HIT 2 -- AND IT IS DEEPER THAN MY OWN FINDING. I recorded that Delta R is unimodal and the greedy stopping rule has a premature-stop band. True, but a symptom. The cause is that Delta R is the change CONDITIONAL on non-detection, while the decision is taken BEFORE the branch is known and needs the EXPECTED improvement, which with perfect repair is exactly **R*q** -- monotone, with NO peak and NO band. At R=0.99, q=0.3 the conditional gives 0.004225 and the expectation 0.297000, a factor of **70.30**; at theta=0.05 the 2 rules disagree outright, and z3 returns a witness at R=1/2, q=1/8. This also BOUNDS the Phase 2 conservatism result: that the blend never understates risk is true, and it does not follow that a stopping rule built on it is safe. HIT 3 -- TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN REPORTING, BOTH CONFIRMED. (a) THE FIGURES HAD NO PRODUCER. Mann-Whitney 0.746836, Welch 0.421469, KS 0.900813 and the seeded permutation 0.627119 were quoted against `scripts/scorer_discrimination_2026-09-20.py`, which contains **0** occurrences of any of those tests. Computed inline, never committed. That is `measured-rate-travels-with-its-script`, the rule I had invoked against others in the same session. `scripts/scorer_separation_is_circular_2026-09-21.py` is the missing producer and reproduces every figure. (b) THE "AFTER" SEPARATION IS CIRCULAR. I wired the cure/non-cure verdict INTO the score, then measured that the score separates cure from non-cure, and reported p = 1.428e-18 as evidence the repair works. It is near-tautological. What stands untouched is the BEFORE half: those scores were computed with no cure/non-cure input at all and were independent of whether the fix worked. AND A NON-CIRCULAR TEST, RUN RATHER THAN PROMISED. Extensions are filed by OTHER models and `e1_efficacy` never reads them, so they are a genuine held-out signal. Of 192 admitted entries, 14 later attracted one (7.2917%, Wilson [4.3929%, 11.8659%]). Mean sk 0.964300 extended against 0.951370 not -- the WRONG direction if sk were predictive -- Mann-Whitney p = 0.161004, Welch p = 0.176940. Smallest detectable effect at 80% power is d = 0.7776 against an observed d = 0.3616. UNDERPOWERED: the archive can pose the question and cannot answer it. **A non-circular validation of the repaired scorer requires a NEW RUN**, which makes Astra's third question and the planned simulated study the same instrument. Appendix: additive, no equation changed. 78 targeted guards pass. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: Commission the 5 safe flags, record the 3 harmful ones as study items with reasons
verbatim: Commission the 5 safe flags, record the 3 harmful ones as study items with reasons THE FOUNDER'S INSTRUCTION, 2026-09-21: "enable it all now and test it in the next simulated run and add them all to the programme of study, including the two outstanding ones and confirm explicitly with me that this has now finally been done!" And, on the 3 that would defeat the study: "clearly don't enable those harmful fixes. That isn't what I'm advising you to do. If they have the potential to meet our additive standard, but we don't know yet how well they will work (or at all), then that is what the simulated runs and programme of study are for!" ENABLED (5), in bench/tools/run_simulated_experiment.py: ALREADY ON, and my sweep summary missed it: discrimination_control_ask (:299), severity_calibration_enabled, latent_tagger_enabled. ADDED TODAY: hierarchical_novelty_convergence, sk_score_prose_listings. sk_score_prose_listings IS INERT ON THE DEFAULT TARGET AND THE COMMENT SAYS SO. `--target` defaults to bench/dm/_memory.py, a PYTHON file, and `_gateable_source` returns python unchanged -- verified by execution (.py -> unchanged; .md with a fenced block -> 1 listing extracted). Setting it on a .py target would report "enabled" while proving nothing, which is exactly the difference between a flag being SET and a capability being EXERCISED. TO COMMISSION A19 THE STUDY MUST RUN A PROSE TARGET CARRYING FENCED CODE. NOT ENABLED (3), each with its recorded reason rather than a silent omission: * discrimination_control_blocks -- REFUTED by the 2026-08-12 panel: satisfied by ACCESS rather than DEPENDENCE, defeated by `open(TARGET).read()` with the contents discarded, and it FAILS GREEN, reporting full coverage while discriminating nothing. The study item is whether a DEPENDENCE-based test repairs it, not whether the refuted design works. The founder's own "Go with option A" ruling of 2026-08-30 is what put it behind a switch that cannot silently arm. * immune_memory_consume_rk0 -- the memory is a SINGLE PERSISTENT FILE, bench/state/immune_memory.json, so consumption couples runs. 19 configs have recording on, including 52_factorial_cell_B and _C, so a global enable destroys the 2x2 factorial's independence and the zero-plant control, and the run would complete and produce numbers regardless. Study it with the memory file RESET first, which scopes consumption to that run. * hil_review -- NOT a dormant capability. It is an operator stepping mode that pauses and resumes, and I was WRONG to say it makes a run impossible: it does NOT change the stopping condition, which remains convergence or round exhaustion, as the founder said and as it has been from the start. A CORRECTION TO MY OWN SWEEP SUMMARY. "19 not live / armed by nothing" was measured over JSON configs only. `run_simulated_experiment.py` is a PYTHON config and already armed 3 of the 5. Several sweep agents said so explicitly ("Only bench/tools/run_simulated_experiment.py:299") and my aggregation lost it. OUTSTANDING_QUEUE_to_BR2.md is 29 days stale with 577 of his messages since. The project diagnosed this on 2026-09-09 -- "the defect is in the write-back, not in his answering" -- and the write-back still had not happened. 401 targeted tests pass. title: The write-back: a stale source must say so, and a test now requires it
verbatim: The write-back: a stale source must say so, and a test now requires it THE FOUNDER, 2026-09-21: "You have a habit of asking me more than once about the same things. Sometimes multiple times. And each time I give you an answer, you forget." He is right, and the cause is measured rather than mnemonic. The project diagnosed it on 2026-09-09: "A source written before a founder message cannot record what he said in it ... The defect is in the write-back, not in his answering." `scripts/decision_label_staleness_2026-09-09.py` reports 5 of 5 canonical sources in that condition, 100.0%, Wilson [56.6%, 100.0%]. THE SCRIPT WAS WRITTEN 12 DAYS AGO AND THE WRITE-BACK NEVER HAPPENED. That is the whole lesson: a checker nobody runs is the same as no checker. So this is a TEST, not another script. WHAT CHANGED. * `experimental_notes/OUTSTANDING_QUEUE_to_BR2.md` now carries a supersession banner. It was 29 days stale with 577 founder messages since, and silent about it. It is kept as history -- its items and evidence are a real record of the 2026-08-01 arc -- and it now says so at the top, naming CDSFL_MASTER_TASK_LIST.md and RECOVERY.md as the current sources. * `bench/tests/test_a_stale_source_says_so_2026-09-21.py` requires any canonical source older than 14 days to carry such a banner. THE WEAK FORM IS DELIBERATE. The test does not require freshness -- freshness cannot be legislated and an old document is often exactly right. It requires only that a stale source SAY SO, so history cannot be mistaken for current state. That is precisely the difference between the 2 documents this session tripped over: RUNWAY_to_BR2 carries a dated status banner and was read correctly; OUTSTANDING_QUEUE carried none and was not. NOT VACUOUS, CHECKED. It examines 5 real sources taken from the script rather than re-listed (2 copies drift; that is the defect class execute-do-not-grep names), correctly classifies 1 as stale at 29.3 days and 4 as fresh, and `test_the_banner_check_can_actually_fail` drives it against a fabricated stale-and-silent file and a fabricated banner. 4 tests pass. title: Full scope for the commissioning study: the hold is lifted, 5 arms, 4 rulings outstanding
verbatim: Full scope for the commissioning study: the hold is lifted, 5 arms, 4 rulings outstanding THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT CHANGE. The 2026-09-17 programme holds work in 2 places on a condition that is now satisfied: "The run is already held until the revised mathematical model is reviewed" and "Question 9 holds A19's panel review until the revised mathematical model has been reviewed". THAT REVIEW IS COMPLETE -- 6 paid rounds plus 1 free round across 7 seats, adjudicated against an external assessment on 2026-09-21. 4 items were held on it and are released: the run itself, A19's panel review, the I31 drift detector (whose founder ruling was conditional on exactly this), and the Q6 composer refactor. 5 ARMS, 2 OF THEM NEW. * Arms 1-3 unchanged from the base programme. * Arm 4, the PROSE arm, is not optional if A19 is to be commissioned. All 3 original arms target a Python module and `_gateable_source` returns Python unchanged, so `sk_score_prose_listings` cannot bite. Verified: .py unchanged, .md with a fenced block extracts 1 listing. Setting the flag on a Python target reports "enabled" while proving nothing. * Arm 5, the PAIRED BASELINE at a2a0197 against HEAD, is the only arm that can answer "did the 15 days help". AND WHAT THE STUDY CANNOT DO, BOUNDED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT. 345 commits in the window, 194 touching runtime code, 56.2319%, Wilson [50.9568%, 61.3697%]. title: Final review brief: corrections to what exists, or nothing
verbatim: Final review brief: corrections to what exists, or nothing THE FOUNDER'S BINDING CONSTRAINT, and it is Section 1 of the brief rather than a footnote: "That is not a request for a crap ton of new code, because if that is what you ask the models that is what they will give you." So the brief states, as its first instruction, that a recommendation requiring a new module, gate, channel or parameter is OUT OF SCOPE unless nothing existing can do the job, and that "change nothing" is a respectable answer for any item and for the whole. His goal, verbatim: "I just want a functioning instrument that 'does everything it says on the tin'". WHAT THE BRIEF ASKS, in 6 substantive sections. * Adjudicate an external review (Astra) against CC1's analysis -- 3 claims, all 3 of which CC1 checked by execution and conceded, 2 against itself. The brief explicitly invites the panel to find that CC1 CONCEDED TOO READILY, "that is as much a defect as resisting too long". * The commissioning split: 5 enabled, 3 studied. Is it right, and did the sweep judge anything too harshly? * The `discrimination_control_blocks` CONFLICT, stated as a conflict: his 2026-09-15 ruling says arm and test it; the 2026-08-12 panel refuted the design as satisfied by ACCESS rather than DEPENDENCE and FAILING GREEN. * The routing ladder: 2 of up to 5 rungs reached, `max_rungs` hardcoded at 2 with no config surface, 3 of 6 declared seats never routed to. * 4 rulings the programme of study left open. * The 2 unmeasured rates, phi and an independent nu, each of which would retire a confound. "Name the smallest thing, not the best thing." FIGURES ARE DECLARED AND RE-EXECUTED. title: The panel corrected 2 of my claims and found a gamma demotion in the appendix
verbatim: The panel corrected 2 of my claims and found a gamma demotion in the appendix 6 of 7 seats responded (kimi returned empty at 1116.8s; quarantined seat). TOTAL NEW APPARATUS RECOMMENDED ACROSS ALL 6: NONE. cc2's own summary: "Total new practitioner parameters: zero." The founder's constraint held. THE MOST SERIOUS FINDING IS AGAINST THE APPENDIX, NOT ANY SEAT. cc2's F1: the appendix demotes gamma at line 1087 -- "gamma is no longer a convergence gate at all ... it does not trigger or block termination" -- dated 23-29 May 2026. The founder's two-sided-gate directive of 2026-06-10, TWELVE DAYS LATER, says the opposite, and the shipped predicate agrees with the directive: it reads `theta = cfg.gamma_alt_threshold` and returns False when `gamma_critical < theta` with the reason "BOTH sides of the gate must agree". So the canonical maths document contradicted both a standing founder directive and the running code, and survived 66 lines of revision unnoticed. Corrected in place, preserving what paragraph 2 gets RIGHT (the C4 polarity-inverted gate was retired; the stall detector's gamma trigger is off by default -- neither is the two-sided gate). Reproducer `scripts/gamma_is_still_a_gate_2026-09-21.py` drives the real predicate and fires. AND THE BRIEF'S "CONFLICT" WAS MINE, NOT THE RECORD'S. cc2 F3 and fable both found the 2026-08-12 refutation stale. Verified by execution: the interception probe IS a dependence test -- an access-only falsifier yields DISC_NOT_INTERCEPTED, a member of DISC_INDETERMINATE, so it fails INDETERMINATE and NOT green. The dependence check the panel demanded already exists inside the control it refuted. So the founder's 2026-09-15 "armed and tested live" ruling is ALREADY SATISFIED: with `ask` on and `blocks` off the control runs and records; only the reversal is gated. Both readings hold at once. The operative reason to keep `blocks` off is different and measured in the runner's own comment at :5207-5231: DISC_FAILED cannot separate a non-discriminating instrument from an ineffective fix, and 51.2% of fixes, Wilson [45.0%, 57.4%], do not silence their own falsifier. The stale comment is corrected in place. FABLE CORRECTED MY OWN SCOPE DOCUMENT. Measurement 11's `R*q` is the sigma=1, nu=0 CORNER. The general expected improvement is `R*q*sigma*(1-nu) - nu*(1-R)`, which SymPy confirms is identical to the derivation and which overstates by up to 0.164350 at sigma=0.5, nu=0.1; z3 returns unsat on `R*q` ever UNDERSTATING, so the corner is always an upper bound and never a conservative one. Appendix and scope both corrected. AND I CAUGHT MYSELF BEFORE SHIPPING A CONFOUNDED FIGURE. ds proposed measuring nu by applying each archived fix and counting new failures -- correct, and its literal form needs 902 suite runs. I reached for the archived `e2_regression` readings instead and got 214 of 762 = 0.280840, Wilson [0.250091, 0.313787], concluding the shipped nu_b = 0.05 is 5.62x too optimistic. THAT CONCLUSION IS WITHDRAWN. `_run_effect_regression` computes `passed / total` with NO baseline -- verified by reading the function, which never mentions one -- so e2 < 1.0 conflates a fix breaking tests with a suite that was ALREADY red, which is frequently why a defect existed. The confound runs both ways, so it is neither bound. nu therefore needs the commissioning run, as the scorer's non-circular validation does: 2 open questions, 1 instrument. PROPOSED, NOT APPLIED: record the baseline pass rate beside the post-fix one in `_run_effect_regression`. 1 field, removes nothing, makes nu recoverable without a new run. Converged rulings: routing ladder study-not-raise (4 seats); hil_review nothing to commission (4 seats, unanimous); Wolfram denial stands (unanimous); I31 save/restore not mid-commissioning. Added to Measurement 8 from fable: condition DISC_FAILED on the probe's FIX_CURES result, which separates the 51.2% confound using outputs that already exist. title: The first file a restore reads was lying about git, and age could not see it
verbatim: The first file a restore reads was lying about git, and age could not see it `rs` at 22:14 BST read the operational tracker, which its own header calls the "First resource to read after any compaction or long break", and every git fact in its live resume pointer was false: it named HEAD `d17ab01` and "11 ahead of origin/main — NOT PUSHED" when HEAD was `2b56916`, 23 commits later, with origin/main identical to HEAD and nothing unpushed. The banner guard built earlier today could not catch it and was not at fault. It keys on how OLD a file is — 14 days, from git — and the tracker had been committed 2 days earlier, so no banner was owed and none was missing. Age is simply not the variable that goes wrong in a resume pointer. A pointer goes wrong by being FALSE, and a false one can be hours old. This is `execute-do-not-grep` applied to a document instead of a module: the tracker is internally consistent either way, so only resolving its commit against the repository shows that the document and the repository disagree. `scripts/resume_pointer_truth_2026-09-21.py` resolves each git claim the recovery documents make. Its FIRST version over-reported and was corrected before it was believed: it charged RECOVERY.md with naming a HEAD 399 commits behind, and CURRENT_STATE.md likewise, when both explicitly label those commits historical and CURRENT_STATE.md's header states the git block is by construction the PARENT of the commit carrying it. Recording history must stay cost-free, or a future session gets pressure to delete accurate history to go green. With the disclaimer test added: 1 of 1 sources asserting a current git claim stated it falsely, Wilson [20.6549%, 100.0000%] — wide, because the denominator is 1, and reported that way. After the repair: 0 of 1. Wilson bounds cross-verified by 2 independent routes, statsmodels proportion_confint against the closed form in mpmath at 50 dps, agreement asserted to 1e-12 rather than assumed. 7 new tests, 11 with the sister suite, exit code 0. Two of them hold the disclaimer exemption shut from both sides: a HISTORICAL label 40 lines below a live pointer must NOT excuse it, and a correctly labelled historical block must NOT be charged. The revert check reconstructs the stale pointer verbatim and requires all 3 of its false claims to be found. The stale pointer is demoted in place, not deleted — this file is a record, and it now carries the account of its own defect. title: Arm 3 could not be asked for, and "no weight can close it" was too strong
verbatim: Arm 3 could not be asked for, and "no weight can close it" was too strong TWO THINGS FOUND BY EXECUTION WHILE FOLDING TODAY'S FIXES INTO THE RUNNER. 1. THE SEAT CONTRAST ARM WAS UNLAUNCHABLE. The simulated runner took its panel as `VENDORS[:args.models]` — a COUNT resolved as a PREFIX of a fixed list ordered CC2, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Gemini, Codex, Fable. Arm 3 of the commissioning study is a contrast between Codex-SIM and ChatGPT-SIM, positions 4 and 2, and no value of `--models` selects that pair. Not a flag left off: an arm with no way to ask for it, found before the money was spent rather than after. `--seats` names them instead, order preserved because seat 0 takes the `player_manager` role and sorting would hand it elsewhere silently. Duplicates are refused rather than de-duplicated, because the runner builds 2 lists from this selection and its own comment records that they must agree "or the runner counts a different panel than it dispatches" — so the selection is now resolved ONCE and both lists read it, where before they were 2 expressions that happened to match. Omitted, the prefix behaviour is exact, so no existing caller moves. 11 tests, including one pinning that NO `--models` value yields the contrast pair, so the arm cannot quietly become unlaunchable again. 2. A COMMITTED PRODUCER OVERSTATED ITS OWN FINDING, AND ITS OWN TABLE REFUTED IT. `scripts/scorer_gate_limits_2026-09-21.py` was headed "THE DILUTION NO WEIGHT CAN CLOSE" while printing `w=8 -> sk = 0.384615`, which is below the corrected break-even S* = 0.50493. Two claims had been run together: that no finite weight drives sk to 0 (TRUE, and it is the limit the script computes), and that no finite weight changes the VERDICT (FALSE). A fix is rejected at sk < S*, not at sk = 0, and S* is about one half, so the first does not imply the second. Solved rather than tabulated: rejection needs `w > W_rest*(1-S*)/S*`, finite for every S* > 0 and exactly W_rest at S* = 1/2. On a Python target that is 4.9024 against other gates totalling 5; on prose, 2.9414 against 3. z3 confirms the bound is tight — no w at or below it rejects, unsat. So the dilution IS closable by weight, at a weight making efficacy worth about as much as every other available gate combined. That is a demanding design statement and a decidable one, and it stays the founder's call; recording it as impossible would have foreclosed an option he should get to rule on. MEASURED ON THE PROSE TARGET, EXECUTED AGAINST THE SHIPPED SCORER at `bench/BUILD_BOT_TEST_BENCH_FIX_SPEC.md`: a fix that PROVABLY does not cure its own falsifier scores sk = 0.600000 and is ADMISSIBLE, because e2 is unavailable on prose and the remaining harm gates are clean. The ruff baseline of 4 over the extracted listings reproduces A19's figure, so the substrate repair is working; it is the threshold that is not. S* is computed per entry from nu_b, nu_f, q and R, so the required weight moves with the operating point and the formula is reported in place of a single number. title: The arms needed settings the runner had no way to accept
verbatim: The arms needed settings the runner had no way to accept `CDSFL_Programme_of_Study_2026-09-17.txt` says its 3 arms run "with routing, the falsifier gate and the admissibility gate on, and the hardened gate, merge arbitration and immune memory off", and the same document records, in its own words, that the run it describes "has no launcher". Checked against the shipped config rather than taken from the note, which is 4 days old: every item in that sentence was already reachable except merge arbitration, which was a bare `True` in the config literal with no flag anywhere. `--no-merge-arbitration` exposes it, DEFAULT UNCHANGED. Turning it off by default would disable a shipped capability with no measurement showing the run is better without it, which the additive standard forbids in that direction. The flag makes the pre-registered configuration reachable; which arms use it stays the founder's. `--domain` likewise: it was the literal "statistics" for every target, and it selects the composer's per-domain directives, so a registry-engine or markdown target was being briefed as a statistics problem. THE PARSER IS NOW BUILDABLE WITHOUT RUNNING THE EXPERIMENT. While it lived inside `main()`, the only way to check that a flag existed and reached its config field was to read the source — and a test that reads source proves only that the file describes itself consistently. `build_parser()` lets the tests parse real argument lists and assert on the namespace, which is the executing form. 16 tests. A FALSE ALARM RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-RAISED. The config sets `gamma_telemetry_only_until=20` against `max_rounds` of 16 by default and 8 for these arms, which reads like a gate that can never fire. It is deliberate and already documented at `reference_runner_v3.py:14799`: there are 2 gamma gates on 2 different series. `_check_gamma_gate` on `gamma_all` is telemetry-only in every live config by design; `_check_gamma_alt_convergence` on `gamma_critical` is the founder's 2026-06-10 two-sided gate and is ACTIVE on the critical-quiescence path. Gamma is exercised. The record answered this before I could mis-report it. CANARY SEEDING IS UNAVAILABLE AND THAT BOUNDS WHAT THE RUN CAN CONCLUDE. The sandboxed launcher seeds only when `CDSFL_CANARY_CATALOGUE` names a catalogue; no catalogue exists outside the repository and the catalogue is answer-key material, so it is the founder's in person. Without seeded ground truth a CRITICAL_QUIESCENCE convergence cannot distinguish "the target is clean" from "the panel is dead" — the launcher's own note records that happening on 2026-09-01 with a vacuous curve. Generating one alone is refused by design: `Canary.generator` is load-bearing and `detection_rate` will not report on a single-generator held-out set. The route that works is cc2 and fable as independent generators, which is free and follows. title: 8 red tests, all 8 reproduced, all 8 accounted for
verbatim: 8 red tests, all 8 reproduced, all 8 accounted for THE SUITE RAN RED AND THE NOTIFICATION SAID IT WAS GREEN. `pytest` reported 8 failed, 8286 passed, 5 skipped, 1641.45 s, captured exit code 1. The harness notification said exit code 0, because the background command ended with a trailing `tail` and the shell returns the LAST command's status. This is the exit-code-masking defect corrected earlier today in its pipe form, reintroduced in its sequence form. The captured `$?` in the output file is the reliable value; the notification is not. All 8 were reproduced SERIALLY before anything was touched, which is what separates a real defect from a parallelism artefact. All 8 reproduced. 4 TESTS — UNMIRRORED PANEL RECORDS. The `final_review_2026-09-21` round sat in the ignored log directory and had never been copied out. The test named its own remedy. 11 files copied; the check now reports 90 of 90 rounds preserved, 100.0000%, Wilson [95.9064%, 100.0000%], Clopper-Pearson [95.9841%, 100.0000%]. 2 TESTS — THE UNREACHED-SCRIPT RATCHET. `estimate_nu_from_archive_2026-09-21.py` and `gamma_is_still_a_gate_2026-09-21.py` were reached by nothing. Both are evidence for live questions and are now cited in the morning report, which is the honest discharge rather than a suppression: the first's conclusion is WITHDRAWN and the note says so. 167 of 167 reached. 1 TEST — A GUARD THAT READ SOURCE INSTEAD OF RUNNING IT. `test_the_simulated_launcher_sets_both_lists` required the literal string `models=VENDORS[:args.models]` to appear in the launcher. The launcher now has both lists read one resolved variable — a STRONGER guarantee than 2 expressions that happen to agree — and the text matcher went red on the improvement. Its real failure is that it cannot tell a correct refactor from a regression. It now RUNS the launcher with both config constructors intercepted and compares the lists actually built. Mutation-verified: diverging RunnerConfig.models yields `['Codex-SIM','ChatGPT-SIM'] vs ['CC2-SIM','DeepSeek-SIM']` and a red test. 1 TEST — A PAID PANEL'S OUTPUT WAS NEVER PRESERVED, AND 1 SEAT DIED UNDIAGNOSED. The final review round returned roughly 92,000 characters across 6 seats and had no FULL RECORD note. The standing requirement is that external review output is kept "in full and in unfiltered format"; 107,833 bytes now are. The kimi seat returned 0 characters with ok=False after 29 SUCCESSFUL tool calls over 1116.8 s, its last call having computed `expected_binary_review(1/2, 4/5, 0, (1,0), (0,0)) = 1/10`. So the work was in flight and the synthesis returned nothing. THE CAUSE CANNOT BE RECOVERED, AND THAT IS THE DEFECT: `stopped_reason` and `tool_iterations` are assigned only in the openrouter branch of `confer_maths_panel_2026-09-05.py`, while the record is built with `locals().get(...)`, so on the moonshot route those fields are None BY CONSTRUCTION rather than because nothing went wrong. Not a recurrence of the r3 temperature defect, which is fixed and does reach this route; it is the same SHAPE as the r3 `ge` entry — a diagnostic living on a sibling path and not on the one the paid seat runs. Recorded as a P5 shortfall with `fixed: false`. The instrumentation gap is the actionable item, and it is deliberately NOT attempted tonight: validating a change to a paid dispatch path costs a paid dispatch. It does not block the commissioning study, which is simulated and spends nothing. 6 of 7 seats carried a disagreement, so the round was not smoothed to consensus — 1 seat died. Also: the arm caller the 17 September programme asked for, "a caller and a test that asserts the settings the runner actually received". 16 tests feed each arm's own argv through the runner's own parser. One of them failed at first for a reason worth recording: a module loaded by path must be registered in `sys.modules` BEFORE execution, or `dataclasses` cannot resolve the string annotations that `from __future__ import annotations` produces, and the class dies with "'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__'" — which reads like a bug in the module under test and is a bug in the loader. title: Two correct safety mechanisms deadlocked every sandboxed simulated run
verbatim: Two correct safety mechanisms deadlocked every sandboxed simulated run The sandbox SEVERS git history on purpose, so `git diff` cannot hand a seat the planted set. The runner then confines the panel to a disposable git worktree so a seat's relative writes cannot reach the live target, and REFUSES when it cannot build one. Inside the sandbox it never can. Measured, not predicted: arm 1 of the commissioning study exited 2 at 22:51:57 BST with "fatal: not a git repository". No sandboxed simulated run could launch. What the refusal is FOR is the LIVE repository. Inside the sandbox the whole tree is already a throwaway copy, so that protection is already in force and the right move is to build the same disposable cwd by COPYING. The wrapper now exports the directory it created and the runner VERIFIES it against its own resolved root, so a stale or hostile value naming another directory does not unlock the fallback and the refusal still stands where it should. title: Lock the sandbox fallback: 12 tests, mostly on the lock rather than the key
verbatim: Lock the sandbox fallback: 12 tests, mostly on the lock rather than the key The previous commit added an escape hatch to a safety refusal, and an escape hatch is the thing that must be shown not to open by accident. The marker is a DIRECTORY rather than a flag so it can be VERIFIED: the wrapper exports the tree it built, the runner resolves it and compares against its own root. Unset, empty, or naming another directory -- none unlocks anything. One test records where the protection actually rests. If the live checkout were exported as the sandbox root the predicate would be satisfied by construction, so the marker must not be the only thing between a seat and the live target. It is not: inside a real checkout `git worktree add` SUCCEEDS and the fallback branch is never reached. The test asserts that the live repo is a git checkout, because the day it stops being one the marker becomes load-bearing alone. The copy excludes .git, logs and __pycache__. Copying .git back would restore through `git diff` exactly the planted set the sandbox severs history to hide. title: My own guard would have gone red on every commit, and a test passed by accident
verbatim: My own guard would have gone red on every commit, and a test passed by accident TWO FAULTS IN THE RESUME-POINTER CHECK I WROTE 45 MINUTES EARLIER, both found by executing it rather than re-reading it. 1. IT REQUIRED THE POINTER TO NAME THE CURRENT HEAD. A resume pointer is written once; HEAD moves with every commit. Run after 6 further commits it failed, and it would have failed after every commit thereafter, including commits with nothing to do with project state. A check that is red by default is one that gets disabled, and a disabled check is worse than none. What a resume pointer legitimately does is record where a session stopped. The named commit must be REAL and an ANCESTOR of HEAD -- which still catches a fabricated hash, a rewritten history or another branch -- and its distance is now reported as INFORMATION. The original defect is still caught by the part that always should have carried it: "11 ahead of origin/main -- NOT PUSHED" are claims about the state RIGHT NOW, and both were false. 2. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` CONFLATES "no" WITH "git failed". It exits 0 for ancestor, 1 for not an ancestor, and other codes for errors. Reading any non-zero as "not an ancestor" produced a confident false statement -- "it is on another branch or from a rewritten history" -- about a repository git had merely failed to read. AND THE TEST WAS GREEN FOR THAT EXACT REASON. The revert check monkeypatches REPO to a tmp directory and redirected only `git`, not the raw subprocess call, so `merge-base` ran against a non-repository, errored, and was counted as a refutation. It asserted 3 failures and got 3 -- the wrong 3. `git_rc` now sits beside `git` so both redirect together, and the test asserts the 2 present-tense claims plus the ancestor NOTE by name rather than counting them. 9 tests. 2 are new: a commit from another history is charged, and a git error is reported as UNCHECKED rather than as refuted. NOTE ON THIS MESSAGE. The first attempt was written with `-m` inside double quotes, so the shell executed every backticked term as a command and silently deleted them from the record -- "command not found: merge-base". Amended through a heredoc, which is how the rest of tonight's commits were written. title: The run's first real finding: seats understate their own R_k, 17 times of 17
verbatim: The run's first real finding: seats understate their own R_k, 17 times of 17 Round 0 of commissioning arm 1 closed at 23:09 and the pipeline ran end to end: 8 CONFIRMED, 0 REFUTED, 3 to HIL from the falsifier gate, with tools deciding rather than models voting; 17 corrected copies accepted, 0 refused, 0 unmatched, 0 dropped; discrimination control DISCRIMINATES=5, INDETERMINATE_ERROR=2, NO_DISCRIMINATION=1; 1 mechanical fault escalated to a human rather than closed. `e1_efficacy` FIRED IN A LIVE RUN — `FIX_CURES_ITS_OWN_FALSIFIER` on C0007 — so tonight's scorer repair is commissioned in practice, not only in tests. Then R_k validation rejected 17 self-reported proofs: CC2-SIM 4, Gemini-SIM 4, DeepSeek-SIM 5, ChatGPT-SIM 4, and Codex-SIM PASSED 5 of 5. EVERY ONE OF THE 17 DELTAS IS POSITIVE. Recomputed exceeds stated in 17 of 17 and never once the other way: 100.0000%, Wilson [81.5682%, 100.0000%], Clopper-Pearson [80.4936%, 100.0000%]. Exact sign test against p=0.5 gives 1.525878906e-05, computed twice and agreeing to 1e-12 (scipy binomtest against the closed-form tail in mpmath at 50 dps). Mean delta 0.204294, median 0.260000, range 0.059000 to 0.348000; t-test p=1.421603e-06, Wilcoxon p=1.525879e-05. A seat making arithmetic slips errs in both directions. A perfectly one-sided result is a systematic difference between what the seats compute and what the runner computes. The seats report LOWER residual risk than the runner derives, which in the model's own terms means overstating how much a fix accomplished. WHY IT MATTERS. `severity_is_proven` requires a stamped R_k proof that RECOMPUTES before a severity demotion is allowed. If proofs routinely fail to recompute, that interlock is never satisfied and the severity-calibration machinery this run exists to exercise cannot reach its demotion path, for a reason that has nothing to do with severity. NOT EXPLAINED, DELIBERATELY. Codex-SIM passed 5 of 5 while 4 seats failed, and every seat is the same stand-in model, so this is not a capability difference. It depends on the findings or their inputs. The producer establishes that a cause exists and that it is one-directional; naming it is the next question. title: Correct 4 things in the R_k finding, one of them material
verbatim: Correct 4 things in the R_k finding, one of them material 1. IT DID NOT REJECT ANYTHING. `_validate_rk_computation` says in its own docstring "Advisory only -- logs discrepancies, never rejects findings". My first write-up said "rejected 17 self-reported proofs". It FLAGGED 17. 2. THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED PRECISELY RATHER THAN SWEEPINGLY. I wrote that the interlock "is never satisfied". It is not globally unsatisfiable -- Codex-SIM's 5 passed. `severity_is_proven` accepts PASS and WARN (0.05 tolerance) and refuses FAIL; all 17 deltas run 0.059 to 0.348, all beyond WARN. So of 23 entries validated this round, 5 are eligible for demotion and 18 are not (17 FAIL plus 1 SKIP) -- roughly 3 in 4, which is the accurate claim. 3. THE LEADING CANDIDATE CAUSE IS PARSING, AND I SHOULD HAVE SAID SO FIRST. The validator receives no structured parameters: it extracts `R_old` and the stated final `R_k` OUT OF THE MODEL'S OWN PROSE with regular expressions, then recomputes. A one-directional gap is at least as consistent with the extractor picking up a different number than the model used as with the models mis-applying a formula they quoted. The standing warning in this project is that parsing errors have plagued it, and prose-to-parameter extraction is where that bites. Calling it "a formula or input discrepancy" buried that. 4. THE SIGN IS NOT IN THE LOG. The logged `delta` is `abs(model_rk - recomputed)` and carries no direction. The one-sidedness was recovered from the `model=` and `recomputed=` values. A reader trusting the logged field could not have found it, and that is worth recording for whoever takes this up. The measurement itself is unchanged: 17 of 17 one-sided, Wilson [81.5682%, 100.0000%], sign test 1.525878906e-05 on 2 agreeing routes, mean delta 0.204294. title: 6 red, 4 real and mine, 1 a guard doing its job, 1 an artefact of my own commits
verbatim: 6 red, 4 real and mine, 1 a guard doing its job, 1 an artefact of my own commits THE FULL SUITE AT `6829faf`: 6 failed, 8349 passed, 5 skipped, 1586.64 s. All 6 reproduced or explained. 1. A CREDENTIAL LEAK I INTRODUCED 40 MINUTES EARLIER. The sandbox fallback copied the tree with a bare `shutil.ignore_patterns(".git", "logs", "__pycache__")` -- a list about SIZE AND NOISE that says nothing about secrets, so it would materialise `.env` in a directory the panel can read. Caught by `test_no_repo_copy_in_bench_still_uses_the_secret_blind_exclusion_list`, whose stated reason for existing is that the same leak had already reached 6 copy sites. Now uses `secret_ignore`, which keeps those exclusions and adds the credential patterns, so the rule lives in 1 place instead of 5. 19 tests green. 2 and 3. BOTH NEW PRODUCERS IGNORED `--help`. Neither parses arguments, so the flag was silently dropped and the whole measurement ran -- a git walk, in one case -- while exiting 0, which is indistinguishable from answering. The founder's ruling on this class is that a `--help` must never cost money. Both now call `answer_help` before doing any work. 48 tests green. 4. A TEST ORACLE THAT WAS WRONG, AND PRE-EXISTING. `test_citation_index_agrees_with_git` compared an index built by extracting whole `bench/logs/[\w./-]+` TOKENS against `git grep`, a SUBSTRING search. Those agree on every path except one that is a PREFIX of another, where they must disagree by construction. It surfaced on a path truncated at a column boundary -- `...report.j`, missing `son` -- which genuinely appears that way in 3 tracked files dated 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-17. THE INDEX WAS RIGHT: claiming a citation of `report.j` because `report.json` is present is a false citation. The oracle now matches on the same terms the index uses. NOT CAUSED BY ME: the test samples every 19th path, so mirroring 11 panel-record files shifted the sample onto it. 5. MY OWN REWRITE, DEFEATED BY A GUARD THAT WAS RIGHT. The in-process version passed alone and failed in the suite because the launcher REFUSES to start when `immune_agents` was imported before `CDSFL_SHADOW_LOG_DIR` was set -- a simulated run would otherwise append to the archival record. In a full suite another test has already imported it. The guard was right; weakening it would have been the wrong fix. The launcher now runs in a FRESH SUBPROCESS where that guard passes on its own terms. Mutation-verified: diverging the lists fails, reverting restores green. 6. NOT A DEFECT. `test_fresh_clone_is_actually_run` refused with "the clone is at 93a39893 and this tree is at c17e1ca9; refusing to report a measurement of a different commit as this one's". I committed 4 times while the suite ran. The guard is correct and the lesson is the same one the first run of the evening taught: a suite run is only meaningful on a tree that does not move under it. title: Three more observations from arm 1, one of which vindicates an earlier decision
verbatim: Three more observations from arm 1, one of which vindicates an earlier decision THE OLD 900s SEAT CAP WAS MARGINAL AND FRESH DATA SAYS SO. Over 25 dispatches: median 600 s, mean 489 s, max 870 s. None would have died at 900 s -- but the slowest sits at 96.7% OF IT. Same "ceiling inside the distribution" shape measured on 2026-09-08, when the largest success was 94% of the cap and 3 of 6 seats were killed at exactly 900 s. The raise to 3600 s is vindicated rather than asserted: the slowest dispatch here uses 24.2% of the current cap. THE B_v2 VERIFIER ABSTAINED ON EVERYTHING IT SAW. 8 of 8 verdicts are UNCERTAIN (0.15), all for one stated reason -- "not a numeric/SMT-verifiable claim". 100.0000%, Wilson [67.5592%, 100.0000%], Clopper-Pearson [63.0583%, 100.0000%]. Small denominator and the run continues, so this is an observation, not a conclusion. Not obviously a defect either: a code-review finding genuinely is not an SMT claim. But on a target of this kind the verifier contributes nothing, which is precisely what the programme's measurement 10 asks -- whether a mechanism the launcher declares actually fires. THE FALSIFIER GATE'S YIELD CHANGED SHARPLY. Round 0: 8 CONFIRMED, 0 REFUTED, 3 to HIL. Next gate: 0 CONFIRMED, 0 REFUTED, 5 to HIL. Nothing refuted in either. Whether that is findings getting subtler or falsifiers losing the ability to decide is NOT established here and needs the completed run. title: Checking the whole set moved both headline figures, which is why one checks
verbatim: Checking the whole set moved both headline figures, which is why one checks The R_k figures reported 25 minutes ago came from ROUND 0 ALONE. Arm 1 kept running, and rounds 1 to 3 change them. THE ONE-SIDEDNESS IS NO LONGER PERFECT. 18 of 19, not 17 of 17: one case now has the recomputed value LOWER. 94.7368%, Wilson [75.3613%, 99.0648%], exact sign test 7.629394531e-05. Still decisive, no longer absolute, and the honest words are "overwhelmingly one-directional" rather than "every single one". THE PROOF PICTURE IS BETTER THAN ROUND 0 IMPLIED. title: Arm 2 converged VACUOUSLY, and the panel/single-seat contrast is the first result
verbatim: Arm 2 converged VACUOUSLY, and the panel/single-seat contrast is the first result ARM 2 (single seat `CC2-SIM`): 4 rounds, converged at 3, 9 findings, 56.7 min, exit code 0, live target unmodified. Its reason is the point: CRITICAL_QUIESCENCE_CONVERGED (two-sided gate, VACUOUS CURVE): zero critical findings across the ENTIRE run (history=[0, 0, 0, 0]) over 9 finding(s) THE VACUOUS-CURVE GUARD EXISTS AND FIRES, WHICH IS BETTER THAN I ASSUMED. This report warned IN ADVANCE that a convergence by finding nothing could not be told from a dead panel. `_check_gamma_alt_convergence` makes that distinction itself and labels the convergence VACUOUS. THE CONTRAST. Arm 1: 5 seats, 8 rounds, 69 findings, 2 criticals, gamma_critical 0.000 -> 0.649, never converged. Arm 2: 1 seat, 4 rounds, 9 findings, 0 criticals, gamma_critical 0.000 throughout, vacuous convergence at round 3. Novel-crit series [1,1,0,0,0,0,0,0] against [0,0,0,0]. THE PANEL FOUND CRITICALS; THE SINGLE SEAT FOUND NONE, which is why its curve never left zero. THE PRODUCTIVITY FIGURES CUT THE OTHER WAY, SO BOTH ARE REPORTED. 69 against 9 is 7.6667x, but arm 1 spent 40 seat-rounds to arm 2's 4, so PER SEAT-ROUND the single seat was MORE productive: 2.2500 against 1.7250. Five seats did not give five times one seat. What they gave was criticals, 2 against 0. SUGGESTIVE, NOT ESTABLISHED. One run per arm; 2 against 0 is a tiny denominator; both arms ran the same underlying stand-in model under different labels, which the runner reports as "5 seats, 1 distinct models"; with no canary catalogue there is no ground truth to say whether those 2 criticals were real or whether the single seat missed real ones; and the arms ran different round counts. TWO CONFIRMATIONS. The live break-even printed during scoring is S* = 0.505, matching the 0.50493 the e1 weight thresholds (4.9024, 2.9414) were derived against. And the scorer admitted everything again: 6 evaluated, 6 ADMISSIBLE. AND THE GATE-COUNT GUARD REFUSED A SECOND TIME THE SAME NIGHT, exactly as the tracker predicted an hour earlier: 3818 -> 3859 tracked, 4405 -> 4446 on disk. Updated with both interval pairs. THE RECURRENCE IS NOW FLAGGED IN THE DOCSTRING AS A DESIGN QUESTION: every completed run appends gate records, so a figure embedded in prose is perishable by construction and this guard goes red after every arm. That is the same "red by default" shape corrected in `resume_pointer_truth_2026-09-21.py` tonight. The difference is that here the number is load-bearing in prose a reader sees, so whether to state a figure at all or cite the producer and a date is the founder's call, not mine. Arm 3 launched 03:58 with `panel 2 agents as ['Codex-SIM', 'ChatGPT-SIM']` -- the pair no value of `--models` could select before tonight. title: Arm 3 complete, and 3 arms make a trend in 2 directions at once
verbatim: Arm 3 complete, and 3 arms make a trend in 2 directions at once ARM 3, the seat contrast (`Codex-SIM` + `ChatGPT-SIM`) that could not be requested at all before last night: 8 rounds, NO convergence, 32 findings, 155.0 min, exit code 0, live target unmodified. Like arm 1 it ran out of rounds rather than material -- final gate `novel=4, contested=2`, residual sweep 26. THE 3 COMPLETED ARMS. 1 seat (arm 2): 4 rounds, 9 findings, 0 criticals, 2.2500/seat-round, VACUOUS convergence at 3 2 seats (arm 3): 8 rounds, 32 findings, 1 critical, 2.0000/seat-round, no convergence 5 seats (arm 1): 8 rounds, 69 findings, 2 criticals, 1.7250/seat-round, no convergence BOTH TRENDS ARE MONOTONE ACROSS ALL 3 ARMS AND RUN IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Criticals rise with panel size (slope 0.4615, r = 0.9608). Findings per seat-round fall (slope -0.1221, r = -0.9680). PANEL SIZE BUYS CRITICALS AT DECLINING PER-SEAT EFFICIENCY: 5 seats gave 7.6667x the findings of 1 seat for 10x the seat-rounds, and what they bought that the single seat never produced at all was criticals. AT n = 3 THE p-VALUES ARE MEANINGLESS AND ARE NOT QUOTED AS SIGNIFICANT. Three points fit a line whatever they do. What is worth keeping is that both orderings are strict with no exception: 0 < 1 < 2 criticals, 2.2500 > 2.0000 > 1.7250. CONFOUNDS UNCHANGED AND RESTATED. Same underlying stand-in model in every arm, which the runner reports itself as "5 seats, 1 distinct models". No canary catalogue, so no ground truth on whether those criticals were real or whether the smaller panels missed real ones. Unequal rounds, because arm 2 stopped at 3 -- and its convergence was VACUOUS, so its efficiency edge is partly an artefact of stopping early on an empty curve. THE GATE-COUNT GUARD REFUSED A THIRD TIME, as predicted: 3859 -> 4020 tracked, 4446 -> 4607 on disk. It then refused AGAIN because I corrected the counts and left the intervals stale -- which is precisely what its own message warns: "fixing one leaves the pair still lying". Both pairs now recomputed. Arm 4, the prose arm that commissions A19, launched 06:33.
