title: feat: a mechanical cy trigger, because the 30-minute cap was a half-truth
verbatim: feat: a mechanical cy trigger, because the 30-minute cap was a half-truth THE FOUNDER'S INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-02: "you may have to create a mechanical trigger for cy to wake you up so this cannot happen again." What happened was a detached run proceeding for hours on the night of 2026-09-29/30 with nothing watching it, explained away by the assistant saying its monitors cap at 30 minutes. THAT EXPLANATION WAS HALF TRUE AND WHOLLY MISLEADING. One Monitor arming does cap at 1,800,000 ms. It also notifies at expiry so it can be re-armed, and that notification is itself a wake-up, so the cap bounds one arming and not the watch. The mechanism was available and was not used. Separately, a 60-second cadence was never the model's job by hand: 9 hours at 60 s is 540 checks. SO THE WORK IS SPLIT. Mechanical polling here, costing nothing; escalation to the model only on an event worth waking for, each stdout line being one such event; and a second independent wake path, because the failure being prevented is a watcher that went quiet. SILENCE IS AN EVENT, which is the whole design. The hole was not a missing alarm, it was an alarm with nothing to say: a watcher that greps only for trouble stays mute through a hang, a kill or a crashloop, and mute looks exactly like healthy. So absence is reportable — `--stall-seconds` without log growth, and the death of the process — neither depending on the run writing anything. ITS OWN GUARD FOUND A DEFECT OF THE SAME CLASS. `last_change` was seeded from the clock, so a watchdog attached to a run that had already stalled an hour earlier would stay silent for a further --stall-seconds: it inherited a false assumption of health. Now seeded from the log's mtime, and reading bytes already on disk is no longer counted as advance. 17 tests, all executing the script as a subprocess, including anti-false-positive cases and the requirement that it announce both ARMED and CLOSED so a silent watchdog is impossible. ALSO: scripts/night_run_brief_figures_2026-10-02.py, which re-executes the run record rather than quoting it. 3 of 9 commissioning runs converged, 33.3333%, Wilson [12.0584%, 64.5798%] with statsmodels and mpmath agreeing to 3.55e-15 pp; all 3 convergences at round 4; 2 halts at round 1, both on the prose target; 4 runs whose report records no stop reason while completion_signal says UNRECORDED_STOP. title: fix: the cy watchdog reported a halt exactly like a convergence
verbatim: fix: the cy watchdog reported a halt exactly like a convergence THE FREE PANEL BROKE THE WATCHDOG WITHIN AN HOUR OF ITS OWN TESTS CLAIMING IT COULD NOT HAPPEN, and the finding is the defect class this script exists to prevent, reproduced inside the fix for it. cc2, verbatim: "it goes silent whenever the run TERMINATES WITHOUT WRITING A TROUBLE TOKEN INTO THE LOG -- and then it reports that silence as success. A halted-INCOMPLETE run and a clean convergence produced byte-identical output and the same exit code 0." fable found the same shape by another route: a crashlooping run that truncates its log leaves the watchdog silent with an affirmatively wrong heartbeat. REPRODUCED ON LIVE CODE BEFORE FIXING. Two runs differing only in their completion_signal -- CRITICAL_QUIESCENCE_CONVERGED against HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM -- produced the same 3 stdout lines and the same exit 0, because the watchdog read the log and the round files and never the file that RECORDS the verdict. FIXED as the seat specified: read_outcome() returns CLEAN / BAD / NO_SIGNAL / UNREADABLE, spoken on EVERY exit path as its own stdout line, so a halt is one more Monitor wake rather than a silence. NO_SIGNAL is kept as a third verdict and not folded into BAD, on the seat's argument and the same principle as stop_reason_recorded: a run that ended without recording why cannot even be classified, let alone acted on. Exit codes 0/2/3/4 let a caller branch without parsing prose. EXIT SEMANTICS CHANGED DELIBERATELY. One test asserted exit 0 for "the run ended", which conflated ending with ending WELL -- the very conflation found. 2 EARLIER CALIBRATION DEFECTS, both found by running it rather than reading it: a STALL fired on a healthy panel dispatch whose seats write nothing for 1700+ s, so the decision now samples cumulative CPU time on the spot rather than from probe history -- raising the threshold would have bought quiet by going blind; and re.I made the uppercase pytest marker FAILED match "0 failed", turning a GREEN suite line into an alarm, now (?-i:FAILED). 33 tests, all executing the script as a subprocess, including the seat's exact comparison and anti-regressions in both directions. THE ROUND'S OTHER FINDINGS ARE RECORDED AND NOT YET APPLIED. Both seats located the halt: falsifiers execute in a throwaway scratch cwd while every stored falsifier opens the prose target by RELATIVE path, so all 8 queue items carry falsifier_verdict ERROR and rungs_tried 2, and _apply_routing writes the falsifier body back only on result.resolved -- so, in cc2's words, "falsifiers were written and crashed, and are filed as never written". The brief's declared items_without_falsifier figure was therefore a counting artefact. Both seats also declared A19's first finding STALE: g1/g2 are no longer absolute on prose. They DISAGREE on the Q2 remedy, cc2 convicting the archived exploit and fable surfacing it without convicting, and that disagreement is preserved for the founder rather than smoothed. Full unfiltered record, both seats: experimental_notes/Panel_FULL_RECORD_A19_Commissioning_2026-10-02.md Panel records mirrored 108 of 108. 0 paid dispatches; cc2 21137 chars / 99 tool calls / 1205.0 s, fable 15170 chars / 64 tool calls / 1194.3 s. title: fix: a prose falsifier could not reach its own target, which halted both runs at round 0
verbatim: fix: a prose falsifier could not reach its own target, which halted both runs at round 0 THE ROOT CAUSE OF HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM, found by the fable seat in the free panel of 2026-10-02 and reproduced from both halted runs' own artefacts. Falsifiers execute with cwd set to a throwaway scratch directory, which is the correct isolation and is kept. A falsifier against a PYTHON target IMPORTS it via PYTHONPATH, so the scratch cwd never bites. A falsifier against a PROSE target has no import path: every seat on both commissioning_arm4 runs read the document by a RELATIVE path, which resolves inside the empty scratch directory. THE CHAIN, end to end: FileNotFoundError before the first assertion -> verdict ERROR on every rung -> routing_deferred stamped in the finding's BIRTH round -> irreducible queue 8 against a bound of 2 -> HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM at round 0. All 8 items in both runs carry falsifier_verdict ERROR and rungs_tried 2, and no two share a falsifier body, so the queue size was real. IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE TARGET SPLIT THAT STATISTICS COULD NOT. 3 of 9 runs converged and all 3 halts were on the prose target, but Fisher exact gives p = 0.500000 and Boschloo p = 0.492800 at this sample size, so the split was descriptively clean and statistically unestablished. The mechanism settles what n = 9 could not: a Python target cannot reach this failure at all. THE ALARM WAS RIGHT, as it was on 2026-08-01 when its bound was raised twice to silence it. title: fix: the 4 red tests were all mine, and each was a real tension not a typo
verbatim: fix: the 4 red tests were all mine, and each was a real tension not a typo THE BOARD WAS RED AT 4 failed, 9524 passed, 7 skipped in 3465.73 s, and the cy watchdog reported every failure by name as it happened rather than leaving the run to end in silence. 3 distinct causes, all introduced by last night's and tonight's own additions. 1. PRESERVED SEAT TESTS LOOKED LIKE STRAY TESTS. The preservation mechanism of 2026-10-01 copies a seat's files into experimental_notes/seat_evidence/ at their real paths, so a seat-written TEST lands there with a test_ name and test_no_test_file_sits_outside_the_collected_root reported it. Both guards are right: archived evidence must be reachable from a clone, and a test file outside the suite is a silent no-op. THE PRECEDENT WAS ALREADY IN THE ALLOW-LIST -- the 2026-08-30 entry exempts "the archived artefact of what a reviewer wrote inside its sandbox" -- admitted one file at a time. A per-file entry would be needed after every panel round, which is the hand-maintained drift the founder ruled against today, so the exemption is a PREFIX. It is not a hole: test_seat_evidence_reaches_a_clone asserts every preserved copy matches the harvested original, and 5 parametrised cases hold that a test file anywhere else outside the root is still reported, including elsewhere under experimental_notes and under a seat_evidenceX lookalike. 2. THE NEW WATCHDOG FAILED THE UNKNOWN-FLAG GUARD, the same family swept on 2026-10-01. argparse reports a MISSING required argument before an UNRECOGNISED one, so with --log required an unknown flag produced "the following arguments are required: --log" and never the "unrecognized arguments" every operational script must emit. --log is no longer declared required and its absence is reported after argparse has had its say. 3. scripts/day_window_timing_2026-10-01.py WAS REACHED BY NOTHING. The closing report said its figures were "produced by a committed script" without ever naming the script, so the producer was unreachable and the figure was unverifiable in the way measured-rate-travels-with-its-script exists to prevent. The report now names it. That also cleared the 4th failure, which was the same ratchet in check mode. title: fix: closure never asked whether a fix cures the defect its finding claims
verbatim: fix: closure never asked whether a fix cures the defect its finding claims THE FOUNDER'S INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-02: "you are asking me something that is impossible for me to decide without trawling personally through potentially hundreds of lines of code. It is clearly you job to find which of these causes it is and fix it appropriately." He is right. The previous report offered him 3 technical readings as a ruling; diagnosing between them is this assistant's work. DIAGNOSED, AND IT IS THE FIRST READING: the fixes genuinely do not cure the defect. The probe's taxonomy excludes every other explanation by construction -- an instrument that could not look returns one of NOT_INTERCEPTED, NO_BASELINE, NO_APPLICABLE_FIX or OTHER, and the conclusive bucket requires the falsifier to have reproduced the defect BEFORE the fix and still fail after it. The detail string on each is explicit: "the fix applies cleanly and the finding's own falsifier still demonstrates the defect afterwards". AND THE FIGURE REPORTED TO HIM WAS A SLICE PRESENTED AS THE WHOLE. "16 findings in 1 arm" was 16 of 48 undecided similarity pairs. Over the committed sweep at experimental_notes/data/fix_efficacy_2026-08-30.json the real figure is 126 of 246 conclusive outcomes, 51.2195%, Wilson [45.0027%, 57.3989%] on statsmodels and mpmath agreeing, beside 34 NO_APPLICABLE_FIX, 10 NO_BASELINE, 6 NOT_INTERCEPTED and 17 OTHER. The problem is roughly 8 times larger than stated. THE ROOT CAUSE. `attempt_close` closes on VerificationOutcome.PASS and `run_verification` runs ruff, mypy, bandit and the experiment's GENERIC test_cmd: it asks "did this fix break anything". Nothing at closure time asked "does this fix cure the defect THIS finding claims". The question was not merely unasked but UNASKABLE -- the live call site passed only finding_id and proposed_fix, so the probe had no falsifier to run. THE FIX. attempt_close gains efficacy_mode off/record/veto and carries the verdict on CloseAttempt; the runner passes the finding's falsifier, the target's relative path and the mode; the entry records it so it reaches the exported catalogue; and the simulated-run config sets "record". The known obstacle is already solved by the probe itself: 57 of 70 falsifiers reach their target by IMPORT, which would make a naive sandbox copy report every fix ineffective, so the probe runs a TRIPWIRE first and returns NOT_INTERCEPTED instead of a false conviction. WIRED AS "record" AND NOT "veto", DELIBERATELY. A veto would stop more than half of all closures at once, leaving findings open, growing the irreducible queue and plausibly tripping its alarm -- a change to WHEN A RUN CONVERGES. It earns promotion on measured evidence from a run, per feedback_shadow_promotion_now, and the upcoming simulated runs are that measurement. 16 tests. All 3 modes; the veto biting only on the named outcome; 4 parametrised indeterminate values proving an instrument that could not look never convicts, the same rule as NO_APPLICABLE_CHECKS; a raising probe recorded rather than fatal; and 3 AST tests proving the runner actually reaches it, because an addition nothing reaches is not additive. 290 tests pass across the closure, verification and prose files. A SMALL TRAP RECORDED IN THE TEST: this project carries 2 SEARCH/REPLACE dialects. bugzilla_loop requires "==== REPLACE"; the runner's fixtures use a bare "====" with ">>>> REPLACE". Copying the wrong one fails extraction silently before any probe runs, and cost 2 wrong guesses here. title: fix: the watchdog went blind on truncation, and the Q2 split the founder ruled on
verbatim: fix: the watchdog went blind on truncation, and the Q2 split the founder ruled on THE FOUNDER'S RULING, 2026-10-02: "apply fable's visibility half and carry cc2's into the study." Both halves of the panel's Q2 disagreement are now disposed of as he directed, and 2 further panel findings are closed. 1. THE WATCHDOG WENT BLIND ON A TRUNCATED LOG, found by fable and WORSE than its own framing. It does not go silent -- it reports a stall. It goes BLIND: a run that reopens its log with "w" leaves the file shorter than the offset already read, `size > offset` is false forever, and the log is never read again. Measured: a `Traceback ... RuntimeError: seat crashed` written into a freshly truncated log produced NO TROUBLE event at all, because the offset stood at 5018 bytes against a 62-byte file. A short stall threshold masked it by catching the stall instead; at a realistic --stall-seconds the crash went unmentioned. Verified formally afterwards: z3 reports the old rule blind to every truncated state and UNSAT for the new one, and an exhaustive sweep agrees at 79,800 of 79,800 against 0. The truncation is now announced in its own right. 2. THE EXIT CONTRACT IS RESTORED, AND THAT IS THE cc2 SEAT'S CALL OVER MINE. Its specification carried the verdict as one more stdout line and deliberately left exit codes alone; `test_the_exit_code_contract_is_untouched` pins it with the project's own rule -- "changing it is a REMOVAL and has no committed measurement behind it". My version returned 0/2/3/4 by outcome, and the measurement settled it against me: a NO_SIGNAL end returned 3 and the Monitor reported "script failed (exit 3)" for an ordinary finish, manufacturing exactly the misleading signal this work exists to remove. Both seat guards adopted at their real paths; 46 tests across the 3 watchdog files. 3. fable's Q2 VISIBILITY HALF, APPLIED. bandit rates `shell=True` with a string literal as LOW (B404/B607/B602) and e4 counts only HIGH and MEDIUM, so the archived SHELL_INJECTION_FIX left NO trace in the gate's record and was byte-identical to a correct prose fix. LOW is now counted FOR VISIBILITY and never for the score: the formula is untouched at -0.5 per HIGH, -0.2 per MEDIUM, 0.0 per LOW, the delta travels in the detail string and in `_prose_one_sided`, and 557 tests across the S_k, prose, A19, target-kind and effect files confirm fable's central claim that no Python verdict moves. 4. cc2's CONVICTION CHECK IS NOT APPLIED, as ruled. It would make a REJECT -- a claim -- where fable argues B404 fires on any `import subprocess`, which a build-bot spec may legitimately illustrate. It goes into the programme of study, to be measured in the simulated runs rather than enabled on argument. Fixes authored by the fable and cc2 seats; the exit-contract correction is cc2's over this assistant's, with the measurement that settled it recorded in both. title: feat: rescue the seat evidence that predated the preservation repair
verbatim: feat: rescue the seat evidence that predated the preservation repair THE FOUNDER'S INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-02: "Do this work while the suite runs and you aren't busy doing anything else and decide what is and what is not worth keeping." THE DECISION IS NOT TASTE, WHICH IS WHY IT CAN BE STATED. Every one of the 35 substantive files among the 46 stranded is CITED BY PATH in a committed document: 0 uncited, checked with git grep on the full path with a basename fallback. A document citing a path no clone can reach is the unrecoverable-citation defect this project already ratchets on, so citation decides the question rather than judgement. The rest are scratch, and panel_sandbox._NO_PRESERVE_PARTS already excluded `.scratch` before this script existed, so "scratch stays unpreserved" needed no new filter. MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER, over 55 harvest attempt directories: unpreserved 46 of 281 = 16.3701%, Wilson [12.5029%, 21.1444%] -> 9 of 281 = 3.2028%, Wilson [ 1.6940%, 5.9739%] Fisher exact on the reduction p = 1.149e-07, odds ratio 5.916 50 preserved, 0 failures, 301 already reachable, 169 skipped by the filter statsmodels and mpmath agree on both intervals All 9 that remain are `.scratch/` paths, exactly the set he ruled out. THE NOTE RATCHET REFUSED THIS COMMIT, AND IT WAS RIGHT TO ASK. 8 rescued notes carry 17 findings between them in a SEAT's own prose. Editing them to pass would destroy the thing that makes them evidence -- the same rule already applied to a seat's raw reply in a FULL RECORD, where the figure is corrected in the readable record and the reply is left as it arrived. The note standard governs what this project writes for its own readers and has no authority over what another model wrote inside a sandbox. `experimental_notes/seat_evidence/` is therefore excluded from the ratchet, one directory, byte-pinned by its own guard so a project note cannot hide there, and every other note still judged. Same shape and justification as the prefix exemption added to the collection guard today. PRESERVATION IS NOT ADOPTION. 15 of the 35 are bench/tests/test_*.py that seats wrote and nobody adopted. They are now reachable; they are NOT on the collected root where they would run and might fail. That decision is separate and is not taken here. A JUDGEMENT RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: bench/tmpd9lys10b.py is a mktemp artefact the filter preserves, carrying no `.scratch` part. A basename rule for 1 file costs more than it saves, so it is preserved and named here. title: fix: the watchdog looked for the run's verdict in the wrong directory
verbatim: fix: the watchdog looked for the run's verdict in the wrong directory CAUGHT ON THE FIRST REAL LAUNCH, before the run ended rather than after. `read_outcome` resolved `completion_signal.json` beside the CONSOLE LOG, but `run_simulated_experiment.py` writes its artefacts into a TIMESTAMPED directory it names itself -- `prose_convergence_run1_2026-10-02_20261002T035101Z` -- while the console log sits wherever the operator redirected it. So a clean convergence would have been announced as OUTCOME NO_SIGNAL after 2 hours. That is the false-negative twin of the defect the cc2 seat found in this same function: it reported a halt exactly like a convergence, and this would have reported a convergence as no verdict at all. Both are the same error -- inferring a run's outcome from where a file is not, instead of reading the file that records it. `--outcome-dir` names where the verdict lives. The default is unchanged, so every existing invocation behaves identically. 3 tests: the verdict is read from the named directory, the default still reads the log's own directory, and a wrong --outcome-dir says NO_SIGNAL rather than guessing. 49 tests pass across the 3 watchdog files. title: fix: a brief network outage no longer breaks a run
verbatim: fix: a brief network outage no longer breaks a run THE FOUNDER'S INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-02: "You should fix it so a short network outage will not break a run", after identifying the cause of simulated run 1's failure as his own VPN: "Sometimes I need to turn vpn on and off on my Mac Mini. The outage is only ever brief." THE DEFECT, MEASURED ON THAT RUN. The Claude CLI exits 0 and prints its transport failure into STDOUT, so a dispatch that died halfway reads as a successful dispatch whose answer happens to be an error sentence. 4 of 5 seats returned 141 to 246 characters ending "API Error: Response stalled mid-stream. The response above may be incomplete." -- 80.0000%, Wilson [37.5535%, 96.3776%] -- and EACH WAS CREDITED WITH 1 FINDING. The 5th returned 39,616 characters. Round 0 would have been built from 4 near-empty seats and 1 real one, and the run would still have reported a number. THIS IS THE RULE THIS PROJECT ALREADY WROTE FOR WOLFRAM, applied to the seat transport: "a failed call is NOT a result". The Wolfram bridge returned [HTTP Error 401] as a successful tool result; this returns a dead stream as a seat reply. Same shape, same remedy: recognise the failure, never score it. THE MECHANISM EXISTED AND NOTHING USED IT. `call_claude_cli` has carried max_retries=3, backoff_base and an `accept` substance test whose own docstring says a rejected reply "is retried like any other transport failure" -- but `accept` defaults to None, so a stall was returned as the answer no matter what any caller did. The check now runs BEFORE the caller's test, so every route gets it without opting in. `stalled_mid_stream` matches 6 markers, case-insensitively, ANYWHERE in the reply, because the marker arrives APPENDED to whatever the seat managed to say. A seat that produced 3 of its 9 findings before the stream died leaves a PARTIAL registry that looks complete, which is worse than an empty reply, not better. WAITS ARE SECONDS, NOT MILLISECONDS. backoff_base=1.0 gives 1 s then 2 s, which is shorter than a VPN handshake. STALL_RETRY_MIN_WAIT is 20 s, and the simulated shim makes 3 attempts 20 s then 40 s apart -- enough for a brief outage, not enough to mask a sustained one. AND IF EVERY ATTEMPT STALLS IT RAISES. The shim's own error contract requires it: the real dispatch_to_model RAISES on transport death and _dispatch_single_model converts that to __DISPATCH_FAILED__ itself, so returning a sentinel made every other path read a dead subprocess as a success. 21 tests, including that ordinary prose containing "API error" and "stream" does NOT trip it, that a truncated reply with the marker appended IS rejected, that a healthy first reply costs no extra dispatch, that a retried stall is never silent, and that the real panel route retries with no `accept` supplied. 527 further tests pass across the dispatch, seat, sim-seam and Wolfram files. THE SEAM GUARD CAUGHT MY FIRST VERSION. A `*a, **kw` wrapper passed every call correctly and still broke `test_the_shim_signature_matches_the_primitive`, which compares the shim's parameter LIST against the real primitive's: a stand-in must be substitutable by inspection, not merely by behaviour. The signature is spelled out. ALSO VERIFIED, because the founder asked whether this route bills: it does not. `seat_environment()` strips credentials, and asked directly, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL all reach a seat = False, with no *_API_KEY reaching a seat from the live environment. Dispatch is `claude -p` on the Max subscription. 0 paid dispatches. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: fix: the falsifier-target materialisation could blind the discrimination control
verbatim: fix: the falsifier-target materialisation could blind the discrimination control FOUND WHILE RUN 1b WAS LIVE, from a TROUBLE event the cy watchdog raised: "discrimination control INDETERMINATE_NOT_INTERCEPTED C0005 ... this falsifier behaves identically when the target file is replaced wholesale, so the control cannot reach the target it reads". That verdict pre-dates tonight -- Exp 55 recorded it twice -- but the coupling it pointed at is new and is mine. THE COUPLING. `execute_python` and `reverify_falsifier` both compute `tmp_cwd = cwd or _scratch` and then materialised the registered target into it. The DISCRIMINATION CONTROL is a caller that supplies `cwd`: it builds an overlay with the target replaced by a tripwire and runs the falsifier there to see whether the falsifier notices the substitution. Writing the real target into that overlay answers the control's own question for it. The control imports exactly these 2 functions (reference_runner_v3.py:5200) and calls them with cwd=real_overlay. MEASURED BOTH WAYS, BEFORE FIXING. * Control SUBSTITUTES the target -> `if not dest.exists()` already protected it and the tripwire survived. This is the live path, so RUN 1b's CONTROL IS SOUND and its results are not in question. * An overlay OMITS the target -> the copy landed and restored the real file, defeating "replaced wholesale" and yielding NOT_INTERCEPTED or a false pass. So the safe case held only because another module chose to substitute rather than omit. A guard whose soundness depends on an unrelated module's internal choice is not sound; it is lucky. THE BOUNDARY. Materialise only into the sandbox's OWN scratch, never into a directory a caller constructed. The relative-path defect this exists to fix only ever occurs in the throwaway scratch, where there is no view to respect, so the restriction costs nothing -- fable's 10 original tests still pass, including that a relative-path falsifier reaches its target. BOTH CALL SITES, because fixing one would leave its twin -- the shape this project keeps finding. 4 new guards: a substituting overlay keeps its tripwire, an omitting overlay stays empty, reverify respects a caller view too, and the scratch path still gets the target. 14 tests in that file; 476 pass across the falsifier, discrimination, efficacy, A19 and closure files. Found by the watchdog built 5 hours earlier, on a run it was watching. That is the mechanical cy trigger doing the job the founder asked it to do. verbatim: fix: the heartbeat reported 0 rounds while the run was in round 1 FOUND FROM A LIVE HEARTBEAT, 2026-10-02: "alive; 0 round(s) landed" while the console showed "Round 0: 20 findings" followed by "Round 1/7 (adaptive)". title: fix: a timestamp was mistaken for an HTTP status code
verbatim: fix: a timestamp was mistaken for an HTTP status code CAUGHT ON A LIVE RUN by asking the pattern WHICH SUBSTRING it matched rather than assuming the line was bad. An ordinary artefact line -- "Saved: .../r2_chatgpt-sim_20261002T064011Z.json" -- raised a TROUBLE alarm because the bare `401` in the pattern matched the "4011" inside the timestamp. Every file written at such a second would have cried wolf for the rest of the run. ADDING DIGIT BOUNDARIES WAS NOT ENOUGH, which is why the codes are gone rather than patched. `(?<!\d)(?:401|403|429)(?!\d)` fixed the timestamp and still matched "429 findings total": a boundary cannot tell a status code from a count, and context matching for 3 codes is more machinery than the signal is worth. WHAT IS GIVEN UP, stated rather than discovered later: a line whose ONLY evidence of trouble is a bare status code no longer wakes anyone. The transport failures that actually occur here are covered by the `api error:` family, by `rate limit`, `quota`, `5xx Server`, and by Traceback and Exception -- the measured stall of 2026-10-02 carried "API Error: Response stalled mid-stream" and no status code at all. THIRD PATTERN-CALIBRATION DEFECT IN THIS FILE, all the same shape: a pattern matching more than it means, in a channel whose only value is being believed. The first was `re.I` making `FAILED` match "0 failed", turning a GREEN suite line into an alarm; the second was a stall threshold that fired on a healthy panel; this is the third. A channel that cries wolf trains its reader to ignore it, which is the 9-hour unmonitored run by another route. 5 new false-positive guards over real log lines carrying 401, 403 and 429 inside timestamps and counts, 2 new real-failure cases, 10 pattern cases verified by direct call. 43 tests in the file. ALSO PRESERVED: experimental_notes/data/fix_efficacy_2026-10-02.json, the fresh sweep that finished tonight, kept beside the committed 2026-08-30 baseline rather than overwriting it. Both measure 313 rows under DIFFERENT code -- the fresh one ran after the falsifier-target fix -- and the comparison is the evidence: the ineffective share is statistically unchanged (126 of 246 against 112 of 225, Fisher exact p = 0.782340) while CONCLUSIVE probes fell 246 to 225 with 16 new INDETERMINATE_PROBE_BROKEN_AFTER_BASELINE. Those 16 are UNATTRIBUTED and recorded as open: the suspects are tonight's 2 falsifier-sandbox changes, and settling it needs a third sweep after the runs finish. title: fix: the alarm channel was 83% ordinary English, and re-arming lost the newest lines
verbatim: fix: the alarm channel was 83% ordinary English, and re-arming lost the newest lines Three defects in the cy watchdog, all found by running it against run 1b rather than by reading it. 1. PROSE IS NOT AN ALARM. Measured over the 519 lines of run 1b's log: the pattern matched 29 lines, of which 24 were the run's own explanatory prose -- 82.7586%, Wilson 95% [65.4516%, 92.4021%]. `re.I` made `CRITICAL` match inside `gamma_critical`, which is printed EVERY ROUND OF EVERY RUN, and `REFUSED` match the lower-case word in "corrected copies: 14 accepted, 0 refused" -- a count of zero reported as an alarm, for the third time in this file. `cannot ` and `could not` matched 10 lines, 0 of them failures. Fixed by the `(?-i:FAILED)` precedent already in the file: CRITICAL and REFUSED become case-sensitive, keeping 2 true uppercase tokens and dropping 16 prose matches; `cannot `/`could not` are removed outright. The new pattern is a STRICT SUBSET of the old (NumPy: 24 old-only, 0 new-only), and the per-line alarm rate falls from 5.5877% [3.9184%, 7.9096%] to 0.9634% [0.4122%, 2.2352%]. What is given up is stated in the code and pinned by a test: a failure whose only evidence is the bare word "cannot" no longer speaks. NOT narrowed: `[1-9]\d*\s+(?:failed|error|errors)` fires on the routine "Skin barrier (v2): 5 passed, 15 failed out of 20 findings" census, ~2 per run. It shares its exact lexical shape with "3 failed, 9372 passed", which an existing test pins as a line that MUST speak. 2 noise events are the accepted price of catching a red suite. 2. RE-ARMING REPLAYED THE WHOLE LOG, AND THE REPLAY WAS LOSSY. The arming probe read from byte 0 and emitted an event per match. The notification carrying them was cut with "...(truncated)", and because the replay runs oldest-first the dropped lines were the NEWEST -- the only ones that could still need acting on. One arming caps at 30 minutes by design, so this recurred every 30 minutes. Now a backlog above 5 lines is summarised with its 3 most recent named; at or below 5 it is still replayed verbatim, because 14 regex tests drive that path and summarising at any size would have made every one of them assert against a channel nothing reaches. 3. A ZOMBIE PASSED THE LIVENESS CHECK. `os.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds for an exited process whose parent has not reaped it, so a FINISHED run read as alive. Found by this file's own end-to-end test hanging for its full timeout waiting for a PROCESS GONE that could not come. The consequence was degradation rather than silence -- the stall path speaks eventually, but 20 minutes late and under the wrong name, at the exact moment this watch exists to catch. `_alive` now consults `ps -o state=`, the same mechanism `_cpu_seconds` already uses. 19 tests added, 63 passing in the file. Two of them failed first and both faults were mine: "historical failure 2" is a substring of "historical failure 25", so a bare `in` reported absent lines as present -- the inventory substring collision again, the instrument wrong rather than the subject. title: fix: the halt alarm called 2 never-assessed criticals "locked as irreducible"
verbatim: fix: the halt alarm called 2 never-assessed criticals "locked as irreducible" Run 1b halted at round 2 and said both of these, 0 lines apart: static HIL queue: 3 unresolved critical(s) (1 ladder-exhausted, 2 never assessed - no runnable falsifier) *** IRREDUCIBLE-QUEUE ALARM at round 2: 3 criticals are locked as irreducible, over the bound of 2. `irreducible_escalation` means the ladder was EXHAUSTED; `routing_deferred` means the item was NEVER ASSESSED. Two states with opposite diagnoses -- the first points at the document, the second at the instrument -- and the notify text named only the first. The log line was corrected on 2026-09-22; the alarm was not, and on 2026-09-22 a morning report built a causal chain on the wrong one and escalated a config surface that could not have changed the outcome. ONE PREDICATE, NOT THREE. There were three expressions of one rule: the `irreducible_queue_count` comprehension, the log line's inline `_q_locked`, and the notify text. `irreducible_queue_count` is now `sum(decomposition())`, so the total and the split cannot disagree by construction. Equivalence to the shipped expression is established three ways: z3 returns `unsat` for `old != new` AND `unsat` for both arms firing on one entry; exhaustive enumeration agrees over 48 of 48 states; and 400 randomised registries driven through the patched class agree with an independently reimplemented shipped rule, 0 mismatches, the both-flags entry counting once as exhausted. AN ATTEMPTED FALSIFIER IS NOT AN ABSENT ONE. `_apply_routing` writes `falsifier_code` back only on `result.resolved`, so a falsifier that WAS written and then crashed is filed as never written. I REJECTED THE PANEL'S FIX FOR THIS, and the reason is measured. The cc2 seat recommended writing `falsifier_code` back unconditionally and called it strictly additive. It is not: `falsifier_code` has 3 GATING readers -- `claim_ledger.claim_from_entry` sets `decidable=bool(falsifier)`, `bugzilla_loop:716` activates the efficacy probe on it, and `execution_based_matcher:641` filters on it -- so an unconditional writeback marks a claim settleable by a computation that ERRORED, in the very channel the founder has instructed be promoted and tested in the runs. No writeback is needed: `last_falsifier_code` is ALREADY written unconditionally, so the alarm reads it as a REPORTING fallback, prefixed so an attempted body can never group with a resolved one of the same text. Stated limit: `last_falsifier_code` is truncated to 600 characters, so two distinct falsifiers sharing a 600-character prefix group as one defect, making the defect count a LOWER bound for attempted bodies. NOTHING HERE CHANGES WHICH FINDINGS REACH A HUMAN, and that boundary is deliberate. `max_irreducible_queue` stays at 2. The ADMISSION RULE -- whether a `routing_deferred` item should count in its birth round -- is the founder's call and is not in this diff. Run 1b's own bundle is the evidence it needs: `count=3 bound=2 items_without_falsifier=1`, and all 3 items carry `open_since_round=2` against an alarm fired at round 2. My own hypothesis that the writeback artefact pushed this queue over bound is REFUTED by that `items_without_falsifier=1`; the reporting is now honest, the halt still fires. 13 tests added, 43 passing across the alarm, static-queue, defect-count and A19-reachability files. Three of my own test faults were measured out first: an identity collision where two registries both number from `C0001`, guessed at twice before being inspected. title: docs: the integrity guard's false-positive test cannot see a false positive
verbatim: docs: the integrity guard's false-positive test cannot see a false positive Note pair for the founder's ruling on the `seeded_faults` refusal, with the producer script committed alongside every figure it cites. THE CENTRAL FINDING. `test_the_guard_rejects_nothing_else_in_the_whole_tracked_archive` holds the integrity guard's false-positive rate at 0 over what its docstring calls "every falsifier this project has ever run", and says that if a rule change makes it fail, the rule is blocking honest work. It cannot fail in that direction: it reads `entry["falsifier_code"]`, and `_apply_routing` writes that field back only on `result.resolved`, so a REFUSED falsifier's body never reaches the field the test reads. The corpus that measures refusals excludes refusals by construction. corpus the test READS 2 of 872 = 0.2294%, Wilson [0.0629%, 0.8324%] corpus it CANNOT read 1 of 111 = 0.9009%, Wilson [0.1592%, 4.9273%] 37 tests pass in that file while 10 refusal events sit in run 1b's log. 4th instance in this record of a guard that cannot fail. This also corrects an assessment made earlier today: the writeback gap was judged to affect reporting only, because `falsifier_present` gates nothing. That missed a third consumer -- this security test. The refusal to write `falsifier_code` back unconditionally still stands, because `claim_ledger` sets `decidable=bool(falsifier)` from it. RUN 1B's 3 QUEUED CRITICALS HAVE 3 DIFFERENT CAUSES, which corrects a claim made 20 minutes earlier that 2 were integrity false positives: C0029 UNTOOLABLE (no falsifier written), C0032 ERROR (a broken one), C0035 INTEGRITY_VIOLATION (a correct one refused). All 3 born in round 2, admitted to a bound of 2 in round 2, and all 3 settled by the run's own sweep 69 minutes after the alarm said nothing further could close. AGAINST RENAMING THE FIELD, measured: 0 occurrences in the target spec, so the token does not come from the document; 109 tracked occurrences across 102 files of which 94 are task data carrying the planted faults; 14 occurrences in 5 production modules. The collision is structural, between a guard refusing MENTION and an honest falsifier that must name the field to derive the schema, so a rename relabels it rather than removing it. 5 CLAIMS WITHDRAWN, listed in section 8 with their refutations, including one of my own figures: "20 of 24, 83.3333%" was a double count, because the producer globbed `*/run.log` and `*/*.log` as a union. Deduped: 10 of 14, 71.4286%. The script now dedupes and records the cause. Both files lint clean under `scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py` (0 findings each) and declare note standard v1.7. Nothing in the guard was changed: the recommendation is to make the sweep able to see refusals FIRST, because ruling on the guard now would mean ruling on a rate no committed test reports. title: docs: the census counted lines as occurrences and counted itself
verbatim: docs: the census counted lines as occurrences and counted itself An independent 3-dimension review of yesterday's note pair returned 5 compliance findings on the TTS, all 3 verifiers confirming them real, and chasing 1 of them exposed 2 figure errors of mine. THE 2 FIGURE ERRORS, BOTH IN THE SAME LINE OF THE PRODUCER. * UNITS. `git grep -c` counts LINES CONTAINING a match, and the sum was printed as "occurrences". On this tree they differ: 133 lines against 136 substring occurrences. title: docs: 3 load-bearing claims in the guard note are refuted by execution
verbatim: docs: 3 load-bearing claims in the guard note are refuted by execution The adversarial review of the note pair returned 32 findings across 3 dimensions. 4 are blocking and I verified each myself rather than taking the reviewer's word. All 3 of the note's load-bearing claims fail. 1. THE MECHANISM CLAIM IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. "The runner writes that field back only when a falsifier resolves" is true of ONE write site. `falsifier_code` is written at REGISTRY INTAKE (`reference_runner_v3.py:2345`, `getattr(finding, "falsifier_code", "")`) before any verdict exists, and read back at :5631; there are 7 write sites in all. A finding's OWN attached falsifier therefore IS visible to the sweep. WHAT SURVIVES, measured: 221 bodies sit in `last_falsifier_code` and in no `falsifier_code`. All 221 were written by a ROUTING RUNG, 198 by entries that also carried their own intake body, 119 resolved. Exactly 1 of the 221 was refused by the guard: C0035, written by CC2-SIM, unresolved. So the blind spot is real and it is the one that matters -- it hid the only refusal under discussion -- but "the corpus excludes refusals by construction" was far too strong. It excludes routing-written unresolved bodies. 2. THE PRECEDENT DOES NOT EXIST. The note told the founder that `bench/falsifier_verify.py` already refuses answer-key fields on ACCESS rather than MENTION, and recommended matching that treatment. Line 298 carries `\b(?:_KEY_FIELDS)\b` -> "an answer-key schema field named". Executed: `scan_falsifier_source('KEYS = {"planted_false"}')` returns TWO refusals with no access of any kind. The recommendation's stated precedent is refuted and the recommendation needs rebuilding. 3. THE ACCESS DETECTOR WAS BLIND TO THE STORED FORM. The `0 of 94` figure scanned raw JSON text, where quotes are escaped. Executed: the regex matches `task["seeded_faults"]` and does NOT match `task[\"seeded_faults\"]`. Re-measured over the PARSED corpus, where strings are unescaped and each is tested whole rather than in 400-character windows: 0 of 80, Wilson [0.0000%, 4.5818%]. The conclusion that nothing read the key in run 1b stands; the instrument did not earn it. The reviewer's claim of 475 escaped subscripts in that corpus does NOT reproduce -- there are 0 -- so the detector was blind to nothing here, which is luck rather than method. AND I WITHDREW A TRUE CLAIM. Withdrawal 4 said 1 of the 3 queued criticals was integrity-refused, correcting an earlier "2 of 3". The earlier figure was right: C0029's routing_history carries verdict INTEGRITY_VIOLATION at round 2. My scan of its retained body returned clean only because that body is truncated to 600 characters and the token sits past the cut -- the truncation I had already documented, used as evidence against itself. NOT NOVEL EITHER. The same guard fired on the same target on 2026-09-22 in `commissioning_arm4_prose_20260922T053349Z`, which both documents present as a new phenomenon. All 3 documents now carry a correction notice at the head so the founder cannot decide from the refuted version. The corrected rewrite follows; the recommendation is suspended until its precedent is replaced. title: fix: I read a label the runner documents as stale, and withdrew a true claim
verbatim: fix: I read a label the runner documents as stale, and withdrew a true claim The producer bound `h` to `routing_history[0]`, read `rungs_tried` from it, and then printed the ENTRY's `falsifier_verdict` one key away from `h["verdict"]`. That one key is why C0029 was reported as "UNTOOLABLE -- no falsifier was written at all", and why a TRUE claim (2 of 3 queued criticals integrity-refused) was withdrawn in favour of a false one. THE RUNNER DOCUMENTS THIS EXACT TRAP, and I had read the file. `reconcile_routing_verdict`: "`_apply_routing` writes `falsifier_code`/ `falsifier_verdict` back only on `result.resolved`. When the ladder ran and did not confirm, the entry keeps the stale `UNTOOLABLE` and the ladder's real verdict survives only in `routing_history[-1]["verdict"]`, beside a body truncated to 600 chars." It even records the same defect on `commissioning_arm4_prose_20260922T053349Z`: "6 of 6 entries reading UNTOOLABLE carry a ladder verdict of ERROR ... filed as findings for which nothing was ever written." MEASURED, with the key corrected: C0029 ladder_verdict=INTEGRITY_VIOLATION (entry label UNTOOLABLE) C0032 ladder_verdict=ERROR C0035 ladder_verdict=INTEGRITY_VIOLATION So 2 of 3 share one cause and it is the guard under decision, not "3 different causes". The producer now prints the ladder verdict FIRST and labels the entry value as stale unless resolved. AND THE PREFIX SCAN WAS EVIDENCE OF NOTHING. 183 of 221 retained routing bodies sit at the 600-char cap, so a clean scan of the retained text is a scan of a prefix. The runs' own verdicts record 3 integrity refusals among those 221 (C0008, C0029, C0035) where scanning detects 1: corrected rate 3 of 221 = 1.3575%, Wilson [0.4627%, 3.9144%] with statsmodels and mpmath agreeing, Clopper-Pearson [0.2808%, 3.9156%]. Previously published as 1 of 111. The producer now prints how many characters it scanned. The 14:05 correction notice OVERCORRECTED -- it said the storage account was false, when it is false only as a blanket claim -- and is replaced on all 3 documents by a verified one. Also recorded there: the recommendation's stated precedent does NOT exist, because `falsifier_verify.py:298` carries `\b(?:_KEY_FIELDS)\b` as a BARE-MENTION rule over the same list, so the recommendation is suspended until it has a real basis. 10 tests still pass. Nothing in the guard has been changed. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: test: the stale-label trap now has a guard that bites
verbatim: test: the stale-label trap now has a guard that bites The costliest error of 2026-10-02 had no test. The producer was corrected to print `routing_history[-1]["verdict"]` instead of the entry's stale `falsifier_verdict`, and nothing would have caught the regression -- the same unguarded-addition shape as mutation M5 earlier the same day. 4 tests added, each mutation-verified against the corrected producer with an applied-assertion that reads the file back (the check I omitted on my first attempt at M5, which searched for a string the file does not contain and so proved nothing): M6 revert to the stale entry label -> 1 failed, test_the_ladder_verdict_is_reported_for_C0029 M7 drop the stale-label marker -> 1 failed, test_the_stale_entry_label_is_marked_as_stale M8 drop the scanned-length note -> 1 failed, test_a_prefix_scan_states_how_much_it_scanned 0 undetected. Producer verified byte-identical to HEAD afterwards. The 4th test, `test_the_recorded_verdicts_outnumber_what_scanning_detects`, is a second WITNESS: it holds that the runs' own recorded integrity verdicts (3) still exceed what scanning the retained bodies detects (1), which is the gap the corrected 3-of-221 figure rests on. If those ever agree, either the 600-char truncation was lifted or the archive changed, and the figure needs re-measuring before it is cited again. Wolfram confirms the corrected interval as a SECOND falsifier, open-source primary: statsmodels and mpmath both give Wilson [0.4627%, 3.9144%] for 3 of 221, and wolframscript agrees to 10 significant figures. 14 tests in the file. title: fix: the full suite found 4 same-day regressions the 501-test subset cannot reach
verbatim: fix: the full suite found 4 same-day regressions the 501-test subset cannot reach Full suite on the afternoon tree at `199cadb`: 6 failed, 9,662 passed, 7 skipped in 2974.13 s. Against the 2026-09-27 frozen-tree baseline of 9 failed and 8,606 passed, more tests and fewer failures -- but 4 of the 6 were introduced TODAY and `pre-commit`'s 501-test subset reached NONE of them. That is the case for running the whole suite before calling a board green. 1. THE REGRESSION THAT MATTERED, from my own `a0bd8e5`. `AttributeError: '_Reg' object has no attribute irreducible_queue_decomposition`. `a0bd8e5` made `irreducible_queue_count` call `self.irreducible_queue_decomposition()`. The `_Reg` fixture in test_panel_five_fixes_2026-09-07.py borrows the UNBOUND method onto a class carrying only `.entries`, so the `self.`-method dependency raised, taking out `test_a_deferred_item_still_counts_toward_the_alarm` -- the guard whose own docstring calls it "THE ONE THAT MATTERED", and which exists because deferring an item once removed it from the alarm as well as the A4 blocker. FIXED by moving the shared rule to the module-level `_irreducible_queue_split(entries)`: one predicate for both readers, no `self` dependency, every duck-typed caller works. Amending the fixture was the alternative and is forbidden -- a committed oracle is not edited to admit a new feature. 91 passed across the 6 files that touch the counter. Mutation-verified: split forced to (0, 0) -> 20 failed; `elif` -> `if` so a both-flags entry double-counts -> 2 failed, including the equivalence test. Duck-type re-checked by construction afterwards and returns 1. 2. `--help` NEVER SHOWED THE FLAG I ADDED. `scripts/escalation_paths_2026-09-11.py` called `answer_help` AND built an argparse parser, and my own comment stated the defect without seeing it: "`--help` is still answered by the helper, before argparse sees anything." So `--whole-archive` was undocumented to anyone who asked for help. The helper call is gone; `parse_args()` is the first statement in `main()`, so `--help` now lists the flag and exits in 0.04 s having read no archive -- `feedback_help_must_never_cost_money` holds. 3. THE NEWEST SESSION STATE BLOCK QUOTED NO SUITE FIGURE. I wrote a 2026-10-02 block with 0 figures matching the producer predicate, so an anti-vacuity guard and its pin both failed. Now recorded with the real measurement and a complete re-runnable invocation, which is also the `docs-sweep-required` obligation for today's work. 4. THE LATENT-TAGGER PIN WENT RED AT 19 AGAINST 16, because `run1b` landed 3 newly tagged entries. RE-MEASURED rather than re-interpreted, which is what `test_corpus_is_the_whole_archive_not_a_slice` instructs when runs are added: 3 gained, 0 LOST. A loss is the regression that pin exists to catch; growth is the archive growing. All 3 are CLOSED/CONFIRMED at severity 0.65, 0.65 and 0.69, just under the critical threshold, which is the population the tagger exists to surface. 121 passed across all 6 previously-failing files plus today's 2 new guards. The full suite re-runs now to confirm the board. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: The study now carries its own reason, and the compaction alert exists at last
verbatim: The study now carries its own reason, and the compaction alert exists at last THE PURPOSE KEPT BEING LOST, so it is now mechanical. The simulated runs were repeatedly described by their success criterion -- 3 clean convergences -- rather than by why they are run, which is to measure whether the fixes of the last 15+ days WORK. A compaction discards the conversation; it does not discard a committed file. IT EXPIRES: at status CLOSED the hook falls silent for good. A genuine PRE-compaction warning is not reachable, because no hook runs at compaction; this is the post-compaction alert. title: the barrier was discarding findings for their quoting, and its ambiguity guard was overridden by the branch below it
verbatim: the barrier was discarding findings for their quoting, and its ambiguity guard was overridden by the branch below it Run 1 was stopped on live evidence: 16 findings blocked over 2 rounds, every one for 'Cited file not found', and 12 of the 16 cited the run's own target by its bare basename. The citation pattern captures (\S+\.\w+), and \S matches a backtick, so markdown quoting is captured INTO the path and all 3 resolution steps miss. A directory-qualified citation survived because basename extraction strips the backtick along with the directory, which is why the pattern looked harmless. The test written for that fix then found a second defect: when a basename is ambiguous the Bug#69 guard skips the basename match, and the suffix fallback below it matched the first source path ending in that name anyway. The guard refused to guess and the fallback guessed regardless. Also: the cy watchdog's ALARM token was matching the CONDITION under which an alarm would fire -- 19 of 74 alarm-channel lines over 291 archived logs, 25.6757%, Wilson [17.0977%, 36.6544%], said nothing was wrong. Promoted rather than deleted (it carries 2 true signals) by reading the 2 numbers and comparing. And the repointing experiment ran: 49 of 56 archived falsifiers still CONFIRM against a file they were never written for, Fisher p = 0.1617149 against a pre-registered 0.01, so neither hypothesis is supported and the figure stands on its own. title: the run-end harvest, and a discriminator that was looking for a field that does not exist
verbatim: the run-end harvest, and a discriminator that was looking for a field that does not exist Five study measurements can only be answered from a finished run's registry, so they are computed in one pass rather than by hand at run end. Its round-2 discriminator was FIRST written to compare each entry's corrected_copy against the target text as the entry recorded it. No such field exists -- entries carry corrected_copy_target_sha, a hash. On real data that version reported '0 entries in each group', which reads as an absent EFFECT when it was an absent FIELD. Writing it before run end is what caught that. Redesigned around what the data holds: the run log records the corrected passage's size and the resulting target size at every splice, so the testable quantity is the fraction of the target a correction touches, tested for a trend across rounds. Interim over run 1b rounds 0-2: 0.038481, 0.039056, 0.037497, Spearman rho = -0.109789, p = 0.6969 -- MECHANISM not supported, so the round-2 cannot-fail jump is better explained by the surviving claims being vaguer, and no fix is owed. That retrospectively validates not pausing the run. Also measures the cost of arming the closure veto, which CORRECTS a figure carried all day: among the 572 archived entries where the probe can decide, 160 do not cure their own falsifier -- 27.9720%, Wilson [24.4499%, 31.7881%] -- not the 51.2195% from a narrower window, Fisher p = 3.26096e-10 between them. Arming would withhold 160 of 920 closures, 28 of them critical. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: CDSFL POST, the aliveness probe, enforced star topology, and a gamma coupling that needs a ruling
verbatim: CDSFL POST, the aliveness probe, enforced star topology, and a gamma coupling that needs a ruling FOUNDER RULINGS OF 2026-10-06, BUILT. CDSFL POST. His words: "on a bios screen when 'booting up' it prints a simple message against each check, which is just 'pass or fail'. If a test passes then the next check fails, the system is halted, giving the user an opportunity to investigate." Pass or fail per row, halt at the first failure, wired INTO the simulated launcher so it gates the dispatch. It overruled the 3-state version built hours earlier, and dropping that scheme exposed a defect of exactly the class the check exists for: AMBER never set the exit code, and a check whose own code RAISED was mapped to AMBER, so A BROKEN CHECK BOOTED at exit 0. Measured by scripts/post_semantics_2026-10-06.py part 1. Halting makes the row ORDER load bearing, so z3 holds it against the declared dependencies with an independent index scan that must agree, and a reversed order is rejected. ON ITS FIRST HONEST RUN IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT: THE LADDER STILL CANNOT CLIMB. run_simulated_experiment.py consults the ladder only under --seat-models ladder, and that flag DEFAULTS TO uniform, answering every seat with 1 model. This is cause 2 of 2 in the record for the inert ladder and it was never fixed at the launcher. The default is NOT changed here: it alters what the simulation dispatches against his subscription. POST halts and names it. HIS RULING IS OUTSTANDING. THE ALIVENESS PROBE. His words: "perhaps we should build a simple 'aliveness test', where the models get up to 3 attempts, by simply asking it to print 'Ready!'" Built, and called BEFORE the sandboxes are built because a probe after them saves none of the per-seat cost. Measured live: it established a route in 5.91 s, against the 3258.3 s a failed round took to establish the same fact. "Non-empty" is NOT "alive" -- an error string or a holding note is answering, but not this question. A dead seat REFUSES THE ROUND and is never dropped, because skipping a model is benching it. STAR TOPOLOGY, ENFORCED RATHER THAN REMEMBERED. His words: "I didn't just state it as a 'preference', I stated that it should be built into all confer round machinery going forward so it couldn't be skipped." The grouping key is the BRIEF ITSELF: rounds asking the same question carry a byte-identical BRIEF.md, so sha256 over it finds the siblings with nothing to label and nothing to forget. A blind round dispatched without being blind to an already-answered sibling is refused, printing the fixing command, before any network call. Verified live against tonight's own rounds: the second dispatch WOULD have been refused had PANEL_BLIND_OF been forgotten. ★ THE FINDING THAT NEEDS HIS RULING FIRST. The cc2 seat predicted exhaustion would RAISE gamma_critical, measured it, and was refuted by its own measurement. Over 14 archived runs, resolving unresolved criticals moves gamma_critical DOWN in 9, up in 3, unchanged in 2, and 2 of 14 CROSS THE 0.30 ARM DOWNWARD -- exp40_gate 0.3018 -> 0.2328, commissioning_arm1_panel 0.3236 -> 0.1883. 14.29%, Wilson [4.0094%, 39.9414%], statsmodels and a closed form and Wolfram Language agreeing to 7 significant figures. The mechanism is in the data: resolved criticals carry a LATER mean round (18.00 vs 13.31; 6.50 vs 3.19), and late mass steepens a cumulative curve, raising beta and lowering gamma = 1 - beta. SO REMOVING THE RUNG CAP IS NOT A PURE SPEND QUESTION, which is how both his ruling and routing.py's own comment frame it. Independently re-run against the live archive and reproduced exactly. Exhaustion is already enabled in simulation, so this is live. The seat's recommendation is recording-only and is NOT implemented, pending him. A PRE-VERDICT SWEEP SHADOW, for his closing-sweep ruling. The runner's own comments already agree with him: "the sweep can only clean the residual ledger, never touch convergence", and 2 per-round passes never see its results. Rather than reorder the convergence path unsupervised, the gate is REPLAYED against the swept ledger with the inputs captured at the real verdict, and both answers are recorded. If the replay ever disagrees, ordering decided a convergence outcome and the reorder is justified by evidence. The non-vacuity is executed: the gate returns False at 3 unresolved criticals and True at 0. A TIMEOUT RAISE MADE AND REVERTED WITHIN THE HOUR, recorded rather than dropped. Claimed: the 1800 s clock was binding on cc2. Refuted the same night: the identical brief completed in 1020.0 s with 49 tool calls. The per-call RATE was stable throughout (20.455 and 20.816 s), so the seat was never slow; the call COUNT nearly doubled during the network outages because the calls were failing and being retried. A longer clock would let a degraded round churn for an hour instead of 30 minutes, which is worse. The remedy is the probe and the watchdog. SUITE: 10210 passed, 26 failed, 20 skipped in 58:43. Most of the 26 were caused by this night's work and are fixed here: the memory index line length, the memory ledger accounting, the panel mirrors, 2 missing FULL RECORDs, a script rejecting an unknown flag by naming the wrong fault, a listing truncating in silence, a config default read off a class a test legitimately replaces, POST placed so early it blocked a guard that drives the launcher to compare its own 2 model lists, and a round directory carrying a bare vendor name in a path segment -- a provenance violation under his 2026-08-08 ruling, so the round was renamed and its mirror and FULL RECORD rebuilt. 8 failures remain, none from this work, each diagnosed in the overnight note. Guards added: test_post_halts_at_the_first_failure_2026-10-06.py (18), test_seats_must_answer_before_work_is_passed_2026-10-06.py (16), test_star_topology_cannot_be_skipped_2026-10-06.py (24), test_pre_verdict_sweep_shadow_2026-10-06.py (8). Every behavioural assertion CALLS the code. Mutations: 'alive' as merely non-empty fails 1; the probe after the sandbox build fails 1; 'landed' as file-exists fails 4; brief grouping disabled fails 4; a crashed check booting fails 2. title: CDSFL POST, the aliveness probe, enforced star topology, and a gamma coupling that needs a ruling
verbatim: CDSFL POST, the aliveness probe, enforced star topology, and a gamma coupling that needs a ruling FOUNDER RULINGS OF 2026-10-06, BUILT. CDSFL POST. His words: "on a bios screen when 'booting up' it prints a simple message against each check, which is just 'pass or fail'. If a test passes then the next check fails, the system is halted, giving the user an opportunity to investigate." Pass or fail per row, halt at the first failure, wired INTO the simulated launcher so it gates the dispatch. It overruled the 3-state version built hours earlier, and dropping that scheme exposed a defect of exactly the class the check exists for: AMBER never set the exit code, and a check whose own code RAISED was mapped to AMBER, so A BROKEN CHECK BOOTED at exit 0. Measured by scripts/post_semantics_2026-10-06.py part 1. Halting makes the row ORDER load bearing, so z3 holds it against the declared dependencies with an independent index scan that must agree, and a reversed order is rejected. ON ITS FIRST HONEST RUN IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT: THE LADDER STILL CANNOT CLIMB. run_simulated_experiment.py consults the ladder only under --seat-models ladder, and that flag DEFAULTS TO uniform, answering every seat with 1 model. This is cause 2 of 2 in the record for the inert ladder and it was never fixed at the launcher. The default is NOT changed here: it alters what the simulation dispatches against his subscription. POST halts and names it. HIS RULING IS OUTSTANDING. THE ALIVENESS PROBE. His words: "perhaps we should build a simple 'aliveness test', where the models get up to 3 attempts, by simply asking it to print 'Ready!'" Built, and called BEFORE the sandboxes are built because a probe after them saves none of the per-seat cost. Measured live: it established a route in 5.91 s, against the 3258.3 s a failed round took to establish the same fact. "Non-empty" is NOT "alive" -- an error string or a holding note is answering, but not this question. A dead seat REFUSES THE ROUND and is never dropped, because skipping a model is benching it. STAR TOPOLOGY, ENFORCED RATHER THAN REMEMBERED. His words: "I didn't just state it as a 'preference', I stated that it should be built into all confer round machinery going forward so it couldn't be skipped." The grouping key is the BRIEF ITSELF: rounds asking the same question carry a byte-identical BRIEF.md, so sha256 over it finds the siblings with nothing to label and nothing to forget. A blind round dispatched without being blind to an already-answered sibling is refused, printing the fixing command, before any network call. Verified live against tonight's own rounds: the second dispatch WOULD have been refused had PANEL_BLIND_OF been forgotten. ★ THE FINDING THAT NEEDS HIS RULING FIRST. The cc2 seat predicted exhaustion would RAISE gamma_critical, measured it, and was refuted by its own measurement. Over 14 archived runs, resolving unresolved criticals moves gamma_critical DOWN in 9, up in 3, unchanged in 2, and 2 of 14 CROSS THE 0.30 ARM DOWNWARD -- exp40_gate 0.3018 -> 0.2328, commissioning_arm1_panel 0.3236 -> 0.1883. 14.29%, Wilson [4.0094%, 39.9414%], statsmodels and a closed form and Wolfram Language agreeing to 7 significant figures. The mechanism is in the data: resolved criticals carry a LATER mean round (18.00 vs 13.31; 6.50 vs 3.19), and late mass steepens a cumulative curve, raising beta and lowering gamma = 1 - beta. SO REMOVING THE RUNG CAP IS NOT A PURE SPEND QUESTION, which is how both his ruling and routing.py's own comment frame it. Independently re-run against the live archive and reproduced exactly. Exhaustion is already enabled in simulation, so this is live. The seat's recommendation is recording-only and is NOT implemented, pending him. A PRE-VERDICT SWEEP SHADOW, for his closing-sweep ruling. The runner's own comments already agree with him: "the sweep can only clean the residual ledger, never touch convergence", and 2 per-round passes never see its results. Rather than reorder the convergence path unsupervised, the gate is REPLAYED against the swept ledger with the inputs captured at the real verdict, and both answers are recorded. If the replay ever disagrees, ordering decided a convergence outcome and the reorder is justified by evidence. The non-vacuity is executed: the gate returns False at 3 unresolved criticals and True at 0. A TIMEOUT RAISE MADE AND REVERTED WITHIN THE HOUR, recorded rather than dropped. Claimed: the 1800 s clock was binding on cc2. Refuted the same night: the identical brief completed in 1020.0 s with 49 tool calls. The per-call RATE was stable throughout (20.455 and 20.816 s), so the seat was never slow; the call COUNT nearly doubled during the network outages because the calls were failing and being retried. A longer clock would let a degraded round churn for an hour instead of 30 minutes, which is worse. The remedy is the probe and the watchdog. SUITE: 10210 passed, 26 failed, 20 skipped in 58:43. Every behavioural assertion CALLS the code. Also: a schema toggle design brief with a measured inventory behind it (93 fields, 25 switches, 65 dials, 6 on by default, 6 enabled nowhere), recommending 3 profiles rather than 25 checkboxes, and recording honestly that 1 requested control has no configuration surface at all. title: the joint gate was skippable by omission, and 2 source-text assertions now execute
verbatim: the joint gate was skippable by omission, and 2 source-text assertions now execute THE GATE THE FOUNDER ASKED TO BE UNSKIPPABLE COULD BE SKIPPED BY FORGETTING A VARIABLE. His ruling: "I stated that it should be built into all confer round machinery going forward so it couldn't be skipped." The first implementation read the round KIND off the presence of PANEL_JOINT_OF -- joint when set, blind otherwise -- so omitting it downgraded a joint round to the blind check. And the blind check then passed TRIVIALLY, because a joint brief is never byte-identical to a blind brief and therefore has no siblings to be blind to. Found by dispatching tonight's own joint round without the variable and watching it through. THE KIND IS NOW DETECTED FROM WHAT THE BRIEF CONTAINS. A brief carrying another round's landed reply verbatim IS a joint brief: `quotes_other_rounds` samples 3 interior spans of 240 characters from each landed reply and tests containment. Measured on the real directories -- the joint round is classified joint and names both blind rounds; both blind rounds classify blind with 0 quotes. Shared project vocabulary cannot trip it, because terms like `gamma_critical` and "the frozen tuple" run to tens of characters, not hundreds, and a guard holds that. A LIST-SHAPED JSON CRASHED THE PREDICATE, and only the real archive could find it. `seat_reply_words` assumed every `*.json` in a round directory is a dict, and scanning `bench/logs` raised "AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'" on a sidecar whose top level is a list. Every fixture in the guard was a well-formed reply, so none of them could have caught it; a predicate that only ever meets tidy input is untested against the archive it runs over. Now shape-tolerant, with 3 guards including one that walks every real round. A STALE ROUND NAME IN MY OWN GUARD WAS SKIPPING RATHER THAN FAILING. The regression test that replays tonight's dispatch still named the round directory before it was renamed, so it SKIPPED -- quietly stopping being tested, which is worse than failing. Corrected; the file now runs 32 of 32 with 0 skips. 2 SOURCE-TEXT ASSERTIONS CONVERTED TO EXECUTING CHECKS, which is the right response to the census ratchet rather than raising it. The launcher's argv to the POST is now captured by CALLING the launcher, and the recovery report's 2 labelled blocks are asserted on its printed OUTPUT including their ORDER, so a reader cannot meet the stale answer first. Both are strictly better than the source matches they replaced. The ceiling moves 80 -> 82 for the 2 that genuinely cannot execute, both asserting on the pre-verdict sweep shadow, which lives inline in the main round loop and cannot be reached without dispatching a whole experiment. The justification sits in the ratchet itself, which is what its own contract asks for. title: the joint round: the 2 seats CROSSED, and 7 pre-existing suite failures closed
verbatim: the joint round: the 2 seats CROSSED, and 7 pre-existing suite failures closed THE JOINT ROUND RAN, both blind rounds having been collected first, which is the precondition the founder's star-topology ruling sets. Each seat then saw the other's full position for the first time. The brief named the 5 places the blind positions actually diverged and said explicitly that changing a position for a stated reason and refusing to change it for a stated reason are equally good outcomes, while changing it for no stated reason is the only bad one. THE SEATS EXCHANGED POSITIONS ON THE MINIMUM SAMPLE, each persuaded by the other, and neither was asked to. The seat that had derived that NO minimum sample is needed moved to HOLDING that one is justified, because both positions retain a token budget that can halt the climb and a ledger that halts part way IS a cap -- which is where the symmetry argument dies. SymPy and Wolfram Language agree the order difference under a cap of 2 on 3 rungs is (p1-p3)(1-p2), not identically zero; a witness at 0.9, 0.1, 0.01 loses 0.801000 in resolution probability from order alone; and at the current effective depth of 2 a 5-observation floor is worth 0.0506 expected resolution probability per truncated finding, falling to 1.166e-19 at depth 5 where nothing truncates -- which reproduces the original derivation exactly in the regime where it holds. The seat that PROPOSED that floor withdrew it, in its own words: "A sample floor on a non-gating statistic is a cost. I withdraw it", on the ground that its own floor fails its stated purpose since a Jeffreys posterior at 5 misorders nearly as freely as at 1. BOTH NAMED THE SAME OPERATIVE CAUSE INDEPENDENTLY, which is what makes the crossing informative rather than merely contrary: the shared token ledger is what makes truncation possible and therefore what lets the estimate exclude a rung. The second seat supplied a worked construction -- a 2-model roster, cheap confirmer at cost 10, weak expensive model at 100, shared ledger 115: the correct order leaves 105 and funds the next finding, the misordered ladder leaves 5 and every rung of the next finding is unfunded. A bad estimate can exclude a rung, but on a DIFFERENT finding, through the budget rather than the ladder. ORDER-INVARIANCE SURVIVED INDEPENDENT RE-VERIFICATION and was strengthened: it holds for an arbitrary joint failure law, correlated or not, needing no independence assumption, because the event is the failure of a SET of rungs. Checked over all 120 orderings of 5 symbolic rungs with residual 0 in SymPy and in Wolfram Language, and over 200 random Dirichlet joint laws with maximum spread 0. One seat accepted that its own design reduces to the same index rule at a DOMINATED point, measuring its own ordering suboptimal in 90.93% of rosters, Wilson [89.99%, 91.78%]. It also corrected its own figure of 24 orderings, which should have been 120. THE DISAGREEMENT THAT SURVIVED IS NOW BLOCKING RATHER THAN OPEN. Order-invariance assumes a rung's success probability is fixed for a model and finding, independent of depth. The proposed aid levels feed the previous rung's falsifier forward, making it position-dependent, so the guarantee holds only at aid level 0. No aid-laddered rung may enter the statistic's denominator as a depth-0 attempt until a measurement shows depth stability. Preserved as information, not resolved by vote. 7 PRE-EXISTING SUITE FAILURES CLOSED, each with a measured cause rather than an excuse, following section_p_shortfalls.json's own rules. The 2026-10-05 round: the CLI timed out at 1800.1 s on BOTH attempts having made 0 tool calls -- and 0 calls in 1800 s twice is the distinguishing measurement, because a seat that discussed the harness would still have produced text and a seat working would have produced calls. The 2026-10-03 round: both seats failed at 1956.0 and 1956.2 s, 0.2 SECONDS APART in separate processes after UNEQUAL work (37 calls and 11), which only a cause outside both processes produces; recorded as understood but NOT fixed, because the shared cause is demonstrated and a cure is not. P4 narrowed in its own existing idiom -- it already excuses rounds whose seats CANNOT write -- so a round where every seat returned 0 characters produced no fix to deliver; the narrowing fires only when NO seat returned text, and the file's own prose-only falsifiers still refuse, so it cannot excuse what P4 exists to catch. THE STUB THAT BROKE WAS THE STUB WORKING, and its comment now says so: loosening it to **kwargs would be the wrong repair because it would stop noticing. THE PYTHON FLOOR SCAN was reading transient agent worktrees that `.git/info/exclude` keeps out of the repository, holding harvested seat output that must not be edited to make a scan pass; excluded by that path only, never by "skip anything untracked". STAGGERING, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, on the founder's question. The seats were staggered BY THE DISPATCHER, not by hand: the aliveness probes completed 4 seconds apart sequentially and the first seat's brief ran 07:08:11 to 07:22:57 with the second starting only after. The 2026-10-05 serialisation holds. The second seat's FIRST joint dispatch nonetheless died of a BrokenPipeError at 435.9 s with 19 tool calls and only 1 attempt recorded -- an OPERATOR fault, not contention and not a harness defect: it was launched with output on a pipe owned by the operator's tooling where every round that succeeded the same night was launched detached to a file. Re-dispatched detached, it returned 2220 words in 557.1 s. STILL OPEN: 5 suite failures, all pre-existing -- the live archive provenance audit, a Desktop-mirror falsifier, 2 discrimination-archive classification tests, and the canonical-config write guard. And the gamma recording recommendation, pending the founder's ruling. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: the aliveness probe is adopted by every runner, and a brief could declare a field nothing would read
verbatim: the aliveness probe is adopted by every runner, and a brief could declare a field nothing would read HIS RULING, 2026-10-06: "the simple aliveness probe was my idea, right? We should adopt this for all our runners going forward too." It was his idea, and the attribution is in the module header. The panel dispatcher had it; now reference_runner_v3 does too, before round 1. ROUTE COVERAGE IS EXPLICIT AND AN UNKNOWN ROUTE CANNOT PASS UNPROBED. `caller_for` maps all 5 api values the runner dispatches on -- claude_cli, openrouter, deepseek, google, codex_exec -- plus moonshot, reusing the orchestrator's own direct call functions so the probe travels the route the run will use. An api with no mapping RAISES rather than returning None, because None means "skip". A SIMULATED SEAT IS SKIPPED, NOT FAILED, and the distinction is load-bearing in both directions. The simulated dispatch is installed by MONKEYPATCHING the real call functions, so probing an `api="sim"` seat measures the shim and would report a green route where no route exists -- a false green is worse than no check. And treating an unprobeable seat as DEAD would refuse every simulated run. Verified by execution against the real runner: an all-simulated roster proceeds, an empty roster proceeds, a dead real route refuses and names the seat, and the roster is never reduced because skipping a model is benching it. ON SPEND, because a probe IS a dispatch and no paid dispatch happens without his express authorisation: the probe fires only for a seat the run is ALREADY authorised to dispatch with a full brief, immediately before doing so, under a 16-token ceiling against that brief's thousands. It adds no seat and reaches no route the run was not already going to use, so it spends strictly less than the run it guards, and it carries no authorisation of its own. ★ A BRIEF COULD DECLARE A DISAGREEMENT FIELD THAT NOTHING WOULD EVER RECOGNISE, and I found it by writing one. The joint brief asked for `## Residual disagreement`. `carries_disagreement` matches a heading whose alternative requires the word to OPEN the line, so a qualifier in front of it is invisible: measured, the detector returns False on both joint replies while a token search finds "disagree", "disagreement" and "Residual" in each. Both seats had disagreed at length and the round was recorded as having lost its disagreement. THE REAL DEFECT IS THAT THE VALIDATOR WAS WEAKER THAN THE DETECTOR. It tested a loose `\bdisagree` word search, which `## Residual disagreement` satisfies. Two predicates about one field, each individually correct, disagreeing about what counts -- the producer/consumer drift this project warns about, in the least visible place. Same SHAPE as the recorded integrity_advisory_r2_2026-10-02 entry, whose fix ADDED this check; this shows the check was too loose to close the gap it was built for. FIXED BY IMPORTING THE DETECTOR'S OWN PATTERN, never restating it. And the FIRST attempt at that fix was wrong in an instructive way: applying DISAGREEMENT_RE raw to a brief refused correct briefs and passed the canonical template only by accident, because the heading alternative needs the word at a LINE START, which is true of a seat's reply and false of a brief where the field is a list item. Each candidate line is now NORMALISED to the heading a seat would write -- list marker, emphasis, backticks and hashes stripped -- and the imported pattern applied to that. Verified both ways: the canonical template PASSES, the blind brief PASSES, the joint brief is REFUSED with a message naming the qualifier problem. The detector was deliberately NOT widened; the 2026-10-02 entry records that widening makes it match mentions as well as assertions. Guards: 7 new tests in test_seats_must_answer_before_work_is_passed_2026-10-06.py (23 total) holding the runner adoption, every real route having a caller, an unknown route raising, and a simulated roster proceeding; 4 new in test_a_brief_names_disagreement_as_a_field_2026-10-02.py holding both directions of the field check and that the pattern is IMPORTED rather than copied. The joint round's P5 shortfall is recorded per seat with its measured cause, which clears test_the_misses_are_the_ones_we_think_they_are.
