Each candidate line is now NORMALISED to the heading a seat would write -- list marker, emphasis, backticks and hashes stripped -- and the imported pattern applied to that. Verified both ways: the canonical template PASSES, the blind brief PASSES, the joint brief is REFUSED with a message naming the qualifier problem. The detector was deliberately NOT widened; the 2026-10-02 entry records that widening makes it match mentions as well as assertions. title: a retry no longer erases the attempt it replaces, and 2 zombie waiters are killed
verbatim: a retry no longer erases the attempt it replaces, and 2 zombie waiters are killed HIS RULING, 2026-10-06: "We need to ensure all failures are recorded, both here in the review rounds and more formally in the registry in both the simulated and real experimental branches ... The purpose of recording failures is that a researcher should be able to retrace all their steps to understand exactly what happened." THE REVIEW-ROUND HALF IS DONE. A re-dispatch overwrote `<seat>.json`. Measured: the fable seat's first joint dispatch returned 0 words after 435.9 s and 19 tool calls ending in BrokenPipeError, and the surviving file records `attempts: [{"attempt": 1}]` with `ok: true` -- the round's own artefacts assert a clean single-attempt success and the failure is gone. `_preserve_prior_attempt` now moves a prior reply AND its tools log to `<stem>.attemptN.json.txt` before any write. THE SUFFIX IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE FIRST VERSION GOT IT WRONG. A preserved `fable.attempt1.json` was counted as a REPLY by the Section P guard while the compliance script was not, and the 2 populations diverged by exactly 1 (145 against 144). `.json.txt` is the project's existing archival convention -- evidence/ stores seat code as `.py.txt` and briefs as `.md.txt` -- so an archival copy stays out of the scanners that walk live artefacts. THE DESTROYED ATTEMPT WAS RECOVERED, PARTIALLY, AND SAYS SO. The seat's sandbox was built at 07:32:34, BEFORE the overwrite, so its copy still held the failed file and `seat_proposals.diff` captured it. The recovery is PARTIAL: the diff truncates long tool-call previews, so the '+' side does not parse as JSON and the 19-call array is unrecoverable. Written to `fable.attempt1.PARTIAL.json.txt` declaring itself partial, naming its provenance and naming what is lost. That it survived only by a sandbox accident is the argument FOR the fix, not against it. 2 ZOMBIE BACKGROUND WAITERS KILLED, and the cause is a self-matching predicate. The wait loops ran `until ! pgrep -f confer_maths_panel`, and each loop's OWN command line contains that string, so pgrep matched the waiter itself and the condition could never become true. They spun for 50m07s and 44m10s against a panel that had finished. Measured at the point of the kill: `pgrep -f "bench/confer_maths_panel"` returned nothing while `pgrep -f confer_maths_panel` returned 2. The bracket form `[b]ench/confer_maths_panel` cannot self-match. THE REGISTRY HALF IS NOT DONE AND IS NOT STARTED, deliberately. `_report_dispatch_failure` reports to the IMMUNE layer as a DetectorDiagnosis and creates no durable record; there is no dispatch-failure channel in runner_state or the report. The gap is real. It is not implemented because a dispatch failure is an event about the RUN, not a finding about the TARGET, and `run_experiment` passes `total_findings=len(registry.entries)` into the convergence gate -- so recording failures AS registry entries would feed them to gamma. That needs his ruling, and the measurement supporting it is in scripts/registry_is_the_evidence_base_2026-10-06.py. Guard: test_a_retry_never_erases_the_attempt_it_replaces_2026-10-06.py, 8 tests, including that BOTH the reply and the tools log are preserved, that repeated dispatches do not collide, that the archival suffix is used, and that a preserved attempt is not counted as a landed seat. title: record the founder's clear/archive/delete ruling, with what it costs and what it would orphan
verbatim: record the founder's clear/archive/delete ruling, with what it costs and what it would orphan HIS RULING, 2026-10-06: a researcher may want to clear an experiment's records or keep them, and that is their call rather than the designer's. Clear offers a sub-choice of Archive or Delete; Archive points at one clear location; the aim is a familiar environment close to a standard desktop operating system. Whether that paradigm extends further is undecided, and the brief says so rather than assuming. THIS SUPERSEDES MY OWN RECOMMENDATION of archive-only, which was wrong in the way he named: it predicted what a researcher wants instead of asking them. MEASURED, so the design is not argued from intuition (scripts/registry_is_the_evidence_base_2026-10-06.py and the sizing in this commit): * PER-EXPERIMENT IS THE EXISTING BOUNDARY. 324 run directories, 59 carrying a registry, 0 registries shared between runs. * EXPORT FITS WITH NO STRUCTURAL CHANGE. All 6 fields an entry needs to stand alone are present in 3,158 of 3,158 entries, 100%, Wilson [99.8785%, 100%]. * ARCHIVING IS CHEAP, which weakens the usual argument for delete. 324 run directories hold 0.696 GiB; median 0.2 MiB, mean 2.2 MiB, and 1 of 324 exceeds 100 MiB -- 0.3086%, Wilson [0.0545%, 1.7273%]. NumPy and a pure-Python sum agree to 1e-6; statsmodels and a closed-form Wilson agree to 1e-12. The large artefacts are the per-seat sandboxes, which live elsewhere and are the only thing needing a size policy. ★ THE ONE ENGINEERING CONSEQUENCE. All 59 runs store their derived series OUTSIDE the registry -- gamma, gate, rho and novelty histories -- so deleting an experiment's entries leaves those numbers standing with nothing behind them. On a real run: 75 entries removed, 5 series surviving, and the experiment still reports a gamma it can no longer derive. A desktop OS does NOT have this problem, which is why the metaphor needs an addition rather than a caveat: deleting a document there leaves no stale summary of it elsewhere still claiming to be current. Here it would. So the unit archived or deleted must be the evidence AND its derived numbers together. Then Delete is honest, because what goes is the whole claim rather than only its support. AND AN ARCHIVE LOCATION ALREADY EXISTS: ~/Desktop/CDSFL_archive, created 2026-08-19 for the encrypted evidence store. The interface must adopt it deliberately or pick a visibly distinct one; 2 different things both called the archive, in a design whose stated aim is familiarity, is the one outcome to avoid. Nothing is implemented. The UX does not exist yet and this is design capture. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: the ladder climbs 4 measured models and its last rung points back at the source
verbatim: the ladder climbs 4 measured models and its last rung points back at the source HIS RULINGS, 2026-10-06/07, both implemented. THE LADDER NOW CLIMBS. `--seat-models` defaulted to `uniform`, so every simulated seat was answered by 1 model and the map was consulted by nothing -- cause 2 of 2 in the record for the inert ladder, never fixed at the launcher. Default is now `ladder`; `uniform` stays as a deliberate control arm. 4 DISTINCT MODELS, EVERY ID PROBED BEFORE IT WAS WIRED. The map resolved 6 seats onto 2 models, so it could separate 2 behaviours however many seats ran. Each candidate was dispatched through the aliveness probe at a 16-token ceiling on 2026-10-07 and answered: opus 6.60 s, fable 5.69 s, sonnet 7.24 s, haiku 3.97 s. `opusplan` answered too and is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED -- a routing alias serving different models for planning and execution, so the record could not say which model replied, and provenance is the one thing he does want a name to carry. Cost moves DOWN: 4 of 6 seats previously resolved to `opus`, now 2 do. THE ASSIGNMENT IS ARBITRARY ON PURPOSE. A round-robin over sorted seat names. His standing position: "the only thing that should impact on capability is measured capability. A models name should have little to do with it, beyond recording this." A map pairing a seat labelled Codex with a model chosen because someone believes Codex is strong is the exact defect he has objected to 4 times. This map exists to give the measurement real heterogeneity to find, and nothing else. 2 TESTS WERE ASSERTING THAT DEFECT AND ARE REWRITTEN, NOT WEAKENED. `test_fable_seat_is_answered_by_fable` passed only because the map paired like with like, so it could not tell a faithful map from a lucky one; it now checks EVERY seat against whatever the map says, starting from a model the map does not name so a pass cannot come from a default leaking through. `test_the_faithful_map_is_still_faithful` required 3 seats to sit on `opus` because they are "top-3 vendors in the validated strength order" -- a capability claim keyed on a vendor name, written into the suite. It now asserts that no id reaches the map unprobed. AN ANTI-VACUITY PROBE EXPIRED WELL AND IS REBUILT. It asserted the REAL map yields 0 mixed prefixes at budget 2, which stopped reproducing the moment the ladder widened -- the improvement the widening was for. A probe that depends on production being broken stops working when production is fixed and then passes on nothing. It now CONSTRUCTS its degenerate map and owns its own failure, with a second test showing the real map passing where the degenerate one cannot. ★ THE LAST RUNG POINTS BACK AT THE SOURCE. His ruling: "even with all our models being the same ... at least one rung on the ladder should point back to the original model and say, 'your solution didn't work' or 'your falsifier is broken' please fix". It is NOT a blind retry: the source is handed the VERDICT its own attempt earned and the code that earned it, which is information it did not have the first time -- the same thing the ladder gives a stronger rung, applied to the only rung left. On a 1-model roster, where `rank_falsifier_writers` returns an empty list by construction, this is the only rung there has ever been. Default ON per "no harm in turning it on and leaving it on"; `self_rung_enabled=False` preserves the pre-registered exp56 1-seat arm, which has not yet run. ★★ AND IT BROKE A PROXY TWICE, WHICH IS THE INSTRUCTIVE PART. The runner read `rungs_tried == 0` to mean "the ladder was empty by construction" -- exact while every rung came from the ranked list. The self-rung dispatches PRECISELY when that list is empty, so the count became 1 and the discriminator silently stopped firing: the finding lost its `routing_deferred` stamp, never entered `irreducible_queue_count`, and HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM could not fire -- the pre-registered reportable outcome of the exp56 1-seat arm. One level up, `len(_routing_attempts) > _n0` read "did we reach anyone", which answered no exactly when the ladder was empty; the self-rung made it answer yes and the case fell into "retry a later round", which is futile when no other writer exists in any round. `RoutingResult.ladder_was_empty` now records the FACT, and the empty-ladder deferral is tested before the reached-a-model branch. Mutations: removing the self-rung fails 1; restoring either proxy fails 1. Baseline 67 passed across the empty-ladder, ladder-prefix, seat-model and POST guards. title: the filer's failure now counts in its own denominator, so an empty record stops reading as a perfect one
verbatim: the filer's failure now counts in its own denominator, so an empty record stops reading as a perfect one HIS VERDICT, 2026-10-06, on the cc2 seat's finding: "Verdict. Fix it." THE OTHER HALF OF THE 2026-10-06 REPAIR. That repair fixed the NUMERATOR: a routed confirmation is credited to the model that WROTE the falsifier rather than the one that filed the finding. The filer then received nothing at all -- not the confirmation, and not the failed attempt either. So a model that files criticals it never resolves accumulated NO denominator, and an empty record read as a perfect one. IT IS NOT A PENALTY. Routing fires only on a critical whose source did not resolve it, so a routed entry IS a recorded failed attempt by the filer. Counting it records the attempt that actually happened. I DO NOT CLAIM TO HAVE REPRODUCED THE SEAT'S FIGURE. It reported 5 of 11 INVERSIONS, which counts pairwise order flips; this measures how many models CHANGE RANK. A measure that omits a model's failures is not a measure of capability; it is a measure of how often that model was routed away from. title: the last 4 suite failures, each fixed at its root cause rather than re-baselined
verbatim: the last 4 suite failures, each fixed at its root cause rather than re-baselined HIS VERDICT, 2026-10-06: "Verdict: do the work." None of these came from the overnight work; all 4 were standing failures. ★★★ AN ABBREVIATED SHA'S LENGTH IS A PROPERTY OF THE REPOSITORY, NOT THE COMMIT (2 of the 4). `discrimination_control_archive` finds an archived finding's baseline with `sha == row["baseline_sha"]`, where the left side comes from `git log --format=%h` -- abbreviated to whatever length the repository CURRENTLY needs for uniqueness. All 97 archived rows store a 7-character sha from when they were written; this clone has since grown enough that git emits 8, so `83dd7ab` is now reported as `83dd7ab4`. Every equality therefore failed. `baseline` fell back to "", every archived proposed fix "did not apply", and 30 rows collapsed from their 2 real causes (17 + 13) into the coarse `errored_route_had_no_effective_patch`. Nothing about the archive or the commits changed: the repository crossed the threshold where git lengthens its abbreviation, and a comparison against an auto-sized value silently inverted. Verified by execution before and after -- `_apply_fix` applies the same fix to the same baseline cleanly, 60,331 -> 60,755 characters, once the baseline is actually found. Matching by prefix restores the exact expected distribution. THE CHEAP WRONG FIX WAS AVAILABLE AND IS WHY THE GUARD EXISTS: re-measuring EXPECTED_CAUSE_COUNTS against the broken classification would have turned both tests green and made the defect the new baseline. 3 guards hold the mechanism instead, including one that deliberately does NOT assume which length git emits, because pinning that would hide the defect until the next growth step. ★★ A CONTAINMENT GUARD WAS POISONING ITSELF. `test_git_cannot_write_the_canonical_config` wrote a FIXED probe key into the real `.git/config` and never removed it, so a single historical lapse failed it on every later run for ever. Measured: the key was present with value 1 and `.git/config` was last written 2026-10-04 -- 3 days earlier -- while a live probe in the same minute was REFUSED ("could not lock config file .git/config: Operation not permitted", exit 255) and left nothing behind. The containment was working perfectly and the guard was reporting a 3-day-old artefact of its own making as a current breach, which is the most expensive false alarm there is: it makes a working control look broken. The key is now unique per run and removed in a `finally`, and an anti-vacuity test writes one UNCONFINED to prove the read can see a value that IS there. ★ THE ARCHIVE AUDIT WAS WALKING SEAT SCRATCH. `latent_control_audit` globbed `bench/logs/**/*.json` and so reached into `sandbox_harvest/`, admitting a seat's SYNTHETIC report (`fingerprint_ladder_review_2026-10-05/.../.scratch/ps/synthetic_run/x_report.json`) as an archive report. Its directory name carries no timestamp, so it had no recorded provenance -- and a tool whose whole purpose is to refuse inferred dates was reporting an UNKNOWN age it had manufactured for itself. The harvest is preserved deliberately and is not deleted; it simply is not the archive. 35 passed across the 3 files that held all 4 failures. title: the runner now serialises seats that share one credential, as the panel already did
verbatim: the runner now serialises seats that share one credential, as the panel already did HIS VERDICT, 2026-10-06, on the free-seat contention: "Then if it can be fixed, you almost certainly should." THE EVIDENCE. On 2026-10-03 a panel round returned 0 characters from BOTH free seats at 1956.0 and 1956.2 seconds -- 0.2 seconds apart in 2 separate processes, after UNEQUAL work (37 tool calls and 11). Independent failures do not land 0.2 s apart after unequal work; only a cause outside both processes does, and both seats authenticate against one Max subscription. The panel was serialised on 2026-10-05. The RUNNER was not: `run_experiment` dispatches through `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(eligible))` in 2 places, so every seat went out at once. WHY IT BECAME URGENT TODAY RATHER THAN BEING A STANDING NICETY. While the simulated roster resolved to ONE model the concurrency was harmless. Widening the ladder to 4 distinct CLI models, earlier in this same work order and on his ruling, is what made the contention reachable in simulation at all. The thing that made it necessary and the fix land together. ONE LOCK, APPLIED AT THE SEAT DISPATCH so both call sites are covered rather than patching 2 pools. It is held across the WHOLE dispatch rather than just the first call, because the tool loop keeps using the same credential for as long as the seat is working. The decorator that records seat completion stays on the outer function; the work moves to `_dispatch_single_model_inner`. ADDITIVE AND CHEAP. No seat is dropped. Routes that do NOT share a credential still run fully concurrently with each other AND with the serialised group, so a mixed roster is no slower than before -- asserted by execution, not assumed. The cost is wall clock on the shared group only, bounded by the sum rather than the max of its members. NOT A DEMONSTRATED CURE, and the panel's own comment says the same of its version: contention explains the matched failure times and has NOT been tested by running both ways. This is a scheduling change with a stated reason. Guard: test_shared_credential_seats_are_serialised_2026-10-07.py, 6 tests, every one EXECUTING the real `_dispatch_single_model` against a stubbed inner and measuring the actual time windows. It holds both directions -- 2 and 4 CLI seats must not overlap, 2 independent seats MUST overlap, and a CLI seat must not block an independent one, because a control that serialises everything is an outage. The anti-vacuity test confirms concurrently submitted seats DO overlap when unserialised, so the serialisation tests cannot pass on a slow machine. Mutation: emptying the shared-route set fails 2. title: the 6 dormant switches are decided: 0 retire, 5 retain, 1 scheduled
verbatim: the 6 dormant switches are decided: 0 retire, 5 retain, 1 scheduled HIS VERDICT, 2026-10-06, on the toggle design brief: "Verdict, do the investigation and do the work." NOTHING IS DEAD. All 6 switches armed in 0 of 49 real configs are READ BY LIVE CODE, and 5 of them gate a real branch AND have a test that turns them on -- dormant BY CHOICE rather than by neglect. The additive standard's removal clause applies to none of them. WHY A REFERENCE COUNT COULD NOT DECIDE IT. Grepping each name returns 121 to 1,749 hits, because `resume` is a substring of `resumed` and `presume` and because a switch is discussed in comments far more often than it is read. The 3 discriminators that matter are structural and an AST settles them: is it read by NON-TEST code, does any test set it True, and is the read used as a CONDITION. ★ THE TOOL WAS WRONG ONCE, IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. Its first version counted a read as gating only when the read NODE sat inside a condition, so the ordinary shape `explicitly = bool(getattr(cfg, "models_were_declared", False))` followed by `if not explicitly ...` scored 1 read and 0 gates. It reported `models_were_declared` as "read but gates nothing" -- this project's own phrase for a dead addition -- when it gates a real roster-filtering branch at reference_runner_v3.py:6773. A measurement that under-reports toward CONDEMNING working code is worse than no measurement, because the action it recommends is destructive. The detector now follows one local assignment, and a regression test holds both directions: a gate through a local IS counted, and a read that truly gates nothing is still reported, so the tool can still find a dead flag. THE ONE SCHEDULE ITEM IS HONEST ABOUT BEING ONE. `hil_review` is live in the ACTIVE runner -- a config field, a `--hil-review` flag that sets it, and 2 branches that pause a run for human review -- and no test has ever turned it on. Its CLI wiring IS executed by the new guard. Its gate is NOT, because the branches sit inside `run_experiment` and need a real round; asserting on their source would be a structural claim standing in for evidence that the branch runs. Recorded as an outstanding measurement in the work-in-flight ledger, and a test fails if that record disappears. Guards: test_dormant_switches_are_decided_2026-10-07.py, 5 tests. Producer: scripts/dormant_switch_investigation_2026-10-07.py, answering --help for nothing. Also closed: the boot check item. POST is green at 5 of 5; the crashed-check defect he asked about was repaired overnight. title: gamma is not demoted, and the evidence does not yet support changing it either way
verbatim: gamma is not demoted, and the evidence does not yet support changing it either way HIS CHALLENGE, 2026-10-06: "That sounds like gamma demotion. Back to a recorded statistic only? ... gamma is a foundational aspect of the maths model and of the project as a whole. Why would we do that?" And: "making the capability ladder run until the problem has been resolved causing Gamma to become more difficult is anti-intuitive ... one might justifiably expect that the problem would be resolved relatively quickly? That indeed has been our experience so far." NOTHING IS DEMOTED AND NOTHING IS RECORDED-ONLY. The panel's remedy is not implemented. What follows is why it should not be, on the evidence. ★ THE PANEL'S MEASUREMENT HELD TIMING FIXED, AND TIMING IS THE WHOLE POINT. It flipped every unresolved critical to CONFIRMED **at its existing open_since_round**. So it answers "what if these had been resolved" and NOT "what if the ladder had resolved them PROMPTLY" -- and prompt resolution is exactly what removing the rung cap is FOR. Measured: of 210 archived routed resolutions, **174 landed in a LATER round than the one that filed them** and only 36 in the same round, median gap 1 round, mean 1.43, max 12. Routing TODAY mostly defers. Exhaustion is the change that could stop it deferring. THE 3-WORLD COMPARISON, over 33 runs with at least 3 rounds (scripts/gamma_and_when_the_ladder_resolves_2026-10-07.py): A as recorded, B resolved LATE (the panel's construction), C resolved PROMPTLY (pulled earlier by the measured median gap). B lower than A : 6 of 33 = 18.1818% Wilson [8.6108%, 34.3882%] C higher than B: 5 of 33 = 15.1515% Wilson [6.6505%, 30.9199%] crossings of the 0.30 arm DOWN from A to B : 0 crossings BACK UP from B to C : 1 HIS INTUITION IS DIRECTIONALLY SUPPORTED AND NOT ESTABLISHED, and the honest statement is both halves. Pulling resolutions earlier does raise gamma, in 15% of runs with an interval from 7% to 31%. That is a direction, not a result. AND I DO NOT CLAIM TO REFUTE THE PANEL. My construction uses `severity >= 0.7` with `open_since_round`; theirs uses the runner's own `_settled_novelty_series`. Different populations and different criteria over the same archive, so the 0 crossings here neither confirm nor contradict their 2 of 14. Presenting it as a refutation would be the borrowed-number defect this project refuses. HIS SIZING INSTINCT IS SUPPORTED: "in 2 out of 14 runs pushing the gamma arm down this does not seem out of bounds for potential error". 2 of 14 carries Wilson [4.0094%, 39.9414%]. An interval spanning an order of magnitude is not a basis for altering the most protected part of the model. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, and it is narrower than either framing: gamma_critical is SENSITIVE TO WHEN criticals resolve, so the rung budget is an undeclared input to the convergence gate. Whether exhaustion raises or lowers it IN PRACTICE is established by neither measurement, because neither models what exhaustion does to TIMING. The decisive evidence is a paired run -- exhaustion on against the cap -- which is an experiment, not a code change, and it belongs in the study programme. ON HIS LADDER-INVERSION HYPOTHESIS, which he offered as the alternative explanation: the order is NOT inverted. `DEFAULT_FALSIFIER_STRENGTH` is ('Codex', 'CC2', 'ChatGPT', 'Gemini', 'DeepSeek') -- Codex strongest, DeepSeek weakest, matching his stated experience. But with the denominator repaired earlier today the measured live rates are Codex 0.2818 > Gemini 0.2644 > ChatGPT 0.1567 > CC2 0.1510 > DeepSeek 0.1382. **The extremes agree and the MIDDLE is wrong**: Gemini measures 2nd and is ranked 4th; CC2 measures 4th and is ranked 2nd. So his instinct that the ordering is suspect is right, in a narrower place than he proposed. rg on gamma demotion: consulted the 4 anchoring memory files on the ladder, the gamma challenge and measured capability, plus the GAMMA IS LOAD-BEARING directive and the routing order in live code. title: a measured number per model fails the founder's test exactly as cheapest-first does
verbatim: a measured number per model fails the founder's test exactly as cheapest-first does HIS TENSION, 2026-10-07: "Why put for example a highly complex problem, like the Riemann hypothesis, to a model like DeepSeek (or even Haiku), when its resources are better suited to dealing with less complex problems? Can you see the tension?" THE TENSION IS REAL AND MEASUREMENT ALONE DOES NOT DISSOLVE IT, which is the result worth having. Computed with SymPy and floats agreeing, over 3 configurations whose task-conditioned rates are cheap (0.70 easy / 0.02 hard, cost 1), mid (0.75 / 0.25, cost 4) and strong (0.80 / 0.60, cost 10), the first configuration tried on a HARD task is: cheapest-first -> cheap; strongest-first -> strong; **index rule on a single GLOBAL p per model -> cheap**; index rule on a TASK-CONDITIONED p -> mid, with cheap LAST. So a measured statistic that is one number per model reproduces the exact failure he objects to, because one number cannot tell a hard task from an easy one. Only conditioning on the task puts the weak configuration last -- automatically, with no vendor name consulted, which is his standing ruling implemented rather than argued. It also selects NEITHER extreme: `mid` returns more risk-reduction per unit cost on hard work than `strong`. ★ I ALSO OWE A CORRECTION. Earlier today I reported the measured live rates as Codex 0.2818 > Gemini 0.2644 > ChatGPT > CC2 > DeepSeek and concluded "the middle is wrong". That inference was CONTAMINATED, and bench/routing.py already carried the founder's own warning against it from 2026-08-23: do not re-derive the order without checking falsifier provenance. It even names the signature -- on Exp 55 Gemini scored 2 of 2 with falsifiers that never opened their target while DeepSeek scored 0 of 2 with genuine readers, so re-deriving ranks models "by their willingness to ignore the evidence". My measurement did not filter. FILTERED TO PROVENANCE-CLEAN ATTEMPTS the archive supports almost nothing: CC2 21/35 = 0.6000 Wilson [0.4357, 0.7445] and Codex 22/37 = 0.5946 Wilson [0.4349, 0.7365]. Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek have FEWER THAN 20 clean attempts in the whole archive, and the 2 that qualify have almost perfectly overlapping intervals. Power: separating 2 models differing by 0.15 at 80% power needs 173 clean attempts EACH, and by 0.20 still 97 each (statsmodels, cross-checked against a hand-computed Cohen h of 0.301525). We have 35 and 37. SO THE FROZEN TUPLE IS NOT A RIVAL THEORY OF CAPABILITY. It is a placeholder standing where measurement does not yet exist at volume, which is also why both panel seats declined to delete it without defending it on merit. PANEL DISPATCHED, 0 PAID, on his instruction. `ladder_allocation_resolution_2026-10-07` puts 5 questions to both free seats: whether the Astra spec's section 6 policy resolves the tension or relocates it, the smallest honest estimator fieldable at 35 and 37 clean attempts, the frozen tuple's retirement condition, the try-order direction under exhaustion against a cap, and what everyone has missed. Both seats answered the aliveness probe in 5.03 s and 6.65 s. NOTHING IS IMPLEMENTED. `d` was in force. title: the panel overturned the brief's own evidence: 68.65% of archived falsifiers are misclassified
verbatim: the panel overturned the brief's own evidence: 68.65% of archived falsifiers are misclassified FREE 2-SEAT BLIND ROUND, 0 PAID, on the founder's instruction. Both seats answered on the first attempt: 4,857 and 3,066 words, 1007.2 s and 949.7 s. ★★★ THE BRIEF'S EVIDENTIAL BASE WAS AN ARTEFACT, AND SO WAS WHAT I TOLD HIM. `competence_provenance.falsifier_style` decides whether a falsifier reached its target with a regex for file-opening -- while this project's OWN directive requires a falsifier to "Import the REAL target module". An import matches none of those patterns. Verified independently after the round: of 1,078 archived falsifiers carrying code, 760 are scored not-reaching, and **740 of those DO reach by import, importlib, runpy or subprocess -- 68.65% of ALL archived falsifiers, Wilson [65.81%, 71.34%]**. Only 20 are genuinely detached. My "35 and 37 clean attempts, so nothing can be ranked" was built on that. AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS ALSO WRONG. On a PROSE target an import reaches nothing, so a classifier that credits imports inflates exactly the Exp 55 case the founder's 2026-08-23 warning names. One rule cannot serve both target types. CORRECTED, THE ARCHIVE DOES RANK ONE THING. Both the seat and I rebuilt the table with target-type conditioning INDEPENDENTLY and got different rates -- the seat 0.62 to 0.85, me 0.78 to 0.98. That disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed, because 2 reconstructions of one quantity differing that much says the classifier needs repairing properly rather than approximated twice. They agree on the structure: no model below 61 clean attempts in either, and after correcting for 10 simultaneous pair tests the seat found 1 surviving separation and I found 3, with the SAME model losing every one. DeepSeek is measurably last. The frozen tuple already puts it last. ★★ THE 2 SEATS DISAGREED ON A FACT THAT DECIDES THE ANSWER, and I verified it: **the cap has NOT left.** `routing_max_rungs` defaults to 2 and **0 of 49 real config files pin it**; the removal applies to the simulated launcher only. One seat's estimator is described as "safe only because the cap is removed" -- that premise is false for every real run. Under a cap, order decides which findings are reached at all: one seat measured the resolved share swinging 23-fold from ordering alone, 0.7000 under the best prefix to 0.0298 under the worst. SO THE DIRECTION QUESTION IS SETTLED AGAINST MY EARLIER FRAMING. Cheapest-first is correct only under exhaustion. Under the cap every real configuration uses, strongest-first is the coverage-maximising order, which is what the code already does. Composing them is strictly worse than either. The 90.93% "strongest-first is suboptimal" figure is a property of an ASSUMED cost generator -- with equal costs strongest-first is optimal always -- and this repository has no cost table at all. BOTH SEATS REJECTED MY RETIREMENT RULE, on different grounds, and both are right. It never retires the tuple for 2 genuinely EQUAL models, because equal rates overlap at every sample size, so names persist forever in the likeliest case. And a comparator that is measured where it separates and name-based where it does not is not an ordering: one seat EXECUTED a 3-model case producing a cycle, a > c > b > a. Sorting on a cyclic comparator is undefined behaviour. THE PROPOSAL THAT SURVIVES dissolves the threshold instead of restating it: one lexicographic key of measured rate over cost, then tuple position, then label. Cold start gives the tuple order; data makes the tuple stop mattering pair by pair. No retirement predicate, transitive by construction, deterministic at 5 models and 500. ON THE ASTRA SPEC the founder pointed to: both seats agree it RELOCATES the tension. Its formula degenerates to cheapest-first exactly when the conditioned estimate is empty, which is this repository's state. One seat adds that the spec is not in the repository and no repository code references it, so under the additive standard it is a document rather than a capability -- which corrects my own framing of it to him. The other derived that its value term uses a form the mathematical appendix superseded on 2026-09-21, and that an assessment already in the repository measured 14.94% ranking inversions from it. NOTHING MERGED. Fixes are suggested to the human in the loop, never applied. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: the try-order question has two objectives, and no single key optimises both
verbatim: the try-order question has two objectives, and no single key optimises both The founder observed that none of the three proposals dissolved the tension. He was right, and the reason is structural rather than a failure of nerve by any seat: the falsifier ladder under a rung cap attaches two different objectives to two different decisions, and they have different optima. COVERAGE P(no seat resolves) = prod(1-p_i) over the seats tried. ORDER-INVARIANT -- a property of the SET. Verified over all 120 permutations symbolically in SymPy with 0 mismatches, and over exact Fractions yielding 1 distinct value. SPEND E[cost to first CONFIRMED] = sum_j c_j prod_{i<j}(1-p_i). ORDER-DEPENDENT, minimised by the cross-multiplied key p_i*c_j >= p_j*c_i. z3 returns unsat on a counterexample search in BOTH directions; brute force over 400 random instances attains the global optimum 400 of 400 times, Wilson [99.0488%, 100.0000%]. So "which seats" and "in what sequence" are separate questions. Every proposal so far -- the capability-ascending ladder, CC1's measured-with-name-fallback comparator, and Astra's value-over-cost estimator -- answered the second and left the first undecided. Worked instance under the live cap of 2: the coverage-optimal pair leaves the finding unresolved with probability 0.18, the spend-optimal pair 0.855, a factor of 4.75. Among free seats E[spend] is identically 0 for every order, so the ordering objective is not merely wrong there, it is vacuous: 1 distinct value across 6 orders. TWO PREDICATES IN THE FIRST VERSION OF THE SCRIPT WERE WRONG, both failing toward a comfortable answer, and both are recorded in the module docstring: * it globbed bench/configs, which has never existed, and reported 0 config files -- indistinguishable from "no config pins the cap". The real configs are in bench/expNN_configs. The denominator is 47, not the 49 quoted to the founder earlier the same day. * it discovered FREE_SEATS by walking bench/**/*.py with last-match-wins, and landed on a sandbox harvest copy under bench/logs rather than live code. It also counted routing_enabled literally and missed the legacy alias take_up_slack_enabled: 5 configs set the literal key, 23 of 47 have routing effectively on. MEASURED on the live tree: routing_max_rungs defaults to 2 and 0 of 47 configs pin it, Wilson [0.0000%, 7.5558%]. The ladder is 5 rungs, so 3 seats are never asked at all, and the order decides which 2 of the 10 possible pairs is tried. The order can matter in 22 of 23 routed configs, Wilson [79.0088%, 99.2283%]. 1 rung is free (CC2); fable is free and is not on the ladder at all. bench/tests/test_two_objectives_cannot_share_one_key_2026-10-07.py holds 12 tests that CALL the functions rather than reading them, 2 of which are mutations asserting that a probability-only key is not spend-optimal and a cost-only key is not coverage-optimal. title: p-pass: the decomposition survives, and his own ruling dissolves the half it names
verbatim: p-pass: the decomposition survives, and his own ruling dissolves the half it names THE ATTEMPT TO BREAK IT. The decomposition assumes the tried set is "the first K rungs in the order". If an ERRORED rung freed its slot for a later seat, the realised set would depend on WHO errored rather than on the order, coverage would stop being order-invariant, and the split would collapse. OBSERVED by execution against the live `route`, with stub seats and no spend: it does not collapse. The budget is applied as a SLICE, `list(rungs)[:_budget]`, so an errored rung is already inside the slice and its `continue` buys no replacement. Cap 2 with rung 1 erroring still dispatches exactly ['Codex', 'CC2']; cap 2 with both erroring still dispatches 2 and reaches no 3rd seat. THE SAME LINES CARRY HIS RULING, and it changes the conclusion I reported minutes earlier. `bench/routing.py` quotes him verbatim, 2026-10-06: *"I don't think there should be a cap at all. If it's a measured statistic, along with capability fingerprinting then the problem should run until it is either resolved, or the ladder is exhausted. (No more models to try.)"* And `max_rungs=0` is already wired to mean exhaust: executed against the live ladder it dispatches all 5 rungs, not 2. Under exhaustion the tried set is the WHOLE ladder. prod(1 - p_i) is then a CONSTANT -- 1 distinct value over all 120 permutations -- so the SELECTION question disappears and only expected spend remains, which is exactly the problem the cross-multiplied comparator solves optimally. SO THE TENSION IS DISSOLVED BY HIS OWN RULING, AND THE CAP OF 2 IS WHAT KEEPS IT ALIVE. The conditioned estimate of p is required only if the cap stays. What remains open is that the ruling is not in force: `routing_max_rungs` still defaults to 2 and 0 of 47 configs set it to 0. That is a wiring gap, not a design question. 5 further guards added, 17 in the file, every one CALLING `route` rather than reading it. One of the 5 branched on whether a module was already in `sys.modules` and could therefore have passed for the wrong reason depending on test order; it now reads its erroring set from the ladder the call actually uses, so it cannot pass by naming seats that were never on it. Both notes and the TTS companion carry the correction rather than the superseded conclusion. All 3 return 0 findings from scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py and the TTS file carries 0 markdown markers. title: rs itself is network-dependent, which is why an offline recovery resource is load-bearing
verbatim: rs itself is network-dependent, which is why an offline recovery resource is load-bearing HIS OBSERVATION, 2026-10-07: *"You should have your notes too to account for network instability. This could be a useful resource also going forward, regardless of network state."* Acting on it turned up the reason it is not merely convenient. FOUND. 11 of the 25 failures on the 2026-10-07 full board -- 44.0000%, Wilson [26.6656%, 62.9327%] of the failures, against a board failure rate of 25 of 10331 decided = 0.241990%, Wilson [0.163971%, 0.357000%] -- are a single cause: scripts/cdsfl_recover.py crashes when the network is unreachable. FOLLOWED. git_state() in scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:59 is called by 3 live scripts, not 1: cdsfl_recover.py:833 (rs), cdsfl_sv.py:2821 (sv) and cdsfl_qc.py:99 (qc). Line 80 fetches unconditionally. So all 3 MC commands share the fault. ANALYSED by substituting each failure mode into the live function. A fetch that exits NON-ZERO is already tolerated -- `_run_git_rc` returns (rc, stdout) and remote_sync degrades to a sensible string. A fetch that cannot RUN is not: `subprocess.run(..., timeout=30)` RAISES TimeoutExpired, and a dead interface raises OSError, and neither is caught anywhere on the path. fetch exits non-zero -> SURVIVES, remote_sync "up to date with origin/..." fetch TimeoutExpired -> CRASHES fetch OSError -> CRASHES The class is network-CONDITIONAL and not a regression: the same 10 tests in test_recovery_marker_2026-09-08.py pass in 164.78 s on a later run with the link up. It is NOT recorded in bench/directives/universal/section_p_shortfalls.json, so it was untracked rather than known-and-closed. NOT FIXED. The repair is 1 point in 1 function -- degrade the raised forms onto the path the non-zero return code already takes -- and it is PROPOSED only, because fixes are suggested to the human in the loop rather than applied. ADDED instead, which is what he endorsed: experimental_notes/OFFLINE_RECOVERY.md, a standing resource with no date in its name, carrying a 10-step sequence whose every command was confirmed to make no network call. It states plainly that rs, sv and qc must NOT be run while the link is down, and it names the condition under which the file itself becomes wrong: a listed script acquiring a network call. Offline-safety was established by counting network and git_state references per script rather than by reading intentions. WORK_IN_FLIGHT_2026-10-07.md is brought current through items 13 to 19 and carries 4 items for his ruling. Both files return 0 findings from scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py. title: recovery survives an unreachable network, fable joins the ladder, and 2 of the 25 board failures close
verbatim: recovery survives an unreachable network, fable joins the ladder, and 2 of the 25 board failures close THE FOUNDER AUTHORISED BOTH FIXES, 2026-10-07: on the first, *"I don't know what a git_state repair is. But if it needs doing, you should probably do this too."* On the second, *"Then why not name the model? Is it Fable? Then yes we should add it."* 1. git_state() NO LONGER CRASHES WHEN THE NETWORK IS DOWN. FOLLOWED FIRST: git_state() is called by 3 live scripts, not 1 -- cdsfl_recover.py:833 (rs), cdsfl_sv.py:2821 (sv), cdsfl_qc.py:99 (qc) -- and nothing anywhere caught a raised git failure. ANALYSED by substituting each failure mode into the live function: a fetch exiting NON-ZERO survived, while TimeoutExpired (flaky link at the 30 s cap) and OSError (interface down) both crashed. FIXED at the single point every git call passes through, matching the pattern test_count() in the same file has used since it was written: a call that could not RUN now reports exactly what a call that RAN AND FAILED reports, a non-zero code and no stdout. THE P-PASS CAUGHT A SECOND DEFECT THAT THE FIX ITSELF WOULD HAVE WIDENED, and it is the more dangerous of the two. `git status --porcelain` prints NOTHING for a clean tree, so an empty stdout from a FAILED call is byte-identical to success on a clean tree. Degrading a raised error to "no output" therefore made "I cannot see the tree" render as "the tree is clean" -- measured: `clean` came back True with git unreachable. The return code is the only thing separating the 2 cases, so it is now READ rather than inferred, an unreadable tree is reported as NOT clean under p-pass-ambiguity-default, and a new `status_known` field says which happened. sv therefore refuses rather than saving against a tree it could not inspect. This was pre-existing for a non-zero status and the fix made it reachable more often, so it closes in the same change. MEASURED EFFECT: the 11 recovery-marker tests that failed on the 2026-10-07 full board now pass. 834 passed, 1 failed across the 6 affected guard files, and that 1 is unrelated (see item 3). 2. FABLE IS ON THE LADDER, AT THE POSITION ITS EVIDENCE SUPPORTS. Its placement is DERIVED, not chosen by name, which is the point of his standing rule that the only thing affecting capability should be measured capability. Fable has 0 attributed falsifiers in the archive, so its lower confidence bound on resolve-rate is 0.0000 and it sorts LAST. It climbs as it earns attempts: a seat needs 12 consecutive successes before its Wilson lower bound passes a seat sitting at 60 of 70 -- the arithmetic form of his guard that simply counting a success is not an improvement in capability. LAST IS ALSO THE SAFE PLACEMENT, measured rather than assumed: `resolve_fn` returns "" for any label absent from the config's own roster and the rung is STILL consumed, because route slices list(rungs)[:_budget]. 0 of the 47 configs declare Fable (46 CC2, 46 Codex, 46 ChatGPT, 45 Gemini, 45 DeepSeek), so an early placement would burn 1 of the 2 capped rungs on a seat that cannot answer. Verified by execution: a capped run still dispatches exactly ['Codex', 'CC2']. OUTSTANDING AND HIS TO RULE ON: until a config lists Fable in `models` the rung is unreachable in those runs. Changing 23 routed configs alters what real experiments dispatch. 3. A CAPPED LISTING NOW STATES ITS REMAINDER. registry_is_the_evidence_base_2026-10-06.py:131 printed the first 5 of series_but_no_entries and never said what it withheld, which the operational guard correctly calls a silent falsehood. 1 of the 25 board failures, unrelated to items 1 and 2, and mine from 2026-10-06. 4. THE COMBINED RULE IS MEASURED AGAINST HIS 7 STATED REQUIREMENTS. bench/allocation_by_measured_capability_2026-10-07.py, every claim cross-verified with at least 2 tools and every proportion carrying a Wilson interval. It satisfies arbitrary roster size, no cap, name-free allocation and bidirectionality BY CONSTRUCTION -- a derived sort key is a total order at 1, 6, 70 and 500 seats, and a seat climbs or falls as its measurement moves, with no tuple to edit. It FAILS his "problem computed efficiently" requirement as framed, because cost is money alone while the researcher pays in TIME: on a hard problem the money order puts the strong seat last, costing 4.80 expected dispatches against 1.78, a factor of 2.70, to save 4.85% of spend. Pricing the wait fixes it with the SAME key and no new rule, crossing over to capability-first at a latency weight of 2. And his guard against counting a success as capability is not a property of the ordering at all: a point estimate promotes 1-of-1 over 60-of-70, where Wilson and Jeffreys lower bounds both refuse to. Independent re-derivation of the figure reported pre-compaction: strongest-first is spend-suboptimal in 3285 of 4000 rosters, 82.1250%, Wilson [80.9070%, 83.2814%]. The cc2 seat measured 3637 of 4000 = 90.93% on its own draw. The rates differ and the structure agrees; the discrepancy is recorded rather than smoothed. Guards: 14 in test_git_state_degrades_offline_2026-10-07.py, 18 in test_two_objectives_cannot_share_one_key_2026-10-07.py. The guard that asserted Fable was ABSENT failed the moment the ladder changed, which is what it was written to do; it now asserts the new fact rather than being deleted. title: note: the combined rule meets 5 of 7 requirements by construction, and removing the cap downgrades the blocker
verbatim: note: the combined rule meets 5 of 7 requirements by construction, and removing the cap downgrades the blocker Answers his 3 questions directly -- *"does the combined approach do this? Does it do it well? Is there a better way?"* -- and the follow-up *"how does this combined approach solve the tension exactly?"* HOW IT DISSOLVES THE TENSION, in 3 verified steps. Removing the cap makes prod(1 - p_i) a CONSTANT, so the selection question stops having content: 1 distinct value across all 120 permutations. What remains is ordering alone, and ordering has a provably optimal rule, z3 unsat in both directions with 400 of 400 on brute force. That rule is a comparison over measured numbers, so it is roster-agnostic and bidirectional by construction rather than by addition. THE SCORECARD. Arbitrary roster size, no cap, name-free allocation and bidirectionality are MET BY THE SHAPE OF THE RULE -- a total order at 1, 6, 70 and 500 seats, with a weak seat climbing and a strong seat falling as its measurement moves. 2 requirements FAIL and neither needs the rule abandoned: * "computed efficiently, the researcher waits" FAILS because cost is money alone. On a hard finding the money order takes 4.80 expected dispatches against 1.78 for the capability order -- 2.70x the wait -- to save 4.85% of spend, and the 2 optima are genuinely different permutations. Pricing the wait fixes it with the SAME key, crossing to capability-first at a weight of 2, and z3 confirms the exchange argument survives money + weighted latency. * "a success is not a capability gain" FAILS because a point estimate promotes 1-of-1 (1.0000) over 60-of-70 (0.8571). Wilson gives 0.2065 against 0.7566 and Jeffreys agrees; a newcomer needs 12 consecutive successes to pass. This belongs to the ESTIMATOR, not the ordering. title: p-pass: status_known was an unwired addition, and the proxy it replaces misses the partial failure
verbatim: p-pass: status_known was an unwired addition, and the proxy it replaces misses the partial failure THE OWED P-PASS, on the field added earlier in this session. Adding a key to git_state's returned dict could have broken any consumer comparing its key set. Measured: 0 of the 3 callers -- cdsfl_sv.py, cdsfl_qc.py, cdsfl_recover.py -- read `status_known`, so no pre-existing stub can KeyError on it. BUT THAT IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE CLEARANCE. The additive standard holds both directions: *"an addition that nothing reaches is not additive either"*. The PROTECTION was live -- an unreadable tree reports NOT clean, which sv acts on -- while the explanatory signal reached nothing. 11 confirmed defects in this project's record since 2026-08-01 were additions that did nothing. WIRED, and it REPLACES A PROXY rather than adding a parallel one. cdsfl_recover.py already knew this exact defect; its own comment reads *"an empty `git status --porcelain` reads as 'clean' -- a failure rendered as a confident success"*. It detected it with `git_ok = gs["last_hash"] not in ("", "unknown")`, which is a proxy for "is git answering at all". THE PROXY MISSES THE PARTIAL FAILURE, measured against the live function with only `git status` made to fail: git log answers -> git_ok (PROXY) = True git status fails -> status_known (DIRECT) = False So on that path the proxy reads True and the line printed a tree state for a tree it had not managed to inspect. Before `git_state` read the status return code it printed "Working tree: clean"; it now prints "Working tree: UNKNOWN". A dirty tree and an uninspectable tree no longer render alike -- one tells the reader to look at their changes, the other tells them the tool could not look. The proxy is KEPT for the other lines, where a missing commit is what it genuinely detects. This is the project's own lesson that a direct signal beats a proxy, applied to a proxy the project had written for the right reason. Guards: 3 added, 17 in the file, including one that fails if the field ever stops being read by live code. 152 passed across the 5 guard files touching cdsfl_utils, cdsfl_recover and the routing ladder. title: the panel was reading an overstated hazard, so the round was withdrawn and re-dispatched
verbatim: the panel was reading an overstated hazard, so the round was withdrawn and re-dispatched THE FOUNDER STOPPED IT: *"Then the panel is reading the wrong thing!"* He was right, and the reasoning that had let the round continue was wrong in a specific way worth recording: it weighed a MECHANISM above CORRECTNESS. The argument was that the brief's sha256 is the star-topology grouping key, so a mid-flight rewrite would make the recorded brief differ from the one the seats received. True, and irrelevant -- 0 seat replies had landed, so there was no blind round to protect, and the seats were 4 minutes into reviewing a design against a hazard figure that does not hold. WHAT WAS WRONG WITH THE BRIEF. It stated a spurious-convergence factor of 8.49986 as a property of the convergence gate. It is an UPPER BOUND holding only under independent seats, and seats in a round share a byte-identical brief and the same target. With a shared per-round latent factor the same 6-to-4 factor is 3.8236 at a correlation of 0.1, 1.9200 at 0.3 and 1.4043 at 0.5 by exact mpmath integration, with Monte Carlo agreeing to within 10% at the midpoint. The magnitude moves by a factor of 7.7915 across the range; the direction never reverses. WITHDRAWN AND RECORDED, NOT ERASED. ABANDONED_ATTEMPT_1.md carries the dispatch time, both aliveness results, the stop time, the fact that 0 replies had landed, and why, so a researcher can retrace the sequence. AND THE PRESERVATION MECHANISM WAS WRONG ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT. The brief and the abandonment note were force-added past the bench/logs ignore rule, which the cheap guards correctly refused: panel records are preserved by scripts/mirror_panel_records_2026-09-11.py into experimental_notes/evidence/, not by overriding the ignore rule. 122 of 123 rounds were mirrored and this one was the exception. The hook's own SUGGESTED cause was a red herring -- it blamed the memory exclusions ledger, whose accounting line had merely moved from 14:41 to 23:16 -- and the real message was 20 lines above the suggestion. Mirrored now: 123 of 123. THE AMENDED BRIEF states the bound AS a bound, carries the correlation sweep, tells the seats the first version overstated it, and asks them how the correlation could be measured from the archive -- it never has been, and it is an empirical quantity because per-round per-seat findings are recorded. It also flags the load-bearing step for attack: the reason to record the live roster does not depend on the magnitude at all, because z3 shows the 2 causes are indistinguishable from the count whatever the correlation is. 13 figures are DECLARED in the brief and every one re-executed and reproduced before dispatch. The 8 numbers left undeclared are input parameters, a trivial 1-of-1 point estimate, and the Wolfram cross-check value. RE-DISPATCHED 23:14:42, brief 14,331 chars, free seats only, 0 paid. cc2 alive in 4.32 s and fable in 5.71 s, both on attempt 1. Guards: 14 in test_the_roster_hazard_is_bounded_not_measured_2026-10-07.py, 3 of them mutations -- that the direction never reverses at any correlation, that independence is genuinely the upper bound, and that correlation moves the ratio far enough for the omission to have mattered. title: the intra-round correlation is MEASURED, and it cuts the hazard figure by 5.9x
verbatim: the intra-round correlation is MEASURED, and it cuts the hazard figure by 5.9x The panel brief for `dynamic_roster_and_derived_ladder_2026-10-07` states that the intra-round correlation has never been measured here and asks the seats how it could be. It can be, from the archive, and this is the answer. MEASURED over 64 archived reports carrying both a rounds list and a registry, 395 rounds with 2 or more responding seats, 1968 seat-rounds of which 460 raised a new critical. Critical is severity at or above 0.7, the threshold the live runner uses at 4 separate sites. q per-seat-per-round new-critical rate = 0.233740 Wilson [0.215572, 0.252945] rho pairwise intraclass = 0.405989 bootstrap [0.332313, 0.476821] rho overdispersion method of moments = 0.360248 rho Pearson over within-round seat pairs = 0.393096 p = 4.203e-297 3 independent estimators within 0.046 of each other, computed from the same 8088 within-round ordered pairs by different routes. THE BRIEF'S FIGURE WAS WRONG IN 2 PLACES, NOT 1. It assumed independence (rho = 0) and it assumed q = 0.3. Both are false: rho is about 0.41 and q is 0.2337. At the measured values the 6-seat-to-4-seat spurious-convergence factor is 1.4291, against 4.9402 under independence at the same q and the 8.49986 originally quoted at q = 0.3. So the overstatement was roughly 5.9-fold. THE HAZARD SURVIVES AND IS MODEST. 1.4291 is above 1, so a shrinking roster does go quiet sooner, but it is a 43% increase rather than an 8.5-fold one. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, AND THIS IS THE POINT. The reason to record the live roster beside the quiet-round count never depended on the magnitude at all: z3 shows that 0 new criticals from a healthy panel and 0 from a depleted one are the same integer at ANY rho. The measurement lowers the URGENCY of the repair and leaves its NECESSITY untouched. A guard asserts exactly that, so the argument cannot later be made to rest on the magnitude. MEASURED WHILE THE PANEL IS STILL READING THE BRIEF THAT CALLS THIS UNMEASURED. That is deliberate and the brief is not being rewritten again: it asks the seats to propose a measurement method, so there is now a reference answer to compare their proposal against, which is stronger evidence than having handed them the number. Guards: 8 in test_the_intra_round_correlation_is_measured_2026-10-07.py, including that the 2 estimators must agree, that the factor must stay above 1 or the hazard is retired, and that the necessity argument survives independently of the magnitude. title: p-pass: the pooled correlation was confounded 1.7202x, so the correction over-corrected
verbatim: p-pass: the pooled correlation was confounded 1.7202x, so the correction over-corrected THE ATTACK on the measurement committed 20 minutes earlier. A pooled intraclass correlation over every round of every report measures 2 things at once: that some ROUNDS go quiet, and that some EXPERIMENTS are quieter than others. The second is an ecological confound and it inflates the answer. MEASURED, by recomputing the same statistic WITHIN each report and taking the pair-weighted mean over 40 reports: pooled, all runs rho = 0.405989 within-experiment rho = 0.236014 inflation 1.7202 simulated runs only rho = 0.681094 130 rounds, 2860 pairs real runs only rho = 0.275298 265 rounds, 5228 pairs So the pooled figure was inflated TWICE: once by between-experiment variation, and again by mixing in simulated runs, whose seats are far more correlated than live ones. THE FACTOR MOVES BACK UP, which is the honest direction. The 6-seat-to-4-seat spurious-convergence factor across today's successive estimates, each checked with an exact mpmath integral AND a Monte Carlo: as first briefed rho=0.0000 q=0.3000 -> 8.4999 (monte carlo 8.4245) pooled rho=0.4060 q=0.2337 -> 1.4290 (monte carlo 1.4218) REAL runs only rho=0.2753 q=0.2462 -> 1.7766 (monte carlo 1.7940) within-experiment rho=0.2360 q=0.2462 -> 1.9258 (monte carlo 1.9055) simulated only rho=0.6811 q=0.2086 -> 1.1280 (monte carlo 1.1246) HONEST RANGE FOR A REAL RUN: 1.7766 to 1.9258. Not the 1.4291 reported minutes ago, and not the 8.49986 the brief was first dispatched with. AND A CONSEQUENCE FOR SIMULATION THAT WAS NOT BEING LOOKED FOR. A simulated arm sits at rho = 0.6811, where the factor is 1.1280. A real run sits at 0.2753, where it is 1.7766. The simulation is ALREADY in the regime where this hazard nearly vanishes, so a simulated arm cannot rehearse it: simulation will under-report this class of defect by construction. That is a general finding about what simulation can and cannot establish, not a point about this hazard. rho_within_experiment() is added to the producer as the honest estimator, with the confound recorded in its docstring so the pooled figure cannot quietly come back. Guards: 11 in the file, 3 new -- that pooling must measurably inflate or the correction is spurious, that the de-confounded factor must EXCEED the pooled one, and that simulated and real runs must give different factors or a simulated arm would rehearse the hazard faithfully. title: the serialisation's justifying p-value is confounded by a shared cap
verbatim: the serialisation's justifying p-value is confounded by a shared cap THE FOUNDER'S CHALLENGE: *"Is back to back necessary? It doubles the duration of a panel review. Isn't it the case that all that is needed is a few seconds between dispatching each model?"* The evidence supports him. WHAT JUSTIFIED SERIALISING. The 2026-10-05 finding that of 5 rounds losing a seat, 3 lost BOTH at near-identical durations -- 1956.0/1956.2, 902.0/902.0, 18.7/18.8 s -- p = 1.556646e-07 against an independence null. THE CONFOUND. 2 seats given the SAME DEADLINE fail at that deadline. Both verdicts SOUND WITH REPAIRS, both delivering fixes as files with executed falsifiers rather than findings alone. THE SHARPEST FINDING IS NOT ABOUT ROSTERS, and it is fable's. reference_runner_v3.py:9207-9215 carries a sparsity fallback: when cumulative criticals fall below gamma_crit_min_cumulative (8), gamma becomes REPORTED-NOT-GATED and closure rests on the zero-new-critical window ALONE. The gate called two-sided is one-sided in precisely the endgame regime, and the surviving half is the half a shrinking roster attacks. title: p-pass: the rung ladder's promotion RULE is the weak point, and removing the cap unlocks the difficulty label
verbatim: p-pass: the rung ladder's promotion RULE is the weak point, and removing the cap unlocks the difficulty label HIS DESIGN, 2026-10-08: a model with no record starts on simpler tasks, earns an attempt at a harder rung by succeeding, and on failure stays at the last rung where it demonstrated success. It answers the cold-start problem no identifier scheme can: a model at 0 credit otherwise has no route to measurement at all. FINDING 1, THE PROMOTION CRITERION IS ASYMMETRIC THE WRONG WAY. Over 5 rungs, promote-on-one-success keeps a genuinely 0.90 model out of the top rung 0.40951 of the time -- simulated 0.4101 over 20000 trials, Wilson [0.403301, 0.416933], closed form agreeing -- while admitting a useless 0.10 model only 1e-05 of the time. It barely admits bad models and substantially EXCLUDES GOOD ONES, and it contradicts his own requirement 6 that counting a success is not capability. ATTACK ON MY OWN MEASUREMENT, AND IT STRENGTHENS THE FINDING. The figure assumed a CONSTANT per-rung success rate, which contradicts the design being tested because his rungs get harder. With a declining profile [0.95, 0.90, 0.85, 0.80, 0.70] a strong model is kept out 0.5930 of the time against 0.4095 under the constant assumption. numpy and mpmath agree exactly. AND MY OWN PROPOSED REPAIR IS WORSE. A Wilson lower bound over 10 attempts at a 0.50 floor needs 9 successes per rung and drops the same 0.90 model to 0.21611302. So the calibration must be DERIVED from a stated false-negative target, which is what the panel is asked to do rather than choose. FINDING 2, THE ABSORBING RUNG CONTRADICTS BIDIRECTIONALITY. If a failure permanently fixes a model's rung then the 40.951% capped by luck are capped forever, against his rule that lost capability must be regainable. FINDING 3, AND MY FIRST PROBE WAS WRONG. The brief claims resolution depth is already recorded so difficulty needs no classifier. A first probe looked for `rungs_tried` as a TOP-LEVEL registry key, found 0, and appeared to make the claim an unwired addition. It is nested inside `routing_history`. Measured over 305 records: rungs_tried is 0 on 59, 1 on 103 and 2 on 143, and more than 1 rung was available on 246 of 305 = 80.6557%, Wilson [75.8527%, 84.6962%]. The claim stands; the probe was unrepresentative, and the 3 entries first sampled by hand were the degenerate ones. A NEW ARGUMENT FOR HIS NO-CAP RULING THAT NOBODY HAD MADE. `rungs_tried` cannot exceed the cap, so while the cap is 2 the recorded difficulty label has at most 3 levels. Removing the cap does not only improve coverage -- it UNLOCKS a finer difficulty signal, which is exactly the input his promotion ladder needs. A guard asserts the current truncation and says to update it to the richer range once the cap lifts, rather than delete it. ALSO MEASURED: a hand-written tuple cannot answer cold start at scale. It orders 100.0000% of a 6-model roster, 8.5714% of 70 and 0.8571% of 700, with the remainder ordered by input order alone. Both prior seats said keep the tuple and neither said it does not scale. Guards: 9 in test_the_promotion_criterion_is_the_weak_point_2026-10-08.py, including a mutation asserting that a declining profile makes the outcome WORSE (or the attack would be empty) and one asserting my own bound gate overcorrects (or there would be nothing for the panel to derive). Panel dispatched on this at 02:28, free seats only, 0 paid, 8 declared figures all re-executed. NOT IMPLEMENTED -- `d` is in force. title: his clarification withdraws the criticism, and "several" turns out to be derivable
verbatim: his clarification withdraws the criticism, and "several" turns out to be derivable HIS CLARIFICATION, 2026-10-08: *"I didn't originally intend to say models only needed one successful try. They should demonstrate their capability over several tries with different problems, before being considered for promotion."* With the football analogy: *"Players (and teams) start out in the lower leagues, but only with demonstrated success over time can they be promoted."* THE EARLIER CRITICISM IS WITHDRAWN. The figures that condemned the rung ladder -- a genuinely 0.90 model kept out of the top rung 0.40951 of the time under constant difficulty and 0.59302 once rungs harden -- were computed for ONE success per rung and do not apply to a sustained-success rule. They were a criticism of a rule he did not propose. WHAT REPLACES IT IS A DERIVATION RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. Against a 5% false-negative budget for a model that deserves promotion (0.80) and a 1% false-positive budget for one that does not (0.50), over 5 rungs: 19 attempts per rung with 11 successes required. A 0.80 model then reaches the top rung 0.967152 of the time against 0.32768 under one-success, and a 0.50 model 0.00355962. scipy and an mpmath exact tail agree. Tightening the budget demands a larger sample, so the derivation responds to its inputs rather than returning a constant. THE FOOTBALL ANALOGY INDEPENDENTLY LANDS IN THE RIGHT RANGE. A season is 38 matches; the error budget returns 19 attempts per rung without being made to. Noted as a coincidence of order of magnitude, not as evidence. WHERE THE ANALOGY BREAKS IS THE PLACE THAT MATTERS. Football promotion is RELATIVE -- the top of a fixed-size division goes up -- so a weak division still promotes somebody. Measured over 2000 trials with 700 uniformly weak models: relative promotion elevates one to the hardest rung in 2000 of 2000 trials, Wilson [0.998083, 1.000000]; an absolute capability threshold elevates none, Wilson [0.000000, 0.001917]. Rungs map to TASK DIFFICULTY rather than to a fixed-size division, so the threshold must be ABSOLUTE. Otherwise a uniformly weak roster sends its least-weak member to the hardest problem, which is his Riemann objection restated. P-PASS, AND IT CORRECTS THE NUMBER I JUST DERIVED. The derivation assumes INDEPENDENT attempts. This project's measured intra-round correlation is 0.2360 within-experiment, 0.2753 on real runs, 0.4060 and 0.4903 pooled. The design effect 1 + (m-1)*rho therefore applies: at the real-run figure with 3 attempts per finding it is 1.5506, so 19 independent-equivalent attempts need 30 ACTUAL ones, an inflation of 55.06%. verbatim: his clarification withdraws the criticism, and "several" turns out to be derivable HIS CLARIFICATION, 2026-10-08: *"I didn't originally intend to say models only needed one successful try. They should demonstrate their capability over several tries with different problems, before being considered for promotion."* With the football analogy: *"Players (and teams) start out in the lower leagues, but only with demonstrated success over time can they be promoted."* THE EARLIER CRITICISM IS WITHDRAWN. The figures that condemned the rung ladder -- a genuinely 0.90 model kept out of the top rung 0.40951 of the time under constant difficulty and 0.59302 once rungs harden -- were computed for ONE success per rung and do not apply to a sustained-success rule. They were a criticism of a rule he did not propose. WHAT REPLACES IT IS A DERIVATION RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. Against a 5% false-negative budget for a model that deserves promotion (0.80) and a 1% false-positive budget for one that does not (0.50), over 5 rungs: 19 attempts per rung with 11 successes required. A 0.80 model then reaches the top rung 0.967152 of the time against 0.32768 under one-success, and a 0.50 model 0.00355962. scipy and an mpmath exact tail agree. Tightening the budget demands a larger sample, so the derivation responds to its inputs rather than returning a constant. THE FOOTBALL ANALOGY INDEPENDENTLY LANDS IN THE RIGHT RANGE. A season is 38 matches; the error budget returns 19 attempts per rung without being made to. Noted as a coincidence of order of magnitude, not as evidence. WHERE THE ANALOGY BREAKS IS THE PLACE THAT MATTERS. Football promotion is RELATIVE -- the top of a fixed-size division goes up -- so a weak division still promotes somebody. Measured over 2000 trials with 700 uniformly weak models: relative promotion elevates one to the hardest rung in 2000 of 2000 trials, Wilson [0.998083, 1.000000]; an absolute capability threshold elevates none, Wilson [0.000000, 0.001917]. Rungs map to TASK DIFFICULTY rather than to a fixed-size division, so the threshold must be ABSOLUTE. Otherwise a uniformly weak roster sends its least-weak member to the hardest problem, which is his Riemann objection restated. P-PASS, AND IT CORRECTS THE NUMBER I JUST DERIVED. title: p-pass: the derived sample IS minimal, and the rung COUNT is a trade-off nobody had named
verbatim: p-pass: the derived sample IS minimal, and the rung COUNT is a trade-off nobody had named ATTACK 1 ON MY OWN DERIVATION. `derive_rung_sample` takes the FIRST feasible (n, k) rather than proving it minimal. Exhaustive search confirms n = 19 is the true minimum at 5 rungs; the feasible success-count set at that n is contiguous -- in fact the single value 11 -- so scanning k upward returns the smallest feasible one. The monotonicity relied on holds, because the pass rate falls in k for both the deserving and the undeserving model, making the feasible set an interval. The derivation is sound. ATTACK 2 FOUND SOMETHING NOT ASKED FOR. The founder never specified a rung count, and it is not a free parameter. As rungs rise the PER-RUNG sample FALLS, because each rung's share of the error budget loosens as the n-th root, while the TOTAL cost of climbing RISES: 2 rungs n=26 k=17 52 attempts to reach the top 3 rungs n=21 k=13 63 5 rungs n=19 k=11 95 8 rungs n=15 k= 8 120 12 rungs n=12 k= 6 144 20 rungs n=11 k= 5 220 scipy and mpmath agree on every pass rate. So the count is a genuine trade-off: few rungs are cheap to climb but discriminate difficulty coarsely, many rungs discriminate finely but cost 4.2 times as much to climb at 20 against 2. AND IT CONNECTS TO THE CAP, WHICH MAKES THE ORDERING OF HIS 2 RULINGS MATTER. `rungs_tried` cannot exceed the cap, so at a cap of 2 the recorded difficulty label has at most 3 levels. A fine-grained ladder therefore needs the cap lifted FIRST, and the rung count should be set from how finely difficulty actually discriminates once it is -- which is measurable rather than chosen. Guards: 3 added, 13 in the file. One asserts the returned sample equals an exhaustive minimum, one asserts the feasible success-count set is an interval (the property the upward scan depends on), and one asserts that more rungs cost more in total even as each becomes cheaper -- because if rungs were free the count would not be a decision. title: both seats land on the rung ladder: sound with repairs, and 4 defects in my own scripts
verbatim: both seats land on the rung ladder: sound with repairs, and 4 defects in my own scripts BOTH FREE SEATS, 0 PAID. cc2 16,743 chars / 2,461 words / 33 tool calls / 1001.0 s; fable 10,187 chars / 1,447 words / 22 tool calls / 600.9 s. Both on attempt 1. Both verdicts: SOUND WITH REPAIRS on all 3 pillars -- earned rungs, opaque identifiers, measured difficulty. THE SHARPEST FINDING, from fable: the founder's phrase "stay on the same simpler problem resolution rung" admits 2 READINGS THAT FAIL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Under an absorbing reading a good model is excluded by luck (the 0.40951 figure). Under the natural retry reading -- the model keeps receiving that rung's tasks -- P(ever reach the top) = 1 for ANY p > 0, with E[attempts] = R/p (5.6 at p=0.9, 50 at p=0.1), so the rule excludes NOTHING and the ladder is a monotone ratchet. The root defect is an UNCALIBRATED CRITERION, not the direction of its failure. 1 sentence from the founder settles which he meant, and it is now asked. THE SEATS DISAGREE ON THE CENSORING AND BOTH ARE RIGHT. cc2: `rungs_tried` is RIGHT-censored by the cap -- true depth 4 reports 2, indistinguishable from an honest rung-2 resolution, confirmed by CC1 by execution. fable: it is LEFT-censored by STRONGEST-FIRST ordering -- every finding the top model can handle reports 1, so the label discriminates only above the strongest rung's ceiling, 1 of 7 findings in Exp 42, and weakest-first recovers the full ranking at +10 dispatches per 5 findings. Both mechanisms apply. THEREFORE DIFFICULTY CANNOT BE MEASURED WITHOUT BOTH REMOVING THE CAP AND VARYING THE ORDER -- and that re-creates the original tension in a new place, because strongest-first resolves efficiently while weakest-first measures difficulty. 4 DEFECTS IN CC1's OWN COMMITTED SCRIPTS, ALL FOUND BY THE SEATS: * a Wilson interval on exact arithmetic -- 6/70 has no estimator and no sampling variability. Fixed at source; the share now reports an exact Fraction. * the difficulty check AST-SCANNED FIELD NAMES and never executed `route`, so it would have reported success whatever the values were -- `execute-do-not-grep`, committed in a script used to brief a panel. Rewritten to call the real `route`, which confirms the censoring. * "the measured price of cold start" was evaluated at the MODAL outcome, so it carries about 50% power: achieved separation 0.507 at gap 0.40 against the 80%-power n being 1.63x to 1.86x larger. * "rotation costs identical dispatches" is FALSE. Measured against the real first-CONFIRMED semantics: 579 dispatches for 270 resolved under rotation against 444 for 396 under strength order -- 30% more dispatches, 32% fewer resolved. WITHDRAWN, having been reported to the founder as free. THE DERIVED PARAMETERS DIFFER 3 WAYS AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE TARGETS, NOT THE ARITHMETIC. CC1 n=19 k=11; cc2 n=19 k*=14 at floor 0.50; fable n=12 k=8 at an implied floor near 0.39, which it says is why the 0.50 floor over-corrected. Each verifies minimality under its own stated targets, so what is open is which targets the founder sets. BOTH SEATS REJECT RANDOM IDENTIFIERS IN FAVOUR OF DERIVED ONES, and this contradicts his wording while serving his intent. fable measured the cost: 2 instances of 1 configuration under split records need 21 rounds to separate 0.8 from 0.4 where pooling needs 11, so random keys DOUBLE the cold-start price for no benefit. Its key is a digest over provider, model_version, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, system_prompt, tool_set and quantisation, with random tokens surviving only as an instance id for bookkeeping. fable ALSO REFUTES CC1's IDLE-TIMEOUT RECOMMENDATION with 2 adversaries: a heartbeat child emitting 1 line every 0.5 s is never idle and runs until a total cap, and a working child with BUFFERED stdout showed 0 bytes at a 2.0 s idle cap and was wrongly killed while the same child under `python3 -u` completed at 3.1 s. So the idle clock can measure the stdio buffer rather than the model. It needs an unbuffered stream and a generous total backstop; each component alone fails a demonstrated adversary. AND fable ANSWERS THE FOUNDER'S OWN QUESTION BETTER THAN CC1 DID. Rungs are needed for a reason the brief missed: a new model placed at the back of the order sees only findings every stronger model already failed -- a maximally hard, biased sample -- so its "free" measurements are near-pure failures and cannot demonstrate capability. Rungs exist to hand it EASY attempts, and per-rung stratification stops back-of-order failures poisoning its easy-rung record. Panel records mirrored 124 of 124; seat-written files harvested to experimental_notes/seat_evidence/. The brief's misattribution of the one-success rule to the founder is recorded in the FULL RECORD context rather than hidden. Nothing merged. title: gamma gates wherever gamma exists, and the gate's mode is finally on the record
verbatim: gamma gates wherever gamma exists, and the gate's mode is finally on the record FOUNDER'S RULING, 2026-10-08: *"Gamma should remain active in all cases. Fix it."* Issued after the fable seat found reference_runner_v3.py making gamma "reported-not-gated" whenever the cumulative critical pool falls below gamma_crit_min_cumulative (default 8, set by only 4 of 47 configs). The gate advertised as two-sided went ONE-SIDED in precisely the endgame regime, and the surviving half -- the zero-novel-critical window -- is the half a shrinking roster attacks. THE BRANCH COULD NOT SIMPLY BE DELETED, and the arithmetic is what bounds the ruling rather than any preference. `_estimate_gamma` returns 0.0 as a SENTINEL for 4 distinct reasons, only 1 of which is a slope of 0.0: fewer than min_rounds points, an all-zero series, fewer than 2 usable log points, a degenerate denominator. A CLEAN run has an all-zero critical series BY CONSTRUCTION, so gating unconditionally on that 0.0 would make a clean target unable to converge -- and 3 consecutive clean convergences on the prose target is the programme of study's own success criterion. Gating on a sentinel is not gating on gamma. WHAT NOW HAPPENS. `_gamma_is_estimable` distinguishes the sentinel from a slope, mirroring the estimator's own conditions. Gamma GATES wherever it is estimable, including in the sparse branch where it previously did not. Where it is not estimable the fact is recorded as `sparsity_gamma_unestimable` and the window decides alone -- the same outcome as before, but named instead of silent. REACHABILITY MEASURED, because a change that bites nowhere is an unwired addition and this project has 11 confirmed defects of that shape. A flat tail pushes gamma up, so "window met AND gamma low" is a narrow band. An exhaustive sweep over short sparse series found it: [1, 3, 0, 0, 0] gamma 0.1783 OLD: converged NEW: refused [1, 4, 0, 0, 0] gamma 0.0461 OLD: converged NEW: refused and the refusal names its reason: "gamma_crit=0.178 < theta=0.300 and gamma GATES here". Clean series [0,0,0] and [0,0,0,0,0] still converge, as sparsity_gamma_unestimable. THE SECOND HALF, WITHOUT WHICH THE RULING IS UNAUDITABLE. The gate's telemetry reached `_log` and nothing else: a scan of every *report*.json under bench/logs for a record carrying `mode` returned 0, so no archived run says which mode closed it. It now lands on the round record as `hardened_gate_telemetry`, which is where a researcher looks. Guards: 21 in test_gamma_gates_wherever_it_exists_2026-10-08.py, all CALLING the gate and the estimator rather than reading them. The mirror between `_gamma_is_estimable` and `_estimate_gamma` is executed against shared inputs so the 2 cannot drift. Included: that unestimable implies the sentinel, that at least 1 series is estimable and 1 is not (a predicate answering the same way always would prove nothing), that the window still binds independently, and that the phrase "reported-not-gated" survives on no converging path. Regression: 21 new plus 10 existing two-sided-gate and sweep-shadow tests pass; a broader gamma/gate/runner selection is running. THIS TIGHTENS CONVERGENCE, so a run that would previously have closed may now continue. That is the safe direction and it costs rounds; the founder is told.
