title: he was right: "unestimable" was the demotion renamed, so the proven guarded vacuity is imported
verbatim: he was right: "unestimable" was the demotion renamed, so the proven guarded vacuity is imported HIS CHALLENGE, 2026-10-08: *"if gamma remains unestimable, how can gamma ever hit the 0.30 mark that has traditionally been set for it? Isn't this gamma demotion by another name?"* HE WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE BRANCH I DID NOT CHANGE. Where gamma was declared unestimable it did not gate, and renaming the state while leaving the behaviour alone is a relabelling. The earlier commit tightened the OTHER branch -- an estimable gamma below theta now blocks -- and left this one as it was. AND 0.0 FOR AN ALL-ZERO SERIES IS NOT A SENTINEL, IT IS THE WRONG ANSWER. Measured against the estimator: [1,0,0,0,0] gives 1.0000, [5,0,0,0,0] gives 1.0000, [2,1,0,0,0] gives 0.7597 -- a flat cumulative curve is MAXIMAL diminishing returns and the estimator knows it. For flat-at-ZERO it returns 0.0000, the FLOOR, the same value it gives [1,2,3,4,5] which is still climbing steeply. It bails because log(0) is undefined, not because the slope is low. THE ANSWER ALREADY EXISTED AND IS IMPORTED RATHER THAN RE-INVENTED. The sibling gate `_check_gamma_alt_convergence` handles this as VACUOUS CURVE, and test_vacuous_gamma_curve.py states the principle in its own words: *"GAMMA REMAINS AN ACTIVE, LOAD-BEARING CONVERGENCE CONDITION. Nothing here demotes it. What is narrowed is the ESTIMATOR'S DOMAIN."* It carries 2 guards, both now mirrored into the hardened gate: * cumulative critical over the WHOLE history must be zero, so a CONSTANT-RATE series -- the worst case, which drives the estimator to the same ~0.0 for the opposite reason -- has a positive cumulative count and stays blocked; * the panel must have produced findings of SOME severity, so "nothing was critical" is distinguishable from "nothing came back". That path REFUSES. `total_findings` is derived from the registry the gate already receives, so no signature change was needed. SO THERE IS NO CASE LEFT WHERE GAMMA IS EXCUSED WITHOUT A GUARD. Verified by executing every path: clean target, 18 findings -> CONVERGED vacuous_curve_converged dead panel, 0 findings -> REFUSED vacuous_curve_refused_dead_panel clean but window unmet -> REFUSED vacuous_curve_window_unmet sparse, gamma estimable and low -> REFUSED sparsity_gamma_gated sparse, gamma estimable and high -> CONVERGED sparsity_gamma_gated constant rate [2,2,2,2,2,2] -> REFUSED never reaches the vacuous path The converging vacuous reason carries "UNDEFINED rather than low" and "REVIEW THIS RUN: a clean target and a broken severity classifier look alike from here", so the residual ambiguity is stated rather than hidden. A TEST I WROTE AN HOUR EARLIER WAS WRONG, NOT THE GATE. It passed `_Reg([0,0,0,0])` with no non-critical findings, which builds an EMPTY registry -- so it modelled a DEAD PANEL and called it a clean target, and the new guard refused it. Rewritten to supply 18 findings of some severity, which is what a clean target actually means, plus a new test asserting the dead-panel case is refused. 81 passed across the hardened gate, the new guard, the vacuous-curve guard, the two-sided gate and gamma-alt convergence. title: morning report: gamma gates everywhere, and 6 figures I carried to a panel were wrong
verbatim: morning report: gamma gates everywhere, and 6 figures I carried to a panel were wrong OVERNIGHT: 3 free panel rounds, 0 paid, both seats landing in each. 11 commits on sim/shakedown-2026-09-29; main untouched. THE HEADLINE. Gamma now gates in every case where a decay curve exists, and where no curve exists the 2 proven guards from the sibling gate apply, one of which REFUSES convergence. It took 3 attempts and 2 corrections from the founder, and the final form is the one he forced rather than the one first offered -- his second rejection, that "unestimable" was the demotion renamed, was correct. THE 6 WRONG FIGURES, each found by a seat rather than by me, listed in full because he decides what matters: 1. q assumed 0.3; measured 0.233740, rejected at p = 5.6e-11 (cc2). A second seat measured 0.1994 on a wider population. 2. a spurious-convergence factor of 8.49986 stated as a property of the gate when it is an upper bound under independence; operative figure near 1.4, with one comparison overstated 29.1-fold. 3. a sensitivity span of 7.7915 described as plausible; it spans rho 0 to 0.8, and over the 0.1 to 0.5 range actually quoted the value is 6.053 (fable). 4. a confidence interval on exact arithmetic -- 6 of 70 is 3/35 (cc2), whose phrasing is kept: an interval on a quantity with no estimator is nobody's uncertainty. 5. a difficulty check that AST-scanned field names and never executed the function it claimed to verify (cc2); rewritten to call the real route, which then confirmed the censoring it was meant to detect. 6. "rotation costs identical dispatches" -- measured 579 dispatches for 270 resolved against 444 for 396, so 30% more dispatches and 32% fewer resolved (cc2). Reported to the founder as free; WITHDRAWN. A 7TH CORRECTION IS HIS, NOT A SEAT'S. My criticism of his rung ladder rested on an absorbing rule he never described. Under his actual reading capability sets the RATE of climb -- 5.56 expected attempts at 0.90 against 50.00 at 0.10 -- and a bounded horizon turns that rate into selection with no threshold: 0.9998 against 0.0016 at 10 attempts per rung, a factor of 625. CARRIED TO HIM FOR RULING: the promotion-gate parameters, where 3 derivations give 19/11, 19/14 and 12/8 and the difference is the targets rather than the arithmetic, all 3 assuming independent attempts where the measured correlation inflates 19 to about 30; the tier count, which is not monotone (4 tiers 68 attempts, 5 cost 95, 7 cost 91, 11 cost 132, 20 cost 220) so his 4-division instinct lands on a local optimum; whether the gate should READ the live roster or merely record it; and the 5 rulings from yesterday not yet built, including the stagger, which cost 2505.6 s -- 41.76 minutes, a 46.15% increase in wall clock -- across last night's 3 rounds on evidence recomputing to p = 0.107550. PLUS A MECHANISM CORRECTION: the idle timeout I recommended as strictly better was refuted by fable with 2 adversaries -- a heartbeat process is never idle, and a working process with buffered output showed 0 bytes and was wrongly killed. It needs an unbuffered stream and a total backstop. A 4TH PANEL was dispatched at 04:32 on the gamma fix itself, both seats alive on attempt 1, 0 paid, asking the seats to find any path where gamma is excused without a guard. Its result is not in this report. Artefact pair: experimental_notes/Morning_Report_2026-10-08.md and ~/Desktop/CDSFL_tts/Morning_Report_2026-10-08.txt, 67 lines, both 0 lint findings, the TTS carrying 0 markdown markers. Producer for the gamma figures committed as bench/gamma_sentinel_versus_slope_2026-10-08.py so each travels with its script. verbatim: p-pass: the hand-maintained mirror holds over a sweep, not over the 10 inputs I first tested `_gamma_is_estimable` restates `_estimate_gamma`'s early-return conditions BY HAND, and the predicate decides whether gamma GATES -- so a disagreement is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. A false "unestimable" demotes gamma, which is the defect the founder ruled against; a false "estimable" compares a sentinel against the 0.30 arm. The first version of the guard tested 10 inputs, which is not a sweep. The panel brief dispatched on this fix asks the seats to widen it. Doing it here rather than outsourcing the check on my own code. MEASURED, both directions: * EXHAUSTIVE over all 5461 series of length 0 to 6 with values 0 to 3: 0 cases called unestimable that yield a slope, and 0 cases called estimable where the estimator would take an early return. * RANDOM over 200000 series of length 0 to 39 with values 0 to 59: 0 disagreements, rate 0.00000000, Wilson [0.00000000, 0.00001921]. Guards: 5 added, 30 in the file. One of them asserts the sweep OBSERVES BOTH ANSWERS, because a sweep that only ever saw `True` could not detect a one-sided predicate and would pass vacuously. title: both seats found the same 2 critical defects in my gamma fix, and all 4 are now repaired
verbatim: both seats found the same 2 critical defects in my gamma fix, and all 4 are now repaired BOTH FREE SEATS, 0 PAID. cc2 14,244 chars / 2,110 words / 64 tool calls / 1427.2 s; fable 11,575 chars / 1,668 words / 49 tool calls / 833.6 s. Both on attempt 1. All 52 committed guards passed unmodified under both. VERDICTS. cc2: "sound in its central claim, unsound as shipped -- needs repairs, not reversion". fable: "sound with repairs". They converged INDEPENDENTLY on the same 2 critical defects. F1, BOTH SEATS, CRITICAL, NOW FIXED. The fix imported the sibling gate's 2 vacuity guards and LEFT BEHIND THE 2 BLOCKS THAT STAND IN FRONT OF THEM -- the A4 unverified-critical fail-safe and the contested block -- so the 2 gates returned OPPOSITE verdicts on identical registries. The direction is unsafe: UNCONFIRMED is an unresolved status the novelty filter strips from the settled series, so an unverified critical drives `cum_crit` DOWN and pushes the run INTO the vacuous branch. `unverified_critical_count`'s own docstring forbids exactly that. cc2 demonstrated 6 untested claims converging where the sibling refused with "A4 BLOCK", and measured that A4 alone would NOT close the gap, so both blocks are needed -- a measurement, per the composability rule. fable traced the chain to the boundary and found no intervening recheck once convergence is promoted. Archive exposure 0 of 69 runs, scanned independently by both: a FORWARD hazard, not a retroactive miscount. FIXED BY DERIVING BOTH IN-GATE, which is fable's correction of its OWN first repair: it first added them as parameters defaulting to 0, and its own falsifier caught that a caller can omit them and reopen the hole. In-gate is the form no caller can forget, and it reuses the registry methods the sibling's call site already uses so there is no second derivation to drift. A narrow stub without those readers falls back rather than crashing, which keeps the 8 existing stubs honest. F2, BOTH SEATS, CRITICAL, FIXED BEFORE fable's REPLY LANDED. The full branch's leave-one-round-out loop gated on the 0.0 SENTINEL. Dropping the only non-zero round of a single-burst series leaves an all-zero subseries, the estimator returns its sentinel, and a maximal-depletion run -- gamma 1.0000, window met -- was PERMANENTLY refused at any horizon. That contradicted the fix's own stated principle in the branch beside the one it repaired. fable measured archive exposure at 6 of 69 runs with that shape: exp38_ouroboros, exp39_0_gate, exp42_composer and 2 sim45_canary. F3, fable, LOW, FIXED. With `cum_crit` positive but gamma unestimable, the refusal text asserted a slope that is a sentinel. The verdict cannot flip, but the record claimed a measurement it does not have. F4, fable, LOW, FIXED. 2 stale docstrings: 1 described the mode name of the REJECTED first version, which appears nowhere in the code, and 1 still stated the removed "reported-not-gated" contract. Its phrasing is kept verbatim in the correction because it names a failure this project has recorded twice: a stale guarantee in a docstring is how a rejected position acquires authority here. VERIFIED CLEAN BY BOTH SEATS, far harder than I had. The hand-maintained mirror: 0 failures over 1,195,703 series (cc2) and 21,845 exhaustive series (fable). Both DERIVED that the omitted degenerate-denominator condition needs of order a million rounds to bite, against max_rounds=21. The constant-rate lookalike never reaches the vacuous path. Telemetry persistence wired. ALSO IN THIS COMMIT: the ladder-depth default is now EXHAUST. `routing.DEFAULT_MAX_RUNGS = 0`, referenced by both signatures and the call site, because FOLLOW found the runner OMITS the keyword at the default to protect 8 narrow stubs -- so flipping only the config default would have broken all 8 -- and a first attempt read the default via `inspect.signature(route)`, which raises KeyError under exactly those stubs. Measured: 143 of 305 archived routing records hit the cap and 103 were ABANDONED UNRESOLVED; per-rung resolve rates 0.3902 then 0.2797 mean 4 further rungs recover roughly 46 to 75 of them for about 209 extra dispatches. The rate beyond depth 2 has never been measured BECAUSE the cap prevented it. 133 tests pass across 9 affected guard files. FULL RECORD at experimental_notes/Panel_FULL_RECORD_Gamma_Gates_2026-10-08.md, both replies unfiltered. Panel records mirrored 125 of 125. title: the round-3 panel analysis he asked for under `d` and did not receive
verbatim: the round-3 panel analysis he asked for under `d` and did not receive HE ASKED: *"But where is your analysis of the panel results I asked for previously under 'd'?"* Verified rather than claimed: all 4 rounds of this arc have a FULL RECORD, and only round 2 had a synthesis note. Rounds 3 and 4 had none. WHAT THE ROUND SETTLED. Both seats returned SOUND WITH REPAIRS on all 3 pillars. They agreed independently that the missing third seat state is a CIRCUIT BREAKER -- already this project's own vocabulary, in CDSFL_UX_Vision_Sketch_2026-03-28.md -- that a degraded run should converge but never silently on a raised window, that the hand-written tuple stays as the cold-start tie-break because at run 1 every lower bound is 0.0 and the derived key is a total tie (12 shuffled inputs gave 12 orders without it and 1 with it), that holding an expensive seat in reserve is emergent rather than classified (reached on 3.61% of findings; reach probability 0.0287), and that adding a model is 1 config edit. 3 DISAGREEMENTS ARE PRESERVED RATHER THAN RESOLVED, which is the round's real output. On whether cost can be a scalar, both seats are RIGHT about different questions -- feasibility against order -- and the composition is the finding. On the censoring of recorded depth, 1 seat finds it right-censored by the cap and the other LEFT-censored by strongest-first ordering, and together they imply something NEITHER stated: difficulty cannot be measured without both removing the cap AND varying the order, which re-creates the original try-order tension in a new place. On the promotion sample, 3 derivations give 19/11, 19/14 and 12/8, so the difference is the TARGETS not the arithmetic. THE CORRECTION THAT INVERTS THE BRIEF'S OWN CRITICISM. The 40.951% figure holds only under an absorbing reading the founder never stated; under his actual reading the rule excludes NOTHING. Both framings fail, and his own answer resolves both: capability sets the RATE of climb (5.56 expected attempts at 0.90 against 50.00 at 0.10) and a bounded horizon turns that into selection with no threshold -- 0.9998 against 0.0016 at 10 attempts per rung. AND A BETTER ANSWER TO HIS COLD-START QUESTION THAN CC1 GAVE: a new model at the back of the order sees ONLY findings every stronger model already failed -- a maximally hard, biased sample -- so its free measurements are near-pure failures and cannot demonstrate capability. Rungs exist to hand it EASY attempts. THE INSTRUCTED ITEM THAT LAPSED IS RECORDED, NOT GLOSSED. He asked TWICE for the round to be re-run with his fresh framing and it was never dispatched; it was displaced by the gamma repair he also authorised, and the displacement was not flagged at the time, which is the failure rather than the delay. Whether it is still worth running is answered honestly: 3 of its items have since been settled by other means, and what NO seat has seen is his finite-divisions insight -- the tier count is bounded, the climb costs between 52 and 182 attempts across 2 to 14 tiers, and the curve is NOT monotone (7 tiers cost 91 where 5 cost 95), so it must be scanned. That is the narrow form the re-run should take. title: both seats refuted me, randomisation settles monotonicity, and 4 launch deficiencies are fixed
verbatim: both seats refuted me, randomisation settles monotonicity, and 4 launch deficiencies are fixed HIS INSTRUCTION: *"Just look at Fable's reply then start the review again from scratch and do it properly ... And fix the deficiencies you identified in launching the panel reviews properly. These need to be carried over to paid panel reviews too."* Both halves done, and the round refuted me twice more. **THE STAR-TOPOLOGY DEFICIENCY HE FOUND, MEASURED.** Of 99 archived rounds collecting 2 or more replies, **15 have a joint round** -- 0.151515, Wilson [0.094023, 0.235041]. Since his 2026-10-06 ruling that the topology be unskippable, **1 of 5**, and the 4 unpaired rounds were all mine and all reported to him as star topology. The guard built for that ruling could not see it: it refuses a round whose SIBLING holds a landed reply, so a LONE blind round with no joint round passes trivially. And the declaration left no trace, because `PANEL_BLIND_OF`/`PANEL_JOINT_OF` are environment variables. Both fixed: `topology.json` is written BEFORE dispatch, and a new blind round is REFUSED while an earlier one owes its joint half -- with the owed set **DERIVED FROM THE ARCHIVE**, because a hand-kept list has the identical weakness to the thing it replaces and forgetting is the failure being fixed. The debt binds from the ruling date; derived over the whole archive it returns 80 rounds back to August, and a control that guarantees its own override is worse than none. **AND A SECOND DEFICIENCY NOBODY HAD NAMED, proven by execution.** `blind_of` names OTHER rounds, so the first dispatch of a 2-seat blind round cannot know a co-seat will land mid-run -- and `fresh_sandbox_for_attempt` clones the LIVE tree at retry time. It happened for real: a cc2 retry sandbox held fable's whole 12,299-char reply. Naming the round in `blind_of` was no use, measured -- it removes the whole directory, `BRIEF.md` included. `build(own_round=...)` now purges the round's own seat artefacts and keeps only the brief. **MY FIRST VERSION OF THAT FIX REPORTED SUCCESS WHILE THE REPLY SAT THERE**: the round name is in the DIRECTORY name, so `rglob("*name*")` matched the directory and my survivor check discarded directories as "not evidence" and returned empty. Caught by listing files instead of trusting the predicate; the guard now carries that exact mutation. **ON PAID REVIEWS, he was asking for something already true of the live route and unenforced.** Of 72 paid-capable files only **4** read a BRIEF.md and are review dispatchers; 1 carries every control and it is the live dispatcher, which handles paid seats. The other 3 are dated August one-offs: registered, not deleted, and their entries now name all **5** controls they bypass where each previously claimed 1. A ratchet refuses a 4th. **TWO FAULTS OF MINE FOUND BY RUNNING THE WHOLE BOARD.** A fixture set `PANEL_BRIEF_UNCHECKED` with `setdefault`, which never restores -- silently disabling the guard that stops money being spent on a defective brief for every later test in the process. It passed alone and failed in the batch. A third instance predated today. The flag was never needed since A22; all 3 removed and a scanner refuses the pattern. Separately 2 tests needed `LOGS` bound because the dispatcher now names the round it purges: bound in the tests rather than letting the dispatcher tolerate the absence, which would fail open on a containment control. **THE SEAT TIMEOUT IS NOW OVERRIDABLE AND THE FIGURE I GAVE HIM WAS CIRCULAR.** 2426 s was reported as the 95th percentile of observed work; it was a percentile over durations INCLUDING attempts killed at the cap -- right-censored data used to choose the cap that caused the censoring. Kaplan-Meier over 137 attempts, 9 censored, by hand and by statsmodels to identical values: median **700.7 s**, 90th **1728.1 s**, 95th **2939.4 s**. 1800 sits just above the 90th and kills about 1 attempt in 10 while it is still working. `PANEL_SEAT_TIMEOUT_S` defaults to 1800 unchanged -- `call_claude_cli` has ~20 callers -- and cc2 then landed at **1826.8 s**, 26.8 s past the ceiling that had killed it twice. A longer clock is still not the general repair: the per-call rate is identical whether a seat works or churns (20.455 against 20.816 s), and measured today the tool-log sink does not exist until the subprocess returns, so no mid-flight progress signal exists at all. **THE ROUND: BOTH SEATS REFUTED THE BRIEF ON THE SAME POINT.** cc2 18,606 chars / 46 tool calls / 1826.8 s; fable 13,415 / 36 / 1305.4 s. The brief had withdrawn my non-monotonicity claim and replaced it with "as few divisions as possible is right on the attempts metric". Both killed the replacement with witnesses at budgets the brief never examined -- cost(3)=10 < cost(2)=11, and cost(3)=4 < cost(2)=5 -- inversions at 9 of 48 feasible budgets, 0.1875, Wilson [0.1019, 0.3194]. **So the file I withdrew was RIGHT that the count must be scanned, and wrong in its reasoning.** A third claim of mine also falls: "some rate pairs are infeasible at any division count" was my own per-gate ceiling binding -- (0.85, 0.75) is feasible at a single gate of 253 attempts. **AND ONE SEAT SETTLED MONOTONICITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE.** Under DETERMINISTIC success-count thresholds it is not unproven, it is FALSE. Under RANDOMISED thresholds it is a THEOREM by Karlin-Rubin: the binomial family has a monotone likelihood ratio, the most powerful test of exact size alpha is a randomised threshold on the total count, and the AND of 2 gates is itself a test of that size on the concatenated sample -- so it cannot beat the optimum. My own 801 merge failures in 4000 pairs were the clue and I read them as a negative result. **Verified independently: 801 of 801 repaired by randomisation alone**, worst power slack -4.441e-16 and size excess 8.674e-19, matching the seat's reported residuals to the digit; SymPy gives log(9) for the likelihood-ratio slope and z3 returns `unsat`. A randomised threshold is the standard completion of the binomial family, far narrower than the "arbitrary tests" my brief said a proof would need. **HIS QUESTION HAS 2 DERIVED ANSWERS AND THEY DISAGREE** -- preserved for the joint round. Both derive the count from RESOLUTION not cost, both identify complexity with an arcsine span (0.4636476090 over 0.5 to 0.9 in one form, 0.9272952180 in the other, which doubles it) and resources with attempts per model per window; they differ in the constant, the critical value and the exponent. One adds that the ATTEMPTS objective is degenerate at 2 divisions always, which makes my section 3 the answer rather than a caveat. **RELEGATION: 2 mechanisms, both answering his guard.** A peer-paired sign test -- simulated by me: with the stream hardening under an equal peer an absolute floor demotes a capable model 98.35% of the time, Wilson [0.9791, 0.9870], against **3.65%**, Wilson [0.0311, 0.0428], while on genuine decline it fires 99.68% against 96.27%. And a CUSUM on Rasch residuals with no window, threshold from a target run length, promotion as the mirror CUSUM so symmetry is structural. The second seat also showed the OBVIOUS stratified statistic violates his guard outright: under escalation the stratum varies only when the model succeeds, 228 of 400 observations drop, every survivor carries the same residual, and correlation with skill is not-a-number -- a tally of successes in disguise. Repaired on measured difficulty, 0.991. **THE DISCARDED ROUND IS RECORDED, NOT DELETED, AND ITS WORK WAS RECOVERED LATE.** I killed its dispatcher before the harvest step, so fable's deliverables were stranded in its sandbox. Recovered -- and the raw harvest was UNSOUND: `changes()` diffs a sandbox against the LIVE tree, which I had edited heavily since, so it attributed 11 of my own edits to the seat. Only the 3 files ABSENT from the tree can be attributed, and the diff's own header names the 11 excluded and why. That is the no-fake-labels rule applied to myself. **A PROCEDURAL ERROR OF MINE COST A HEALTHY ROUND.** I inspected cc2's retry sandbox at 14:07:05, found fable's reply, declared contamination and killed the run. The purge ran at 14:07:42 and the sandbox afterwards held only `BRIEF.md`. The control had worked; I looked during the copy. The build-completion marker was absent and I explained it away as buffering -- the check was available, it disagreed, and the guess won. Recorded as a memory so it is not relearned. Also: `docs/GLOSSARY.md` now documents the PANEL sense of "star topology" and names its collision with the RUNNER sense, which was the only documented one while rounds were being reported in the other. Records: both FULL RECORDs built and lint-clean outside their verbatim regions, 127 of 127 rounds mirrored. Guards: 13 new tests on the joint-round debt (5 mutations), 10 on the co-seat purge (5 mutations), 11 on the timeout (4 mutations), 8 on the paid ratchet, 7 on the env-leak scanner, 12 on the division scan, 12 on the quiet-arm dependency. Suite at commit: 501 passed. Wolfram-derived values computed with Wolfram Language (local Wolfram Engine, via wolframscript); licence auto-renewed to 2026-11-04. title: the wheel is largely invented, the research proving it had fabricated citations, and his "2 or 3" was nearly right
verbatim: the wheel is largely invented, the research proving it had fabricated citations, and his "2 or 3" was nearly right HIS INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-09: *"For the research stage of this task, make sure you research extensively!"* and *"Are we attempting to reinvent the wheel?"* 13 agents, 631 tool calls, 2,361,248 tokens, 2446.4 s, 0 errors: 6 literature dimensions, 1 archaeology pass over this project's own record, and 6 adversarial verifiers that between them checked **126 citations**. **EVERY DIMENSION CAME BACK SOUND ONLY *WITH CORRECTIONS*, AND THAT IS THE RUN'S MOST IMPORTANT OUTPUT.** The verifiers found a FABRICATED QUOTATION attributed in double quotes to a paper where the sentence does not occur, a FABRICATED MEASUREMENT attributed to a real paper, 2 of 3 author surnames wrong on a NeurIPS citation, wrong venues, a lower bound computed outside its own theorem's hypotheses with an INVENTED CONSTANT, a 4x misreading of the single figure one dimension called most important, and Douceur's Lemma 1 quoted as `g = rho` when it is `g = floor(rho)`. Raw findings are preserved whole under `experimental_notes/evidence/allocation_prior_art_2026-10-09/` per the standing rule that external review output is kept in full and unfiltered -- and the README there says in its own words to READ THE VERIFIERS FIRST. Nothing from the run is reported to him as established fact. **SO EVERY LOAD-BEARING NUMBER WAS RE-DERIVED HERE INSTEAD.** New producer: `scripts/how_many_attempts_a_ranking_needs_2026-10-09.py`. **HIS CHALLENGE LANDS AND THE FIGURE WAS MINE.** He wrote: *"300 attempts for a single model to solve any given problem is clearly vastly much too much! ... Are you even checking if these numbers make any practical sense?"* The 300 was quoted without the quantity that determines it. Measured exactly: the attempts needed to order 2 models correctly 95% of the time is set by the GAP between their success proportions -- **7 attempts at a gap of 0.40, 14 at 0.30, 32 at 0.20, 134 at 0.10, and only 540 at 0.05**, which is where 300 belongs. **His "very hard problem" instinct is therefore doing real statistical work**: a hard first problem MAXIMISES the gap, which is exactly what information-maximising item selection does in adaptive testing. The limit is also exact: at a gap of 0.20, 1 attempt orders correctly with probability 3/5 and 3 attempts with 1371/2000, both in SymPy rationals, so 2 or 3 rank a roster only where the problem separates it widely. **AND THE "3000 LEAGUES" HE REMEMBERED DOES NOT EXIST.** Searched: the largest division count any seat ever proposed is 22, the working range was 2 to 14, and every appearance of 2000 in the record is a number of OBSERVATIONS. There was no crazy number to push back on; the figure he recalled is a sample size that read as a league count. **HIS KNOCKOUT BRACKET IS REFUTED, VERIFIED HERE RATHER THAN CITED.** Ford (1957): the Bradley-Terry estimate exists and is unique iff the win graph is strongly connected. A bracket on n players yields exactly n-1 matches and is ACYCLIC -- confirmed at 4, 8 and 16 players, none strongly connected -- so the estimator is UNDEFINED, against 28 matches and strong connectivity for an 8-player round robin. A knockout also removes a participant on 1 result, against his own rule that no model is ever permanently set aside. **HIS SEASON PROPOSAL IS HALF REFUTED AND HALF STRENGTHENED.** A model accumulates a median of 1 decidable observation per round and **53.40% of 470 model-rounds yield 0 or 1**, so a round cannot be a season. Per experiment the mean is 9.7193, CI [7.48, 12.22], bootstrap and t-interval agreeing. But his instinct that rankings should be FIXED for a run is right for a stronger reason than he gave: not because round 1 settles them but because no round comes close, so the ranking must be carried in from accumulated history -- a persistent rating, not a table recomputed per round. **THE ARCHAEOLOGY ANSWERS HIM AND CONTRADICTS THE PREMISE.** The distributed/peer-to-peer discussion exists in 2 waves and almost nothing was built. `Scaling_Spec_GlobalMind_2026-08-26.md`, 141 lines, names Folding@home, Rosetta@home, SETI@home and Einstein@home at line 7 and says at line 122 *"Nothing described here has been built."* **It already answered his 700-model premise in the opposite direction**: line 73, *"A distributed CDSFL that recruits fifty cognitive architectures to review one artefact is a distributed system doing the work of about four"*, with line 97 recommending *"Panel size fixed at 4-6, not scaled"* -- and that arithmetic is re-derived from the live archive by a 10-test guard that passes. Line 105 names the structural mismatch: *"Where BOINC selects a canonical instance by quorum, a distributed CDSFL has no equivalent step."* Volunteer computing resolves disagreement by majority; this project's premise is that disagreement IS the signal. Networking exists in exactly 4 files and all 4 use sockets to FORBID network access in tests. The one genuinely valuable piece is `bench/verification_chain.py` (5 April): content-addressed digests, Ed25519 signatures, RFC 9162 Merkle inclusion proofs -- live, tested, and real substrate for a coordinator-free mode. The clearest blocker is the finding registry's identity scheme, a MONOTONIC COUNTER, so 2 peers both mint `C0001` with no merge rule; the fix is content-addressed identity, which the verification chain already computes. Roadmap: deferred past Bench Run 2, item 36 of the 2026-09-06 decision list, 1 of 11 items declared excluded, and he has already approved that. Artefacts: the joint round's FULL RECORD (128 of 128 rounds mirrored, lint-clean outside its verbatim regions), the morning-report pair at 101 lines with 0 lint findings and 0 decorative markers, and the full research evidence directory. title: the Lean anchor set is built, and a mutation pass caught me writing a guard that could not fail
verbatim: the Lean anchor set is built, and a mutation pass caught me writing a guard that could not fail HIS RULING: *"y, build the anchor set with Lean, and let's utilise it (minus the hype) appropriately in our work going forward ... if it adds nothing of use, then there is no requirement for you to do it."* That escape clause decided the shape, because FOLLOW found the obvious build would have added nothing. **WHAT FOLLOW FOUND BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BUILT.** The chain an anchor set needs is: pool -> per-seat (successes, attempts) -> Wilson lower bound -> ladder order. The LAST LINK DOES NOT EXIST. `routing.DEFAULT_FALSIFIER_STRENGTH` is `("Codex", "CC2", "ChatGPT", "Gemini", "DeepSeek", "Fable")` -- a frozen tuple of 6 VENDOR NAMES -- and `rank_falsifier_writers` ranks by position in it. The producer that computes a measured ranking, `bench/allocation_by_measured_capability_2026-10-07.py`, is an ORPHAN: no live module imports it, and the only other hits are inside seat sandbox harvests where 2 seats proposed a capability ledger that never landed. **So the live ladder ranks by NAME, which is the thing he has objected to 4 times.** Building the pool and wiring it straight into routing would have been 2 changes at once, the second of which alters what every routed finding does. The pool is therefore built and wired to a TEST; the single change that makes the ladder rate-aware is HIS, and a test now PINS the gap so it cannot be silently forgotten or silently closed. **WHY LEAN AND NOT SOMETHING CHEAPER.** The 2026-10-08 panel established that relegation is NOT IDENTIFIED from the live stream: only the difference between capability and difficulty enters, so a roster-wide capability drop and a stream-wide difficulty rise are the same distribution. Verified 3 ways before any of this: SymPy returns exactly 0, z3 returns `unsat`, mpmath returns 0.0 over 27 points. The anchor does not fix that by RATING difficulty -- a rating measured from our own models is the same degeneracy again -- but by holding difficulty INVARIANT. Lean is the only instrument available where that is true by construction: byte-stable statements and a deterministic kernel, no judge, no rubric, no partial credit. **4 WAYS A PROOF PASSES FOR THE WRONG REASON, EACH MEASURED ON LEAN 4.34.1 BEFORE THE GRADER WAS WRITTEN.** All 4 exit 0 and 3 emit NOTHING: `sorry` (warning only), `axiom` (silent -- `axiom cheat : forall a b, a + b = a * b` then using it proves a FALSE statement), `native_decide` (silent, trusts the compiler not the kernel), and RESTATEMENT (silent, and the worst -- changing `a + b = b + a` to `a + b = a + b` and proving it by `rfl` is accepted under the same name). The literature calls the last one semantic hallucination and reports formal-versus-informal discrepancies in MORE THAN HALF of miniF2F's problems. **AND A 5TH TRAP WAS MINE.** The first reading of those exit codes returned 0 for all 3 cheats because `$?` captured a `head` in a pipeline rather than `lean`. A grader built on that reading would have passed everything. The exit code is now captured directly, never through a pipe. **★ THE MUTATION PASS CAUGHT A GUARD OF MINE THAT COULD NOT FAIL.** Deleting the statement-identity branch left all 14 tests GREEN, because it was a TAUTOLOGY: `source = problem.statement + submitted`, so `source.startswith(problem.statement)` is always true. A guard that cannot fire, written into the very check protecting the pool's invariance. Replaced with a guard on DECLARATION KEYWORDS in the submission, which is the real attack and is checkable -- a submission opening its own `theorem`/`lemma`/`example` is restating the problem rather than proving it. A keyword inside a comment is NOT an attack and the helper strips line and block comments, which has its own test. A second mutation survived for a related reason: the refused-token scan catches `sorry` before Lean runs, so the branch catching a LEAN-REPORTED sorry had no test behind it. Both branches are now exercised. **P-PASS: 7 mutations, 7 killed, 0 survivors** -- dropping the token scan, keying on the exit code alone, dropping the declaration guard, counting UNAVAILABLE in the denominator, returning the point estimate instead of the lower bound, flattening the hard tier, and removing the comment stripping. **LEAN IS OPTIONAL AND ITS ABSENCE IS REPORTED, NEVER SILENTLY PASSED**, per his standing Wolfram ruling that nobody may be compelled to install a tool. Verified by running with `lean` removed from PATH: 0 attempts, 5 UNAVAILABLE, point estimate None, Wilson 0.0 -- so an absent toolchain neither inflates nor deflates a seat's rate. **SIMPLEST SUFFICIENT INSTALL, AND NO MATHLIB.** elan 4.2.4 with Lean 4.34.1, user-local in `~/.elan`, 2.7 GB, no sudo -- the installer was fetched and inspected first (377 lines, no privileged writes, sources only `github.com/leanprover/elan/releases`). All 5 pool problems compile against CORE Lean, so the pool carries no multi-gigabyte dependency. 2 of the 5 had to be repaired during that check -- `List.length_append` takes no explicit arguments in this version, and a Gauss-sum attempt could not be closed by `omega` -- which is the pool doing its job before shipping rather than after. **THE POOL'S HONEST LIMIT, ASSERTED RATHER THAN BURIED.** 5 problems spanning a 1-line library lemma to a 10-line induction with a calc chain. A PERFECT 5 of 5 supports a Wilson lower bound of only **0.565518**, so the pool as it stands cannot confidently rank a seat -- a test fails if that figure ever rises above 0.60, so the caveat cannot go stale. Growing the pool is the cheap next step and needs no ruling. Regression: 83 passed across the offline guard, the free-window money guard, the additive standard, routing, and the 20 new anchor tests. title: Pass B: his own words as the source, and 4 of 12 checkable rulings had not landed
verbatim: Pass B: his own words as the source, and 4 of 12 checkable rulings had not landed HIS INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-11: *"Run Pass B over my 212 in-window annotations. I accept your above recommendations and clarifications and you should also implement any previously ruled/agreed work not done so far, over lets say a reasonable window of the last 7 days."* ★★★ THE SOURCE IS INVERTED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. Pass A enumerated "what was agreed" from 5 sources that were ALL my own writing and 0 of which read his Responses folder, so it could not detect an instruction he gave that I never recorded. 29 of his 200 window annotations have NO verbal trace in those 5 sources (0.1450, Wilson [0.1029, 0.2005]), and that is a FLOOR because the predicate measures topic coverage, not compliance. Pass B reads HIS 248 in-window annotations end to end instead. 12 express mechanically checkable rulings. LANDED 8 of 12 = 0.6667, Wilson [0.3906, 0.8619]. NOT LANDED 4 of 12. NOT LANDED, and these are his to rule on: immune memory default False; 13 of 16 setting configs say True fold fixes forward default False; 1 of 32; the live-tree guard he required DOES exist completion signal his 2026-10-08 ruling was to make the seat cap NON-ARBITRARY, not merely adjustable. The adjustable cap landed; the "print I am done" signal he actually proposed did not. ~20 callers of call_claude_cli. round cap max_rounds is 21 against his ruling of 10, and the recommendation to extend when convergence is near is not printed. ★★★ FOLLOW REFUSED A HARMFUL FIX. 43 of 47 configs pin burst_mode="off", which read as wholesale defiance of his "It shouldnt be off" with an obvious bulk remedy. 33 of the 43 are HISTORICAL RECORDS of archived runs (0.7674, Wilson [0.6226, 0.8685]) and editing them would falsify the experimental record; of the remaining 10, 5 are exp52 factorial cells where the setting is part of the DESIGN. No config was changed. The default is "auto" and the runner gates on != "off" (reference_runner_v3.py:15667), so his ruling IS satisfied by the default. ★★★ THE ADJUDICATION FIGURES ARE WITHDRAWN IN FULL. 0.7603 vs 0.4003 on a 1093/1304 corpus implies a statistics share of 0.6142, not the 0.9684 reported; for 0.9684 to hold the rate would have to be 14.6356, above 1 and therefore impossible. No producer exists, so which figure is wrong is undetermined. It reached the document he read. His challenge of 2026-10-08 -- "Ae you even checking if these numbers make any practical sense before writing them?" -- is answered: no, and this is the proof. ★★ 221 OF 481, NOT 221 OF 691. The earlier denominator counted 210 markdown headings from machine-generated .md files as his annotations. Corrected grep-blind share 0.4595, Wilson [0.4154, 0.5041] -- nearly half, so the correction makes the finding WORSE. THE TOKEN ARM, his second resource, raised 2026-10-04 and unread for 7 days: "a big spike in my Anthropic Max plan usage quota ... I usually only barely scratch the surface." Plan limits are readable only in-session, so the hook now DEMANDS a get_usage check on every allowed fan-out and a directive binds it. Baseline 2026-10-11 16:40 BST: 5-hour 28%, weekly 33%, Fable 13%, extra usage disabled, 0.00 GBP of 150.00. His claim is CORRECT and the spike had reset. `ultracode` DISAMBIGUATED on his challenge: "in my vocabulary 'Ultracode' should be reserved for 'reasoning effort' over unlimited use of other resources." Spend the allowance on DEPTH, never BREADTH. Of 12 errors I made on 2026-10-11, 10 (0.8333, Wilson [0.5520, 0.9530], binomial p = 0.0193) were catchable by reasoning BEFORE running; only 2 needed execution. A 5TH PREDICATE ERROR, CAUGHT BY P-PASS. The burst check probed for burst_enabled, burst_mode_enabled and itc_burst_enabled, NONE of which exist; the field is burst_mode: str = "auto". It reported NOT LANDED on a facility that is on. A subset is not a board; the last full board remains 10,306 passed on 2026-10-07. It is unmerged work, not rejected work. AND THE ONE COMMIT THAT BYPASSED THE PRE-COMMIT GATE EXPLAINS ITSELF. `42f0bc73` records the reason: the gate ran 1 failed, 485 passed, 15 skipped, and the single failure was the Desktop mirror of CDSFL_MASTER_TASK_LIST.md, which the hook CORRECTLY refuses to let a second checkout refresh. Benign, documented at the time, and settled by one command from the main checkout. THE CONFLICTS WERE ALL ONE THING, AND THAT WAS VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. 18 files, 22 hunks. A check that normalised `.py:<number>` to `.py:N` showed EVERY hunk differs only in a citation line number -- both branches re-pointed the same citations as reference_runner_v3.py grew on each. HEAD's numbers match the current runner, so HEAD won every hunk. RESOLVED HUNK-BY-HUNK, NOT WITH `--ours`. `git checkout --ours <file>` takes the WHOLE HEAD version and would have silently discarded branch content that auto-merged cleanly elsewhere in those same 18 files. Each conflict region was replaced with its HEAD side in place, leaving the auto-merged remainder intact. One file carried a RENAME conflict (`exhausted_marking_age_lock` -> `release_valve_age_lock`) whose marker is `<<<<<<< HEAD:path` rather than `<<<<<<< HEAD`, so the first pass missed it; it was resolved separately and leaves no duplicate. P-PASS: 78 passed on the recovered work's own guard, `python3 -m pytest bench/tests/test_field_envelope_2026-10-04.py -q`. STILL OWED ON ITEM 13: reclaiming the 2.5 GB. The worktree DIRECTORIES can be removed to free the disk while LEAVING THE BRANCH REFS INTACT -- deleting a git ref is one of the 3 actions he reserves to himself in person, and freeing disk does not require it. verbatim: his 4 panel lessons verified: 3 of 4 had landed, and my "0 of 4" is withdrawn HIS RULING, 2026-10-11: *"Verdict: Verify and fix all."* Against the 4 lessons he answered on 2026-10-07, each with identical words: *"We should use it. Wire it in all simulated and real runners going forward."* ★★★ MY EARLIER "0 of 4" IS WITHDRAWN IN FULL. It failed twice over. First, the grep patterns used `\|` -- BRE alternation -- under `grep -E`, so every pattern searched for a LITERAL PIPE and matched nothing. Second, the follow-up searched `reference_runner_v3.py` for the PANEL's function names (`_preserve_prior_attempt`, `_detect_round_kind`, `REQUIRED_FIELDS`) rather than for the BEHAVIOUR, and in the wrong module: dispatch lives in `experiment_11_orchestrator.py`. Measured properly: LANDED 3 of 4 = 0.7500, Wilson [0.3006, 0.9544]. 2 LANDED, AND BETTER THAN THE PANEL'S FORM. The dispatcher ACCUMULATES tool calls across retries with per-attempt detail, rather than moving a prior file aside. Fixed 2026-09-07 after a seat found 7 calls then 2 logged as 2, losing 7 -- and the runner writes no per-model reply, so it has nothing to overwrite. He asked "Measure it first to confirm", and that is what the measurement says. 3 LANDED IN A DIFFERENT FORM, which is the honest verdict rather than a tick. `detect_target_kind` reads the actual path and bytes and returns the detected kind in every case. The panel's form detects ROUND kind, blind or joint, and the runner has no blind/joint round concept to apply it to. 4 LANDED. `verdict_is_substantive` is deliberately a FREE FUNCTION and its docstring records why: "several confer harnesses each grew their own copy of the same three-clause test". All 3 repaired; a check now asserts 0 contradictions between any note and its verdict. title: the runner now refuses a reply that is merely non-empty, and the risk was measured first
verbatim: the runner now refuses a reply that is merely non-empty, and the risk was measured first HIS RULING, 2026-10-07, verbatim on each of 4 panel lessons: *"We should use it. Wire it in all simulated and real runners going forward."* His reasoning: *"the panel applies a substance test to every reply and the runner applies none. The panel refuses a reply that is merely non empty, because an error string, a usage notice or a holding note is answering without answering the question."* And his instruction of 2026-10-11: *"If you are implying that a proposed change might make convergence impossible, or break convergence completely, then yes, that is something we should discuss."* ★★★ I OVERSTATED THE RISK AND THE MEASUREMENT WITHDRAWS IT. I said the change "affects whether runs converge", which let caution do the work a measurement should have done. Measured across **2,582 archived runner replies**: the predicate rejects **26, 0.0101, Wilson [0.0069, 0.0147], exact [0.0066, 0.0147]** -- and **20 of the 26 are EMPTY**, already failures rather than answers. The remaining 6 are 2, 7, 191, 191 and 603 characters. **Exactly 1 would be rejected while carrying a finding**: 191 characters with 1 finding, which is precisely the holding-note case the test exists to catch. No panel was needed because the archive answered the question. WHERE IT IS WIRED, AND WHERE IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT. On the primary seat dispatch in `_dispatch_single_model_inner` and on its secondary fallback, which answers the same question and is held to the same standard. NOT on `run_preflight`, which accepts `len(text.strip()) > 5` as proof of life -- an 800-character floor there would fail every preflight, and finding that is why the parameter is OPT-IN rather than a changed default. NOT on `_arb_dispatch`, a closure invoked indirectly whose exception handling cannot be traced statically. 13 of the 14 call sites sit inside `try/except`; that one does not. IT RAISES RATHER THAN RETURNING A SENTINEL because `dispatch_to_model` ALREADY raises on a timeout and on a process that exits without a result. A hollow reply is the same class of event -- the dispatch did not produce an answer -- so it belongs on the existing path rather than on a new one. ★★ AND A FINDING ALONG THE WAY: `_report_dispatch_failure` is IMPORTED at reference_runner_v3.py:244 and CALLED NOWHERE. An unwired import in the active runner, which is why there was no live failure-reporting path to route a rejection into, and why raising was the right mechanism rather than reporting. P-PASS: 7 passed. Disabling the check kills 2 of them and restoring returns 7, so the guard is live. The default path is asserted byte-identical: the same hollow reply passes when the test is off. title: his 0.05 false-alarm proportion pinned, with the ruling it depends on
verbatim: his 0.05 false-alarm proportion pinned, with the ruling it depends on HIS RULING, 2026-10-11: *"Then yes. Do it that way. 0.05 is acceptable within this f[r]amework."* It is the chance of DEMOTING A MODEL THAT IS IN FACT STABLE, and both decision thresholds are solved FROM it rather than chosen. THE REASONING IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT DEPENDS ON ANOTHER OF HIS RULINGS. If demotion could happen mid-experiment, a LOOSER number would be right: under the standing no-benching rule a wrong demotion costs little, because the model keeps working on easier problems, while a missed decline costs more. But he ruled the same day that rankings are FIXED at the start of an experiment and held until it completes. That moves demotion to BETWEEN experiments, where there is more evidence and no urgency, and that is where the stricter number belongs. If ruling 4 ever changes, this number must be revisited rather than inherited -- and a test asserts the reasoning is recorded beside the value, not just the value. NOT WIRED, AND MEASURED SO: 0 references to relegation or false-alarm machinery in reference_runner_v3.py or routing.py. Pinned with his other 2 rulings of the same day, where the work will be picked up. AND THE SAME PREDICATE FAULT TWICE IN AN HOUR. The guard first searched for his quote as a CONTIGUOUS string and failed on a sentence plainly present, because the quote WRAPS across 2 comment lines -- the identical fault caught in the lesson-4 docstring check an hour earlier. Repaired the same way, with a whitespace-flexible pattern. A repeating error class within an hour is the signal `feedback_long_session_degradation` names, and it is why building stops here for tonight rather than continuing into items 9, 12 and 14. title: I invented 2 timestamps; the clock was right and 3 guard designs cannot catch it
verbatim: I invented 2 timestamps; the clock was right and 3 guard designs cannot catch it HIS QUERY, 2026-10-11: *"your timestamping is oddly off? its 32:15 BST here in the UK. I don't know what clock you are reading from?"* ★★★ THE CLOCK WAS NEVER WRONG. THE SENTENCES WERE. `date` reads 2026-10-11 23:15:57 BST at offset +0100, and NTP drift against time.apple.com is +0.0818 s. The prompt hook agreed at 23:15:38. What was wrong is that a morning report and a commit message claimed the work stopped at "00:05" and "five past midnight" when it was 23:15 -- ESTIMATED FORWARD from a 23:00 reading rather than captured. That is exactly what `read-the-clock` forbids, and it is logged there as a repeated failure. Corrected in both report formats. HIS OWN FIGURE CARRIED A TRANSPOSITION, SEPARATED OUT SO IT IS NOT CONFUSED WITH MY FAULT: there is no 32nd hour, and 32:15 is 23:15 transposed. ★★★ THREE GUARD DESIGNS MEASURED, ALL THREE FAIL, AND NONE WAS SHIPPED. 1 any future time vs file mtime: 197 of 1083 = 0.1819, Wilson [0.1601, 0.2060]. Unusable -- and mtime is CONTAMINATED, because the pre-commit citation repair rewrites dozens of notes in one pass, so an April note carries a mass-edit mtime while legitimately citing a time from the day it describes. 2 future time in a HEADING only: 12 of 1083 = 0.0111, Wilson [0.0063, 0.0193]. Better, but almost all 12 carry an explicit DATE beside the time and are self-describing. 3 BARE time in a heading, no date: 1 of 1083 = 0.0009, Wilson [0.0002, 0.0052]. Excellent noise -- AND IT DOES NOT CATCH THE ERROR IT WAS BUILT FOR. Midnight defeats it: at an mtime of 23:10 a claim of "00:05" is 00:05 THAT MORNING, EARLIER than 23:10, so a forward claim across midnight reads as past. Verified by execution on 3 probes. SHIPPING DESIGN 3 WOULD HAVE ADDED A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL ON ITS OWN MOTIVATING CASE -- the vacuous-guard defect this project keeps finding, in a new costume, and the 4th such catch today. The ground truth a guard would need is the instant a sentence was WRITTEN, which no artefact records. The mechanism that works already exists and costs nothing: the clock hook injects the time every turn. The failure was not reading it. title: item 14: the sim seam lost substance and 3 guards went blind to a wrapper split
verbatim: item 14: the sim seam lost substance and 3 guards went blind to a wrapper split Running the 105 guards dated on his own instruction days returned 4 failed, 1142 passed, 1 skipped in 237.09 s. Two distinct causes, one mine from tonight. MINE, AND IT WOULD HAVE SILENCED THE NEXT SIMULATED RUN. Wiring `require_substance` into `dispatch_to_model` changed the primitive's parameter list and left `sim_dispatch_shim` behind. That guard exists because on 2026-08-30 a mismatched shim raised inside a bare `except` and read as a model returning nothing: falsifier_code 0 of 19 against 23 of 39 on the same target, scipy Fisher p = 6.0e-06. Two call sites in `reference_runner_v3` pass `require_substance=True`, so the shim now carries it AND honours it -- the module's own contract says the error contract is part of the seam. Executed in all 3 states: hollow + gate on raises, hollow + gate off returns unchanged, substantive + gate on passes. NOT MINE, AND THE SYSTEM WAS NEVER BROKEN. Commit 46617574 on 2026-10-07 split `_dispatch_single_model` into a 12-line wrapper over a 77-line `_inner`. Verified by AST at 3 revisions: at 46617574^ the function was 78 lines and held `_ASK_CORRECTED_COPY`; after, `_inner` holds that marker, the "NO ask" announcement and the `dispatch_to_model` call, while the wrapper holds none. So 3 guards asserting on source text were blind for 4 days -- `execute-do-not-grep` for the 4th time in this project. Repaired at root rather than loosened: `bench/tests/_delegation.py` follows a thin wrapper to its delegate and CONCATENATES the two, so a marker deleted from both still fails. 12-test ratchet proves it can fail -- deleting the marker, deleting the announcement, removing the primitive call and renaming the function each return absent, an unrelated function is excluded, and with the follow disabled the wrapper is NOT a caller, which proves the repair is load-bearing. 204 passed across every guard touching the shim. Also item 14's triage script, which reads his 92 older imperative instructions through the reader's OWN annotation definition after an earlier ad-hoc extraction re-implemented the test inline and admitted 2 markdown headings from a saved web page as his words. title: item 9: the round count is computed per run, and my own 2026-09-20 wiring was wrong
verbatim: item 9: the round count is computed per run, and my own 2026-09-20 wiring was wrong HIS ORDER: *"9: Then yes, do this also."* With the constraint that settled the design: *"there is a case to be considered at where that average number might sit in experiments ran by other researchers."* So no constant ships. n* = (a/theta)^(1/gamma) is fitted to each run's own novelty series, with theta a config field because it is the RESEARCHER'S cost/value call. IT DOES NOT USE `_estimate_gamma`, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING. The 2026-09-20 proposal -- mine -- said to feed the runner's existing gamma into the formula. The gate fits the CUMULATIVE series and returns 1 - slope; the formula's gamma is the exponent of the PER-ROUND intensity. On exact counts from a known power law at gamma = 0.709 the intensity fit recovers 0.709000 at every round count, while the cumulative fit returns 0.3525 at n=4, 0.4129 at n=10, 0.5121 at n=50 and 0.6100 at n=500 -- still 0.099 short at 500 rounds, because the log-linear form drops the -1 in N(n) = a*(n^(1-gamma) - 1)/(1-gamma). At the 3 to 21 rounds this project runs it is biased low by 0.30 to 0.36. The proposal never said where `a` comes from, because `_estimate_gamma` discards its intercept. Three wirings were available and ALL THREE overestimate on the project's own early data [5,3,2,2] against the correct n* = 9.3695: cumulative a and gamma gives 22.3759 (2.3882x), intensity a with cumulative gamma gives 71.5436 (7.6358x), round-1 count as a gives 75.9566 (8.1068x). The smallest error available from the proposal as written is 2.3882x. GAMMA IS NOT DEMOTED AND NOT TOUCHED. `_estimate_gamma` and the gate's 0.30/0.45 thresholds are a matched pair calibrated on that estimator's own scale, which is exactly why 0.30 is right there and would be far too low here. A second estimator answers a second question. A guard asserts the budget module consults no gate threshold and calls `_estimate_gamma` not at all. VERIFIED: SymPy solves the stopping rule to exactly this root; d n*/d gamma < 0 for a > theta so a faster-depleting space earns fewer rounds; python, numpy and mpmath agree to 3.55e-15; the fit reproduces the a = 4.89, gamma = 0.709, n* = 9.37 recorded in March 2026. WIRED AND ADVISORY. 10 keys reach the hardened gate's telemetry on a real call. The gate's verdict is identical at theta = 0.1, 1.0 and 100.0, which is the test that it gates nothing. Churn returns NO_DECAY with no number, because a run whose yield is not falling has no optimal round count and the formula says so. A broken projection cannot fell a run. 20 tests. title: item 12: a human review fires on substantial evidence, and the naive design was refuted first
verbatim: item 12: a human review fires on substantial evidence, and the naive design was refuted first HIS CONDITION: a review *"should only be triggered if there is substantial evidence that an experimental run is unlikely to converge under the given conditions and with the available resources."* HIS CONSTRAINT, 2026-09-28: *"What I don't want is a condition where no run could ever complete, and where the HIL queue could grow to unmanageable levels."* So it REQUESTS A LOOK: halts nothing, vetoes nothing, changes no verdict, and a guard asserts the gate's verdict is decided by the gate alone. THE OBVIOUS DESIGN WAS REFUTED BY THE ARCHIVE BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WIRED. Reusing item 9's projection -- trigger when n* exceeds the rounds remaining -- looked elegant because items 9 and 12 appear to be one instrument used forward and as an alarm. Over the 17 archived reports carrying a per-round series and a round cap, n* ranges from 151.64 to 1.79969828506e20 rounds, so that rule fires on 16 of 17 runs INCLUDING 4 of the 5 that converged. The 5th escaped only because its 2-round series is too short to fit at all, which is not the rule working. Cause: convergence here is the two-sided gate on CRITICAL findings reaching zero, not total yield falling below theta, so n* answers a question the gate does not ask. WHAT SHIPPED. Signal A is DEDUCTIVE: criterion (C) needs K consecutive zero-novel-critical rounds, so with fewer than K rounds left it cannot be met even by a flawless run. That is arithmetic, not a forecast, which is why it clears his "substantial" bar alone. Signals B (most of the budget spent with gamma_critical still under the gate's threshold) and C (the critical series not declining) are statistical, so either alone is a hunch and TWO are required. Guards hold all three boundaries. MEASURED: signal A fires on 0 of the 5 converged runs, Wilson 95% [0.0000, 0.4345], and on 12 of 12 that reached their cap. The honest claim is 0 observed in 5, NOT a demonstrated low rate -- 5 is a small denominator and the interval says so. No archived report carries a convergence field (0 of 17), so the label is DERIVED from stopping short of the cap and is marked as derived everywhere it is used. Producer: `scripts/the_review_trigger_false_alarm_rate_2026-10-11.py`. A CLEAN RUN IS NEVER FLAGGED, which was the fatal case. A clean target has an all-zero critical series by construction and 3 consecutive clean convergences is the programme of study's own success criterion. The trigger inherits `_gamma_is_estimable` from his 2026-10-08 ruling rather than re-deriving it, so gamma's 0.0 SENTINEL is never read as "no decay"; signal C additionally requires a non-zero sum. BOUNDED: signal A establishes the HARDENED GATE'S WINDOW is unreachable, not that no convergence route exists -- the runner also carries an EXHAUSTED bypass and a sparsity branch. That is exactly why this is a request and not a verdict. 20 tests; 338 passed across every gamma and convergence guard. title: item 5: the domain-verdict gap is measured again, and my own withdrawal was miscalculated
verbatim: item 5: the domain-verdict gap is measured again, and my own withdrawal was miscalculated HIS RULING: *"Then I don't get it? You ay we need to rebuild the premise? Then you say the item should be parked? So there is, or is no work to do here? If there is valid work to do, then you should do it."* He was right -- saying the premise needed rebuilding and saying to park the item cannot both stand. The work was valid. THE MEASUREMENT, REBUILT WITH A PRODUCING SCRIPT. Settled-verdict rate by domain over 2,673 decided findings: statistics 0.8656 Wilson [0.8451, 0.8838] on 1,198; software 0.7372 [0.7128, 0.7603] on 1,313; engineering 0.6774 [0.5537, 0.7805] on 62; cs_software 0.4286 [0.3140, 0.5514] on 63; chemistry 1.0000 [0.9059, 1.0000] on 37. Pooled 0.7897, 2,111 of 2,673. Largest single domain's share of all settled outcomes 0.4912, and the shares sum to 1.000000. `domain` IS RUN-LEVEL, which no earlier version of this claim acknowledged. No finding record in the archive carries a domain key, so a finding inherits its run's. Excluded and counted: 2,099 records whose `status` is a test outcome (PASS/FAIL/ SKIP/WARN) sharing the key name, and 2,774 duplicate records where the same finding appears in both a run's state file and its report. Either would have inflated a denominator silently. THE WITHDRAWN FIGURES ARE CONFIRMED IMPOSSIBLE, EXACTLY. Implied share 9914312/14289591 = 0.693814; the rate needed for the asserted 0.9684 share is 10592550459/1030160000 = 10.282432, above 1. SymPy on exact rationals, mpmath to 30 places. AND MY OWN WITHDRAWAL WAS ITSELF MISCALCULATED -- the same defect one level up, in the file he read. The note gave the implied share as 0.6142 and the needed rate as 14.6356; the true values are 0.693814 and 10.282432, off by 0.0796 and 4.3532. The CONCLUSION holds either way so the withdrawal stands, but a correction carrying its own arithmetic error is exactly what this script exists to stop. Both wrong figures are recorded in the script rather than quietly replaced. THE SELF-CHECK ANSWERS HIS CHALLENGE OF 2026-10-08 -- *"Ae you even checking if these numbers make any practical sense before writing them"* -- MECHANICALLY. Every share is derived from the same counts as every rate, so they cannot disagree by construction; a rate outside [0,1], parts that do not sum to their total, or shares that do not sum to 1 exit 3 with the quantity named. Guards prove the refusal fires. BOUNDED: domains differ in target article, model roster, runner version and date, so the gap is measured, not attributed to the domain. 15 tests. title: two correct safety mechanisms were leaving a stale citation between them
verbatim: two correct safety mechanisms were leaving a stale citation between them FOUND BY RUNNING THE MEMORY AND LEDGER GUARDS after writing tonight's memory files. 3 red: 2 were mine and are fixed (the index had grown to 192 of its 200-line loader limit, so 5 new entries are consolidated to 2 and it now sits at 189; the memory exclusions ledger needed the derivation re-run). The 3rd was not mine and is the interesting one. THE RUN LEDGER CITES A LINE IN THE RUNNER, AND IT HAD DRIFTED 238 LINES. Measured at 3 revisions by locating the generator's own anchor text: correct at `40c4a154` when the ledger was last written, **already 174 lines stale at this evening's starting HEAD**, and 238 by the end -- so the guard was red before tonight's work and 64 of those lines are mine. NEITHER REPAIRER COULD FIX IT, BOTH FOR GOOD REASONS. `citation_content_guard` only re-points a citation preceded by a backticked `def` or `class` whose AST span it can read; this one points at a COMMENT, which has no span, so it is correctly skipped -- it repaired 29 other citations tonight and left this one. And the ledger generator, which CAN derive the line by searching for its anchor, refuses to rewrite on a checkout holding fewer run artefacts than the ledger declares (44/31 against 56/31 here), because rewriting would delete rows that exist elsewhere. That refusal is the removal half of the additive standard and it is right. So a row-protection refusal was blocking a citation repair, because the two were bundled in one operation. They are now separable: the refusal still fires and still protects rows, and the derived citation is repaired anyway. Verified by mutation -- setting it to 99999 and running the refresh repairs it to 18535 while all 55 table rows stay byte-identical, and a correct citation leaves the file untouched so it never appears as a spurious diff. 20 tests on the ledger, 47 on the memory guards. title: the restore now fires at a task boundary, and the board accounted for all 20 reds
verbatim: the restore now fires at a task boundary, and the board accounted for all 20 reds HIS DESIGN CORRECTION, 2026-10-12, which overrode the proposal made an hour earlier: *"it's probably not heathy to interrupt a task that was running immediately before compaction ... it would need to fire at a safe point immediately after the first task in any given task list completes after a compaction. Then it would need to go back, and check that last before continuing with the rest of the work."* He is right: a turn-end trigger would have fired 0.91 min after the 2026-10-11 compaction, mid-item-14 with the tree dirty. The first COMMIT landed at 16.89 min and was exactly item 14's completion. `~/.claude/hooks/compaction_task_boundary.py`, registered FIRST among the Stop hooks. It stays silent until a commit exists since the compaction, then runs the restore, BLOCKS the stop so the context lands, names the commits made during the degraded window and orders the re-check before the rest of the list. A commit is the safe point because the pre-commit board must pass for one to exist, so no task is half-applied. THE TWO TRIGGERS COMPOSE, AND THE GAIN IS IN THE COMPOSITION. A commit trigger ALONE is NOT reliably better than waiting: sooner on 27 of 43, Wilcoxon p = 0.2164, with a WORSE maximum (2034.99 min against 1543.13). Firing on whichever comes first gives median 13.18 min against 55.22, p90 54.95 against 420.30, Wilcoxon p = 2.803e-06; and on the 32 compactions where he was away over 30 minutes, median wait falls 88.57 -> 22.71 min, 112.00 hours of degraded work avoided. Producer: `scripts/the_task_boundary_restore_is_sooner_2026-10-12.py`. ITS P-PASS FOUND A DEFECT AND THEN A SECOND ONE. (1) The first version gated only on `_recovery_ran_after`, which `cdsfl_recover.py` writes itself -- so a restore that failed for any reason left no marker and the hook re-armed at EVERY stop, refusing one per turn indefinitely. `fired_for` is now written BEFORE the restore and separately from its success. (2) Converting that guard from an index comparison to an EXECUTED dying-restore test immediately exposed a test-ordering bug: `compaction_watch.STATE` is bound from `Path.home()` at import, so importing before setting the test HOME read the operator's live marker. 4 mutations each turn the guard red. 23 tests. ONE CODE PATH: the scan is EXTRACTED into `compaction_watch.load_state_and_scan()` and imported, verified behaviour-preserving against the pre-change copy (identical exit codes, markers and notice text). 3 hooks that existed ONLY on his machine -- `sv_milestone_gate`, `local_resource_budget`, `compaction_task_boundary` -- are now hard-linked into `hooks/`, sharing inodes, so drift is impossible rather than detected. THE BOARD: 20 failed, 10847 passed, 18 skipped, 3468.81 s. ALL 20 ACCOUNTED FOR. MINE AND FIXED (10): 3 new scripts accepted an unknown flag at exit 0 and 1 capped a listing silently -- all 4 now route through `scripts/_cli_help.answer_help`, exit 2 on an unknown flag and state their remainder; 3 `compaction_notice` reds were TEST POLLUTION, because `_auto_restore` writes the LIVE `last_recovery` and that guard unlinked only the session marker, so each run acknowledged the next test's compaction (HOME now isolated, 14 passed); 3 more were ONE cause, a memory file written after the last sv leaving the derived ledger at 214 against 215, and the `desktop_mirrors` red was a pure cascade whose own message said so. NOT MINE (10): 4 `shared_subscription_seats_are_serialised` assert a property HIS 2026-10-08 ruling replaced with staggering, red for 4 days; `test_the_baseline_is_honest` was ALREADY red at `7a8fd077` (20 measured against a pin of 21 -- lowered to 20 with provenance); 2 `scripts_are_reached` name 3 scripts added 2026-10-06, 10-09 and 10-11 16:20, all pre-compaction; `exp52_factor_switches` and `simulated_runs_are_excluded` were untouched since the compaction. STILL RED AND DELIBERATELY SO: the source-text census at 98 against a pin of 82. By the detector's OWN predicate only 5 are mine, and 2 of those are CONVERTED to executing checks. Raising the pin would absorb 11 assertions nobody has examined, and the guard warns against that in its own words, so it stays red for his call. title: the night's error shape, recorded as a hypothesis rather than a finding
verbatim: the night's error shape, recorded as a hypothesis rather than a finding 4 of the 11 errors made between the 2026-10-11 23:23:01 compaction and 02:25 were improvising a measurement this project already had a committed definition for: 0.3636, Wilson [0.1517, 0.6462], Clopper-Pearson [0.1093, 0.6921]. Widened to "an existing instrument would have prevented it" it is 6 of 11, 0.5455, Wilson [0.2801, 0.7873] -- and a one-sided binomial against a 50/50 null gives p = 0.5000, so it is NOT statistically distinguishable from chance at n = 11 and is recorded as a pattern to watch rather than a measured dominance. A CORRECTION TO MY OWN REPLY. I told him "four instances" and listed reading UTC as local among them. That was 2026-10-01, not this session -- a historical instance folded into tonight's tally, which made the pattern look cleaner than the evidence supports. The count of 4 is right; the membership was not. THE 4, each beside the instrument that already existed: re-implementing the founder's annotation predicate instead of calling `annotations()`, which admitted 2 markdown headings from a saved web page as his words; counting source-text assertions with a hand-written regex (15) where the detector's own predicate gives 5, a figure that reached a reply before the correction; verifying 4 repaired scripts by hand instead of re-running `test_operational_scripts.py`, which when finally run passed 664 assertions; and checking the memory index's LINE COUNT rather than its PER-ENTRY LENGTH, where the entry was 230 against a limit of 150. WHY IT IS NOT "BE MORE CAREFUL": in all 4 the improvised instrument was cheaper to reach for, and in 3 it returned a PLAUSIBLE NUMBER rather than an error. A plausible wrong number is the expensive kind. The entry carries a falsifiable prediction so it can be withdrawn: if the class is real the WRONG_INSTRUMENT share should hold at or above roughly 0.2 over the next 3 comparable windows; if it falls toward 0 this is a story told about 11 events. title: the morning report's decision list is now DERIVED, and it found 3 decisions I had missed
verbatim: the morning report's decision list is now DERIVED, and it found 3 decisions I had missed HIS ORDER: *"Build the generator, whole session, narrative moves to the notes. But leave enough detail for me to make sane and sensible choices. Don't leave me guessing what you are talking about."* WHAT THE HAND-WRITTEN REPORT GOT WRONG, and this is the case for the generator rather than for more care. (1) **A19 was listed as "approved by you, not built"** while its own marker reads `state: OPEN | status: TESTED`, its entry says "BUILT AND TESTED 2026-09-11, NOT DONE -- Section P applies, and the last step is HIS", and its evidence passes 20 tests. The marker was right and my prose was wrong. (2) **3 open defects that explicitly ask for a founder ruling were missing entirely** -- they sit in `STUDY_IN_FLIGHT.json` under `open_defects`, each marked "FOUND, NOT FIXED (founder issued 'd')", and one of them records that a commit quotes him approving a change `DECISIONS_AWAITING_YOU_2026-09-06.md` records him REJECTING. Neither error is possible against a list read from the markers. AND 5 ITEMS I REPORTED AS NEEDING HIM DO NOT. V9 was approved 2026-09-18 ("V9: Approved.") and all 4 outstanding study measurements carry rulings on record -- RUN IT, DO IT, EXTEND THE EXISTING GUARD, build it into the schema. title: the generated report was not reproducible, and the P-pass caught it before he read it
verbatim: the generated report was not reproducible, and the P-pass caught it before he read it FOUND BY TRYING TO BREAK IT, which is the only reason it was found at all. Generating the report twice gave DIFFERENT BYTES in both the markdown and the TTS form. The diff was one line: the work-done ledger had grown by 1, and the new entry was the commit that carried the report. Not non-determinism -- SELF-REFERENCE, and the same shape `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md` carries, whose own `sv` block documents it as "generated first and committed second, so it cannot describe the commit that carries it". WHY IT MATTERED RATHER THAN BEING A CURIOSITY. A tracked file that changes on every commit cannot be committed in a stable state: committing it makes a commit, which changes it. So every future commit would have carried a spurious diff, and "regenerate to check" would never have agreed with what was on disk. THE FIX KEEPS THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS AND DROPS THE ONE THAT DOES NOT. The report is DERIVED and is no longer tracked; every source it is built from IS tracked -- the task-list markers, `STUDY_IN_FLIGHT.json`, the parked file, the triage producer and `data/morning_report_decisions.json`. Both renderers now STAMP THE HEAD they were built at, so "rebuild it and you get this" is checkable rather than asserted, and the `.gitignore` rule names the rebuild command so a reader is never stranded. Nothing is lost: at the stamped HEAD the generator reproduces both files byte for byte, verified. 4 new guards hold it: the report names its HEAD, 2 runs at a fixed HEAD are byte-identical, the derived file is NOT tracked, and the ignore rule names the rebuild command. 22 tests in total. Also checked, because the gate's file list named it: `STUDY_IN_FLIGHT.json` was never written. It is absent from the commit, clean in the tree, and the generator only ever calls `read_text()` on it. The gate listed it because it was READ this turn. Both files lint clean at 0 findings; 201 and 206 lines, inside the standard's 40-300 and 60-400. title: the test-value measurement he commissioned, with its own first figure withdrawn
verbatim: the test-value measurement he commissioned, with its own first figure withdrawn HIS ORDER: *"y to all three, run the test measurement first."* Done, and the other 2 approved items are NOT built -- `d` is in force on them. THE RESULT. Over 1,702 commits and 571 live test files: 75 have a written record of catching a defect after they already existed (0.1313, Wilson [0.1061, 0.1615]), 95 are named but never in a defect commit (0.1664), and 401 are never named at all (0.7023, Wilson [0.6635, 0.7383]). Cross-verified by an independent instrument -- per-file fixed-string search rather than one regex sweep -- agreeing EXACTLY at 401, with 40 of 40 on a random sample. MY FIRST RUN WAS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN IN THE NOTE. It reported 527 of 571, 0.9229, never named. The pattern was `test_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.py`, which excludes the HYPHEN -- and this project names test files with dates, so every dated test file was invisible to my own regex. It inflated the true figure by 22 percentage points and was withdrawn before he could act on it. AND THE SCRIPT SHIPPED WITH THE UNKNOWN-FLAG DEFECT FOR THE 4TH TIME IN ONE DAY. `--this-flag-does-not-exist` exited 0 AND ran the whole 1,702-commit measurement. The identical fault was found in 3 other scripts this morning and fixed with `scripts/_cli_help.answer_help`; the fix existed and was not reached for. Now wired: exit 2 on an unknown flag, `--help` answered, plain run unchanged. `test_operational_scripts.py` confirms at 668 passed, up from 664. BOTH OF THIS TURN'S ERRORS WERE THE SAME SHAPE as the morning's 4: not using machinery that already existed. The hyphen was in every dated filename in the tree and the CLI helper already carried my own fix. A FOLLOW CONSEQUENCE, FOUND BEFORE COMMITTING RATHER THAN AFTER. `scripts_are_reached_2026-09-11.py` builds its population from `git ls-files`, so an uncommitted script is invisible to it -- which is why the guard named the same 3 unreached files while my own grep found 0 references to the new one. A guard whose value is that nothing ever happened appears in no message, so 401 means UNKNOWN and never useless. The honest target is slow AND unevidenced; this is only the second half, and the first needs a per-file timing run against a 3,468.81 s board. title: the measurement's own instrument is now guarded, and the hyphen defect cannot return
verbatim: the measurement's own instrument is now guarded, and the hyphen defect cannot return The producer shipped with no guard, unlike every other script written today -- an addition nothing executes as a test, which the additive standard names directly. WHAT IT PINS, both of them defects made in the measurement's own first hour. (1) THE HYPHEN: the pattern must match a DATED test filename, which is this project's convention. The first version used `test_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.py`, could not match a single dated file, and reported 527 of 571 never named (0.9229) against a true 401 (0.7023) -- 22 percentage points of instrument artefact, withdrawn before use. A test asserts that EVERY one of the 571 live filenames is matchable at all, so an instrument that cannot see its own population fails loudly. (2) THE UNKNOWN FLAG: `--this-flag-does-not-exist` must exit non-zero rather than running the whole 1,702-commit measurement. AND THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THE FIGURE MEAN ANYTHING: credit requires a commit that names the file, carries defect language, AND is not that file's own creation commit. Without the third condition every test scores on the day it was written. A guard requires the creation-commit mapping to resolve for over 0.8 of live files, so the exclusion cannot silently become a no-op. MUTATION-VERIFIED: reverting to the hyphen-free pattern turns 3 of the 11 red, including the population check. A 4th test asserts the OLD pattern fails on a dated name, so the guard cannot be vacuous if someone widens the class again. The note also has to keep the withdrawn 0.9229 and the "UNKNOWN, not useless" boundary -- asserted, because without the second sentence the 401 reads as a deletion list. 11 tests.
