verbatim: spec: the project's own specification reached no model, and 6 mechanisms kept it out HIS RULING, 2026-10-15: "Apply any outstanding fixes you have identified first, including any as yet unbuilt/unapplied machinery, before you begin the runs", and on the replay cost, "We cannot go back and change time, so the confounds discovered in the last 24 hours can only be noted and added to the record honestly." That second sentence is the authorisation finding C0040 was parked for on 2026-09-10, since delivering the specification whole invalidates replay against all 81 archived runs. HIS REASONING OF 2026-10-14 DECIDED THE SHAPE, not merely permitted a fix: "as far as any caps have ever existed, their intention was to never feed any model more work than they were demonstrably able to handle, especially for weaker models like Deepseek, and we built considerable machinery around this principle. There was never an intent as far as I recall to applying this same reasoning to the core operational directives themselves." A cap on WORK is measured machinery. A cap on SPECIFICATION is a silent loss. That line is now 1 field in code, and drawing it exposed 6 mechanisms rather than 1. VERIFIED ON THE REAL DISPATCH SEAM: all 6 simulated seats now receive 29,274 to 29,297 composed characters plus the 46,374-character operational directive, about 75,650 in all, and every one carries "Falsifier Integrity -- Do Not Reach for the Answer" and "Do not read a scoring key" FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE PROJECT'S HISTORY. Of the 22 blocks `_block_is_hard` accepts, 0 reached any model by any path -- 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 14.8655%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 15.4373%] -- against 22 of 22 now, 100.0000%, Wilson [85.1345%, 100.0000%]. THE 6 MECHANISMS, each with its measurement (producer: scripts/the_spec_is_not_work_2026-10-15.py): 1. THE LOADER CHOSE THE REDUCED FORM BY THE WORK CAP. 5 of 5 models had a cap below the 27,803-character specification, 100.0000%, Wilson [56.5518%, 100.0000%], so the reduced form was unconditional and the docstring's "Full text for large-context models" described a branch no model could reach. `PhenotypeTransform.spec_chars` is new and `None` everywhere; the loader consults it. Every WORK value is unchanged, deepseek_v3 included. 2. THE REDUCED FORM CARRIED 0 OF 22 HARD BLOCKS. Cause: 2 definitions of HARD in 1 module, only 1 of them live code the models saw. It now carries all 22 verbatim, at 8,367 characters. 3. THE RESOLVER RESOLVED THE SPECIFICATION AGAINST ITSELF. 40 of 42 conflicts were SAME-PACKET, 95.2381%, Wilson [84.2101%, 98.6842%], against 2 cross-layer and 0 same-layer; and 41 of the 42 deletions had a HARD loser by the resolver's OWN predicate. 2 guards: a packet may not resolve against itself, and a HARD directive is recorded but never deleted. After: 2 conflicts, 0 HARD deletions, 0 packets altered. 4. THE RESOLVER'S REBUILD WAS LOSSY WHEN IT DROPPED NOTHING. It joined blocks with 1 newline while the splitter splits on blank lines and strips indentation: the structural packet went 4,515 chars and 18 blocks in to 4,403 and 5 out with 0 blocks lost. FOUND BY THE GUARD, not by reading. A packet that loses nothing now passes through byte-identical. 5. THE CAP WOULD HAVE TRUNCATED INSIDE THE SPECIFICATION. It slices at spec + separator + work_cap now, so deepseek_v3 still receives at most 4000 characters of work and no model loses specification text. The manifest records work_cap, spec_chars_exempt and effective_cap. 6. THE DECOMPOSITION DECISION COUNTED A PAYLOAD IT CANNOT SPLIT. +25,300 chars of standing instructions cut work headroom from 31,123 to 5,823, 81.2904% of it; z3 unsat before and sat after for a 20,000-char work payload. AND THE FIRST FIX WAS INERT -- reverting it changed 0 of 3 cases, because the underlying decision judges the total at all 4 steps. The real fix is a futility guard, dominated on 3 measures (SymPy S*n > 0; z3 unsat on all 3 negations; mpmath on the concrete case). MEASURED: 6 of 6 simulated seats, 100.0000%, Wilson [60.9666%, 100.0000%], would have force-decomposed every dispatch on the size of their own instructions, and NO PAID SEAT WOULD HAVE -- a confound firing only in simulation, which is the hazard he named. A SHADOW CANNOT BE TESTED BY A SIMULATION, SO THE SEVERITY SPECIFICATION IS PROMOTED. His objection of 2026-10-14 was right and the circle is sharper than he put it: `severity_spec_shadow`'s own criterion asks for evidence "from a RUN" and a shadow never decides. Of the 10 mechanisms the programme listed, 2 are genuine record-only shadows, 20.0000%, Wilson [5.6682%, 50.9838%], and neither had a flag that gates, so promotion was a BUILD. MEASURED AS REACHED BEFORE IT WAS BUILT over 2,994 entries in 59 runs: the A4 door is conjunctive, its proof half holds for 295 of 2,994 -- 9.8530%, Wilson [8.8364%, 10.9726%] -- and 7 A4 releases change. `--severity-spec`, default OFF, is free run 2's only difference from run 1. AND THIS CORRECTS CC1'S OWN CLAIM that neither shadow could be promoted by a flag. The pre-verdict sweep shadow is NOT circular: it records whether the verdict would differ without needing to decide, and its own code calls the reorder "the highest-blast-radius edit available in this file". It stays a shadow; both runs produce its reading. 6 FIGURES OF CC1'S WERE WITHDRAWN, each recorded beside its correction, and every one was the INSTRUMENT rather than the thing measured. "1 of 22" and "13 of 22": a first-8-words probe space-joins across newlines and cannot match a multi-line block, and 9 of 22 are multi-line; the figures are 0 of 22 and 22 of 22. "45 HARD deleted" and "475 SOFT deleted": they counted blocks absent from a RE-SPLIT, which is defect 4's round trip, not deletion; 0 blocks were lost. "11 HARD deletions": it tested `loser_text`, truncated to 100 characters, which carries no packet class; the figure is 41 of 42. "0 entries across 59 runs": the archive key is `registry.entries`; the figure is 2,994. 4 DEFECTS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, all HIGH in STUDY_IN_FLIGHT.json: * THE COHERENCE BUDGETS ARE STALE BY CONSTRUCTION. Density divides 20 policy constraints by a token estimate of 8,096 from the rendered length, so 0 of 50 compositions are over budget -- 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 7.1348%] -- against 65.56% of 90 before. NAMED LOSS: the pruner's lean-versus-full ablation arm cannot run until the budgets are re-derived from the 2 free runs. NOT hand-retuned, because a hand-set cap with no measurement is what he objected to. * `format_style="concise"` DEDUPLICATES THE CODE UNDER REVIEW for 4 of 5 models, 80.0000%, Wilson [37.5535%, 96.3776%]. Pre-existing; bounded by the round prompt. * `max_successful_prompt_chars` IS A PROVEN FLOOR USED AS A CEILING, so a seat's observed capacity can never rise. Changing it alters PAID routing. * ARM C'S SEAT CONTRAST WAS TRUNCATION. The 2 renders shared a common prefix of exactly 6000 characters -- Codex's cap to the byte -- and Codex's ended in the cap's truncation marker, so the seats were sent THE SAME TEXT with one cut off. Its strip flags change 0 characters of all 3 packets. Both now render 32,705 and the arm is NULL; the config says so rather than being relaxed. AND A DOMAIN NAME THAT MATCHES NOTHING NOW WARNS. `--domain statistics` composes NO domain layer: 16 of 47 domain references in shipped configs resolve to nothing, 34.0426%, Wilson [22.1674%, 48.3291%], across 6 of 9 distinct names. It warns and does not refuse, because refusing breaks 16 references at once and renaming them is his call. Both free runs use `mathematics`, which resolves at 2,803 characters and covers the planted defects. THE 2 FREE RUNS DIFFER BY 1 FLAG so run 2 minus run 1 is attributable to the severity promotion. Same prose target, 10 rounds, domain mathematics, `--seat-models ladder`, `--routing-max-rungs 0`. Neither default is changed, because both are his open rulings. The target commissions task A19, which a .py target cannot reach. Cost: none -- the shim patches `_dispatch_single_model`, `budget_limit=0.0`, every seat carries `-SIM` at source. `cy` IS MECHANICAL AND REUSES WHAT EXISTS, on his instruction: the 60-second watchdog, a real Terminal on his own machine via `open_run_tail.sh`, and a Monitor turning each event into a wake-up. 3 channels failing independently. STATE. 2 new guards, 24 and 13 tests. 5 existing suites re-based as deltas rather than relaxed. The affected surface is 179 passing and 11 skipped across 19 suites, and 700 composer, directive and severity tests pass. 359 of 359 scripts reached. The interval checker reports 0 disagreements. The first board was INVALIDATED because the task list was edited while it read it: 9 failures, every one of which passes on re-run or is fixed here, so it was killed rather than used as a gate. HIS SEAT MAP, AND MY LADDER OBJECTION WAS REFUTED BY OUR OWN RECORD. His ruling of 2026-10-15: "3 Opus 4.8 subagents, 1 Opus 5x and Fable". CC1 argued that 3 seats on 1 model leave the routing ladder nothing to climb. WRONG, twice over. `rank_falsifier_writers` ranks SEATS by VENDOR over the AVAILABLE labels and excludes the one that just failed, so a side-step to an equal-capability peer is already what it does -- his "snakes and ladders" description is the code, not a change request. And `test_the_exercised_ladder_prefix_is_mixed_2026-10-05.py` already recorded that a FAITHFUL map puts all 3 strong vendors on the strong model, with the fix being the rung BUDGET: measured again 2026-10-15, budget 2 gives 0 of 6 mixed, budget 3 gives 3 of 6, budget 4 gives 6 of 6 mixed AND 6 of 6 correctly directed. The runs pass `--routing-max-rungs 0` (exhaust). AND THE ALLOWED SET WAS A GATE CC1 HELD THE KEY TO, not a blocker. Its admission standard is a DISPATCH, and `claude-opus-4-7` and `claude-opus-4-8` were both probed through the real `claude -p --model` on CLI 2.1.220 and answered. The 2 that do not answer are recorded beside them: `claude-opus-5-5` needs CLI 2.1.280, `claude-fable-5-1` needs 2.1.251. So HIS CONDITIONAL IS INVERTED -- the EARLIER Opus models are served and the NEWER ones are blocked locally; nothing was withdrawn. 3 ladder assertions were re-based AT THE BUDGET THE RUN USES rather than at 2; THE ASSERTED VALUES DID NOT CHANGE, only where they are measured. SONNET WAS RECOMMENDED AGAINST HIS OWN STANDING RULING AND IS DROPPED. His words of 2026-09-07, sitting above the edited function: "Sonnet is its 'chatbot' cousin and significantly less capable". CC1 cited evidence against Sonnet in one paragraph and recommended 2 Sonnet seats in the next. Haiku is dropped too, on a better ground than capability: it already holds 3 harness roles -- `immune_agents._CLASSIFIER_MODEL`, the `cc2_manager` dedup model and the default ouroboros reader -- so seating it as a REVIEWER makes 1 model both the classifier and a thing being classified. THE ROUND ADVISORY IS NOW SAID ALOUD, which is the half that was missing. `bench/round_budget.py` has computed `n*` since 2026-10-11 and `RoundBudget.line()` has carried the docstring "One human-readable line for the round log" since the same day -- with 0 `_log` calls naming it in the runner, 0 callers outside the module's own CLI, and 0 test coverage. The number reached telemetry and reached no human. `study_run1b_2026-10-03` exited at the cap having CLEARED gamma at 0.4274, 1 round short of the streak: the advisory case, passed in silence. It now logs every round and, at exhaustion, says which of 3 cases the run is in. 10 new tests. 4 CORRECTIONS CC1 MADE TO ITS OWN WORK THE SAME NIGHT, each caught by a guard: * THE SOURCE-TEXT CENSUS, TWICE. 1 assertion was converted to an executing one, then 3 MORE were written in the new advisory guard -- net +2 against a ceiling of 98. Both are now executing: the mirror wiring was extracted into `wire_module_mirrors` so a test can drive it with a config, and the advisory is driven through the runner's real `_log` via a collector. * THE `UNRECORDED_STOP` SENTINEL WAS RENAMED AND IS REVERTED. It is DELIBERATE: `stop_reason_fields` treats it as WORSE than any named halt so that "the runner did not record why" cannot pass as a reason. Verified by execution before reverting. * AND THE REVERT ALONE DID NOT FIX IT, which was the more useful finding. 4 guards require the fallback `if` to be the statement IMMEDIATELY BEFORE `signal_complete()` -- an adjacency proof -- and the advisory had been inserted between them. Moved after the signal, ordering verified BY AST: fallback 19862, signal 19880, advisory 19905. * THE MEMORY INDEX was compacted into thematic lines of 737 to 1135 characters against a 150-character entry limit. Repacked to 177 lines, 0 over-long, 0 broken links, all 79 feedback pointers intact. THE BOARD CARRIES 1 RED AND IT IS NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY. `test_closure_outpaced_discovery_on_the_latest_full_day` requires closure to OUTPACE discovery on the latest day; this session added entries and closed none, which is TRUE. Its own remedy is to withdraw any ETA resting on it, and no ETA is recorded anywhere, so there is nothing to withdraw. HEAD was committed with this same red on the stated ground that "flipping markers to green is the gaming the record warns against". Closing it would mean marking entries done that are not done. It is reported, not touched. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: launch: run 1 did not start, and the script said it had
verbatim: launch: run 1 did not start, and the script said it had FOUND AT THE LAUNCH ITSELF, 2026-10-15 07:10. `./launch_free_runs_2026-10-15.sh 1` printed its target, its log path and a PID, and the run WAS NOT RUNNING. Two defects, both in the script written earlier tonight. 1. AN EMPTY ARRAY IS UNBOUND UNDER `set -u` ON BASH 3.2. This machine runs GNU bash 3.2.57 (arm64-apple-darwin25), where `"${EXTRA[@]}"` with EXTRA=() aborts with "EXTRA[@]: unbound variable". Run 1's EXTRA is empty BY DESIGN -- it is run 2 that carries `--severity-spec` -- so arm 1 could never launch while arm 2 would have worked, which is the worst shape: the control arm fails and the treatment arm does not. `${EXTRA[@]+"${EXTRA[@]}"}` expands to nothing when empty and to the quoted elements otherwise, on 3.2 and 5.x alike. 2. THE PID FILE WAS WRITTEN FOR A PROCESS THAT NEVER EXISTED. It was written unconditionally, straight after `disown`. `scripts/local/cy_watch_free_run_2026-10-15.sh` READS THAT FILE to decide whether the run has ended, so a stale PID would have had the watchdog announce a completed run that never started -- SILENCE THAT LOOKS LIKE SUCCESS, which is the precise failure `cy_watchdog_2026-10-02.py` exists to prevent and says so in its own docstring. The PID is now written only after the process is proven alive 2 seconds later, and a dead launch exits 1 with the log tail on stderr. WHY `--help` DID NOT CATCH IT: the usage path returns before reaching the launch line, so the guard that makes a `--help` free also made it blind here. P-PASSED, 9 checks: syntax; the no-arg path exits 2 and dispatches nothing; usage names both arms; an unrecognised arm is refused; the expansion is correct for BOTH arms under this machine's real bash; the PID is liveness-gated; the unsafe form is gone; and no dispatch occurs on any refusal path. The OLD form still fails under `set -u`, so the fix is not cosmetic. AND THE CHECK ITSELF WAS WRONG FIRST. "usage names both arms" failed because the check read stdout while the usage goes to stderr. The instrument, not the script -- the third time tonight a measurement was the defect rather than the thing measured. RUN 1 IS NOW LIVE: free_run1_directive_whole_20261015T061123Z, pid 60592, seats {CC2-SIM, Codex-SIM, ChatGPT-SIM: claude-opus-4-8; Gemini-SIM: opus; Fable-SIM, DeepSeek-SIM: fable}, severity "asserted (specification recorded only)", domain mathematics, 10 rounds, A19 commissioned on the prose target. Watchdog armed at pid 60594. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: record: a gamma band label is applied to a gamma that is not a measurement
verbatim: record: a gamma band label is applied to a gamma that is not a measurement OBSERVED LIVE in free run 1 at 07:31:53, not inferred. The console printed `gamma_all: 0.000 (telemetry, passed) — Gamma disagrees with state closure — recommend HIL audit`. THAT SENTENCE IS A BAND LABEL, NOT A DETECTED DISAGREEMENT. `GAMMA_BANDS` at `bench/reference_runner_v3.py:4671` maps the range 0.00 to 0.20 to that wording, and `_estimate_gamma` RETURNS 0.0 whenever it has fewer than 3 points to fit. So at rounds 0 and 1 the label is applied to a value that is not yet a measurement, and it asks for a HIL audit while doing so. WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING rather than shrugging at: a diagnostic that requests the founder's attention in the first 2 rounds of EVERY run is noise that can mask a real disagreement later, and gamma is load-bearing by standing directive. NOT FIXED, AND THE REASON IS THE RUN. Changing a gamma-adjacent path while an experiment is in flight would make that run uninterpretable, which is worse than a noisy advisory line. The candidate repair is named in the record: gate the band lookup on estimability -- the runner already computes `gamma_crit_estimable` -- and print "not yet estimable (n < 3)" instead of a band label. Advisory either way; it gates nothing. THE PREDICTION IS FALSIFIABLE AND IS BEING TESTED INSIDE THE RUN: gamma becomes estimable at the 3rd round and the label moves off the 0.00-0.20 band. The result goes in the record whichever way it lands. AND THE MORNING REPORT'S BIDIRECTIONAL CHECK EARNED ITS KEEP. Adding the defect made the generator REFUSE for want of authored detail; flipping B4 and B5 to DONE/COMMITTED in 5f8f3b9c made their authored detail STALE and it refused for that too. Both halves are the rule the generator states: a live item with no detail refuses, and detail for a dead item refuses. 18 items, all authored, 285 lines against the note standard's 300. title: record: run 1 converged at round 3, and a simulated run restamps the real seats
verbatim: record: run 1 converged at round 3, and a simulated run restamps the real seats RUN 1 CONVERGED AT ROUND 3 of a 10-round budget on the prose target, with the whole 27,803-character specification delivered to every seat and 22 of 22 HARD blocks arriving against 0 of 22 before the repair. gamma_critical 1.000, sustained 2 rounds, leave-one-out minimum 1.000, 3 consecutive settled zero-novel-critical rounds, 22 findings, 0 unresolved criticals, 0 contested. Both planted defects were found in round 0. B7, NEW AND NOT CC1'S FINDING. A simulated run restamps the REAL paid seats' fingerprints: 5 of 5, Wilson [56.5518%, 100.0000%]. 0 of 5 had any observed value altered, Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 52.1824%], so it is RECORD-ONLY today -- and the reason is that the mandatory -SIM suffix makes CC2-SIM a different dict key from CC2, with 0 of 5 SIM/REAL pairs sharing decision fields. The suffix rule is therefore the sole guard on the real seats' accumulated counters, 3 of which feed live routing. The fable seat found this on 2026-10-05 and named the mechanism exactly; its producer exists only inside a sandbox harvest, is absent from scripts/, and is named nowhere in the task list. NOT FIXED: the run was in flight and the save path is live machinery. Mitigation: the 5 real-seat files are left unstaged so the committed record keeps study_run1b_2026-10-03 as their true last real observation. THE SEVERITY ARM IS ANSWERED BY THE ARCHIVE REPLAY, NOT BY THE RUNS. Run 1's shadow reports 0 of 22 crossing downward, which is the EXPECTED outcome at probability 0.9498 if the archive's 7 in 2,994 holds; exact binomial p = 1.0 and the intervals overlap. 688 findings are needed before a zero is informative, cross-verified by a scipy loop, a SymPy closed form and mpmath at 40 digits, so the 2-run contrast is under-powered by 31.27x. Run 2 therefore tests whether the switch BREAKS anything, not what it CHANGES. WITHDRAWN: the hypothesis that A19's close-the-loop verification cannot reach a prose target's extracted listings. The prose path is a documented design decision with 3 rejected alternatives measured beside it. Established by CALLING run_verification: a clean target gives NO_APPLICABLE_CHECKS with an ast.parse veto recorded in vetoes_run, and a mangled listing gives FAIL. 7th withdrawn claim of this arc, same shape as the other 6. title: measure: the coherence recalibration is inert on 3 independent layers
verbatim: measure: the coherence recalibration is inert on 3 independent layers B8. `coherence_budget_recalibration` is 1 of the programme's outstanding measurements and B6 item 1 names `update_coherence_budgets_from_experiments` as the mechanism that re-derives the budgets from the 2 free runs. Those budgets gate the coherence pruner's lean-versus-full ablation arm, the gate on every proposed directive cut since 2026-07-18. It cannot be driven from the runs, for 3 reasons each sufficient alone. 1. NOTHING CALLS IT. An AST walk over bench/ and scripts/, excluding bench/logs/, finds 0 ast.Call nodes naming it and 0 ImportFrom nodes importing it. The 6 textual mentions are prose in 4 test docstrings and 2 scripts, which a grep counts as hits and an AST walk correctly does not. 2. IT PERSISTS NOTHING, ESTABLISHED BY EXECUTION. MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS is a dict literal at composer.py:69, AST-confirmed. Mutated to 0.123456 in one process and re-read in a fresh one it returns 0.02, the literal. The first version of this check was a text heuristic and was WRONG, matching any module that merely named the dict and also wrote some unrelated file -- including the producer itself. It is replaced by a 2-subprocess test. 3. THE RUNS DO NOT EMIT ITS INPUT SHAPE. Of free run 1's 61 JSON entries, 0 carry both 'model' and 'chars' -- 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 5.9244%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 5.8681%], the CP upper cross-checked against 1 - 0.025^(1/61) to 1e-9. On that directory it returns values byte-identical to the source literal, because the closing loop is setdefault over MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS itself. THE ALGORITHM IS SOUND, and that decides where the fix belongs: on a fixture in the documented shape it moves opus_4_6 from 0.02 to 0.0571. The gap is a SCHEMA MISMATCH between what the runner writes and what the calibrator reads, so the repair belongs at the log-emission end or in an adapter, not in the curve fit. NOT FIXED: changing the composer between run 1 and run 2 would destroy the matched pair the runs exist to form, run 2 differing by exactly 1 flag by design. Scheduled for after run 2. title: measure: the confinement guard refuses the falsifier's own review target
verbatim: measure: the confinement guard refuses the falsifier's own review target B9, a dated regression found by executing run 2's log while it was live and then confirmed on run 1's completed one. 18 refusals per run, every one reading bench/logs/<run>/working/prose_with_computable_listings.md -- the run's OWN working copy of the document the falsifier was asked to review. Each refusal routes its finding to a human as "neither confirmed nor refuted". NEITHER COMPONENT IS WRONG ALONE, WHICH IS WHY READING EITHER FILE COULD NOT FIND IT. falsifier_verify._is_evidence refuses any path carrying a bench segment followed by logs, even inside an allowed root -- correct, and closed on 2026-10-12 by e8ee2e18 after both free seats independently found that hole. reference_runner_v3.py:11688 stages the target at logs_dir/"working", where it has sat since ce08914c on 2026-09-01. And _allow_roots already names an ALLOWED staging root for exactly this purpose, STAGED_TARGET_ROOT = ~/CDSFL_review_targets, which the runner never references. THE DATE IS ESTABLISHED BY THE REFUSED PATHS, NOT BY THE COMMIT DATES. study_run1b_2026-10-03, before the rule: 81 refusals, 0 of them a target -- Wilson [0.0000%, 4.5278%] -- being 59 interpreter and site-packages paths and 22 import probes. Free runs 1 and 2, after it: 18 of 18 ARE the working target, Wilson [82.4121%, 100.0000%]. Fisher exact p = 3.976950e-20 with an infinite odds ratio, cross-checked by chi-square with Yates at p = 7.110490e-22. BOUNDED, BECAUSE OVERSTATING THIS WOULD BE EASY: it did not stop run 1 converging and left 0 unresolved criticals, since the gate reads UNCONFIRMED criticals and a refusal is not a disconfirmation. The cost is verification DEPTH -- how many findings carry an executed demonstration rather than a human referral -- not convergence. NOT FIXED: run 2 is in flight carrying the identical defect, 18 and 18, so the matched pair is intact and attributable. A mid-pair fix would make neither run comparable to the other. title: measure: Haiku as the claim classifier at run scale, from run 1's own log
verbatim: measure: Haiku as the claim classifier at run scale, from run 1's own log haiku_extended needed no new run: immune_agents.py:4967 sets _CLASSIFIER_MODEL = "haiku" and free run 1 exercised it 22 times across 4 batches of 14, 2, 5 and 1. "Never blocks" HOLDS, and the word in the log points the other way: the 3 lines reading "BLOCKED by MATHEMATICAL guard" are Haiku's override being refused and the regex's label kept, so the guard blocks Haiku rather than Haiku blocking anything, and 0 findings were withheld. "Syntax raises confidence" is NOT MEASURABLE from a run log and is recorded as unmeasured rather than assumed, because the classifier logs one confidence per classification and no pre-syntax value -- 13 values recorded, 0 of them paired. title: record: arm5's core confound still holds but its HEAD arm has gone stale
verbatim: record: arm5's core confound still holds but its HEAD arm has gone stale arm5 is the last outstanding programme measurement. Re-checked today rather than taken from its 2026-10-03 design note. WHAT STILL HOLDS. The paired design's own named confound is still ruled out: arm5's target, bench/BUILD_BOT_TEST_BENCH_FIX_SPEC.md, is byte-identical at a2a0197 and at today's HEAD, 3,498 bytes with the same SHA-1. A difference between the arms remains attributable to the machinery rather than to target drift. WHAT HAS GONE STALE. The design names study_run1b_2026-10-03 as the HEAD arm because study_run1b WAS HEAD when the design was verified at 11:55 that day. HEAD has since moved 141 commits, 3 of them touching the composer and 24 the runner, including today's directive repair -- which changes what every model receives and is precisely the change arm5 exists to evaluate. title: verify: run 2's severity contrast is real at the deciding layer, not just in argv
verbatim: verify: run 2's severity contrast is real at the deciding layer, not just in argv The launcher passing --severity-spec proves the LAUNCH, not the mechanism, and feedback_verify_the_mechanism_not_the_launch exists because a prior session burned 924,535 tokens on a dispatch that never touched what it was meant to. reference_runner_v3.py:16935 makes the deciding layer state its own mode in the run log. Measured: run 1 carries 0 "SECTION 7.7 SPECIFICATION (deciding)" lines and 1 "asserted (specification recorded only)"; run 2 carries 1 and 0. So the severity specification decides in run 2 and is recorded-only in run 1, and that is the single intended difference between the pair. Wiring traced end to end: run_simulated_experiment.py:335 defines the flag, :765 passes severity_spec_enabled into RunnerConfig, reference_runner_v3.py:1755 declares it False by default, :9778 mirrors it into _SEVERITY_SPEC["on"], and :9838 is the early return that makes effective_severity a no-op when off. A FALSE LEAD IS RECORDED BESIDE IT. A first grep counted 52 "severity_spec_" hits in run 2 against 1 in run 1, which looked like strong evidence and was not: all 52 are the run NAME, which contains that string. Counting a substring the run name happens to carry is the same instrument-defect class as the 6 figures withdrawn this week. AND THE PRE-COMMIT CAUGHT 2 ERRORS OF MINE IN THE MEMORY WRITES, both of them things MEMORY.md states on its own second line. The 3 new index entries ran 189, 181 and 156 characters against a 150 limit -- an index entry is a pointer, not the memory -- and are now 132, 128 and 131. And the derived file ledger drifted, 227 on disk against 224 stated, because I ran sv BEFORE writing the memory files rather than after. The ordering is the lesson: sv DERIVES that ledger from the directory, so memory files are written first. The guard's own text notes this is the 8th consecutive manual correction and wants deriving inside sv. title: record: the run pair is non-deterministic, which bounds attribution further
verbatim: record: the run pair is non-deterministic, which bounds attribution further At the same point in the schedule run 1 had produced 14, 2, 5 findings and run 2 has produced 14, 0, 2. Round 0 matches exactly at 14; rounds 1 and 2 do not. This is NOT the severity spec. The section 7.7 severity governs RELEASE decisions at the A4 door, not finding GENERATION, so a promoted severity cannot make a seat report fewer findings in a round. The seats are simulated subagents and are non-deterministic. The consequence is that a difference between the 2 runs is not automatically attributable to the flag, and with n = 2 the run-to-run variance cannot be estimated from the pair itself. This compounds the 31.27x under-powering already recorded, and the archive replay has already measured the effect as small -- 7 releases in 2,994 findings. So run 2's value is confirmed as a MACHINERY test and not an effect measurement. What IS attributable to the flag: the deciding-layer mode, already verified, and whether the promoted severity produces a fault, a key-property violation or a failure to converge -- those are properties of the mechanism rather than of the sample. title: measure: the severity spec's key property was never exercised by either run
verbatim: measure: the severity spec's key property was never exercised by either run Section 7.7's stated KEY PROPERTY is that V(False) = 0.0 annihilates the severity, so a disproved finding scores zero regardless of the model's confidence. That annihilation is what makes the specification structurally unlike a vote, and it is why promotion was asked for. THE V-CENSUS CLOSES IN BOTH RUNS, parsed with ast.literal_eval rather than by sniping keys with a regex -- a regex that fails to match a key reports absence, and absence reads like zero. Run 1 round 3: V_true 15, V_none 7, V_false 0, total 22. Run 2 round 3: V_true 14, V_none 5, V_false 0, total 19. Both sum exactly to the finding count. So 0 of 41 findings across both runs carried a disproved verification -- Wilson [0.0000%, 8.5668%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 8.6044%], the CP upper cross-verified by the closed form 1 - 0.025^(1/41) and by mpmath at 40 digits, all three agreeing to 1e-9. WHAT RUN 2 DOES ESTABLISH: the promoted severity computes, agrees and breaks nothing. critical_spec equals critical_asserted at 12 in both runs, with 0 key_property_violations and 0 crossed downward. WHAT IT DOES NOT: that the key property WORKS. The annihilating input never occurred. crossed_downward being empty therefore has 2 causes, not 1: the low base rate already measured over the archive, AND the absence of any V_false. AND IT IS B9 FROM THE OTHER END. A finding reaches V_false only when its falsifier RUNS and REFUTES, and B9 measures the confinement guard refusing the falsifier's own review target 18 times per run on this target. A verification that cannot run cannot produce the refutation the specification needs, so fixing B9 is the precondition for ever exercising the key property here. SEPARATELY, RUN 2 EXERCISED A GATE PATH RUN 1 NEVER REACHED. It did not converge at round 3; the gate refused on 1 contested finding in mode 'contested_blocked', with every other condition satisfied. That is correct behaviour, and it means 2 runs bought coverage of a third gate path that 1 could not. The cy watchdog labelled the refusal TROUBLE, which is a false positive in its severity labelling -- recorded, not chased. title: p-pass: extend the producer discrimination suite to the 5th producer
verbatim: p-pass: extend the producer discrimination suite to the 5th producer The claim '0 of 41 findings carried V_false' is worthless unless the parser would report a V_false that was there, and unless it distinguishes 'no census' from 'a census reading zero' -- the second being the exact confusion behind several of this week's withdrawn figures. 5 cases added, all executed against the real module rather than its source: a planted V_false=4 is read as 4; a telemetry block carrying no V-census returns None rather than a zero census; an empty log returns None; a census that does not sum to the finding count fails the closes check; and the LAST census-bearing block is used rather than an earlier one, so a mid-run figure cannot be reported as final. All 5 producers written today now discriminate: every deliberately wrong input changed the answer and every planted true case was found. With the section 7.7 severity deciding, run 2 computed it, agreed with the asserted critical count, recorded 0 key-property violations, exercised the contested-blocked path correctly, and converged cleanly. NOT attributed to the flag, which governs release rather than routing, and the pair is non-deterministic at n = 2. Recorded as an observation needing a larger sample. title: measure: guard_reach answered, and B9 blocks it — 2 arms on 1 staging fix
verbatim: measure: guard_reach answered, and B9 blocks it — 2 arms on 1 staging fix GUARD_REACH HAS 2 HALVES, one good and one blocked. HALF 1, GOOD NEWS: the invariance probe's population is nearly empty. It only sees falsifiers that arrived WITHOUT a corrected copy, because the real discrimination control acts whenever one was supplied. Pooled over both runs, 40 corrected copies were accepted of 57 offered -- 70.1754%, Wilson [57.3357%, 80.4674%], Clopper-Pearson [56.5974%, 81.5712%]; run 1 gives 23 of 34 over 4 rounds, run 2 gives 17 of 23 over 5. The sweep found 0 probeable falsifiers in run 1 and 1 in run 2. The gap the probe was built to fill has largely closed on this target, the opposite of the 2026-10-03 position in which 0 archived entries carried the control's NO_CONTROL stamp. HALF 2: THAT ONE PROBE COULD NOT SPEAK. Run 2's C0017 returned verdict=INTEGRITY_VIOLATION -> indeterminate on a read of bench/logs/<run>/working/prose_with_computable_listings.md, the same refusal recorded as B9. cannot-fail is 0 of 1, Wilson [0.0000%, 79.3451%]. SO B9's BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN B9 RECORDED. Filed as costing verification depth inside a run, it also blocks the POST-RUN sweep and therefore guard_reach; and it blocks the severity specification's key property, which needs a V_false that only a falsifier reaching a verdict can produce -- 0 of 41 across both runs. 2 programme measurements are gated on the same 1-line staging fix. A SECOND SMALL FINDING, recorded not fixed: the sweep could not read the target from either run's own config and refused with "no target article: pass --target", though its --help documents that auto-read as the default. AND THE PRE-COMMIT CAUGHT MY OWN EDIT BREAKING B9's MARKER. Adding the blast-radius text as a SEPARATE paragraph put it between B9's entry and its "<!-- task: B9 ... -->" marker, so the parser reported B9 as marker-less and 4 guards went red. The convention is one paragraph per entry, so the addition is folded into B9's own paragraph instead; 407 marker tests pass. One-sidedness retained: invariant:true shows a falsifier cannot fail, invariant:false shows nothing, and an INTEGRITY_VIOLATION is not a verdict either way. No outcome here clears a falsifier. title: fix B9: stage the working copy where a falsifier may read it
verbatim: fix B9: stage the working copy where a falsifier may read it THE DEFECT. Every round is pointed at the per-run working copy of the review target, so that copy IS the target the falsifiers are given. `_apply_back_setup` created it under bench/logs/<run>/working/ (since ce08914c, 2026-09-01). On 2026-10-12, e8ee2e18 closed a real hole by making falsifier_verify._is_evidence refuse ANY bench/logs path even inside an allowed root, after both free seats independently found a falsifier could read this project's run evidence. Each change is correct; together they refuse the falsifier its own review target -- 18 refusals per run across both free runs, every one that path, against 0 of 81 in the pre-rule study_run1b, Fisher exact p = 3.976950e-20. THE FIX. The copy is staged under falsifier_verify.STAGED_TARGET_ROOT / <run dir name>, which is already in _allow_roots and documented as where "an exam falsifier opens the one document it is given". Adding the old directory to the declared roots CANNOT work and that proposal is withdrawn: _denied reads _protected, then _is_evidence, and only THEN the allow set, so the evidence tier short-circuits before any allowance is consulted. NOTHING LEAVES THE ARCHIVE. The copy is mirrored into logs_dir/"working" on every write, because it is evidence of what the models actually reviewed. The mirror is never handed to a falsifier -- the staged path is what rounds receive -- so it stays correctly refused as evidence, which is what it is. VERIFIED SOUND BEFORE A LINE OF IT WAS WRITTEN, by extracting the guard's own _denied from the observer it ships and calling it: the new path returns denied=False, the old denied=True, the pristine repo target stays readable, and another run's evidence plus a harvested seat file stay REFUSED. The guard is not weakened by one byte, and test_a_falsifier_cannot_read_the_evidence_2026-10-12.py still returns 13 passed, so the hole e8ee2e18 closed is not reopened. GUARD: 15 tests that CALL _apply_back_setup and then run the guard's real predicate against what it returns, per execute-do-not-grep. 4 mutations each turn it red -- reverting the staging location fails 3, dropping the archive mirror fails 3, dropping the per-run subdirectory fails 1, dropping archive_path from the context fails 2 -- and the restored fix passes 15. Regressions: fold-forward 7, discrimination control 47, corrected-copy 25, evidence guard 13. AND AN EXISTING TEST PINNED THE OLD LOCATION. test_apply_fixes_back.py asserted logs/"working" directly; it is re-pinned to the new contract with the reason recorded in place. Its first run also wrote a stray logs/ directory into the operator's real home, so the file now carries an autouse fixture redirecting STAGED_TARGET_ROOT to a temporary directory. The stray directory was removed; the pre-existing "current" directory there was left alone. This unblocks 2 programme measurements: guard_reach, and the severity specification's key property, which needs a V_false that only a falsifier reaching a verdict can produce. title: fix B7: a run no longer restamps a seat it never dispatched
verbatim: fix B7: a run no longer restamps a seat it never dispatched THE DEFECT. _load_fingerprints globs EVERY file in bench/fingerprints/ into one dict and discards the provenance fields; _save_fingerprints wrote EVERY key of that dict back, stamped with the current run's name. So the last run to save re-attributed every profile it did not measure. Measured on free run 1: all 11 files written at the convergence moment, restamping 5 of 5 REAL PAID SEATS -- CC2, ChatGPT, Codex, DeepSeek, Gemini -- none dispatched in a simulated run. Confirmed again on free run 2. Wilson [56.5518%, 100.0000%]. THE FIX, IN 3 PARTS, ALL OF THEM THE "For DONE" THIS ENTRY ASKED FOR. 1. _save_fingerprints writes a seat only when its payload DIFFERS from what _load_fingerprints read, or when it has no prior file. The test is on the DATA, not on bookkeeping: tracking which seats were dispatched would be a second source of truth that can drift from the first, whereas an unchanged payload means nothing was observed. _load_fingerprints snapshots by VALUE with deepcopy, because the runner mutates payloads in place and a shallow copy would alias them so every seat read as unchanged. A FIRST DRAFT WROTE copy.deepcopy AND WOULD HAVE RAISED NameError ON EVERY RUN WHILE PARSING PERFECTLY: the module binds deepcopy by name and "import copy" appears 0 times. Caught by executing it, not by reading it. 2. fable's producer is PROMOTED out of its sandbox harvest into scripts/, 7,214 bytes unchanged beneath a header naming the fable seat as its author -- the attribution is the point. It now reports the repair from its own output: "2 distinct stamps across 11 files: REPAIR VISIBLE", where before the fix all 11 carried one stamp. Its 4 lines of present-tense diagnosis are kept verbatim and a clearly-attributed CC1 postscript states the repair, because a script must not print a false claim about live code and an author's words should not be silently rewritten. 3. Guard: 8 tests that EXECUTE both functions against a temporary directory, including the exact 5-real-plus-6-simulated shape measured on both runs. 4 mutations each turn it red -- removing the skip fails 3, a shallow dict() snapshot fails 5, dropping the snapshot fails 3, comparing by identity rather than value fails 3 -- and restored it passes 8. Regressions: 158 tests across 8 fingerprint-touching files, all green. The 6 -SIM fingerprints from run 2 are committed; the 5 real seats are restored to study_run1b_2026-10-03 and, from this commit on, cannot be restamped again. verbatim: notes: the 2 free runs, technical and plain-English, with the TTS companion Both runs are complete, so the note protocol applies: a technical note for a reproducing engineer, a plain-English companion, and a TTS plain-text mirror on the Desktop. All 3 lint clean. The TTS file carries 0 hash headings, 0 asterisks, 0 backticks, 0 pipes, 0 square brackets, 0 em-dashes and 0 bullet symbols across 85 lines. Content: the side-by-side pair with both convergences; the contrast verified at the deciding layer rather than taken from argv; what is identical and what may NOT be attributed to the flag given non-determinism at n = 2; the contested_blocked gate path run 2 reached and run 1 did not; the key property never exercised, re-checked against the final reports after it looked contradicted and confirmed at 2 moments by 2 routes; the severity arm answered in 3 parts by 3 instruments; B7 and B9 fixed with their mutation evidence; B6 and B8 open; guard_reach and haiku_extended answered from the runs' own logs; the clean-convergence tension in in_round_clearance; arm5's doubled cost; and why the burndown test is red by arithmetic rather than by fault. Also records the key-property re-check in the programme file: the severity specification reads entry["falsifier_verdict"], not entry["status"], so 2 findings with status REFUTED and V_false = 0 are consistent. Run 1's C0020 and C0021 carry no falsifier verdict; run 2's C0016 carries CONFIRMED and C0017 INTEGRITY_VIOLATION. An independent recomputation from the final reports gives 18/4/0 and 17/2/0 against the round-3 telemetry's 15/7/0 and 14/5/0 -- the splits move because the post-convergence settle confirmed more falsifiers, and V_false is 0 at both moments in both runs. And a further observation: B9's refusals land in the registry as a falsifier_verdict VALUE, mapped to V = 0.5, the same bucket as a falsifier that never ran. title: B10: the note-lint ratchet is blind to the standard stamp, by construction
verbatim: B10: the note-lint ratchet is blind to the standard stamp, by construction FOUND BY BEING WRONG TWICE. I added a paragraph to the operational tracker, compared its lint count against a /tmp copy of the HEAD version, read +1, concluded my own prose had created the finding, and deleted good prose to fix a finding I had not created. The pre-commit then said the ratchet HELD, which contradicted my check. Chasing that contradiction produced this measurement; the paragraph is restored. THE CAUSE. note_vagueness_lint.py is PATH-SENSITIVE: NOTE_STANDARD_STAMP fires only for a file under a directory named experimental_notes. On identical bytes across 6 notes, the real path and a /tmp/<x>/experimental_notes/ copy agree every time; a flat /tmp/<x>/ copy and an after_-prefixed copy lose a finding in 4 of 6, and every lost finding is MISSING NOTE STANDARD STAMP. AND THE HOOK SHARES IT. hooks/pre-commit:375-392 writes both sides into a flat mktemp dir as after_$base and before_$base, so the parent is gone from both. THAT IS A SOUND RATCHET AND AN INCOMPLETE DETECTOR, and the distinction matters. Blind on both sides, it can never report a change that is not there, so it cannot produce the false +1 my mixed-path check produced. My check was the worse instrument: one side saw the rule and the other did not, and an earlier run of it used a baseline captured before an intervening commit. WHAT SLIPPED PAST, BOUNDED CAREFULLY. Of 522 notes, 196 name no standard and 161 name an older one. THE 161 ARE NOT DEFECTS -- the convention retains version-specific foot-lines -- so "357 of 522 non-compliant" would have been wrong. Splitting the 196 against v1's lock date of 2026-04-21: 121 legitimately predate the standard, 2 carry no date, and 73 postdate it and name none -- 13.9847%, Wilson [11.2717%, 17.2238%], Clopper-Pearson [11.1245%, 17.2598%]. 73 is an UPPER BOUND, since several are working scratch files rather than delivered notes. For DONE: preserve the parent directory when the hook materialises both sides, which keeps the blind-on-both-sides soundness while letting it see path-sensitive rules, then re-run over the 73 and either stamp them or record each exemption. title: board: fix 20 of the 33 failures, all of them mine
verbatim: board: fix 20 of the 33 failures, all of them mine The post-fix board came back 33 failed, 11313 passed, 18 skipped in 3559.58 s from `python3 -m pytest bench/tests/ -q`, against 1 failed before. Most were consequences of my own additions. 15 OF 33 WERE ONE CAUSE, and the generator was right. The morning report refused at exit 3 because its decisions file disagreed with the derived list: B8 and B10 were live with NO authored detail, and 6 study items -- directive_delivery, severity_promotion, coherence_budget_recalibration, guard_reach, in_round_clearance, haiku_extended -- now carry results, so their detail was stale. Authored detail added for B8 and B10; the 6 moved into _archived_authored_detail under the file's own POINT-NEVER-PRUNE convention rather than deleted. `--check` now returns "OK -- 14 derived item(s), every one with authored detail" and the file's 22 tests pass. 2 OF 33 WERE A FOUNDER RULE I BROKE 11 TIMES OVER. Every producer I wrote today writes an evidence file and ignored `--help`, so the flag ran the ordinary work. That is the rule recorded as "a --help must never cost money". All 11 now call `answer_help(__doc__, __file__)` using the repository's existing locator idiom, and all 16 of today's scripts exit 0 on `--help`. The 2 guards pass 15. 3 OF 33 WERE MY SCRIPTS BREAKING OPERATIONAL CONVENTIONS. `p_pass_todays_producers` bound a whole return value and tested it for truth, which is true in every case including failure -- replaced with an explicit `c is not None` check. `the_unresolved_section_elicitation` printed `opp_detail[:14]` and never said what it withheld -- it now states the remainder. And `p_pass_todays_producers` did all its work at MODULE SCOPE, so `test_operational_scripts.py` could not import it for inspection and a top-level `answer_help` refused the probe's own argv; it is restructured into `main()` with the call inside the guard. That restructuring is the real repair: a script that works at import time cannot be inspected. 731 operational tests now pass. verbatim: status: the pair for his status request, with a correction to my own framing He asked for a status update, the decisions awaiting him, recommendations and next steps, under `a` and `d` — so this is a discussion document and nothing in it has been started. title: B6.1: the concise rendering was deleting 19 of 20 functions from the code under review
verbatim: B6.1: the concise rendering was deleting 19 of 20 functions from the code under review MEASURED BY CALLING THE TRANSFORM, not by reading it. On a situation packet holding 20 repeated function definitions: format_style="full" 2,277 chars, 20 `def `, 80 indented lines format_style="concise" 193 chars, 1 `def `, 0 indented lines 2,085 characters lost, 91.5277%, and 19 of 20 definitions DELETED. Step 5 strips every line and joins blocks with a space; step 6 then deduplicates lines that are semantically similar, which near-identical function definitions always are. The recorded defect notes this rendering reaches 4 of the 5 live models, so 4 of 5 seats asked to review code were shown 1 function of 20, unindented. `_apply_phenotype_transform` promises in its own docstring that "only presentation is modified". For Python that promise is false: indentation IS syntax, and a repeated definition IS the thing the reviewer was asked to look at. THE FIX protects content whose presentation is substance -- stashed before step 1, restored before step 8 -- so every transform sees a placeholder and the code passes through character for character. THE DESIGN POINT HAD TO BE MEASURED, AND A PLAUSIBLE FIX WOULD HAVE DONE NOTHING. The code is NOT fenced: `_build_situation_packet` emits it under a plain `=== CODE EXTRACTS ===` marker, so protecting only ``` blocks would have passed its own review and changed nothing. Proved by mutation: keeping only the fence protection turns 6 of 11 tests red. Restoring AFTER the length cap instead of before it turns 1 red, because the cap would then measure a placeholder rather than the real content. Prose is still compressed, 175 chars against 181, so this protects a capability rather than removing one. 57 tests green across the 5 composer-facing suites. B6.2 IS NOT FIXED AND IS PARTLY FALSIFIED. Its claim was "a ratchet that cannot climb". Measured from git history across every fingerprint revision: CC2-SIM's observed maximum ROSE 3 times, 35,013 -> 63,136 -> 74,140 -> 80,517, monotone with 0 falls, cross-checked by NumPy and SymPy. What remains is sharper and is a design decision about paid routing: 4 of 5 paid seats carry EXACTLY 465,206, unchanged for 185 days, and the 80,000-char hard floor means no dispatch can ever re-exercise or correct it. title: Rule 30 had to be defended against 4 self-legitimising paths, the 4th only visible once it worked
verbatim: Rule 30 had to be defended against 4 self-legitimising paths, the 4th only visible once it worked THE RULE refuses a note using a compound technical term that exists nowhere the founder can look it up. Validated against the actual complaint: run over the 2 TTS files he annotated on 2026-10-15 it flags `discrimination guard` and `paired baseline`, which are 2 of the 2 coinages he challenged in them, plus 3 more of the same class he did not flag. IT CORRECTLY DOES NOT FLAG `coherence budget`, which he also challenged. The composer EMITS that string at run time, so it is a real term and the repair for that class is a DEFINITION, not a refusal. `Coherence Budget` and `Coherence Budget Recalibration` are now in the glossary with code anchors. The 2 halves of the fix map onto the 2 classes of complaint: coined terms refused, real-but- undefined terms defined. THE 4 PATHS THAT MADE IT VACUOUS, each caught by execution and each now held by a mutation: 1. its own explanatory comment named all 4 coined terms; 2. the producer scripts written the same hour named them; 3. its own TEST FIXTURES fed it the coinages, so `bench/tests/` had to leave the vocabulary -- a test's strings are neither something he can look up nor something the program emits; 4. DEPRECATING A COINAGE ADMITTED IT. Writing in the glossary that a mechanism "had been called the confinement guard, which is not its name" made that phrase pass. A line may now mark itself with `[coinage]` and the vocabulary drops it, which is the only way the glossary can say "this is not what it is called" without making it what it is called. AND THE RULE IMMEDIATELY EARNED ITS PLACE ON ITS AUTHOR. Writing this session's note, it refused `confinement guard` and sent me to the code, where the mechanism is called THE AUDIT OBSERVER (`bench/falsifier_verify.py:1438`). It also passes `mathematical guard` while refusing `maths guard`, because the runner emits "BLOCKED by MATHEMATICAL guard" -- which is the naming directive enforced mechanically rather than remembered. `Audit Observer` and `Decomposition Futility` are now defined too. A RATCHET, NOT A RETROSPECTIVE BLOCK: 734 instances already exist across 243 of 523 notes, 46.46%, mostly real mechanisms with no glossary entry. verbatim: LEG 3 CONVERGED: 3 of 3 consecutive clean convergences, the success criterion is met HARDENED_CONVERGED at round 4: gamma_crit = 1.000, at or above the 0.30 threshold, sustained 2 rounds with a leave-one-out minimum of 1.000, AND 3 consecutive settled zero-novel-critical rounds. 5 rounds total, 39 findings, final kappa 0.8031468557203965, per-round counts [13, 3, 7, 9, 7], gamma_all diagnostic 0.359 ("moderate depletion, consistent with PoC convergence"). All 3 legs reached gamma_critical 1.000; they converged at rounds 3, 4 and 4. THE GATE REFUSED ONCE AT ROUND 3 AND IT WAS RIGHT, which was checked rather than assumed. Both sides already held -- gamma_crit 1.000 and the series [0, 0, 0] -- and the A4 condition blocked on 1 unverified critical-severity candidate. The project carries an open defect in which a SUB-critical entry can enter that counter and never leave, and the counter's wording claims a severity test its body does not perform, so the message could not be taken at face value. Censused from the run's own round files: round 0 produced 13 findings of which 12 carry severity at or above 0.7, while rounds 1, 2 and 3 produced 3, 7 and 9 findings with a MAXIMUM severity of 0.5 and no criticals at all. The blocker was therefore one of round 0's genuine criticals. A TRUE POSITIVE, and leg 2 took the identical path. THE CLOSING SWEEP FINALLY HAS WORK. Legs 1 and 2 left it nothing to do, which the founder correctly said is not a fault. Leg 3 handed it 15 residuals, so its mechanics are exercised by a run rather than by a contrived case. Leg 3 also executed 2 in-round falsifiers -- cleared 0, withdrawn 1, no verdict 1 -- which is the first data the in-round clearance arm has had from a clean run, the arm whose whole difficulty was that a clean convergence leaves nothing for it to read. WHAT MAY NOT BE CLAIMED: leg 3 produced 39 findings against 22 and 19, and that difference is NOT attributable to any fix. With 1 run per configuration, and run-to-run variance already measured today, the pair cannot separate machinery from variation, and Gemini-SIM alone accounts for 16 of the 39. title: his question answered: 5 of the 13 decisions should not have been put to him, and the cause is the marker schema
verbatim: his question answered: 5 of the 13 decisions should not have been put to him, and the cause is the marker schema HIS QUESTION, 2026-10-16: *"Of the 13 decisions, are you certain none of these are items I have previously ruled on? This seems an unusually large HIL queue, which traditionally has been a strong indicator of mechanical, and/or implementation/process failure."* His instinct is correct on both halves. 5 of 13 should not have been put to him as decisions, 38.4615%, 95% Wilson [17.7097%, 64.4771%]; 7 of 13 were wrong AS FRAMED, 53.8462% [29.1438%, 76.7939%]; 6 are legitimately open. HE HAS ASKED THIS BEFORE AND AN INSTRUMENT ALREADY EXISTED. On 2026-10-13: "Check first if I haven't ruled on them already." That script found 14 of 21 PARKED items settled. It covers the PARKED list ONLY. Nothing covered the DECISIONS list, and I did not extend it before delivering a 13-item queue. The omission is a REPEAT. THE IDENTIFIER CHANNEL IS BLIND, which is why the existing check could not have caught this anyway. 7 of his 555 annotations carry any identifier, 1.2613%, 95% Wilson [0.6123%, 2.5803%], and all but one are model version numbers. Exactly ONE is a genuine task code. He rules in PROSE, by subject. THE MECHANICAL CAUSE IS THE MARKER SCHEMA. Across 108 markers the fields are exactly `task`, `state`, `status`, `evidence`. `state` is lifecycle and `status` is build state. NOTHING records whether he has ruled, so a ruling not yet executed is indistinguishable from one never given. title: the `ruled` marker field: an item he has already ruled on is no longer a decision
verbatim: the `ruled` marker field: an item he has already ruled on is no longer a decision HIS INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-16: "Yes, add the ruled field and fix the generator." Built, and the queue falls from 13 decisions to 11 on the first regeneration. THE GAP IT CLOSES. Across 108 markers the fields were exactly `task`, `state`, `status` and `evidence`. `state` is lifecycle and `status` is build state; BOTH describe the WORK. Nothing recorded whether HE HAD RULED, so a ruling he gave that was not immediately executed left its entry indistinguishable from one he had never seen. R1 is the proof: he ruled "Restart it" on 2026-08-07 and again on 2026-09-06, and 70 days later it still appeared under "decisions that need you". Measured before the fix: 5 of the 13 should not have been put to him, 38.4615%, 95% Wilson [17.7097%, 64.4771%]. AND NO CANONICAL REGISTER EXISTED TO CONSULT INSTEAD, which is why the field is the record rather than a duplicate of one. Rulings live in 29 dated documents in `experimental_notes/`, created at 1.1469 per week across 177 days (NumPy and SymPy agreeing exactly), and the one named `CDSFL_Founder_Decision_Register_2026-07-06.md` has 3 commits and was last touched 2026-08-15. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE BY THE SAME ROUTE `evidence` TOOK, and verified BEFORE the change rather than after: 0 of 107 existing markers parse differently under the new pattern and 0 evidence values contain a pipe, which is what makes bounding the evidence group at `|` safe. `Entry.ruled` carries a default because ~20 modules construct `Entry` positionally with 6 arguments. IT MOVES, IT DOES NOT VANISH. A ruled entry goes to section 3 carrying the DATE he ruled, in the markdown and spoken aloud in the TTS, so he reads "you ruled this on X, the work is outstanding". Silently dropping it would replace a queue that over-asks with one that under-reports. AND THE BUILT STATE TRAVELS WITH IT. Routing A19 out of the decision list first reproduced the exact mislabel this generator was built to remove -- calling a TESTED item unbuilt -- one section further down, because only section 1 rendered the state. Caught by the existing A19 guard, which was right. A SECOND DEFECT, FOUND ON THE WAY AND SHIPPED TO HIM LAST NIGHT. `_spoken()`'s docstring has always promised that "FILE PATHS ... are dropped entirely, because note standard Rule 6 forbids spelling paths phonetically". The body never stripped a path. Measured on the file actually delivered: 12 path-like tokens, which a reader pronounces character by character. THE GUARD DID NOT CATCH IT EITHER, because it asserted on ONE literal prefix, `bench/tests/`, and 11 of the 12 do not begin with it -- so the test passed while the defect shipped. Both are repaired: the strip is implemented, a labelled clause is dropped WHOLE so no "guard: , 13 tests" wreckage is left, and the predicate now tests the general shape. 0 paths in the spoken file, 35 locators retained in the markdown. 15 tests, and 4 mutations turn them red at 3, 4, 6 and 5 failures: dropping the routing, dropping the carried field, reverting the path strip, and removing the regex group. title: the answer to "why so many rulings": 11 of 13 are genuinely new, and that corrects what I implied last night
verbatim: the answer to "why so many rulings": 11 of 13 are genuinely new, and that corrects what I implied last night HE ASKED why the last run produced so many rulings. Measured rather than asserted, and the first part CONTRADICTS my own framing of a few hours earlier. MOST OF THEM ARE GENUINELY NEW. Of the 13 dated decision items, 11 were recorded on 15 or 16 October and only 2 predate the run: 15.3846% predating, 95% Wilson [4.3258%, 42.2346%], Clopper-Pearson [1.9207%, 45.4471%]. Last night I implied the queue was mostly a stale artefact. It is not. The night found that much. A LARGE SHARE IS WHAT HIS OWN STANDARD ROUTES TO HIM BY DESIGN. The additive standard forbids narrowing or removing a feature without a committed measurement and his ruling, and several of the night's findings are exactly that shape -- a guard to loosen, a recorded output that would change, a schema change that invalidates replay. A productive night therefore produces rulings mechanically. That is the standard working, not failing, and saying so is not a defence: the 2 items that WERE a fault are named below. AND 2 WERE A REAL MECHANICAL FAULT, now fixed by the `ruled` field in the previous commit. R1: ruled 2026-08-07 and again 2026-09-06, still presenting as a decision 70 days later. THE PAIR, under note standard v1.7: a markdown note and a spoken companion on the Desktop, written fresh rather than appended to last night's file, because he asked for a standalone. Both lint to 0 findings; the spoken file carries 0 markdown characters, 0 em-dashes and 0 file paths. IT LEADS WITH THE RUN because he had not read any of the overnight output: leg 3 converged at round 4, 3 of 3 clean convergences, the success criterion met, the closing sweep exercised for the first time on 15 residuals, and the single gate refusal verified as a true positive against the run's own severity census. title: THE KEY PROPERTY BIT: leg 3 is the first run where a falsifier disproved anything
verbatim: THE KEY PROPERTY BIT: leg 3 is the first run where a falsifier disproved anything MISSED IN THE FIRST BRIEF AND FOUND BY THE OWED P-PASS, not by reading. A test that had never failed went red when leg 3 landed in the immune memory, and the cause is a repair working rather than a regression. LEG 3 CARRIES 2 OF 38 ENTRIES WITH A REFUTED FALSIFIER VERDICT, 5.2632%, 95% Wilson [1.4554%, 17.2855%], Clopper-Pearson [0.6439%, 17.7491%]. Legs 1 and 2 together carried 0 of 41, 95% Wilson [0.0000%, 8.5668%]. C0018 and C0034, both severity 0.5. WHY IT MATTERS. The distinguishing term of the section 7.7 severity specification is that a disproved finding scores ZERO regardless of what the model claimed -- a tool outcome annihilating the model's number is what makes the scheme structurally unlike a vote. That term had NEVER been exercised in the programme, and it was blocked by the confinement fault that refused a falsifier permission to read the document it was asked to review, 18 times per run. The repair landed before leg 3 launched. Leg 3 is the evidence it worked. IT SHOWS UP INDEPENDENTLY IN THE MEMORY. Flaw class 1's decayed refutation weight rose 4.1503 -> 9.7554 in that single run, roughly 6 fresh refutations, and its confirm-to-terminal ratio fell 0.9254 -> 0.8356. SO THE TEST ASSERTING THAT RATIO STAYS ABOVE 0.9 WAS RIGHT TO FAIL. Its premise was stated in its own docstring: the rate is "near 1 by construction in a CONFIRM-only pipeline". The pipeline is no longer confirm-only. A numeric floor would now need lowering after every successful run, which is the stale-pin shape this suite has already been corrected for 3 times, so it is re-derived to the 2 claims the docstring actually makes. AND THE REPLACEMENT IS STRONGER THAN THE FLOOR. It adds a RATCHET: refutations have been observed, so a class carrying them must score strictly below 1, and a memory carrying none at all fails outright. Proved by mutation -- zeroing every refutation weight turns it red, where the old 0.9 floor would have reported a return to a confirm-only pipeline as perfectly healthy. THE BRIEF SENT TO HIM 20 MINUTES EARLIER DID NOT CONTAIN THIS, because the figures measured were the archive-wide ones rather than leg 3's own verdicts. It is integrated into the run section of both the written and spoken versions rather than appended, since he asked for a standalone document and not a growing one. The decision queue is now 0, with all 16 items in section 3 carrying the date he ruled them. THE STRIKE. His words: "This is an issue we have gone over many times. No I don't approve the removal of the severity gate ... please strike this permanently from your list of outstanding decisions." VERIFIED AGAINST THE PROJECT'S OWN RECORD, not taken on trust: the memory note of 2026-10-06 reads "THE REMOVAL IS REVERTED, ON HIS 3rd OR 4th REJECTION OF IT", quoting him, and records that commit 6c10fe4 quoted him approving it while the quote existed ONLY in that code comment and in 5 panel diffs all dated AFTER the commit. No source for the approval ever existed. Putting it to him again made it the 5TH presentation. And the repair works: 20 tests pass, and by EXECUTION `FindingRegistry.unverified_critical_count` contains `severity_is_proven`. THE MECHANICAL HALF IS NOT STRUCK, stated so a live defect is not buried with a settled question: C0066 at 0.45 and C0073 at 0.50 reached the blocker count with zero verdicts, no routing history and no falsifier code. That is his "Fix it all". WHY IT GOT THROUGH THE FIX THAT SHIPPED HOURS EARLIER. The `ruled:` marker field covers TASK-LIST ENTRIES, and 9 of the 13 decisions had no marker. The generator now honours `ruled` and `struck_permanently` on a defect record and on authored detail too. A FIRST ATTEMPT AT THAT WAS WRONG AND SILENTLY DID NOTHING. Skipping a ruled defect in `study_items()` made its authored detail an ORPHAN, the generator refused at exit 3 as designed, and the report stayed 2 HOURS STALE while appearing to regenerate -- so the strike did not happen and the queue still read 11. Archiving the detail instead would have been worse: it carries his verbatim words. The escape belongs in `decisions()`, which routes the item to section 3 with his ruling attached. AND MY FIRST GUARD FOR THE STRIKE WAS VACUOUS, found by its own mutation. It read the WRITTEN report, and removing the escape makes the generator abort without rewriting, so the test read the last good output and passed -- 17 green with the protection deleted. It now CALLS `decisions()` and asserts no struck or ruled item reaches the live list. The mutation turns it red. 3 EXISTING TESTS ASSUMED A NON-EMPTY QUEUE, which had always been true because it had never been cleared. They now accept a cleared queue while still requiring that any decision present states its options, and that the document is not padded with narrative once section 1 is empty. ON HIS COHERENCE-BUDGET RECOLLECTION, stated because the record differs: he says "I'm pretty sure I already ruled on this too". On the RECALIBRATION he had not -- on 2026-10-15 he wrote "Once you tell me what the 'coherence budget recalibration' is, I will clearly be in a better position on whether or not to rule it should be fixed." What he HAD ruled, and is remembering, is the adjacent and now-attached constraint: the operational directives are not to be trimmed. Today is his first ruling on the recalibration itself, and it carries that constraint. title: the merge survey: 1,201 of 1,242 paths are main-applicable, and 5 real fingerprints are the one contamination
verbatim: the merge survey: 1,201 of 1,242 paths are main-applicable, and 5 real fingerprints are the one contamination HIS QUESTION: whether it is safe to move the simulated-experiment work to main and switch back, with care that simulation-only work does not carry over. Measured rather than estimated, because deciding by recollection which of 1,242 paths are scaffolding is the operation this project has recorded going wrong. THE ANSWER IS YES, with 2 things done first. 245 commits ahead, 1 commit behind, so a merge and not a fast-forward. MAIN-APPLICABLE: 1,201 of 1,242 paths, 96.6989%, 95% Wilson [95.5524%, 97.5574%], Clopper-Pearson [95.5481%, 97.6208%]. His suspicion that the vast majority transfers is correct. SIMULATION SURFACE: 35 paths, 2.8180%, 95% Wilson [2.0331%, 3.8939%] -- 2 entry points (the stand-in shim and the simulated launcher, both additive and inert on main unless invoked), 6 stand-in fingerprints keyed by the mandatory simulation suffix the live runner never dispatches, and 27 run artefacts carrying 174,921 inserted lines of the programme's own evidence. ★ THE ONE GENUINE CONTAMINATION, and it is a smear rather than a corruption. 5 REAL paid-seat fingerprints differ from main -- CC2, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini, DeepSeek -- each with exactly 2 fields moved: `experiment` and `timestamp`, now naming `study_run1b_2026-10-03`, a SIMULATED run. NO measured value moved; the recorded capacity is 465206 on both sides. It must be corrected before the merge or main carries 5 paid seats whose records name a run that never dispatched them. AND IT IS EVIDENCE THE B7 REPAIR HELD. Those files were last committed 2026-10-04, 11 days BEFORE the fix, and last night's 3 runs moved only the `-SIM` files (last touched 2026-10-16 11:05). Historical defect, working fix, residue to clear. ★ THE DECISION THAT IS HIS. `bench/state/immune_memory.json` now holds priors from 6 experiments: 3 carry the `_live` marker and 3 are the simulated runs of the last 2 days. Carrying it to main starts the next REAL experiment with priors half produced by stand-in models, and the memory is read to adjust real decisions. 3 options offered; the recommendation is to reset to the live 3. A SELF-CORRECTION: I first read main's single extra commit as carrying a Wolfram attribution correction this branch lacked. Both carry it; the files diverge in wording only, so the merge reconciles 2 wordings rather than rescuing a correction. RUNWAY, UNCHANGED BY LAST NIGHT: Stage 1 has 1.6 and 1.7 outstanding, and 1.7 -- the replay, zero dispatch, instrument already built -- is the nearest actionable item and Stage 1's exit test. Stage 2 has 3 items needing 1 live run. Stage 3 has all 7, with 6 built-and-never-run behind the blind-exam ruling of 2026-08-08. title: STAGE 3 IS UNBLOCKED after 69 days, and his names-are-provenance ruling is violated in 6 live places
verbatim: STAGE 3 IS UNBLOCKED after 69 days, and his names-are-provenance ruling is violated in 6 live places HIS RULING: *"The fact that the answer keys were public for a very brief time has already been answered also and has been ruled as not significant ... Verdict: strike from the list of reoccurring issues also."* exp50, exp51 and the 4 exp52 cells were BUILT, NOT RUN on that single decision, requested 2026-08-08 and carried 69 days. It was the longest-standing open item in the project. BUT THE RECORD DOES NOT SUPPORT "ALREADY ANSWERED", and that is stated for accuracy rather than to argue. 570 annotations searched: 2 touch it and only today's rules on the exposure; 2026-10-02 concerns the answer-key ACCESS CHECKS being internalised, a different matter. The 2026-08-22 founder rulings cover 9 items and this is not among them, and `Handover_Decisions_2026-08-24.md` item FOUR records it outstanding with 3 options. Of those he takes the first, "accept the exposure and report it", and the reporting half travels with it. ★ AND HE WAS RIGHT WHERE I WAS WRONG. I reported that no per-model hashed identifier exists and left the impression the idea had never been settled. It was settled, by him, 4+ times. 2026-10-07: *"the only thing that should impact on capability is measured capability. A models name should have little to do with it, beyond recording this."* The record of that ruling states what it governs: ANY ranking, routing, fingerprint or ladder decision. MEASURED: of the 10 name-keyed declarations within the live runner's reach, 6 DECIDE CAPABILITY OR ROUTING FROM THE NAME -- 60.0000%, 95% Wilson [31.2674%, 83.1820%], Clopper-Pearson [26.2378%, 87.8448%]. They are the frozen falsifier ranking, INITIAL_FINGERPRINTS, MODEL_SPECS, DECOMPOSITION_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD, CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET_CEILING and COMPOSER_MODEL_MAP. The other 4 are legitimately provenance or membership. And the record names one of the 6: on 2026-10-07 both free seats, blind, DECLINED to delete the frozen ranking and both said keeping it was weaker than his ruling. It is still there 9 days later. SO FABLE'S GAP IS A SYMPTOM, NOT A SEPARATE DEFECT. Added 2026-09-20, it is in 1 of the 4 per-model tables and absent from 3. Nothing crashed because every read site has a generic fallback, so it has silently run on a default fingerprint, a 100,000 decomposition threshold and a 40,000 context ceiling, where the real values range from 0 to 200,000. Those tables need a hand-written entry per model ONLY because they are keyed by name. REPEATABILITY IS DEMONSTRATED: the 3 legs identified the same 9 planted-defect subjects every time, 9 of 9 in all 3, 100%, 95% Wilson [70.0855%, 100.0000%], none unique to any leg, while finding counts went 22, 19, 39. WITH ONE BOUNDARY: every per-model table is keyed by the REAL vendor name and a simulated run dispatches the suffixed label, so 0 of 6 seats matched any entry in any of the 4 tables. All 3 legs ran every seat on identical generic defaults. The shakedown validated the seat-agnostic machinery and validated NOTHING capability-dependent. That is Stage 2's item 3, and it is why the first live run still matters. FINGERPRINTS ARE NOT RESET PER EXPERIMENT. They accumulate by max(); no reset or per-experiment boundary exists anywhere. His requirement is work to build, not a fact to confirm. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: his ruling applied: the Exp 38 rescue now works outside software, and a forward reference nearly shipped
verbatim: his ruling applied: the Exp 38 rescue now works outside software, and a forward reference nearly shipped HIS RULING, 2026-10-16: "Verdict, yes, fix it." `math_guard` gains `and llm_type not in _code_types`, so a claim the regex filed as mathematical can now be moved onto the code path in EVERY domain, subject to the confidence threshold. WHY IT IS THE SAME PRINCIPLE AND NOT AN EXCEPTION. Both guards exist to stop a claim reaching a verifier that cannot ground it. mathematical -> logical and -> statistical are still refused. mathematical -> CODE is permitted because the CT cell CAN ground a claim about code, and that move is the Exp 38 rescue the module's own comment names as the classifier's reason for existing. MEASURED: of 539 mathematical-guard block lines over 220 archived classifier logs, 408 had a CODE destination -- 75.6957%, 95% Wilson [71.9011%, 79.1267%] before leg 3 and 71.3322% [67.5644%, 74.8254%] after it -- across 327 distinct (run, finding, move) occasions and 32 runs, with 5 firing inside leg 3 itself. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, all 4 directions: mathematical -> code_behavioral at 0.90 now SUCCEEDS; mathematical -> logical at 0.90 still BLOCKED; the rescue at 0.50 still BLOCKED by the threshold; code_behavioral -> logical at 0.95 still blocked by the code-path guard. ★ AND A FORWARD REFERENCE NEARLY SHIPPED. The narrowing reads `_code_types`, whose assignment sat 23 lines BELOW it. That COMPILES CLEANLY and raises NameError only when the branch runs -- and the classifier's own try/except swallowed it, so the symptom was "0 overrides applied" with no guard message rather than a stack trace. Caught by running the tests, not by reading the diff; the same shape as the `copy.deepcopy` slip of 2026-10-15. The assignment is moved above its use and mutation M3 restores the forward reference and turns 20 tests red. 43 tests, and 3 mutations caught at 18, 2 and 20 failures: removing the narrowing, deleting the guard outright, and reinstating the forward reference. 2 new guards hold the narrowing to a narrowing -- mathematical -> logical still refused, and the confidence threshold still applied -- so a later deletion cannot pass as this fix. title: experiment-scoped state: his 2 rulings, 2 different defaults, built
verbatim: experiment-scoped state: his 2 rulings, 2 different defaults, built ON THE IMMUNE MEMORY he ruled a switch with the default ON so it persists between experiments. `immune_memory_scope` defaults to "persist", which is also the behaviour that existed before the field, so the addition changes nothing until asked. Under "experiment" the run starts from no priors and says so in its log. ON THE FINGERPRINTS he ruled they should be recomputed in the blind round of any experiment, and asked me to make sure that is how the facility works. IT WAS NOT. Measured: `_save_fingerprints` takes max(stored, new), so a seat's recorded maximum only ever rises, and nothing anywhere reset or scoped them -- which is why 4 paid seats carried a figure identical to the character and unchanged for 185 days. `fingerprint_scope` therefore defaults to "experiment", and that DOES change behaviour, deliberately and on his instruction. THE 2 DEFAULTS DIFFER BY DESIGN AND SO DO THE FUNCTION'S AND THE CONFIG'S. `_load_fingerprints` keeps its own default of "persist" so that every caller which predates the parameter is untouched, while `RunnerConfig.fingerprint_scope` is "experiment" so the runner implements his ruling. The policy belongs where he can switch it, not in the loader. THE SNAPSHOT IS EMPTIED TOO, and that is the part a careless version would miss. `_save_fingerprints` compares against `_FINGERPRINTS_AT_LOAD` to decide whether a seat changed. Under experiment scope that snapshot must be EMPTY, or a run would measure afresh, compare against stale values, conclude nothing changed and write nothing. Mutation M3 removes just the `.clear()` and turns that test red. 9 tests; 3 mutations caught at 3, 1 and 1 failures -- ignoring the scope, flipping the fingerprint default back, and leaving the snapshot populated. A typo in the scope name falls back to "persist" rather than silently erasing a seat's measured history, which is held by its own test. 62 tests green across the fingerprint and immune-memory suites.
