title: his 2 rulings built: a seat's own vendor token no longer survives, and the recalibration finally has an input
verbatim: his 2 rulings built: a seat's own vendor token no longer survives, and the recalibration finally has an input HIS RULING ON IDENTIFIERS, 2026-10-16: "We normalise going forward, since recording vendor names is purely a recording statistic and has no impact on capability, or how our experiments work." THE DEFECT. The runner prefixed the seat label to whatever identifier a model chose for itself, so Gemini-SIM writing `GEMINI_F004` produced `Gemini-SIM_GEMINI_F004` and a reader grepping identifiers met a bare vendor name. The seat label was always right; the bare name arrived inside the model's own text. MEASURED, WITH THE PREDICATE NAMED. The project carried 3 different figures for this one defect and none said what it counted. All are now reproduced by one producer: 64 occurrences under the task list's predicate (quoted, `_` separator), 81 widening the separator set, 98 including console logs, 4 recorded findings, 2 distinct identifiers, 1 run. The 38 quoted in an earlier brief is reproducible by NO predicate in that lattice and is WITHDRAWN. FIXED AT SIX SITES, NOT ONE. `_structurally_valid_fid`'s own docstring records 5 model-supplied paths, each carrying its own copy of the compose, plus a 6th on the verdict-owner path. One shared `_compose_finding_id` replaces all 6. 5 of the 6 reverts turn the suite red; the survivor is provably inert, because `_MD_HDR` constrains its token to `F\d{2,4}` and 0 of 135 token/seat pairs change. An earlier draft of that comment claimed the unification repaired a live defect there; that claim was FALSE and is withdrawn in place. P-PASS CAUGHT A HAZARD IN MY OWN FIX. The first version took its candidates from the whole roster, so under seat CC2-SIM the identifier `GEMINI_F004` -- a CC2 reply REFERRING to Gemini's finding -- stripped to `F004` and composed to `CC2-SIM_F004`, which resolves to CC2's OWN F004. Cross-model mis-attribution, the shape `lookup_alias_any` records from 2026-08-30, and reachable: the added forms were new in 36 of 48 key/seat pairs (75.0000%, Wilson [61.2156%, 85.0794%]). Narrowed to the seat's own token, which loses nothing measured -- both archived instances are a seat prefixing its own name -- and removes the roster dependency entirely, so nothing here is keyed on a table of model names. AND IT FOLLOWED THE IDENTIFIER INTO THE RESOLVERS, where a miss is not cosmetic: an unresolved MERGE source is MANDATED to be read as a CONFIRM, so a model saying "these two are the same defect" would be recorded as AGREEING the target is real. `_resolve_finding_key` needed the stripped forms and has them. `_resolve_merge_source` did NOT -- its regex can only yield `F<digits>`, 0 of 48 pairs change, and the composed form equalled an existing candidate in 48 of 48 -- so the candidates added there were REVERTED. An addition nothing reaches is not additive. THE BOARD FAILURE IS CLOSED WITHOUT REWRITING EVIDENCE. The sim-naming guard pinned the 2 pre-repair identifiers BY NAME, fails on any other, and refuses a pin that names something the archive does not contain -- so the pin can describe history but never licence a future. A second, previously masked cause was found in the same test: 8 violations in harvested COPIES of resources/ONBOARDING.md and RECOVERY.md, where `ChatGPT`, `cc2`, `Gemini` and `Codex` are correct as written and `PANEL_ONLY=cc2,fable` is his own mandated launch argument. A harvested copy of a repository file is out of this guard's scope, conditioned on the path resolving to a real repository file outside the scanned tree. HIS RULING ON THE COHERENCE BUDGET: "It should be fixed, providing it doesn't trim the operational directives. It exists so that models never get fed work that is larger than they have been demonstrably proven to be able to handle." THE ROOT CAUSE IS ARITHMETIC, MEASURED END TO END. 0 of 30,442 dispatch entries carried constraint_density, constraint_count, token_estimate, coherence_budget or cid -- 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.0126%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 0.0121%]. What they carried was prompt_length, and 3,589 of 3,709 equal 203 (96.7646%, Wilson [96.1451%, 97.2874%]) because every save_output is passed `prompt[:200] + "..."`. SymPy, NumPy and mpmath agree floor(203/70)/floor(203/4) = 1/25 = 0.04 exactly, and z3 and SymPy independently agree {200,201,202,203} is the COMPLETE integer band on which that ratio is 1/25 -- so the truncation length lands at the top of the band and 0.04 was forced. Every threshold the calibrator ever produced was an artefact of a truncation constant. THE FIX IS A WRITE, NOT A REWRITE. The composer already computed all 5 values. They are now recorded at all 4 dispatch sites, with the untruncated size beside `prompt_length` rather than replacing it -- rewriting it would silently change what 3,709 archived entries mean. A composer fallback records `composer_fallback: true`, because an absent key and a failed composition are different facts. Replay is NOT invalidated, which is narrower than was reported to him on 2026-10-15. NOT BUILT, DELIBERATELY: wiring a caller and persisting the budgets. The budget's only effectful consumer was the pruner he retired on 2026-10-13; its sole remaining effect is a warning asserting a kappa penalty that NOTHING computes. And the purpose he names is a SIZE ceiling, which the per-seat fingerprint already measures. That needs his ruling, not code. A COMMITTED CLAIM WAS ATTACKED AND THE ATTACK FAILED; BOTH ARE RECORDED. The 2026-10-13 claim of 4 distinct per-seat budgets was wrongly withdrawn after a measurement that DROPPED the COMPOSER_MODEL_MAP hop. Through the full chain the claim is correct, the withdrawal is itself withdrawn, and a test now fails if the 2 resolutions ever stop disagreeing. SEPARATELY, NEEDING HIS RULING: 4 of the 5 budget keys name SUPERSEDED versions (80.0000%, Wilson [37.5535%, 96.3776%]), so a live seat inherits a dense-instruction allowance written for a model no longer in the roster, selected by its name. His ruling of 2026-10-07: names are provenance only. 31 stale citations repaired with the instrument that exists; the guard now exits 0 and 2 hand-measured spot-checks match. Tests: 3 new files, 105 tests, 20 mutations each turning them red. 579 pass across every suite this touched. title: the band verdict no longer rests on a sentinel, and his model-admission question is answered with a number
verbatim: the band verdict no longer rests on a sentinel, and his model-admission question is answered with a number HIS RULING on the 7 smaller defects, 2026-10-16: "Fix it all." THE BAND VERDICT WAS DERIVED FROM A SENTINEL. `_estimate_gamma` returns 0.0 for FOUR distinct reasons and only one is a slope of 0.0 -- its own mirror `_gamma_is_estimable` names the other three. `gamma_threshold_profile` compared the two band edges for equality, so two SENTINELS compared equal and the run was reported robust to the whole rubric disagreement on the strength of a quantity never measured. MEASURED OVER THE ARCHIVE, with its producer committed beside it: 10 of 26 blocks claim `verdict_robust_to_band: true` on two 0.0 sentinels -- 38.4615%, Wilson [22.4286%, 57.4651%], Clopper-Pearson [20.2260%, 59.4292%], statsmodels and scipy agreeing to 1e-9. 4 more compare a real edge against a sentinel, so 14 of 26 verdicts carried no information (53.8462%, Wilson [35.4579%, 71.2441%]). IT FAILED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is why the repair is a gate and not a sign flip. Two sentinels read TRUE where the answer is "unreadable". One real edge against a sentinel read FALSE -- a false alarm claiming fragility from a number that does not exist. A false "robust" is the worse half: it retires a measured question, since in that band the numeric proxy and the five-clause rubric agree on only 141 of 259 judgeable findings while two blind readers agreed with each other on 86 of 93 (Cohen's kappa 0.837). THE FIX. Estimability now travels with the number: each per-threshold row carries `gamma_is_estimable`, from the SAME predicate the gate uses, so no consumer re-derives a second opinion. The band block emits `band_is_readable` and `not_readable_because`, and `verdict_robust_to_band` is null where either edge is not estimable. Both edge values are still reported unchanged -- the inputs are not withheld, only the verdict that cannot rest on them. Nothing archived is rewritten. 9 tests drive the real reporter against a controlled novelty series; 7 mutations each turn them red, including one that restores the original equality and one that withholds the edge values. HIS QUESTION, 2026-10-16: "adding, removing, or changing models in the harness should be an entirely trivial affair (by design) and should not require major code changes ... The question is, is it? Have we adequately addressed this particular design objective?" ANSWERED BY TWO INDEPENDENT METHODS, NOT BY OPINION. Structurally, an AST walk over bench/ and scripts/ finds 156 per-model tables across 67 files, but that raw total overstates it about 3x and the split is load-bearing: 86 sites are TESTS, which guard the roster rather than admit to it; 50 are HISTORICAL one-off experiment runners whose edit would alter what those runs did; 5 are measurement scripts; 3 are simulated-seat tools. The LIVE harness is 12 tables across 6 files -- reference_runner_v3.py, runner_core.py, composer.py, experiment_11_orchestrator.py, routing.py, dm/_types.py -- plus one per-model registry .toml. SO THE COUNT IS MODEST AND THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT. Executed: a model that does not exist, `Kimi` (he names Kimi K3 as a candidate for re-admission), was put through the real resolution chain. Of 7 steps, 5 default SILENTLY and only 2 fail loudly -- 71.4286%, Wilson [35.8934%, 91.7781%], Clopper-Pearson [29.0421%, 96.3307%]. A researcher who misses one table gets a seat that RUNS while losing whatever that table gated, which is the class `base_model_label`'s own docstring calls "a capability lost with no error" and which this project has recorded 8 times. Making admission trivial therefore means making the misses LOUD first. A single registration point is the fix and it NEEDS HIS RULING, because it changes how every seat is configured. 31 citations were repaired earlier this session; the guard still exits 0. title: a ratchet that could not say what tripped it now names the path, and the swap it used to miss
verbatim: a ratchet that could not say what tripped it now names the path, and the swap it used to miss FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, NOT CAUSED BY IT. A full-board run stopped at 12% showed one failure: `test_the_unrecoverable_present_set_has_not_grown` with `assert 21 <= 20`. Establishing whether this session caused it took half a dozen measurements -- resolving every cited path, listing the citing document for each, and `git log -S` on two candidates to date them. BOTH CITATIONS PREDATE THIS SESSION by 1 to 2 days (4405667e, 82efc9b1), so the failure is INHERITED. None of today's new files cites a `bench/logs` path at all. THAT COST IS THE DEFECT. A count tells a reader the number moved and nothing about which path moved, so every reader who meets this failure redoes the same six measurements. The pin is now a SET of the 21 paths, each named, so a failure says what changed and in which direction in one read. IT IS STRICTLY STRONGER, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The set implies the count, and it also catches a SWAP -- one path becoming recoverable while another becomes unrecoverable, leaving the total at 21. Executed: with the swap applied, the set form fails and the COUNT-ONLY form passes it silently, 8 of 8 green. 3 mutations each turn the set form red: a path dropped from the pin, a path pre-excused that is not actually unrecoverable, and the swap. NOTHING IS REMOVED. The count assertion is kept beside the set. The pin's comment states the preference plainly: make a path recoverable -- commit it, or mirror it under experimental_notes/evidence/ -- rather than widen the pin, and POINT, NEVER PRUNE applies, so the artefact is not deleted to make the citation go away. THE BOARD RUN WAS STOPPED DELIBERATELY, and this is the reason. His machine had 1.60 GiB available of 8, the compressor holding 2.74 GiB and swap already at 2.56 GiB of 4. A 2-hour pytest job and a panel round together would have pushed it into heavy swapping, and the standing budget is 2 heavy processes. The panel is his explicit instruction; every suite the session's changes touch has already been run directly and is green. The board is owed and is named as owed. title: the capacity number measured, his admission question answered, and a hypothesis that died on the way
verbatim: the capacity number measured, his admission question answered, and a hypothesis that died on the way HIS LIST item 5, verbatim: "A capacity number shared identically by 4 paid models and untouched for 185 days." His ruling: "Fix it all." MEASURED RATHER THAN CHANGED, and the runner's own comment says why: "a ratchet that cannot climb ... Changing it alters routing for paid seats and is a design decision, not a repair." So the contribution is the measurement that makes the decision decidable. `max_successful_prompt_chars` stands at 465,206 on CC2, ChatGPT, Codex and Gemini -- 4 of 5 paid seats -- against DeepSeek's 110,076, first committed on 2026-04-13, 186 days before the repository's newest commit, which confirms his figure. Against each seat's own 50-dispatch history it sits 6.49x above CC2's recent maximum, 6.64x above ChatGPT's, 6.50x above Codex's, 4.89x above Gemini's and 1.51x above DeepSeek's. `measured_attention_span` and `compression_threshold` repeat the same number on all 5, so 3 fields carry 1 figure. IT HAS NEVER BEEN BOUNDED FROM ABOVE. `max_failed_context_chars` is 0 and `max_failed_prompt_chars` unset on every paid seat, so the arm that would lower the number has never fired, and one large dispatch in one old run still sets today's routing ceiling. A HYPOTHESIS DIED ON THE WAY AND IS RECORDED. The first explanation tried was that every seat in a star round gets the SAME prompt, so the field would record the runner's largest prompt rather than any model's capacity. REFUTED by the seats' own histories: not identical, sharing only 7 to 17 of 48 distinct values, recent maxima 70,045 to 95,045. The mechanism is simpler and worse -- a lifetime maximum that never decays. AND IT BEARS ON HIS COHERENCE RULING. He said the budget "exists so that models never get fed work that is larger than they have been demonstrably proven to be able to handle in any experiment". The mechanism that actually serves that purpose is this fingerprint ceiling, and it cannot currently detect overload at all, being 6.5x above recent experience with no upper bound. HIS ADMISSION QUESTION IS ANSWERED IN B13 with the measurement already committed: 12 live-harness tables across 6 files plus one registry .toml, and 5 of 7 resolution steps defaulting SILENTLY (71.4286%, Wilson [35.8934%, 91.7781%]). The count is modest; the failure mode is not. Loud-first, consolidate second, and it needs his ruling because it changes how every seat is configured. Both are recorded as OPEN/TESTED with producers, and both are in the free panel's brief as open questions. The list is 109 entries, 9 open -- it GREW today, and that is the honest state rather than a closure to report. title: 94 of 212 blockers could never be worked, and now a run says so
verbatim: 94 of 212 blockers could never be worked, and now a run says so HIS LIST item 3 of the 7 smaller defects: "A counter whose release condition disagrees with it about severity." His ruling: "Fix it all." THE DISAGREEMENT IS REAL AND NOW QUANTIFIED. `unverified_critical_count` blocks release on an UNCONFIRMED entry at ANY severity, because his 2026-09-06 ruling removed the raw severity gate. `_apply_routing`, which obtains the falsifier that would resolve it, admits a sub-critical entry only with a routable instrument fault and an unspent attempt, or when no instrument ever touched it. An entry between the two blocks release forever and can never be worked. Measured by CALLING the admission predicate against every archived runner_state.json: of 3,400 entries, 212 are blockers and 94 of those would be REFUSED -- 44.3396%, Wilson [37.8121%, 51.0686%], Clopper-Pearson [37.5377%, 51.3020%] -- across 18 runs. The reasons are named, not guessed: 88 not escalated and already served, 6 with a spent one-attempt guard. Leg 3 of the shakedown, the most recent run, carries 5 of its 9 blockers in that state. BUILT: THE RUNNER REPORTS THEM. `blockers_routing_cannot_serve` is a pure reader and an `A4 LIMBO` line now prints beside A4, naming the identifiers. One shared predicate `_routing_would_admit` backs both the router and the reader so they cannot drift. NOT BUILT, AND IT NEEDS HIS RULING. Releasing them loosens the A4 gate on a model-assigned severity float -- rejected 4 times and struck permanently on 2026-10-16. Widening routing costs a paid dispatch per entry per round and changes paid-run behaviour. His 2026-10-12 ruling says such a finding must be "fed back into the mechanics of the harness for resolution"; reporting is the additive half, and the choice between widening routing and leaving them to the human is his. TWO OF MY OWN FIXTURES WERE WRONG AND THE TESTS CAUGHT IT. A routing record of {"rung": "x"} does NOT count as a reading: `_routing_ladder_never_served` treats a verdict of '' or 'UNRESOLVED' as no reading, so the entry stayed never-served and 2 assertions asserted the opposite of what they claimed. The fixture is now read from the module's own sentinel set, and the shape that fooled the first draft is kept as the counterexample. 8 mutations each turn the suite red, including the 2 that remove the counter's own pre-severity skips -- an `exhausted` entry is already released through the age valve, so reporting it as limbo would send him after a non-finding. The archive happens to contain no entry that is both exhausted and unservable, so that case is built synthetically; the mutation survived until it was. 103 tests pass across every A4, routing, never-served and key-access suite. title: I repeated the citation omission 40 minutes after recording it, so it is now a script
verbatim: I repeated the citation omission 40 minutes after recording it, so it is now a script WHAT HAPPENED. The citation guard was run and repaired 31 anchors, and the commit message recorded the lesson: it must run after the LAST edit to a cited file and before the commit. The next body of work shifted bench/reference_runner_v3.py again, and the SAME omission happened, so a second commit went out with 27 stale anchors in it. A LESSON RECORDED IN PROSE IS NOT A MECHANISM. That is this project's own finding, applied to me: an addition nothing reaches is not additive, and a rule written into a commit message reaches nothing. 27 citations repaired and the guard exits 0. scripts/precommit_docs_sweep_2026-10-16.sh now runs the 3 things that have to happen before a commit in one invocation: the citation guard in repair mode and then in report mode, the task-list marker summary, and the refresh of the Desktop mirror he actually reads, with a byte comparison that fails the sweep if the mirror diverges. A SCRIPT RATHER THAN A GIT HOOK, deliberately. A hook is invisible to review and would fire in every checkout for every commit. This is invoked explicitly and its output is read, which is the discipline that was missing rather than the automation. title: the panel's first seat found a regression I shipped, and 2 of my 3 repairs were worse than inert
verbatim: the panel's first seat found a regression I shipped, and 2 of my 3 repairs were worse than inert CC2 returned in 872.5s with 165 tool calls, 3 findings and 2 SOUND verdicts. Its fixes are applied as written, from the files it wrote into its sandbox, which were preserved before teardown. F001 -- A REGRESSION I COMMITTED AND DID NOT SEE. The estimability gate broke bench/tests/test_boundary_band_executes_2026-09-04.py: 2 failed, 3 passed. I never ran it, because I did not search for existing tests over the band before changing its verdict. CC2's diagnosis is sharper than the breakage: that 2026-09-04 test was itself asserting `False` ON THE SENTINEL, so it rested on the very defect the gate removed -- and nothing replaced its coverage, because my own replacement reaches all 3 values only through a monkeypatched `_settled_novelty_series`, with one half of the producer/consumer pair stubbed. It enumerated 390,625 registry fixtures through the real `gamma_threshold_profile` and found 149,795 in which both edges are estimable, non-zero and DIFFER, so `False` is still reachable and the diagnostic was not narrowed -- only its test was unmoored. Its repair adds a discriminating fixture, guards that both edges be estimable AND non-zero, and widens the reachability assertion from {True, False} to {True, False, None}. No assertion deleted. F002 -- MY `composer_fallback` FLAG WAS WORSE THAN INERT. It is written at 4 sites and read at 0, which is the addition-nothing-reaches class. Worse: the same helper writes `directive_chars` and `prompt_chars_full` on the FALLBACK branch, both ahead of `prompt_length` in the estimator's or-chain while `constraint_count` is absent there -- so a failed composition took the floor(c/70)/floor(c/4) estimator on the FULL prompt. Executed: the archive shape calibrates to 0.04, the new fallback keys to 0.0567, which is the 2/35 asymptote of the same character arithmetic. My repair would have traded a visibly constant artefact for a VARYING one that reads as measured while containing no constraints at all. Its guard skips an entry whose flag is True, wiring the flag to its only possible consumer in 3 lines. F003 -- the kappa warning, which I flagged and it fixed. The log told an operator a detection penalty had been applied. None had. The density comparison is still reported; only the unsupported consequence is withdrawn. SOUND on the identifier narrowing: 810 seat-and-reference pairs through the real functions, and the prefix relation that makes cross-attribution possible holds ONLY between a seat and its own -SIM form, so no reference to seat B can shed B's token under seat A. 134 of 134 naming tests pass. AND IT CAUGHT A FALSE CLAIM IN MY OWN COMMENT. I wrote that an already-composed identifier "is not shortened to SIM_F004" unconditionally. Executed: STRIP("CC2-SIM_F004", "CC2") returns SIM_F004. The guarantee holds only when the seat label carries the suffix. Unreachable live, and corrected rather than repaired -- but a false statement in a comment is a defect here whether or not it is reachable. Q1 is upheld with a harder fact than mine: `update_coherence_budgets_from_experiments` writes keys from the raw seat label while the consumer reads the composer key, so 0 of 5 seats match. The recalibration pipeline writes into a key space its consumer never reads, which survives my input repair entirely -- I fixed the input to a pipeline whose output cannot land. 13 tests pass in its 2 files; 72 pass across every suite its fixes touch. Fable is still running and is not included. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: my admission figure was understated, and the producer had the defect it reports
verbatim: my admission figure was understated, and the producer had the defect it reports CC2's panel finding corrected my measurement in 3 places, each verified by execution before acceptance. (1) The composer step is NOT a loud failure. `compose` raises in isolation, but `_dispatch_single_model_inner` catches it, logs "COMPOSER FALLBACK for <seat>" and continues on a degraded prompt. Counting it as loud understated the silent share. (2) The structural filter had a blind spot of its own shape. `MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS` and `PHENOTYPE_TRANSFORMS` are keyed on COMPOSER keys (`opus_4_6`), not roster labels, so a scan looking for 2 or more current roster names as keys skipped both tables entirely. (3) The worst single instance was missing altogether. `runner_core.py:1888` reads MODEL_SPECS.get(_spec_key(label), {}).get("L", float("inf")) and the next line gates on `estimated_tokens > model_L`, so a missing entry sets L to INFINITY and the context-budget gate can NEVER fire. `_spec_key`'s own docstring names that hazard verbatim, which makes it a known class rather than a new one. CORRECTED: 9 of 10 steps fail silently -- 90.0000%, Wilson [59.5850%, 98.2124%], Clopper-Pearson [55.4984%, 99.7471%] -- against the 5 of 7 (71.4286%) I committed earlier today. AND THE PRODUCER CARRIED THE DEFECT IT REPORTS. It emitted a 5th outcome class, SILENT DEGRADE, while tallying only 4, so 1 of 10 steps was printed and not counted. It now asserts that the categories sum to the step total and refuses to print a total that does not add up. CC2's answer on the mechanism is recorded in B13 in full: loudness first, and it REJECTS both a raise (15 edit sites, fails at first use after spend, and this codebase swallows broad exceptions near dispatch) and refusing to dispatch the seat (that is benching, forbidden by the rule `_refuse_if_a_route_is_dead` already encodes). It adopts a run-level preflight and names `validate_all_policies()` as the architectural precedent that is not yet wired into the live runner, so the repair extends it rather than adding a parallel mechanism. That remains his ruling to give. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: a gate whose exit code is discarded is not a gate
verbatim: a gate whose exit code is discarded is not a gate I wrote the pre-commit sweep, ran it, WATCHED IT FAIL on an orphaned task-list marker, and committed anyway -- because the invocation was `sh sweep | tail` and a pipeline reports the exit status of the LAST command, which was `tail`. The same class as the defects this session has been finding all day, committed by me within minutes of building the instrument meant to prevent it. THE ORPHANED MARKER, and why it happened. B13's entry is a single long line followed by its marker, and the marker must be the line IMMEDIATELY after the heading. Inserting the correction paragraphs into the middle of that line split it, leaving the marker many lines below and the heading unmarked. The addendum now sits AFTER the marker, and its leading bold is reworded so it cannot be read as an entry heading in its own right. The sweep's header now records the pipeline trap in full, and the task-list step is noted as fatal: the marker summary asserts its state counts sum to the entry total, so an orphaned marker fails the sweep rather than reaching a commit. This commit was made only after running the sweep UNPIPED and checking its status. 415 marker tests pass; 110 entries, 10 open. verbatim: a harvested seat file is verbatim seat output, and I walked into the trap its own test documents sv REFUSED TO SAVE and was right twice over. The memory folder was untouched -- that step genuinely had not happened -- and the interval checker was red. MY OWN TWO LINES WERE WRONG AND ARE FIXED. The end-of-day note wrote `Wilson [0.0000, 0.0646]` with no units inside the brackets, so the checker read them as proportions and computed [0.0000, 0.0006]. The figures were right as percentages and stated ambiguously; they now carry the units, as every other interval in the repository does. MY FIRST CLASSIFICATION OF THE REST WAS WRONG, and the checker's own output corrected it. I reasoned that one row failed and 12 were notes. Running the script said the opposite: 15 were "wider than computed -- valid but loose" notes, and the only 2 real disagreements were in FABLE'S OWN delivered test file. Reasoning about a predicate is not running it. FABLE'S INTERVAL DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Its test states [48.4039%, 74.7631%] for 30 of 48. Wilson is [48.3628%, 74.7847%]; Clopper-Pearson, Agresti-Coull, normal and continuity-corrected Wilson are all further away. It matches NO standard method and is narrower than Wilson at both ends. The finding it supports -- 30 of 48 cross-seat forms mis-attributed -- stands; the interval must be corrected to Wilson before the fix is adopted. Recorded in B15 in THIS project's voice, which is where a claim about a seat's work belongs. THE HARVESTED COPY IS NOT EDITED. The precedent is explicit: a seat quoted a figure "nobody here may correct", and editing it "would make the record a paraphrase". That exemption was span-level; a harvested seat FILE is the same case at file granularity. `scripts/wilson_interval_consistency.py` now skips `sandbox_harvest/` and `seat_evidence/` and says how many it skipped: 2,680 files scanned, 1,201 skipped, 0 disagreements. The scope is narrow and that is measured -- our own files appear inside a harvest as copies and every one is still checked at its canonical path, which is the identical argument accepted twice already today. 3 mutations turn the guard red, including one that WIDENS the exemption. AND I WALKED INTO THE TRAP THE TEST FILE DOCUMENTS. Its docstring records that a literal interval in its own source is scanned by the checker under test, and that this "happened on the first version of this file". I added the new case with the seat's figure spelled out and it happened again. The numbers are now assembled at run time, as the file's other case already does. 3 memory files written and MEMORY.md updated with 3 one-line pointers, after sv refused a save that would have left the next recovery reading an index that had never heard of this session. title: the fingerprint reset is partial, and the 3 legs repeat by containment not replication
verbatim: the fingerprint reset is partial, and the 3 legs repeat by containment not replication B16 and B17 added to the master task list; 113 entries, 0 problems. A CORRECTION TO MY OWN CLAIM. I was about to report that the per-experiment fingerprint reset was not wired to its consumer. It is, and it was built today on his ruling. Executed: RunnerConfig.fingerprint_scope defaults to 'experiment'; _load_fingerprints('experiment') returns 0 seats against 11 under 'persist', and clears the at-load snapshot. My earlier claim rested on grepping _load_fingerprint_cache, which is a DIFFERENT function. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG IS NARROWER AND REAL. That different function is the second loader, imported at reference_runner_v3.py:250 and called at :459 inside the decomposition futility guard. It takes no scope parameter and returns 11 seats while the main path returns 0. Its max_successful_prompt_chars is multiplied by 0.9 to set the payload-split ceiling, so a run that believes it is measuring its seats afresh splits on inherited numbers. 4 of the 5 paid seats share the identical 465,206, which ties this to B12 and shows the shared high-water mark is what the guard USES, not merely what is recorded. THE MERGE-SAFETY ARGUMENT SURVIVES, FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN I GAVE. Both loaders key on the seat label, so a live run asking for CC2 reads CC2.json and never CC2-SIM.json. The protection comes from the LABEL, not the scope switch. REPEATABILITY, his merge question, cross-verified on statsmodels, scipy and mpmath. Run level: converged at rounds 3, 4, 4. Finding volume 22, 19, 38. Finding level, on token overlap at 30%: 81.8182% of leg 1's findings have a partner in leg 3 (Wilson [61.4834%, 92.6931%]) and 89.4737% of leg 2's do (Wilson [68.6059%, 97.0641%]), but only 55.2632% of leg 3's have one in either earlier leg. That is CONTAINMENT, not instability -- leg 3 found what they found plus new material. And the 3 legs were not run under identical conditions, so this is consistency across changing conditions rather than replication. BOUNDARY STATED. The finding catalogue carries no defect-identity field; `mechanism` is a pipeline label and `canonical_id` is per-run. So "did the same defect recur" cannot be read from the record, and the text overlap above is an UPPER BOUND. title: WITHDRAWN: my repeatability figure measured a status phrase, and my own P-pass broke it
verbatim: WITHDRAWN: my repeatability figure measured a status phrase, and my own P-pass broke it THE CLAIM WITHDRAWN. 20 minutes ago I reported to him that 81.8182% of leg 1's findings have a partner in leg 3, 89.4737% of leg 2's do, and 55.2632% of leg 3's have one in an earlier leg, and I concluded "containment, not instability". All 3 figures are withdrawn and the conclusion with them. WHAT WAS WRONG. The producer compared the `demonstrated` and `evidence` fields of `*_finding_catalogue.jsonl`. `demonstrated` is a BOOLEAN and `evidence` is a boilerplate status string. Leg 3 carries 3 distinct combined texts across 38 findings and 18 of them read "True verified fix, no unresolved challenges". So the measure counted how many findings share a status phrase. HOW IT WAS CAUGHT: the Stop gate refused the turn for leaving no failable check after a code change, and the attacks written to satisfy it broke the measure immediately. The rate was 90.0000% at EVERY threshold from 0.10 to 0.99 -- the signature of a measure that discriminates nothing -- and a shuffled control scored 75.0000% against a real 90.0000%. This is the defect class `feedback_verify_the_deciding_layer` names: I measured a field without checking what it contained. THE CORRECTED MEASURE, which now carries its own 4 attacks and refuses to print a figure if any fails. The finding text lives in `runner_state.json` under `registry.entries.<id>.description`: 22, 19 and 38 distinct descriptions of median length 825, 720 and 843 characters. Rebuilt on that source, disjoint text scores 0, identical scores 1, the rate falls monotonically as the threshold tightens, and the shuffled control scores 0.0000% against a real 45.4545%. CORRECTED FIGURES at a 0.30 Jaccard threshold, Wilson from statsmodels and mpmath agreeing exactly, Clopper-Pearson from scipy: leg1 -> leg2 11 of 22 50.0000% [30.7221%, 69.2779%] leg1 -> leg3 10 of 22 45.4545% [26.9203%, 65.3402%] leg2 -> leg1 13 of 19 68.4211% [46.0104%, 84.6356%] leg2 -> leg3 10 of 19 52.6316% [31.7078%, 72.6702%] leg3 -> leg1 12 of 38 31.5789% [19.0846%, 47.4558%] leg3 -> leg2 11 of 38 28.9474% [17.0033%, 44.7571%] Roughly half the withdrawn figures, and the conclusion changes with them: fewer than half of leg 1's findings recur in leg 3, so "almost entirely contained" is false. The direction of the asymmetry survives; the magnitude does not support the word containment. AND THE THRESHOLD IS LOAD-BEARING, so the sweep is now printed rather than one figure from it: the rate runs from 100% at 0.10 to 0% at 0.70. At 0.70 the overlap is 0% in every direction, so no finding in any leg is a near-duplicate of one in another. Whatever repeats, repeats thematically rather than verbatim. The run-level figures are untouched: converged at rounds 3, 4, 4, volumes 22, 19 and 38, read from the committed reports rather than from this measure. title: the audit found 20 confirmed gaps in his record, 12 of them rulings never carried out
verbatim: the audit found 20 confirmed gaps in his record, 12 of them rulings never carried out HIS SUSPICION WAS CORRECT AND CC1'S FIRST ANSWER WAS WRONG IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION. He said the short work list made him "suspicious that you are not reading/parsing my responses in full". A word-overlap measure reported 198 of 199 of his verdicts covered, 99.4975%. It PASSED its own control test -- his verdicts averaged 81.38% overlap against 33.65% for unrelated STEM prose, separating by 47.74 points -- and still answered the WRONG QUESTION, because whether his topic words appear in the list says nothing about whether his instructions were acted on. THE AUDIT THAT ANSWERS THE RIGHT QUESTION. 302 annotations dated 2026-10-01 or later, read with the dedicated reader because 319 of his 579 verdicts sit in files a naive text search treats as binary, examined instruction by instruction by 5 independent auditors, every claimed gap then handed to a separate agent briefed to REFUTE it and to default to "not a gap" when uncertain. 266 instructions identified 44 gaps claimed 24 of 44 REFUTED by the adversarial pass, 54.5455% -- an unverified single pass would have overstated the result by more than double 20 CONFIRMED = 20 of 266 = 7.5188% Wilson (statsmodels) [4.9197%, 11.3274%] Clopper-Pearson (scipy) [4.6530%, 11.3735%] Wilson (mpmath) [4.9197%, 11.3274%] Wolfram {4.919703024776954, 11.32741445387045}, VERIFIED 4 tools agreeing to 7 significant figures. Computed with Wolfram Language (local Wolfram Engine, via wolframscript). OF THE 20: 12 rulings given and not carried out -- 4.5113% of all instructions, Wilson [2.5992%, 7.7185%] -- 4 instructions nothing tracks, 4 direct questions never answered. Dates span 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-16. Entered as C1 to C20, each carrying his verbatim words, why nothing tracks it, and the verifier's failed refutation. C0 is the measurement. THE SHAPE MATTERS MORE THAN THE RATE: not one of the 20 was lost because it was hard. Each was answered in conversation, or partly built, then never written into the list that survives a compaction. Same shape as the 2026-10-15 finding about a seat's work sitting unread in a sandbox for 10 days. THE ENTRIES ARE NOW GUARDED, because the audit's finding is that entries get LOST rather than refuted. 45 tests pin the SET of 20 identifiers rather than a count, require each to carry his words and the verifier's refutation, and require every ruling entry to carry its ruling date. 5 mutations each turn it red. TWO MUTATIONS FIRST PASSED AND EXPOSED REAL FAULTS: one was an invalid mutation targeting a question entry as though it were a ruling, and one was a genuinely vacuous assertion whose fixed 40-character window ran past a short quotation into the next heading, so an emptied quote still measured 40 characters of the following heading. Its threshold is now derived from the data -- his shortest genuine quotation is 34 characters, an emptied one strips to 0. Also: 5 C entries had an unbalanced quote because CC1's own generator truncated his words mid-quotation, breaking the linter's verbatim exemption -- the exact failure mode recorded under B10 earlier tonight. Rebalanced. And 5 glossary entries added for terms now load-bearing: the 3 role names he defined, plus adversarial verifier and bidirectional ladder. title: the ownership distinction is now guarded, and 1 of 3 mutations exposed it as too weak
verbatim: the ownership distinction is now guarded, and 1 of 3 mutations exposed it as too weak WHAT WAS UNGUARDED. Earlier this turn the audit's 3 severities were re-read as 3 kinds of OWNERSHIP rather than 3 kinds of work: a ruling he gave -> he decided; it needs DOING an instruction nothing tracks -> he decided; it needs DOING a question never answered -> HE is owed an answer; nothing to decide That distinction cut his apparent decision queue from 11 items to 3. It was applied to the entries and then protected by nothing, so it would have held for exactly as long as the memory of drawing it -- which is the failure mode the whole audit measured. 2 assertions now hold it, and a 3rd was added because mutation proved the first 2 insufficient: N1 strip an instruction entry's date -> 2 failed (caught) N2 date a single question entry -> 47 PASSED (NOT caught) N3 date all 20 entries -> 1 failed (caught) N2 is the instructive one. `test_only_a_question_may_lack_a_date` asserted that every UNDATED entry is a question. Dating 1 question left the other 3 undated, so the property still held and the mutation passed. The rule had to be stated POSITIVELY: a question may not carry a date at all, because a dated question is presented to him as a decision he already took when in fact he is owed an answer. With that assertion added, N2 fails as it should. 47 tests pass restored. This is the second vacuous assertion of CC1's that mutation caught in this turn; the first was a 40-character window that ran past a short quotation into the next heading. verbatim: he was right: 2 ladder entries were rediscoveries, and my search for novelty was too narrow twice HIS CHALLENGE, 2026-10-17: "Your routing ladder work is a rediscovery, we already addressed this again just recently." And then, on my claim that his Snakes-and-Ladders framing was new: "The snakes and ladders framing is explicitly not new at all. You said exactly that 'this is how the routing ladder already works'!" Executed: run_simulated_experiment.py declares --seat-models with default="ladder", its help recording "THE DEFAULT since commit e228a214, 2026-10-07". The memory note cdsfl_the_ladder_still_cannot_climb_2026-10-06.md is headed "SUPERSEDED ON ITS HEADLINE CLAIM" and says "Do not raise either with the founder again." C11 WITHDRAWN. "Is it Fable? Then yes we should add it" was filed against the finding that a free model is absent from the ladder. Executed: DEFAULT_LADDER maps Fable-SIM -> fable, 1 of 3 distinct backing models. Both WITHDRAWN rather than deleted, with the evidence recorded in place, because the audit's own finding is that entries get lost rather than refuted. The guard test still passes 47 for that reason. That search covered experimental_notes/ and the memory corpus only -- not the source tree, the docs, or the chat transcripts. It is the same defect as the audit itself, whose brief named the task list alone. A narrow negative reported as evidence of novelty. SETTLED by that panel: determinism AND exchangeability, price 0 additional attempts; one division-count formula, not two, bracket 1.228677 at 19 attempts. NOT IDENTIFIABLE AT ALL: relegation on sustained degradation without an externally-anchored item pool, since only capability-minus-difficulty enters the model -- verified by symbolic algebra returning exactly 0, a constraint solver returning unsatisfiable, and arbitrary-precision arithmetic returning 0 across 27 points. REJECTED BY HIM AND NEVER RECORDED: the ~300 attempts per model per window, "clearly vastly much too much", against his proposal of 2 or 3. HIS OWN DESIGN, WHICH SOLVES THE 300-ATTEMPT PROBLEM AND IS NOT BUILT: a season is 1 ROUND. Rankings are computed from the first round's evidence and frozen for the rest of the experiment. That bounds the evidence requirement to 1 round. Plus a cold-start knockout draw assuming no capability, with no model knocked out under the no-benching rule. 3 questions of his from 2026-10-09 remain unanswered and are named in C21. verbatim: the ticket store goes first, and the orchestrator's 3 questions are answered on his 3rd asking C22 ADDED AT THE TOP, ON HIS INSTRUCTION. "This Bugzilla fix should probably be placed at the top of your currents list." The machinery he remembers exists: bench/bugzilla_loop.py, 898 lines, implements OPEN -> CONFIRMED -> CLOSED where CLOSED is "challenge-resistant, terminal", DUPLICATE -> MERGED, and CLOSED -> REOPENED only by "explicit REOPEN + HIL escalation", with CLOSED findings carrying a "do not re-describe" instruction. That IS the set-in-concrete facility. What it does not cover is project-level instructions, whose state CC1 infers from prose. THE EVIDENCE THAT INFERENCE CANNOT WORK, and the reason this is first. 6 attempts to determine settledness or novelty from text failed in one night: a coverage measure that passed its control and answered the wrong question; a repeatability measure saturated at 90.0000% across every threshold; a lint claim that was a type error returning []; a triage that self-matched because the corpus held the task list; a novelty search returning 0 files because it covered neither the source tree nor the transcripts; and a call with the wrong positional argument. Each produced a CLEAN answer that was an artefact of scope or signature. A recorded state field has neither. AND THE HARVEST MUST COVER CHAT: 0 of his 579 annotations mention the orchestrator question he has asked 3 times. It exists only in chat. The transcripts are readable -- his 2026-10-15T03:40:13 message and CC1's reply 103 seconds later were both recovered by timestamp -- so this is feasible. title: the 94 blockers block nothing that matters, and the figure itself is withdrawn
verbatim: the 94 blockers block nothing that matters, and the figure itself is withdrawn HIS QUESTION, 2026-10-17: "What are the 94 unservable blockers? I don't remember hearing about this before? What exactly if anything do they block?... I won't tell you to make 94 potentially significant code changes to clear these 'blockers' without first knowing if they are real." ANSWERED BY CALLING THE DECIDING LAYER, NOT BY READING IT. FindingRegistry.unverified_critical_count instantiated against each leg's archived state and called: leg1 -> 0 blockers, routing-cannot-serve 0 leg2 -> 0 blockers, routing-cannot-serve 0 leg3 -> 9 blockers, routing-cannot-serve 5 And leg3 CONVERGED at round 4, HARDENED_CONVERGED, gamma_crit = 1.000. So the gate that closed the run does not read the blocker count, and 2 of 3 legs carried none -- 1 of 3 affected, Wilson [6.1492%, 79.2340%]. THEY DO NOT BLOCK THE TASK LIST, CONVERGENCE, OR THE RUNWAY. What they cost is verification DEPTH: such a finding goes to the human instead of receiving an executed falsifier. Real, but not a blocker. THE HEADLINE "can neither be resolved nor released" IS FALSE. The counter has 5 independent skip conditions, any 1 sufficient, one of them commented "THE `exhausted` RELEASE PATH THAT ALREADY EXISTS (2026-09-07, panel cc2)". The true and narrower finding is that the exhausted valve cannot FIRE in the runs used, because exhausted_round_threshold defaults to 8 while the legs ran 4, 5 and 5. That is threshold reachability, not unresolvability. THERE ARE NO 94 CODE CHANGES, which was his explicit concern. The reader is built, committed and guarded by 12 tests, and the runner already prints an A4 LIMBO line. What remains is 1 decision: widen routing, or leave them to the human. Zero changes per entry. AND THE FIGURE IS WITHDRAWN. 3 denominators now exist for 1 quantity: 212 from the producer, 197 from a correction of 2026-10-16, and 174 from calling the counter across all 62 archived runs today. Cause: the producer calls _routing_would_admit at line 85 and NEVER calls the counter, so it reimplements the blocker test -- the exact defect the 2026-10-16 correction claimed to fix. The 94 numerator is suspect on the same grounds. Rebuilding the producer to call the counter is now part of B14. On "is it just you again regurgitating old material": no -- the item came from his own list of 7 smaller defects on 2026-10-16. But CC1's framing was overstated and its arithmetic is unreproducible, and both are corrected here rather than defended. title: the ticket store: settled is now a recorded field, and the subject tier is what works
verbatim: the ticket store: settled is now a recorded field, and the subject tier is what works HIS INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-17: repurpose the Bugzilla machinery so settled issues cannot be resurrected, check it mechanically, harvest from chat as well as his replies, give every issue and resolution a hashed id in a searchable registry that must be consulted before proposing work, and prove it beats a word search so it does not become decoration. WHAT IS REUSED. The runner's own status vocabulary, version 2026-08-22: terminal statuses CLOSED, CONFIRMED, DUPLICATE, MERGED, REFUTED, and live statuses OPEN, REOPENED, UNCONFIRMED, CONTESTED, CORROBORATED, WITHHELD. The terminal set is TOOL-ONLY in that vocabulary, and the store preserves it: close() REFUSES without a verification record, and reopen() and reject() refuse anyone but the founder. So the assistant cannot declare a ticket settled by saying so. THREE LOOKUP TIERS, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT PICKED THE THIRD. tid exact digest over kind + verbatim text. Catches a literal repeat. nid normalised digest. Catches a light rewording. subjects EXACT code identifiers the ticket concerns. Catches a PARAPHRASE. The third tier exists because text similarity was MEASURED INSUFFICIENT on the real case: his wording of 2026-10-15 and the paraphrase of 2026-10-17 share a Jaccard of 0.1429 on normalised tokens, 4 shared of 28 union, so no digest collides and no threshold would catch it without catching everything. What actually caught it was a recorded terminal state on the SUBJECT -- the memory note said "Do not raise either with the founder again" about the ladder, not about a sentence. Seeded with his 3 settled instructions and handed 4 candidate proposals whose right answers are already established, the store gets 4 of 4 and beats word overlap, and a test FAILS if it ever stops beating it. 4 MUTATIONS, AND THE 1 THAT PASSED FOUND A REAL HOLE. Disabling the subject tier fails 2, an unverified close fails 1, letting the assistant reopen fails 1 -- but blinding the exact-digest lookup left the suite GREEN, because every scoring case carried a subject and the subject tier caught it first. A tier no test reaches is an addition nothing executes. 2 tier-isolation tests now cover the exact and normalised paths alone, and the mutation fails 2. 3 DEFECTS OF MY OWN, EACH FOUND BY ITS OWN TEST RATHER THAN BY READING. The search log was module-global, so searches leaked between stores and "was a search recorded for this proposal?" became unanswerable -- now scoped to the store. The stemmer was ASYMMETRIC, mapping "refuses" to "refus" while leaving "refuse" alone, so his wording and a rewording normalised differently and the tier silently missed; corrected to one suffix pass plus a trailing `e`, which is symmetric on 8 of 11 pinned pairs, 72.7273%, Wilson [43.4355%, 90.2539%], with the 3 failures named as a ratchet. And an idempotence assertion was wrong in principle: `_stem` is not idempotent and does not need to be, because `_norm_tokens` applies it exactly once; digest stability is pinned instead. 17 tests pass. Nothing is wired yet; the harvester and the gate follow. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. verbatim: the harvester, the subject narrowing, and the Stop gate that prods until done 3 PARTS LANDED. title: B18 built: his 2026-10-11 ruling is 2 of 2, and a third condition it never stated
verbatim: B18 built: his 2026-10-11 ruling is 2 of 2, and a third condition it never stated HIS RULING, 2026-10-11: "Folding fixes forward should be on by default, providing that means folding forward at the end of an experiment and not during it so that the target under study does not keep constantly changing." BOTH CONDITIONS MET, re-measured by execution. default RunnerConfig.apply_fixes_back_enabled is True placement the sole _apply_back_promote call is outside the per-round loop, verified by walking the module's real parse tree, not its text A THIRD CONDITION HE DID NOT STATE, WITHOUT WHICH THE OTHER 2 WERE EMPTY. B18 claimed the facility was armed in 1 of 49 configs. That counted JSON configs only; bench/tools/run_simulated_experiment.py:710 sets it True in CODE, so all 3 shakedown legs ran with it ON and every attempt failed: 8 of 8 promotion attempts REJECTED, 100.0000% Clopper-Pearson [63.0583%, 100.0000%]; closed form agrees to 0.00e+00 all 8 with the identical cause: ast:unterminated string literal, line 47 The target was a 56-line PROSE document whose line 47 reads "over-read a single round's movement than one who sees only a central value." An apostrophe in a quoted sentence is an unterminated string to ast.parse, because it was parsing English as Python. The facility was enabled, attempted promotions in all 3 legs, and folded NOTHING -- which is why convergence was unaffected: the moving target never moved. bugzilla_loop.is_python_target existed for this decision and the runner did not import it. It does now, the syntax check is conditional on it, and a non-Python target is refused with a reason that SAYS SO. A prose fix still cannot be promoted, because green-only promotion needs a suite; the right check is the finding's own falsifier, tracked separately. GUARD: 7 tests, 4 mutations each turning it red, including deleting the closing promotion, because removing the in-loop call left 0 call sites and a facility nothing reaches is not additive either. Regressions: 77 pre-existing tests green. 4 DEFECTS THE NEW MACHINERY FOUND IN ITSELF WHILE DOING THIS. Harvest coverage: a heading-driven rule missed 47 of 141 entries, 33.3333%, Wilson [26.0856%, 41.4651%], for 3 reasons no single example shows. Marker-driven extraction closed it to 0 of 141, 0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 2.6522%], ratcheted. Lost aliases: B18 matched an existing ticket, so its own identifier went nowhere and a search for B18 found nothing. Aliases are recorded now. A SWALLOWED ENTRY, for the second time by one mechanism: an addendum written without a trailing blank line ran into the next heading, "...all green.**B19.", and B19 left the index entirely, 141 becoming 140, while the marker checker AND the note linter both reported no problem. A new guard compares the SET of identifiers against HEAD, because a count cannot say what moved; the mutation reproducing the exact failure turns it red. And B18's own evidence field named a line range in the runner rather than a test, which the DONE-marker guard refused -- V9's rule doing its job. Repointed at the 2 collected test files. title: B19 built: the budget guard now tells a command from a prohibition
verbatim: B19 built: the budget guard now tells a command from a prohibition HIS RULING, 2026-10-17: "Make the guard aware of negation as you have suggested." THE FIX SPLITS BY PART OF SPEECH, and a first attempt did not. A COMMAND NAME is imperative by itself -- `pytest` is an executable, so `agent('pytest')` instructs it exactly as typing it at a shell would. Demanding a verb of every mention let that real instruction through, and the existing contract test of 2026-10-11 failed on precisely that case, correctly. A NOUN PHRASE is not: "the suite has 606 tests" commands nothing, so "the suite" and "full board" now need a verb of execution nearby. NEGATION SUPPRESSES BOTH, inside a short window of 140 characters before and 60 after. The window is short on purpose: a negation 200 characters earlier does not govern the sentence in hand, and treating it as though it did would let any brief smuggle an instruction past the guard behind an opening disclaimer. A test pins that too. AMBIGUITY IS NOW ALLOWED RATHER THAN REFUSED, which is the substance of the change. Refusing on ambiguity is what produced both false positives of 2026-10-17: the first on an explicit "do NOT run pytest", the second on "cost more than a full board run" inside the same prohibition. VERIFIED END TO END on the 2 briefs that were actually refused: both now pass, and a genuine delegated instruction is still refused with the remedy named. 16 new tests plus the 15 pre-existing contract tests, 31 green. 3 mutations each turn it red: ignoring negation fails 7, demanding a verb of everything fails 3, always reporting an instruction fails 10. A RECOVERY ERROR OF MINE IS RECORDED IN THE ENTRY because it nearly lost the work. A mutation was reverted by copying back a backup taken BEFORE the fix, which removed the fix entirely. The new suite caught it at once, 11 of 13 failing, which is the argument for writing the test before the mutation rather than after. 3 more guards are now in the cheap pre-commit list: the fold-back placement, this one, and the ticket harvester. title: all 12 session hooks are now one file, reachable from the repo and unlosable
verbatim: all 12 session hooks are now one file, reachable from the repo and unlosable FOUND WHILE TRYING TO ADD A REDUNDANT MIRROR, which is the useful part. Had it been 1 of the 6 separate copies, nothing would have. ALL 12 ARE NOW HARD-LINKED, 100.0000%, Wilson [75.7506%, 100.0000%]. A hard link makes the 2 paths ONE file: editing either edits both, so git sees every change and no copy can drift. Contents were compared before each link, because linking silently keeps one of 2 versions. GUARD: 26 tests checking by INODE rather than by contents, because identical contents today says nothing about tomorrow. 2 mutations turn it red -- same-bytes-but-separate-inode, and an absent repo copy. title: B16 built: one fingerprint scope, declared once, honoured by both loaders
verbatim: B16 built: one fingerprint scope, declared once, honoured by both loaders HIS RULING, 2026-10-16: "The fingerprints should be recomputed in the first/blind run of any experiment anyway." IT HELD ON ONE PATH AND WAS BYPASSED ON THE OTHER. Two loaders read bench/fingerprints/ inside one run. reference_runner_v3._load_fingerprints honoured cfg.fingerprint_scope and returned nothing under "experiment". run_exp17_immune._load_fingerprint_cache took NO scope and returned 11 records while the main path returned 0 -- and it is called from the decomposition futility guard, where max_successful_prompt_chars times 0.9 is the ceiling that decides whether a payload is SPLIT. So a run that believed it was measuring its seats afresh was splitting payloads on a prior experiment's numbers, with 4 of 5 paid seats sharing the identical 465,206. NOW: run_exp17_immune carries a module scope with a set_fingerprint_scope setter that also invalidates the cache, and the runner calls it once from cfg.fingerprint_scope beside its own load. One declaration governs both. Verified by calling both in the same process: persist gives 11 and 11, experiment gives 0 and 0. GUARD: 8 tests that CALL both loaders. The defect was invisible to reading because each function was individually correct and agreed with its own docstring; only calling them in one process under one scope exposed it. 3 MUTATIONS, AND THE SECOND FIRST PASSED AND FOUND A REAL HOLE. Removing the invalidation from the setter left the suite green, because the experiment-scope check sits BEFORE the cache check and masks a stale cache in that direction. The direction it does not mask is persist to persist, where a cache populated earlier in the same process is returned however the disk has changed since. The setter's contract is now asserted on the cache object directly, and the mutation turns it red. REGRESSIONS: 32 decomposition and specification tests green. 688 in the cheap guard set. 2 glossary entries added for mechanisms now named repeatedly: the decomposition guard and the fingerprint scope. title: B10 built, and the ticket store had 3 defects of its own, the worst one mine
verbatim: B10 built, and the ticket store had 3 defects of its own, the worst one mine B10, ON HIS RULING OF 2026-10-17: "We fix going forward and leave the archive alone." THE ROOT CAUSE WAS A PATH, NOT A PATTERN. The pre-commit ratchet lints COPIES of the staged and HEAD versions under a mktemp directory, and the stamp rule's scope test asks whether the path sits under experimental_notes/ or a *_tts/ folder. A temporary path does neither, so the rule returned nothing for BOTH sides of every comparison and never participated in the ratchet at all. `--as` now declares the path the bytes REPRESENT, passed on both sides, so a pre-existing stamp cancels out while a stamp REMOVED by an edit shows up. AND REACHING THE ARCHIVE IS NOT JUDGING IT. When `--as` first let the rule through, 357 of 536 notes produced a finding -- 66.6045%, Wilson [62.5061%, 70.4665%] -- of which 161 were WRONG VERSION on notes that are CORRECTLY stamped. A note written in April under v1.3 and stamped v1.3 does exactly what the stamp exists for, which his instruction of 2026-10-11 says is traceability rather than uniformity. Grandfathering the real earlier standards leaves 196, 36.5672%, Wilson [32.5989%, 40.7266%], all a genuine absence, on archive notes he has ruled are left alone. An INVENTED version is still a defect. 9 tests, 4 mutations red, including declaring the path on ONE ratchet side -- worse than neither, since HEAD would then score lower than staged on every note and every commit touching a note would refuse. THEN THE STORE'S OWN INTEGRITY CHECK FOUND 2 MORE, AND MY FIRST FIX MADE IT WORSE. OVER-MERGING: 3 settled tickets concealed 5 OPEN task entries -- 3.1a hid B14 and C12, A12 hid A19 and C17, V8 hid B11 -- because subject and text similarity outranked an explicit task reference. A hidden open item is worse than a rediscovery: the work is never done and the store says it is. DESTRUCTION, WHICH I INTRODUCED. The naive fix created a separate ticket, but the identity was a digest of kind and text ONLY, so 2 entries worded identically produced the SAME id and the second OVERWROTE the first -- which was CLOSED. Over-merging hides a record; this DELETED one. Caught by the test written for the first fix. The task reference is now part of the identity. A BLOCKED task is live work that cannot proceed, and the vocabulary has WITHHELD for that; mapping it to OPEN overstated open work by 1. THE STORE NOW MATCHES THE TASK LIST EXACTLY: 34 open to 34, 1 withheld to 1 blocked, 106 settled to 106, 0 coverage gap of 141, all 3 properties pinned by a test that runs against the live list. 6 recurring mechanisms documented in the glossary -- the pre-commit ratchet, the note-lint ratchet, the note-standard stamp, the confinement guard, the estimability gate and the context-budget gate -- which cleared my new term and 5 pre-existing ones, 38 findings down to 33. title: B14 built: the 94 was never right, and his 2026-10-12 feed-back is now on by default
verbatim: B14 built: the 94 was never right, and his 2026-10-12 feed-back is now on by default HIS QUESTION, 2026-10-17: "What are the 94 unservable blockers?... What exactly if anything do they block?... I won't tell you to make 94 potentially significant code changes to clear these 'blockers' without first knowing if they are real." THE FIGURE WAS NEVER RIGHT, AND THAT IS THE ANSWER. 4 numbers reached him for one quantity: 212 from the producer, 197 from a correction, 174 from an ad-hoc call, and 73 of 167 -- 43.7126%, Wilson [36.4145%, 51.2934%], Clopper-Pearson [36.0626%, 51.5897%] -- from calling the live methods over the 61 top-level run states. 2 independent causes. SCOPE: the producer walked rglob and found 74 state files where there are 61 runs. 10 sit inside sandbox_harvest/, which are archived copies of what a SEAT saw, and 3 at other nesting. TWO PREDICATES: unverified_critical_count held 6 release doors while blockers_routing_cannot_serve held a COPY of 3. So the reader named entries the counter does not count as blockers, and commissioning_arm3_contrast_20260922T025824Z gave 4 from the counter and 11 from the reader -- a numerator larger than its own denominator, which makes any ratio between them meaningless. The reader's docstring claimed the 2 "cannot drift"; that was true of the routing half and FALSE of the blocker half. blocking_entry_ids now holds the doors ONCE, the counter is a thin wrapper over its length, and the unservable reader takes that same set as its input. WHAT THEY BLOCK: NOTHING THAT MATTERS, and that half stands. Leg 3 carried 9 and converged at round 4 on the hardened gamma gate, which does not read the blocker count. 2 of the 3 legs carried none. The cost is verification DEPTH. And there were never 94 code changes. HIS RULING OF 2026-10-12 IS NOW HONOURED BY DEFAULT. The post-convergence sweep IS the machinery he named and it already reaches these entries, since UNCONFIRMED is not in its terminal set -- but it was OFF by default: enabled in 18 of 49 configs, 36.7347%, Wilson [24.6652%, 50.7329%], including every live exam config, while 31 left it unset and therefore at 0. It defaults to 1 round now. AND HIS CONCERN OF 2026-10-13 IS SATISFIED RATHER THAN TRADED AGAINST. He asked whether feeding findings back "could block or severely delay convergence". The sweep "runs strictly after the verdict -- can never block, reverse, or improve convergence", registers no new findings, and is bounded. So the feed-back happens where it cannot delay anything, and a test asserts that contract rather than trusting it. 1 round and not more: leg 3 was handed 9 and cleared 0, which is the honest residue, not an argument for a bigger budget. GUARD: 66 tests, one parametrised across every archived run, 3 mutations red. REGRESSIONS: 200 tests across the A4, exhausted-valve, severity-calibration and sweep paths, all green. verbatim: C22 closed, 12 mechanisms documented, and 1 lint finding deliberately left standing THE STORE IS BUILT AND ALIGNED EXACTLY WITH THE TASK LIST: 34 open to 34, 1 withheld to 1 blocked, 108 settled to 108, 0 coverage gap of 141. title: C19 built, B8 closed by supersession: the density ceiling is retired
verbatim: C19 built, B8 closed by supersession: the density ceiling is retired HIS LATEST WORD SUPERSEDES HIS EARLIER ONE. On 2026-10-16 he asked "What would be the consequence of retiring it completely? ... The 'density' of a prompt shouldn't matter to a model, so long as the core system/directives prompt survives untouched, and the overall prompt length stays within a model's measured capability ceiling." That replaces his earlier "it should be fixed", and the replacement he names already exists and is already measured. RETIREMENT CARRIES A COMMITTED MEASUREMENT, NOT A JUDGEMENT, which is what the additive standard requires before anything is narrowed. The density ceiling is provably counterproductive: test_falsifier_C0001_prune_inversion_2026-09-10.py establishes by z3 that "pruning shortened the text AND density did not worsen" is UNSATISFIABLE. Density is constraints over tokens, so pruning shrinks the denominator while the constraint count stands, and pruning to REDUCE density RAISES it. The replacement is prompt LENGTH against max_successful_prompt_chars, enforced by the decomposition guard at 0.9 of it, measured per seat from observed behaviour where the ceiling was a hand-set constant. update_coherence_budgets_from_experiments now RAISES, and the refusal names his ruling, the proof and the replacement, so anyone who wires it up learns at once; a retired function that silently no-ops cannot be told from a working one. The original body is KEPT VISIBLE as _retired_update_coherence_budgets_from_experiments, because point-never-prune applies to code as much as to sandboxes. The pruning itself stays callable: the C0001 proof needs it to demonstrate the inversion, so retiring the ceiling must not delete the evidence for retiring it. B8 IS CLOSED BY THIS rather than by work. It asked whether the recalibration should be repaired, which meant 2 extra fields per dispatch in every run's records and replay invalidated against every older run. Retiring the density ceiling costs none of that. AND ITS PRODUCER WAS UPDATED rather than left to go stale, the a_producer_outlives_its_defect pattern: the inertness producer now reports the supersession and states that its layer-3 verdict of "algorithm no longer sound" IS the retirement being detected, not a regression. GUARD: 6 tests, one of which fails if the z3 proof file disappears, because without it the retirement is a judgement and must be re-argued. TASK-LIST VAGUENESS FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE, not glossed around it. The addendum first wrote "the mechanism" and "the thing being calibrated" where it meant the density ceiling, and the note linter caught both. Naming the subject is the fix; widening the glossary would have been the wrong one, because neither phrase is a project term. title: C23: a ticket identity is the entry's reference, not its prose
verbatim: C23: a ticket identity is the entry's reference, not its prose HIS RULING OF 2026-10-17 requires every issue and resolution to carry a hashed identifier in a searchable registry, and that the registry be searched "before you do, or suggest any new work." An identity that moves when the entry is reworded cannot serve that. The register built hours earlier had exactly that defect, and it had already fired. FOUR FAULTS, EACH MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED. 1. tid_of digested the entry's TEXT as well as its reference. An entry is reworded every time an addendum is written, and where entries share a blank-line-separated block the slice taken for one entry also held the addendum written for its neighbour. 5 references -- R10, 3.2, 6.2, B15 and B20 -- already carried 2 tickets each, and merely improving the extraction rule re-minted 114 of 141 identities in a single step, which would have orphaned every identifier already cited. 2. The title was the first 160 characters of the block between 2 markers, so 9 of 141 titles named a DIFFERENT entry -- 6.3830%, Wilson [3.3941%, 11.6854%]. A lookup of B11 returned prose about B10, which either re-proposes settled work or passes over open work. 3. The label comparison could never converge. The caller held a 160-character string; the store held it stripped to 159, because truncating a normalised string can leave a trailing space. 18 of 141 rows re-wrote an identical record on every run of a file that is append-only by design. 4. 22 of 141 ticket texts were stubs of the form "task A1: A1. DONE ...", because stripping the reference left a 15-character status stamp under the 20-character floor. A stub matches nothing in the tier that catches the same issue arriving in different words. WHAT WAS DONE. A reference is now the whole identity where one exists: unique across 141 entries, so it cannot cause the collision the reference was added to prevent, while surviving every later edit to the prose. The body is anchored on the entry's own heading, the status stamp is stripped as well as the reference, and the label normalisation lives in ONE function that callers compare against rather than re-spelling -- the same single-expression rule the note linter's own paragraphs() records, where 2 spellings of one rule drifted apart and broke an exemption set. Three new store paths carry the consequences, each refusing more than it permits: retitle moves a search label only, restate tracks current wording, migrate_identity moves a ticket and KEEPS THE OLD RECORD as a redirect so a cited identifier still resolves. 56 references migrated carrying 40 closures intact; 17 live records stranded at superseded identities were swept into their canonical tickets. The register went from 46 open against 31 live references to 31 against 31, with 0 disagreements with the task list on what is settled, and 3 consecutive harvests now append nothing. AND THE REGISTER REFUSED THIS COMMIT ONCE, CORRECTLY. C23 was written into the task list before it was harvested, so the register and the list disagreed by 1 entry and 3 guards went red. That is the mechanism he asked for doing its job on its own author. MY OWN INSTRUMENTS WERE WRONG TWICE, BOTH RECORDED. The measuring script's identifier pattern omitted trailing-letter references, so R5a and 3.1a were scored as naming no identifier when both name their own -- the harvester was right and the measurer was wrong. And the over-merge check counted a MERGED record as a concealment, reporting 4 false positives, when MERGED is a redirect that leads to the live ticket; a check that cries wolf is one an operator learns to wave through, which this project has already recorded once in the containment alarm. A VACUOUS ASSERTION, FOUND BY MUTATION, IN 3 PLACES. Ticket.tid is a stored field that asdict copies, so "nt.tid != t.tid" could never fire whatever the digest did -- deleting it left all 19 guards green. Two were rewritten to RECOMPUTE the digest from the new content, and the third was removed with its reason stated, because an unreachable gate is an addition nothing reaches, which the additive standard forbids in the same breath as a removal. GUARDS. 21 tests in test_a_ticket_identity_survives_a_reword, 6 of 6 mutations caught, 2 of which monkeypatch the digest so the recomputing gates actually fire rather than being trusted. 1 test added to the store suite pinning the redirect exclusion, with its own negative case so the exclusion cannot be silently widened. 6 GLOSSARY entries, because the undefined-term rule was firing on real mechanisms. The cheap guard set goes 793 -> 816 tests, all passing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: C23: a ticket identity is the entry's reference, not its prose
verbatim: C23: a ticket identity is the entry's reference, not its prose HIS RULING OF 2026-10-17 requires every issue and resolution to carry a hashed identifier in a searchable registry, and that the registry be searched "before you do, or suggest any new work." An identity that moves when the entry is reworded cannot serve that. The register built hours earlier had exactly that defect, and it had already fired. FOUR FAULTS, EACH MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED. 1. tid_of digested the entry's TEXT as well as its reference. An entry is reworded every time an addendum is written, and where entries share a blank-line-separated block the slice taken for one entry also held the addendum written for its neighbour. 5 references -- R10, 3.2, 6.2, B15 and B20 -- already carried 2 tickets each, and merely improving the extraction rule re-minted 114 of 141 identities in a single step, which would have orphaned every identifier already cited. 2. The title was the first 160 characters of the block between 2 markers, so 9 of 141 titles named a DIFFERENT entry -- 6.3830%, Wilson [3.3941%, 11.6854%]. A lookup of B11 returned prose about B10, which either re-proposes settled work or passes over open work. 3. The label comparison could never converge. The caller held a 160-character string; the store held it stripped to 159, because truncating a normalised string can leave a trailing space. 18 of 141 rows re-wrote an identical record on every run of a file that is append-only by design. 4. 22 of 141 ticket texts were stubs of the form "task A1: A1. DONE ...", because stripping the reference left a 15-character status stamp under the 20-character floor. A stub matches nothing in the tier that catches the same issue arriving in different words. WHAT WAS DONE. A reference is now the whole identity where one exists: unique across 141 entries, so it cannot cause the collision the reference was added to prevent, while surviving every later edit to the prose. The body is anchored on the entry's own heading, the status stamp is stripped as well as the reference, and the label normalisation lives in ONE function that callers compare against rather than re-spelling -- the same single-expression rule the note linter's own paragraphs() records, where 2 spellings of one rule drifted apart and broke an exemption set. Three new store paths carry the consequences, each refusing more than it permits: retitle moves a search label only, restate tracks current wording, migrate_identity moves a ticket and KEEPS THE OLD RECORD as a redirect so a cited identifier still resolves. 56 references migrated carrying 40 closures intact; 17 live records stranded at superseded identities were swept into their canonical tickets. The register went from 46 open against 31 live references to 31 against 31, with 0 disagreements with the task list on what is settled, and 3 consecutive harvests now append nothing. AND THE REGISTER REFUSED THIS COMMIT ONCE, CORRECTLY. C23 was written into the task list before it was harvested, so the register and the list disagreed by 1 entry and 3 guards went red. That is the mechanism he asked for doing its job on its own author. MY OWN INSTRUMENTS WERE WRONG TWICE, BOTH RECORDED. The measuring script's identifier pattern omitted trailing-letter references, so R5a and 3.1a were scored as naming no identifier when both name their own -- the harvester was right and the measurer was wrong. And the over-merge check counted a MERGED record as a concealment, reporting 4 false positives, when MERGED is a redirect that leads to the live ticket; a check that cries wolf is one an operator learns to wave through, which this project has already recorded once in the containment alarm. A VACUOUS ASSERTION, FOUND BY MUTATION, IN 3 PLACES. Ticket.tid is a stored field that asdict copies, so "nt.tid != t.tid" could never fire whatever the digest did -- deleting it left all 19 guards green. Two were rewritten to RECOMPUTE the digest from the new content, and the third was removed with its reason stated, because an unreachable gate is an addition nothing reaches, which the additive standard forbids in the same breath as a removal. GUARDS. 21 tests in test_a_ticket_identity_survives_a_reword, 6 of 6 mutations caught, 2 of which monkeypatch the digest so the recomputing gates actually fire rather than being trusted. 1 test added to the store suite pinning the redirect exclusion, with its own negative case so the exclusion cannot be silently widened. 6 GLOSSARY entries, because the undefined-term rule was firing on real mechanisms. The cheap guard set goes 793 -> 816 tests, all passing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17.
