title: C24 and C25: the 94 of 212 figure is corrected, and an entry was invisible
verbatim: C24 and C25: the 94 of 212 figure is corrected, and an entry was invisible HIS CORRECTION OF 2026-10-16, which he called the first thing to fix: "A figure published earlier today, 94 of 212, does not reproduce. The producer carries a hand written copy of the counter's release conditions instead of calling the counter." And his question of 2026-10-17: "What are the 94 unservable blockers? What exactly if anything do they block?" THE AUTHORITATIVE FIGURE IS 73 OF 167. Of 3,020 archived entries across 61 runs, 167 are counted as blockers by unverified_critical_count and 73 of those are entries _apply_routing would decline to admit: 43.7126%, Wilson [36.4145%, 51.2934%], Clopper-Pearson [36.0626%, 51.5897%], with statsmodels and mpmath agreeing on Wilson and statsmodels and scipy on Clopper-Pearson to 4 decimal places. Across 16 runs. WHY 94 OF 212 EXISTED, DECOMPOSED RATHER THAN DISMISSED, by a new script that runs both forms over the same archive and compares them PER ENTRY, because 2 sets of equal size can still differ. Two independent causes, and together they reproduce the old number exactly. SCOPE: the guarding test walked the archive with no depth restriction, so 13 of the 74 run states it read were nested copies of what a single seat saw inside sandbox_harvest/, contributing 35 of the 45 excess blockers and 11 of the 21 excess unservable entries. PREDICATE: at the same scope a hand-rolled copy of the release conditions returns 177 and 83 against the counter's 167 and 73, disagreeing on 10 entries across 2 runs. The test's own scope and predicate return 212 and 94. The figure was never invented; it measured something else, which is exactly why a test must call the counter rather than restate it. WHAT THEY BLOCK, READ OFF THE CODE PATH AND NOT THE DESCRIPTION. The convergence gate reads the counter and, on any non-zero value, records telemetry mode a4_blocked and returns False, so one such entry stops a run converging and it burns to its round cap. Routing declines to admit them, so no seat is ever dispatched: 72 of the 73 are "not escalated and already served" and 1 has a spent one-attempt guard. They hold the release gate shut and cannot themselves be worked. THE GUARDING TEST NOW CALLS THE COUNTER, restricts to top-level run states, and DERIVES ITS BAND FROM THE ARCHIVE -- a share outside the recorded measurement's own 95% Wilson interval fails it -- rather than pinning a literal, per his standing ruling on baselines. The runner docstring and B14's body carry the corrected figure with the supersession named. The 2 dated notes of 2026-10-16 are LEFT UNTOUCHED per his ruling that "we fix going forward and leave the archive alone". MY FIRST ATTEMPT AT THE COMPARISON IS WITHDRAWN. It guessed the test's conditions and reported 532 blockers against 167, measuring a predicate the test does not use. The withdrawn figure is recorded in the script's own docstring: a comparison is only as sound as its weaker side, and here the weaker side was mine. C25, FOUND WHILE DOING C24 AND WORSE THAN IT. C24's first draft opened its heading with a star marker, which the entry pattern does not admit, so the entry was invisible to EVERY consumer -- the ticket register, the DONE-evidence guard, the parsed entries, the resume pointer -- while --check answered "coherent, 143 entries, 0 problems". An injected orphan marker reproduced it exactly. The existing guard does not cover this: it compares the identifier set against HEAD, so it catches an entry that disappears, while one that never appeared is absent from both sides. check() now names any marker no parsed entry carries. The pattern was deliberately NOT widened to admit a star, because a star marks an addendum and an addendum's first line routinely names an identifier, so widening would mint a phantom entry for every addendum written; a test pins that decision. AND AN INVENTED TIMESTAMP WAS CAUGHT IN THE SAME EDIT. C24 carried 09:04:11 where the clock read 08:58:49 -- typed rather than read, which is the one fault no linter can catch. Replaced with the captured value. GUARDS: 2 tests added to the marker suite, both red when the orphan check is removed; 2 GLOSSARY entries. The cheap guard set goes 821 -> 831 tests, all passing. title: C26: two more corrections -- the glossary contradicted the code, and a comment miscounted
verbatim: C26: two more corrections -- the glossary contradicted the code, and a comment miscounted HIS WORDS, 2026-10-16: "The glossary still states the penalty claim both panel seats retracted, and still describes the retired pruner as active. It is the definition an operator looks up." And: "A code comment about the symbol kappa is false by count, and the coherence penalty itself does appear in the tree inside a prompt used for a mathematics audit, which both seats' comments drop." WHY BOTH SURVIVED. Both panel seats repaired the composer's own warning text on 2026-10-16 and NEITHER touched the glossary. So the code stopped claiming a detection penalty while the definition an operator reads went on claiming it, and described the pruner as routinely pruning when it has defaulted to off since his ruling of 2026-10-13. Nothing was checking the pair. THE COMMENT, MEASURED. Its justification read "every kappa in the live tree is kappa_set". Enumerated over 1,545 live-tree Python files: 355 occurrences across 10 distinct identifiers, of which kappa_set is 53. The other 302 are bare kappa at 187, kappa_stuck 60, kappa_rate 24, Greek kappa 13, kappa_adopt 9, kappa_load and kappa_focus 3 each, kappa_converged 2 and kappa_values 1. Its claim about its own directory was wrong too: composer.py holds 3 Greek-kappa occurrences, not 1. HIS SECOND HALF WAS RIGHT TO THE LINE NUMBER, AND MY INSTRUMENT MISSED IT FIRST. The census initially searched only the ASCII spelling and reported the penalty meaning ABSENT from the live tree, which would have contradicted him. bench/gemini_math_audit.py writes it with the GREEK letter: 7 occurrences, 0 ASCII. Corrected to cover both spellings, and to exclude the census's own prose, it finds exactly the 3 sites he named -- lines 72, 77 and 116 -- plus the composer comment and 2 test assertions. Third time this session that the instrument rather than the thing measured held the fault. THE OPERATIVE HALF SURVIVES, RE-ESTABLISHED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. All 6 live occurrences are prose: a prompt payload describing the mathematics to a model, test assertions, and the comment recording the withdrawal. No code computes or applies it, so withdrawing the penalty claim was correct; only the arithmetic supporting it was not. FIXED. The comment carries the enumeration and the surviving conclusion. The Coherence Budget entry states the pruner is retired by default and that no detection penalty is applied, quoting the retracted wording as withdrawn rather than asserting it. The Coherence Budget Recalibration entry -- stale since C19 -- records that the function now RAISES, with its line references corrected from 1536 to 1647 and 1694. GUARD: 5 tests built CODE-FIRST. Each reads the live default off the function object, or counts the symbol's live occurrences, and then requires the prose to match what was executed -- a test that only grepped the glossary would establish that the glossary agrees with itself. 4 of 4 mutations caught: re-asserting the penalty unmarked, deleting the retirement statement, re-arming pruning in code, and making the recalibration return instead of raise. AND THE GUARD'S OWN FIRST PREDICATE WAS TOO CRUDE. It failed on the corrected entry, because that entry quotes the retracted wording in order to explain the withdrawal. Quoting a retracted claim is not asserting it -- the same distinction the note linter draws with its verbatim-quote exemption -- so each occurrence is now read in its sentence and is a defect only where nothing marks it withdrawn. Cheap guard set 831 -> 836 tests, all passing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: C27: his last 2 corrections -- one was already fixed, one inverted every CC2 merge
verbatim: C27: his last 2 corrections -- one was already fixed, one inverted every CC2 merge THE RUNWAY CORRECTION WAS ALREADY DISCHARGED, and saying so is the honest answer rather than claiming the work. He wrote that the runway "exists only on the Desktop, unversioned", and that 6 of its stage 3 rows still claimed to be blocked on a ruling given at 14:46 that day. Checked: the document is versioned at experimental_notes/RUNWAY_to_BR2_2026-08-18.md, it is the 4th entry in the declared Desktop-mirror table, a guard fails on any drift between the copies, and the two are byte-identical at 848 lines and 118,308 bytes. Stage 3 was unblocked by commit 102444cc at 14:46:18 -- the same minute as the ruling -- and line 297 now reads that exp50, exp51 and the 4 exp52 cells are no longer blocked on a ruling. The correction describes a state the 14:46 commit had already left behind. THE OTHER WAS REAL AND WORSE THAN STATED. "Stage 1 item 1.2 is marked done on an incomplete repair ... it still fails for 2 of 8 model labels." _resolve_merge_source located the finding id with an UNANCHORED search for a C or an F followed by digits, which returns the first such place in the string -- and CC2 is exactly that shape. Handed CC2_F004 it returned C2, which no alias key holds. Measured by CALLING the resolver with the alias map populated the way register() populates it: 2 of 12 seat labels failed, 16.6667%, Clopper-Pearson [2.0863%, 48.4138%] -- CC2 and CC2-SIM, the same 2 seats he named. The consequence is not a dropped merge. cdsfl_topology_formal.md:126-127 MANDATES reading an unresolved merge source as a CONFIRM on the target, and the call site sends both an unresolved and a self-resolving source down that same branch. So every merge CC2 ever proposed was recorded as CC2 AGREEING the target is real: the verdict inverted. CC2 issued 308 of the 800 archived MERGE verdicts, the largest share of any seat. WHY A DONE MARKER SURVIVED IT, AND WHY THE ARCHIVE CANNOT SETTLE IT. A resolved merge is recorded as merged_into=...; a failed one is recorded as an ordinary CONFIRM, indistinguishable from a genuine one. All 800 archived MERGE verdicts are successes BY CONSTRUCTION, so reading the record can only ever show the successes. The fault is visible only by calling the resolver -- the execute-do-not-grep class, now at its fifth fault here and found by reading in none of them. THE REPAIR IS ADDITIVE. Every candidate id in the string is tried in the order the string gives them, so the historical first match is still first and anything that resolved before resolves identically; what is added is that a later candidate is tried when an earlier one fails. The per-candidate lookup is unchanged, split out as _resolve_one_merge_candidate so order and lookup are separate concerns. AND A GUARD I ADDED WAS REMOVED AGAIN THE SAME HOUR, BY MUTATION. A lookbehind excluding a candidate beginning inside a longer token looked necessary, but deleting it left all 18 guard tests green: with every candidate tried in order, C2 fails its 2 lookups and F004 resolves on the next pass. It could only matter if a 1-digit id were itself resolvable, and canonical ids are C\d{4,} by construction. An addition no test can reach is not additive, so the simpler form stands. GUARDS: 18 tests, every seat label parametrised with CC2 and CC2-SIM also pinned by name so a sweep that stopped covering them could not look green. 2 of 2 mutations caught: reverting to the single first-match lookup fails 17 of 18, truncating the candidate list to 1 fails 4. The runway's 1.2 row records what was incomplete and what finished it. Cheap guard set 840 -> 858 tests, all passing. Checked: the document is versioned at experimental_notes/RUNWAY_to_BR2_2026-08-18.md, it is the 4th entry in the declared Desktop-mirror table, a guard fails on any drift between the copies, and the two are byte-identical at 848 lines and 118,308 bytes. Stage 3 was unblocked by commit 102444cc at 14:46:18 -- the same minute as the ruling -- and line 297 now reads that exp50, exp51 and the 4 exp52 cells are no longer blocked on a ruling. The correction describes a state the 14:46 commit had already left behind. THE OTHER WAS REAL AND WORSE THAN STATED. "Stage 1 item 1.2 is marked done on an incomplete repair ... it still fails for 2 of 8 model labels." _resolve_merge_source located the finding id with an UNANCHORED search for a C or an F followed by digits, which returns the first such place in the string -- and CC2 is exactly that shape. Handed CC2_F004 it returned C2, which no alias key holds. Measured by CALLING the resolver with the alias map populated the way register() populates it: 2 of 12 seat labels failed, 16.6667%, Clopper-Pearson [2.0863%, 48.4138%] -- CC2 and CC2-SIM, the same 2 seats he named. The consequence is not a dropped merge. cdsfl_topology_formal.md:126-127 MANDATES reading an unresolved merge source as a CONFIRM on the target, and the call site sends both an unresolved and a self-resolving source down that same branch. So every merge CC2 ever proposed was recorded as CC2 AGREEING the target is real: the verdict inverted. CC2 issued 308 of the 800 archived MERGE verdicts, the largest share of any seat. WHY A DONE MARKER SURVIVED IT, AND WHY THE ARCHIVE CANNOT SETTLE IT. A resolved merge is recorded as merged_into=...; a failed one is recorded as an ordinary CONFIRM, indistinguishable from a genuine one. All 800 archived MERGE verdicts are successes BY CONSTRUCTION, so reading the record can only ever show the successes. The fault is visible only by calling the resolver -- the execute-do-not-grep class, now at its fifth fault here and found by reading in none of them. THE REPAIR IS ADDITIVE. Every candidate id in the string is tried in the order the string gives them, so the historical first match is still first and anything that resolved before resolves identically; what is added is that a later candidate is tried when an earlier one fails. The per-candidate lookup is unchanged, split out as _resolve_one_merge_candidate so order and lookup are separate concerns. AND A GUARD I ADDED WAS REMOVED AGAIN THE SAME HOUR, BY MUTATION. A lookbehind excluding a candidate beginning inside a longer token looked necessary, but deleting it left all 18 guard tests green: with every candidate tried in order, C2 fails its 2 lookups and F004 resolves on the next pass. It could only matter if a 1-digit id were itself resolvable, and canonical ids are C\d{4,} by construction. An addition no test can reach is not additive, so the simpler form stands. GUARDS: 18 tests, every seat label parametrised with CC2 and CC2-SIM also pinned by name so a sweep that stopped covering them could not look green. 2 of 2 mutations caught: reverting to the single first-match lookup fails 17 of 18, truncating the candidate list to 1 fails 4. title: C28: the commit gate cried wolf twice, and the repair it declined was safe
verbatim: C28: the commit gate cried wolf twice, and the repair it declined was safe OBSERVED, NOT REASONED ABOUT. On the C24/C25 commit and again on the C27 commit the gate printed, 4 times each, that the master task list "is partially staged AND the repair collides with a hunk you left out. NOT staged: staging it would commit work you withheld." No work had been withheld on either commit: both were staged with git add -A. The citation repair lagged a commit behind twice, and each time needed a separate follow-up commit to land. THE CAUSE. cdsfl_is_partially_staged asks whether a path has both staged and unstaged changes, and it is evaluated AFTER the stage-0 repairs have written. A fully staged file that a repair has just touched satisfies that test by construction. It has no snapshot copy -- the snapshot is taken before any repair writes and copies only paths partially staged THEN -- so cdsfl_stage_repair_delta cannot compute a delta, returns 1, and the caller reports a collision that did not occur. THIRD DISTINCT CAUSE OF A FALSE COLLISION MESSAGE IN THAT ONE BRANCH. The helper's own comments record the first two: a path containing a space was word-split and never snapshotted, and a repair that changed nothing produced an empty patch returning the collision code. Each was fixed where it was found. The branch kept crying wolf because the predicate was RE-DERIVED after the fact rather than read from the one record that cannot drift. FIXED by keying the branch on the snapshot. The delta mechanism runs only where a snapshot copy exists, which is exactly the set of paths the author partially staged before anything wrote. Everywhere else a plain git add is used, and it is safe there by construction, because nothing was withheld to sweep. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NOISE. A guard that cries wolf on the ordinary case is one an operator learns to wave through -- the pattern already recorded here in the containment alarm -- and this failure mode is silent: had the follow-up commit been forgotten, stale citations would have shipped while the working tree looked correct. That is the 2026-09-11 defect, found then only by cloning HEAD. AND THE INVENTED-TIMESTAMP FAULT RECURRED WHILE WRITING THE ENTRY, hours after C25 recorded it. The entry first carried 09:38:52 where the clock read 09:36:37. The clock WAS captured in the same step and the value was still typed from memory rather than read from what came back, which is the only way this fault happens. Recording it once did not prevent it, so what changes is the order of operations: capture, read what came back, then compose. GUARD: 3 tests in a new class reproducing the exact scenario -- fully stage with no withheld hunk, let a repair write, then re-stage -- asserting the repair reaches the index, that no collision is reported, and that the plain add is used rather than the delta path. Reverting the condition fails all 3. 47 tests across the 2 commit-gate files. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: C20 CLOSED: all 5 of his corrections discharged, and 2 were faults in the list itself
verbatim: C20 CLOSED: all 5 of his corrections discharged, and 2 were faults in the list itself The list he gave on 2026-10-16 under "What is owed as a correction rather than a decision" held 5 items. Each is now carried by its own entry with its own guard. 1. The 94 of 212 figure -- C24. The authoritative figure is 73 of 167, 43.7126%, and both causes of the old one are quantified. His own corrected 94 of 197 is ALSO superseded: the counter returns 79 at that scope, not 94, so the denominator correction was right and the numerator moved with it. 2. The glossary's retracted penalty claim, and the pruner described as active -- C26. 3. The kappa comment, wrong by 302 of 355 occurrences -- C26. His second half was right to the line number, after my own census first missed it by searching one spelling of the symbol. 4. The runway unversioned, and 6 stage 3 rows blocked on a ruling already given -- C27, and this one NEEDED NO WORK: the document was already versioned, already a declared Desktop mirror with a drift guard, and stage 3 was unblocked by commit 102444cc at 14:46:18, the same minute as the ruling. 5. Stage 1 item 1.2 marked done on an incomplete repair -- C27, and it was worse than stated: every merge CC2 ever proposed inverted to a CONFIRM. Two of the five were faults in the correction list itself rather than in the code or documents it corrected. Saying so is the honest reading rather than the agreeable one. AND CLOSING C20 EXPOSED A GAP IN THE REGISTER, caught by its own guards within minutes. The harvester closed a ticket only on the pass that CREATED it, so an entry already filed as OPEN and later marked DONE stayed live for ever: the list said DONE, the register said OPEN, and the counts disagreed by 1. That is the drift the register exists to prevent, arriving through the one path that never re-read the recorded state. The harvester now carries a transition to DONE or WITHDRAWN across. ONE DIRECTION ONLY. A marker moving BACKWARDS is reported, not acted on: REOPEN is founder-only by design, and a tool that could undo a closure on its own would defeat the point of a terminal status. 2 tests hold both directions. AND MY OWN RATCHET COMPARISON WAS KEYED ON PARAGRAPH NUMBERS, which shift when text is inserted, so a renumbered old finding read as new. Comparing by kind and term instead is renumber-stable. Register: 29 open, 117 settled, exactly matching the list's 29 open plus 1 blocked and 110 done plus 7 withdrawn. Cheap guard set 866 -> 872 tests, all passing. title: C8: the hardened gate is on by default, 12 days after he ruled it
verbatim: C8: the hardened gate is on by default, 12 days after he ruled it HIS RULING, 2026-10-05: "Then this should also be on, by default in all our runners." hardened_gate_enabled defaulted to False, and the only place that turned it on unconditionally was bench/tools/run_simulated_experiment.py -- so it was on in the SIMULATED runner and off in every other one, the exact inverse of the ruling. THE DEFAULT NOW HAS ONE EXPRESSION, BECAUSE IT HAD FOUR. The rule lived in the dataclass field and in 3 getattr fallbacks. A fallback is the path a config object WITHOUT the field takes, so leaving those at False would have let a stub config keep the superseded behaviour silently -- the silent-defaulting class this project keeps finding. HARDENED_GATE_DEFAULT is the only expression now, and a test parses the runner to fail if a second one appears. WHAT CHANGES, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because this is a behaviour change and not a threshold move. The gate becomes the CONJUNCTION of a sustained, leave-one-round-out-robust critical gamma and N consecutive settled rounds carrying no novel critical, computed on the settled post-reconciliation registry; the legacy gamma-alt path is bypassed and all-novelty gamma is kept as a diagnostic. It is not simply stricter, so the evidence that it converges rather than stalling matters: all 3 shakedown legs ran with it ON and converged at rounds 3, 4 and 4, each reaching 1.000 on the decay curve. AN EXPLICIT False IS STILL HONOURED, and a test pins it. His ruling sets the default, and an experiment reproducing an archived run must still be able to select the gate that run used, or replay becomes impossible -- a cost he did not agree to. GUARD: 7 tests, 3 of 3 mutations caught. AND ONE WAS VACUOUS AT FIRST: it compared the field's default to the constant with `is`, and since both are True and True is a singleton, writing the field as a bare literal left all 7 green. Whether a rule has one expression is a property of the SOURCE, so that test now parses the runner while the behaviour stays covered by the runtime tests beside it. 2 GLOSSARY entries, for the hardened gate and the legacy gate it bypasses. Register: 28 open. Cheap guard set 872 -> 879 tests. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: C13: the required quiet run is 7, and C29 reports that the list may not terminate
verbatim: C13: the required quiet run is 7, and C29 reports that the list may not terminate C13, HIS RULING OF 2026-10-08 on "the absolute false quiet chance of 0.1159 at full roster, which no roster aware fix addresses": "Fix it." The knob had never moved off 3 and the measurement that discharges the ruling was already committed. THE CURVE, off the archive with no model involved. Premature closes over windows, Wilson intervals agreeing EXACTLY between statsmodels and mpmath and Clopper-Pearson to 6.94e-18 between statsmodels and scipy: K=3 23/182 0.126374 [0.085705, 0.182488]; K=4 12/153 0.078431; K=5 6/131 0.045802 [0.021158, 0.096324]; K=6 3/114 0.026316; K=7 0/99 0.000000 [0.000000, 0.037353]; K=8 0/84 [0, 0.043732]; K=9 0/72 [0, 0.050651]. WHY 7, AND WHY NOT MORE. K=5 meets the 0.05 target on the POINT ESTIMATE only, with an upper bound of 0.096324, nearly twice the target. K=7 is the first window with zero premature closes observed and the smallest whose upper bound meets the target. Going further eventually hurts: by K=9 the upper bound has risen back to 0.050651, above the target, because the denominator shrinks as the window lengthens. The choice is bounded on both sides by evidence. WHAT IT COSTS, because he pays it: about 4 extra rounds on any run that would otherwise have converged, roughly an hour on leg 3's measured 71.5 minutes and 4 more rounds of paid dispatch. K=5 halves that and still meets the target on the point estimate; that choice is flagged for him. BOTH GATES READ IT, verified not assumed: the legacy quiet arm and condition (C) of the hardened conjunction gate that C8 made default the same morning. The committed implementation check independently flipped this item from MEASURED_NOT_ACTED to LIVE. THE BLAST RADIUS WAS 8 TESTS AND NONE WAS SILENCED. Each encoded a literal 3-zero tail or a pinned round; every one now DERIVES it from the configured quiet run. Checked by running the whole convergence suite at K=3, 5 and 7: 425 pass at 7, and at 3 and 5 exactly 1 fails -- the guard asserting the archive holds no premature window, which SHOULD fail at an unfixed value. Two needed more than a derived literal. The recorded-live-run replay has only 3 trailing zeros, so lengthening it would have falsified the record; it now asserts the historical result at K=3 AND that the same run does not converge within its 7 recorded rounds at K=7. And the producer behind the justifying measurement broke when the thing it measured was fixed -- the a_producer_outlives_its_defect pattern. Its window length was hard-coded twice, so it asked the gate about 3-round windows while the gate now wants 7, and read as REFUTED. The window is now a parameter defaulting to 3, and the gate is handed a config whose quiet run EQUALS the window; otherwise the count arm refuses and the gamma arm is never reached, which is a different question. The historical claim reproduces exactly: 23 of 23, gamma blocked none. C29 IS NOT A TEST TO FIX, AND IS LEFT RED DELIBERATELY. A test written on 2026-09-11 carries in its own docstring: "THIS TEST EXISTS TO FAIL IF THAT STOPS BEING TRUE ... that is a conversation to have rather than a number to quietly restate." It has happened. R, new entries per entry closed, has risen from 0.4444 [0.3009, 0.6565] to 0.8148 [0.6154894, 1.0786915], exact binomial p 0.0872911. The interval now ADMITS R >= 1, so termination is no longer established -- though it does NOT say the list is supercritical: the point estimate is still below 1. AND A FIGURE OF MINE IS WITHDRAWN WITH IT. Recomputing from the per-day series gave R = 1.3243 [1.0357, 1.6934], which would have read as decisively supercritical. It counts the 59 entries of the list's founding population as offspring of closures, when they are the generation-zero ancestors. The discrepancy is exactly those 59. What drove the rise: today the list gained 34 entries and closed 17, and the verdict-coverage audit alone added 22, each recording an instruction of his that nothing tracked. The rise is substantially the cost of having LOOKED. The ruling needed is whether to keep filing every discovered gap, which is what makes the record complete, or raise the bar, which lowers R by changing policy rather than work. The bar has NOT been changed unilaterally. 3 GLOSSARY entries. Cheap guard set 883 -> 887 tests, all passing. title: C14: the better way is recovered, verified and built -- incremental stream-json
verbatim: C14: the better way is recovered, verified and built -- incremental stream-json HE ASKED TWICE. 2026-10-08: "clearly the cap doesn't need to be arbitrary, at 900, or 1800, or however many seconds. We can tell the models to print 'I am done' at the end of all their outputs, then watch for this signal in their output logs. Or perhaps there is a better way to do this?" And 2026-10-11, after an adjustable cap had been built instead: "I also asked if there was better way. You said there was. I can't remember what that better way was, but you should try to recover it and to see if your way really is the better option." RECOVERED, from What_Was_Actually_Implemented_2026-10-11.md under "Item 8 recovered": incremental stream-json parsing. VERIFIED RATHER THAN RESTATED, and it dominates on a named property. A COMPLETION MARKER separates printed from not printed, and a dead seat never prints it either, so it cannot tell finished from died. THE CLOCK separates nothing: a degraded attempt issued 88 tool calls at 20.455 s per call and never converged, a healthy one converged in 49 at 20.816 s, a third ran at 15.024 s -- a spread of 5.792 s across all 3. The rate is stable whether a seat works or churns; only the count differs, so a longer clock buys churn. A LIVE CALL COUNT separates all 3 states. AND WHY IT COMES BEFORE THE BOUND. All 135 archived per-attempt records carry a total count and a total elapsed and NOT ONE carries a time per call, so the inter-call gap distribution -- the only thing a non-arbitrary stall bound can be derived from -- is unmeasurable today. A count threshold alone would not do it either: the 2 attempts killed at the cap had 78 and 89 calls, both below the p90 of 95, so they were killed by TIME at a normal count. This produces the missing data. The derived bound is step 2 and is NOT claimed as done. BUILT: _run_cli_incrementally consumes stdout as it arrives, so the call count is observable mid-flight and logged every 10th call where no progress signal existed at all; partial output SURVIVES a timeout, where subprocess.run discarded it and the old handler never read e.output -- the recorded "1800 s for 0 words"; and every call is stamped with its arrival time. STRICTLY ADDITIVE: it runs only where a tool-log sink is set, already the only place stream-json is asked for, so the text path keeps subprocess.run untouched -- pinned by a test that parses the dispatcher to require both calls present. The timeout raises the same exception type, so retries are unchanged. ONE PARSING RULE, NOT TWO. The per-line parse was factored out of _parse_stream_json so the incremental reader and the whole-capture parser cannot drift -- the shape the note linter's paragraphs() records breaking an exemption set. The caller compares the 2 counts over the same bytes and REPORTS a disagreement rather than preferring one. GUARDS: 9 tests, 5 of 5 mutations caught, including re-spelling the per-line rule, which fails 7 of 9. AND 2 DEFECTS OF MINE SURFACED WHILE DOING IT. My earlier counter refactor left an unreachable `return len(blocking)` after the real return, naming a variable no longer in that scope -- it would have raised NameError had anything reached it. And test_a_deferred_critical_can_stop_blocking_A4_eventually asserted on the SOURCE TEXT of unverified_critical_count, searching for a string the refactor had moved; the behaviour never changed, but a source-text test cannot tell a behaviour change from a rename. It now marks a critical exhausted and requires the counter to stop counting it, and requires the sibling routing reader to agree. Disabling the valve turns it red. AND B20's FIGURE NOW HAS A PRODUCER. The commit-time check caught B20 as the one entry quoting a figure with no script behind it: "77 of 79 adjudications were tool-made". It reproduces exactly -- 97.4684%, Wilson [91.2314%, 99.3030%] matching the quoted interval to 4 decimal places, statsmodels and mpmath agreeing to 0.0e+00. My first predicate for the producer was WRONG and returned 79 of 79, treating any entry carrying a falsifier verdict as tool-made; the record is unambiguous, status_adjudicator reads "tool" on 77 and "runner" on 2, and those 2 carry mechanism "model_confirm_quorum (3/1 independent)". Carrying a tool's output is not being decided by one. Register: 27 open. Cheap guard set 887 -> 900 tests, all passing. title: C17: the immune memory is reset, the priors are archived, and a promised script existed only in a comment
verbatim: C17: the immune memory is reset, the priors are archived, and a promised script existed only in a comment HIS RULING, 2026-10-16: "No. We reset immune memory for the upcoming live experiments, since simulation can probably only tell us so much about how this facility will function in real live/paid experiments." Pressed the same day: "isn't the best time to do this now, immediately before the transition back to main is made?" TWO OF THE THREE HALVES WERE BUILT: the researcher switch immune_memory_scope, defaulting to persist exactly as he directed, and its consumer. THE THIRD WAS A CODE COMMENT PROMISING A FILE THAT DID NOT EXIST -- the runner named scripts/reset_experiment_scoped_state_2026-10-16.py as the one-off reset and no such script was ever written. A test now fails if the runner names a script that is absent. THE STATE IT WAS RUN AGAINST WAS WORSE THAN HE WAS TOLD. The store held priors from 6 counted experiments and NAMED only 3 -- and those 3 are exactly the simulated shakedown runs, totalling 139.111445 confirmed and 12.000838 rejected across 7 flaw classes. The memory's own provenance_complete property reports this on every load, and it carries a consequence nobody had stated: the duplicate-ingestion guard refuses an id it has SEEN, so it cannot refuse a re-run of an unnamed one, and re-ingesting any of the 3 live experiments would have silently DOUBLED its counts. A fresh store has complete provenance by construction, so the reset he ordered for the first reason closes the second too. IT ARCHIVES, VERIFIES, THEN RESETS. The live file is replaced only after the archive is written and read back with a matching SHA-256, with a sidecar recording the state and his ruling verbatim. --restore puts any copy back and the round trip is byte-exact, proven rather than promised. Dry run is the default. AND THE SCRIPT'S OWN FIRST TEST DESTROYED THE THING IT PROTECTS, WHICH IS WHY THE GUARD EXISTS. The archive glob matched the *.why.json sidecar, which sorts AFTER the real copy, so restoring "the latest" wrote the SIDECAR over the live memory -- the runner would then have loaded 0 priors believing that to be the truth. Recovered byte-exactly from the verified archive, which is the entire reason the archive is written and checked before the live file is touched. Fixed in 2 places: one definition of what an archived memory IS, used by both listing and restore, and a --restore that refuses any file lacking the required keys and names the restorable copies instead. A reporting helper that called relative_to was also crashing on a path outside the repository, which is a fault in code whose only job is to describe what is happening. GUARDS: 9 tests, 5 of 5 mutations caught -- dropping the restore validation, admitting a sidecar as a memory, skipping the archive verification, writing during a dry run, and wiping the tuning as well as the counts. 2 read the REAL live file: the store is reset with complete provenance, and the 6-experiment state is still in the archive and inspectable. Register: 26 open. Cheap guard set 900 -> 913 tests, all passing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: C15: the season is built and wired; the ladder order is measured, not a vendor tuple
verbatim: C15: the season is built and wired; the ladder order is measured, not a vendor tuple HIS RULING, 2026-10-09, made four times by the project's own record: "there should probably be no distinction between models participating in an experiment other than a 'ranking number' ... the only things that should denote a model's ranking in any given experiment is derived/demonstrable capability", with the timing fixed as "one round of an experimental run could potentially constitute a season ... then for the rest of the rounds the positions of these models in their rankings stays fixed". WHAT THE ARCHIVE CAN AND CANNOT FOUND, over all 3,020 archived entries. The only recorded quantity measuring falsification capability rather than productivity is falsifier_verdict: NO fingerprint field records a falsification outcome at all, and ranking on finding rate was REFUTED by a free seat on 2026-10-06 because it reproduces the inversion competence_provenance exists to prevent. Gemini 10/701 Wilson [0.7767%, 2.6058%]; DeepSeek 6/521 [0.5288%, 2.4895%]; ChatGPT 0/373; CC2 0/366; Codex 0/342. 26 refutations in the whole archive, ZERO for 3 of 5 paid seats. THE RESULT IS SUBTLE. The omnibus test REJECTS equality -- chi2 14.5802, dof 4, p = 0.005656 -- so the seats genuinely differ. Yet 0 of 10 pairwise comparisons survive Holm or Bonferroni at 0.05; the widest contrast is raw p = 0.035825, Holm 0.286597. A ranking IS a set of pairwise orderings, so heterogeneity is established and ORDER is not. Two tools: scipy and statsmodels, plus an independent mpmath hypergeometric tail of 0.018413. SO HIS SEASON DESIGN IS NOT A PREFERENCE BUT THE ONLY SOUND FOUNDING. season_strength_order measures the experiment's own outcomes, freezes the result on the registry, and a later round CANNOT reshuffle it -- a test drives a second round whose evidence reverses the ranking and requires the frozen order to survive. Where a round does not discriminate, the vendor fallback is used AND THE REASON IS LOGGED, which is the half that was silent: a tuple of vendor names looked like a capability ranking precisely because nothing said it was a default. FALSIFIER_STRENGTH_IS_ESTABLISHED is now False in code. THE DECISION I DID NOT TAKE. I emptied DEFAULT_FALSIFIER_STRENGTH and reverted it within the hour. It collides with his EARLIER ruling of 2026-10-07, "Then yes we should add it", which is implemented AS MEMBERSHIP of that tuple and verified by a guard asserting ladder_length == 6. 8 guards went red for that reason, not from staleness. Membership and order are separable and that is the proposal -- but separating them changes recorded behaviour, so it is his to rule on, with the measurement now in hand. 2 DEFECTS OF MINE, both recorded in the code. Moving the literal onto the new name broke 5 guards with "malformed node or string", because competence_provenance reads the constant from source with ast.literal_eval, which takes a literal and not a name. And wiring the season made the call site pass strength_order unconditionally, breaking 8 routing-admission tests with "fake_route() got an unexpected keyword argument" -- the same call site already documents omit-at-default for max_rungs and I failed to apply it to the keyword beside it. GUARDS: 12 tests, 4 of 4 mutations caught. AND ONE OF THOSE TESTS HELD A VACUOUS LINE I LEFT IN -- a malformed "or ... if False else True" that evaluated True unconditionally -- found by reading the file back and removed. Cheap guard set 913 -> 925 tests, all passing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. Kind 'pf' comes from the stated first-word rule in scripts/backfill_the_register_from_history_2026-10-17.py, not from anyone's classification. Author: jebus197.

title: C15 follow-up: the omit-at-default rule is executed, not restated
verbatim: C15 follow-up: the omit-at-default rule is executed, not restated The gap left by the previous commit. Wiring the season made the call site pass strength_order unconditionally, which broke 8 routing-admission tests because they monkeypatch route with a narrow stub -- the exact case the call site's own comment about max_rungs exists to protect. The rule was fixed but nothing guarded it. The existing max_rungs test says the branch "only runs inside a live routing round, which this test does not stand up", and re-implements the rule in the test instead. That form agrees with itself. These 2 tests DRIVE the real _apply_routing with a recording stub that rejects an unexpected keyword, exactly as the real stubs do, and read which keywords actually arrived. Both directions are pinned, so the rule cannot collapse either way: with the default order the keyword must NOT travel, and with a measured order that separates it MUST. Mutations confirm: passing it unconditionally fails the first, disabling the season entirely fails the second. Cheap guard set 925 -> 927 tests, all passing. title: V9: the evidence must go red, and 2 of 19 DONE entries do not
verbatim: V9: the evidence must go red, and 2 of 19 DONE entries do not TASK V9, approved by the founder 2026-09-18: "V9: Approved." Task V1 set 3 conditions on a DONE marker's evidence. 2 were implemented and guarded -- it must exist and it must pass. The 3rd, that undoing the fix makes the SAME evidence fail, was implemented nowhere. R3 is the worked example: its evidence passed against a reverted fix on 2026-09-17 and a HUMAN noticed, not a mechanism. HOW THE FIX IS UNDONE WITHOUT GUESSING AT A PATCH. For entry X the checker finds the commit that introduced "task: X | state: DONE" -- the commit which claimed the work -- and checks out its PARENT. The entry's current evidence files are copied into that old tree and run there, so today's test meets yesterday's code, which is exactly the question V9 asks. All 114 DONE entries are checkable: every one names an existing test file and every one's closing commit is locatable. MEASURED on a reproducible sample of 24: 17 DISCRIMINATES, 2 DECORATIVE, 5 INCONCLUSIVE. So 2 of 19 decided = 10.5263% decorative, Wilson [2.9359%, 31.3941%], Clopper-Pearson [1.3012%, 33.1377%] -- roughly 1 DONE entry in 10 rests on evidence that would have stayed green with its own fix absent. THE 2 ARE NAMED, because a rate with no members is not actionable. A11: 27 of 27 tests pass at the parent commit, so it discriminates nothing. R2: 4 passed and 14 SKIPPED -- a test that skips when its subject is absent is always green, the most deceptive form because it reads as a pass. Both pass today, which is why this was invisible until the evidence ran against a tree WITHOUT the fix. Repairing those 2 is separate work and is not claimed here. A THIRD OUTCOME EXISTS AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THE FIGURE HONEST. 5 of 24 are INCONCLUSIVE: the evidence cannot be COLLECTED at the parent commit, because the module it imports did not exist yet. That is not discrimination, it is the test failing to run, and counting it as a pass would repeat the error this project recorded when a crashed check was read as passing. Excluded from the denominator and reported separately. The 114-entry sweep is NOT gated at commit time: it costs a git worktree and a pytest run per entry and this machine is a fixed resource. What is gated is that the checker exists, that all 114 remain checkable, that the inconclusive class is still distinguished, and that the 2 known decorative entries are RECORDED as a ratchet -- the set may shrink when one is repaired but may not grow without the new member being named with the measurement that found it. title: A19 measured: the script that seemed to argue against the flag says the opposite
verbatim: A19 measured: the script that seemed to argue against the flag says the opposite HIS DESIGN POINT, 2026-09-10: "it should simply mark a purely prose input as 'inadmissible', while still solving any computationally reducible elements within that prose! This is STEM." The mechanism already exists as sk_score_prose_listings, defaulting OFF because it changes what reaches a verdict and the entry records that as his call. AND THE STANDING OBJECTION TURNS OUT TO BE A FILENAME, NOT A FINDING. scripts/a19_flag_admits_harmful_fixes_2026-09-22.py reads as an argument against turning the flag on. Re-measured over all 5 fixtures, both fix kinds and both flag states -- 20 rows: harmful fix, flag OFF : 5 of 5 NO_SCORE (passes through UNSCORED) harmful fix, flag ON : 3 of 5 REJECTED, 2 of 5 NO_SCORE correct fix, flag OFF : 5 of 5 NO_SCORE correct fix, flag ON : 5 of 5 NO_SCORE (0 wrongly rejected) The `admitted` column is 0 on ALL 20 rows, so Property 1 -- a harmful fix is never admitted -- holds in BOTH states. What the flag changes is that 3 of the 5 harmful fixes become actively REJECTED instead of silently unscored. The state that lets a harmful prose fix through without an opinion is the flag being OFF, the inverse of what the filename says. The name is kept because renaming breaks the citations pointing at it; the docstring now carries the correction. WHY IT WAS NOT FLIPPED ANYWAY. 0 of 5 correct fixes were wrongly rejected, and 0 of 5 bounds the false-rejection rate only at Wilson [0.0000%, 43.4482%], Clopper-Pearson [0.0000%, 52.1824%]. The catch rate is 3 of 5, 60.0000%, Wilson [23.0724%, 88.2379%]. A default deciding which fixes reach a verdict should not be flipped on an upper bound that wide. The measurement is now complete, so his ruling is one line either way. AND A READING OF MINE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED IN PLACE. The nan in the R_old and R_new columns looked like a corrupted R_k. It is neither: those keys are absent from sk_result on a REJECTED outcome because Property 2 governs an UNMEASURED fix, and a rejected fix has been measured. Three probes were spent before that was established, on an item the entry itself measures at 0 occurrences in 5,834 archived outcomes -- a real gap that has never yet bitten, which is why it stays low priority and why the drilling stopped there. title: C3: the note standard is v1.8, and half of its new rule was already a rule
verbatim: C3: the note standard is v1.8, and half of its new rule was already a rule HIS INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-04: "Just use official project terminology in both cases, and where no project terminology exists, just name the process itself exactly. Why is that so difficult for you? Either way our notes standard still needs tweaking I think." And, naming the form the fault had taken: "you have now clearly resorted [to] vagueness (or what you seem to think is 'simplification') through outright omission." AND HIS COMPLAINT IS SHARPER THAN MY FIRST DRAFT ALLOWED. Rule 19 has said since v1.4: "Name the subject -- never 'the mechanism' / 'one component'; if it cannot be named the note is not ready." So he was not reporting a missing rule. He was reporting that a rule in force across 4 standard versions was still being broken, which is exactly why he asked why it was so difficult. My first draft of v1.8 presented the naming requirement as new; that flattered the work and is corrected in the standard itself and in the entry. WHAT v1.8 GENUINELY ADDS: the second pattern -- a claim about a measure carrying no value -- as a numbered requirement rather than a near-miss of Rule 22's worked-example rule; the record that the fault returned as outright OMISSION, which Rule 19's wording does not obviously cover; and above all the ENFORCEMENT, because Rule 19 had a rule and no check for 4 versions. A rule written, restated and re-violated across 4 versions does not need a fourth statement; it needs a check that fails. THE BUMP IS SAFE AND THAT WAS MEASURED. 191 notes carry the v1.7 stamp. Moving v1.7 into ARCHIVAL_NOTE_STANDARDS keeps every one CORRECTLY stamped rather than retrospectively wrong: across all 537 notes, stamp findings went 197 to 196, the single change being today's closing report re-stamped to v1.8. The 196 remaining never carried a stamp at all, which predates this. AND A FIGURE WAS WITHDRAWN BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The first draft of the standard claimed these patterns produced "28 findings across the notes written that day". That came from memory of the session with no script behind it -- the defect measured-rate-travels-with-its-script names, and a standard is the worst place to invent a number. Replaced by a reproducible one: today's closing report reaches 0 findings, re-runnable with the linter. 4 DOCS GUARDS CAUGHT REAL DRIFT I HAD JUST INTRODUCED and all 4 are fixed: the project instructions and the glossary foot-line still named v1.7, and the memory ledger needed refreshing after the v1.8 file was added. GUARDS: 6 tests, 3 of 3 mutations caught -- reverting to v1.7, dropping v1.7 from the archival set, and archiving every version so the stamp means nothing. One drives both patterns through the linter, because numbering a dead check would be worse than not numbering it. Register: 24 open. Cheap guard set 936 -> 946 tests, all passing. title: C5: the serialisation cure is a hypothesis, and its measurement is now scheduled
verbatim: C5: the serialisation cure is a hypothesis, and its measurement is now scheduled HIS INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-05: "Then that measurement should be added to our outstanding programme of study." WHAT WAS LIVE AND WHAT WAS NOT. The scheduling change was made -- free seats sharing one subscription are dispatched one at a time -- and this project labelled that change itself "a hypothesis with strong correlational support, not a demonstrated cure". The correlation behind it was measured at p = 1.6e-7, which is strong evidence that the failures are MATCHED across seats sharing a subscription and no evidence at all that serialising them removes the cause. The measurement that would settle it was on neither the master task list nor the programme of study, so nothing scheduled could ever settle it. It stayed untracked for 12 days. ADDED as the 13th measurement in STUDY_IN_FLIGHT.json, with his ruling cited, the design recorded, and result and headline deliberately null. The design: one brief, one seat roster, 2 arms differing ONLY in dispatch scheduling, with the matched-failure rate as the outcome. The arms must share the brief and the roster or the comparison measures the brief instead. Free seats only, so it costs no money. AND THE PROGRAMME'S OWN HOOK NOW REPORTS IT. Before this it read "every measurement now has a result and a headline. Set STUDY_IN_FLIGHT.json status to CLOSED to retire this hook." It now reads "1 of 13 measurements outstanding: serialisation_cures_matched_failures", naming it. That is the difference between a programme that looks finished and one that says what is left. GUARDS: 5 tests, 3 of 3 mutations caught -- removing the measurement, INVENTING a result for a measurement that has not been run, and deleting the honest record that the live change rests on a correlation. The second matters most: a fabricated outcome is the one thing worse than an unscheduled measurement. Register: 23 open. Cheap guard set 946 -> 951 tests, all passing. title: C30: the register was dropping his shortest rulings, and they are his most decisive
verbatim: C30: the register was dropping his shortest rulings, and they are his most decisive FOUND WHILE TRIAGING, NOT BY LOOKING FOR IT. The register held 270 UNCONFIRMED items harvested from his replies. Before triaging them the population was checked against the reader, which finds 318 annotations dated 2026-10-01 or later. The register held tickets for 275, so 43 of 318 were MISSING -- 13.5220%, Wilson [10.1962%, 17.7186%], Clopper-Pearson [9.9617%, 17.7790%], statsmodels and mpmath agreeing on Wilson to 4 decimal places. Triaging the 270 would have been a triage over an incomplete set. TWO DEFECTS, AND THE FIRST IS WORSE. from_responses carried "if len(txt) < 25: continue" -- a bare length floor with no stated reason -- which discarded 37 of the 43, 11.6352%, Wilson [8.5602%, 15.6261%], PURELY FOR BEING SHORT. Every distinct one under 25 characters: "Do it." 3 times, "Fix it." twice, "Fix them.", "Fix them now.", "Fix it all.", "Add it.", "Implement it.", "Yes adopt it.", "Yes run it.", "Verdict: do the work.", "Verdict. fix it.", "Verdict, yes, fix it.", "Already ruled. Fix it.", "Then fix them.", "Yes. Use both." Brevity correlates with DECISIVENESS, so a length filter removes precisely the instructions that matter most. This is the same fault he named on 2026-10-17 when he said he was "suspicious that you are not reading/parsing my responses in full" -- reappearing inside the register built to prevent it. THE SECOND: CONTENT ADDRESSING COLLAPSED SEPARATE RULINGS. An annotation carries no task reference, so its identity was its text -- and "Do it." appears 3 times on 3 different subjects. All 3 became ONE ticket, losing 2 rulings in silence. Removing the floor alone did not fix it: a harvest of all 318 then created only 16 tickets and reported 302 reworded-match, because the alias tiers absorbed every annotation into whichever content-matching ticket already existed. THE REPAIR. Each annotation is anchored to <file>#<text digest>#<ordinal among identical texts in that file>, and an anchor now overrides the alias tiers exactly as a task reference does. The ORDINAL is used rather than the line number deliberately: he RE-ANNOTATES files, which shifts every line below the insertion and would re-mint every identity in that file -- the same instability that gave 5 task references 2 tickets each this morning. 318 annotations now yield 318 distinct anchors, the 286 superseded content-keyed records are retired as redirects, and coverage is 318 of 318, 100.0000%, Wilson [98.8064%, 100.0000%]. The harvest is idempotent. AND MY FIRST ANCHOR WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT WOULD HAVE LOOKED FINE. It keyed the ordinal on (file, text) but emitted only file#ordinal, so every distinct text in a file got ordinal 0: 318 rows produced 29 anchors and 24 collided. Caught by asserting distinct-anchors equals row-count BEFORE anything was written, which is the only reason it never reached the store. WHERE AN UNANCHORED RECORD CANNOT SAY WHICH OCCURRENCE IT WAS, that is recorded rather than guessed: merged into the first successor by file and ordinal, with the resolution saying so, so no reader is left believing the mapping was certain. GUARDS: 7 tests, 4 of 4 mutations caught -- restoring the floor, dropping the digest from the anchor, stopping the anchor overriding the alias tiers, and reverting the anchor to a line number. The short rulings are pinned BY NAME, because a sweep that quietly stopped covering them would otherwise still pass. Cheap guard set 955 -> 966 tests, all passing. Triaging the 270 would have been a triage over an incomplete set. TWO DEFECTS, AND THE FIRST IS WORSE. from_responses carried "if len(txt) < 25: continue" -- a bare length floor with no stated reason -- which discarded 37 of the 43, 11.6352%, Wilson [8.5602%, 15.6261%], PURELY FOR BEING SHORT. Every distinct one under 25 characters: "Do it." 3 times, "Fix it." twice, "Fix them.", "Fix them now.", "Fix it all.", "Add it.", "Implement it.", "Yes adopt it.", "Yes run it.", "Verdict: do the work.", "Verdict. fix it.", "Verdict, yes, fix it.", "Already ruled. Fix it.", "Then fix them.", "Yes. Use both." Brevity correlates with DECISIVENESS, so a length filter removes precisely the instructions that matter most. title: C31: the register beats a word search on the error that matters
verbatim: C31: the register beats a word search on the error that matters HIS REQUIREMENT, 2026-10-17: the register must be "much more useful ... than just relying on semantic searches/vocabulary/word searches on their own ... ensure that it does work better than other methods for this purpose and so that it doesn't risk simply becoming decoration that does nothing useful." It owed a demonstration, not an assertion, and until now it had none. GROUND TRUTH FROM THE REPOSITORY, NOT FROM A MODEL. The task list is under version control, so its history supplies labels nobody invented. Searching the list as it stood at 60d0d536: the 107 entries that existed then are POSITIVES -- querying them with today's wording is exactly the rediscovery case -- and the 42 added afterwards are NEGATIVES, genuinely unknown then. No sentence-embedding model is involved, which is the limit the sibling operating-characteristic script had to state about its own labels. MADE FAIR BEFORE IT WAS RUN. The query carries NO identifier, since a rediscovery happens when work is described rather than cited and "B14" would let the register win on an exact lookup. The word search gets a real stop-list of over 100 common project words and is swept over 19 thresholds and reported at its BEST. THE RESULT over 149 queries. Register: recall 104/107 = 97.1963% Wilson [92.0792%, 99.0420%]; specificity 42/42 = 100.0000%; accuracy 146/149 = 97.9866%. Word search at its best threshold 0.95: recall 106/107 = 99.0654%; specificity 36/42 = 85.7143% Wilson [72.1589%, 93.2840%]; accuracy 142/149 = 95.3020%. WHICH ERROR MATTERS, AND WHY THIS IS NOT A TIE. A false positive says "already known" about work that is NEW, so it SUPPRESSES work and does so invisibly. A false negative merely duplicates work, visible the moment the duplicate is proposed. The word search suppresses 6 of 42 new items; the register suppresses none. Fisher exact p = 0.025811, with an mpmath one-sided point mass of 0.012905 on the observed table. The word search's apparent recall advantage is NOT significant -- Fisher p = 0.621454. So the register is better on the error that cannot be seen and no worse on the one that can. AND 2 OF MY OWN FAIRNESS GUARDS WERE SATISFIED BY PROSE RATHER THAN CODE. One checked that the baseline is still swept by testing '"BEST" in src and "swept" in src' -- both words appear in the script's own DOCSTRING, so pinning the sweep to one threshold left it green. It now parses the loop and counts thresholds, requiring at least 10. The other checked identifier-stripping on ONE constructed example; it now checks all 149 real queries. Both found by mutation, and one mutation had to be re-applied by line index after a regex failed to match -- a mutation that does not apply proves nothing, so each is now verified to have changed the file. STILL OWED FROM THE SAME ANNOTATION: whether the harness's own FindingRegistry should adopt these principles. Not assessed, and recorded as outstanding rather than claimed. Cheap guard set 966 -> 975 tests, all passing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: C32: the harness registry does not work like the ticket register, and should not
verbatim: C32: the harness registry does not work like the ticket register, and should not HIS QUESTION, 2026-10-17: "The full harness already has a registry, but I don't know if it currently works this way either? But if it doesn't and you do gauge it to be genuinely useful you should probably apply these principles to the harness registry too." THE DIRECT ANSWER IS NO, and the code said so before this was measured. FindingRegistry.register assigns C{next:04d} -- a sequential counter -- and dedupes LATER through merge and the ladder's duplicate check rather than looking up before minting. Its own comment records the consequence, measured 2026-09-02: "2 of 2,050 archived findings are recorded as raised by more than one model, because when two models find one defect the runner mints two unlinked canonicals." AND I DO NOT RECOMMEND APPLYING IT, which is the opposite of the agreeable answer. Measured across 61 runs and 2,954 described findings using the harness's OWN _routing_similarity, so the judgement is the system's rather than mine: 33 pairs reach the 0.85 threshold the routing ladder actually uses. But only 6 of the 33 carry substantial descriptions on BOTH sides. 6 are fragments of 8 distinct words or fewer and 21 are mid-length, where word overlap hits 0.85 on shared code tokens like `finding_id: str` without the findings being the same defect. Several of the 6 are findings ABOUT other findings -- "Addresses C0007", "VERDICT: CONFIRM C0014" -- legitimately distinct. MY OWN FIRST FIGURE IS WITHDRAWN IN THE SAME BREATH. The script initially reported 33 pairs and 66 of 2,954 findings involved, 2.2343%, Wilson [1.7601%, 2.8325%], and recommended putting the change to him. That is an inflated upper bound dominated by the fragment artefact, and the examples printed beneath it are what exposed it: every one was a code snippet, not a defect description. The script now reports the breakdown and the corrected verdict instead of the headline. WHY A PRE-MINT LOOKUP WOULD DO HARM HERE. It would catch very little real duplication and would risk MERGING genuinely distinct findings whose descriptions share code tokens -- the over-merge direction, which this project has already measured as the more damaging one. The ticket register's own integrity check exists because 3 settled tickets once concealed 5 open task entries. WHAT THE 2 REGISTERS LEGITIMATELY DIFFER ON, the useful part. A task entry has an external, stable reference and is written once by one author. A finding has neither: it is minted by a model mid-run and its description is whatever that model wrote, so a counter is an honest label. The principle that transferred was never the hash -- it was that a lookup happens before an identity is minted, and that needs a signal reliable enough to act on. On this archive, description overlap is not that signal. GUARDS: 4 tests, which pin the FACT rather than the judgement -- that identity is still a counter, and that the overlap-detectable duplication is still dominated by short fragments. If a future archive shows substantial duplication instead, they fail and his question is genuinely reopened. Cheap guard set 975 -> 983 tests, all passing. Run 1 looked perfect; committing after one run would have shipped a file that grew on every regeneration. blocker_triage.park now inserts AHEAD of the settled section. The end of the file is now the archive, so a plain append would bury each newly parked item on arrival. A PYTEST TEARDOWN WAS CHMODDING REAL FILES THROUGH SYMLINKS. bench/tests/conftest.py walked tmp_path setting files to 600 and directories to 700, and Path.chmod follows a symlink. title: sv could no longer save: its commit timeout was outgrown by its own hook
verbatim: sv could no longer save: its commit timeout was outgrown by its own hook FOUND BY EXECUTION, and caused by this session's own additions. scripts/cdsfl_sv.py committed through a subprocess with a fixed 60-second timeout. The set of tests hooks/pre-commit runs had grown to 1,001 over 35 files, taking 143 s, so every sv --commit died with subprocess.TimeoutExpired and STATE COULD NOT BE SAVED AT ALL. The error read as a git failure rather than as a guard set that had outgrown its waiter. A LARGER TYPED NUMBER WOULD ONLY MOVE THE DATE OF THE NEXT FAILURE, which is the objection he raised on 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14 to a cap with no measurement behind it. So hooks/pre-commit now records its own elapsed seconds on EXIT -- on exit, so a REFUSED commit records a duration too -- and sv.commit_timeout() sizes the wait at 4x that, with a 300 s floor for a fresh checkout that has no record. Guard: bench/tests/test_sv_can_still_commit_through_its_own_hook_2026-10-17.py, 9 assertions, in the pre-commit set. It CALLS commit_timeout against crafted records rather than reading the source, and covers 0 and a negative explicitly because a multiplication would have returned 0 and a 0-second timeout kills the commit instantly, which is worse than the defect being fixed. Its last assertion is a RATCHET comparing the live recorded duration against the live derived wait, so the next time the set grows into the headroom it says so while there is still headroom left, instead of failing a save. Both mutations go red: the floor back to 60 fails the floor assertion, and a hook that records nothing fails the producer-consumer agreement. Also carries the written note for B3 and today's teardown finding, in both formats required by the output protocol. title: the duration recorder was silently discarded by a later trap
verbatim: the duration recorder was silently discarded by a later trap FOUND IMMEDIATELY, by checking that the mechanism I had just added actually ran. It did not. hooks/pre-commit registered the recorder with "trap _cdsfl_record_hook_seconds EXIT", and 400 lines later the note-lint stage ran "trap 'rm -rf $STAGED_COPY' EXIT". In POSIX shell a second trap on the same signal REPLACES the first rather than chaining, so the recorder never fired, no duration was ever written, and sv.commit_timeout() would have fallen back to its 300 s floor forever. That is a new mechanism nothing reaches, which is the failure the additive standard names in its second half. THE ASSERTION THAT MISSED IT read the hook's source for the strings "trap" and "EXIT". Both were present -- in the very line that broke it. Replaced with one that EXTRACTS the hook's exit-handler preamble, RUNS it, and requires both a written duration of at least 1 s and a registered cleanup to have executed. Paired with a structural test for a later trap, because a thief appearing after the executed slice would pass the executing test. The structural one goes red when the original trap is restored. There is now ONE exit handler. Later cleanup appends to CDSFL_EXIT_EXTRA, which the handler evals before recording, so cleanup and measurement no longer compete for the same signal. title: B12: the ceiling cannot be lowered by a measured failure, not merely has not been
verbatim: B12: the ceiling cannot be lowered by a measured failure, not merely has not been MEASURED BY EXECUTION through the live routing predicate rather than re-derived from the formula. scripts/can_a_measured_failure_ever_lower_the_ceiling_2026-10-17.py bisects _decomposition_is_futile over fixed_chars with a crafted fingerprint, so the figure is the one the routing path computes. A paid seat's effective ceiling is 418,686 characters, from max_successful_prompt_chars of 465,206 taken at 90%. Injecting a recorded FAILURE at 10,000, at 80,000 or at 200,000 leaves it at 418,686, UNCHANGED. The failure applies only when the success field is 0, where the ceiling becomes 80,001. The cause is the shape of the consumer: max_failed_prompt_chars is read inside the else of "if observed > 0", and all 5 paid seats have a non-zero observed maximum. B12 recorded that the failure arm "has never fired". The stronger statement is that it CANNOT, and it changes which of his 3 options is available: bounding the ceiling by a measured failure needs the CONSUMER changed, not only the recorder. THE OBVIOUS HYPOTHESIS WAS REFUTED BY THE ARCHIVE. The recorder is gated on the literal phrase "context length" appearing in the dispatch error, and a narrow phrase was the suspect. Across 172 archived json files carrying an error field and 37 distinct error strings, 0 are overflow-shaped under a deliberately broad pattern covering context length, token limits, 413, context_length_exceeded, "too long", "request too large" and "reduce the length". No dispatch has ever hit a context limit, so the phrase is UNTESTED rather than wrong. It is left alone: widening an untested predicate on no evidence is the shape of fix he objected to on 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14. NOTHING WAS CHANGED, and B12 stays OPEN. Which option to take alters routing for paid seats and is his decision, as the runner says in its own words. bench/tests/test_a_measured_failure_cannot_lower_the_ceiling_2026-10-17.py is a CHANGE DETECTOR rather than a correctness guard: it pins the present behaviour so it cannot move unnoticed, its docstring says to rewrite it when his ruling lands, and 3 of its 4 parametrised cases go red under precisely the consumer change option 2 would need. The 4th, a failure at 465,205, correctly does not fire, which is why the parametrisation earns its keep. With 151 entries of which 21 are open: the master task list in full is 654,237 characters; the open entries capped at 90 cost 2,009; at 120, 2,639; with their ruled state at 110, 2,828; identifiers alone, 97. THE COMPARISON IS THE ANSWER: the notice ALREADY injects roughly 2,600 characters of file PATHS each post-compaction turn, so the state itself costs 1.09x the paths that point at it. title: a ruled entry may not still ask, and the check for it was vacuous twice
verbatim: a ruled entry may not still ask, and the check for it was vacuous twice THE DEFECT, AND I COMMITTED IT MYSELF TODAY. The `ruled:` marker field was added on 2026-10-16 because the zero-plant control was ruled "restart it" on 2026-08-07 and again on 2026-09-06 and was still listed under decisions needing him 70 days later. The field fixed the REPORT GENERATOR. It did not fix the ENTRY: a marker records the DATE he ruled while the prose still carries the question put to him, and nothing reconciles the two. So a reader takes the prose at its word and asks again, which is exactly what I did with B12. FOUR ENTRIES RECONCILED against his annotations, read with scripts/read_founder_responses_2026-10-11.py rather than from recollection. B12 -- his 2026-10-16 ruling rejected all 3 options and named a fourth. B6 -- its remaining question was the same design decision B12 settled. B11 -- he ruled (b) verbatim on 2026-10-16: "We normalise going forward, since recording vendor names is purely a recording statistic". That is BUILT and REACHED: runner_core._compose_finding_id strips a redundant bare vendor token, is idempotent, and has live call sites in 7 places. Only (c), what the baseline should be after a run lands, is still open. B20 -- it said placement needed his ruling while quoting that ruling 2 paragraphs above its own request for it. A CLAIM WITHDRAWN. An earlier brief of mine asserted he had ruled "derive each baseline from the archive rather than pin a number". The reader returns 0 annotations containing any such ruling. That sentence was my prose wearing his name and B11 now records the withdrawal. THE CHECK WAS VACUOUS TWICE, and both were caught before any figure was quoted. First it flagged every ruled entry that asked, which B11 showed is too strong: an entry with 2 questions can be ruled on one and open on the other. Narrowing it to "asks while recording NO ruling at all" then made it vacuous outright, because RECORDS_A_RULING contains "HIS RULING", a SUBSTRING of "NEEDS HIS RULING" -- so every asking entry also counted as recording one and it reported 0 problems whatever the list said. The asking phrases are now stripped before the recording test. AND THE ANTI-VACUITY TEST WAS ITSELF WRONG FIRST. It asserted the live data was still broken, so it went red the moment the last entry was reconciled: a guard that fails when its subject is repaired cannot tell a working detector from a clean list. It now PLANTS a known-bad entry and requires detection, which holds at 0 outstanding or at 11. MEASURED: of 151 entries, 45 carry a ruling date, 9 ask at all -- and those 9 record what he ruled AND name what remains, which is correct -- and 0 ask while recording no ruling, Wilson [0.0000%, 7.8652%]. The guard pins the SET, now empty, so a new member is a regression rather than a backlog item. 1,034 tests pass across 39 guard files. title: C12: the false-quiet fix was in the default and every caller overrode it
verbatim: C12: the false-quiet fix was in the default and every caller overrode it HIS RULING, 2026-10-08: "Fix it and check your fix with the free panel." The fix half is now done; the panel half is still owed and C12 stays OPEN for it. RunnerConfig.gamma_alt_consecutive_zero_crit derives from REQUIRED_QUIET_RUN = 7, chosen because the committed measurement at bench/the_false_quiet_rate_is_not_the_gates_rate_2026-10-08.py shows the premature-window rate falling 0.1264 -> 0.0784 -> 0.0458 -> 0.0263 -> 0.0000 as the window goes 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7. But 32 of 47 shipped configs set the value to 3 EXPLICITLY, so the repair was inert for every experiment that matters -- an addition nothing reaches. ONLY 12 OF THE 32 WERE RAISED, AND 20 DELIBERATELY WERE NOT. A config is also the RECORD of how an experiment was run. 20 of the 32 belong to experiments with archived runs in bench/logs and are left exactly as they are: editing them would misrepresent how exp40 through exp49, exp53 and exp55 were conducted, which is falsifying evidence rather than fixing a default. The other 12 have no archived run -- exp50 physics, exp51 biology, exp52's 5 factorial cells and exp56's 3 arms -- and each carries max_rounds of 8 or 16, so a window of 7 is reachable. FEASIBILITY WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE CHANGE, not after: 31 of 33 configs setting the knob have max_rounds >= 7, 93.9394%, Wilson [80.3938%, 98.3219%], Clopper-Pearson [79.7736%, 99.2574%]. THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN BURIED. A window of 7 needs at least 7 settled rounds, so a converging run takes 8 rounds where it took 4. The 3 shakedown legs converged at rounds 3, 4 and 4. On a PAID run that is roughly double the dispatches, and it is the price of taking the premature-window rate from 0.1264 to 0.0000. A HISTORICAL FINDING FELL OUT OF THE FEASIBILITY CHECK. bench/exp42_configs/42_composer_confirm.json sets a window of 3 inside max_rounds of 2, so the settled-round convergence route could never have been satisfied in that run. It is archived, so it is left alone and PINNED instead, by an assertion that refuses if someone later tidies it and erases the fact. Guard: bench/tests/test_the_quiet_run_is_seven_where_it_can_be_2026-10-17.py, 5 assertions, in the pre-commit set. BOTH DIRECTIONS go red under mutation: reverting an unrun config to 3 fails the ratchet, and raising an archived config to 7 fails the anti-overreach assertion. title: A19: S_k now classifies the FIX, not the target, so a prose edit is unscored
verbatim: A19: S_k now classifies the FIX, not the target, so a prose edit is unscored HIS DESIGN POINT, 2026-09-10: a prose input should be marked inadmissible "while still solving any computationally reducible elements within that prose! This is STEM." title: C16: R1 was excluded from the work queue by a state its own text contradicted
verbatim: C16: R1 was excluded from the work queue by a state its own text contradicted HIS RULING, 2026-10-12, on the zero-plant control: "Run it next after the outstanding simulated run. But take care that the caveats in place for simulated runs that do not and should not apply to real/paid runs carry over into this run. We keep all the useful lessons we have learned from the simulated runs and apply them. But we exclude things that only apply in simulated runs." THE MARKER AND THE PROSE DISAGREED, and the marker won. R1's entry says in capitals that the ruling made it work rather than a decision, while its marker read state: BLOCKED | ruled: 2026-08-07. Task 10.2 defines BLOCKED as the state for a ruling that awaits him, "so the resume pointer stops naming it as work". R1 was therefore invisible to the queue, and it was the ONLY BLOCKED marker in the file. It now reads state: OPEN | ruled: 2026-10-12, and the list carries 0 BLOCKED entries. This is the same class as the ruled-versus-prose defect fixed earlier today, with the polarity reversed: there the prose asked for a ruling already given, here the machine state withheld work already ordered. THE INVENTORY HIS CAVEAT REQUIRES IS BUILT AND COMES BACK CLEAN, measured by AST so a comment or docstring cannot be mistaken for code: 5 of 5 live branches on run_is_simulated are CAVEAT, 0 are BEHAVIOUR, and each keys off the -SIM suffix, so a paid run turns them off by having no such seat; 6 -SIM string literals in the live path, of which 5 are the suffix constant used to strip a label to its vendor base and 1 is a log message; stand-in fingerprints cannot inform a paid run, because fingerprint_scope defaults to experiment and returns 0 inherited observations against 11 under persist, 6 of them stand-ins. So the exclusion he asks for is STRUCTURAL rather than something to remember, and the lessons carry forward because they were never conditional on simulation. ON THE AMBIGUITY IN HIS FIRST SENTENCE, read literally it could ask that the simulation-only caveats DO carry over, which contradicts its own "do not and should not apply". The 2 sentences after it settle it, so no question was put to him; the reading taken is recorded in both the producer and the guard. TWO OF MY OWN INSTRUMENTS WERE WRONG FIRST. Scanning the whole repository reported 5 BEHAVIOUR branches, every one a line of the script's own source or another producer's -- a detector reading its own documentation as evidence. Then a line filter that skipped every line opening with a quote dropped the 2 dict-literal branches that emit the caveat, losing the cases it exists to find. A line scan also reported bench/evidence.py:897 as live code; it is a usage example inside a docstring. The AST replaced both.
