title: C18: capability is now keyed on a hashed identity, not on a model name
verbatim: C18: capability is now keyed on a hashed identity, not on a model name HIS QUESTION, 2026-10-16: "Didn't you say all you had to do was build what had already been recommended and that you would put this to the panel for their final take on your design? Why didn't you do that yet?" The build is now done. The panel's final take needs a dispatch his machine cannot take at present, recorded beside the owed runs on C12 and C15 with the same resource figures. THE DESIGN, as put to the free panel on 2026-10-14: "Key every capability decision on a STABLE IDENTITY -- a hash over (provider, model identifier, version) -- with the vendor name recorded as PROVENANCE and deciding nothing." WHAT IS BUILT, AND IT IS WIRED RATHER THAN OFFERED. bench/routing.py now carries capability_identity(provider, model_identifier, version), a stable 12-character digest over the normalised triple, with capability_provenance() carrying the readable inputs for a reader and deciding nothing. falsification_evidence_by_identity() pools each seat's refuted-of-total pair onto the identity it resolves to, through the registry's own resolve_model, and season_strength_order() now ranks IDENTITIES and orders the seats by the rank of the identity each carries. Two seats of one model share a position instead of being ranked against each other -- the same reasoning the refutation tally already applies when it counts distinct models. WHY A DIGEST RATHER THAN THE READABLE TRIPLE. The runner already held registry.model_identity, mapping a seat to model_id@api. That is an identity, but it is a NAME, and a name invites a capability decision keyed on it, which is the practice he has rejected 4 times. A digest cannot be read as a vendor, so a ranking keyed on it cannot smuggle one in. A stand-in seat shares the identity of the model it stands in for, which under-separates DELIBERATELY: under-separation makes auto-refutation harder, the direction that preserves findings. An empty identifier is REFUSED rather than hashed, because an identity derived from nothing is stable, shared by every such model, and silently wrong. THE MEASURED GAIN, by execution rather than by argument. Two seats of one model against one seat of another, with outcomes of 2 refuted of 2 and 2 of 2 against 0 of 4: ranked PER SEAT it does NOT establish and falls back to the vendor tuple; ranked PER IDENTITY it DOES establish and returns a measured order. Pooling both raises the sample per identity and cuts the comparisons Holm must correct for, 1 pair instead of 3, so a measurement survives where it previously did not. AND IT DOES NOT FABRICATE: with 2 of 2, 1 of 2 and 0 of 4 it still refuses. HIS "LOUD, NEVER DEFAULTED" CLAUSE IS NOW HONOURED. An identity carrying no falsification evidence is NAMED in the reason, with its digest, so a roster with no evidence reads differently from one whose evidence failed to separate. Before this both produced the same sentence. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: retiring DEFAULT_FALSIFIER_STRENGTH, the other half of the panel design. Emptying it collides with his earlier 2026-10-07 ruling about ladder MEMBERSHIP -- measured earlier today, it breaks 8 guards implementing that ruling -- and the collision is already recorded for him beside the constant. The fallback still exists; the gain is that it is reached less often. Guard: bench/tests/test_capability_is_keyed_on_an_identity_not_a_name_2026-10-17.py, 16 assertions, in the pre-commit set. Both mutations go red: ranking per seat again fails the measured-gain assertion, and making the identity readable fails both the stability and the no-vendor-name assertions. title: B13 and B21: a seat missing from a per-model table is now NAMED, not defaulted
verbatim: B13 and B21: a seat missing from a per-model table is now NAMED, not defaulted HIS RULING, 2026-10-16: "adding and removing models can become much simpler, because the only thing that governs capability is demonstrated measured capability, not model names", and "The ideal scenario is that ... this should become a trivial feature of the harness for a researcher to do." THE MEASURED PROBLEM IS THE FAILURE MODE, NOT THE COUNT. scripts/how_many_places_must_change_to_add_a_model_2026-10-16.py reports that a researcher adding a seat must edit 12 per-model tables across 6 live-harness files plus 1 registry .toml -- and that of the 10 steps a new seat passes through, 9 fail SILENTLY and 1 fails loudly: 90.0000%, Wilson [59.5850%, 98.2124%], Clopper-Pearson [55.4984%, 99.7471%]. A researcher who misses a table gets a seat that RUNS while losing whatever that table gated, which base_model_label's own docstring calls "a capability lost with no error". The POST screen now carries "every seat is fully registered", which names each absent table per seat across 4 of them: runner_core.MODEL_SPECS, runner_core.INITIAL_FINGERPRINTS, composer.PHENOTYPE_TRANSFORMS and composer.MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS. Executed against a hypothetical new seat it reports "Kimi: absent from 4 table(s)" and names every one, while CC2 and ChatGPT report "present in all 4". IT RETURNS PASS, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The screen is 2-state and halts at the first failure, with post_semantics_2026-10-06.py reasoning over that order in z3. A missing entry degrades a seat rather than invalidating a run, and a check that refused every run with an unregistered stand-in would be switched off -- the same reasoning the suite gate already applies to STALE. The absences travel in the headline and the notes, which the screen prints on a PASS as well as a FAIL. The check is placed LAST, because one that cannot fail on a degraded seat must not sit above one that can. A FALSE POSITIVE WAS CAUGHT ON ITS FIRST RUN AND IS PINNED. The check keyed every table through base_model_label and reported CC2 and ChatGPT as absent from PHENOTYPE_TRANSFORMS, when both are present under the composer's own keys (opus_4_6, chatgpt_5_4). The mapping is composer.COMPOSER_MODEL_MAP, which the measuring producer already used -- the instrument existed and the check reinvented its key derivation and got it wrong. AND A STALE FIGURE FELL OUT OF IT. post_semantics_2026-10-06.py illustrated the halt cost by substituting a literal 5, the number of checks when it was written. It now derives from len(POST_ORDER) and reads 6, so the sentence stays true as checks are added. STILL NEEDING HIS RULING: the single registration point, because that changes how every seat is configured. C18's hashed capability identity is the other half of making admission trivial and landed earlier today. title: B11: a reset immune memory was being reported as the confinement defect returning
verbatim: B11: a reset immune memory was being reported as the confinement defect returning RE-DIAGNOSED. This entry classified 7 failures as a SNAPSHOT of a growing archive, which is a question about baselines. Re-run today, the latent-tagger and field-envelope suites PASS, and all 6 remaining failures sit in test_immune_memory_evaluation.py with a different cause entirely: his ruling of 2026-10-16 was carried out, the immune memory was RESET, 6 experiments' priors were archived and the live store holds 0 records. AND THE SUITE CALLED THAT A REGRESSION. Its own message read: "NO class carries any refutation weight. Refutations were observed from leg 3 onward, so this means falsifiers have stopped reaching a refutation -- the confinement defect of 2026-10-15, or one like it, is back". IT IS NOT BACK. The memory is empty because he ordered it emptied, and a reader following that message would have hunted a defect that does not exist. A false alarm that names a real past defect is the most expensive kind to raise. FIXED BY READING THE RESET'S OWN RECORD. verbatim: Close C2 and C9; a dropped-in brief was being read as his verdicts Timestamp: 2026-10-17T17:52:00+01:00 C2 -- the three counting mistakes. bench/counting.py gives one place to count: `occurrences` for matches, `lines_containing` for lines, and `count_over` whose `unit` is KEYWORD-ONLY WITH NO DEFAULT, so a figure carries its unit out of the function. Both call sites in each live runner terminate the process with exit 42 after writing a partial report, so it sits at neither boundary he reviews. Turning it on converts 1 autonomous run into N sequential sessions, and the rounds after an intervention are not the same process as the rounds before -- so a convergence figure spanning one is not a measurement of autonomous convergence, which is this programme's success criterion. 0 shipped configs enable it; 0 archived runs paused. Its guard reads the default off the LIVE RunnerConfig dataclass and establishes the halt property with ast over both runners, FAILING IF IT FINDS NO BRANCH. 4 mutations, 1 test red each. THE COMMIT WAS REFUSED FIRST, by 2 guards, and the cause was his attachment. He dropped a Gemini Web design brief at Responses/design_brief.txt; its own title block opens 3 lines with a hash, and the reader counted all 3 as annotations of his -- 318 live register tickets against 321 annotations found. `_looks_like_a_markdown_heading` already existed and matches all 3 lines. It was gated on `.md` and `.markdown` only, on the stated assumption that every `.txt` there is one of his annotated reports. That assumption held until he began dropping FOREIGN DOCUMENTS in. FOUR SHAPE-BASED FIXES WERE MEASURED AND ALL FOUR REFUTED: * dated-filename filter: drops 8 of 598, 1.3378% Wilson [0.6794%, 2.6174%]; * markdown-structure detection: marks FINAL_REPORT_FOR_OPUS, which holds a real verdict, and misses design_brief.txt entirely; * removing the `.md` gate: drops 18 of 598, 3.0100% Wilson [1.9123%, 4.7076%], 12 of them REAL verdicts including "Verdict: y", "Go with option B" and "Go with option A"; * area from `subjects`: resolves for 11.0865% of tickets only. So the exclusion is EXPLICIT AND PER FILE, each with its reason, in `NOT_HIS_ANNOTATIONS`, and placed in a new predicate rather than in `is_a_response_file` -- narrowing that one would stop a genuinely unreadable file being reported as a reader gap. 598 annotations to 590; 0 live tickets were anchored to an excluded file, so nothing needed reconciling. The guard states the over-reach direction AS A SET and names the 5 short verdicts at risk, because a count cannot say which one went missing. 3 mutations, red each time. The word layer costs 27.7689 ms mean [24.1092, 31.4286] and grows linearly, so the brief's inverted-index proposal addresses something real. title: C6, C7 and B17: the notice now delivers the work instead of naming it
verbatim: C6, C7 and B17: the notice now delivers the work instead of naming it Timestamp: 2026-10-17T19:04:09+01:00 C6 -- "Are the 12 skipped safe to ignore?", 2026-10-05, unanswered for 12 days because no script existed that could answer it. STATIC: 472 skip SITES across 232 files, found with ast rather than by matching text, since `pytest.skip` appears in docstrings throughout. A SITE IS NOT A SKIP. 3 are literal `pytest.mark.skip`: 2 are the suite's deliberate offline default and the third decorates a `parametrize` placeholder used only when the real list is empty, so it is conditional in effect. 0 are dangerous. LIVE, over the pre-commit guard set: 1171 passed, 0 SKIPPED. For the gate that refuses every commit there are no un-made assertions at all. THE CLASSIFIER REFUSES TO FLATTER. UNCLASSIFIED is its own class and is never folded into SAFE, because a classifier that defaults the unknown to safe reports that everything is fine whatever the input. C7 -- "The routing ladder should be a measured statistic, not simply a list of named vendors", 2026-10-05. THE ORDER IS NOT ESTIMABLE FROM THE ARCHIVE: the omnibus test rejects equality, so the seats differ, but 0 of 10 pairwise orderings survive Holm or Bonferroni at 0.05, and a ranking IS a set of pairwise orderings. THE SUBSTANTIVE FINDING. The live panel roster is ['cx','cgpt','ge','ds','cc2','fable','kimi'] and the order is ('Codex','CC2','ChatGPT','Gemini','DeepSeek','Fable'). NOT ONE roster key matches, so the "ladder" returns the roster UNCHANGED -- reverse the input and the ranking reverses with it. It looks like a ranking and is an identity function. BEHAVIOUR IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: case-folding the match would REORDER the live panel, which changes which seat is asked first and needs his ruling. What changes is that a pass records `strength_order_was_unestablished` and `strength_order_matched`, carried into `routing_history`. TWO OF MY MEASUREMENTS WERE WRONG AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE RECORDED: a keyword-only parameter read as positional, then a literal-keyword search that missed the runner's `**_route_kw` and reported 7 of 7 where the answer is 6 of 7. Then the counter itself disagreed with the ranking -- 2 of 7 against 0 of 7 -- so `labels_the_order_ranks` is now the single rule and a test executes both on 5 rosters. B17 -- "If you can detect compaction mechanically, why can't you also make rs run mechanically too after compaction?", 2026-10-16. TWO THIRDS WERE ALREADY MECHANICAL and the honest answer names the third that was not: the hook already runs `cdsfl_recover.py --record-restore` and the task-boundary hook already returns 2 to refuse the stop. What a hook CANNOT do is make the assistant OPEN a document it names. On 2026-10-16 the notice supplied 10 paths, the restore ran, and the session still spent hours recovering. SO THE OPEN WORK IS INJECTED INLINE, measured before the shape was chosen: the full list is 654,237 characters; the open entries capped at 90 cost 2,009, at 120 cost 2,639, with their `ruled` state at 110 cost 2,828, and the identifiers alone cost 97. The 2,828 shape is used because `ruled` is the field that separates a decision he has given from a question he is owed -- the distinction whose absence left the zero-plant control in his queue for 70 days. The live brief measures 2,627 characters for 16 open entries. The cap and the budget are flags, so the budget stays his. THE LOGIC IS IN THE REPOSITORY and the hook is a shim, because a hook under `~/.claude/` is unversioned and exists on one machine: a fix that lives only there is one disk failure from never having existed. The call is wrapped, so a failure degrades to the old path list and the hook still exits 0. TRUNCATION IS ANNOUNCED AND THE IDENTIFIERS ALWAYS SURVIVE, proven at a 900-character budget: every open identifier is still nameable. A GUARD WHOSE VERDICT DEPENDED ON COMMENT LENGTH, found by it failing. Two tests sliced 1,100 characters from the `routing_history` append and checked for key names in the text; the comment added here pushed `last_falsifier_code` past the cut. That file already recorded the SAME failure twice for its third test, which had been converted to the syntax tree -- the lesson had been applied to 1 of 3. Both now parse the dict, which is also STRICTER: a key named only in a comment satisfied the slice and now fails, proven by mutation. THE REGISTER REFUSED THIS COMMIT ONCE, CORRECTLY. C6 and C7 were closed in the task list while their register tickets stayed OPEN, and the cross-check caught the disagreement -- 134 closed against the list's 136. Closing an entry now means closing it in both places, and B17 was closed in both at once. MUTATIONS: 3 on the brief, 3 on the matching rule, 4 on the stamp, 2 on the parsed guard, 3 on the skip classifier. Each turns the intended test red. GUARDS: 57 files. title: C1: the claim channel's commissioning measurement, which was never produced
verbatim: C1: the claim channel's commissioning measurement, which was never produced Timestamp: 2026-10-17T19:09:32+01:00 HIS INSTRUCTION, 2026-10-02: *"Also implement this and test it on the upcoming simulated runs."* His reply to the position that the claim channel's promotion into the scoring equations *"waits on a commissioning run measuring how often it is wrong against known ground truth"*. THE TEST HALF WAS DONE AND THE MEASURE HALF WAS NOT. `bench/claim_ledger.py` still carries `informative_only = True`, and its header still says the ledger is promoted "only after a commissioning run measures its error". The channel DID run in both free runs of 2026-10-15 -- 22 claims, 19 decidable, 3 routed -- so it was exercised. Its error had never been measured, and no entry recorded that as outstanding. WHAT "ITS ERROR" CAN MEAN, which decides what could honestly be measured. `claim_from_entry` does NOT judge whether a claim is true. It TRANSCRIBES the falsifier path: `decidable` is whether a falsifier exists, `verdict` is the falsifier's own verdict when that verdict is one of the decided five, and `routed_to` records where an undecidable claim went. So the channel's own error is TRANSCRIPTION error, and the end-to-end accuracy it inherits belongs to the falsifier path. Reporting one as the other would credit or blame the wrong mechanism, so both are measured separately and the boundary is stated. MEASURED against the 29 ground-truth-tagged claims in 5 prose STEM documents, under the project's own decider `falsifier_verify.reverify_falsifier`: * THE FALSIFIER PATH DISCRIMINATES BOTH WAYS on 5 of 5 documents -- CONFIRMED on the pristine text where the false claim is planted, REFUTED on the corrected text -- 100.0000%, Wilson [56.5518%, 100.0000%]. A template that always confirmed would pass half of this and fail the other half. * THE CHANNEL TRANSCRIBES 58 OF 58 VERDICTS EXACTLY, 100.0000%, Wilson [93.7882%, 100.0000%], Clopper-Pearson [93.8379%, 100.0000%], so its transcription error is bounded below about 6.2% at 95%. * ALL 4 ROUTING PROPERTIES HOLD: an undecidable claim is not decidable, its verdict is UNVERIFIED rather than a decision, it routes to a human, and a `state` claim routes to [VERIFY:current] instead. THE FIRST VERSION OF THE TRANSCRIPTION FIGURE WAS TOO WEAK TO GATE ANYTHING. It used 1 claim per document, n=10, Wilson [72.2467%, 100.0000%] -- bounding the error only below about 28%. All 29 tagged claims against both verdicts gives n=58 for no extra falsifier runs, because the verdicts were already in hand. PROMOTION IS NOT DONE, AND DELIBERATELY. The channel is not wired into sigma, S_k or R_k, and NO DOCUMENT SPECIFIES HOW it would enter them -- as a weight, a multiplier, a gate or a term. Clearing `informative_only` without that form would not promote the channel; it would stop the code describing itself truthfully while changing nothing, and then invent a model term to make it true. This project has one near-miss of exactly that shape: a proposal to replace the model-derived severity with a rubric already measured as agreeing no better than chance (kappa = -0.0227, Fisher p = 0.78), caught by the founder and not by a mechanism. So C1 stays OPEN at status TESTED: the measurement his gate asked for exists, and THE FORM IS HIS DECISION. The guard says that in the one place it cannot be missed: if `informative_only` is ever cleared, the same commit must wire the channel into a named term and re-derive the test, rather than delete it. ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS WAS WRONG AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT. The first version asserted that adding an undecidable claim to a decided ledger CHANGES the aggregate. `CLAIM_ADDRESSABLE` means, in the module's own words, "At least 1 claim in this target is decidable by computation", so a mixed ledger is still claim-addressable and the aggregate is not a mixedness measure. The test now asserts what is worth asserting: that all 3 of its states are REACHABLE, since an unreachable state is a distinction that decides nothing. MUTATIONS: 4, each turning the intended test red -- laundering an unknown verdict through, calling an undecidable claim decidable, clearing the promotion flag with nothing wired, and collapsing the [VERIFY:current] route into the human one. GUARDS: 58 files. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> BACKFILLED from project history on his instruction of 2026-10-17. title: B21 step 4 wired; step 1 refused on measurement; and a skip survey that lied
verbatim: B21 step 4 wired; step 1 refused on measurement; and a skip survey that lied Timestamp: 2026-10-17T19:21:00+01:00 B21 STEP 4 IS DONE AND IS SAFE. `check_policy_layers_merge` is registered in the preflight's CHECKS, in POST_ORDER and in DEPENDENCIES, so the halt-on-first-failure boot actually reaches it. It only ever refuses a run whose policy layers do not merge, so it cannot change what a passing run does. 17 of 17 layers merge, 100.0000% Wilson [81.5682%, 100.0000%] -- stated plainly as a RATCHET, because a check that lands green is not evidence it was needed. IT WAS PLACED WRONG FIRST AND A GUARD CAUGHT IT. I appended it after "every seat is fully registered", which is LAST deliberately: that check depends on nothing and REPORTS rather than refuses, so under halt-on-first-failure it can never hide a check above it -- and a refusing check placed after it would hide IT. `test_the_check_is_on_the_screen_and_last` refused the commit. B21 STEP 1 WAS MEASURED AND REFUSED, AND THE PLAN IT CONTRADICTS WAS MINE. * THE VOCABULARIES BARELY OVERLAP: the merged policy for domain=mathematics has 46 leaves and exactly 1 shares a name with a `RunnerConfig` field, `protocol.max_rounds`. For the other 45 there is nothing to wire. * THE ONE OVERLAP CONFLICTS: runner default 21, policy 5, same meaning. * THE POLICY'S VALUE AGREES WITH NO EXPERIMENT: of 47 shipped configs, 0 leave `max_rounds` unset (0.0000%, Wilson [0.0000%, 7.5558%]), so the runner's 21 is DEAD and the configs always decide. Values are 2, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 16, 20, 29. Letting the policy decide would CAP 46 OF 47 -- 97.8723%, Wilson [88.8870%, 99.6234%] -- below their configured round count and truncate the programme. So step 1 is not a wiring task but the question of WHICH LAYER OWNS `max_rounds`. Reported, not taken: each option has a different consequence for replay. The guard is written to notice the OPPOSITE -- if the shared-name set grows or the configs stop exceeding the policy value, it fails and says to re-measure. AND MY OWN SKIP SURVEY REPORTED A CLEAN RESULT FROM A DEAD PROCESS. The all-scope pass's pytest subprocess produced no output at all, giving 0 parsed skip reports, and the script printed "NOTHING SKIPPED IN THIS SCOPE. That is the strongest possible answer for it". That is the checker-that-decides-nothing shape, in the very script written to find it, and it survived about an hour -- caught only because the output looked too good for a 12,000-test suite. `fired()` now returns whether the run was READABLE, and an unreadable pass refuses with exit 3 instead of concluding anything. Two tests drive both directions with a monkeypatched subprocess -- a killed run and a completed one -- because 0 skips and a crash are otherwise indistinguishable. THE REFUSAL WAS RIGHT AND THE CALL WAS WRONG: `--scope all` was enumerating ~700 file paths into argv. It now passes the tests DIRECTORY, which pytest collects itself. GUARDS: 59 files. title: Rule 27 forbids a spelled number and the linter only catches a compound one
verbatim: B24. Rule 27 forbids a spelled number and the linter only catches a compound one. Added 2026-10-17T19:54:28+01:00. HIS RULING, 2026-09-04, verbatim: *"Never write a number in word form. Digits only, in every context without exception - chat replies, notes, TTS files, commit messages, code comments, briefs to other models. 'twenty-nine' is forbidden; '29' is required. This includes numbers embedded in prose."* He issued it after the rule had been stated and re-violated repeatedly, and recorded that the failure was never the absence of a rule or a checker but never running the checker. THE CHECKER DOES RUN NOW, AND IT UNDER-ENFORCES. `scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py`'s `WORD_NUMBER` pattern requires a MULTI-WORD number: a number word followed by at least 1 more. So `twenty-nine` is caught and `seven predicates` is not. Found 2026-10-17 while linting a note written to his standard: the linter returned 0 spelled-number findings on a file containing 22 of them. MEASURED BEFORE PROPOSING ANYTHING, because the fix is not small. A bare-word detector with an idiom whitelist (`no one`, `one another`, `one of three`, `one-off`, ordinals) over the 539 notes in `experimental_notes/` returns 16,743 occurrences across 522 notes, 96.8460%, Wilson [95.0074%, 98.0216%], Clopper-Pearson [94.9981%, 98.1522%]. The worst single file holds 692. WHY THIS IS HIS DECISION AND NOT MINE. The note lint is a RATCHET in `hooks/pre-commit` and currently holds at 87 findings. Widening the detector takes it to roughly 16,743, which either blocks every commit or forces a re-baseline - and re-baselining a ratchet to accommodate a detector change is lowering a number by changing the policy rather than the work, which is the exact move entry C29 was raised to refuse. THE OPTIONS, each with its cost: (1) enforce Rule 27 in full and clean 522 notes, which is a large mechanical edit over documents that include archived panel records whose wording is evidence; (2) enforce it on NEW notes only, by dating the ratchet so files written after a cutoff are held to the full rule and older ones are not, which is 1 condition and keeps the archive untouched; (3) leave the detector as it is and accept that bare counts pass, which makes the committed rule and the committed checker disagree. THE RECOMMENDATION IS (2), because it enforces his rule going forward without rewriting evidence, and it is the same shape as his own ruling of 2026-10-16 on vendor names: *"We normalise going forward ... I am not suggesting rewriting history."* Producer: the measurement above is reproducible from `scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py`'s own pattern plus the bare-word variant quoted in this entry. NEEDS HIS RULING.

title: The verdict-coverage audit recorded a count and not a set, so its result cannot be reconciled to the register
verbatim: B25. The verdict-coverage audit recorded a count and not a set, so its result cannot be reconciled to the register. Added 2026-10-17T20:13:17+01:00. WHAT IS WRONG. Entry C0 reports that an audit of 302 of his annotations found 20 confirmed gaps, of which 12 were rulings he gave that were never carried out. That audit produced the whole C-series and most of it is now closed. But C0 NAMES NO PRODUCING SCRIPT: searching its text for a script path returns nothing, and no script under `scripts/` carries the audit. SO THE FIGURES ARE A CLAIM ABOUT EVIDENCE RATHER THAN EVIDENCE, which is the exact shape his ruling of 2026-09-04 forbids: a measured count may be cited only if the script that produced it is committed alongside it. The project has already paid for this once, when a figure quoted as 282 of 711 could not be reproduced and 2 panel reviewers independently derived 680 and 4,874 as the denominator from the same archive. WHAT IT NOW BLOCKS, MEASURED. The register holds 318 annotation tickets in the UNCONFIRMED state, every one of them an annotation of his harvested from his Responses directory. Of those, 306 carry an anchor dated 2026-10-01 or later, which is C0's stated window, and 12 are older and were never in scope: 306 of 318, 96.2264%, Wilson [93.5209%, 97.8284%], Clopper-Pearson [93.5011%, 98.0352%]. C0 CLAIMS 302 AND THE WINDOW HOLDS 306. Those 4 cannot be identified, because a count cannot say WHICH items it covered and a set can, which is his own instruction of 2026-10-16: pin a set, not a count, because a count cannot say what moved and a set catches a swap. WHY THE OBVIOUS SHORTCUT IS REFUSED. Closing all 306 with C0 as the verification would assert that the audit covered 4 annotations it may never have read, and the direction of that error is the dangerous one: it would record an instruction of his as handled when nothing established that. The register's own rule is that CLOSED is tool-only and requires a verification rather than an assertion. THE FIX, AND IT IS BOUNDED. Write the audit as a committed producer that emits, for every annotation anchor in its window, the anchor and the verdict it reached: covered, gap, or undecidable. Then the register close becomes mechanical and per-anchor rather than a blanket claim, the 4-item discrepancy resolves itself into named items, and C0's figures become reproducible by anyone. The 12 pre-window tickets stay UNCONFIRMED until the window is widened deliberately. THIS IS WORK AND NOT A DECISION, so it needs no ruling from him; it is recorded here because it was found after the rest of the list's code work was complete and it is the only thing standing between the register and a fully settled state. Producer owed: none exists, which is the entry.

title: A mixed simulated panel: he has specified it at least 3 times and nothing tracks it
verbatim: B26. A mixed simulated panel: he has specified it at least 3 times and nothing tracks it. Added 2026-10-17T21:10:33+01:00. HIS WORDS, 2026-10-05: *"That is largely just expected behaviour in simulated runs. However I pointed (at least 2 times before now) to a partial solution for simulated runs too, where we could have a mixed panel of Opus 4.8, Opus 5x and Fable."* AND AGAIN, 2026-10-06: *"I have now addressed this multiple times. The simulated runs can involve a mix of models from Anthropic, from Opus 4.8 (and possibly 4.7), to you Opus 5.5, to Fable, and possible Sonnet 5.5 ... This would theoretically restore at least 5 models in the count. But why should the schema, or capability fingerprints, or the ladder care about model names at all?"* WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A PREFERENCE. A simulated panel of identical seats is STATISTICALLY FLAT, and the project's own record says what that costs: the capability ladder was found inert in simulation twice, on 2026-08-30 and again on 2026-10-05, because every rung resolved to the same model. So the one arm that Bench Run 2 depends on cannot be rehearsed at all while the simulated panel is uniform, and his proposal fixes that without spending on paid seats. His second point is the stronger one: if capability is a measured statistic, an unresolved finding should pass to a seat with demonstrably better measured capability, and the schema should not care what any of them is called. MEASURED 2026-10-17, which is why this is a gap and not a restatement. Searching all 154 task entries for a mixed or heterogeneous simulated panel, for a mix of models, for the specific model names he lists, and for the flat-panel problem returns 0 covering entries. The register does hold his 2 annotations, as 2 UNCONFIRMED tickets and 2 superseded MERGED ones, so the words were harvested and nothing was built from them. FOUND BY AUDITING HIS ANNOTATIONS ONE BY ONE, under entry B25, which is the half of that work no script can do. The verdict-coverage audit of entry C0 did not surface it, and C0 recorded no per-annotation verdicts, so it cannot be established whether C0 read these 2 and judged them covered or never reached them. THE FIX, AND IT IS SMALL FOR WHAT IT BUYS: give the simulated dispatch a roster of genuinely different Anthropic models rather than 1 model under 6 labels, so a simulated run exercises the ladder it is meant to rehearse. The capability-identity work of entry C18 already supplies the keying this needs, since a hashed identity per model is exactly what distinguishes 3 real models from 6 labels of one. NEEDS NO RULING FROM HIM: he has ruled it 3 times.

title: The verdict-coverage audit recorded a count and not a set, so its result cannot be reconciled to the register
verbatim: B25. The verdict-coverage audit recorded a count and not a set, so its result cannot be reconciled to the register. Added 2026-10-17T20:13:17+01:00. WHAT IS WRONG. Entry C0 reports that an audit of 302 of his annotations found 20 confirmed gaps, of which 12 were rulings he gave that were never carried out. That audit produced the whole C-series and most of it is now closed. But C0 NAMES NO PRODUCING SCRIPT: searching its text for a script path returns nothing, and no script under `scripts/` carries the audit. SO THE FIGURES ARE A CLAIM ABOUT EVIDENCE RATHER THAN EVIDENCE, which is the exact shape his ruling of 2026-09-04 forbids: a measured count may be cited only if the script that produced it is committed alongside it. The project has already paid for this once, when a figure quoted as 282 of 711 could not be reproduced and 2 panel reviewers independently derived 680 and 4,874 as the denominator from the same archive. WHAT IT NOW BLOCKS, MEASURED. The register holds 318 annotation tickets in the UNCONFIRMED state, every one of them an annotation of his harvested from his Responses directory. Of those, 306 carry an anchor dated 2026-10-01 or later, which is C0's stated window, and 12 are older and were never in scope: 306 of 318, 96.2264%, Wilson [93.5209%, 97.8284%], Clopper-Pearson [93.5011%, 98.0352%]. C0 CLAIMS 302 AND THE WINDOW HOLDS 306. Those 4 cannot be identified, because a count cannot say WHICH items it covered and a set can, which is his own instruction of 2026-10-16: pin a set, not a count, because a count cannot say what moved and a set catches a swap. WHY THE OBVIOUS SHORTCUT IS REFUSED. Closing all 306 with C0 as the verification would assert that the audit covered 4 annotations it may never have read, and the direction of that error is the dangerous one: it would record an instruction of his as handled when nothing established that. The register's own rule is that CLOSED is tool-only and requires a verification rather than an assertion. THE FIX, AND IT IS BOUNDED. Write the audit as a committed producer that emits, for every annotation anchor in its window, the anchor and the verdict it reached: covered, gap, or undecidable. Then the register close becomes mechanical and per-anchor rather than a blanket claim, the 4-item discrepancy resolves itself into named items, and C0's figures become reproducible by anyone. The 12 pre-window tickets stay UNCONFIRMED until the window is widened deliberately. THIS IS WORK AND NOT A DECISION, so it needs no ruling from him; it is recorded here because it was found after the rest of the list's code work was complete and it is the only thing standing between the register and a fully settled state. Producer owed: none exists, which is the entry.

title: Rule 27 forbids a spelled number and the linter only catches a compound one
verbatim: B24. Rule 27 forbids a spelled number and the linter only catches a compound one. Added 2026-10-17T19:54:28+01:00. HIS RULING, 2026-09-04, verbatim: *"Never write a number in word form. Digits only, in every context without exception - chat replies, notes, TTS files, commit messages, code comments, briefs to other models. 'twenty-nine' is forbidden; '29' is required. This includes numbers embedded in prose."* He issued it after the rule had been stated and re-violated repeatedly, and recorded that the failure was never the absence of a rule or a checker but never running the checker. THE CHECKER DOES RUN NOW, AND IT UNDER-ENFORCES. `scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py`'s `WORD_NUMBER` pattern requires a MULTI-WORD number: a number word followed by at least 1 more. So `twenty-nine` is caught and `seven predicates` is not. Found 2026-10-17 while linting a note written to his standard: the linter returned 0 spelled-number findings on a file containing 22 of them. MEASURED BEFORE PROPOSING ANYTHING, because the fix is not small. A bare-word detector with an idiom whitelist (`no one`, `one another`, `one of three`, `one-off`, ordinals) over the 539 notes in `experimental_notes/` returns 16,743 occurrences across 522 notes, 96.8460%, Wilson [95.0074%, 98.0216%], Clopper-Pearson [94.9981%, 98.1522%]. The worst single file holds 692. WHY THIS IS HIS DECISION AND NOT MINE. The note lint is a RATCHET in `hooks/pre-commit` and currently holds at 87 findings. Widening the detector takes it to roughly 16,743, which either blocks every commit or forces a re-baseline - and re-baselining a ratchet to accommodate a detector change is lowering a number by changing the policy rather than the work, which is the exact move entry C29 was raised to refuse. THE OPTIONS, each with its cost: (1) enforce Rule 27 in full and clean 522 notes, which is a large mechanical edit over documents that include archived panel records whose wording is evidence; (2) enforce it on NEW notes only, by dating the ratchet so files written after a cutoff are held to the full rule and older ones are not, which is 1 condition and keeps the archive untouched; (3) leave the detector as it is and accept that bare counts pass, which makes the committed rule and the committed checker disagree. THE RECOMMENDATION IS (2), because it enforces his rule going forward without rewriting evidence, and it is the same shape as his own ruling of 2026-10-16 on vendor names: *"We normalise going forward ... I am not suggesting rewriting history."* Producer: the measurement above is reproducible from `scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py`'s own pattern plus the bare-word variant quoted in this entry. NEEDS HIS RULING.
